techniques.fullNamePt: Canais de Fallback
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem utilizar fallback or alternate communication channels if the primary channel is compromised or inaccessible com o objetivo de maintain reliable Command and Control (C2) and to avoid data transfer thresholds.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific protocol used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various malware families and versions. Adversaries will likely change tool C2 signatures over time or construct protocols in such a way as para evitar deteção by common defensive tools.  `[Ref: University of Birmingham C2]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

detections.name: Behavioral Detection of Fallback or Alternate C2 Channels

analytics.name: Analytic 1376
analytics.descriptionPt: Establishing network connections on uncommon ports or protocols following C2 disruption or blocking. Often executed by processes that typically exhibit no network activity.

mutableElements.description: Can be tuned to include unexpected or high-entropy ports not typically associated with the process.
Useful to filter benign applications vs suspicious fallback attempts.
Tunable ratio of sent/received bytes to indicate potential C2 beaconing or exfiltration.
Adjust temporal window to match likely fallback C2 retries after primary channel fails.

analytics.name: Analytic 1377
analytics.descriptionPt: Creation of outbound connections on alternate ports or using covert transport (e.g., ICMP, DNS) from non-network-intensive processes, following known disruption or blocked traffic.

mutableElements.description: Can filter for rare fallback channel types (e.g., ICMP, DNS over HTTP).
Tuning by user (e.g., root vs. service account) helps suppress noise.

analytics.name: Analytic 1378
analytics.descriptionPt: Outbound fallback traffic from low-profile or background launch agents using unusual protocols or destinations after primary channel inactivity.

mutableElements.description: Used to suppress known legitimate agents.
Can help isolate covert or encrypted fallback traffic.

analytics.name: Analytic 1379
analytics.descriptionPt: Outbound traffic from host management services or guest-to-host interactions over unusual interfaces (e.g., backdoor API endpoints or external VPN tunnels).

mutableElements.description: May vary based on ESXi build and should be filtered to suppress known interfaces.
Environment-specific ranges to ignore (e.g., DR tunnels or out-of-band mgmt).

tools.name: Linfo
tools.procedurePt: **Linfo** (`S0211`) creates a backdoor through which remote attackers can change C2 servers. `[Ref: Symantec Linfo May 2012]`

tools.name: CHOPSTICK
tools.procedurePt: **CHOPSTICK** (`S0023`) can switch to a new C2 channel if the current one is broken. `[Ref: ESET Sednit Part 2]`

tools.name: HOPLIGHT
tools.procedurePt: **HOPLIGHT** (`S0376`) has multiple C2 channels in place in case one fails. `[Ref: US-CERT HOPLIGHT Apr 2019]`

tools.name: InvisiMole
tools.procedurePt: **InvisiMole** (`S0260`) has been configured with several servers available for alternate C2 communications. `[Ref: ESET InvisiMole June 2018]` `[Ref: ESET InvisiMole June 2020]`

tools.name: SslMM
tools.procedurePt: **SslMM** (`S0058`) has a hard-coded primary and backup C2 string. `[Ref: Baumgartner Naikon 2015]`

groups.name: OilRig
groups.procedurePt: **OilRig** (`G0049`) malware ISMAgent falls back to its DNS tunneling mechanism if it is unable to reach the C2 server over HTTP. `[Ref: OilRig ISMAgent July 2017]`

groups.name: APT41
groups.procedurePt: **APT41** (`G0096`) used the Steam community page as a fallback mechanism for C2. `[Ref: FireEye APT41 Aug 2019]`

groups.name: Lazarus Group
groups.procedurePt: **Lazarus Group** (`G0032`) malware SierraAlfa sends data to one of the hard-coded C2 servers chosen at random, and if the transmission fails, chooses a new C2 server to attempt the transmission again. `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster]` `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster RATs]`

groups.name: FIN7
groups.procedurePt: **FIN7** (`G0046`)'s Harpy backdoor malware can use DNS as a backup channel for C2 if HTTP fails. `[Ref: Crowdstrike GTR2020 Mar 2020]`

groups.name: UNC3886
groups.procedurePt: **UNC3886** (`G1048`) has employed layers of redundancy para manter acesso a compromised environments including network devices, hypervisors, and máquina virtual (VM)s. `[Ref: Google Cloud Mandiant UNC3886 2024]`

blockers: M1031 (Network Intrusion Prevention): Reverse shell ou beacon C2 não conecta para o exterior; conexões TCP diretas bloqueadas ou terminadas pelo Proxy/Firewall.
Firewall Egress restritiva, Proxy com inspeção SSL/TLS e bloqueio de domínios sem reputação ou DLP ativo.
bypasses: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

Empregar canais sobre Web Services legítimos permitidos (Microsoft Graph, GitHub, OneDrive), respeitar o Proxy do sistema via `WinINet` com credenciais integradas da sessão atual, aplicar jitter/sleep randomization e fragmentar transferências abaixo dos limiares de DLP.
blindSpots: **DestinationPort**: Can be tuned to include unexpected or high-entropy ports not typically associated with the process.
**ProcessName**: Useful to filter benign applications vs suspicious fallback attempts.
**DataVolumeRatio**: Tunable ratio of sent/received bytes to indicate potential C2 beaconing or exfiltration.
**TimeWindow**: Adjust temporal window to match likely fallback C2 retries after primary channel fails.
**ProtocolType**: Can filter for rare fallback channel types (e.g., ICMP, DNS over HTTP).

techniques.fullNamePt: Application Window Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of open application windows. Window listings could convey information about how the system is used. `[Ref: Prevailion DarkWatchman 2021]` Por exemplo, information about application windows could be used identify potential data to collect as well as identifying security tooling (**Security Software Discovery** (`T1518.001`)) to evade. `[Ref: ESET Grandoreiro April 2020]`

Adversaries typically abuse system features for this type of enumeration. Por exemplo, they may gather information through native system features such as **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`) commands and **Native API** (`T1106`) functions.

detections.name: Detection of Application Window Enumeration via API or Scripting

analytics.name: Analytic 0271
analytics.descriptionPt: Processes using Win32 API calls (e.g., EnumWindows, GetForegroundWindow) or scripting tools (e.g., PowerShell, VBScript) to enumerate open windows. These often appear with reconnaissance or data collection TTPs.

mutableElements.description: Tune to focus on suspicious function calls (e.g., user32.dll!EnumWindows).
Detect behavior from non-interactive or low-privileged users where enumeration is uncommon.
Shorten detection scope to rapid successive window enumeration attempts.

analytics.name: Analytic 0272
analytics.descriptionPt: Scripted or binary usage of X11 utilities (e.g., xdotool, wmctrl) or direct /proc/*/window mappings to discover open GUI windows and active desktops.

mutableElements.description: Common window management utilities can be tuned to reduce noise (e.g., xprop, xwininfo).
Restrict detection to processes executing under graphical sessions (e.g., DISPLAY=:0).

analytics.name: Analytic 0273
analytics.descriptionPt: Processes that utilize AppleScript, `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo`, or `NSRunningApplication` APIs to list active application windows and foreground processes.

mutableElements.description: Tunable to ignore benign scripting like automation by known apps.
Useful to suppress expected automation processes.

tools.name: SILENTTRINITY

techniques.namePt: Exfiltração por Outro Meio de Rede
techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração por Outro Meio de Rede
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar exfiltrate data over a different network medium than the Command and Control (C2) channel. If the Command and Control (C2) network is a wired Internet connection, the exfiltration may occur, for example, over a WiFi connection, modem, cellular data connection, Bluetooth, or another radio frequency (RF) channel.

Os adversários podem choose to do this if they have sufficient access or proximity, and the connection might not be secured or defended as well as the primary Internet-connected channel because it is not routed through the same enterprise network.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable WiFi connection, modem, cellular data connection, Bluetooth, or another radio frequency (RF) channel in local computer security settings or by group policy if it is not needed dentro do ambiente alvo.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent the creation of new network adapters where possible. `[Ref: Microsoft GPO Bluetooth FEB 2009]` `[Ref: TechRepublic Wireless GPO FEB 2009]`

detections.name: Detection of Exfiltration Over Alternate Network Interfaces

mutableElements.description: Filter for specific interface categories (e.g., WiFi, Bluetooth, 4G).
Tunable for environment-specific large file access events pre-transfer.

mutableElements.description: Match known interface manipulation utilities or driver invocations.
Tunable to non-default or rarely used interfaces (e.g., wlan1, hci0).

blockers: M1042 (Disable or Remove Feature or Program): `powershell.exe` bloqueado por GPO, ou Macros VBA desativadas por política de Mark-of-the-Web (MotW).

techniques.fullNamePt: Query Registry
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem interact with the Windows Registry to gather information about the system, configuration, and installed software.

The Registry contains a significant amount of information about the sistema operativo, configuration, software, and security. `[Ref: Wikipedia Windows Registry]` Information can easily be queried using the **Reg** (`S0075`) utility, though other means to access the Registry exist. Some of the information may help adversaries to further their operation within a network. Os adversários podem utilizar the information from **Query Registry** (`T1012`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions.

analytics.descriptionPt: Registry read access associated with suspicious or non-interactive processes querying system config, installed software, or security settings.

mutableElements.description: Focus detection on registry hives or keys likely to reveal environment info (e.g., HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion).
May tune for suspicious parent processes such as cmd.exe, wscript.exe, or mshta.exe.
Controls how closely registry access must follow process creation for correlation.

techniques.fullNamePt: Rootkit
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar rootkits to hide the presence of programs, files, network connections, services, drivers, and other system components. Rootkits are programs that hide the existence of malware by intercepting/hooking and modifying sistema operativo API calls that supply system information.  `[Ref: Symantec Windows Rootkits]` 

Rootkits or rootkit enabling functionality may reside at the user or kernel level in the sistema operativo or lower, to include a hypervisor or **System Firmware** (`T1542.001`).  `[Ref: Wikipedia Rootkit]` Rootkits have been seen for Windows, Linux, and Mac OS X systems.  `[Ref: CrowdStrike Linux Rootkit]`  `[Ref: BlackHat Mac OSX Rootkit]`

Rootkits that reside or modify boot sectors are known as **Bootkit** (`T1542.003`)s and specifically target the boot process of the sistema operativo.

detections.name: Detection of Kernel/User-Level Rootkit Behavior Across Platforms

analytics.name: Analytic 1061
analytics.descriptionPt: Unauthorized or anomalous loading of kernel-mode drivers or DLLs, concealed services, or abnormal modification of boot components indicative of rootkit activity.

mutableElements.description: Signed vs unsigned drivers; many environments restrict unsigned drivers, but some legacy systems allow them.
Suspicious driver or DLL drop locations, e.g., \System32\Drivers\ or \Temp\
Rootkit installation via admin or SYSTEM account.

analytics.name: Analytic 1062
analytics.descriptionPt: Abnormal loading of kernel modules, direct tampering with /dev, /proc, or LD_PRELOAD behaviors hiding processes or files.

mutableElements.description: Directories where kernel modules or tampering could be staged (e.g., /lib/modules/).
Regex or heuristic match to anomalous module names (e.g., suspicious entropy or gibberish).
Monitor presence of suspicious preload values that mask processes or files.

analytics.name: Analytic 1063
analytics.descriptionPt: Execution of unsigned kernel extensions (KEXTs), tampering with LaunchDaemons, or userspace hooks into system libraries.

mutableElements.description: Allowable level of unsigned/3rd-party kernel extensions varies by organization.
Detect whether the extension was loaded by an untrusted process or non-root user.
Detection tuned based on deviation from known/approved LaunchDaemon plist files.

techniques.namePt: Descoberta de Configuração de Rede do Sistema
techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Configuração de Rede do Sistema
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem look for details about the network configuration and settings, such as IP and/or MAC addresses, of systems they access or through information discovery of sistemas remotos. Several sistema operativo administration utilities exist that pode ser utilizado para gather this information. Examples include **Arp** (`S0099`), **ipconfig** (`S0100`)/**ifconfig** (`S0101`), **nbtstat** (`S0102`), and **route** (`S0103`).

Os adversários podem também leverage a **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) on network devices to gather information about configurations and settings, such as IP addresses of configured interfaces and static/dynamic routes (e.g. `show ip route`, `show ip interface`). `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` `[Ref: Mandiant APT41 Global Intrusion ]` On ESXi, adversaries may leverage esxcli to gather network configuration information. Por exemplo, the command `esxcli network nic list` will retrieve the MAC address, while `esxcli network ip interface ipv4 get` will retrieve the local IPv4 address. `[Ref: Trellix Rnasomhouse 2024]`

Os adversários podem utilizar the information from **System Network Configuration Discovery** (`T1016`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including determining certain access within the rede alvo and what actions to do next.

detections.name: Behavioral Detection of System Network Configuration Discovery

analytics.name: Analytic 0559
analytics.descriptionPt: Execution of built-in tools (e.g., ipconfig, route, netsh) or PowerShell/WMI queries to enumerate IP, MAC, interface status, or routing configuration.

mutableElements.description: Filter known/legit CLI chains (e.g., explorer.exe → cmd.exe) to reduce FP
Target executions by non-admin or unexpected users
Cluster enumeration commands within short time windows

analytics.name: Analytic 0560
analytics.descriptionPt: Execution of `ifconfig`, `ip a`, or access to `/proc/net/` indicating collection of local interface and route configuration.

mutableElements.description: Match regex for variations in enumeration syntax (e.g., `ip -4 addr show`)
Differentiate scripted versus interactive sessions

analytics.name: Analytic 0561
analytics.descriptionPt: Execution of `ifconfig`, `networksetup`, or `system_profiler` to query IP/MAC/interface configuration and status.

mutableElements.description: Scripted tools (e.g., bash calling `ifconfig`) vs GUI-initiated inspection
Enumerations executed frequently or across multiple interfaces may indicate enumeration loops

analytics.name: Analytic 0562
analytics.descriptionPt: Use of `esxcli network` commands (e.g., `esxcli network nic list`, `esxcli network ip interface ipv4 get`) via SSH or hostd to enumerate adapter and IP information.

mutableElements.description: Detection may vary based on internal vs remote terminal usage
Distinguish between benign status checks and deep enumeration chains

techniques.fullNameEn: System Network Configuration Discovery: Internet Connection Discovery
techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Configuração de Rede do Sistema: Internet Connection Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem check for Internet connectivity on compromised systems. This may be performed during automated discovery and can be accomplished in numerous ways such as using **Ping** (`S0097`), `tracert`, and GET requests to websites, or performing initial speed testing to confirm bandwidth.

Os adversários podem utilizar the results and responses from these requests to determine if the system is capable of communicating with their C2 servers before attempting to connect to them. The results may also be used to identify routes, redirectors, and proxy servers.

techniques.fullNameEn: System Network Configuration Discovery: Wi-Fi Discovery
techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Configuração de Rede do Sistema: Wi-Fi Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem pesquisar for information about Wi-Fi networks, such as network names and passwords, on compromised systems. Os adversários podem utilizar Wi-Fi information as part of **Account Discovery** (`T1087`), **Remote System Discovery** (`T1018`), and other discovery or **Credential Access** (`TA0006`) activity to support both ongoing and future campaigns.

Os adversários podem recolher various types of information about Wi-Fi networks from hosts. Por exemplo, on Windows names and passwords of all Wi-Fi networks a device has previously connected to may be available through `netsh wlan show profiles` to enumerate Wi-Fi names and then `netsh wlan show profile “Wi-Fi name” key=clear` to show a Wi-Fi network’s corresponding password. `[Ref: BleepingComputer Agent Tesla steal wifi passwords]` `[Ref: Malware Bytes New AgentTesla variant steals WiFi credentials]` `[Ref: Check Point APT35 CharmPower January 2022]` Additionally, names and other details of locally reachable Wi-Fi networks can be discovered using calls to `wlanAPI.dll` **Native API** (`T1106`) functions. `[Ref: Binary Defense Emotes Wi-Fi Spreader]`

Em sistemas Linux, names and passwords of all Wi-Fi-networks a device has previously connected to may be available in files under ` /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/`. `[Ref: Wi-Fi Password of All Connected Networks in Windows/Linux]` Em sistemas macOS, the password of a known Wi-Fi may be identified with ` security find-generic-password -wa wifiname` (requires admin username/password). `[Ref: Find Wi-Fi Password on Mac]`
codeArtifacts: netsh wlan show profile “Wi-Fi name” key=clear
[Ref: BleepingComputer Agent Tesla steal wifi passwords]
[Ref: Malware Bytes New AgentTesla variant steals WiFi credentials]

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Sistemas Remotos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier on a network that may be used for Lateral Movement from the current system. Functionality could exist within remote access tools to enable this, but utilities available on the sistema operativo could also be used such as  **Ping** (`S0097`), `net view` using **Net** (`S0039`), or, on ESXi servers, `esxcli network diag ping`.

Os adversários podem também analyze data from local host files (ex: `C:\Windows\System32\Drivers\etc\hosts` or `/etc/hosts`) or other passive means (such as local **Arp** (`S0099`) cache entries) com o objetivo de discover the presence of sistemas remotos in an environment.

Os adversários podem também target discovery of network infrastructure as well as leverage **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) commands on network devices to gather detailed information about systems within a network (e.g. `show cdp neighbors`, `show arp`). `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` `[Ref: CISA AR21-126A FIVEHANDS May 2021]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração Automatizada: Traffic Duplication
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de traffic mirroring com o objetivo de automate data exfiltration over compromised infrastructure. Traffic mirroring is a native feature for some devices, often used for network analysis. Por exemplo, devices may be configured to forward tráfego de rede to one or more destinations for analysis by a network analyzer or other monitoring device.  `[Ref: Cisco Traffic Mirroring]` `[Ref: Juniper Traffic Mirroring]`

Os adversários podem abusar de traffic mirroring to mirror or redirect tráfego de rede through other infrastructure they control. Malicious modifications to network devices to enable traffic redirection may be possible through **ROMMONkit** (`T1542.004`) or **Patch System Image** (`T1601.001`). `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`

Many cloud-based environments also support traffic mirroring. Por exemplo, AWS Traffic Mirroring, GCP Packet Mirroring, and Azure vTap allow users to define specified instances to collect traffic from and specified targets to send collected traffic to. `[Ref: AWS Traffic Mirroring]` `[Ref: GCP Packet Mirroring]` `[Ref: Azure Virtual Network TAP]`

Os adversários podem utilizar traffic duplication in conjunction with **Network Sniffing** (`T1040`), **Input Capture** (`T1056`), or **Adversary-in-the-Middle** (`T1557`) depending on the goals and objectives of the adversary.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que all wired and/or wireless traffic is encrypted appropriately. Use best practices for authentication protocols, such as Kerberos, and ensure web traffic that may contain credentials is protected by SSL/TLS.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Em ambientes Cloud, ensure that users are not granted permissions to create or modify traffic mirrors unless this is explicitly required.

techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços Remotos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to log into a service that accepts remote connections, such as telnet, SSH, and VNC. The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user.

In an enterprise environment, servers and workstations can be organized into domains. Domains provide centralized identity management, allowing users to login using one set of credentials across the entire network. If an adversary is able to obtain a set of valid domain credentials, they could login to many different machines using remote access protocols such as secure shell (SSH) or remote desktop protocol (RDP). `[Ref: SSH Secure Shell]` `[Ref: TechNet Remote Desktop Services]` They could also login to accessible SaaS or IaaS services, such as those that federate their identities to the domain, or management platforms for internal virtualization environments such as VMware vCenter. 

Legitimate applications (such as **Software Deployment Tools** (`T1072`) and other administrative programs) may utilize **Remote Services** (`T1021`) to access remote hosts. Por exemplo, Apple Remote Desktop (ARD) on macOS is native software used for remote management. ARD leverages a blend of protocols, including **VNC** (`T1021.005`) to send the screen and control buffers and **SSH** (`T1021.004`) for secure file transfer. `[Ref: Remote Management MDM macOS]` `[Ref: Kickstart Apple Remote Desktop commands]` `[Ref: Apple Remote Desktop Admin Guide 3.3]` Adversaries can abuse applications such as ARD to gain Remote Code Execution (RCE) and perform lateral movement. In versions of macOS prior to 10.14, an adversary can escalate an SSH session to an ARD session which enables an adversary to accept TCC (Transparency, Consent, and Control) prompts without user interaction and gain access to data. `[Ref: FireEye 2019 Apple Remote Desktop]` `[Ref: Lockboxx ARD 2019]` `[Ref: Kickstart Apple Remote Desktop commands]`

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent unnecessary remote access to file shares, hypervisors, sensitive systems, etc. Mechanisms to limit access may include use of network concentrators, RDP gateways, etc. `[Ref: Sygnia ESXi Ransomware 2024]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Perform audits or scans of systems, permissions, insecure software, insecure configurations, etc. to identify potential weaknesses.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the accounts that may use remote services. Limit the permissions for accounts that are at higher risk of compromise; for example, configure SSH so users can only run specific programs.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: If remote services, such as the ability to make direct connections to cloud máquina virtual (VM)s, are not required, disable these connection types where feasible. On ESXi servers, consider enabling lockdown mode, which disables direct access to an ESXi host and requires that the host be managed remotely using vCenter. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence ESXi Hardening 2023]` `[Ref: Broadcom ESXi Lockdown Mode]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication on remote service logons where possible.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not reuse Administrador Local account passwords across systems. Ensure password complexity and uniqueness such that the passwords cannot be cracked or guessed.

techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços Remotos: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to log into a computer using the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP). The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user.

Remote desktop is a common feature in sistema operativos. It allows a user to log into an interactive session with a system desktop interface gráfica (GUI) on a remote system. Microsoft refers to its implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) as Remote Desktop Services (RDS). `[Ref: TechNet Remote Desktop Services]` 

Os adversários podem connect to a remote system over RDP/RDS to expand access if the service is enabled and allows access to accounts with known credentials. Adversaries will likely use Credential Access techniques to acquire credentials to use with RDP. Os adversários podem também use RDP in conjunction with the **Accessibility Features** (`T1546.008`) or **Terminal Services DLL** (`T1505.005`) for Persistence. `[Ref: Alperovitch Malware]`

mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not leave RDP accessible from the internet. Enable firewall rules to block RDP traffic between network security zones within a network.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços Remotos: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to interact with a remote network share using Server Message Block (SMB). The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user.

SMB is a file, printer, and serial port sharing protocol for Windows machines on the same network or domain. Os adversários podem utilizar SMB to interact with file shares, allowing them para realizar movimentação lateral throughout a network. Linux and macOS implementations of SMB typically use Samba.

Windows systems have hidden network shares that are accessible only to administrators and provide the ability for remote file copy and other administrative functions. Example network shares include `C$`, `ADMIN$`, and `IPC$`. Os adversários podem utilizar this technique in conjunction with administrator-level **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to remotely access a networked system over SMB, `[Ref: Wikipedia Server Message Block]` to interact with systems using remote procedure calls (RPCs), `[Ref: TechNet RPC]` transfer files, and run transferred binaries through remote Execution. Example execution techniques that rely on authenticated sessions over SMB/RPC are **Scheduled Task/Job** (`T1053`), **Service Execution** (`T1569.002`), and **Windows Management Instrumentation** (`T1047`). Adversaries can also use NTLM hashes to access administrator shares on systems with **Pass the Hash** (`T1550.002`) and certain configuration and patch levels. `[Ref: Microsoft Admin Shares]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Remote Services: Distributed Component Object Model
techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços Remotos: Distributed Component Object Model
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to interact with remote machines by taking advantage of Distributed Component Object Model (DCOM). The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user.

The Windows Component Object Model (COM) is a component of the native Windows application programming interface (API) that enables interaction between software objects, or executable code that implements one or more interfaces. Through COM, a client object can call methods of server objects, which are typically Dynamic Link Libraries (DLL) or executables (EXE). Distributed COM (DCOM) is transparent middleware that extends the functionality of COM beyond a local computer using remote procedure call (RPC) technology. `[Ref: Fireeye Hunting COM June 2019]` `[Ref: Microsoft COM]`

Permissions to interact with local and remote server COM objects are specified by access control lists (ACL) in the Registry. `[Ref: Microsoft Process Wide Com Keys]` Por omissão, only Administrators may remotely activate and launch COM objects through DCOM. `[Ref: Microsoft COM ACL]`

Through DCOM, adversaries operating in the context of an appropriately privileged user can remotely obtain arbitrary and even direct shellcode execution through Office applications `[Ref: Enigma Outlook DCOM Lateral Movement Nov 2017]` as well as other Windows objects that contain insecure methods. `[Ref: Enigma MMC20 COM Jan 2017]` `[Ref: Enigma DCOM Lateral Movement Jan 2017]` DCOM can also execute macros in existing documents `[Ref: Enigma Excel DCOM Sept 2017]` and may also invoke **Dynamic Data Exchange** (`T1559.002`) (DDE) execution directly through a COM created instance of a Microsoft Office application `[Ref: Cyberreason DCOM DDE Lateral Movement Nov 2017]`, bypassing the need for a malicious document. DCOM can be used as a method of remotely interacting with **Windows Management Instrumentation** (`T1047`).  `[Ref: MSDN WMI]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Enigma Outlook DCOM Lateral Movement Nov 2017]

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling DCOM through Dcomcnfg.exe. `[Ref: Microsoft Disable DCOM]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure all COM alerts and Protected View are enabled. `[Ref: Microsoft Protected View]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços Remotos: SSH
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to log into remote machines using Secure Shell (SSH). The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user.

SSH is a protocol that allows authorized users to open remote shells on other computers. Many Linux and macOS versions come with SSH installed by default, although typically disabled until the user enables it. On ESXi, SSH can be enabled either directly on the host (e.g., via `vim-cmd hostsvc/enable_ssh`) or via vCenter. `[Ref: Sygnia ESXi Ransomware 2025]` `[Ref: TrendMicro ESXI Ransomware]` `[Ref: Sygnia Abyss Locker 2025]` Modern versions of Windows include a built-in SSH server and client. `[Ref: Windows SSH]` The SSH server can be configured to use standard password authentication or public-private keypairs in lieu of or in addition to a password. In this authentication scenario, the user’s public key must be in a special file on the computer running the server that lists which keypairs are allowed to login as that user (i.e., **SSH Authorized Keys** (`T1098.004`)).

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable the SSH daemon on systems that do not require it, especially ESXi servers. For macOS, ensure Remote Login is disabled under Sharing Preferences. `[Ref: Apple Unified Log Analysis Remote Login and Screen Sharing]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Require multi-factor authentication for SSH connections wherever possible, such as password protected SSH keys.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços Remotos: VNC
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to remotely control machines using Virtual Network Computing (VNC).  VNC is a platform-independent desktop sharing system that uses the RFB (“remote framebuffer”) protocol to enable users to remotely control another computer’s display by relaying the screen, mouse, and keyboard inputs over the network. `[Ref: The Remote Framebuffer Protocol]`

VNC differs from **Remote Desktop Protocol** (`T1021.001`) as VNC is screen-sharing software rather than resource-sharing software. Por omissão, VNC uses the system's authentication, but it can be configured to use credentials specific to VNC. `[Ref: MacOS VNC software for Remote Desktop]` `[Ref: VNC Authentication]`

Os adversários podem abusar de VNC to perform malicious actions as the logged-on user such as opening documents, downloading files, and running comandos arbitrários. An adversary could use VNC to remotely control and monitor a system to collect data and information to pivot to other systems within the network. Specific VNC libraries/implementations have also been susceptible to brute force attacks and memory usage exploitation. `[Ref: Hijacking VNC]` `[Ref: macOS root VNC login without authentication]` `[Ref: VNC Vulnerabilities]` `[Ref: Offensive Security VNC Authentication Check]` `[Ref: Attacking VNC Servers PentestLab]` `[Ref: Havana authentication bug]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: MacOS VNC software for Remote Desktop]
[Ref: macOS root VNC login without authentication]

mitigations.descriptionPt: Uninstall any VNC server software where not required.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: VNC defaults to TCP ports 5900 for the server, 5800 for browser access, and 5500 for a viewer in listening mode. Filtering or blocking these ports will inhibit VNC traffic utilizing default ports.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.descriptionPt: Inventory workstations for unauthorized VNC server software.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços Remotos: Windows Remote Management
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to interact with sistemas remotos using Windows Remote Management (WinRM). The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user.

WinRM is the name of both a Windows service and a protocol that allows a user to interact with a remote system (e.g., run an executable, modify the Registry, modify services). `[Ref: Microsoft WinRM]` It may be called with the `winrm` command or by any number of programs such as PowerShell. `[Ref: Jacobsen 2014]` WinRM  can be used as a method of remotely interacting with **Windows Management Instrumentation** (`T1047`). `[Ref: MSDN WMI]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable the WinRM service.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: If the service is necessary, lock down critical enclaves with separate WinRM accounts and permissions.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: If the service is necessary, lock down critical enclaves with separate WinRM infrastructure and follow WinRM best practices on use of host firewalls to restrict WinRM access to allow communication only to/from specific devices. `[Ref: NSA Spotting]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços Remotos: Cloud Services
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem log into accessible cloud services within a compromised environment using **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) that are synchronized with or federated to on-premises user identities. The adversary may then perform management actions or access cloud-hosted resources as the logged-on user. 

Many enterprises federate centrally managed user identities to cloud services, allowing users to login with their domain credentials com o objetivo de access the cloud control plane. Similarly, adversaries may connect to available cloud services through the web console or through the cloud command line interface (CLI) (e.g., **Cloud API** (`T1059.009`)), using commands such as `Connect-AZAccount` for Azure PowerShell, `Connect-MgGraph` for Microsoft Graph PowerShell, and `gcloud auth login` for the Google Cloud CLI.

In some cases, adversaries may be able to authenticate to these services via **Application Access Token** (`T1550.001`) instead of a username and password.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication on cloud services whenever possible.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the number of high-privileged domain and cloud accounts, and ensure that these are not used for day-to-day operations. Garantir que on-premises accounts do not have privileged cloud permissions and that isolated, cloud-only accounts are used for managing cloud environments. `[Ref: Protecting Microsoft 365 From On-Premises Attacks]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Remote Services: Direct Cloud VM Connections
techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços Remotos: Direct Cloud VM Connections
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to log directly into accessible cloud hosted compute infrastructure through cloud native methods. Many cloud providers offer interactive connections to virtual infrastructure that can be accessed through the **Cloud API** (`T1059.009`), such as Azure Serial Console `[Ref: Azure Serial Console]`, AWS EC2 Instance Connect `[Ref: EC2 Instance Connect]` `[Ref: lucr-3: Getting SaaS-y in the cloud]`, and AWS System Manager. `[Ref: AWS System Manager]`.

Methods of authentication for these connections can include passwords, application access tokens, or SSH keys. These cloud native methods may, by default, allow for privileged access on the host with SYSTEM or root level access. 

Os adversários podem utilize these cloud native methods to directly access virtual infrastructure and pivot through an environment. `[Ref: SIM Swapping and Abuse of the Microsoft Azure Serial Console]` These connections typically provide direct console access to the VM rather than the execution of scripts (i.e., **Cloud Administration Command** (`T1651`)).

techniques.fullNamePt: Data from Removable Media
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem pesquisar connected removable media on computers they have compromised to find files of interest. Sensitive data can be collected from any removable media (optical disk drive, USB memory, etc.) connected to the compromised system prior to Exfiltration. Interactive command shells may be in use, and common functionality within **cmd** (`S0106`) pode ser empregue para gather information. 

Some adversaries may also use **Automated Collection** (`T1119`) on removable media.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or otherwise obfuscating its contents on the system or in transit. This is common behavior that can be used across different platforms and the network to evade defenses. 

Payloads may be compressed, archived, or encrypted com o objetivo de avoid detection. These payloads may be used during Initial Access or later to mitigate detection. Sometimes a user's action may be required to open and **Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information** (`T1140`) for **User Execution** (`T1204`). The user may also be required to input a password to open a password protected compressed/encrypted file that was provided by the adversary. `[Ref: Volexity PowerDuke November 2016]` Os adversários podem também use compressed or archived scripts, such as JavaScript. 

Portions of files can also be encoded to hide the plain-text strings that would otherwise help defenders with discovery. `[Ref: Linux/Cdorked.A We Live Security Analysis]` Payloads may also be split into separate, seemingly benign files that only reveal malicious functionality when reassembled. `[Ref: Carbon Black Obfuscation Sept 2016]`

Os adversários podem também abuse **Command Obfuscation** (`T1027.010`) to obscure commands executed from payloads or directly via **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`). Environment variables, aliases, characters, and other platform/language specific semantics pode ser utilizado para evade signature based detections and application control mechanisms. `[Ref: FireEye Obfuscation June 2017]` `[Ref: FireEye Revoke-Obfuscation July 2017]` `[Ref: PaloAlto EncodedCommand March 2017]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider periodic review of common fileless storage locations (such as the Registry or WMI repository) to potentially identify abnormal and malicious data.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10+, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent execution of potentially obfuscated payloads.  `[Ref: win10_asr]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que a finite amount of ingress points to a software deployment system exist with restricted access for those required to allow and enable newly deployed software.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically detect and quarantine suspicious files. Consider utilizing the Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) on Windows 10+ to analyze commands after being processed/interpreted.  `[Ref: Microsoft AMSI June 2015]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Binary Padding
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Binary Padding
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar binary padding to add junk data and change the on-disk representation of malware. This can be done without affecting the functionality or behavior of a binary, but can increase the size of the binary beyond what some security tools are capable of handling due to file size limitations. 

Binary padding effectively changes the checksum of the file and pode também ser utilizado para avoid hash-based blocklists and static anti-virus signatures. `[Ref: ESET OceanLotus]` The padding used is commonly generated by a function to create junk data and then appended to the end or applied to sections of malware. `[Ref: Securelist Malware Tricks April 2017]` Increasing the file size may decrease the effectiveness of certain tools and detection capabilities that are not designed or configured to scan large files. This may also reduce the likelihood of being collected for analysis. Public file scanning services, such as VirusTotal, limits the maximum size of an uploaded file to be analyzed. `[Ref: VirusTotal FAQ]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Software Packing
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Software Packing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem realizar software packing or máquina virtual (VM) software protection to conceal their code. Software packing is a method of compressing or encrypting an executable. Packing an executable changes the file signature in an attempt to avoid signature-based detection. Most decompression techniques decompress the executable code in memory. Virtual machine software protection translates an executable's original code into a special format that only a special máquina virtual (VM) can run. A máquina virtual (VM) is then called to run this code. `[Ref: ESET FinFisher Jan 2018]` 

Utilities used to perform software packing are called packers. Example packers are MPRESS and UPX. A more comprehensive list of known packers is available, but adversaries may create their own packing techniques that do not leave the same artifacts as well-known packers to evade defenses. `[Ref: Awesome Executable Packing]`

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Employ heuristic-based malware detection. Ensure updated virus definitions and create custom signatures for observed malware.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Steganography
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar steganography techniques com o objetivo de prevent the detection of hidden information. Steganographic techniques pode ser utilizado para hide data in digital media such as images, audio tracks, video clips, or text files.

**Duqu** (`S0038`) was an early example of malware that used steganography. It encrypted the gathered information from a victim's system and hid it within an image before exfiltrating the image to a C2 server. `[Ref: Wikipedia Duqu]` 

By the end of 2017, a threat group used `Invoke-PSImage` to hide **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) commands in an image file (.png) and execute the code on a victim's system. In this particular case the **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) code downloaded another obfuscated script to gather intelligence from the victim's machine and communicate it back to the adversary. `[Ref: McAfee Malicious Doc Targets Pyeongchang Olympics]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Compile After Delivery
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Compile After Delivery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar make payloads difficult to discover and analyze by delivering files to victims as uncompiled code. Text-based source code files may subvert analysis and scrutiny from protections targeting executables/binaries. These payloads will need to be compiled before execution; typically via native utilities such as ilasm.exe `[Ref: ATTACK IQ]`, csc.exe, or GCC/MinGW. `[Ref: ClearSky MuddyWater Nov 2018]`

Source code payloads may also be encrypted, encoded, and/or embedded within other files, such as those delivered as a **Phishing** (`T1566`). Payloads may also be delivered in formats unrecognizable and inherently benign to the native OS (ex: EXEs on macOS/Linux) before later being (re)compiled into a proper executable binary with a bundled compiler and execution framework. `[Ref: TrendMicro WindowsAppMac]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Indicator Removal from Tools
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Remoção de Indicadores (Anti-Forensics) from Tools
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem remove indicators from tools if they believe their malicious tool was detected, quarantined, or otherwise curtailed. They can modify the tool by removing the indicator and using the updated version that is no longer detected by the target's defensive systems or subsequent targets that may use similar systems.

A good example of this is when malware is detected with a file signature and quarantined by anti-virus software. An adversary who can determine that the malware was quarantined because of its file signature may modify the file to explicitly avoid that signature, and then re-use the malware. `[Ref: Files and antivírus (AV) Detection]`

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Indicator Removal from Tools - Post-AV Evasion Modification

analytics.name: Analytic 0540
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection of known tools or malware flagged by antivírus (AV), followed by a near-term drop of a similar binary with modified signature and resumed activity (execution, C2, or persistence).

mutableElements.description: Vendor-specific signature string or detection message that can be correlated to threat intel context.
The time between AV alert and similar file/process activity (e.g., 5–30 minutes)
String or hash similarity thresholds between original and modified binary.

analytics.name: Analytic 0541
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection of anti-malware quarantining or flagging a tool, followed by a new binary written to disk with a similar function or name and a resumed process chain.

mutableElements.description: Tunable list of directories often abused for dropped binaries (e.g., /tmp, ~/.cache, /opt/soft/).
Limit how far up the tree to trace tool modification behavior for detection.

analytics.name: Analytic 0542
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection of XProtect or AV quarantining a known tool, followed by modification (file size, hash, string) and subsequent re-execution by the same or related user.

mutableElements.description: File hash delta or binary string diff score to tolerate renamed/mutated variants.
User or group expected to use dev tools; reduce false positives from legitimate repacking.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: HTML Smuggling
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem smuggle data and files past content filters by hiding malicious payloads inside of seemingly benign HTML files. HTML documents can store large binary objects known as JavaScript Blobs (immutable data that represents raw bytes) that can later be constructed into file-like objects. Data may also be stored in Data URLs, which enable embedding media type or MIME files inline of HTML documents. HTML5 also introduced a download attribute that pode ser empregue para initiate file downloads. `[Ref: HTML Smuggling Menlo Security 2020]` `[Ref: Outlflank HTML Smuggling 2018]`

Os adversários podem deliver payloads to victims that bypass controlos de segurança through HTML Smuggling by abusing JavaScript Blobs and/or HTML5 download attributes. Security controls such as web content filters may not identify smuggled malicious files inside of HTML/JS files, as the content may be based on typically benign MIME types such as `text/plain` and/or `text/html`. Malicious files or data can be obfuscated and hidden inside of HTML files through Data URLs and/or JavaScript Blobs and can be deobfuscated when they reach the victim (i.e. **Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information** (`T1140`)), potentially bypassing content filters.

Por exemplo, JavaScript Blobs pode ser abusado para dynamically generate malicious files in the victim machine and may be dropped to disk by abusing JavaScript functions such as `msSaveBlob`. `[Ref: HTML Smuggling Menlo Security 2020]` `[Ref: MSTIC NOBELIUM May 2021]` `[Ref: Outlflank HTML Smuggling 2018]` `[Ref: nccgroup Smuggling HTA 2017]`

mitigations.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Use Browser Extensions or Built-in Security Tools that:

- Monitor JavaScript API calls such as `Blob`, `URL.createObjectURL,` and `msSaveOrOpenBlob`
- Intercept and analyze HTML5 `download` attributes for suspicious payload generation
- Alert or block behaviors that match known HTML smuggling patterns (e.g., blob-to-disk payload construction)

Apply Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to:

- Restrict inline JavaScript and dynamic script generation
- Disallow downloads from unauthorized sources or blob URIs
- Prevent cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) abuse commonly used in smuggling chains

Enable or enforce enterprise browser controlos de segurança, such as:

- Endpoint's Network Protection and Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules, which can block Office and browser processes from creating child processes or writing to disk in suspicious ways
- Google Chrome Enterprise Policies, which can control file download behavior, restrict extensions, and isolate risky browsing environments

Deploy browser sandboxing solutions that can isolate JavaScript execution environments and enforce behavioral policy restrictions

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Dynamic API Resolution
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Dynamic API Resolution
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem ofuscar then dynamically resolve API functions called by their malware com o objetivo de conceal malicious functionalities and impair defensive analysis. Malware commonly uses various **Native API** (`T1106`) functions provided by the OS to perform various tasks such as those involving processes, files, and other system artifacts.

API functions called by malware may leave static artifacts such as strings in payload files. Defensive analysts may also uncover which functions a binary file may execute via an import address table (IAT) or other structures that help dynamically link calling code to the shared modules that provide functions. `[Ref: Huntress API Hash]` `[Ref: IRED API Hashing]`

To avoid static or other defensive analysis, adversaries may use dynamic API resolution to conceal malware characteristics and functionalities. De forma semelhante a **Software Packing** (`T1027.002`), dynamic API resolution may change file signatures and obfuscate malicious API function calls until they are resolved and invoked during runtime.

Various methods pode ser empregue para obfuscate malware calls to API functions. Por exemplo, hashes of function names are commonly stored in malware in lieu of literal strings. Malware can use these hashes (or other identifiers) to manually reproduce the linking and loading process using functions such as `GetProcAddress()` and `LoadLibrary()`. These hashes/identifiers can also be further obfuscated using encryption or other string manipulation tricks (requiring various forms of **Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information** (`T1140`) during execution). `[Ref: BlackHat API Packers]` `[Ref: Drakonia HInvoke]` `[Ref: Huntress API Hash]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Stripped Payloads
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Stripped Payloads
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar make a payload difficult to analyze by removing symbols, strings, and other human readable information. Scripts and executables may contain variables names and other strings that help developers document code functionality. Symbols are often created by an sistema operativo’s `linker` when executable payloads are compiled. Reverse engineers use these symbols and strings to analyze code and to identify functionality in payloads. `[Ref: Mandiant golang stripped binaries explanation]` `[Ref: intezer stripped binaries elf files 2018]`

Os adversários podem utilizar stripped payloads com o objetivo de make malware analysis more difficult. Por exemplo, compilers and other tools may provide features to remove or obfuscate strings and symbols. Adversaries have also used stripped payload formats, such as run-only AppleScripts, a compiled and stripped version of **AppleScript** (`T1059.002`), para evadir deteção and analysis. The lack of human-readable information may directly hinder detection and analysis of payloads. `[Ref: SentinelLabs reversing run-only applescripts 2021]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Embedded Payloads
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Embedded Payloads
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem embed payloads within other files to conceal malicious content from defenses. Otherwise seemingly benign files (such as scripts and executables) may be abused to carry and obfuscate malicious payloads and content. In some cases, embedded payloads may also enable adversaries to **Subvert Trust Controls** (`T1553`) by not impacting execution controls such as assinaturas digitais and notarization tickets. `[Ref: Sentinel Labs]` 

Os adversários podem embed payloads in various file formats to hide payloads. `[Ref: Microsoft Learn]` This is similar to **Steganography** (`T1027.003`), though does not involve weaving malicious content into specific bytes and patterns related to legitimate digital media formats. `[Ref: GitHub PSImage]` 

Por exemplo, adversaries have been observed embedding payloads within or as an overlay of an otherwise benign binary. `[Ref: Securelist Dtrack2]` Adversaries have also been observed nesting payloads (such as executables and run-only scripts) inside a file of the same format. `[Ref: SentinelLabs reversing run-only applescripts 2021]` 

Embedded content may also be used as **Process Injection** (`T1055`) payloads used to infect benign system processes. `[Ref: Trend Micro]` These embedded then injected payloads may be used as part of the modules of malware designed to provide specific features such as encrypting C2 communications in support of an orchestrator module. Por exemplo, an embedded module may be injected into default browsers, allowing adversaries to then communicate via the network. `[Ref: Malware Analysis Report ComRAT]`

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically detect and quarantine suspicious files.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent execution of potentially obfuscated scripts. `[Ref: win10_asr]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Command Obfuscation
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Command Obfuscation
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem ofuscar content during command execution to impede detection. Command-line obfuscation is a method of making strings and patterns within commands and scripts more difficult to signature and analyze. This type of obfuscation can be included within commands executed by delivered payloads (e.g., **Phishing** (`T1566`) and **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`)) or interactively via **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`). `[Ref: Akamai JS]` `[Ref: Malware Monday VBE]`

Por exemplo, adversaries may abuse syntax that utilizes various symbols and escape characters (such as spacing,  `^`, `+`. `$`, and `%`) to make commands difficult to analyze while maintaining the same intended functionality. `[Ref: RC PowerShell]` Many languages support built-in obfuscation in the form of base64 or URL encoding. `[Ref: Microsoft PowerShellB64]` Os adversários podem também manually implement command obfuscation via string splitting (`“Wor”+“d.Application”`), order and casing of characters (`rev <<<'dwssap/cte/ tac'`), globing (`mkdir -p '/tmp/:&$NiA'`), as well as various tricks involving passing strings through tokens/environment variables/input streams. `[Ref: Bashfuscator Command Obfuscators]` `[Ref: FireEye Obfuscation June 2017]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Fileless Storage
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Fileless Storage
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem store data in "fileless" formats to conceal malicious activity from defenses. Fileless storage can be broadly defined as any format other than a file. Common examples of non-volatile fileless storage in Windows systems include the Windows Registry, event logs, or WMI repository. `[Ref: Microsoft Fileless]` `[Ref: SecureList Fileless]` Shared memory directories on Linux systems (`/dev/shm`, `/run/shm`, `/var/run`, and `/var/lock`) and volatile directories on Network Devices (`/tmp` and `/volatile`) may also be considered fileless storage, as files written to these directories are mapped directly to RAM and not stored on the disk. `[Ref: Elastic Binary Executed from Shared Memory Directory]` `[Ref: Akami Frog4Shell 2024]` `[Ref: Aquasec Muhstik Malware 2024]` `[Ref: Bitsight 7777 Botnet]` `[Ref: CISCO Nexus 900 Config]`.

De forma semelhante a fileless in-memory behaviors such as **Reflective Code Loading** (`T1620`) and **Process Injection** (`T1055`), fileless data storage may remain undetected by antivírus (AV) and other endpoint security tools that can only access specific file formats from disk storage. Leveraging fileless storage may also allow adversaries para contornar (bypass) the protections offered by read-only sistema de ficheiross in Linux. `[Ref: Sysdig Fileless Malware 23022]`

Os adversários podem utilizar fileless storage to conceal various types of stored data, including payloads/shellcode (potentially being used as part of **Persistence** (`TA0003`)) and collected data not yet exfiltrated from the victim (e.g., **Local Data Staging** (`T1074.001`)). Adversaries also often encrypt, encode, splice, or otherwise obfuscate this fileless data when stored. 

Some forms of fileless storage activity may indirectly create artifacts in the sistema de ficheiros, but in central and otherwise difficult to inspect formats such as the WMI (e.g., `%SystemRoot%\System32\Wbem\Repository`) or Registry (e.g., `%SystemRoot%\System32\Config`) physical files. `[Ref: Microsoft Fileless]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider periodic review of common fileless storage locations (such as the Registry or WMI repository) to potentially identify abnormal and malicious data.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: LNK Icon Smuggling
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: LNK Icon Smuggling
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem smuggle commands to download malicious payloads past content filters by hiding them within otherwise seemingly benign windows shortcut files. Windows shortcut files (.LNK) include many metadata fields, including an icon location field (also known as the `IconEnvironmentDataBlock`) designed to specify the path to an icon file that is to be displayed for the LNK file within a host directory. 

Os adversários podem abusar de this LNK metadata to download malicious payloads. Por exemplo, adversaries have been observed using LNK files as phishing payloads to deliver malware. Uma vez que invoked (e.g., **Malicious File** (`T1204.002`)), payloads referenced via external URLs within the LNK icon location field may be downloaded. These files may also then be invoked by **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`)/**System Binary Proxy Execution** (`T1218`) arguments within the target path field of the LNK. `[Ref: Unprotect Shortcut]` `[Ref: Booby Trap Shortcut 2017]`

LNK Icon Smuggling may also be utilized post compromise, such as malicious scripts executing an LNK on an infected host to download additional malicious payloads.

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Encrypted/Encoded File
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem encriptar or encode files to obfuscate strings, bytes, and other specific patterns to impede detection. Encrypting and/or encoding file content aims to conceal malicious artifacts within a file used in an intrusion. Many other techniques, such as **Software Packing** (`T1027.002`), **Steganography** (`T1027.003`), and **Embedded Payloads** (`T1027.009`), share this same broad objective. Encrypting and/or encoding files could lead to a lapse in detection of static signatures, only for this malicious content to be revealed (i.e., **Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information** (`T1140`)) at the time of execution/use.

This type of file obfuscation can be applied to many file artifacts present on victim hosts, such as malware log/configuration and payload files. `[Ref: File obfuscation]` Files can be encrypted with a hardcoded or user-supplied key, as well as otherwise obfuscated using standard encoding schemes such as Base64.

The entire content of a file may be obfuscated, or just specific functions or values (such as C2 addresses). Encryption and encoding may also be applied in redundant layers for additional protection.

Por exemplo, adversaries may abuse password-protected Word documents or self-extracting (SFX) archives as a method of encrypting/encoding a file such as a **Phishing** (`T1566`) payload. These files typically function by attaching the intended archived content to a decompressor stub that is executed when the file is invoked (e.g., **User Execution** (`T1204`)). `[Ref: SFX - Encrypted/Encoded File]` 

Os adversários podem também abuse file-specific as well as custom encoding schemes. Por exemplo, Byte Order Mark (BOM) headers in text files may be abused to manipulate and obfuscate file content until **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`) execution.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically detect and quarantine suspicious files, including those with high entropy measurements or with otherwise potentially malicious signs of obfuscation.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt:
On Windows 10+, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts. `[Ref: Obfuscated scripts]`

Security tools should be configured to analyze the encoding properties of files and detect anomalies that deviate from standard encoding practices.
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.
