techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Polymorphic Code
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Polymorphic Code
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilize polymorphic code (also known as metamorphic or mutating code) para evadir deteção. Polymorphic code is a type of software capable of changing its runtime footprint during code execution. `[Ref: polymorphic-blackberry]` With each execution of the software, the code is mutated into a different version of itself that achieves the same purpose or objective as the original. This functionality enables the malware to evade traditional signature-based defenses, such as antivírus (AV) and antimalware tools. `[Ref: polymorphic-sentinelone]` 
Other obfuscation techniques can be used in conjunction with polymorphic code to accomplish the intended effects, including using mutation engines to conduct actions such as **Software Packing** (`T1027.002`), **Command Obfuscation** (`T1027.010`), or **Encrypted/Encoded File** (`T1027.013`). `[Ref: polymorphic-linkedin]` `[Ref: polymorphic-medium]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Compression
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar compression to obfuscate their payloads or files. Compressed file formats such as ZIP, gzip, 7z, and RAR can compress and archive multiple files together to make it easier and faster to transfer files. Adicionalmente a compressing files, adversaries may also compress shellcode directly - for example, com o objetivo de store it in a Windows Registry key (i.e., **Fileless Storage** (`T1027.011`)). `[Ref: Trustwave Pillowmint June 2020]`

In order to further evade detection, adversaries may combine multiple ZIP files into one archive. This process of concatenation creates an archive that appears to be a single archive but in fact contains the central directories of the embedded archives. Some ZIP readers, such as 7zip, may not be able to identify concatenated ZIP files and miss the presence of the malicious payload. `[Ref: Perception Point]`

File archives may be sent as one **Spearphishing Attachment** (`T1566.001`) through email. Adversaries have sent malicious payloads as archived files to encourage the user to interact with and extract the malicious payload onto their system (i.e., **Malicious File** (`T1204.002`)). `[Ref: NTT Security Flagpro new December 2021]` Contudo, some file compression tools, such as 7zip, pode ser utilizado para produce self-extracting archives. Os adversários podem enviar self-extracting archives to hide the functionality of their payload and launch it sem necessitar de multiple actions from the user. `[Ref: The Hacker News]`

**Compression** (`T1027.015`) may be used in combination with **Encrypted/Encoded File** (`T1027.013`) where compressed files are encrypted and password-protected.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically detect and quarantine suspicious files. Consider anti-virus products capable of unpacking and inspecting compressed files recursively, as well as analyzing SFX archives.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Junk Code Insertion
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Junk Code Insertion
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar junk code / dead code to obfuscate a malware’s functionality. Junk code is code that either does not execute, or if it does execute, does not change the functionality of the code. Junk code makes analysis more difficult and time-consuming, as the analyst steps through non-functional code instead of analyzing the main code. It also may hinder detections that rely on static code analysis due to the use of benign functionality, especially when combined with **Compression** (`T1027.015`) or **Software Packing** (`T1027.002`). `[Ref: ReasonLabs]` `[Ref: ReasonLabs Cyberpedia Junk Code]`

No-Operation (NOP) instructions are an example of dead code commonly used in x86 assembly language. They are commonly used as the 0x90 opcode. When NOPs are added to malware, the disassembler may show the NOP instructions, leading to the analyst needing to step through them. `[Ref: ReasonLabs]`

The use of junk / dead code insertion is distinct from **Binary Padding** (`T1027.001`) because the purpose is to obfuscate the functionality of the code, rather than simply to change the malware’s signature.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically detect and quarantine suspicious files. Behavior-based detections, rather than reliance on static code analysis, may help to identify malicious files that rely heavily on junk code. `[Ref: ReasonLabs]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: SVG Smuggling
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: SVG Smuggling
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem smuggle data and files past content filters by hiding malicious payloads inside of seemingly benign SVG files. `[Ref: Trustwave SVG Smuggling 2025]` SVGs, or Scalable Vector Graphics, are vector-based image files constructed using XML. As such, they can legitimately include `<script>` tags that enable adversaries to include malicious JavaScript payloads. Contudo, SVGs may appear less suspicious to users than other types of executable files, as they are often treated as image files. 

SVG smuggling can take a number of forms. Por exemplo, threat actors may include content that: 

* Assembles malicious payloads `[Ref: Talos SVG Smuggling 2022]`
* Downloads malicious payloads `[Ref: Cofense SVG Smuggling 2024]`
* Redirects users to malicious websites `[Ref: Bleeping Computer SVG Smuggling 2024]`
* Displays interactive content to users, such as fake login forms and download buttons. `[Ref: Bleeping Computer SVG Smuggling 2024]`

SVG Smuggling may be used in conjunction with **HTML Smuggling** (`T1027.006`) where an SVG with a malicious payload is included inside an HTML file. `[Ref: Talos SVG Smuggling 2022]` SVGs may also be included in other types of documents, such as PDFs.

techniques.fullNameEn: Obfuscated Files or Information: Invisible Unicode
techniques.fullNamePt: Ficheiros ou Informação Ofuscada: Invisible Unicode
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de invisible or non-printing Unicode characters to conceal malicious content within files, scripts, or text. By inserting characters that do not visibly render, adversaries may hide data, alter how content is interpreted, or make código malicioso appear as benign text or whitespace. Os adversários podem encode these malicious payloads, using binary, Base64, or custom schemes, to be reconstructed at runtime through scripting features such as **JavaScript** (`T1059.007`) Proxy traps, `eval()`, or other dynamic execution methods. This technique enables adversaries to evade visual inspection and basic static analysis by hiding malicious encoded content in innocuous text. `[Ref: PUAs Unicode - Eriksen]` `[Ref: Tycoon2FA - Unicode]` `[Ref: Unicode - Veracode]` 

Unicode is a standardized character encoding model that assigns a unique numerical value, known as a code point, to every character across writing systems, enabling consistent text representation across platforms, applications, and languages. Code points are represented as `U+` followed by a hexadecimal value and may be encoded using formats such as `UTF-8` or `UTF-16`. Os adversários podem abusar de the valid code points in Unicode that are not visibly rendered but still take up bytes, such as zero-width spaces, variation selectors, or bidirectional formatting controls, to conceal malicious payloads. `[Ref: Tycoon2FA - Unicode]` `[Ref: GlassWorm - Unicode]` `[Ref: Unicode and Hidden Prompts - Perets]`

Os adversários podem additionally exploit Private Use Area (PUA) characters, a range of code points reserved for custom assignment. PUA characters that are not defined by a font or application are typically rendered blank. `[Ref: PUAs Unicode - Eriksen]`

Unicode characters may also be leveraged in support of other techniques such as **Phishing** (`T1660`), **Right-to-Left Override** (`T1036.002`), or **User Execution** (`T1204`). Por exemplo, some adversaries may embed artificial intelligence (AI) prompt injections using invisible Unicode characters in emails or documents that appear benign when processed by AI systems. `[Ref: LLMs and Unicode - Medium]` `[Ref: Invisible Prompt Injection - Trend Micro]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Transferência Agendada
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem schedule data exfiltration to be performed only at certain times of day or at certain intervals. This could be done to blend traffic patterns with normal activity or availability. `[Ref: Delay Code Execution in Java]`

When scheduled exfiltration is used, other exfiltration techniques likely apply as well to transfer the information out of the network, such as **Exfiltration Over C2 Channel** (`T1041`) or **Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol** (`T1048`).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary Command and Control (C2) infrastructure and malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific obfuscation technique used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various malware families and versions. Adversaries will likely change tool Command and Control (C2) signatures over time or construct protocols in such a way para evitar deteção by common defensive tools.  `[Ref: University of Birmingham C2]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

Empregar canais sobre Web Services legítimos permitidos (Microsoft Graph, GitHub, OneDrive), respeitar o Proxy do sistema via `WinINet` com credenciais integradas da sessão atual, aplicar jitter/sleep randomization e fragmentar transferências abaixo dos limiares de DLP.
blindSpots: **PacketSizeThreshold**: Minimum repetitive size in bytes to consider as anomalous behavior (e.g., 512B or 1024B)
**IntervalRepeatWindow**: Timeframe over which repeated, evenly spaced transfers are flagged
**KnownServicePorts**: Common ports expected to exhibit protocol behavior; outliers flagged if not matching expected usage
**ProcessNetworkBaseline**: Whitelist of typical binaries expected to generate outbound connections (e.g., wget, curl)
**PayloadLengthVariance**: Deviation threshold to consider data 'fixed size' (e.g., ±5% size delta)

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta do Utilizador/Proprietário do Sistema
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar identify the primary user, currently logged in user, set of users that commonly uses a system, or whether a user is actively using the system. They may do this, for example, by retrieving account usernames or by using **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`). The information may be collected in a number of different ways using other Discovery techniques, because user and username details are prevalent throughout a system and include running process ownership, file/directory ownership, session information, and system logs. Os adversários podem utilizar the information from **System Owner/User Discovery** (`T1033`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions.

Various utilities and commands may acquire this information, including `whoami`. In macOS and Linux, the currently logged in user can be identified with `w` and `who`. On macOS the `dscl . list /Users | grep -v '_'` command pode também ser utilizado para enumerate user accounts. Environment variables, such as `%USERNAME%` and `$USER`, may also be used to access this information.

On network devices, **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) commands such as `show users` and `show ssh` pode ser utilizado para display users currently logged into the device. `[Ref: show_ssh_users_cmd_cisco]` `[Ref: US-CERT TA18-106A Network Infrastructure Devices 2018]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar manipulate features of their artifacts to make them appear legitimate or benign to users and/or security tools. Masquerading occurs when the name or location of an object, legitimate or malicious, is manipulated or abused for the sake of evading defenses and observation. This may include manipulating file metadata, tricking users into misidentifying the file type, and giving legitimate task or service names.

Renaming abusable system utilities to evade security monitoring is also a form of **Masquerading** (`T1036`). `[Ref: LOLBAS Main Site]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Auditar regularmente user accounts to ensure that each one has a defined purpose.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider defining and enforcing a naming convention for user accounts to more easily spot generic account names that do not fit the typical schema.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Train users not to open email attachments or click unknown links (URLs). Such training fosters more secure habits within your organization and will limit many of the risks.

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Require signed binaries.
mitigations.bypassHint: Recorrer a DLL Side-Loading (`T1574.002`) utilizando um executável legítimo assinado (vulnerável a sequestro de ordem de procura de DLL) que carregue a nossa DLL em memória, ou utilizar binários assinados nativos (LOLBAS - `T1218`). Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar controlos de segurança on the endpoint, such as a Host Intrusion Prevention System (HIPS), to identify and prevent execution of potentially malicious files (such as those with mismatching file signatures).
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use sistema de ficheiros access controls to protect folders such as C:\\Windows\\System32.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically quarantine suspicious files.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use tools that restrict program execution via application control by attributes other than file name for common sistema operativo utilities that are needed.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Invalid Code Signature
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar mimic features of valid code signatures to increase the chance of deceiving a user, analyst, or tool. Code signing provides a level of authenticity on a binary from the developer and a guarantee that the binary has not been tampered with. Adversaries can copy the metadata and signature information from a signed program, then use it as a template for an unsigned program. Files with invalid code signatures will fail digital signature validation checks, but they may appear more legitimate to users and security tools may improperly handle these files. `[Ref: Threatexpress MetaTwin 2017]`

Unlike **Code Signing** (`T1553.002`), this activity will not result in a valid signature.

Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Right-to-Left Override
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de the right-to-left override (RTLO or RLO) character (U+202E) to disguise a string and/or file name to make it appear benign. RTLO is a non-printing Unicode character that causes the text that follows it to be displayed in reverse. Por exemplo, a Windows screensaver executable named `March 25 \u202Excod.scr` will display as `March 25 rcs.docx`. A JavaScript file named `photo_high_re\u202Egnp.js` will be displayed as `photo_high_resj.png`. `[Ref: Infosecinstitute RTLO Technique]`

Os adversários podem abusar de the RTLO character as a means of tricking a user into executing what they think is a benign file type. A common use of this technique is with **Spearphishing Attachment** (`T1566.001`)/**Malicious File** (`T1204.002`) since it can trick both end users and defenders if they are not aware of how their tools display and render the RTLO character. Use of the RTLO character has been seen in many targeted intrusion attempts and criminal activity. `[Ref: Trend Micro PLEAD RTLO]` `[Ref: Kaspersky RTLO Cyber Crime]` RTLO can be used in the Windows Registry as well, where regedit.exe displays the reversed characters but the command line tool reg.exe does not by default.

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Rename Legitimate Utilities
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem rename legitimate / system utilities to try to evade security mechanisms concerning the usage of those utilities. Security monitoring and control mechanisms may be in place for legitimate utilities adversaries are capable of abusing, including both built-in binaries and tools such as PSExec, AutoHotKey, and IronPython. `[Ref: LOLBAS Main Site]` `[Ref: Huntress Python Malware 2025]` `[Ref: The DFIR Report AutoHotKey 2023]` `[Ref: Splunk Detect Renamed PSExec]` It may be possible para contornar (bypass) those security mechanisms by renaming the utility prior to utilization (ex: rename `rundll32.exe`). `[Ref: Elastic Masquerade Ball]` An alternative case occurs when a legitimate utility is copied or moved to a different directory and renamed para evitar deteçãos based on these utilities executing from non-standard paths. `[Ref: F-Secure CozyDuke]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Masquerade Task or Service
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar manipulate the name of a task or service to make it appear legitimate or benign. Tasks/services executed by the Task Scheduler or systemd will typically be given a name and/or description. `[Ref: TechNet Schtasks]` `[Ref: Systemd Service Units]` Windows services will have a service name as well as a display name. Many benign tasks and services exist that have commonly associated names. Os adversários podem give tasks or services names that are similar or identical to those of legitimate ones.

Tasks or services contain other fields, such as a description, that adversaries may attempt to make appear legitimate. `[Ref: Palo Alto Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Fysbis Dr Web Analysis]`

techniques.nameEn: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
techniques.fullNameEn: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
techniques.namePt: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem match or approximate the name or location of legitimate files, Registry keys, or other resources when naming/placing them. This is done for the sake of evading defenses and observation. 

This may be done by placing an executable in a commonly trusted directory (ex: under System32) or giving it the name of a legitimate, trusted program (ex: `svchost.exe`). Alternatively, a Windows Registry key may be given a close approximation to a key used by a legitimate program. In containerized environments, a threat actor may create a resource in a trusted namespace or one that matches the naming convention of a container pod or cluster. `[Ref: Aquasec Kubernetes Backdoor 2023]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use sistema de ficheiros access controls to protect folders such as `C:\Windows\System32`.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use tools that restrict program execution via application control by attributes other than file name for common sistema operativo utilities that are needed.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Require signed binaries and images.
mitigations.bypassHint: Recorrer a DLL Side-Loading (`T1574.002`) utilizando um executável legítimo assinado (vulnerável a sequestro de ordem de procura de DLL) que carregue a nossa DLL em memória, ou utilizar binários assinados nativos (LOLBAS - `T1218`). Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Space after Filename
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries can hide a program's true filetype by changing the extension of a file. With certain file types (specifically this does not work with .app extensions), appending a space to the end of a filename will change how the file is processed by the sistema operativo.

Por exemplo, if there is a Mach-O executable file called `evil.bin`, when it is double clicked by a user, it will launch Terminal.app and execute. If this file is renamed to `evil.txt`, then when double clicked by a user, it will launch with the default text editing application (not executing the binary). Contudo, if the file is renamed to `evil.txt ` (note the space at the end), then when double clicked by a user, the true file type is determined by the OS and handled appropriately and the binary will be executed  `[Ref: Mac Backdoors are back]`.

Adversaries can use this feature to trick users into double clicking benign-looking files of any format and ultimately executing something malicious.

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Double File Extension
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de a double extension in the filename as a means of masquerading the true file type. A file name may include a secondary file type extension that may cause only the first extension to be displayed (ex: `File.txt.exe` may render in some views as just `File.txt`). Contudo, the second extension is the true file type that determines how the file is opened and executed. The real file extension may be hidden by the sistema operativo in the file browser (ex: explorer.exe), as well as in any software configured using or similar to the system’s policies. `[Ref: PCMag DoubleExtension]` `[Ref: SOCPrime DoubleExtension]` 

Os adversários podem abusar de double extensions to attempt to conceal dangerous file types of payloads. A very common usage involves tricking a user into opening what they think is a benign file type but is actually executable code. Such files often pose as email attachments and allow an adversary to gain **Initial Access** (`TA0001`) into a user’s system via **Spearphishing Attachment** (`T1566.001`) then **User Execution** (`T1204`). Por exemplo, an executable file attachment named `Evil.txt.exe` may display as `Evil.txt` to a user. The user may then view it as a benign text file and open it, inadvertently executing the hidden malware. `[Ref: SOCPrime DoubleExtension]`

Common file types, such as text files (.txt, .doc, etc.) and image files (.jpg, .gif, etc.) are typically used as the first extension to appear benign. Executable extensions commonly regarded as dangerous, such as .exe, .lnk, .hta, and .scr, often appear as the second extension and true file type.

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Masquerade File Type
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem masquerade malicious payloads as legitimate files through changes to the payload's formatting, including the file’s signature, extension, icon, and contents. Various file types have a typical standard format, including how they are encoded and organized. Por exemplo, a file’s signature (also known as header or magic bytes) is the beginning bytes of a file and is often used to identify the file’s type. Por exemplo, the header of a JPEG file,  is ` 0xFF 0xD8` and the file extension is either `.JPE`, `.JPEG` or `.JPG`. 

Os adversários podem edit the header’s hex code and/or the file extension of a malicious payload com o objetivo de bypass file validation checks and/or input sanitization. This behavior is commonly used when payload files are transferred (e.g., **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`)) and stored (e.g., **Upload Malware** (`T1608.001`)) so that adversaries may move their malware without triggering detections. 

Common non-executable file types and extensions, such as text files (`.txt`) and image files (`.jpg`, `.gif`, etc.) may be typically treated as benign.  Based on this, adversaries may use a file extension to disguise malware, such as naming a PHP backdoor code with a file name of `test.gif`. A user may not know that a file is malicious due to the benign appearance and file extension.

Polyglot files, which are files that have multiple different file types and that function differently based on the application that will execute them, may also be used to disguise malicious malware and capabilities. `[Ref: polygot_icedID]`

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar controlos de segurança on the endpoint, such as a Host Intrusion Prevention System (HIPS), to identify and prevent execution of files with mismatching file signatures.
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically quarantine suspicious files.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Break Process Trees
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode attempt to evade process tree-based analysis by modifying executed malware's parent process ID (PPID). If endpoint protection software leverages the “parent-child" relationship for detection, breaking this relationship could result in the adversary’s behavior not being associated with previous process tree activity. On Unix-based systems breaking this process tree is common practice for administrators to execute software using scripts and programs. `[Ref: 3OHA double-fork 2022]` 

On Linux systems, adversaries may execute a series of **Native API** (`T1106`) calls to alter malware's process tree. Por exemplo, adversaries can execute their payload without any arguments, call the `fork()` API call twice, then have the parent process exit. This creates a grandchild process with no parent process that is immediately adopted by the `init` system process (PID 1), which successfully disconnects the execution of the adversary's payload from its previous process tree.

Another example is using the “daemon” syscall to detach from the current parent process and run in the background. `[Ref: Sandfly BPFDoor 2022]` `[Ref: Microsoft XorDdos Linux Stealth 2022]`

These behaviors sever the parent-child relationship and obscure the execution origin in process tree analysis.

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Masquerade Account Name
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem match or approximate the names of legitimate accounts to make newly created ones appear benign. This will typically occur during **Create Account** (`T1136`), although accounts may also be renamed at a later date. This may also coincide with **Account Access Removal** (`T1531`) if the actor first deletes an account before re-creating one with the same name. `[Ref: Huntress MOVEit 2023]`

Often, adversaries will attempt to masquerade as service accounts, such as those associated with legitimate software, data backups, or container cluster management. `[Ref: Elastic CUBA Ransomware 2022]` `[Ref: Aquasec Kubernetes Attack 2023]` They may also give accounts generic, trustworthy names, such as “admin”, “help”, or “root.” `[Ref: Invictus IR Cloud Ransomware 2024]` Sometimes adversaries may model account names off of those already existing in the system, as a follow-on behavior to **Account Discovery** (`T1087`).  

Note that this is distinct from **Impersonation** (`T1684.001`), which describes impersonating specific trusted individuals or organizations, rather than user or service account names.

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Overwrite Process Arguments
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar a process's in-memory arguments to change its name com o objetivo de appear as a legitimate or benign process. Em sistemas Linux, the sistema operativo stores command-line arguments in the process’s stack and passes them to the `main()` function as the `argv` array. The first element, `argv[0]`, typically contains the process name or path - by default, the command used to actually start the process (e.g., `cat /etc/passwd`). Por omissão, the Linux `/proc` filesystem uses this value to represent the process name. The `/proc/<PID>/cmdline` file reflects the contents of this memory, and tools like `ps` use it to display process information. Since arguments are stored in user-space memory at launch, this modification can be performed without privilégios elevados. 

During runtime, adversaries can erase the memory used by all command-line arguments for a process, overwriting each argument string with null bytes. This removes evidence of how the process was originally launched. They can then write a spoofed string into the memory region previously occupied by `argv[0]` to mimic a benign command, such as `cat resolv.conf`. The new command-line string is reflected in `/proc/<PID>/cmdline` and displayed by tools like `ps`. `[Ref: Sandfly BPFDoor 2022]` `[Ref: Microsoft XorDdos Linux Stealth 2022]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Mascaramento de Identidade/Binário (Masquerading): Browser Fingerprint
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar blend in with legitimate traffic by spoofing browser and system attributes like sistema operativo, system language, platform, user-agent string, resolution, time zone, etc.  The HTTP User-Agent request header is a string that lets servers and network peers identify the application, sistema operativo, vendor, and/or version of the requesting user agent. `[Ref: Mozilla User Agent]`

Os adversários podem recolher this information through **System Information Discovery** (`T1082`) or by users navigating to adversary-controlled websites, and then use that information to craft their web traffic to evade defenses. `[Ref: Gummy Browsers Targeted Browser Spoofing against State-of-the-Art Fingerprinting Techniques]`

techniques.namePt: Scripts de Inicialização de Boot ou Logon
techniques.fullNamePt: Scripts de Inicialização de Boot ou Logon
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar scripts automatically executed at boot or logon initialization to establish persistence. `[Ref: Mandiant APT29 Eye Spy Email Nov 22]` `[Ref: Anomali Rocke March 2019]` Initialization scripts pode ser utilizado para perform administrative functions, which may often execute other programs or send information to an internal logging server. These scripts can vary based on sistema operativo and whether applied locally or remotely.  

Os adversários podem utilizar these scripts to maintain persistence on a single system. Dependendo de the access configuration of the logon scripts, either local credentials or an administrator account may be necessary. 

Um adversário pode also be able to escalate their privileges since some boot or logon initialization scripts run with higher privileges.

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: Login Hook
techniques.fullNamePt: Scripts de Inicialização de Boot ou Logon: Login Hook
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar a Login Hook to establish persistence executed upon user logon. A login hook is a plist file that points to a specific script to execute with root privileges upon user logon. The plist file is located in the `/Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow.plist` file and can be modified using the `defaults` command-line utility. This behavior is the same for logout hooks where a script can be executed upon user logout. All hooks require administrator permissions to modify or create hooks. `[Ref: Login Scripts Apple Dev]` `[Ref: LoginWindowScripts Apple Dev]` 

Adversaries can add or insert a path to a malicious script in the `com.apple.loginwindow.plist` file, using the `LoginHook` or `LogoutHook` key-value pair. The malicious script is executed upon the next user login. If a login hook already exists, adversaries can add additional commands to an existing login hook. There can be only one login and logout hook on a system at a time. `[Ref: S1 macOs Persistence]` `[Ref: Wardle Persistence Chapter]`

**Note:** Login hooks were deprecated in 10.11 version of macOS in favor of **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`) and **Launch Agent** (`T1543.001`)

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict write access to logon scripts to specific administrators.

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: Network Logon Script
techniques.fullNamePt: Scripts de Inicialização de Boot ou Logon: Network Logon Script
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar network logon scripts automatically executed at logon initialization to establish persistence. Network logon scripts can be assigned using Active Directory (AD) or Group Policy Objects. `[Ref: Petri Logon Script AD]` These logon scripts run with the privileges of the user they are assigned to. Dependendo de the systems within the network, initializing one of these scripts could apply to more than one or potentially all systems.  
 
Os adversários podem utilizar these scripts to maintain persistence on a network. Dependendo de the access configuration of the logon scripts, either local credentials or an administrator account may be necessary.

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: RC Scripts
techniques.fullNamePt: Scripts de Inicialização de Boot ou Logon: RC Scripts
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence by modifying RC scripts, which are executed during a Unix-like system’s startup. These files allow system administrators to map and start custom services at startup for different run levels. RC scripts require root privileges to modify.

Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence by adding a malicious binary path or shell commands to `rc.local`, `rc.common`, and other RC scripts specific to the Unix-like distribution. `[Ref: IranThreats Kittens Dec 2017]` `[Ref: Intezer HiddenWasp Map 2019]` Upon reboot, the system executes the script's contents as root, resulting in persistence.

Adversary abuse of RC scripts is especially effective for lightweight Unix-like distributions using the root user as default, such as ESXi hypervisors, IoT, or embedded systems. `[Ref: intezer-kaiji-malware]` As ESXi servers store most system files in memory and therefore discard changes on shutdown, leveraging `/etc/rc.local.d/local.sh` is one of the few mechanisms for enabling persistence across reboots. `[Ref: Juniper Networks ESXi Backdoor 2022]`

Several Unix-like systems have moved to Systemd and deprecated the use of RC scripts. This is now a deprecated mechanism in macOS in favor of Launchd. `[Ref: Apple Developer Doco Archive Launchd]` `[Ref: Startup Items]` This technique can be used on Mac OS X Panther v10.3 and earlier versions which still execute the RC scripts. `[Ref: Methods of Mac Malware Persistence]` To maintain backwards compatibility some systems, such as Ubuntu, will execute the RC scripts if they exist with the correct file permissions. `[Ref: Ubuntu Manpage systemd rc]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limitar os privilégios das contas de utilizador so only authorized users can edit the `rc.common` file.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: Startup Items
techniques.fullNamePt: Scripts de Inicialização de Boot ou Logon: Startup Items
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar startup items automatically executed at boot initialization to establish persistence. Startup items execute during the final phase of the boot process and contain shell scripts or other executable files along with configuration information used by the system to determine the execution order for all startup items. `[Ref: Startup Items]`

This is technically a deprecated technology (superseded by **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`)), and thus the appropriate folder, `/Library/StartupItems` isn’t guaranteed to exist on the system by default, but does appear to exist by default on macOS Sierra. A startup item is a directory whose executable and configuration property list (plist), `StartupParameters.plist`, reside in the top-level directory. 

Um adversário consegue create the appropriate folders/files in the StartupItems directory to register their own mecanismo de persistência. `[Ref: Methods of Mac Malware Persistence]` Additionally, since StartupItems run during the bootup phase of macOS, they will run as the elevated root user.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Since StartupItems are deprecated, preventing all users from writing to the `/Library/StartupItems` directory would prevent any startup items from getting registered.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.namePt: Escuta de Tráfego de Rede (Network Sniffing)
techniques.fullNamePt: Escuta de Tráfego de Rede (Network Sniffing)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem passively sniff tráfego de rede to capture information about an environment, including authentication material passed over the network. Network sniffing refers to using the network interface on a system to monitor or capture information sent over a wired or wireless connection. Um adversário pode place a network interface into promiscuous mode to passively access data in transit over the network, or use span ports to capture a larger amount of data.

Data captured via this technique may include user credentials, especially those sent over an insecure, unencrypted protocol. Techniques for name service resolution poisoning, such as **Name Resolution Poisoning and SMB Relay** (`T1557.001`), pode também ser utilizado para capture credentials to websites, proxies, and internal systems by redirecting traffic to an adversary.

Network sniffing may reveal configuration details, such as running services, version numbers, and other network characteristics (e.g. IP addresses, hostnames, VLAN IDs) necessary for subsequent **Lateral Movement** (`TA0008`) and/or **Stealth** (`TA0005`) activities. Os adversários podem likely also utilize network sniffing during **Adversary-in-the-Middle** (`T1557`) (AiTM) to passively gain additional knowledge about the environment.

In cloud-based environments, adversaries may still be able to use traffic mirroring services to sniff tráfego de rede from máquina virtual (VM)s. Por exemplo, AWS Traffic Mirroring, GCP Packet Mirroring, and Azure vTap allow users to define specified instances to collect traffic from and specified targets to send collected traffic to. `[Ref: AWS Traffic Mirroring]` `[Ref: GCP Packet Mirroring]` `[Ref: Azure Virtual Network TAP]` Often, much of this traffic will be in cleartext due to the use of TLS termination at the load balancer level to reduce the strain of encrypting and decrypting traffic. `[Ref: Rhino Security Labs AWS VPC Traffic Mirroring]` `[Ref: SpecterOps AWS Traffic Mirroring]` The adversary can then use exfiltration techniques such as Transfer Data to Cloud Account com o objetivo de access the sniffed traffic. `[Ref: Rhino Security Labs AWS VPC Traffic Mirroring]`

On network devices, adversaries may perform network captures using **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) commands such as `monitor capture`. `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` `[Ref: capture_embedded_packet_on_software]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Em ambientes Cloud, ensure that users are not granted permissions to create or modify traffic mirrors unless this is explicitly required.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication wherever possible.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que all wired and/or wireless traffic is encrypted appropriately. Use best practices for authentication protocols, such as Kerberos, and ensure web traffic that may contain credentials is protected by SSL/TLS.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Deny direct access of broadcasts and multicast sniffing, and prevent attacks such as **Name Resolution Poisoning and SMB Relay** (`T1557.001`)
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Network Sniffing Across Platforms

analytics.name: Analytic 0875
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects suspicious execution of network monitoring tools (e.g., Wireshark, tshark, Microsoft Message Analyzer), driver loading indicative of promiscuous mode, or non-admin user privilege escalation to access NICs for capture.

mutableElements.description: Adjust list of known sniffing tools based on environment and known administrator usage.
Tune time of day or frequency of capture sessions to reduce false positives from authorized use.

analytics.name: Analytic 0876
analytics.descriptionPt: Correlates interface mode changes to promiscuous with execution of sniffing tools like tcpdump, tshark, or custom pcap libraries. Detects abnormal NIC configurations and unauthorized sniffing from non-root sessions.

logSources.name: networkconfig
logSources.channel: interface flag PROMISC, netstat | ip link | ethtool

mutableElements.description: Limit analysis to external interfaces (e.g., eth0, wlan0) and exclude virtual adapters.
Raise alerts if interface remains in PROMISC longer than threshold duration.

analytics.name: Analytic 0877
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects enabling of interface sniffing via packet capture tools or AppleScript triggering `tcpdump`. Leverages Unified Logs and process lineage to identify suspicious use of `pfctl`, `tcpdump`, or `libpcap` libraries.

logSources.name: fs:fsusage
logSources.channel: access to BPF devices or interface IOCTLs

mutableElements.description: Whitelist Apple-native tools used by IT admins and mobile device management (MDM).
Prioritize detections from non-admin or low-privilege users performing packet captures.

analytics.name: Analytic 0878
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects creation of traffic mirroring sessions (e.g., AWS VPC Traffic Mirroring, Azure vTAP) that redirect traffic from critical assets to other virtual instances, often followed by file creation or session establishment.

mutableElements.description: Identify VMs or containers where mirror sessions are abnormal or unexpected.
Monitor whether mirror target roles match administrative expectations.

Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração pelo Canal de C2
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem roubar data by exfiltrating it over an existing Command and Control (C2) channel. Stolen data is encoded into the normal communications channel using the same protocol as Command and Control (C2) communications. `[Ref: C2 FRAMEWORKS]`

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific obfuscation technique used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various malware families and versions. Adversaries will likely change tool Command and Control (C2) signatures over time or construct protocols in such a way para evitar deteção by common defensive tools.  `[Ref: University of Birmingham C2]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Exfiltration Over C2 Channel

analytics.name: Analytic 0988
analytics.descriptionPt: Identifies suspicious outbound traffic volume mismatches from processes that typically do not generate network activity, particularly over C2 protocols like HTTPS, DNS, or custom TCP/UDP ports, following file or data access.

mutableElements.description: Set threshold for outbound transfer size exceeding typical C2 traffic (e.g., >1MB in <5min).
List of approved processes that may exhibit high outbound traffic (e.g., updates).

analytics.name: Analytic 0989
analytics.descriptionPt: Monitors for processes reading sensitive files then immediately initiating unusual outbound connections or bulk transfer sessions over persistent sockets, particularly with encrypted or binary payloads.

mutableElements.description: Threshold for high-entropy payloads indicative of encoded or encrypted exfil data.
Defines length of time over which transfer size must be aggregated to trigger detection.

analytics.name: Analytic 0990
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects unauthorized applications or scripts accessing dados sensíveis followed by establishing encrypted outbound communication to rare external destinations or with abnormal byte ratios.

mutableElements.description: Enables defenders to tune legitimate vs. suspicious lineage (e.g., launchd → curl is uncommon).
Focus detection on unusual protocols (e.g., IRC, FTP, DNS over HTTPS).

analytics.name: Analytic 0991
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects VMs sending outbound traffic through non-standard services or to unknown destinations. Exfiltration over reverse shells tunneled via VMkernel or custom payloads routed via hostd/vpxa.

mutableElements.description: Limit detection to sensitive or externally-exposed VMs handling confidential data.

blockers: M1031 (Network Intrusion Prevention): Reverse shell ou beacon C2 não conecta para o exterior; conexões TCP diretas bloqueadas ou terminadas pelo Proxy/Firewall.
Firewall Egress restritiva, Proxy com inspeção SSL/TLS e bloqueio de domínios sem reputação ou DLP ativo.
bypasses: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

Empregar canais sobre Web Services legítimos permitidos (Microsoft Graph, GitHub, OneDrive), respeitar o Proxy do sistema via `WinINet` com credenciais integradas da sessão atual, aplicar jitter/sleep randomization e fragmentar transferências abaixo dos limiares de DLP.

**KnownBenignProcesses**: List of approved processes that may exhibit high outbound traffic (e.g., updates).

**ParentProcessAncestry**: Enables defenders to tune legitimate vs. suspicious lineage (e.g., launchd → curl is uncommon).

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Serviços de Rede
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of services running on remote hosts and local network infrastructure devices, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation. Common methods to acquire this information include port, vulnerability, and/or wordlist scans using tools that are brought onto a system. `[Ref: CISA AR21-126A FIVEHANDS May 2021]`   

Within cloud environments, adversaries may attempt to discover services running on other cloud hosts. Additionally, if the cloud environment is connected to a on-premises environment, adversaries may be able to identify services running on non-cloud systems as well.

Within macOS environments, adversaries may use the native Bonjour application to discover services running on other macOS hosts within a network. The Bonjour mDNSResponder daemon automatically registers and advertises a host’s registered services on the network. Por exemplo, adversaries can use a mDNS query (such as `dns-sd -B _ssh._tcp .`) to find other systems broadcasting the ssh service. `[Ref: apple doco bonjour description]` `[Ref: macOS APT Activity Bradley]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que unnecessary ports and services are closed to prevent risk of discovery and potential exploitation.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use network intrusion detection/prevention systems to detect and prevent remote service scans.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper network segmentation is followed to protect critical servers and devices.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

analytics.name: Analytic 1057
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects processes performing network enumeration (e.g., port scans, service probing) by correlating process creation, socket connections, and sequential destination IP probing within a time window.

mutableElements.description: Defines the number of unique destination IPs or ports accessed within a time window that may indicate a scan.
List of binaries allowed to scan or used by IT (e.g., Nmap, Nessus).
Temporal bounds for correlating sequential connections (e.g., 60 seconds).

analytics.descriptionPt: Detects use of network scanning utilities or scripts performing rapid connections to multiple services or hosts using auditd and netflow/pcap telemetry.

Trusted IPs or systems performing routine discovery.

Expected tools that could trigger mDNS or TCP/UDP scans (e.g., dns-sd, nmap).

blockers: M1042 (Disable or Remove Feature or Program): `powershell.exe` bloqueado por GPO, ou Macros VBA desativadas por política de Mark-of-the-Web (MotW).
M1031 (Network Intrusion Prevention): Reverse shell ou beacon C2 não conecta para o exterior; conexões TCP diretas bloqueadas ou terminadas pelo Proxy/Firewall.
M1030 (Network Segmentation): Sem conectividade direta da sub-rede atual para servidores de produção ou Domain Controllers.
bypasses: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).
blindSpots: **ScanRateThreshold**: Defines the number of unique destination IPs or ports accessed within a time window that may indicate a scan.
**KnownScannerExeList**: List of binaries allowed to scan or used by IT (e.g., Nmap, Nessus).
**TimeWindow**: Temporal bounds for correlating sequential connections (e.g., 60 seconds).
**PortScanThreshold**: Defines number of ports targeted per host within a short period.
**ToolPatternRegex**: Regex to match common scanner arguments (e.g., `nmap -sS`, `nc -zv`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução via Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos commands and payloads. WMI is designed for programmers and is the infrastructure for management data and operations on Windows systems. `[Ref: WMI 1-3]` WMI is an administration feature that provides a uniform environment to access Windows system components.

The WMI service enables both local and remote access, though the latter is facilitated by **Remote Services** (`T1021`) such as **Distributed Component Object Model** (`T1021.003`) and **Windows Remote Management** (`T1021.006`). `[Ref: WMI 1-3]` Remote WMI over DCOM operates using port 135, whereas WMI over WinRM operates over port 5985 when using HTTP and 5986 for HTTPS. `[Ref: WMI 1-3]`  `[Ref: Mandiant WMI]`

Um adversário consegue use WMI to interact with local and sistemas remotos and use it as a means to execute various behaviors, such as gathering information for **Discovery** (`TA0007`) as well as **Execution** (`TA0002`) of commands and payloads. `[Ref: Mandiant WMI]` Por exemplo, `wmic.exe` can be abused by an adversary to delete shadow copies with the command `wmic.exe Shadowcopy Delete` (i.e., **Inhibit System Recovery** (`T1490`)). `[Ref: WMI 6]`

**Note:** `wmic.exe` is deprecated as of January of 2024, with the WMIC feature being “disabled by default” on Windows 11+. WMIC will be removed from subsequent Windows releases and replaced by **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) as the primary WMI interface. `[Ref: WMI 7,8]` Adicionalmente a PowerShell and tools like `wbemtool.exe`, COM APIs pode também ser utilizado para programmatically interact with WMI via C++, .NET, VBScript, etc. `[Ref: WMI 7,8]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent credential overlap across systems of administrator and privileged accounts.  `[Ref: FireEye WMI 2015]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to block processes created by WMI commands from running. Note: many legitimate tools and applications utilize WMI for command execution.  `[Ref: win10_asr]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Por omissão, only administrators are allowed to connect remotely using WMI. Restrict other users who are allowed to connect, or disallow all users to connect remotely to WMI.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) configured to block execution of `wmic.exe` if it is not required for a given system or network to prevent potential misuse by adversaries. Por exemplo, in Windows 10 and Windows Server 2016 and above, Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy rules may be applied to block the `wmic.exe` application and to prevent abuse. `[Ref: Microsoft WDAC]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração por Protocolo Alternativo
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem roubar data by exfiltrating it over a different protocol than that of the existing Command and Control (C2) channel. The data may also be sent to an alternate network location from the main Command and Control (C2) server.  

Alternate protocols include FTP, SMTP, HTTP/S, DNS, SMB, or any other network protocol not being used as the main Command and Control (C2) channel. Os adversários podem também opt to encrypt and/or obfuscate these alternate channels. 

**Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol** (`T1048`) can be done using various common sistema operativo utilities such as **Net** (`S0039`)/SMB or FTP. `[Ref: Palo Alto OilRig Oct 2016]` On macOS and Linux `curl` pode ser empregue para invoke protocols such as HTTP/S or FTP/S para exfiltrar dados from a system. `[Ref: 20 macOS Common Tools and Techniques]`

Many IaaS and SaaS platforms (such as Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft SharePoint, GitHub, and AWS S3) support the direct download of files, emails, source code, and other informação sensível via the web console or **Cloud API** (`T1059.009`).

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Follow best practices for network firewall configurations to allow only necessary ports and traffic to enter and exit the network. `[Ref: TechNet Firewall Design]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Data Loss Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Data loss prevention can detect and block dados sensíveis being uploaded via web browsers.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de proxies and use dedicated servers for services such as DNS and only allow those systems to communicate over respective ports/protocols, instead of all systems within a network. Cloud service providers support IP-based restrictions when accessing cloud resources. Consider using IP allowlisting along with user account management to ensure that data access is restricted not only to valid users but only from expected IP ranges to mitigate the use of stolen credentials to access data.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary Command and Control (C2) infrastructure and malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use access control lists on cloud storage systems and objects.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar user permissions groups and roles for access to cloud storage. `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Storage Security, 2019]` Implementar strict Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls to prevent access to storage solutions except for the applications, users, and services that require access. `[Ref: Amazon S3 Security, 2019]` Garantir que temporary access tokens are issued rather than permanent credentials, especially when access is being granted to entities outside of the internal security boundary. `[Ref: Amazon  AWS Temporary Security Credentials]`

detections.name: Behavioral Detection Strategy for Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

analytics.name: Analytic 0367
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects unusual outbound file transfer behavior using protocols like FTP, SMB, SMTP, or DNS, involving non-standard processes, off-hour activity, or uncommonly high volume.

mutableElements.description: Set threshold for outbound volume (e.g., >50MB in a single connection).
Allow-listed protocols in use for specific machines or users (e.g., FTP allowed for backups).
Define allowed time-of-day windows (e.g., flag after-hours file transfer).
Identify anomalous parent-child process relationships (e.g., `winword.exe` spawning `ftp.exe`).

analytics.name: Analytic 0368
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects file exfiltration using tools like curl, scp, or custom binaries over protocols such as FTP, HTTP/S, or DNS tunneling, especially outside baseline user behavior.

mutableElements.description: Flag unexpected protocols (e.g., HTTP on port 53 or FTP traffic from non-standard tools).
Scope for privilege escalation or service account behavior.
Track movement of file types of interest (e.g., `.csv`, `.sql`, `.key`).

analytics.name: Analytic 0369
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects non-native file transfer via curl, Python scripts, or AppleScript using uncommon protocols like FTP, SMTP, or DNS exfiltration through mDNSResponder abuse.

mutableElements.description: Weight rarely-used protocols in user space.
Track which binaries usually call curl/nc and alert on deviation.

analytics.name: Analytic 0370
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects access to cloud APIs or CLI tools to move or sync files from sensitive buckets to external endpoints using protocols like HTTPS or S3 APIs.

mutableElements.description: Detect unauthorized use of roles for cloud storage manipulation.
Alert on outbound flows to geo-locations not seen in training baseline.

techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração por Protocolo Alternativo: Exfiltration Over Symmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem roubar data by exfiltrating it over a symmetrically encrypted network protocol other than that of the existing Command and Control (C2) channel. The data may also be sent to an alternate network location from the main Command and Control (C2) server. 

Symmetric encryption algorithms are those that use shared or the same keys/secrets on each end of the channel. This requires an exchange or pre-arranged agreement/possession of the value used to encrypt and decrypt data. `[Ref: Exfiltration Over Symmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol]`

Network protocols that use asymmetric encryption often utilize symmetric encryption once keys are exchanged, but adversaries may opt to manually share keys and implement symmetric cryptographic algorithms (ex: RC4, AES) vice using mechanisms that are baked into a protocol. This may result in multiple layers of encryption (in protocols that are natively encrypted such as HTTPS) or encryption in protocols that not typically encrypted (such as HTTP or FTP).

techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração por Protocolo Alternativo: Exfiltration Over Asymmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem roubar data by exfiltrating it over an asymmetrically encrypted network protocol other than that of the existing Command and Control (C2) channel. The data may also be sent to an alternate network location from the main Command and Control (C2) server. 

Asymmetric encryption algorithms are those that use different keys on each end of the channel. Also known as public-key cryptography, this requires pairs of cryptographic keys that can encrypt/decrypt data from the corresponding key. Each end of the communication channels requires a private key (only in the procession of that entity) and the public key of the other entity. The public keys of each entity are exchanged before encrypted communications begin. 

Network protocols that use asymmetric encryption (such as HTTPS/TLS/SSL) often utilize symmetric encryption once keys are exchanged. `[Ref: Cybersecurity Advisory GRU Brute Force Campaign July 2021]` Os adversários podem opt to use these encrypted mechanisms that are baked into a protocol.
