blockers: M1031 (Network Intrusion Prevention): Reverse shell ou beacon C2 não conecta para o exterior; conexões TCP diretas bloqueadas ou terminadas pelo Proxy/Firewall.
M1037 (Filter Network Traffic): Movimentação lateral via `PsExec`, `evil-winrm` ou `wmiexec` falha por timeout de porta.
M1030 (Network Segmentation): Sem conectividade direta da sub-rede atual para servidores de produção ou Domain Controllers.
Firewall Egress restritiva, Proxy com inspeção SSL/TLS e bloqueio de domínios sem reputação ou DLP ativo.
bypasses: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

Empregar canais sobre Web Services legítimos permitidos (Microsoft Graph, GitHub, OneDrive), respeitar o Proxy do sistema via `WinINet` com credenciais integradas da sessão atual, aplicar jitter/sleep randomization e fragmentar transferências abaixo dos limiares de DLP.
blindSpots: **UnencryptedProtocolList**: Set of protocols considered suspicious for outbound data exfiltration (e.g., FTP, HTTP).
**DataTransferSizeThreshold**: Defines what amount of outbound data is considered abnormal for a host/user.
**ParentProcessDenylist**: Processes that should not launch FTP/HTTP clients (e.g., winword.exe launching ftp.exe).
**SensitiveDirectoryWatchlist**: Flag access to paths known to store sensitive or regulated data.
**ProcessBaseline**: Define which binaries are allowed to communicate externally using HTTP/FTP.

techniques.namePt: Descoberta de Ligações de Rede Ativas
techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Ligações de Rede Ativas
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of network connections to or from the compromised system they are currently accessing or from sistemas remotos by querying for information over the network. 

An adversary who gains access to a system that is part of a cloud-based environment may map out Virtual Private Clouds or Virtual Networks com o objetivo de determine what systems and services are connected. The actions performed are likely the same types of discovery techniques depending on the sistema operativo, but the resulting information may include details about the networked cloud environment relevant to the adversary's goals. Cloud providers may have different ways in which their virtual networks operate. `[Ref: Amazon AWS VPC Guide]` `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Virtual Network Overview]` `[Ref: Google VPC Overview]` Similarly, adversaries who gain access to network devices may also perform similar discovery activities to gather information about connected systems and services.

Utilities and commands that acquire this information include **netstat** (`S0104`), "net use," and "net session" with **Net** (`S0039`). In Mac and Linux, **netstat** (`S0104`) and `lsof` pode ser utilizado para list current connections. `who -a` and `w` pode ser utilizado para show which users are currently logged in, similar to "net session". Additionally, built-in features native to network devices and **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) may be used (e.g. `show ip sockets`, `show tcp brief`). `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` On ESXi servers, the command `esxi network ip connection list` pode ser utilizado para list active network connections. `[Ref: Sygnia ESXi Ransomware 2025]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração por Meio Físico
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar exfiltrate data via a physical medium, such as a removable drive. In certain circumstances, such as an air-gapped network compromise, exfiltration could occur via a physical medium or device introduced by a user. Such media could be an external hard drive, USB drive, cellular phone, MP3 player, or other removable storage and processing device. The physical medium or device could be used as the final exfiltration point or to hop between otherwise disconnected systems. `[Ref: USB Drives Threaten Enterprise Security]` `[Ref: Tropic Trooper’s USBferry]` `[Ref: APT37 Adds New Capabilities for Air-Gapped Networks]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Tarefa ou Job Agendado (Scheduled Task/Job)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de task scheduling functionality to facilitate initial or recurring execution of código malicioso. Utilities exist within all major sistema operativos to schedule programs or scripts to be executed at a specified date and time. A task can also be scheduled on a remote system, provided the proper authentication is met (ex: RPC and file and printer sharing in Windows environments). Scheduling a task on a remote system typically may require being a member of an admin or otherwise privileged group on the remote system. `[Ref: TechNet Task Scheduler Security]`

Os adversários podem utilizar task scheduling to execute programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis for persistence. These mechanisms can also be abused to run a process under the context of a specified account (such as one with elevated permissions/privileges). De forma semelhante a **System Binary Proxy Execution** (`T1218`), adversaries have also abused task scheduling to potentially mask one-time execution under a trusted system process. `[Ref: ProofPoint Serpent]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limitar os privilégios das contas de utilizador and remediate Privilege Escalation vectors so only authorized administrators can create tarefas agendadas (Scheduled Tasks) on sistemas remotos.

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar settings for tarefas agendadas (Scheduled Tasks) to force tasks to run under the context of the authenticated account instead of allowing them to run as SYSTEM. The associated Registry key is located at `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\SubmitControl`. The setting can be configured through GPO: Computer Configuration > [Policies] > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options: Domain Controller (DC): Allow server operators to schedule tasks, set to disabled.  `[Ref: TechNet Server Operator Scheduled Task]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict access by setting directory and file permissions that are not specific to users or privileged accounts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar the Increase Scheduling Priority option to only allow the Administrators group the rights to schedule a priority process. This can be can be configured through GPO: Computer Configuration > [Policies] > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment: Increase scheduling priority.  `[Ref: TechNet Scheduling Priority]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Toolkits like the PowerSploit framework contain PowerUp modules that pode ser utilizado para explore systems for permission weaknesses in tarefas agendadas (Scheduled Tasks) that could be used para escalar privilégios.  `[Ref: Powersploit]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNamePt: Tarefa ou Job Agendado (Scheduled Task/Job): At
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de the **at** (`S0110`) utility to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of código malicioso. The **at** (`S0110`) utility exists as an executable within Windows, Linux, and macOS for scheduling tasks at a specified time and date. Although deprecated in favor of **Scheduled Task** (`T1053.005`)'s **schtasks** (`S0111`) in Windows environments, using **at** (`S0110`) requires that the Task Scheduler service be running, and the user to be logged on as a member of the Administrador Locals group. Adicionalmente a explicitly running the `at` command, adversaries may also schedule a task with **at** (`S0110`) by directly leveraging the **Windows Management Instrumentation** (`T1047`) `Win32_ScheduledJob` WMI class. `[Ref: Malicious Life by Cybereason]`

On Linux and macOS, **at** (`S0110`) may be invoked by the superuser as well as any users added to the `at.allow` file. If the `at.allow` file does not exist, the `at.deny` file is checked. Every username not listed in `at.deny` is allowed to invoke **at** (`S0110`). If the `at.deny` exists and is empty, global use of **at** (`S0110`) is permitted. If neither file exists (which is often the baseline) only the superuser is allowed to use **at** (`S0110`). `[Ref: Linux at]`

Os adversários podem utilizar **at** (`S0110`) to execute programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis for **Persistence** (`TA0003`). **at** (`S0110`) can also be abused to conduct remote **Execution** (`TA0002`) as part of **Lateral Movement** (`TA0008`) and/or to run a process under the context of a specified account (such as SYSTEM).

In Linux environments, adversaries may also abuse **at** (`S0110`) to break out of restricted environments by using a task to spawn an interactive system shell or to run system commands. Similarly, **at** (`S0110`) may also be used for **Privilege Escalation** (`TA0004`) if the binary is allowed to run as superuser via `sudo`. `[Ref: GTFObins at]`

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration

techniques.fullNamePt: Tarefa ou Job Agendado (Scheduled Task/Job): Cron
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de the `cron` utility to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of código malicioso. `[Ref: 20 macOS Common Tools and Techniques]` The `cron` utility is a time-based job scheduler for Unix-like sistema operativos.  The ` crontab` file contains the schedule of cron entries to be run and the specified times for execution. Any `crontab` files are stored in sistema operativo-specific file paths.

Um adversário pode use `cron` in Linux or Unix environments to execute programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis for **Persistence** (`TA0003`). In ESXi environments, cron jobs must be created directly via the crontab file (e.g., `/var/spool/cron/crontabs/root`). `[Ref: CloudSEK ESXiArgs 2023]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Review changes to the `cron` schedule. `cron` execution can be reviewed within the `/var/log` directory. To validate the location of the `cron` log file, check the syslog config at `/etc/rsyslog.conf` or `/etc/syslog.conf`.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: `cron` permissions are controlled by `/etc/cron.allow and /etc/cron.deny`. If there is a `cron.allow` file, then the user or users that need to use `cron` will need to be listed in the file. `cron.deny` é utilizado para explicitly disallow users from using cron. If neither files exist, then only the super user is allowed to run cron.

techniques.fullNamePt: Tarefa ou Job Agendado (Scheduled Task/Job): Scheduled Task
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of código malicioso. There are multiple ways to access the Task Scheduler in Windows. The **schtasks** (`S0111`) utility can be run directly on the command line, or the Task Scheduler can be opened through the GUI within the Administrator Tools section of the Control Panel. `[Ref: Stack Overflow]` In some cases, adversaries have used a .NET wrapper for the Windows Task Scheduler, and alternatively, adversaries have used the Windows netapi32 library and **Windows Management Instrumentation** (`T1047`) (WMI) to create a scheduled task. Os adversários podem também utilize the Powershell Cmdlet `Invoke-CimMethod`, which leverages WMI class `PS_ScheduledTask` to create a scheduled task via an XML path. `[Ref: Red Canary - Atomic Red Team]`

Um adversário pode use Windows Task Scheduler to execute programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis for persistence. The Windows Task Scheduler can also be abused to conduct remote Execution as part of Lateral Movement and/or to run a process under the context of a specified account (such as SYSTEM). De forma semelhante a **System Binary Proxy Execution** (`T1218`), adversaries have also abused the Windows Task Scheduler to potentially mask one-time execution under signed/trusted system processes. `[Ref: ProofPoint Serpent]`

Os adversários podem também create "hidden" tarefas agendadas (Scheduled Tasks) (i.e. **Hide Artifacts** (`T1564`)) that may not be visible to defender tools and manual queries used to enumerate tasks. Especificamente, an adversary may hide a task from `schtasks /query` and the Task Scheduler by deleting the associated Security Descriptor (SD) registry value (where deletion of this value must be completed using SYSTEM permissions). `[Ref: SigmaHQ]` `[Ref: Tarrask scheduled task]` Os adversários podem também employ alternate methods to hide tasks, such as altering the metadata (e.g., `Index` value) within associated registry keys. `[Ref: Defending Against Scheduled Task Attacks in Windows Environments]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Tarefa ou Job Agendado (Scheduled Task/Job): Systemd Timers
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de systemd timers to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of código malicioso. Systemd timers are unit files with file extension `.timer` that control services. Timers can be set to run on a calendar event or after a time span relative to a starting point. They can be used as an alternative to **Cron** (`T1053.003`) in Linux environments. `[Ref: archlinux Systemd Timers Aug 2020]` Systemd timers may be activated remotely via the `systemctl` command line utility, which operates over **SSH** (`T1021.004`). `[Ref: Systemd Remote Control]`

Each `.timer` file must have a corresponding `.service` file with the same name, e.g., `example.timer` and `example.service`. `.service` files are **Systemd Service** (`T1543.002`) unit files that are managed by the systemd system and service manager. `[Ref: Linux man-pages: systemd January 2014]` Privileged timers are written to `/etc/systemd/system/` and `/usr/lib/systemd/system` while user level are written to `~/.config/systemd/user/`.

Um adversário pode use systemd timers para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos code at system startup or on a scheduled basis for persistence. `[Ref: Arch Linux Package Systemd Compromise BleepingComputer 10JUL2018]` `[Ref: gist Arch package compromise 10JUL2018]` `[Ref: acroread package compromised Arch Linux Mail 8JUL2018]` Timers installed using privileged paths pode ser empregue para maintain root level persistence. Os adversários podem também install user level timers to achieve user level persistence. `[Ref: Falcon Sandbox smp: 28553b3a9d]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict read/write access to systemd `.timer` unit files to only select privileged users who have a legitimate need to manage system services.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Tarefa ou Job Agendado (Scheduled Task/Job): Container Orchestration Job
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de task scheduling functionality provided by container orchestration tools such as Kubernetes to schedule deployment of containers configured para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos code. Container orchestration jobs run these automated tasks at a specific date and time, similar to cron jobs on a Linux system. Deployments of this type can also be configured to maintain a quantity of containers over time, automating the process of maintaining persistence within a cluster.

In Kubernetes, a CronJob pode ser empregue para schedule a Job that runs one or more containers to perform specific tasks. `[Ref: Kubernetes Jobs]` `[Ref: Kubernetes CronJob]` An adversary therefore may utilize a CronJob to schedule deployment of a Job that executes código malicioso in various nodes within a cluster. `[Ref: Threat Matrix for Kubernetes]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar code into processes com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. Process injection is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Execution via process injection may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process. 

There are many different ways to inject code into a process, many of which abuse legitimate functionalities. These implementations exist for every major OS but are typically platform specific. 

More sophisticated samples may perform multiple process injections to segment modules and further evade detection, utilizing named pipes or other inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms as a communication channel.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilize Yama (ex: /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope) to mitigate ptrace based process injection by restricting the use of ptrace to privileged users only. Other mitigation controls involve the deployment of security kernel modules that provide advanced access control and process restrictions such as SELinux, grsecurity, and AppArmor.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: Some endpoint security solutions can be configured to block some types of process injection based on common sequences of behavior that occur during the injection process. Por exemplo, on Windows 10, Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules may prevent Office applications from code injection.  `[Ref: win10_asr]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Dynamic-link Library Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) into processes com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. DLL injection is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process.  

DLL injection is commonly performed by writing the path to a DLL in the virtual address space of the target process before loading the DLL by invoking a new thread. The write can be performed with native Windows API calls such as `VirtualAllocEx` and `WriteProcessMemory`, then invoked with `CreateRemoteThread` (which calls the `LoadLibrary` API responsible for loading the DLL).  `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]` 

Variations of this method such as reflective DLL injection (writing a self-mapping DLL into a process) and memory module (map DLL when writing into process) overcome the address relocation issue as well as the additional APIs to invoke execution (since these methods load and execute the files in memory by manually preforming the function of `LoadLibrary`). `[Ref: Elastic HuntingNMemory June 2017]` `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]` 

Another variation of this method, often referred to as Module Stomping/Overloading or DLL Hollowing, may be leveraged to conceal injected code within a process. This method involves loading a legitimate DLL into a remote process then manually overwriting the module's `AddressOfEntryPoint` before starting a new thread in the target process. `[Ref: Module Stomping for Shellcode Injection]` This variation allows attackers to hide malicious injected code by potentially backing its execution with a legitimate DLL file on disk. `[Ref: Hiding Malicious Code with Module Stomping]` 

Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Execution via DLL injection may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Portable Executable Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar portable executables (PE) into processes com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. PE injection is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. 

PE injection is commonly performed by copying code (perhaps without a file on disk) into the virtual address space of the target process before invoking it via a new thread. The write can be performed with native Windows API calls such as `VirtualAllocEx` and `WriteProcessMemory`, then invoked with `CreateRemoteThread` or additional code (ex: shellcode). The displacement of the injected code does introduce the additional requirement for functionality to remap memory references.  `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]` 

Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Execution via PE injection may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Thread Execution Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar código malicioso into hijacked processes com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. Thread Execution Hijacking is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. 

Thread Execution Hijacking is commonly performed by suspending an existing process then unmapping/hollowing its memory, which can then be replaced with código malicioso or the path to a DLL. A handle to an existing victim process is first created with native Windows API calls such as `OpenThread`. At this point the process can be suspended then written to, realigned to the injected code, and resumed via `SuspendThread `, `VirtualAllocEx`, `WriteProcessMemory`, `SetThreadContext`, then `ResumeThread` respectively. `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]`

This is very similar to **Process Hollowing** (`T1055.012`) but targets an existing process rather than creating a process in a suspended state.  

Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Execution via Thread Execution Hijacking may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Asynchronous Procedure Call
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar código malicioso into processes via the asynchronous procedure call (APC) queue com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. APC injection is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. 

APC injection is commonly performed by attaching código malicioso to the APC Queue  `[Ref: Microsoft APC]` of a process's thread. Queued APC functions are executed when the thread enters an alterable state. `[Ref: Microsoft APC]` A handle to an existing victim process is first created with native Windows API calls such as `OpenThread`. At this point `QueueUserAPC` pode ser utilizado para invoke a function (such as `LoadLibrayA` pointing to a malicious DLL). 

A variation of APC injection, dubbed "Early Bird injection", involves creating a suspended process in which código malicioso can be written and executed before the process' entry point (and potentially subsequent anti-malware hooks) via an APC.  `[Ref: CyberBit Early Bird Apr 2018]` AtomBombing  `[Ref: ENSIL AtomBombing Oct 2016]` is another variation that utilizes APCs to invoke código malicioso previously written to the global atom table. `[Ref: Microsoft Atom Table]`

Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Execution via APC injection may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Thread Local Storage
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar código malicioso into processes via thread local storage (TLS) callbacks com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. TLS callback injection is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. 

TLS callback injection involves manipulating pointers inside a portable executable (PE) to redirect a process to código malicioso before reaching the code's legitimate entry point. TLS callbacks are normally used by the OS to setup and/or cleanup data used by threads. Manipulating TLS callbacks may be performed by allocating and writing to specific offsets within a process’ memory space using other **Process Injection** (`T1055`) techniques such as **Process Hollowing** (`T1055.012`). `[Ref: FireEye TLS Nov 2017]`

Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Execution via TLS callback injection may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Ptrace System Calls
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar código malicioso into processes via ptrace (process trace) system calls com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. Ptrace system call injection is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. 

Ptrace system call injection involves attaching to and modifying a running process. The ptrace system call enables a debugging process to observe and control another process (and each individual thread), including changing memory and register values. `[Ref: PTRACE man]` Ptrace system call injection is commonly performed by writing código arbitrário into a running process (ex: `malloc`) then invoking that memory with `PTRACE_SETREGS` to set the register containing the next instruction to execute. Ptrace system call injection can also be done with `PTRACE_POKETEXT`/`PTRACE_POKEDATA`, which copy data to a specific address in the target processes’ memory (ex: the current address of the next instruction).  `[Ref: PTRACE man]` `[Ref: Medium Ptrace JUL 2018]` 

Ptrace system call injection may not be possible targeting processes that are non-child processes and/or have higher-privileges. `[Ref: BH Linux Inject]` 

Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Execution via ptrace system call injection may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Proc Memory
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar código malicioso into processes via the /proc filesystem com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. Proc memory injection is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. 

Proc memory injection involves enumerating the memory of a process via the /proc filesystem (`/proc/[pid]`) then crafting a return-oriented programming (ROP) payload with available gadgets/instructions. Each running process has its own directory, which includes memory mappings. Proc memory injection is commonly performed by overwriting the target processes’ stack using memory mappings provided by the /proc filesystem. This information pode ser utilizado para enumerate offsets (including the stack) and gadgets (or instructions within the program that pode ser utilizado para build a malicious payload) otherwise hidden by memória do processo protections such as address space layout randomization (ASLR). Uma vez que enumerated, the target processes’ memory map within `/proc/[pid]/maps` can be overwritten using dd. `[Ref: Uninformed Needle]` `[Ref: GDS Linux Injection]` `[Ref: DD Man]` 

Other techniques such as **Dynamic Linker Hijacking** (`T1574.006`) pode ser empregue para populate a target process with more available gadgets. De forma semelhante a **Process Hollowing** (`T1055.012`), proc memory injection may target child processes (such as a backgrounded copy of sleep). `[Ref: GDS Linux Injection]` 

Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Execution via proc memory injection may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.fullNameEn: Process Injection: Extra Window Memory Injection
techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Extra Window Memory Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar código malicioso into process via Extra Window Memory (EWM) com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. EWM injection is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. 

Before creating a window, graphical Windows-based processes must prescribe to or register a windows class, which stipulate appearance and behavior (via windows procedures, which are functions that handle input/output of data). `[Ref: Microsoft Window Classes]` Registration of new windows classes can include a request for up to 40 bytes of EWM to be appended to the allocated memory of each instance of that class. This EWM is intended to store data specific to that window and has specific application programming interface (API) functions to set and get its value.  `[Ref: Microsoft GetWindowLong function]`  `[Ref: Microsoft SetWindowLong function]`

Although small, the EWM is large enough to store a 32-bit pointer and is often used to point to a windows procedure. Malware may possibly utilize this memory location in part of an attack chain that includes writing code to shared sections of the process’s memory, placing a pointer to the code in EWM, then invoking execution by returning execution control to the address in the process’s EWM.

Execution granted through EWM injection may allow access to both the target process's memory and possibly privilégios elevados. techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Process Hollowing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar código malicioso into suspended and hollowed processes com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses. Process hollowing is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process.  

Process hollowing is commonly performed by creating a process in a suspended state then unmapping/hollowing its memory, which can then be replaced with código malicioso. A victim process can be created with native Windows API calls such as `CreateProcess`, which includes a flag to suspend the processes primary thread. At this point the process can be unmapped using APIs calls such as `ZwUnmapViewOfSection` or `NtUnmapViewOfSection`  before being written to, realigned to the injected code, and resumed via `VirtualAllocEx`, `WriteProcessMemory`, `SetThreadContext`, then `ResumeThread` respectively. `[Ref: Leitch Hollowing]` `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]`

This is very similar to **Thread Local Storage** (`T1055.005`) but creates a new process rather than targeting an existing process. This behavior will likely not result in privilégios elevados since the injected process was spawned from (and thus inherits the security context) of the injecting process. Contudo, execution via process hollowing may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): Process Doppelgänging
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar código malicioso into process via process doppelgänging com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. Process doppelgänging is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. 

Windows Transactional NTFS (TxF) was introduced in Vista as a method to perform safe file operations.  `[Ref: Microsoft TxF]` To ensure data integrity, TxF enables only one transacted handle to write to a file at a given time. Until the write handle transaction is terminated, all other handles are isolated from the writer and may only read the committed version of the file that existed at the time the handle was opened.  `[Ref: Microsoft Basic TxF Concepts]` To avoid corruption, TxF performs an automatic rollback if the system or application fails during a write transaction.  `[Ref: Microsoft Where to use TxF]`

Although deprecated, the TxF application programming interface (API) is still enabled as of Windows 10.  `[Ref: BlackHat Process Doppelgänging Dec 2017]`

Os adversários podem abusar de TxF to a perform a file-less variation of **Process Injection** (`T1055`). De forma semelhante a **Process Hollowing** (`T1055.012`), process doppelgänging involves replacing the memory of a legitimate process, enabling the veiled execution of código malicioso that may evade defenses and detection. Process doppelgänging's use of TxF also avoids the use of highly-monitored API functions such as `NtUnmapViewOfSection`, `VirtualProtectEx`, and `SetThreadContext`.  `[Ref: BlackHat Process Doppelgänging Dec 2017]`

Process Doppelgänging is implemented in 4 steps  `[Ref: BlackHat Process Doppelgänging Dec 2017]`:

* Transact – Create a TxF transaction using a legitimate executable then overwrite the file with código malicioso. These changes will be isolated and only visible within the context of the transaction.
* Load – Create a shared section of memory and load the malicious executable.
* Rollback – Undo changes to original executable, effectively removing código malicioso from the sistema de ficheiros.
* Animate – Create a process from the tainted section of memory and initiate execution.

This behavior will likely not result in privilégios elevados since the injected process was spawned from (and thus inherits the security context) of the injecting process. Contudo, execution via process doppelgänging may evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem injetar código malicioso into processes via VDSO hijacking com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. Virtual dynamic shared object (vdso) hijacking is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. 

VDSO hijacking involves redirecting calls to dynamically linked shared libraries. Memory protections may prevent writing executable code to a process via **Ptrace System Calls** (`T1055.008`). Contudo, an adversary may hijack the syscall interface code stubs mapped into a process from the vdso shared object to execute syscalls to open and map a malicious shared object. This code can then be invoked by redirecting the execution flow of the process via patched memory address references stored in a process' global offset table (which store absolute addresses of mapped library functions). `[Ref: ELF Injection May 2009]` `[Ref: Backtrace VDSO]` `[Ref: VDSO Aug 2005]` `[Ref: Syscall 2014]`

Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Execution via VDSO hijacking may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

techniques.fullNamePt: Injeção em Processos (Process Injection): ListPlanting
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de list-view controls to inject código malicioso into hijacked processes com o objetivo de evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. ListPlanting is a method of executing código arbitrário in the address space of a separate live process. `[Ref: Hexacorn Listplanting]` Code executed via ListPlanting may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

List-view controls are user interface windows used to display collections of items. `[Ref: Microsoft List View Controls]` Information about an application's list-view settings are stored within the process' memory in a `SysListView32` control.

ListPlanting (a form of message-passing "shatter attack") may be performed by copying code into the virtual address space of a process that uses a list-view control then using that code as a custom callback for sorting the listed items. `[Ref: Modexp Windows Process Injection]` Adversaries must first copy code into the target process’ memory space, which can be performed various ways including by directly obtaining a handle to the `SysListView32` child of the victim process window (via Windows API calls such as `FindWindow` and/or `EnumWindows`) or other **Process Injection** (`T1055`) methods.

Some variations of ListPlanting may allocate memory in the target process but then use window messages to copy the payload, to avoid the use of the highly monitored `WriteProcessMemory` function. Por exemplo, an adversary can use the `PostMessage` and/or `SendMessage` API functions to send `LVM_SETITEMPOSITION` and `LVM_GETITEMPOSITION` messages, effectively copying a payload 2 bytes at a time to the allocated memory. `[Ref: ESET InvisiMole June 2020]` 

Finally, the payload is triggered by sending the `LVM_SORTITEMS` message to the `SysListView32` child of the process window, with the payload within the newly allocated buffer passed and executed as the `ListView_SortItems` callback.

techniques.fullNamePt: Captura de Input (Keylogging / API Hooking): Keylogging
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem log user keystrokes to intercept credentials as the user types them. Keylogging is likely to be used to acquire credentials for new access opportunities when **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`) efforts are not effective, and may require an adversary to intercept keystrokes on a system for a substantial period of time before credentials can be successfully captured. In order to increase the likelihood of capturing credentials quickly, an adversary may also perform actions such as clearing browser cookies to force users to reauthenticate to systems. `[Ref: Talos Kimsuky Nov 2021]`

Keylogging is the most prevalent type of input capture, with many different ways of intercepting keystrokes. `[Ref: Adventures of a Keystroke]` Some methods include:

* Hooking API callbacks used for processing keystrokes. Unlike **Credential API Hooking** (`T1056.004`), this focuses solely on API functions intended for processing keystroke data.
* Reading raw keystroke data from the hardware buffer.
* Windows Registry modifications.
* Custom drivers.
* **Modify System Image** (`T1601`) may provide adversaries with hooks into the sistema operativo of network devices to read raw keystrokes for login sessions. `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`

techniques.namePt: GUI Captura de Input (Keylogging / API Hooking)
techniques.fullNamePt: Captura de Input (Keylogging / API Hooking): GUI Captura de Input (Keylogging / API Hooking)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem mimic common sistema operativo GUI components to prompt users for credentials with a seemingly legitimate prompt. When programs are executed that need additional privileges than are present in the current user context, it is common for the sistema operativo to prompt the user for proper credentials to authorize the privilégios elevados for the task (ex: **Bypass User Account Control** (`T1548.002`)).

Os adversários podem mimic this functionality to prompt users for credentials with a seemingly legitimate prompt for a number of reasons that mimic normal usage, such as a fake installer requiring additional access or a fake malware removal suite. `[Ref: OSX Malware Exploits MacKeeper]` This type of prompt pode ser utilizado para collect credentials via various languages such as **AppleScript** (`T1059.002`) `[Ref: LogRhythm Do You Trust Oct 2014]` `[Ref: OSX Keydnap malware]` `[Ref: Spoofing credential dialogs]` and **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`). `[Ref: LogRhythm Do You Trust Oct 2014]` `[Ref: Enigma Phishing for Credentials Jan 2015]` `[Ref: Spoofing credential dialogs]` On Linux systems adversaries may launch dialog boxes prompting users for credentials from malicious shell scripts or the command line (i.e. **Unix Shell** (`T1059.004`)). `[Ref: Spoofing credential dialogs]`

Os adversários podem também mimic common software authentication requests, such as those from browsers or email clients. This may also be paired with user activity monitoring (i.e., **Browser Information Discovery** (`T1217`) and/or **Application Window Discovery** (`T1010`)) to spoof prompts when users are naturally accessing sensitive sites/data.

techniques.fullNamePt: Captura de Input (Keylogging / API Hooking): Web Portal Capture
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem install code on externally facing portals, such as a VPN login page, to capture and transmit credentials of users who attempt to log into the service. Por exemplo, a compromised login page may log provided user credentials before logging the user in to the service.

This variation on input capture may be conducted post-compromise using legitimate administrative access as a backup measure to maintain network access through **External Remote Services** (`T1133`) and **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) or as part of the initial compromise by exploitation of the externally facing web service. `[Ref: Volexity Virtual Private Keylogging]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not allow administrator accounts that have permissions to modify the Web content of organization login portals to be used for day-to-day operations that may expose them to potential adversaries on unprivileged systems.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Captura de Input (Keylogging / API Hooking): Credential API Hooking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem hook into Windows application programming interface (API) functions and Linux system functions to collect user credentials. Malicious hooking mechanisms may capture API or function calls that include parameters that reveal user authentication credentials. `[Ref: Microsoft TrojanSpy:Win32/Ursnif.gen!I Sept 2017]` Unlike **Keylogging** (`T1056.001`), this technique focuses specifically on API functions that include parameters that reveal user credentials. 

In Windows, hooking involves redirecting calls to these functions and can be implemented via:

* **Hooks procedures**, which intercept and execute designated code in response to events such as messages, keystrokes, and mouse inputs. `[Ref: Microsoft Hook Overview]` `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]`
* **Import address table (IAT) hooking**, which use modifications to a process’s IAT, where pointers to imported API functions are stored. `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]` `[Ref: Adlice Software IAT Hooks Oct 2014]` `[Ref: MWRInfoSecurity Dynamic Hooking 2015]`
* **Inline hooking**, which overwrites the first bytes in an API function to redirect code flow. `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]` `[Ref: HighTech Bridge Inline Hooking Sept 2011]` `[Ref: MWRInfoSecurity Dynamic Hooking 2015]`

In Linux and macOS, adversaries may hook into system functions via the `LD_PRELOAD` (Linux) or `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` (macOS) variáveis de ambiente, which enables loading shared libraries into a program’s address space. Por exemplo, an adversary may capture credentials by hooking into the `libc read` function leveraged by SSH or SCP. `[Ref: Intezer Symbiote 2022]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Processos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get information about running processes on a system. Information obtained could be used to gain an understanding of common software/applications running on systems within the network. Administrator or otherwise elevated access may provide better process details. Os adversários podem utilizar the information from **Process Discovery** (`T1057`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions.

In Windows environments, adversaries could obtain details on running processes using the **Tasklist** (`S0057`) utility via **cmd** (`S0106`) or `Get-Process` via **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`). Information about processes can also be extracted from the output of **Native API** (`T1106`) calls such as `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot`. In Mac and Linux, this is accomplished with the `ps` command. Os adversários podem também opt to enumerate processes via `/proc`. ESXi also supports use of the `ps` command, as well as `esxcli system process list`. `[Ref: Sygnia ESXi Ransomware 2025]` `[Ref: Crowdstrike Hypervisor Jackpotting Pt 2 2021]`

On network devices, **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) commands such as `show processes` pode ser utilizado para display current running processes. `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` `[Ref: show_processes_cisco_cmd]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries. These interfaces and languages provide ways of interacting with computer systems and are a common feature across many different platforms. Most systems come with some built-in interface de linha de comandos (CLI) and scripting capabilities, for example, macOS and Linux distributions include some flavor of **Unix Shell** (`T1059.004`) while Windows installations include the **Windows Command Shell** (`T1059.003`) and **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`).

There are also cross-platform interpreters such as **Python** (`T1059.006`), as well as those commonly associated with client applications such as **JavaScript** (`T1059.007`) and **Visual Basic** (`T1059.005`).

Os adversários podem abusar de these technologies in various ways as a means of executing comandos arbitrários. Commands and scripts can be embedded in **Initial Access** (`TA0001`) payloads delivered to victims as lure documents or as secondary payloads downloaded from an existing C2. Os adversários podem também execute commands through interactive terminals/shells, as well as utilize various **Remote Services** (`T1021`) com o objetivo de achieve remote Execution. `[Ref: Powershell Remote Commands]` `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - Command History]` `[Ref: Remote Shell Execution in Python]`

mitigations.name: Limit Software Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent user installation of unrequired command and scripting interpreters.

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Where possible, only permit execution of signed scripts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Recorrer a DLL Side-Loading (`T1574.002`) utilizando um executável legítimo assinado (vulnerável a sequestro de ordem de procura de DLL) que carregue a nossa DLL em memória, ou utilizar binários assinados nativos (LOLBAS - `T1218`). Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Desativar ou remover any unnecessary or unused shells or interpreters.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) where appropriate. Por exemplo, PowerShell Constrained Language mode pode ser utilizado para restrict access to sensitive or otherwise dangerous language elements such as those used to execute arbitrary Windows APIs or files (e.g., `Add-Type`). `[Ref: Microsoft PowerShell CLM]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically quarantine suspicious files.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt:
When PowerShell is necessary, consider restricting PowerShell execution policy to administrators. Be aware that there are methods of bypassing the PowerShell execution policy, depending on environment configuration. `[Ref: Netspi PowerShell Execution Policy Bypass]`

PowerShell JEA (Just Enough Administration) may also be used to sandbox administration and limit what commands admins/users can execute through remote PowerShell sessions. `[Ref: Microsoft PS JEA]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Inventory systems for unauthorized command and scripting interpreter installations.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: Script blocking extensions can help prevent the execution of scripts and HTA files that may commonly be used during the exploitation process. For código malicioso served up through ads, adblockers can help prevent that code from executing in the first place.

techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: PowerShell
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de PowerShell commands and scripts for execution. PowerShell is a powerful interactive interface de linha de comandos (CLI) and scripting environment included in the Windows sistema operativo. `[Ref: TechNet PowerShell]` PowerShell can also be installed on Linux and macOS. `[Ref: Powershell installation]` Adversaries can use PowerShell to perform a number of actions, including discovery of information and execution of code. Examples include the `Start-Process` cmdlet which pode ser utilizado para run an executable and the `Invoke-Command` cmdlet which runs a command locally or on a remote computer (though administrator permissions are required to use PowerShell to connect to sistemas remotos).

PowerShell may also be used to download and run executables from the Internet, which can be executed from disk or in memory without touching disk.

A number of PowerShell-based offensive testing tools are available, including **Empire** (`S0363`),  **PowerSploit** (`S0194`), **PoshC2** (`S0378`), and PSAttack. `[Ref: Github PSAttack]`

PowerShell commands/scripts can also be executed without directly invoking the `powershell.exe` binary through interfaces to PowerShell's underlying `System.Management.Automation` assembly DLL exposed through the .NET framework and Windows Common Language Interface (CLI). `[Ref: Sixdub PowerPick Jan 2016]` `[Ref: SilentBreak Offensive PS Dec 2015]` `[Ref: Microsoft PSfromCsharp APR 2014]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt:
It may be possible to remove PowerShell from systems when not needed, but a review should be performed to assess the impact to an environment, since it could be in use for many legitimate purposes and administrative functions.

Disable/restrict the WinRM Service to help prevent uses of PowerShell for remote execution.

techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: AppleScript
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de AppleScript for execution. AppleScript is a macOS scripting language designed to control applications and parts of the OS via inter-application messages called AppleEvents. `[Ref: Apple AppleScript]` These AppleEvent messages can be sent independently or easily scripted with AppleScript. These events can locate open windows, send keystrokes, and interact with almost any open application locally or remotely.

Scripts can be run from the command-line via `osascript /path/to/script` or `osascript -e "script here"`. Aside from the command line, scripts can be executed in numerous ways including Mail rules, Calendar.app alarms, and Automator workflows. AppleScripts can also be executed as plain text shell scripts by adding `#!/usr/bin/osascript` to the start of the script file. `[Ref: SentinelOne AppleScript]`

AppleScripts do not need to call `osascript` to execute. Contudo, they may be executed from within mach-O binaries by using the macOS **Native API** (`T1106`)s `NSAppleScript` or `OSAScript`, both of which execute code independent of the `/usr/bin/osascript` command line utility.

Os adversários podem abusar de AppleScript to execute various behaviors, such as interacting with an open SSH connection, moving to remote machines, and even presenting users with fake dialog boxes. These events cannot start applications remotely (they can start them locally), but they can interact with applications if they're already running remotely. On macOS 10.10 Yosemite and higher, AppleScript has the ability to execute **Native API** (`T1106`)s, which otherwise would require compilation and execution in a mach-O binary file format. `[Ref: SentinelOne macOS Red Team]` Since this is a scripting language, it pode ser utilizado para launch more common techniques as well such as a reverse shell via **Python** (`T1059.006`). `[Ref: Macro Malware Targets Macs]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: Require that all AppleScript be signed by a trusted developer ID before being executed - this will prevent random AppleScript code from executing. `[Ref: applescript signing]` This subjects AppleScript code to the same scrutiny as other .app files passing through Gatekeeper.

techniques.fullNameEn: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: Windows Command Shell
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de the Windows command shell for execution. The Windows command shell (**cmd** (`S0106`)) is the primary command prompt on Windows systems. The Windows command prompt pode ser utilizado para control almost any aspect of a system, with various permission levels required for different subsets of commands. The command prompt can be invoked remotely via **Remote Services** (`T1021`) such as **SSH** (`T1021.004`). `[Ref: SSH in Windows]`

Batch files (ex: .bat or .cmd) also provide the shell with a list of sequential commands to run, as well as normal scripting operations such as conditionals and loops. Common uses of batch files include long or repetitive tasks, or the need to run the same set of commands on multiple systems.

Os adversários podem tirar partido de **cmd** (`S0106`) to execute various commands and payloads. Common uses include **cmd** (`S0106`) to execute a single command, or abusing **cmd** (`S0106`) interactively with input and output forwarded over a Command and Control (C2) channel.

techniques.fullNameEn: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: Unix Shell
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Unix shell commands and scripts for execution. Unix shells are the primary command prompt on Linux, macOS, and ESXi systems, though many variations of the Unix shell exist (e.g. sh, ash, bash, zsh, etc.) depending on the specific OS or distribution. `[Ref: DieNet Bash]` `[Ref: Apple ZShell]` Unix shells can control every aspect of a system, with certain commands requiring privilégios elevados.

Unix shells also support scripts that enable sequential execution of commands as well as other typical programming operations such as conditionals and loops. Common uses of shell scripts include long or repetitive tasks, or the need to run the same set of commands on multiple systems.

Os adversários podem abusar de Unix shells to execute various commands or payloads. Interactive shells may be accessed through Command and Control (C2) channels or during lateral movement such as with **SSH** (`T1021.004`). Os adversários podem também leverage shell scripts to deliver and execute multiple commands on victims or as part of payloads used for persistence.

Some systems, such as embedded devices, lightweight Linux distributions, and ESXi servers, may leverage stripped-down Unix shells via Busybox, a small executable that contains a variety of tools, including a simple shell.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) where appropriate. On ESXi hosts, the `execInstalledOnly` feature prevents binaries from being run unless they have been packaged and signed as part of a vSphere installation bundle (VIB). `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence ESXi Hardening 2023]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNameEn: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: Visual Basic
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Visual Basic (VB) for execution. VB is a programming language created by Microsoft with interoperability with many Windows technologies such as **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`) and the **Native API** (`T1106`) through the Windows API. Although tagged as legacy with no planned future evolutions, VB is integrated and supported in the .NET Framework and cross-platform .NET Core. `[Ref: VB .NET Mar 2020]` `[Ref: VB Microsoft]`

Derivative languages based on VB have also been created, such as Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) and VBScript. VBA is an event-driven programming language built into Microsoft Office, as well as several third-party applications. `[Ref: Microsoft VBA]` `[Ref: Wikipedia VBA]` VBA enables documents to contain macros used to automate the execution of tasks and other functionality on the host. VBScript is a default scripting language on Windows hosts and can also be used in place of **JavaScript** (`T1059.007`) on HTML Application (HTA) webpages served to Internet Explorer (though most modern browsers do not come with VBScript support). `[Ref: Microsoft VBScript]`

Os adversários podem utilizar VB payloads para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos commands. Common malicious usage includes automating execution of behaviors with VBScript or embedding VBA content into **Spearphishing Attachment** (`T1566.001`) payloads (which may also involve **Mark-of-the-Web Bypass** (`T1553.005`) to enable execution). `[Ref: Default VBS macros Blocking ]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Turn off or restrict access to unneeded VB components.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically quarantine suspicious files.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) where appropriate. VBA macros obtained from the Internet, based on the file's Mark of the Web (MOTW) attribute, may be blocked from executing in Office applications (ex: Access, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, and Word) by default starting in Windows Version 2203. `[Ref: Default VBS macros Blocking ]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent **Visual Basic** (`T1059.005`) scripts from executing potentially malicious downloaded content  `[Ref: win10_asr]`.
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: Script blocking extensions can help prevent the execution of scripts and HTA files that may commonly be used during the exploitation process. For código malicioso served up through ads, adblockers can help prevent that code from executing in the first place.

techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: Python
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Python commands and scripts for execution. Python is a very popular scripting/programming language, with capabilities to perform many functions. Python can be executed interactively from the command-line (via the `python.exe` interpreter) or via scripts (.py) that can be written and distributed to different systems. Python code can also be compiled into binary executables. `[Ref: Zscaler APT31 Covid-19 October 2020]`

Python comes with many built-in packages to interact with the underlying system, such as file operations and device I/O. Adversaries can use these libraries to download and execute commands or other scripts as well as perform various malicious behaviors.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Inventory systems for unauthorized Python installations.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically quarantine suspicious files.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent users from installing Python where not required.

techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: JavaScript
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de various implementations of JavaScript for execution. JavaScript (JS) is a platform-independent scripting language (compiled just-in-time at runtime) commonly associated with scripts in webpages, though JS can be executed in runtime environments outside the browser. `[Ref: NodeJS]`

JScript is the Microsoft implementation of the same scripting standard. JScript is interpreted via the Windows Script engine and thus integrated with many components of Windows such as the **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`) and Internet Explorer HTML Application (HTA) pages. `[Ref: JScrip May 2018]` `[Ref: Microsoft JScript 2007]` `[Ref: Microsoft Windows Scripts]`

JavaScript for Automation (JXA) is a macOS scripting language based on JavaScript, included as part of Apple’s Open Scripting Architecture (OSA), that was introduced in OSX 10.10. Apple’s OSA provides scripting capabilities to control applications, interface with the sistema operativo, and bridge access into the rest of Apple’s internal APIs. As of OSX 10.10, OSA only supports two languages, JXA and **AppleScript** (`T1059.002`). Scripts can be executed via the command line utility `osascript`, they can be compiled into applications or script files via `osacompile`, and they can be compiled and executed in memory of other programs by leveraging the OSAKit Framework. `[Ref: Apple About Mac Scripting 2016]` `[Ref: SpecterOps JXA 2020]` `[Ref: SentinelOne macOS Red Team]` `[Ref: Red Canary Silver Sparrow Feb2021]` `[Ref: MDSec macOS JXA and VSCode]`

Os adversários podem abusar de various implementations of JavaScript to execute various behaviors. Common uses include hosting malicious scripts on websites as part of a **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`) or downloading and executing these script files as secondary payloads. Since these payloads are text-based, it is also very common for adversaries to obfuscate their content as part of **Obfuscated Files or Information** (`T1027`).

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent **JavaScript** (`T1059.007`) scripts from executing potentially malicious downloaded content  `[Ref: win10_asr]`.
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

techniques.fullNameEn: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Network Device CLI
techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: Network Device CLI
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de scripting or built-in command line interpreters (CLI) on network devices para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos command and payloads. The CLI is the primary means through which users and administrators interact with the device com o objetivo de view system information, modify device operations, or perform diagnostic and administrative functions. CLIs typically contain various permission levels required for different commands. 

Scripting interpreters automate tasks and extend functionality beyond the command set included in the network OS. The CLI and scripting interpreter are accessible through a direct console connection, or through remote means, such as telnet or **SSH** (`T1021.004`).

Adversaries can use the network CLI to change how network devices behave and operate. The CLI pode ser empregue para manipulate traffic flows to intercept or manipulate data, modify startup configuration parameters to load malicious system software, or to disable security features or logging para evitar deteção. `[Ref: Cisco Synful Knock Evolution]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: TACACS+ can keep control over which commands administrators are permitted to use through the configuration of authentication and command authorization.  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - TACACS]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use of Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) systems will limit actions administrators can perform and provide a history of user actions to detect unauthorized use and abuse. TACACS+ can keep control over which commands administrators are permitted to use through the configuration of authentication and command authorization `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - AAA]`  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - TACACS]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use of Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) systems will limit actions users can perform and provide a history of user actions to detect unauthorized use and abuse. Ensure least privilege principles are applied to user accounts and groups so that only authorized users can perform configuration changes.  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - AAA]`
