techniques.fullNameEn: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Cloud API
techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: Cloud API
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de cloud APIs para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos commands. APIs available in cloud environments provide various functionalities and are a feature-rich method for programmatic access to nearly all aspects of a tenant. These APIs may be utilized through various methods such as command line interpreters (CLIs), in-browser Cloud Shells, **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) modules like Azure for PowerShell `[Ref: Microsoft - Azure PowerShell]`, or software developer kits (SDKs) available for languages such as **Python** (`T1059.006`).  

Cloud API functionality may allow for administrative access across all major services in a tenant such as compute, storage, identity and access management (IAM), networking, and security policies.

With proper permissions (often via use of credentials such as **Application Access Token** (`T1550.001`) and **Web Session Cookie** (`T1550.004`)), adversaries may abuse cloud APIs to invoke various functions that execute malicious actions. Por exemplo, CLI and PowerShell functionality may be accessed through binaries installed on cloud-hosted or on-premises hosts or accessed through a browser-based cloud shell offered by many cloud platforms (such as AWS, Azure, and GCP). These cloud shells are often a packaged unified environment to use CLI and/or scripting modules hosted as a container in the cloud environment.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) where appropriate to block use of PowerShell CmdLets or other host based resources to access cloud API resources.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use of proper Identity and Access Management (IAM) with Role Based Access Control (RBAC) policies to limit actions administrators can perform and provide a history of administrative actions to detect unauthorized use and abuse.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Command and Scripting Interpreter: AutoHotKey & AutoIT
techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: AutoHotKey & AutoIT
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar commands and perform malicious tasks using AutoIT and AutoHotKey automation scripts. AutoIT and AutoHotkey (AHK) are scripting languages that enable users to automate Windows tasks. These automation scripts pode ser utilizado para perform a wide variety of actions, such as clicking on buttons, entering text, and opening and closing programs. `[Ref: AutoIT]` `[Ref: AutoHotKey]`

Os adversários podem utilizar AHK (`.ahk`) and AutoIT (`.au3`) scripts para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos code on a victim's system. Por exemplo, adversaries have used for AHK to execute payloads and other modular malware such as keyloggers. Adversaries have also used custom AHK files containing embedded malware as **Phishing** (`T1566`) payloads. `[Ref: Splunk DarkGate]`

These scripts may also be compiled into self-contained executable payloads (`.exe`). `[Ref: AutoIT]` `[Ref: AutoHotKey]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) to prevent execution of `AutoIt3.exe`, `AutoHotkey.exe`, and other related features that may not be required for a given system or network to prevent potential misuse by adversaries.

Os adversários podem abusar de Lua commands and scripts for execution. Lua is a cross-platform scripting and programming language primarily designed for embedded use in applications. Lua can be executed on the command-line (through the stand-alone lua interpreter), via scripts (`.lua`), or from Lua-embedded programs (through the `struct lua_State`). `[Ref: Lua main page]` `[Ref: Lua state]`

Lua scripts may be executed by adversaries for malicious purposes. techniques.fullNameEn: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Container CLI/API
techniques.fullNamePt: Interpretador de Comandos e Scripting: Container CLI/API
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de built-in CLI tools or API calls para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos commands in containerized environments.

The Docker CLI is used for managing containers via an exposed API point from the `dockerd` daemon. Some common examples of Docker CLI include Docker Desktop CLI and Docker Compose, but users are also able to use SDKs to interact with the API. Por exemplo, Docker SDK for Python pode ser utilizado para run commands within a Python application. `[Ref: Docker Desktop CLI]`

Os adversários podem tirar partido de the Docker CLI, API, or SDK to pull or build Docker images (i.e., **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`), **Build Image on Host** (`T1612`)), run containers (i.e., **Deploy Container** (`T1610`)), or execute commands inside running containers (i.e., **Container Administration Command** (`T1609`)). In some cases, threat actors may pull legitimate images that include scripts or tools that they can leverage - for example, using an image that includes the `curl` command to download payloads. `[Ref: Intezer]` Os adversários podem também utilize `docker inspect` and `docker ps` to scan for cloud variáveis de ambiente and other running containers (i.e., **Container and Resource Discovery** (`T1613`)). `[Ref: Cisco Talos Blog]` `[Ref: aquasec]`

Kubernetes is responsible for the management and orchestration of containers across clusters. The Kubernetes control plane, which manages the state of the cluster and is responsible for scheduling, communication, and resource monitoring, can be invoked directly via the API or indirectly via CLI tools such as `kubectl`. It may also be accessed within client libraries such as Go or Python. By utilizing the API, administrators can interact with resources within the cluster such as listing or creating pods, which is a group of one or more containers. Adversaries call the API server via `curl` or other tools, allowing them to obtain further information about the environment such as pods, deployments, daemonsets, namespaces, or sysvars. `[Ref: aquasec]` They may also run various commands regarding resource management.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict permissions on API access. RBAC in Kubernetes involve permissions that are additive, meaning there are no explicit "deny" rules. These permissions can be defined within a particular namespace or within cluster-scoped resources. Securing the Docker daemon can be done by using SSH or TLS with certificate authorization. Container management tools such as Docker and Podman may offer ways to run containers as rootless, which prevents them from running with privileged permissions.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. techniques.fullNamePt: Exploração para Escalada de Privilégios
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem explorar software vulnerabilities in an attempt to elevate privileges. Exploitation of a software vulnerability occurs when an adversary takes advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the sistema operativo software or kernel itself to execute adversary-controlled code. Security constructs such as permission levels will often hinder access to information and use of certain techniques, so adversaries will likely need to perform privilege escalation to include use of software exploitation to circumvent those restrictions.

When initially gaining access to a system, an adversary may be operating within a lower privileged process which will prevent them from accessing certain resources on the system. Vulnerabilities may exist, usually in sistema operativo components and software commonly running at higher permissions, that can be exploited to gain higher levels of access on the system. This could enable someone to move from unprivileged or user level permissions to SYSTEM or root permissions depending on the component that is vulnerable. This could also enable an adversary to move from a virtualized environment, such as within a máquina virtual (VM) or container, onto the underlying host. This may be a necessary step for an adversary compromising an endpoint system that has been properly configured and limits other privilege escalation methods.

Os adversários podem bring a signed vulnerable driver onto a compromised machine so that they can exploit the vulnerability to execute code in kernel mode. This process is sometimes referred to as Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD). `[Ref: ESET InvisiMole June 2020]` `[Ref: Unit42 AcidBox June 2020]` Os adversários podem include the vulnerable driver with files delivered during Initial Access or download it to a compromised system via **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`) or **Lateral Tool Transfer** (`T1570`).

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Update software regularly by employing patch management for internal enterprise endpoints and servers.

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Security applications that look for behavior used during exploitation such as Windows Defender Exploit Guard (WDEG) and the Enhanced Mitigation Experience Toolkit (EMET) pode ser utilizado para mitigate some exploitation behavior.  `[Ref: TechNet Moving Beyond EMET]` Control flow integrity checking is another way to potentially identify and stop a software exploit from occurring.  `[Ref: Wikipedia Control Flow Integrity]` Many of these protections depend on the architecture and target application binary for compatibility and may not work for software components targeted for privilege escalation.

mitigations.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Make it difficult for adversaries to advance their operation through exploitation of undiscovered or unpatched vulnerabilities by using sandboxing. Other types of virtualization and application microsegmentation may also mitigate the impact of some types of exploitation. Risks of additional exploits and weaknesses in these systems may still exist.  `[Ref: Ars Technica Pwn2Own 2017 VM Escape]`

mitigations.name: Threat Intelligence Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Develop a robust cyber threat intelligence capability to determine what types and levels of threat may use software exploits and 0-days against a particular organization.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider blocking the execution of known vulnerable drivers that adversaries may exploit to execute code in kernel mode. Validate driver block rules in audit mode to ensure stability prior to production deployment. `[Ref: Microsoft Driver Block Rules]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Grupos de Permissão
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar discover group and permission settings. This information can help adversaries determine which user accounts and groups are available, the membership of users in particular groups, and which users and groups have elevated permissions.

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar discover group permission settings in many different ways. This data may provide the adversary with information about the compromised environment that can be used in follow-on activity and targeting. `[Ref: CrowdStrike BloodHound April 2018]`

Time threshold for correlating group discovery with subsequent suspicious activity (e.g., lateral movement).
Whether the user performing discovery is in a sensitive group or running under unusual context (e.g., non-admin querying Domain Admins).

analytics.descriptionPt: Detection of group enumeration using commands like 'id', 'groups', or 'getent group', often followed by privilege escalation or SSH lateral movement.

mutableElements.description: Variations of enumeration commands tailored to different Linux distros (e.g., 'getent group', 'cut -d' in /etc/group parsing).
TTY context or source terminal (remote shell vs local login) to reduce noise.

analytics.descriptionPt: Group membership checks via 'dscl', 'dscacheutil', or 'id', typically executed via terminal or automation scripts.

mutableElements.description: Filters for suspicious execution of 'dscl . -read /Groups', etc.
Flag group enumeration from automation tools (e.g., LaunchAgents or suspicious apps).

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Grupos de Permissão: Local Groups
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar find local system groups and permission settings. The knowledge of local system permission groups can help adversaries determine which groups exist and which users belong to a particular group. Os adversários podem utilizar this information to determine which users have elevated permissions, such as the users found within the Administrador Locals group.

Commands such as `net localgroup` of the **Net** (`S0039`) utility, `dscl . -list /Groups` on macOS, and `groups` on Linux can list local groups.

Used to determine whether enumeration was triggered by a script or terminal.

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar find domain-level groups and permission settings. Os adversários podem utilizar this information to determine which users have elevated permissions, such as domain administrators.

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Grupos de Permissão: Cloud Groups
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar find cloud groups and permission settings. The knowledge of cloud permission groups can help adversaries determine the particular roles of users and groups dentro do ambiente alvo, as well as which users are associated with a particular group.

With authenticated access there are several tools that pode ser utilizado para find permissions groups. The `Get-MsolRole` PowerShell cmdlet pode ser utilizado para obtain roles and permissions groups for Exchange and Office 365 accounts  `[Ref: Microsoft Msolrole]` `[Ref: GitHub Raindance]`.

Azure CLI (AZ CLI) and the Google Cloud Identity Provider API also provide interfaces to obtain permissions groups. The command `az ad user get-member-groups` will list groups associated to a user account for Azure while the API endpoint `GET https://cloudidentity.googleapis.com/v1/groups` lists group resources available to a user for Google. `[Ref: Microsoft AZ CLI]` `[Ref: Black Hills Red Teaming MS AD Azure, 2018]` `[Ref: Google Cloud Identity API Documentation]` In AWS, the commands `ListRolePolicies` and `ListAttachedRolePolicies` allow users to enumerate the policies attached to a role. `[Ref: Palo Alto Unit 42 Compromised Cloud Compute Credentials 2022]`

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar list ACLs for objects to determine the owner and other accounts with access to the object, for example, via the AWS `GetBucketAcl` API  `[Ref: AWS Get Bucket ACL]`. Using this information an adversary can target accounts with permissions to a given object or leverage accounts they have already compromised to access the object.

techniques.fullNamePt: Remoção de Indicadores (Anti-Forensics)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem selectively delete or modify artifacts generated to reduce indications of their presence and blend in with legitimate activity. Rather than broadly removing evidence, adversaries may target specific artifacts that appear anomalous or are likely to draw scrutiny, while leaving sufficient data intact to maintain the appearance of normal system behavior.

Artifacts such as command histories, log entries, or file metadata may be altered in ways that align with expected user or system activity. Location, format, and type of artifact (such as command or login history) are often platform-specific, allowing adversaries to tailor modifications that minimize suspicion.

These actions may not prevent detection entirely but can delay recognition of malicious activity or reduce the fidelity of alerts by making events appear benign or consistent with routine operations. Additionally, selectively removed or modified artifacts may still be recoverable through deeper forensic analysis, though their absence or alteration can complicate timeline reconstruction and attribution.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Obfuscate/encrypt event files locally and in transit to avoid giving feedback to an adversary.

mitigations.name: Remote Data Storage
mitigations.descriptionPt: Automatically forward events to a log server or data repository to prevent conditions in which the adversary can locate and manipulate data on the local system. When possible, minimize time delay on event reporting to avoid prolonged storage on the local system.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Protect generated event files that are stored locally with proper permissions and authentication and limit opportunities for adversaries to increase privileges by preventing Privilege Escalation opportunities.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Remoção de Indicadores (Anti-Forensics): Clear Command History
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adicionalmente a clearing system logs, an adversary may clear the command history of a compromised account to conceal the actions undertaken during an intrusion. Various command interpreters keep track of the commands users type in their terminal so that users can retrace what they've done.

On Linux and macOS, these command histories can be accessed in a few different ways. While logged in, this command history is tracked in a file pointed to by the environment variable `HISTFILE`. When a user logs off a system, this information is flushed to a file in the user's home directory called `~/.bash_history`. The benefit of this is that it allows users to go back to commands they've used before in different sessions. Os adversários podem eliminar their commands from these logs by manually clearing the history (`history -c`) or deleting the bash history file `rm ~/.bash_history`.  

Os adversários podem também leverage a **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) on network devices to clear command history data (`clear logging` and/or `clear history`). `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` On ESXi servers, command history may be manually removed from the `/var/log/shell.log` file. `[Ref: Broadcom ESXi Shell Audit]`

On Windows hosts, PowerShell has two different command history providers: the built-in history and the command history managed by the `PSReadLine` module. The built-in history only tracks the commands used in the current session. This command history is not available to other sessions and is deleted when the session ends.

The `PSReadLine` command history tracks the commands used in all PowerShell sessions and writes them to a file (`$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\PSReadLine\ConsoleHost_history.txt` by default). This history file is available to all sessions and contains all past history since the file is not deleted when the session ends. `[Ref: Microsoft PowerShell Command History]`

Os adversários podem run the PowerShell command `Clear-History` to flush the entire command history from a current PowerShell session. This, however, will not delete/flush the `ConsoleHost_history.txt` file. Os adversários podem também delete the `ConsoleHost_history.txt` file or edit its contents to hide PowerShell commands they have run. `[Ref: Sophos PowerShell command audit]` `[Ref: Sophos PowerShell Command History Forensics]`

mitigations.name: Remote Data Storage

mitigations.descriptionPt: Preventing users from deleting or writing to certain files can stop adversaries from maliciously altering their `~/.bash_history` or `ConsoleHost_history.txt` files.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Making the variáveis de ambiente associated with command history read only may ensure that the history is preserved. `[Ref: Securing bash history]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Remoção de Indicadores (Anti-Forensics): File Deletion
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem eliminar files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity. Malware, tools, or other non-native files dropped or created on a system by an adversary (ex: **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`)) may leave traces to indicate to what was done within a network and how. Removal of these files can occur during an intrusion, or as part of a post-intrusion process to minimize the adversary's footprint.

There are tools available from the host sistema operativo to perform cleanup, but adversaries may use other tools as well. `[Ref: Microsoft SDelete July 2016]` Examples of built-in **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`) functions include `del` on Windows, `rm` or `unlink` on Linux and macOS, and `rm` on ESXi.

techniques.fullNamePt: Remoção de Indicadores (Anti-Forensics): Timestomp
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar file time attributes to hide new files or changes to existing files. Timestomping is a technique that modifies the timestamps of a file (the modify, access, create, and change times), often to mimic files that are in the same folder and blend malicious files with legitimate files.

In Windows systems, both the `$STANDARD_INFORMATION` (`$SI`) and `$FILE_NAME` (`$FN`) attributes record times in a Master File Table (MFT) file. `[Ref: Inversecos Timestomping 2022]` `$SI` (dates/time stamps) is displayed to the end user, including in the File System view, while `$FN` is dealt with by the kernel. `[Ref: Magnet Forensics]`

Modifying the `$SI` attribute is the most common method of timestomping because it can be modified at the user level using API calls. `$FN` timestomping, however, typically requires interacting with the system kernel or moving or renaming a file. `[Ref: Inversecos Timestomping 2022]`

Adversaries modify timestamps on files so that they do not appear conspicuous to forensic investigators or file analysis tools. In order para evadir deteçãos that rely on identifying discrepancies between the `$SI` and `$FN` attributes, adversaries may also engage in “double timestomping” by modifying times on both attributes simultaneously. `[Ref: Double Timestomping]`

In Linux systems and on ESXi servers, threat actors may attempt to perform timestomping using commands such as `touch -a -m -t <timestamp> <filename>` (which sets access and modification times to a specific value) or `touch -r <filename> <filename>` (which sets access and modification times to match those of another file). `[Ref: Inversecos Linux Timestomping]` `[Ref: Juniper Networks ESXi Backdoor 2022]`

Timestomping may be used along with file name **Masquerading** (`T1036`) to hide malware and tools. `[Ref: WindowsIR Anti-Forensic Techniques]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Indicator Removal: Clear Network Connection History and Configurations
techniques.namePt: Clear Network Connection History and Configurations
techniques.fullNamePt: Remoção de Indicadores (Anti-Forensics): Clear Network Connection History and Configurations
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem clear or remove evidence of malicious network connections com o objetivo de clean up traces of their operations. Configuration settings as well as various artifacts that highlight connection history may be created on a system and/or in application logs from behaviors that require network connections, such as **Remote Services** (`T1021`) or **External Remote Services** (`T1133`). Defenders may use these artifacts to monitor or otherwise analyze network connections created by adversaries.

Network connection history may be stored in various locations. Por exemplo, RDP connection history may be stored in Windows Registry values under  `[Ref: Microsoft RDP Removal]`:

* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Default`
* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers`

Windows may also store information about recent RDP connections in files such as `C:\Users\\%username%\Documents\Default.rdp` and `C:\Users\%username%\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Terminal
Server Client\Cache\`. `[Ref: Moran RDPieces]` Similarly, macOS and Linux hosts may store information highlighting connection history in system logs (such as those stored in `/Library/Logs` and/or `/var/log/`). `[Ref: Apple Culprit Access]` `[Ref: FreeDesktop Journal]` `[Ref: Apple Unified Log Analysis Remote Login and Screen Sharing]`

Malicious network connections may also require changes to third-party applications or network configuration settings, such as **Disable or Modify System Firewall** (`T1686`) or tampering to enable **Proxy** (`T1090`). Os adversários podem eliminar or modify this data to conceal indicators and/or impede defensive analysis.

techniques.fullNamePt: Remoção de Indicadores (Anti-Forensics): Clear Mailbox Data
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar mail and mail application data to remove evidence of their activity. Email applications allow users and other programs to export and delete mailbox data via command line tools or use of APIs. Mail application data can be emails, email metadata, or logs generated by the application or sistema operativo, such as export requests. 

Os adversários podem manipular emails and mailbox data to remove logs, artifacts, and metadata, such as evidence of **Phishing** (`T1566`)/**Internal Spearphishing** (`T1534`), **Email Collection** (`T1114`), **Mail Protocols** (`T1071.003`) for Command and Control (C2), or email-based exfiltration such as **Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol** (`T1048`). Por exemplo, to remove evidence on Exchange servers adversaries have used the `ExchangePowerShell` **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) module, including `Remove-MailboxExportRequest` to remove evidence of mailbox exports. `[Ref: Volexity SolarWinds]` `[Ref: ExchangePowerShell Module]` On Linux and macOS, adversaries may also delete emails through a command line utility called `mail`  or use **AppleScript** (`T1059.002`) to interact with APIs on macOS. `[Ref: Cybereason Cobalt Kitty 2017]` `[Ref: mailx man page]`

Os adversários podem também remove emails and metadata/headers indicative of spam or suspicious activity (for example, through the use of organization-wide transport rules) to reduce the likelihood of malicious emails being detected by security products. `[Ref: Microsoft OAuth Spam 2022]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Protect generated event files that are stored locally with proper permissions and authentication and limit opportunities for adversaries to increase privileges by preventing Privilege Escalation opportunities.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: In an Exchange environment, Administrators can use `Get-TransportRule` / `Remove-TransportRule` to discover and remove potentially malicious transport rules. `[Ref: Microsoft Manage Mail Flow Rules 2023]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNamePt: Remoção de Indicadores (Anti-Forensics): Clear Persistence
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem clear artifacts associated with previously established persistence on a host system to remove evidence of their activity. This may involve various actions, such as removing services, deleting executables, **Modify Registry** (`T1112`), **Plist File Modification** (`T1647`), or other methods of cleanup to prevent defenders from collecting evidence of their persistent presence. `[Ref: Cylance Dust Storm]` Os adversários podem também delete accounts previously created to maintain persistence (i.e. **Create Account** (`T1136`)). `[Ref: Talos - Cisco Attack 2022]`

In some instances, artifacts of persistence may also be removed once an adversary’s persistence is executed com o objetivo de prevent errors with the new instance of the malware. `[Ref: NCC Group Team9 June 2020]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Protect generated event files that are stored locally with proper permissions and authentication and limit opportunities for adversaries to increase privileges by preventing Privilege Escalation opportunities.

mitigations.name: Remote Data Storage
mitigations.descriptionPt: Automatically forward events to a log server or data repository to prevent conditions in which the adversary can locate and manipulate data on the local system. When possible, minimize time delay on event reporting to avoid prolonged storage on the local system.

techniques.fullNamePt: Remoção de Indicadores (Anti-Forensics): Relocate Malware
techniques.descriptionPt:
Uma vez que a payload is delivered, adversaries may reproduce copies of the same malware on the victim system to remove evidence of their presence and/or avoid defenses. Copying malware payloads to new locations may also be combined with **File Deletion** (`T1070.004`) to cleanup older artifacts.

Relocating malware may be a part of many actions intended to evade defenses. Por exemplo, adversaries may copy and rename payloads to better blend into the local environment (i.e., **Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location** (`T1036.005`)). `[Ref: DFIR Report Trickbot June 2023]` Payloads may also be repositioned to target **File/Path Exclusions** (`T1564.012`) as well as specific locations associated with establishing **Persistence** (`TA0003`). `[Ref: Latrodectus APR 2024]`

Relocating malicious payloads may also hinder defensive analysis, especially to separate these payloads from earlier events (such as **User Execution** (`T1204`) and **Phishing** (`T1566`)) that may have generated alerts or otherwise drawn attention from defenders. Moving payloads into target directories does not alter the Creation timestamp, thereby evading detection logic reliant on modifications to this artifact (i.e., **Timestomp** (`T1070.006`)).

techniques.fullNamePt: Protocolo da Camada de Aplicação
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem communicate using OSI application layer protocols para evitar deteção/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic. Commands to the remote system, and often the results of those commands, will be embedded within the protocol traffic between the client and server. 

Os adversários podem utilize many different protocols, including those used for web browsing, transferring files, electronic mail, DNS, or publishing/subscribing. For connections that occur internally within an enclave (such as those between a proxy or pivot node and other nodes), commonly used protocols are SMB, SSH, or RDP. `[Ref: Mandiant APT29 Eye Spy Email Nov 22]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Mandiant APT29 Eye Spy Email Nov 22]

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use network appliances to filter ingress or egress traffic and perform protocol-based filtering. Configurar software on endpoints to filter tráfego de rede.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Protocolo da Camada de Aplicação: Web Protocols
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem communicate using application layer protocols associated with web traffic para evitar deteção/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic. Commands to the remote system, and often the results of those commands, will be embedded within the protocol traffic between the client and server. 

Protocols such as HTTP/S `[Ref: CrowdStrike Putter Panda]` and WebSocket `[Ref: Brazking-Websockets]` that carry web traffic may be very common in environments. HTTP/S packets have many fields and headers in which data can be concealed. Um adversário pode abuse these protocols para comunicar com systems under their control within a victim network while also mimicking normal, expected traffic.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict and monitor outbound web traffic (HTTP/HTTPS) from critical servers to only approved destinations. Limiting the ability to initiate outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections, especially from public-facing servers, can prevent attackers from using tools like curl or wget para comunicar com external C2 servers or download malicious payloads.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

blockers: M1031 (Network Intrusion Prevention): Reverse shell ou beacon C2 não conecta para o exterior; conexões TCP diretas bloqueadas ou terminadas pelo Proxy/Firewall.
M1037 (Filter Network Traffic): Movimentação lateral via `PsExec`, `evil-winrm` ou `wmiexec` falha por timeout de porta.
Firewall Egress restritiva, Proxy com inspeção SSL/TLS e bloqueio de domínios sem reputação ou DLP ativo.
bypasses: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

Empregar canais sobre Web Services legítimos permitidos (Microsoft Graph, GitHub, OneDrive), respeitar o Proxy do sistema via `WinINet` com credenciais integradas da sessão atual, aplicar jitter/sleep randomization e fragmentar transferências abaixo dos limiares de DLP.

**UserAgentAnomalies**: Detect non-browser user-agents or spoofed headers
**OutboundByteRatioThreshold**: Flag when outbound > inbound volume by 90%+
**CommandLinePatternMatch**: curl or wget in scripts with suspicious domains or silent flags

techniques.fullNameEn: Application Layer Protocol: File Transfer Protocols
techniques.fullNamePt: Protocolo da Camada de Aplicação: File Transfer Protocols
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem communicate using application layer protocols associated with transferring files para evitar deteção/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic. Commands to the remote system, and often the results of those commands, will be embedded within the protocol traffic between the client and server. 

Protocols such as SMB `[Ref: US-CERT TA18-074A]`, FTP `[Ref: ESET Machete July 2019]`, FTPS, and TFTP that transfer files may be very common in environments.  Packets produced from these protocols may have many fields and headers in which data can be concealed. Data could also be concealed within the transferred files. Um adversário pode abuse these protocols para comunicar com systems under their control within a victim network while also mimicking normal, expected traffic.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Filter outbound FTP/SFTP traffic from sensitive systems, allowing file transfers only to trusted internal or known IP addresses. This measure can prevent attackers from transferring data or payloads via FTP/SFTP channels to or from unauthorized external systems.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem communicate using the Domain Name System (DNS) application layer protocol para evitar deteção/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic. Commands to the remote system, and often the results of those commands, will be embedded within the protocol traffic between the client and server. 

The DNS protocol serves an administrative function in computer networking and thus may be very common in environments. DNS traffic may also be allowed even before network authentication is completed. DNS packets contain many fields and headers in which data can be concealed. Often known as DNS tunneling, adversaries may abuse DNS para comunicar com systems under their control within a victim network while also mimicking normal, expected traffic. `[Ref: PAN DNS Tunneling]` `[Ref: Medium DnsTunneling]`

DNS beaconing pode ser empregue para send commands to sistemas remotos via DNS queries. A DNS beacon is created by tunneling DNS traffic (i.e. **Protocol Tunneling** (`T1572`)). The commands may be embedded into different DNS records, for example, TXT or A records. `[Ref: OilRig Uses Updated BONDUPDATER to Target Middle Eastern Government]` DNS beacons may be difficult to detect because the beacons infrequently communicate with infected devices. `[Ref: DNS Beacons]` Infrequent communication conceals the malicious DNS traffic with normal DNS traffic.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider filtering DNS requests to unknown, untrusted, or known bad domains and resources. Resolving DNS requests with on-premise/proxy servers may also disrupt adversary attempts to conceal data within DNS packets.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Protocolo da Camada de Aplicação: Publish/Subscribe Protocols
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem communicate using publish/subscribe (pub/sub) application layer protocols para evitar deteção/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic. Commands to the remote system, and often the results of those commands, will be embedded within the protocol traffic between the client and server. 

Protocols such as `MQTT`, `XMPP`, `AMQP`, and `STOMP` use a publish/subscribe design, with message distribution managed by a centralized broker. `[Ref: wailing crab sub/pub]` `[Ref: Mandiant APT1 Appendix]` Publishers categorize their messages by topics, while subscribers receive messages according to their subscribed topics. `[Ref: wailing crab sub/pub]` Um adversário pode abuse publish/subscribe protocols para comunicar com systems under their control from behind a message broker while also mimicking normal, expected traffic.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider filtering publish/subscribe protocol requests to untrusted or known bad resources over irregular ports (e.g. MQTT’s standard ports are 1883 or 8883).

techniques.fullNamePt: Ferramentas de Distribuição de Software (SCCM/MECM)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem gain access to and use centralized software suites installed within an enterprise to execute commands and move laterally through the network. Configuration management and software deployment applications may be used in an enterprise network or cloud environment for routine administration purposes. These systems may also be integrated into CI/CD pipelines. Examples of such solutions include: SCCM, HBSS, Altiris, AWS Systems Manager, Microsoft Intune, Azure Arc, and GCP Deployment Manager.  

Access to network-wide or enterprise-wide endpoint management software may enable an adversary to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) on all connected systems. The access pode ser empregue para laterally move to other systems, gather information, or cause a specific effect, such as wiping the hard drives on all endpoints.

SaaS-based configuration management services may allow for broad **Cloud Administration Command** (`T1651`) on cloud-hosted instances, as well as the execution of comandos arbitrários on on-premises endpoints. Por exemplo, Microsoft Configuration Manager allows Global or Intune Administrators to run scripts as SYSTEM on on-premises devices joined to Entra ID. `[Ref: SpecterOps Lateral Movement from Azure to On-Prem AD 2020]` Such services may also utilize **Web Protocols** (`T1071.001`) to communicate back to adversary owned infrastructure. `[Ref: Mitiga Security Advisory: SSM Agent as Remote Access Trojan]`

Network infrastructure devices may also have configuration management tools that can be similarly abused by adversaries. `[Ref: Fortinet Zero-Day and Custom Malware Used by Suspected Chinese Actor in Espionage Operation]`

The permissions required for this action vary by system configuration; local credentials may be sufficient with direct access to the third-party system, or specific domain credentials may be required. Contudo, the system may require an administrative account to log in or to access specific functionality.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que any accounts used by third-party providers to access these systems are traceable to the third-party and are not used throughout the network or used by other third-party providers in the same environment. Ensure there are regular reviews of accounts provisioned to these systems to verify continued business need, and ensure there is governance to trace de-provisioning of access that is no longer required. Ensure proper system and access isolation for critical network systems through use of account privilege separation.

mitigations.name: Active Directory Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper system and access isolation for critical network systems through use of group policy.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Patch deployment systems regularly to prevent potential remote access through **Exploitation for Privilege Escalation** (`T1068`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Grant access to application deployment systems only to a limited number of authorized administrators.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Verify that account credentials that pode ser empregue para access deployment systems are unique and not used throughout the enterprise network.

mitigations.name: Limit Software Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict the use of third-party software suites installed within an enterprise network.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper system isolation for critical network systems through use of firewalls.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Have a strict approval policy for use of deployment systems.

Pivotar para protocolos alternativos como DCOM (`MMC20.Application`), WMI sobre RPC, MSSQL Links (`1433`), RDP em modo `RestrictedAdmin`, ou autenticação Kerberos com chaves AES256 (`Overpass-the-Hash`) usando o FQDN do host em vez do endereço IP.

techniques.fullNamePt: Preparação de Dados (Data Staging)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem preparar e hospedar (stage) collected data in a central location or directory prior to Exfiltration. Data may be kept in separate files or combined into one file through techniques such as **Archive Collected Data** (`T1560`). Interactive command shells may be used, and common functionality within **cmd** (`S0106`) and bash pode ser empregue para copy data into a staging location. `[Ref: PWC Cloud Hopper April 2017]`

Em ambientes Cloud, adversaries may stage data within a particular instance or máquina virtual (VM) before exfiltration. Um adversário pode **Create Cloud Instance** (`T1578.002`) and stage data in that instance. `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2020]`

Os adversários podem choose to stage data from a victim network in a centralized location prior to Exfiltration to minimize the number of connections made to their C2 server and better evade detection.

techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Contas Válidas (Valid Accounts)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem obter and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Compromised credentials pode ser empregue para bypass access controls placed on various resources on systems within the network and may even be used for persistent access to sistemas remotos and externally available services, such as VPNs, Outlook Web Access, network devices, and remote desktop. `[Ref: volexity_0day_sophos_FW]` Compromised credentials may also grant an adversary increased privilege to specific systems or access to restricted areas of the network. Os adversários podem choose not to use malware or tools in conjunction with the legitimate access those credentials provide to make it harder to detect their presence.

In some cases, adversaries may abuse inactive accounts: for example, those belonging to individuals who are no longer part of an organization. Using these accounts may allow the adversary para evadir deteção, as the original account user will not be present to identify any anomalous activity taking place on their account. `[Ref: CISA MFA PrintNightmare]`

The overlap of permissions for local, domain, and cloud accounts across a network of systems is of concern because the adversary may be able to pivot across accounts and systems to reach a high level of access (i.e., domain or enterprise administrator) para contornar (bypass) access controls set within the enterprise. `[Ref: TechNet Credential Theft]`

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Applications and appliances that utilize default username and password should be changed immediately after the installation, and before deployment to a production environment. `[Ref: US-CERT Alert TA13-175A Risks of Default Passwords on the Internet]` When possible, applications that use SSH keys should be updated periodically and properly secured.

Policies should minimize (if not eliminate) reuse of passwords between different user accounts, especially employees using the same credentials for personal accounts that may not be defended by enterprise security resources.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Regularly audit user accounts for activity and deactivate or remove any that are no longer needed.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Auditar regularmente domain and local accounts as well as their permission levels routinely to look for situations that could allow an adversary to gain wide access by obtaining credentials of a privileged account.  `[Ref: TechNet Credential Theft]`  `[Ref: TechNet Least Privilege]` These audits should also include if default accounts have been enabled, or if new local accounts are created that have not been authorized. Follow best practices for design and administration of an enterprise network to limit privileged account use across administrative tiers.  `[Ref: Microsoft Securing Privileged Access]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar multi-factor authentication (MFA) across all account types, including default, local, domain, and cloud accounts, to prevent unauthorized access, even if credentials are compromised. MFA provides a critical layer of security by requiring multiple forms of verification beyond just a password. This measure significantly reduces the risk of adversaries abusing valid accounts to gain initial access, escalate privileges, maintain persistence, or evade defenses within your network.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Application Developer Guidance
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que applications do not store dados sensíveis or credentials insecurely. (e.g. plaintext credentials in code, published credentials in repositories, or credentials in public cloud storage).

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Applications may send push notifications to verify a login as a form of multi-factor authentication (MFA). Train users to only accept valid push notifications and to report suspicious push notifications.

mitigations.name: Active Directory Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable legacy authentication, which does not support MFA, and require the use of modern authentication protocols instead.

mitigations.name: Account Use Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use conditional access policies to block logins from non-compliant devices or from outside defined organization IP ranges. `[Ref: Microsoft Common Conditional Access Policies]`

Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

Aplicar Indirect Syscalls com Call Stack Spoofing, evitar permissões de memória `RWX` simultâneas (usar padrão `RW` -> `RX` com Sleep Encryption como Ekko/Cronos durante períodos de inatividade do beacon) e realizar patching de `EtwEventWrite` no processo local.

Explorar objetos COM auto-elevados (`ICMLuaUtil`), sequestro de chaves em `HKCU\Software\Classes` lidas por binários `autoElevate`, abuso de privilégios de Token (`SeImpersonatePrivilege` via PrintSpoofer/GodPotato) ou DLL Hijacking em serviços `SYSTEM`.

**TimeWindow**: Define acceptable hours for interactive logon activity (e.g., 9AM-6PM local).
**GeoIPMismatch**: Trigger on location anomalies based on prior user behavior or policy.
**UserContext**: Identify logins to root or sudoers not aligned with normal usage profiles.
**HostDensityThreshold**: Number of unique systems a user authenticates to in a time window.

techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Contas Válidas (Valid Accounts): Default Accounts
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem obter and abuse credentials of a default account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Default accounts are those that are built-into an OS, such as the Guest or Administrator accounts on Windows systems. Default accounts also include default factory/provider set accounts on other types of systems, software, or devices, including the root user account in AWS, the root user account in ESXi, and the default service account in Kubernetes. `[Ref: Microsoft Local Accounts Feb 2019]` `[Ref: AWS Root User]` `[Ref: Threat Matrix for Kubernetes]`

Default accounts are not limited to client machines; rather, they also include accounts that are preset for equipment such as network devices and computer applications, whether they are internal, open source, or commercial. Appliances that come preset with a username and password combination pose a serious threat to organizations that do not change it post installation, as they are easy targets for an adversary. Similarly, adversaries may also utilize publicly disclosed or stolen **Private Keys** (`T1552.004`) or material de credenciaiss to legitimately connect to remote environments via **Remote Services** (`T1021`). `[Ref: Metasploit SSH Module]`

Default accounts may be created on a system after initial setup by connecting or integrating it with another application. Por exemplo, when an ESXi server is connected to a vCenter server, a default privileged account called `vpxuser` is created on the ESXi server. If a threat actor is able to compromise this account’s credentials (for example, via **Exploitation for Credential Access** (`T1212`) on the vCenter host), they will then have access to the ESXi server. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence VMWare ESXi Zero-Day 2023]` `[Ref: Pentera vCenter Information Disclosure]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence VMWare ESXi Zero-Day 2023]

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar multi-factor authentication (MFA) for default accounts whenever possible to prevent unauthorized access, even if credentials for these accounts are compromised. MFA adds an additional layer of security that requires more than just a username and password, making it significantly harder for adversaries to exploit these accounts for initial access or lateral movement.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Applications and appliances that utilize default username and password should be changed immediately after the installation, and before deployment to a production environment.  `[Ref: US-CERT Alert TA13-175A Risks of Default Passwords on the Internet]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Contas Válidas (Valid Accounts): Domain Accounts
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem obter and abuse credentials of a domain account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. `[Ref: TechNet Credential Theft]` Domain accounts are those managed by Active Directory (AD) Domain Services where access and permissions are configured across systems and services that are part of that domain. Domain accounts can cover users, administrators, and services. `[Ref: Microsoft AD Accounts]`

Os adversários podem comprometer domain accounts, some with a high level of privileges, through various means such as **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`) or password reuse, allowing access to privileged resources of the domain.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Regularly review and manage domain accounts to ensure that only active, necessary accounts exist. Remove or disable inactive and unnecessary accounts to reduce the risk of adversaries abusing these accounts to gain unauthorized access or move laterally within the network.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Integrating multi-factor authentication (MFA) as part of organizational policy can greatly reduce the risk of an adversary gaining control of valid credentials that may be used for additional tactics such as initial access, lateral movement, and collecting information. MFA pode também ser utilizado para restrict access to cloud resources and APIs.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Auditar regularmente domain account permission levels routinely to look for situations that could allow an adversary to gain wide access by obtaining credentials of a privileged account. Do not put user or admin domain accounts in the Administrador Local groups across systems unless they are tightly controlled and use of accounts is segmented, as this is often equivalent to having a Administrador Local account with the same password on all systems. Follow best practices for design and administration of an enterprise network to limit privileged account use across administrative tiers. Limit credential overlap across systems to prevent access if account credentials are obtained.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Applications may send push notifications to verify a login as a form of multi-factor authentication (MFA). Train users to only accept valid push notifications and to report suspicious push notifications.

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar and enforce strong password policies for domain accounts to ensure passwords are complex, unique, and regularly rotated. This reduces the likelihood of password guessing, credential stuffing, and other attack methods that rely on weak or static credentials.

techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Contas Válidas (Valid Accounts): Local Accounts
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem obter and abuse credentials of a local account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Local accounts are those configured by an organization for use by users, remote support, services, or for administration on a single system or service.

Local Accounts may also be abused to elevate privileges and harvest credentials through **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`). Password reuse may allow the abuse of local accounts across a set of machines on a network for the purposes of Privilege Escalation and Lateral Movement.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Auditar regularmente local accounts permission levels routinely to look for situations that could allow an adversary to gain wide access by obtaining credentials of a privileged account.  `[Ref: TechNet Credential Theft]`  `[Ref: TechNet Least Privilege]` Limit the usage of Administrador Local accounts to be used for day-to-day operations that may expose them to potential adversaries. 

Por exemplo, audit the use of service accounts in Kubernetes, and avoid automatically granting them access to the Kubernetes API if this is not required. `[Ref: Kubernetes Service Accounts]` Implementing LAPS may also help prevent reuse of Administrador Local credentials across a domain. `[Ref: Microsoft Remote Use of Local]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) for local accounts to add an extra layer of protection against credential theft and misuse. MFA can be implemented using methods like mobile-based authenticators or hardware tokens, even in environments that do not rely on Domain Controller (DC)s or cloud services. This additional security measure can help reduce the risk of adversaries gaining unauthorized access to local systems and resources.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que Administrador Local accounts have complex, unique passwords across all systems on the network.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de user account management practices for local accounts to limit access and remove inactive or unused accounts. By doing so, you reduce the attack surface available to adversaries and prevent unauthorized access to local systems.

techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Contas Válidas (Valid Accounts): Cloud Accounts
techniques.descriptionPt:
Valid accounts in cloud environments may allow adversaries to perform actions to achieve Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Cloud accounts are those created and configured by an organization for use by users, remote support, services, or for administration of resources within a cloud service provider or SaaS application. Cloud Accounts can exist solely in the cloud; alternatively, they may be hybrid-joined between on-premises systems and the cloud through syncing or federation with other identity sources such as Windows Active Directory (AD). `[Ref: AWS Identity Federation]` `[Ref: Google Federating GC]` `[Ref: Microsoft Deploying AD Federation]`

Service or user accounts may be targeted by adversaries through **Brute Force** (`T1110`), **Phishing** (`T1566`), or various other means para obter acesso a the environment. Federated or synced accounts may be a pathway for the adversary to affect both on-premises systems and cloud environments - for example, by leveraging shared credentials to log onto **Remote Services** (`T1021`). High privileged cloud accounts, whether federated, synced, or cloud-only, may also allow pivoting to on-premises environments by leveraging SaaS-based **Software Deployment Tools** (`T1072`) to run commands on hybrid-joined devices.

Um adversário pode create long lasting **Additional Cloud Credentials** (`T1098.001`) on a compromised cloud account to maintain persistence in the environment. Such credentials may also be used para contornar (bypass) controlos de segurança such as multi-factor authentication. 

Cloud accounts may also be able to assume **Temporary Elevated Cloud Access** (`T1548.005`) or other privileges through various means within the environment. Misconfigurations in role assignments or role assumption policies may allow an adversary to use these mechanisms to leverage permissions outside the intended scope of the account. Such over privileged accounts pode ser empregue para harvest dados sensíveis from online storage accounts and databases through **Cloud API** (`T1059.009`) or other methods. Por exemplo, in Azure environments, adversaries may target Azure Managed Identities, which allow associated Azure resources to request access tokens. By compromising a resource with an attached Managed Identity, such as an Azure VM, adversaries may be able to **Steal Application Access Token** (`T1528`)s para realizar movimentação lateral across the cloud environment. `[Ref: SpecterOps Managed Identity 2022]`

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que cloud accounts, particularly privileged accounts, have complex, unique passwords across all systems on the network. Passwords and access keys should be rotated regularly. This limits the amount of time credentials pode ser utilizado para access resources if a credential is compromised without your knowledge. Cloud service providers may track access key age to help audit and identify keys that may need to be rotated. `[Ref: AWS - IAM Console Best Practices]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable legacy authentication, which does not support MFA, and require the use of modern authentication protocols instead.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Review privileged cloud account permission levels routinely to look for those that could allow an adversary to gain wide access, such as Global Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator in Azure AD. `[Ref: TechNet Credential Theft]` `[Ref: TechNet Least Privilege]` `[Ref: Microsoft Azure security baseline for Azure Active Directory (AD)]` These reviews should also check if new privileged cloud accounts have been created that were not authorized. Por exemplo, in Azure AD environments configure alerts to notify when accounts have gone many days without using privileged roles, as these roles may be able to be removed. `[Ref: Microsoft Security Alerts for Azure AD Roles]` Consider using temporary, just-in-time (JIT) privileged access to Azure AD resources rather than permanently assigning privileged roles. `[Ref: Microsoft Azure security baseline for Azure Active Directory (AD)]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Contaminação de Conteúdo Partilhado
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem deliver payloads to sistemas remotos by adding content to shared storage locations, such as network drives or internal code repositories. Content stored on network drives or in other shared locations may be tainted by adding malicious programs, scripts, or exploit code to otherwise valid files. Uma vez que a user opens the shared tainted content, the malicious portion can be executed to run the adversary's code on a remote system. Os adversários podem utilizar tainted shared content para realizar movimentação lateral.

A directory share pivot is a variation on this technique that uses several other techniques to propagate malware when users access a shared network directory. It uses **Shortcut Modification** (`T1547.009`) of directory .LNK files that use **Masquerading** (`T1036`) to look like the real directories, which are hidden through **Hidden Files and Directories** (`T1564.001`). The malicious .LNK-based directories have an embedded command that executes the hidden malware file in the directory and then opens the real intended directory so that the user's expected action still occurs. When used with frequently used network directories, the technique may result in frequent reinfections and broad access to systems and potentially to new and higher privileged accounts.  `[Ref: Retwin Directory Share Pivot]`

Os adversários podem também compromise shared network directories through binary infections by appending or prepending its code to the healthy binary on the shared network directory. The malware may modify the original entry point (OEP) of the healthy binary to ensure that it is executed before the legitimate code. The infection could continue to spread via the newly infected file when it is executed by a remote system. These infections may target both binary and non-binary formats that end with extensions including, but not limited to, .EXE, .DLL, .SCR, .BAT, and/or .VBS.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus pode ser utilizado para automatically quarantine suspicious files. `[Ref: Mandiant Cloudy Logs 2023]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Identify potentially malicious software that pode ser empregue para taint content or may result from it and audit and/or block the unknown programs by using application control  `[Ref: Beechey 2010]` tools, like AppLocker,  `[Ref: Windows Commands JPCERT]`  `[Ref: NSA MS AppLocker]` or Software Restriction Policies  `[Ref: Corio 2008]` where appropriate.  `[Ref: TechNet Applocker vs SRP]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Protect shared folders by minimizing users who have write access.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use utilities that detect or mitigate common features used in exploitation, such as the Microsoft Enhanced Mitigation Experience Toolkit (EMET).
