techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Informação do Sistema
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode attempt to get detailed information about the sistema operativo and hardware, including version, patches, hotfixes, service packs, and architecture. Os adversários podem utilizar this information to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions. This behavior is distinct from **Local Storage Discovery** (`T1680`) which is an adversary's discovery of local drive, disks and/or volumes.

Tools such as **Systeminfo** (`S0096`) pode ser utilizado para gather detailed system information. If running with privileged access, a breakdown of system data can be gathered through the `systemsetup` configuration tool on macOS. Os adversários podem tirar partido de a **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) on network devices to gather detailed system information (e.g. `show version`). `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` On ESXi servers, threat actors may gather system information from various esxcli utilities, such as `system hostname get` and `system version get`. `[Ref: Crowdstrike Hypervisor Jackpotting Pt 2 2021]` `[Ref: Varonis]`

Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) cloud providers such as AWS, GCP, and Azure allow access to instance and máquina virtual (VM) information via APIs. Successful authenticated API calls can return data such as the sistema operativo platform and status of a particular instance or the model view of a máquina virtual (VM). `[Ref: Amazon Describe Instance]` `[Ref: Google Instances Resource]` `[Ref: Microsoft Virutal Machine API]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Ficheiros e Diretórios
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enumerar files and directories or may search in specific locations of a host or network share for certain information within a sistema de ficheiros. Os adversários podem utilizar the information from **File and Directory Discovery** (`T1083`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions.

Many command shell utilities pode ser utilizado para obtain this information. Examples include `dir`, `tree`, `ls`, `find`, and `locate`. `[Ref: Windows Commands JPCERT]` Custom tools may also be used to gather file and directory information and interact with the **Native API** (`T1106`). Os adversários podem também leverage a **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) on network devices to gather file and directory information (e.g. `dir`, `show flash`, and/or `nvram`). `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]`

Some files and directories may require elevated or specific user permissions to access.

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Contas
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of valid accounts, usernames, or email addresses on a system or within a compromised environment. This information can help adversaries determine which accounts exist, which can aid in follow-on behavior such as brute-forcing, spear-phishing attacks, or account takeovers (e.g., **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`)).

Os adversários podem utilizar several methods to enumerate accounts, including abuse of existing tools, built-in commands, and potential misconfigurations that leak account names and roles or permissions in the targeted environment.

For examples, cloud environments typically provide easily accessible interfaces to obtain user lists. `[Ref: AWS List Users]` `[Ref: Google Cloud - IAM Servie Accounts List API]` On hosts, adversaries can use default **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) and other command line functionality to identify accounts. Information about email addresses and accounts may also be extracted by searching an infected system’s files.

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent administrator accounts from being enumerated when an application is elevating through UAC since it can lead to the disclosure of account names. The Registry key is located `HKLM\ SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\CredUI\EnumerateAdministrators`. It can be disabled through GPO: Computer Configuration > [Policies] > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Credential User Interface: E numerate administrator accounts on elevation.  `[Ref: UCF STIG Elevation Account Enumeration]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Contas: Local Account
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of local system accounts. This information can help adversaries determine which local accounts exist on a system to aid in follow-on behavior.

Commands such as `net user` and `net localgroup` of the **Net** (`S0039`) utility and `id` and `groups` on macOS and Linux can list local users and groups. `[Ref: Mandiant APT1]` `[Ref: id man page]` `[Ref: groups man page]` Em sistemas Linux, local users can also be enumerated through the use of the `/etc/passwd` file. Em sistemas macOS, the `dscl . list /Users` command pode ser utilizado para enumerate local accounts. On ESXi servers, the `esxcli system account list` command can list local user accounts. `[Ref: Crowdstrike Hypervisor Jackpotting Pt 2 2021]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Contas: Cloud Account
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of cloud accounts. Cloud accounts are those created and configured by an organization for use by users, remote support, services, or for administration of resources within a cloud service provider or SaaS application.

With authenticated access there are several tools that pode ser utilizado para find accounts. The `Get-MsolRoleMember` PowerShell cmdlet pode ser utilizado para obtain account names given a role or permissions group in Office 365. `[Ref: Microsoft msolrolemember]` `[Ref: GitHub Raindance]` The Azure CLI (AZ CLI) also provides an interface to obtain user accounts with authenticated access to a domain. The command `az ad user list` will list all users within a domain. `[Ref: Microsoft AZ CLI]` `[Ref: Black Hills Red Teaming MS AD Azure, 2018]` 

The AWS command `aws iam list-users` pode ser empregue para obtain a list of users in the current account while `aws iam list-roles` can obtain IAM roles that have a specified path prefix. `[Ref: AWS List Roles]` `[Ref: AWS List Users]` In GCP, `gcloud iam service-accounts list` and `gcloud projects get-iam-policy` pode ser empregue para obtain a listing of service accounts and users in a project. `[Ref: Google Cloud - IAM Servie Accounts List API]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Black Hills Red Teaming MS AD Azure, 2018]

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Routinely check user permissions to ensure only the expected users have the ability to list IAM identities or otherwise discover cloud accounts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit permissions to discover cloud accounts in accordance with least privilege. Organizations should limit the number of users within the organization with an IAM role that has privilégios administrativos, strive to reduce all permanent privileged role assignments, and conduct periodic entitlement reviews on IAM users, roles and policies.

techniques.fullNamePt: Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar a connection proxy to direct tráfego de rede between systems or act as an intermediary for network communications to a Command and Control (C2) server to avoid direct connections to their infrastructure. Many tools exist that enable traffic redirection through proxies or port redirection, including **HTRAN** (`S0040`), ZXProxy, and ZXPortMap. `[Ref: Trend Micro APT Attack Tools]` Adversaries use these types of proxies to manage Command and Control (C2) communications, reduce the number of simultaneous outbound network connections, provide resiliency in the face of connection loss, or to ride over existing trusted communications paths between victims to avoid suspicion. Os adversários podem chain together multiple proxies to further disguise the source of malicious traffic.

Adversaries can also take advantage of routing schemes in Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) to proxy Command and Control (C2) traffic.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Traffic to known anonymity networks and C2 infrastructure can be blocked through the use of network allow and block lists. It should be noted that this kind of blocking may be circumvented by other techniques like **Domain Fronting** (`T1090.004`).
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific C2 protocol used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various malware families and versions. Adversaries will likely change tool C2 signatures over time or construct protocols in such a way as para evitar deteção by common defensive tools.  `[Ref: University of Birmingham C2]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: SSL/TLS Inspection
mitigations.descriptionPt: If it is possible to inspect HTTPS traffic, the captures can be analyzed for connections that appear to be domain fronting.

techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar an internal proxy to direct Command and Control (C2) traffic between two or more systems in a compromised environment. Many tools exist that enable traffic redirection through proxies or port redirection, including **HTRAN** (`S0040`), ZXProxy, and ZXPortMap. `[Ref: Trend Micro APT Attack Tools]` Adversaries use internal proxies to manage Command and Control (C2) communications inside a compromised environment, to reduce the number of simultaneous outbound network connections, to provide resiliency in the face of connection loss, or to ride over existing trusted communications paths between infected systems to avoid suspicion. Internal proxy connections may use common peer-to-peer (p2p) networking protocols, such as SMB, to better blend in with the environment.

By using a compromised internal system as a proxy, adversaries may conceal the true destination of C2 traffic while reducing the need for numerous connections to external systems.

Adversaries will likely change tool C2 signatures over time or construct protocols in such a way as para evitar deteção by common defensive tools. `[Ref: University of Birmingham C2]`

techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar an external proxy to act as an intermediary for network communications to a Command and Control (C2) server to avoid direct connections to their infrastructure. Many tools exist that enable traffic redirection through proxies or port redirection, including **HTRAN** (`S0040`), ZXProxy, and ZXPortMap. `[Ref: Trend Micro APT Attack Tools]` Adversaries use these types of proxies to manage Command and Control (C2) communications, to provide resiliency in the face of connection loss, or to ride over existing trusted communications paths to avoid suspicion.

External connection proxies são utilizados para mask the destination of C2 traffic and are typically implemented with port redirectors. Compromised systems outside of the ambiente alvo may be used for these purposes, as well as purchased infrastructure such as cloud-based resources or virtual private servers. Proxies may be chosen based on the low likelihood that a connection to them from a compromised system would be investigated. Victim systems would communicate directly with the external proxy on the Internet and then the proxy would forward communications to the C2 server.

techniques.fullNamePt: Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector: Multi-hop Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem chain together multiple proxies to disguise the source of malicious traffic. Typically, a defender will be able to identify the last proxy traffic traversed before it enters their network; the defender may or may not be able to identify any previous proxies before the last-hop proxy. This technique makes identifying the original source of the malicious traffic even more difficult by requiring the defender to trace malicious traffic through several proxies to identify its source.

Por exemplo, adversaries may construct or use onion routing networks – such as the publicly available **Tor** (`S0183`) network – to transport encrypted C2 traffic through a compromised population, allowing communication with any device within the network. `[Ref: Onion Routing]` Os adversários podem também use operational relay box (ORB) networks composed of virtual private servers (VPS), Internet of Things (IoT) devices, smart devices, and end-of-life routers to obfuscate their operations. `[Ref: ORB Mandiant]` 

In the case of network infrastructure, it is possible for an adversary to leverage multiple compromised devices to create a multi-hop proxy chain (i.e., **Network Devices** (`T1584.008`)). By leveraging **Patch System Image** (`T1601.001`) on routers, adversaries can add custom code to the affected network devices that will implement onion routing between those nodes. This method is dependent upon the **Network Boundary Bridging** (`T1599`) method allowing the adversaries to cross the protected network boundary of the Internet perimeter and into the organization’s Wide-Area Network (WAN).  Protocols such as ICMP may be used as a transport.  

Similarly, adversaries may abuse peer-to-peer (P2P) and blockchain-oriented infrastructure to implement routing between a decentralized network of peers. `[Ref: NGLite Trojan]`

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Traffic to known anonymity networks and C2 infrastructure can be blocked through the use of network allow and block lists. It should be noted that this kind of blocking may be circumvented by other techniques like **Domain Fronting** (`T1090.004`).
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector: Domain Fronting
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem take advantage of routing schemes in Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) and other services which host multiple domains to obfuscate the intended destination of HTTPS traffic or traffic tunneled through HTTPS.  `[Ref: Fifield Blocking Resistent Communication through domain fronting 2015]` Domain fronting involves using different domain names in the SNI field of the TLS header and the Host field of the HTTP header. If both domains are served from the same CDN, then the CDN may route to the address specified in the HTTP header after unwrapping the TLS header. A variation of the the technique, "domainless" fronting, utilizes a SNI field that is left blank; this may allow the fronting to work even when the CDN attempts to validate that the SNI and HTTP Host fields match (if the blank SNI fields are ignored).

Por exemplo, if domain-x and domain-y are customers of the same CDN, it is possible to place domain-x in the TLS header and domain-y in the HTTP header. Traffic will appear to be going to domain-x, however the CDN may route it to domain-y.

techniques.fullNamePt: Replicação via Média Removível
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem mover onto systems, possibly those on disconnected or air-gapped networks, by copying malware to removable media and taking advantage of Autorun features when the media is inserted into a system and executes. In the case of Lateral Movement, this may occur through modification of executable files stored on removable media or by copying malware and renaming it to look like a legitimate file to trick users into executing it on a separate system. In the case of Initial Access, this may occur through manual manipulation of the media, modification of systems used to initially format the media, or modification to the media's firmware itself.

Mobile devices may also be used to infect PCs with malware if connected via USB. `[Ref: Exploiting Smartphone USB ]` This infection may be achieved using devices (Android, iOS, etc.) and, in some instances, USB charging cables. `[Ref: Windows Malware Infecting Android]` `[Ref: iPhone Charging Cable Hack]` Por exemplo, when a smartphone is connected to a system, it may appear to be mounted similar to a USB-connected disk drive. If malware that is compatible with the connected system is on the mobile device, the malware could infect the machine (especially if Autorun features are enabled).

mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable Autorun if it is unnecessary.  `[Ref: Microsoft Disable Autorun]` Disallow or restrict removable media at an organizational policy level if it is not required for business operations.  `[Ref: TechNet Removable Media Control]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Non-Protocolo da Camada de Aplicação
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar an OSI non-application layer protocol for communication between host and C2 server or among infected hosts within a network. The list of possible protocols is extensive. `[Ref: Wikipedia OSI]` Specific examples include use of network layer protocols, such as the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP), transport layer protocols, such as the User Datagram Protocol (UDP), session layer protocols, such as Socket Secure (SOCKS), as well as redirected/tunneled protocols, such as Serial over LAN (SOL).

ICMP communication between hosts is one example. `[Ref: Cisco Synful Knock Evolution]` Because ICMP is part of the Internet Protocol Suite, it is required to be implemented by all IP-compatible hosts. `[Ref: Microsoft ICMP]` Contudo, it is not as commonly monitored as other Internet Protocols such as TCP or UDP and may be used by adversaries to hide communications.

In ESXi environments, adversaries may leverage the Virtual Machine Communication Interface (VMCI) for communication between guest máquina virtual (VM)s and the ESXi host. This traffic is similar to client-server communications on traditional network sockets but is localized to the physical machine running the ESXi host, meaning it does not traverse external networks (routers, switches). This results in communications that are invisible to external monitoring and standard networking tools like tcpdump, netstat, nmap, and Wireshark. By adding a VMCI backdoor to a compromised ESXi host, adversaries may persistently regain access from any guest VM to the compromised ESXi host’s backdoor, regardless of network segmentation or firewall rules in place. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence VMWare ESXi Zero-Day 2023]`

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Periodically investigate ESXi hosts for open VMCI ports. Running the `lsof -A` command and inspecting results with a type of `SOCKET_VMCI` will reveal processes that have open VMCI ports. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence ESXi Hardening 2023]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Filter tráfego de rede to prevent use of protocols através da rede boundary that are unnecessary.  If VMCI is not required in ESXi environments, consider restricting guest máquina virtual (VM)s from accessing VMCI services. `[Ref: Broadcom VMCI Firewall]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Properly configure firewalls and proxies to limit outgoing traffic to only necessary ports and through proper network gateway systems. Also ensure hosts are only provisioned to communicate over authorized interfaces.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

blockers: M1031 (Network Intrusion Prevention): Reverse shell ou beacon C2 não conecta para o exterior; conexões TCP diretas bloqueadas ou terminadas pelo Proxy/Firewall.
M1047 (Audit): Operações de enumeração ou persistência geram alertas imediatos no SOC devido a regras Sigma sobre argumentos de linha de comando.
M1037 (Filter Network Traffic): Movimentação lateral via `PsExec`, `evil-winrm` ou `wmiexec` falha por timeout de porta.
M1030 (Network Segmentation): Sem conectividade direta da sub-rede atual para servidores de produção ou Domain Controllers.
bypasses: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).
blindSpots: **ProcessContextAllowList**: Processes normally allowed to use ICMP/UDP (e.g., ping.exe, DNS resolver).
**ByteTransferAnomalyThreshold**: Suspicion if client sends much more data than it receives (e.g., >90%).
**ProtocolUsageBaseline**: Baseline which protocols are normal per host or segment (ICMP, UDP, etc.).
**RawSocketExecutionPath**: Uncommon programs using raw sockets (e.g., netcat, Python, nmap).
**TimeWindow**: Tunable window for correlating execution with network events (e.g., 2m).

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Contas
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem manipular accounts to maintain and/or elevate access to victim systems. Account manipulation may consist of any action that preserves or modifies adversary access to a compromised account, such as modifying credentials or permission groups. `[Ref: FireEye SMOKEDHAM June 2021]` These actions could also include account activity designed to subvert security policies, such as performing iterative password updates para contornar (bypass) password duration policies and preserve the life of compromised credentials. 

In order to create or manipulate accounts, the adversary must already have sufficient permissions on systems or the domain. Contudo, account manipulation may also lead to privilege escalation where modifications grant access to additional roles, permissions, or higher-privileged **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`).

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar access controls and firewalls to limit access to critical systems and Domain Controller (DC)s. Most cloud environments support separate virtual private cloud (VPC) instances that enable further segmentation of cloud systems.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Remove unnecessary and potentially abusable authentication and authorization mechanisms where possible.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que low-privileged user accounts do not have permissions to modify accounts or account-related policies.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restringir o acesso a potentially sensitive files that deal with authentication and/or authorization.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication for user and privileged accounts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not allow domain administrator accounts to be used for day-to-day operations that may expose them to potential adversaries on unprivileged systems.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Protect Domain Controller (DC)s by ensuring proper security configuration for critical servers to limit access by potentially unnecessary protocols and services, such as SMB file sharing.

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Contas: Additional Cloud Credentials
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem add adversary-controlled credentials to a cloud account to maintain persistent access to victim accounts and instances within the environment.

Por exemplo, adversaries may add credentials for Service Principals and Applications in addition to existing credenciais legítimas in Azure / Entra ID. `[Ref: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance]` `[Ref: Blue Cloud of Death]` `[Ref: Blue Cloud of Death Video]` These credentials include both x509 keys and passwords. `[Ref: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance]` With sufficient permissions, there are a variety of ways to add credentials including the Azure Portal, Azure command line interface, and Azure or Az PowerShell modules. `[Ref: Demystifying Azure AD Service Principals]`

In infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) environments, after gaining access through **Cloud Accounts** (`T1078.004`), adversaries may generate or import their own SSH keys using either the `CreateKeyPair` or `ImportKeyPair` API in AWS or the `gcloud compute os-login ssh-keys add` command in GCP. `[Ref: GCP SSH Key Add]` This allows persistent access to instances within the cloud environment without further usage of the compromised cloud accounts. `[Ref: Expel IO Evil in AWS]` `[Ref: Expel Behind the Scenes]`

Os adversários podem também use the `CreateAccessKey` API in AWS or the `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create` command in GCP to add access keys to an account. Alternatively, they may use the `CreateLoginProfile` API in AWS to add a password that pode ser utilizado para log into the AWS Management Console for **Cloud Service Dashboard** (`T1538`). `[Ref: Permiso Scattered Spider 2023]` `[Ref: Lacework AI Resource Hijacking 2024]` If the target account has different permissions from the requesting account, the adversary may also be able to escalate their privileges in the environment (i.e. **Cloud Accounts** (`T1078.004`)). `[Ref: Rhino Security Labs AWS Privilege Escalation]` `[Ref: Sysdig ScarletEel 2.0]` Por exemplo, in Entra ID environments, an adversary with the Application Administrator role can add a new set of credentials to their application's service principal. In doing so the adversary would be able to access the service principal’s roles and permissions, which may be different from those of the Application Administrator. `[Ref: SpecterOps Azure Privilege Escalation]` 

In AWS environments, adversaries with the appropriate permissions may also use the `sts:GetFederationToken` API call to create a temporary set of credentials to **Forge Web Credentials** (`T1606`) tied to the permissions of the original user account. These temporary credentials may remain valid for the duration of their lifetime even if the original account’s API credentials are deactivated.
 `[Ref: Crowdstrike AWS User Federation Persistence]`

In Entra ID environments with the app password feature enabled, adversaries may be able to add an app password to a user account. `[Ref: Mandiant APT42-untangling]` As app passwords are intended to be used with legacy devices that do not support multi-factor authentication (MFA), adding an app password can allow an adversary para contornar (bypass) MFA requirements. Additionally, app passwords may remain valid even if the user’s primary password is reset. `[Ref: Microsoft Entra ID App Passwords]`

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication for user and privileged accounts. Consider enforcing multi-factor authentication for the `CreateKeyPair` and `ImportKeyPair` API calls through IAM policies. `[Ref: Expel IO Evil in AWS]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que low-privileged user accounts do not have permission to add access keys to accounts. In AWS environments, prohibit users from calling the `sts:GetFederationToken` API unless explicitly required. `[Ref: Crowdstrike AWS User Federation Persistence]`

bypasses: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).
blindSpots: **MFABypassMechanism**: App password or legacy auth activity bypassing MFA policies.
**SourceIPAllowlist**: Expected IPs allowed to perform admin identity operations.
**ApplicationCredentialType**: Track types like `client_secret`, `certificate`, `password`, `federated`.
**CallerIdentityContext**: Track root, federated identities, and STS tokens separately.
**NewCredentialUsageWindow**: Time between key creation and first use (default: 5 min).

techniques.fullNameEn: Account Manipulation: Additional Email Delegate Permissions
techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Contas: Additional Email Delegate Permissions
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem grant additional permission levels to maintain persistent access to an adversary-controlled email account. 

Por exemplo, the `Add-MailboxPermission` **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) cmdlet, available in on-premises Exchange and in the cloud-based service Office 365, adds permissions to a mailbox. `[Ref: Microsoft - Add-MailboxPermission]` `[Ref: FireEye APT35 2018]` `[Ref: Crowdstrike Hiding in Plain Sight 2018]` In Google Workspace, delegation can be enabled via the Google Admin console and users can delegate accounts via their Gmail settings. `[Ref: Gmail Delegation]` `[Ref: Google Ensuring Your Information is Safe]` 

Os adversários podem também assign mailbox folder permissions through individual folder permissions or roles. In Office 365 environments, adversaries may assign the Default or Anonymous user permissions or roles to the Top of Information Store (root), Inbox, or other mailbox folders. By assigning one or both user permissions to a folder, the adversary can utilize any other account in the tenant to maintain persistence to the target user’s mail folders. `[Ref: Mandiant Defend UNC2452 White Paper]`

This may be used in persistent threat incidents as well as BEC (Business Email Compromise) incidents where an adversary can add **Additional Cloud Roles** (`T1098.003`) to the accounts they wish to compromise. This may further enable use of additional techniques for gaining access to systems. Por exemplo, compromised business accounts are often used to send messages to other accounts in the network of the target business while creating inbox rules (ex: **Internal Spearphishing** (`T1534`)), so the messages evade spam/phishing detection mechanisms. `[Ref: Bienstock, D. - Defending O365 - 2019]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Contas: Additional Cloud Roles
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode add additional roles or permissions to an adversary-controlled cloud account to maintain persistent access to a tenant. Por exemplo, adversaries may update IAM policies in cloud-based environments or add a new global administrator in Office 365 environments. `[Ref: AWS IAM Policies and Permissions]` `[Ref: Google Cloud IAM Policies]` `[Ref: Microsoft Support O365 Add Another Admin, October 2019]` `[Ref: Microsoft O365 Admin Roles]` With sufficient permissions, a compromised account can gain almost unlimited access to data and settings (including the ability to reset the passwords of other admins). `[Ref: Expel AWS Attacker]`
 `[Ref: Microsoft O365 Admin Roles]` 

This account modification may immediately follow **Create Account** (`T1136`) or other malicious account activity. Os adversários podem também modify existing **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) that they have compromised. This could lead to privilege escalation, particularly if the roles added allow for lateral movement to additional accounts.

Por exemplo, in AWS environments, an adversary with appropriate permissions may be able to use the `CreatePolicyVersion` API to define a new version of an IAM policy or the `AttachUserPolicy` API to attach an IAM policy with additional or distinct permissions to a compromised user account. `[Ref: Rhino Security Labs AWS Privilege Escalation]`

In some cases, adversaries may add roles to adversary-controlled accounts outside the victim cloud tenant. This allows these external accounts to perform actions inside the victim tenant sem necessitar de the adversary to **Create Account** (`T1136`) or modify a victim-owned account. `[Ref: Invictus IR DangerDev 2024]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Contas: SSH Authorized Keys
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar the SSH `authorized_keys` file to maintain persistence on a victim host. Linux distributions, macOS, and ESXi hypervisors commonly use key-based authentication to secure the processo de autenticação of SSH sessions for remote management. The `authorized_keys` file in SSH specifies the SSH keys that can be used for logging into the user account for which the file is configured. This file is usually found in the user's home directory under `<user-home>/.ssh/authorized_keys` (or, on ESXi, `/etc/ssh/keys-<username>/authorized_keys`). `[Ref: SSH Authorized Keys]` Users may edit the system’s SSH config file to modify the directives `PubkeyAuthentication` and `RSAAuthentication` to the value `yes` to ensure public key and RSA authentication are enabled, as well as modify the directive `PermitRootLogin` to the value `yes` to enable root authentication via SSH. `[Ref: Broadcom ESXi SSH]` The SSH config file is usually located under `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`.

Os adversários podem modificar SSH `authorized_keys` files directly with scripts or shell commands to add their own adversary-supplied public keys. Em ambientes Cloud, adversaries may be able to modify the SSH authorized_keys file of a particular máquina virtual (VM) via the command line interface or rest API. Por exemplo, by using the Google Cloud CLI’s “add-metadata” command an adversary may add SSH keys to a user account. `[Ref: Google Cloud Add Metadata]` `[Ref: Google Cloud Privilege Escalation]` Similarly, in Azure, an adversary may update the authorized_keys file of a máquina virtual (VM) via a PATCH request to the API. `[Ref: Azure Update Virtual Machines]` This ensures that an adversary possessing the corresponding private key may log in as an existing user via SSH. `[Ref: Venafi SSH Key Abuse]` `[Ref: Cybereason Linux Exim Worm]` It may also lead to privilege escalation where the máquina virtual (VM) or instance has distinct permissions from the requesting user.

Where authorized_keys files are modified via cloud APIs or command line interfaces, an adversary may achieve privilege escalation on the target máquina virtual (VM) if they add a key to a higher-privileged user. 

SSH keys can also be added to accounts on network devices, such as with the `ip ssh pubkey-chain` **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) command. `[Ref: cisco_ip_ssh_pubkey_ch_cmd]`

blockers: M1022 (Restrict File and Directory Permissions): Permissão negada ao tentar modificar binários de serviços, chaves de registo ou diretórios de sistema.
M1042 (Disable or Remove Feature or Program): `powershell.exe` bloqueado por GPO, ou Macros VBA desativadas por política de Mark-of-the-Web (MotW).
Controlo de elevação (UAC em Windows / falta de permissões sudo ou SUID em Linux / políticas IAM restritivas em Cloud).
bypasses: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

Enumerar Linux Capabilities (`getcap -r /`), sockets UNIX graváveis (`docker.sock`), timers systemd mal configurados, variáveis `LD_PRELOAD`/`PATH` ou permissões de IAM Role PassRole em ambientes Cloud.
blindSpots: **TimeWindow**: Temporal window to correlate file writes and suspicious process launches (e.g., <60s)
**UserContext**: Expected user-to-process correlation (e.g., root writing to non-root authorized_keys)
**TargetPath**: Custom SSH path or user home variation (e.g., /etc/skel/.ssh/)
**ParentProcess**: Track unusual parent process writing to SSH config (e.g., curl -> bash)
**InteractiveSessionFlag**: Flag whether shell session was interactive (normal) or spawned remotely (potential abuse)

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Contas: Device Registration
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem register a device to an adversary-controlled account. Devices may be registered in a multifactor authentication (MFA) system, which handles authentication to the network, or in a device management system, which handles device access and compliance.

MFA systems, such as Duo or Okta, allow users to associate devices with their accounts com o objetivo de complete MFA requirements. An adversary that compromises a user’s credentials may enroll a new device com o objetivo de bypass initial MFA requirements and gain persistent access to a network. `[Ref: CISA MFA PrintNightmare]` `[Ref: DarkReading FireEye SolarWinds]` In some cases, the MFA self-enrollment process may require only a username and password to enroll the account's first device or to enroll a device to an inactive account.  `[Ref: Mandiant APT29 Microsoft 365 2022]`

Similarly, an adversary with existing access to a network may register a device or a máquina virtual (VM) to Entra ID and/or its device management system, Microsoft Intune, com o objetivo de access dados sensíveis or resources while bypassing conditional access policies. `[Ref: AADInternals - Device Registration]` `[Ref: AADInternals - Conditional Access Bypass]` `[Ref: Microsoft DEV-0537]` `[Ref: Expel Atlas Lion 2025]`

Devices registered in Entra ID may be able to conduct **Internal Spearphishing** (`T1534`) campaigns via intra-organizational emails, which are less likely to be treated as suspicious by the email client. `[Ref: Microsoft - Device Registration]` Additionally, an adversary may be able to perform a **Service Exhaustion Flood** (`T1499.002`) on an Entra ID tenant by registering a large number of devices. `[Ref: AADInternals - BPRT]`

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Require multi-factor authentication to register devices in Entra ID. `[Ref: Microsoft - Device Registration]` Configurar multi-factor authentication systems to disallow enrolling new devices for inactive accounts. `[Ref: CISA MFA PrintNightmare]` When first enrolling MFA, use conditional access policies to restrict device enrollment to trusted locations or devices, and consider using temporary access passes as an initial MFA solution to enroll a device. `[Ref: Mandiant APT29 Microsoft 365 2022]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Account Manipulation: Additional Container Cluster Roles
techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Contas: Additional Container Cluster Roles
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode add additional roles or permissions to an adversary-controlled user or service account to maintain persistent access to a container orchestration system. Por exemplo, an adversary with sufficient permissions may create a RoleBinding or a ClusterRoleBinding to bind a Role or ClusterRole to a Kubernetes account. `[Ref: Kubernetes RBAC]` `[Ref: Aquasec Kubernetes Attack 2023]` Where attribute-based access control (ABAC) is in use, an adversary with sufficient permissions may modify a Kubernetes ABAC policy to give the target account additional permissions. `[Ref: Kuberentes ABAC]`
 
This account modification may immediately follow **Create Account** (`T1136`) or other malicious account activity. Os adversários podem também modify existing **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) that they have compromised.  

Note that where container orchestration systems are deployed in cloud environments, as with Google Kubernetes Engine, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service, and Azure Kubernetes Service, cloud-based  role-based access control (RBAC) assignments or ABAC policies can often be used in place of or in addition to local permission assignments. `[Ref: Google Cloud Kubernetes IAM]` `[Ref: AWS EKS IAM Roles for Service Accounts]` `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Kubernetes Service Service Accounts]` In these cases, this technique may be used in conjunction with **Additional Cloud Roles** (`T1098.003`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Account Manipulation: Additional Local or Domain Groups
techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Contas: Additional Local or Domain Groups
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode add additional local or domain groups to an adversary-controlled account to maintain persistent access to a system or domain.

Em ambientes Windows, accounts may use the `net localgroup` and `net group` commands to add existing users to local and domain groups. `[Ref: Microsoft Net Localgroup]` `[Ref: Microsoft Net Group]` Em sistemas Linux, adversaries may use the `usermod` command for the same purpose. `[Ref: Linux Usermod]`

Por exemplo, accounts may be added to the Administrador Locals group on Windows devices to maintain privilégios elevados. They may also be added to the Remote Desktop Users group, which allows them to leverage **Remote Desktop Protocol** (`T1021.001`) to log into the endpoints in the future. `[Ref: Microsoft RDP Logons]` Os adversários podem também add accounts to VPN user groups to gain future persistence on the network. `[Ref: Cyber Security News]` Em sistemas Linux, accounts may be added to the sudoers group, allowing them to persistently leverage **Sudo and Sudo Caching** (`T1548.003`) for privilégios elevados. 

In Windows environments, machine accounts may also be added to domain groups. This allows the local SYSTEM account to gain privileges on the domain. `[Ref: RootDSE AD Detection 2022]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Comunicação via Web Service
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for relaying data to/from a compromised system. Popular websites, cloud services, and social media acting as a mechanism for C2 may give a significant amount of cover due to the likelihood that hosts within a network are already communicating with them prior to a compromise. Using common services, such as those offered by Google, Microsoft, or Twitter, makes it easier for adversaries to hide in expected noise. `[Ref: Broadcom BirdyClient Microsoft Graph API 2024]` Web service providers commonly use SSL/TLS encryption, giving adversaries an added level of protection.

Use of Web services may also protect back-end C2 infrastructure from discovery through malware binary analysis while also enabling operational resiliency (since this infrastructure may be dynamically changed).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comunicação via Web Service: Dead Drop Resolver
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar an existing, legitimate external Web service to host information that points to additional Command and Control (C2) (C2) infrastructure. Os adversários podem post content, known as a dead drop resolver, on Web services with embedded (and often obfuscated/encoded) domains or IP addresses. Uma vez que infected, victims will reach out to and be redirected by these resolvers. `[Ref: Dead Drop Resolver]`

Popular websites and social media acting as a mechanism for C2 may give a significant amount of cover due to the likelihood that hosts within a network are already communicating with them prior to a compromise. Using common services, such as those offered by Google or Twitter, makes it easier for adversaries to hide in expected noise. Web service providers commonly use SSL/TLS encryption, giving adversaries an added level of protection.

Use of a dead drop resolver may also protect back-end C2 infrastructure from discovery through malware binary analysis while also enabling operational resiliency (since this infrastructure may be dynamically changed).

techniques.fullNamePt: Comunicação via Web Service: Bidirectional Communication
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for sending commands to and receiving output from a compromised system over the Web service channel. Compromised systems may leverage popular websites and social media to host Command and Control (C2) (C2) instructions. Those infected systems can then send the output from those commands back over that Web service channel. The return traffic may occur in a variety of ways, depending on the Web service being utilized. Por exemplo, the return traffic may take the form of the compromised system posting a comment on a forum, issuing a pull request to development project, updating a document hosted on a Web service, or by sending a Tweet. 

Popular websites and social media acting as a mechanism for C2 may give a significant amount of cover due to the likelihood that hosts within a network are already communicating with them prior to a compromise. Using common services, such as those offered by Google or Twitter, makes it easier for adversaries to hide in expected noise. Web service providers commonly use SSL/TLS encryption, giving adversaries an added level of protection.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comunicação via Web Service: One-Way Communication
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for sending commands to a compromised system without receiving return output over the Web service channel. Compromised systems may leverage popular websites and social media to host Command and Control (C2) (C2) instructions. Those infected systems may opt to send the output from those commands back over a different C2 channel, including to another distinct Web service. Alternatively, compromised systems may return no output at all in cases where adversaries want to send instructions to systems and do not want a response.

Popular websites and social media acting as a mechanism for C2 may give a significant amount of cover due to the likelihood that hosts within a network are already communicating with them prior to a compromise. Using common services, such as those offered by Google or Twitter, makes it easier for adversaries to hide in expected noise. Web service providers commonly use SSL/TLS encryption, giving adversaries an added level of protection.

techniques.fullNamePt: Canais Multi-Estágio
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar multiple stages for Command and Control (C2) that are employed under different conditions or for certain functions. Use of multiple stages may obfuscate the Command and Control (C2) channel to make detection more difficult.

Remote access tools will call back to the first-stage Command and Control (C2) server for instructions. The first stage may have automated capabilities to collect basic host information, update tools, and upload additional files. A second remote access tool (RAT) could be uploaded at that point to redirect the host to the second-stage Command and Control (C2) server. The second stage will likely be more fully featured and allow the adversary to interact with the system through a reverse shell and additional RAT features.

The different stages will likely be hosted separately with no overlapping infrastructure. The loader may also have backup first-stage callbacks or **Fallback Channels** (`T1008`) in case the original first-stage communication path is discovered and blocked.

techniques.namePt: Transferência de Ferramentas para o Alvo (Ingress Tool Transfer)
techniques.fullNamePt: Transferência de Ferramentas para o Alvo (Ingress Tool Transfer)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment. Tools or files may be copied from an external adversary-controlled system to the victim network through the Command and Control (C2) channel or through alternate protocols such as **ftp** (`S0095`). Uma vez que present, adversaries may also transfer/spread tools between victim devices within a compromised environment (i.e. **Lateral Tool Transfer** (`T1570`)). 

Em ambientes Windows, adversaries may use various utilities to download tools, such as `copy`, `finger`, **certutil** (`S0160`), and **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) commands such as `IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).downloadString()` and `Invoke-WebRequest`. On Linux and macOS systems, a variety of utilities also exist, such as `curl`, `scp`, `sftp`, `tftp`, `rsync`, `finger`, and `wget`. `[Ref: t1105_lolbas]`  A number of these tools, such as `wget`, `curl`, and `scp`, also exist on ESXi. After downloading a file, a threat actor may attempt to verify its integrity by checking its hash value (e.g., via `certutil -hashfile`). `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence COSCMICENERGY 2023]`

Os adversários podem também abuse installers and package managers, such as `yum` or `winget`, to download tools to victim hosts. Adversaries have also abused file application features, such as the Windows `search-ms` protocol handler, to deliver malicious files to victims through remote file searches invoked by **User Execution** (`T1204`) (typically after interacting with **Phishing** (`T1566`) lures). `[Ref: T1105: Trellix_search-ms]`

Files can also be transferred using various **Web Service** (`T1102`)s as well as native or otherwise present tools on the victim system. `[Ref: PTSecurity Cobalt Dec 2016]` In some cases, adversaries may be able to leverage services that sync between a web-based and an on-premises client, such as Dropbox or OneDrive, to transfer files onto victim systems. Por exemplo, by compromising a cloud account and logging into the service's web portal, an adversary may be able to trigger an automatic syncing process that transfers the file onto the victim's machine. `[Ref: Dropbox Malware Sync]`

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware or unusual data transfer over known protocols like FTP pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific obfuscation technique used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various malware families and versions. Adversaries will likely change tool C2 signatures over time or construct protocols in such a way as para evitar deteção by common defensive tools. `[Ref: University of Birmingham C2]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use network filtering to block outbound traffic from compromised systems to unapproved external destinations. Restricting access to known, trusted IP addresses and protocols can prevent attackers from downloading malicious tools or payloads onto compromised servers after gaining initial access.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução via Native API
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem interact with the native OS application programming interface (API) to execute behaviors. Native APIs provide a controlled means of calling low-level OS services within the kernel, such as those involving hardware/devices, memory, and processes. `[Ref: NT API Windows]` `[Ref: Linux Kernel API]` These native APIs are leveraged by the OS during system boot (when other system components are not yet initialized) as well as carrying out tasks and requests during routine operations.

Os adversários podem abusar de these OS API functions as a means of executing behaviors. De forma semelhante a **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`), the native API and its hierarchy of interfaces provide mechanisms to interact with and utilize various components of a victimized system.

Native API functions (such as `NtCreateProcess`) may be directed invoked via system calls / syscalls, but these features are also often exposed to user-mode applications via interfaces and libraries. `[Ref: OutFlank System Calls]` `[Ref: CyberBit System Calls]` `[Ref: MDSec System Calls]` Por exemplo, functions such as the Windows API `CreateProcess()` or GNU `fork()` will allow programs and scripts to start other processes. `[Ref: Microsoft CreateProcess]` `[Ref: GNU Fork]` This may allow API callers to execute a binary, run a CLI command, load modules, etc. as thousands of similar API functions exist for various system operations. `[Ref: Microsoft Win32]` `[Ref: LIBC]` `[Ref: GLIBC]`

Higher level software frameworks, such as Microsoft .NET and macOS Cocoa, are also available to interact with native APIs. These frameworks typically provide language wrappers/abstractions to API functionalities and are designed for ease-of-use/portability of code. `[Ref: Microsoft NET]` `[Ref: Apple Core Services]` `[Ref: MACOS Cocoa]` `[Ref: macOS Foundation]`

Os adversários podem utilizar assembly to directly or in-directly invoke syscalls in an attempt to subvert defensive sensors and detection signatures such as user mode API-hooks. `[Ref: Redops Syscalls]` Os adversários podem também attempt to tamper with sensors and defensive tools associated with API monitoring, such as unhooking monitored functions via **Disable or Modify Tools** (`T1685`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Identify and block potentially malicious software executed that may be executed through this technique by using application control  `[Ref: Beechey 2010]` tools, like Windows Defender Application Control `[Ref: Microsoft Windows Defender Application Control]`, AppLocker,  `[Ref: Windows Commands JPCERT]`  `[Ref: NSA MS AppLocker]` or Software Restriction Policies  `[Ref: Corio 2008]` where appropriate.  `[Ref: TechNet Applocker vs SRP]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent Office VBA macros from calling Win32 APIs.  `[Ref: win10_asr]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

bypasses: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.
blindSpots: **DllName**: May tune DLL filters to focus on low-level API providers (e.g., ntdll.dll)
**Image**: Tune for expected parent processes (e.g., explorer.exe, winlogon.exe)
**TargetProcess**: Scope to suspicious targets like LSASS, csrss, etc.
**SyscallType**: Filter for fork, mmap, ptrace based on context
**ProcessName**: Whitelist known daemon and scheduled task patterns

techniques.fullNamePt: Força Bruta (Brute Force)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar brute force techniques para obter acesso a accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained. `[Ref: TrendMicro Pawn Storm Dec 2020]` Without knowledge of the password for an account or set of accounts, an adversary may systematically guess the password using a repetitive or iterative mechanism. `[Ref: Dragos Crashoverride 2018]` Brute forcing passwords can take place via interaction with a service that will check the validity of those credentials or offline against previously acquired credential data, such as password hashes.

Brute forcing credentials may take place at various points during a breach. Por exemplo, adversaries may attempt to brute force access to **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) within a ambiente alvo leveraging knowledge gathered from other post-compromise behaviors such as **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`), **Account Discovery** (`T1087`), or **Password Policy Discovery** (`T1201`). Os adversários podem também combine brute forcing activity with behaviors such as **External Remote Services** (`T1133`) as part of Initial Access. 

If an adversary guesses the correct password but fails to login to a compromised account due to location-based conditional access policies, they may change their infrastructure until they match the victim’s location and therefore bypass those policies. `[Ref: ReliaQuest Health Care engenharia social Campaign 2024]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: ReliaQuest Health Care engenharia social Campaign 2024]

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Proactively reset accounts that are known to be part of breached credentials either immediately, or after detecting bruteforce attempts.

mitigations.name: Account Use Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Set account lockout policies after a certain number of failed login attempts to prevent passwords from being guessed. Too strict a policy may create a denial of service condition and render environments un-usable, with all accounts used in the brute force being locked-out. Use conditional access policies to block logins from non-compliant devices or from outside defined organization IP ranges. `[Ref: Microsoft Common Conditional Access Policies]` Consider blocking risky authentication requests, such as those originating from anonymizing services/proxies. `[Ref: Okta Block Anonymizing Services]`

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication. Where possible, also enable multi-factor authentication on externally facing services.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Força Bruta (Brute Force): Password Guessing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries with no prior knowledge of credenciais legítimas within the system or environment may guess passwords to attempt access to accounts. Without knowledge of the password for an account, an adversary may opt to systematically guess the password using a repetitive or iterative mechanism. Um adversário pode guess login credentials without prior knowledge of system or environment passwords during an operation by using a list of common passwords. Password guessing may or may not take into account the target's policies on password complexity or use policies that may lock accounts out after a number of failed attempts.

Guessing passwords can be a risky option because it could cause numerous authentication failures and account lockouts, depending on the organization's login failure policies.  `[Ref: Cylance Cleaver]`

Typically, management services over commonly used ports are used when guessing passwords. Commonly targeted services include the following:

* SSH (22/TCP)
* Telnet (23/TCP)
* FTP (21/TCP)
* NetBIOS / SMB / Samba (139/TCP & 445/TCP)
* LDAP (389/TCP)
* Kerberos (88/TCP)
* RDP / Terminal Services (3389/TCP)
* HTTP/HTTP Management Services (80/TCP & 443/TCP)
* MSSQL (1433/TCP)
* Oracle (1521/TCP)
* MySQL (3306/TCP)
* VNC (5900/TCP)
* SNMP (161/UDP and 162/TCP/UDP)

Adicionalmente a management services, adversaries may "target single sign-on (SSO) and cloud-based applications utilizing federated authentication protocols," as well as externally facing email applications, such as Office 365. `[Ref: US-CERT TA18-068A 2018]`. Further, adversaries may abuse network device interfaces (such as `wlanAPI`) to brute force accessible wifi-router(s) via wireless authentication protocols. `[Ref: Trend Micro Emotet 2020]`

In default environments, LDAP and Kerberos connection attempts are less likely to trigger events over SMB, which creates Windows "logon failure" event ID 4625.

techniques.fullNamePt: Força Bruta (Brute Force): Password Cracking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar password cracking to attempt to recover usable credentials, such as passwords em plaintext, when material de credenciais such as password hashes are obtained. **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`) pode ser utilizado para obtain password hashes, this may only get an adversary so far when **Pass the Hash** (`T1550.002`) is not an option. Further,  adversaries may leverage **Data from Configuration Repository** (`T1602`) com o objetivo de obtain hashed credentials for network devices. `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` 

Techniques to systematically guess the passwords used to compute hashes are available, or the adversary may use a pre-computed rainbow table to crack hashes. Cracking hashes is usually done on adversary-controlled systems outside of the rede alvo. `[Ref: Wikipedia Password cracking]` The resulting plaintext password resulting from a successfully cracked hash pode ser empregue para log into systems, resources, and services in which the account has access.

techniques.fullNamePt: Força Bruta (Brute Force): Password Spraying
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to attempt to acquire valid account credentials. Password spraying uses one password (e.g. 'Password01'), or a small list of commonly used passwords, that may match the complexity policy of the domain. Logins are attempted with that password against many different accounts on a network to avoid account lockouts that would normally occur when brute forcing a single account with many passwords.  `[Ref: BlackHillsInfosec Password Spraying]`

Typically, management services over commonly used ports are used when password spraying. Commonly targeted services include the following:

* SSH (22/TCP)
* Telnet (23/TCP)
* FTP (21/TCP)
* NetBIOS / SMB / Samba (139/TCP & 445/TCP)
* LDAP (389/TCP)
* Kerberos (88/TCP)
* RDP / Terminal Services (3389/TCP)
* HTTP/HTTP Management Services (80/TCP & 443/TCP)
* MSSQL (1433/TCP)
* Oracle (1521/TCP)
* MySQL (3306/TCP)
* VNC (5900/TCP)

Adicionalmente a management services, adversaries may "target single sign-on (SSO) and cloud-based applications utilizing federated authentication protocols," as well as externally facing email applications, such as Office 365. `[Ref: US-CERT TA18-068A 2018]`

In order para evitar deteção thresholds, adversaries may deliberately throttle password spraying attempts to avoid triggering security alerting. Additionally, adversaries may leverage LDAP and Kerberos authentication attempts, which are less likely to trigger high-visibility events such as Windows "logon failure" event ID 4625 that is commonly triggered by failed SMB connection attempts. `[Ref: Microsoft Storm-0940]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Força Bruta (Brute Force): Credential Stuffing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar credentials obtained from breach dumps of unrelated accounts para obter acesso a target accounts through credential overlap. Occasionally, large numbers of username and password pairs are dumped online when a website or service is compromised and the user account credentials accessed. The information may be useful to an adversary attempting to compromise accounts by taking advantage of the tendency for users to use the same passwords across personal and business accounts.

Credential stuffing is a risky option because it could cause numerous authentication failures and account lockouts, depending on the organization's login failure policies.

Typically, management services over commonly used ports are used when stuffing credentials. Commonly targeted services include the following:

* SSH (22/TCP)
* Telnet (23/TCP)
* FTP (21/TCP)
* NetBIOS / SMB / Samba (139/TCP & 445/TCP)
* LDAP (389/TCP)
* Kerberos (88/TCP)
* RDP / Terminal Services (3389/TCP)
* HTTP/HTTP Management Services (80/TCP & 443/TCP)
* MSSQL (1433/TCP)
* Oracle (1521/TCP)
* MySQL (3306/TCP)
* VNC (5900/TCP)

Adicionalmente a management services, adversaries may "target single sign-on (SSO) and cloud-based applications utilizing federated authentication protocols," as well as externally facing email applications, such as Office 365. `[Ref: US-CERT TA18-068A 2018]`
