techniques.fullNamePt: Interceção de Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem target multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanisms, (i.e., smart cards, token generators, etc.) para obter acesso a credentials that pode ser utilizado para access systems, services, and network resources. Use of MFA is recommended and provides a higher level of security than usernames and passwords alone, but organizations should be aware of techniques that could be used to intercept and bypass these security mechanisms. 

If a smart card is used for multi-factor authentication, then a keylogger will need to be used to obtain the password associated with a smart card during normal use. With both an inserted card and access to the smart card password, an adversary can connect to a network resource using the infected system to proxy the authentication with the inserted hardware token.  `[Ref: Mandiant M Trends 2011]`

Os adversários podem também employ a keylogger to similarly target other hardware tokens, such as RSA SecurID. Capturing token input (including a user's personal identification code) may provide temporary access (i.e. replay the one-time passcode until the next value rollover) as well as possibly enabling adversaries to reliably predict future authentication values (given access to both the algorithm and any seed values used to generate appended temporary codes).  `[Ref: GCN RSA June 2011]`

Other methods of MFA may be intercepted and used by an adversary to authenticate. It is common for one-time codes to be sent via out-of-band communications (email, SMS). If the device and/or service is not secured, then it may be vulnerable to interception. Service providers can also be targeted: for example, an adversary may compromise an SMS messaging service com o objetivo de steal MFA codes sent to users’ phones. `[Ref: Okta Scatter Swine 2022]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Registry
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem interact with the Windows Registry as part of a variety of other techniques to aid in defense evasion, persistence, and execution.

Access to specific areas of the Registry depends on account permissions, with some keys requiring administrator-level access. The built-in Windows command-line utility **Reg** (`S0075`) may be used for local or remote Registry modification. `[Ref: Microsoft Reg]` Other tools, such as remote access tools, may also contain functionality to interact with the Registry through the Windows API.

The Registry may be modified com o objetivo de hide configuration information or malicious payloads via **Obfuscated Files or Information** (`T1027`). `[Ref: Unit42 BabyShark Feb 2019]` `[Ref: Avaddon Ransomware 2021]` `[Ref: Microsoft BlackCat Jun 2022]` `[Ref: CISA Russian Gov Critical Infra 2018]` The Registry may also be modified to impair defenses, such as by enabling macros for all Microsoft Office products, allowing privilege escalation without alerting the user, increasing the maximum number of allowed outbound requests, and/or modifying systems to store plaintext credentials in memory. `[Ref: CISA LockBit 2023]` `[Ref: Unit42 BabyShark Feb 2019]`

The Registry of a remote system may be modified to aid in execution of files as part of lateral movement. It requires the remote Registry service to be running no sistema alvo. `[Ref: Microsoft Remote]` Often **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) are required, along with access to the remote system's **SMB/Windows Admin Shares** (`T1021.002`) for RPC communication.

Finally, Registry modifications may also include actions to hide keys, such as prepending key names with a null character, which will cause an error and/or be ignored when read via **Reg** (`S0075`) or other utilities using the Win32 API. `[Ref: Microsoft Reghide NOV 2006]` Os adversários podem abusar de these pseudo-hidden keys to conceal payloads/commands used to maintain persistence. `[Ref: TrendMicro POWELIKS AUG 2014]` `[Ref: SpectorOps Hiding Reg Jul 2017]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Recolha de E-mails: Local Recolha de E-mails
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem target user email on local systems to collect informação sensível. Files containing email data can be acquired from a user’s local system, such as Outlook storage or cache files.

Outlook stores data locally in offline data files with an extension of .ost. Outlook 2010 and later supports .ost file sizes up to 50GB, while earlier versions of Outlook support up to 20GB. `[Ref: Outlook File Sizes]` IMAP accounts in Outlook 2013 (and earlier) and POP accounts use Outlook Data Files (.pst) as opposed to .ost, whereas IMAP accounts in Outlook 2016 (and later) use .ost files. Both types of Outlook data files are typically stored in `C:\Users\<username>\Documents\Outlook Files` or `C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook`. `[Ref: Microsoft Outlook Files]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Recolha de E-mails: Email Forwarding Rule
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem setup email forwarding rules to collect informação sensível. Os adversários podem abusar de email forwarding rules to monitor the activities of a victim, steal information, and further gain intelligence on the victim or the victim’s organization to use as part of further exploits or operations. `[Ref: US-CERT TA18-068A 2018]` Ademais, email forwarding rules can allow adversaries to maintain persistent access to victim's emails even after compromised credentials are reset by administrators. `[Ref: Pfammatter - Hidden Inbox Rules]` Most email clients allow users to create inbox rules for various email functions, including forwarding to a different recipient. These rules may be created through a local email application, a web interface, or by interface de linha de comandos (CLI). Messages can be forwarded to internal or external recipients, and there are no restrictions limiting the extent of this rule. Administrators may also create forwarding rules for user accounts with the same considerations and outcomes. `[Ref: Microsoft Tim McMichael Exchange Mail Forwarding 2]` `[Ref: Mac Forwarding Rules]`

Any user or administrator within the organization (or adversary with valid credentials) can create rules to automatically forward all received messages to another recipient, forward emails to different locations based on the sender, and more. Os adversários podem também hide the rule by making use of the Microsoft Messaging API (MAPI) to modify the rule properties, making it hidden and not visible from Outlook, OWA or most Exchange Administration tools. `[Ref: Pfammatter - Hidden Inbox Rules]`

In some environments, administrators may be able to enable email forwarding rules that operate organization-wide rather than on individual inboxes. Por exemplo, Microsoft Exchange supports transport rules that evaluate all mail an organization receives against user-specified conditions, then performs a user-specified action on mail that adheres to those conditions. `[Ref: Microsoft Mail Flow Rules 2023]` Adversaries that abuse such features may be able to enable forwarding on all or specific mail an organization receives.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use of encryption provides an added layer of security to informação sensível sent over email. Encryption using public key cryptography requires the adversary to obtain the private certificate along with an encryption key to decrypt messages.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Enterprise email solutions have monitoring mechanisms that may include the ability to audit auto-forwarding rules on a regular basis.

In an Exchange environment, Administrators can use `Get-InboxRule` / `Remove-InboxRule` and `Get-TransportRule` / `Remove-TransportRule` to discover and remove potentially malicious auto-fowarding and transport rules. `[Ref: Microsoft Tim McMichael Exchange Mail Forwarding 2]` `[Ref: Microsoft Manage Mail Flow Rules 2023]` `[Ref: Microsoft Get-InboxRule]` Adicionalmente a this, a MAPI Editor can be utilized to examine the underlying database structure and discover any modifications/tampering of the properties of auto-forwarding rules. `[Ref: Pfammatter - Hidden Inbox Rules]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Out-of-Band Communications Channel
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Use secure out-of-band authentication methods to verify the authenticity of critical actions initiated via email, such as password resets, financial transactions, or access requests. 

For highly informação sensível, utilize out-of-band communication channels instead of relying solely on email. This reduces the risk of dados sensíveis being collected through compromised email accounts.

Set up out-of-band alerts to notify security teams of unusual email activities, such as mass forwarding or large attachments being sent, which could indicate email collection attempts.

Create plans for leveraging a secure out-of-band communications channel, rather than an existing in-network email server, in case of a security incident. `[Ref: TrustedSec OOB Communications]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Clipboard Data
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem recolher data stored in the clipboard from users copying information within or between applications. 

Por exemplo, on Windows adversaries can access clipboard data by using `clip.exe` or `Get-Clipboard`. `[Ref: MSDN Clipboard]` `[Ref: clip_win_server]` `[Ref: CISA_AA21_200B]` Additionally, adversaries may monitor then replace users’ clipboard with their data (e.g., **Transmitted Data Manipulation** (`T1565.002`)). `[Ref: mining_ruby_reversinglabs]`

macOS and Linux also have commands, such as `pbpaste`, to grab clipboard contents. `[Ref: Operating with EmPyre]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Recolha Automatizada
techniques.descriptionPt:
Uma vez que established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data. Methods for performing this technique could include use of a **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`) to search for and copy information fitting set criteria such as file type, location, or name at specific time intervals. 

In cloud-based environments, adversaries may also use cloud APIs, data pipelines, command line interfaces, or extract, transform, and load (ETL) services to automatically collect data. `[Ref: Mandiant UNC3944 SMS Phishing 2023]` 

This functionality could also be built into remote access tools. 

This technique may incorporate use of other techniques such as **File and Directory Discovery** (`T1083`) and **Lateral Tool Transfer** (`T1570`) to identify and move files, as well as **Cloud Service Dashboard** (`T1538`) and **Cloud Storage Object Discovery** (`T1619`) to identify resources in cloud environments.

mitigations.name: Remote Data Storage
mitigations.descriptionPt: Encryption and off-system storage of informação sensível may be one way to mitigate collection of files, but may not stop an adversary from acquiring the information if an intrusion persists over a long period of time and the adversary is able to discover and access the data through other means.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Encryption and off-system storage of informação sensível may be one way to mitigate collection of files, but may not stop an adversary from acquiring the information if an intrusion persists over a long period of time and the adversary is able to discover and access the data through other means. Strong passwords should be used on certain encrypted documents that use them to prevent offline cracking through **Brute Force** (`T1110`) techniques.

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Hora do Sistema
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode gather the system time and/or time zone settings from a local or remote system. The system time is set and stored by services, such as the Windows Time Service on Windows or `systemsetup` on macOS. `[Ref: MSDN System Time]` `[Ref: Technet Windows Time Service]` `[Ref: systemsetup mac time]` These time settings may also be synchronized between systems and services in an enterprise network, typically accomplished with a network time server within a domain. `[Ref: Mac Time Sync]` `[Ref: linux system time]`

System time information may be gathered in a number of ways, such as with **Net** (`S0039`) on Windows by performing `net time \\hostname` to gather the system time on a remote system. The victim's time zone may also be inferred from the current system time or gathered by using `w32tm /tz`. `[Ref: Technet Windows Time Service]` Além disso, adversaries can discover device uptime through functions such as `GetTickCount()` to determine how long it has been since the system booted up. `[Ref: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion]`

On network devices, **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) commands such as `show clock detail` pode ser utilizado para see the current time configuration. `[Ref: show_clock_detail_cisco_cmd]` On ESXi servers, `esxcli system clock get` can be used for the same purpose.

Além disso, system calls – such as `time()` – have been used to collect the current time on Linux devices. `[Ref: MAGNET GOBLIN]` On macOS systems, adversaries may use commands such as `systemsetup -gettimezone` or `timeIntervalSinceNow` to gather current time zone information or current date and time. `[Ref: System Information Discovery Technique]` `[Ref: ESET DazzleSpy Jan 2022]`

This information could be useful for performing other techniques, such as executing a file with a **Scheduled Task/Job** (`T1053`) `[Ref: RSA EU12 They're Inside]`, or to discover locality information based on time zone to assist in victim targeting (i.e. **System Location Discovery** (`T1614`)). Os adversários podem também use knowledge of system time as part of a time bomb, or delaying execution until a specified date/time. `[Ref: AnyRun TimeBomb]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Video Capture
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário consegue leverage a computer's peripheral devices (e.g., integrated cameras or webcams) or applications (e.g., video call services) to capture video recordings for the purpose of gathering information. Images may also be captured from devices or applications, potentially in specified intervals, in lieu of video files.

Malware or scripts pode ser empregue para interact with the devices through an available API provided by the sistema operativo or an application to capture video or images. Video or image files may be written to disk and exfiltrated later. This technique differs from **Screen Capture** (`T1113`) due to use of specific devices or applications for video recording rather than capturing the victim's screen.

In macOS, there are a few different malware samples that record the user's webcam such as FruitFly and Proton.  `[Ref: objective-see 2017 review]`

techniques.namePt: Trusted Developer Utilities Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution
techniques.fullNamePt: Trusted Developer Utilities Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem take advantage of trusted developer utilities to proxy execution of malicious payloads. There are many utilities used for software development related tasks that pode ser utilizado para execute code in various forms to assist in development, debugging, and reverse engineering. `[Ref: engima0x3 DNX Bypass]` `[Ref: engima0x3 RCSI Bypass]` `[Ref: Exploit Monday WinDbg]` `[Ref: LOLBAS Tracker]` These utilities may often be signed with legitimate certificates that allow them to execute on a system and proxy execution of código malicioso through a trusted process that effectively bypasses application control solutions.

Smart App Control is a feature of Windows that blocks applications it considers potentially malicious from running by verifying unsigned applications against a known safe list from a Microsoft cloud service before executing them. `[Ref: Microsoft Smart App Control]` Contudo, adversaries may leverage "reputation hijacking" to abuse an sistema operativo’s trust of safe, signed applications that support the execution of código arbitrário. By leveraging **Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution** (`T1127`) to run their código malicioso, adversaries may bypass Smart App Control protections. `[Ref: Elastic Security Labs]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Certain developer utilities should be blocked or restricted if not required.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling software installation or execution from the internet via developer utilities.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Specific developer utilities may not be necessary within a given environment and should be removed if not used.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution: MSBuild
techniques.fullNamePt: Trusted Developer Utilities Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: MSBuild
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar MSBuild to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility. MSBuild.exe (Microsoft Build Engine) is a software build platform used by Visual Studio. It handles XML formatted project files that define requirements for loading and building various platforms and configurations. `[Ref: MSDN MSBuild]`

Adversaries can abuse MSBuild to proxy execution of código malicioso. The inline task capability of MSBuild that was introduced in .NET version 4 allows for C# or Visual Basic code to be inserted into an XML project file. `[Ref: MSDN MSBuild]` `[Ref: Microsoft MSBuild Inline Tasks 2017]` MSBuild will compile and execute the inline task. MSBuild.exe is a signed Microsoft binary, so when it is used this way it can execute código arbitrário and bypass application control defenses that are configured to allow MSBuild.exe execution. `[Ref: LOLBAS Msbuild]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

techniques.fullNameEn: Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution: ClickOnce
techniques.fullNamePt: Trusted Developer Utilities Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: ClickOnce
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar ClickUma vez que applications (.appref-ms and .application files) to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility. `[Ref: Burke/CISA ClickUma vez que BlackHat]` ClickUma vez que is a deployment that enables a user to create self-updating Windows-based .NET applications (i.e, .XBAP, .EXE, or .DLL) that install and run from a file share or web page with minimal user interaction. The application launches as a child process of DFSVC.EXE, which is responsible for installing, launching, and updating the application. `[Ref: SpectorOps Medium ClickOnce]`

Because ClickUma vez que applications receive only limited permissions, they do not require administrative permissions to install. `[Ref: Microsoft Learn ClickOnce]` As such, adversaries may abuse ClickUma vez que to proxy execution of código malicioso without needing para escalar privilégios.

ClickUma vez que may be abused in a number of ways. Por exemplo, an adversary may rely on **User Execution** (`T1204`). When a user visits a malicious website, the .NET malware is disguised as legitimate software and a ClickUma vez que popup is displayed for installation. `[Ref: NetSPI ClickOnce]`

Os adversários podem também abuse ClickUma vez que to execute malware via a **Rundll32** (`T1218.011`) script using the command `rundll32.exe dfshim.dll,ShOpenVerbApplication1`. `[Ref: LOLBAS /Dfsvc.exe]`

Additionally, an adversary can move the ClickUma vez que application file to a remote user’s startup folder for continued código malicioso deployment (i.e., **Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder** (`T1547.001`)). `[Ref: Burke/CISA ClickUma vez que BlackHat]` `[Ref: Burke/CISA ClickUma vez que Paper]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Disable ClickUma vez que installations from the internet using the following registry key: 
`\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\.NETFramework\Security\TrustManager\PromptingLevel — Internet:Disabled` `[Ref: NetSPI ClickOnce]` `[Ref: Microsoft Learn ClickUma vez que Config]`

ClickUma vez que may not be necessary dentro do ambiente alvo and should be disabled if not being used.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Disable ClickUma vez que installations from the internet using the following registry key: 
`\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\.NETFramework\Security\TrustManager\PromptingLevel — Internet:Disabled` `[Ref: NetSPI ClickOnce]`

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de binary and application integrity with digital signature verification to prevent untrusted code from executing. `[Ref: Microsoft Learn ClickUma vez que and Authenticode]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Recorrer a DLL Side-Loading (`T1574.002`) utilizando um executável legítimo assinado (vulnerável a sequestro de ordem de procura de DLL) que carregue a nossa DLL em memória, ou utilizar binários assinados nativos (LOLBAS - `T1218`). Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar `JamPlus` to proxy the execution of a malicious script. `JamPlus` is a build utility tool for code and data build systems. It works with several popular compilers and can be used for generating workspaces in code editors such as Visual Studio. `[Ref: JamPlus manual]`

Os adversários podem abusar de the `JamPlus` build utility para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos scripts via a `.jam` file, which describes the build process and required dependencies. Because the malicious script is executed from a reputable developer tool, it may subvert application control security systems such as Smart App Control. `[Ref: Cyble]` `[Ref: Elastic Security Labs]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Shared Modules
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar malicious payloads via loading shared modules. Shared modules are executable files that are loaded into processes to provide access to reusable code, such as specific custom functions or invoking OS API functions (i.e., **Native API** (`T1106`)).

Os adversários podem utilizar this functionality as a way to execute arbitrary payloads on a victim system. Por exemplo, adversaries can modularize functionality of their malware into shared objects that perform various functions such as managing C2 network communications or execution of specific actions on objective.

The Linux & macOS module loader can load and execute shared objects from arbitrary local paths. This functionality resides in `dlfcn.h` in functions such as `dlopen` and `dlsym`. Although macOS can execute `.so` files, common practice uses `.dylib` files. `[Ref: Apple Dev Dynamic Libraries]` `[Ref: Linux Shared Libraries]` `[Ref: RotaJakiro 2021 netlab360 analysis]` `[Ref: Unit42 OceanLotus 2017]`

The Windows module loader can be instructed to load DLLs from arbitrary local paths and arbitrary Universal Naming Convention (UNC) network paths. This functionality resides in `NTDLL.dll` and is part of the Windows **Native API** (`T1106`) which is called from functions like `LoadLibrary` at run time. `[Ref: Microsoft DLL]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Identify and block potentially malicious software executed through this technique by using application control tools capable of preventing unknown modules from being loaded.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

blockers: M1038 (Execution Prevention): Erro "This program is blocked by group policy" ao tentar executar binários em `C:\Users\*` ou `C:\Windows\Temp`.
bypasses: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.
blindSpots: **TimeWindow**: Correlation window between file write → module load → network (e.g., 0–20 minutes).
**SuspiciousPathRegex**: Regex for user-writable/UNC/temp paths to flag (e.g., %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, \\*\share\).

**RareSignerThreshold**: Frequency threshold for unseen/rare signers in last N days.
**MinFileSizeKB**: Ignore tiny DLL stubs to cut noise.

techniques.fullNamePt: Codificação de Dados (Data Encoding)
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem encode data to make the content of Command and Control (C2) traffic more difficult to detect. Command and Control (C2) (C2) information can be encoded using a standard data encoding system. Use of data encoding may adhere to existing protocol specifications and includes use of ASCII, Unicode, Base64, MIME, or other binary-to-text and character encoding systems. `[Ref: Wikipedia Binary-to-text Encoding]` `[Ref: Wikipedia Character Encoding]` Some data encoding systems may also result in data compression, such as gzip.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific obfuscation technique used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various malware families and versions. Adversaries will likely change tool C2 signatures over time or construct protocols in such a way as para evitar deteção by common defensive tools.  `[Ref: University of Birmingham C2]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

techniques.fullNamePt: Serviços de Acesso Remoto Externo
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de external-facing remote services to initially access and/or persist within a network. Remote services such as VPNs, Citrix, and other access mechanisms allow users to connect to internal enterprise network resources from external locations. There are often remote service gateways that manage connections and credential authentication for these services. Services such as **Windows Remote Management** (`T1021.006`) and **VNC** (`T1021.005`) can also be used externally. `[Ref: MacOS VNC software for Remote Desktop]`

Access to **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) to use the service is often a requirement, which could be obtained through credential pharming or by obtaining the credentials from users after compromising the enterprise network. `[Ref: Volexity Virtual Private Keylogging]` Access to remote services may be used as a redundant or persistent access mechanism during an operation.

Access may also be gained through an exposed service that doesn’t require authentication. In containerized environments, this may include an exposed Docker API, Kubernetes API server, kubelet, or web application such as the Kubernetes dashboard. `[Ref: Trend Micro Exposed Docker Server]` `[Ref: Unit 42 Hildegard Malware]`

Os adversários podem também establish persistence on network by configuring a Tor hidden service num sistema comprometido. Os adversários podem utilize the tool `ShadowLink` to facilitate the installation and configuration of the Tor hidden service. Tor hidden service is then accessible via the Tor network because `ShadowLink` sets up a .onion address on the compromised system. `ShadowLink` pode ser empregue para forward any inbound connections to RDP, allowing the adversaries to have remote access. `[Ref: The BadPilot campaign]` Os adversários podem get `ShadowLink` to persist on a system by masquerading it as an MS Defender application. `[Ref: Russian threat actors dig in, prepare to seize on war fatigue]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Access Token
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar access tokens to operate under a different user or system security context to perform actions and bypass access controls. Windows uses access tokens to determine the ownership of a running process. A user can manipulate access tokens to make a running process appear as though it is the child of a different process or belongs to someone other than the user that started the process. When this occurs, the process also takes on the security context associated with the new token.

Um adversário consegue use built-in Windows API functions to copy access tokens from existing processes; this is known as token stealing. These token can then be applied to an existing process (i.e. **Token Impersonation/Theft** (`T1134.001`)) or used to spawn a new process (i.e. **Create Process with Token** (`T1134.002`)). An adversary must already be in a privileged user context (i.e. administrator) to steal a token. Contudo, adversaries commonly use token stealing to elevate their security context from the administrator level to the SYSTEM level. Um adversário consegue then use a token to authenticate to a remote system as the account for that token if the account has appropriate permissions on the remote system. `[Ref: Pentestlab Token Manipulation]`

Any standard user can use the `runas` command, and the Windows API functions, to create impersonation tokens; it does not require access to an administrator account. There are also other mechanisms, such as Active Directory (AD) fields, that pode ser utilizado para modify access tokens.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: An adversary must already have administrator level access on the local system to make full use of this technique; be sure to restrict users and accounts to the least privileges they require.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Limit permissions so that users and user groups cannot create tokens. This setting should be defined for the local system account only. GPO: Computer Configuration > [Policies] > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment: Create a token object.  `[Ref: Microsoft Create Token]` Also define who can create a process level token to only the local and network service through GPO: Computer Configuration > [Policies] > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment: Replace a process level token. `[Ref: Microsoft Replace Process Token]`

Administrators should log in as a standard user but run their tools with administrator privileges using the built-in access token manipulation command `runas`. `[Ref: Microsoft runas]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Access Token: Token Impersonation/Theft
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem duplicate then impersonate another user's existing token para escalar privilégios and bypass access controls. Por exemplo, an adversary can duplicate an existing token using `DuplicateToken` or `DuplicateTokenEx`. `[Ref: DuplicateToken function]` The token can then be used with `ImpersonateLoggedOnUser` to allow the calling thread to impersonate a logged on user's security context, or with `SetThreadToken` to assign the impersonated token to a thread.

Um adversário pode perform **Token Impersonation/Theft** (`T1134.001`) when they have a specific, existing process they want to assign the duplicated token to. Por exemplo, this may be useful for when the target user has a non-network logon session on the system.

When an adversary would instead use a duplicated token to create a new process rather than attaching to an existing process, they can additionally **Create Process with Token** (`T1134.002`) using `CreateProcessWithTokenW` or `CreateProcessAsUserW`. **Token Impersonation/Theft** (`T1134.001`) is also distinct from **Make and Impersonate Token** (`T1134.003`) in that it refers to duplicating an existing token, rather than creating a new one.

techniques.fullNameEn: Access Token Manipulation: Create Process with Token
techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Access Token: Create Process with Token
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar a new process with an existing token para escalar privilégios and bypass access controls. Processes can be created with the token and resulting security context of another user using features such as `CreateProcessWithTokenW` and `runas`. `[Ref: Microsoft RunAs]`

Creating processes with a token not associated with the current user may require the credentials of the target user, specific privileges to impersonate that user, or access to the token to be used. Por exemplo, the token could be duplicated via **Token Impersonation/Theft** (`T1134.001`) or created via **Make and Impersonate Token** (`T1134.003`) before being used to create a process.

While this technique is distinct from **Token Impersonation/Theft** (`T1134.001`), the techniques can be used in conjunction where a token is duplicated and then used to create a new process.

techniques.fullNameEn: Access Token Manipulation: Make and Impersonate Token
techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Access Token: Make and Impersonate Token
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem make new tokens and impersonate users para escalar privilégios and bypass access controls. Por exemplo, if an adversary has a username and password but the user is not logged onto the system the adversary can then create a logon session for the user using the `LogonUser` function. `[Ref: LogonUserW function]` The function will return a copy of the new session's access token and the adversary can use `SetThreadToken` to assign the token to a thread.

techniques.fullNameEn: Access Token Manipulation: Parent PID Spoofing
techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Access Token: Parent PID Spoofing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem falsificar (spoof) the parent process identifier (PPID) of a new process to evade process-monitoring defenses or to elevate privileges. New processes are typically spawned directly from their parent, or calling, process unless explicitly specified. One way of explicitly assigning the PPID of a new process is via the `CreateProcess` API call, which supports a parameter that defines the PPID to use. `[Ref: DidierStevens SelectMyParent Nov 2009]` This functionality is used by Windows features such as User Account Control (UAC) to correctly set the PPID after a requested elevated process is spawned by SYSTEM (typically via `svchost.exe` or `consent.exe`) rather than the current user context. `[Ref: Microsoft UAC Nov 2018]`

Os adversários podem abusar de these mechanisms to evade defenses, such as those blocking processes spawning directly from Office documents, and analysis targeting unusual/potentially malicious parent-child process relationships, such as spoofing the PPID of **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`)/**Rundll32** (`T1218.011`) to be `explorer.exe` rather than an Office document delivered as part of **Spearphishing Attachment** (`T1566.001`). `[Ref: CounterCept PPID Spoofing Dec 2018]` This spoofing could be executed via **Visual Basic** (`T1059.005`) within a malicious Office document or any code that can perform **Native API** (`T1106`). `[Ref: CTD PPID Spoofing Macro Mar 2019]` `[Ref: CounterCept PPID Spoofing Dec 2018]`

Explicitly assigning the PPID may also enable privilégios elevados given appropriate access rights to the parent process. Por exemplo, an adversary in a privileged user context (i.e. administrator) may spawn a new process and assign the parent as a process running as SYSTEM (such as `lsass.exe`), causing the new process to be elevated via the inherited access token. `[Ref: XPNSec PPID Nov 2017]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Access Token: SID-History Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar SID-History Injection para escalar privilégios and bypass access controls. The Windows security identifier (SID) is a unique value that identifies a user or group account. SIDs are used by Windows security in both security descriptors and access tokens.  `[Ref: Microsoft SID]` An account can hold additional SIDs in the SID-History Active Directory (AD) attribute  `[Ref: Microsoft SID-History Attribute]`, allowing inter-operable account migration between domains (e.g., all values in SID-History are included in access tokens).

With Domain Administrator (or equivalent) rights, harvested or well-known SID values  `[Ref: Microsoft Well Known SIDs Jun 2017]` may be inserted into SID-History to enable impersonation of arbitrary users/groups such as Enterprise Administrators. This manipulation may result in elevated access to local resources and/or access to otherwise inaccessible domains via lateral movement techniques such as **Remote Services** (`T1021`), **SMB/Windows Admin Shares** (`T1021.002`), or **Windows Remote Management** (`T1021.006`).

mitigations.name: Active Directory Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Clean up SID-History attributes after legitimate account migration is complete.

Consider applying SID Filtering to interforest trusts, such as forest trusts and external trusts, to exclude SID-History from requests to access domain resources. SID Filtering ensures that any authentication requests over a trust only contain SIDs of security principals from the trusted domain (i.e preventing the trusted domain from claiming a user has membership in groups outside of the domain).

SID Filtering of forest trusts is enabled by default, but may have been disabled in some cases to allow a child domain to transitively access forest trusts. SID Filtering of external trusts is automatically enabled on all created external trusts using Server 2003 or later Domain Controller (DC)s.  `[Ref: Microsoft Trust Considerations Nov 2014]`  `[Ref: Microsoft SID Filtering Quarantining Jan 2009]` However note that SID Filtering is not automatically applied to legacy trusts or may have been deliberately disabled to allow inter-domain access to resources.

SID Filtering can be applied by:  `[Ref: Microsoft Netdom Trust Sept 2012]`

* Disabling SIDHistory on forest trusts using the netdom tool (`netdom trust /domain: /EnableSIDHistory:no` on the Domain Controller (DC))

* Applying SID Filter Quarantining to external trusts using the netdom tool (`netdom trust <TrustingDomainName> /domain:<TrustedDomainName> /quarantine:yes` on the Domain Controller (DC))

* Applying SID Filtering to domain trusts within a single forest is not recommended as it is an unsupported configuration and can cause breaking changes.  `[Ref: Microsoft Netdom Trust Sept 2012]`  `[Ref: AdSecurity Kerberos GT Aug 2015]` If a domain within a forest is untrustworthy then it should not be a member of the forest. In this situation it is necessary to first split the trusted and untrusted domains into separate forests where SID Filtering can be applied to an interforest trust

techniques.namePt: Descoberta de Partilhas de Rede (Network Shares)
techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Partilhas de Rede (Network Shares)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem look for folders and drives shared on sistemas remotos as a means of identifying sources of information to gather as a precursor for Collection and to identify potential systems of interest for Lateral Movement. Networks often contain shared network drives and folders that enable users to access file directories on various systems across a network. 

File sharing over a Windows network occurs over the SMB protocol.  `[Ref: Wikipedia Shared Resource]`  `[Ref: TechNet Shared Folder]` **Net** (`S0039`) pode ser utilizado para query a remote system for available unidades partilhadas (Network Shares) using the `net view \\\\remotesystem` command. It pode também ser utilizado para query unidades partilhadas (Network Shares) on the local system using `net share`. For macOS, the `sharing -l` command lists all shared points used for smb services.

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable Windows Group Policy “Do Not Allow Anonymous Enumeration of SAM Accounts and Shares” security setting to limit users who can enumerate network shares. `[Ref: Windows Anonymous Enumeration of SAM Accounts]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Criação de Conta
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar an account para manter acesso a victim systems. `[Ref: Symantec WastedLocker June 2020]` With a sufficient level of access, creating such accounts pode ser empregue para establish secondary credentialed access that do not require persistent remote access tools to be deployed on the system.

Accounts may be created on the local system or within a domain or cloud tenant. Em ambientes Cloud, adversaries may create accounts that only have access to specific services, which can reduce the chance of detection.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar access controls and firewalls to limit access to Domain Controller (DC)s and systems used to create and manage accounts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Protect Domain Controller (DC)s by ensuring proper security configuration for critical servers.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication for user and privileged accounts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the number of accounts with permissions to create other accounts. Do not allow domain administrator accounts to be used for day-to-day operations that may expose them to potential adversaries on unprivileged systems.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Criação de Conta: Local Account
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar a local account para manter acesso a victim systems. Local accounts are those configured by an organization for use by users, remote support, services, or for administration on a single system or service. 

Por exemplo, with a sufficient level of access, the Windows `net user /add` command pode ser utilizado para create a local account.  In Linux, the `useradd` command can be used, while on macOS systems, the `dscl -create` command can be used. Local accounts may also be added to network devices, often via common **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) commands such as `username`, to ESXi servers via `esxcli system account add`, or to Kubernetes clusters using the `kubectl` utility. `[Ref: cisco_username_cmd]` `[Ref: Kubernetes Service Accounts Security]`

Os adversários podem também create new local accounts on network firewall management consoles – for example, by exploiting a vulnerable firewall management system, threat actors may be able to establish super-admin accounts that could be used to modify firewall rules and gain further access to the network. `[Ref: Cyber Security News]`

Such accounts pode ser empregue para establish secondary credentialed access that do not require persistent remote access tools to be deployed on the system.

mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the number of accounts permitted to create other accounts. Limit the usage of Administrador Local accounts to be used for day-to-day operations that may expose them to potential adversaries.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar a domain account para manter acesso a victim systems. Domain accounts are those managed by Active Directory (AD) Domain Services where access and permissions are configured across systems and services that are part of that domain. Domain accounts can cover user, administrator, and service accounts. With a sufficient level of access, the `net user /add /domain` command pode ser utilizado para create a domain account. `[Ref: Savill 1999]`

Such accounts pode ser empregue para establish secondary credentialed access that do not require persistent remote access tools to be deployed on the system.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication for user and privileged accounts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Protect Domain Controller (DC)s by ensuring proper security configuration for critical servers.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar access controls and firewalls to limit access to Domain Controller (DC)s and systems used to create and manage accounts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the number of accounts with permissions to create other accounts. Do not allow domain administrator accounts to be used for day-to-day operations that may expose them to potential adversaries on unprivileged systems.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

analytics.descriptionPt: Adversary uses built-in tools such as 'net user /add /domain' or PowerShell to create a domain user account. techniques.fullNamePt: Criação de Conta: Cloud Account
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar a cloud account para manter acesso a victim systems. With a sufficient level of access, such accounts pode ser empregue para establish secondary credentialed access that does not require persistent remote access tools to be deployed on the system. `[Ref: Microsoft O365 Admin Roles]` `[Ref: Microsoft Support O365 Add Another Admin, October 2019]` `[Ref: AWS Create IAM User]` `[Ref: GCP Create Cloud Identity Users]` `[Ref: Microsoft Azure AD Users]`

Adicionalmente a user accounts, cloud accounts may be associated with services. Cloud providers handle the concept of service accounts in different ways. In Azure, service accounts include service principals and managed identities, which can be linked to various resources such as OAuth applications, serverless functions, and máquina virtual (VM)s com o objetivo de grant those resources permissions to perform various activities in the environment. `[Ref: Microsoft Entra ID Service Principals]` In GCP, service accounts can also be linked to specific resources, as well as be impersonated by other accounts for **Temporary Elevated Cloud Access** (`T1548.005`). `[Ref: GCP Service Accounts]` While AWS has no specific concept of service accounts, resources can be directly granted permission to assume roles. `[Ref: AWS Instance Profiles]` `[Ref: AWS Lambda Execution Role]`

Os adversários podem criar accounts that only have access to specific cloud services, which can reduce the chance of detection.

Uma vez que an adversary has created a cloud account, they can then manipulate that account to ensure persistence and allow access to additional resources - for example, by adding **Additional Cloud Credentials** (`T1098.001`) or assigning **Additional Cloud Roles** (`T1098.003`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Inicialização de Aplicação Office
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de Microsoft Office-based applications for persistence between startups. Microsoft Office is a fairly common application suite on Windows-based sistema operativos within an enterprise network. There are multiple mechanisms that can be used with Office for persistence when an Office-based application is started; this can include the use of Office Template Macros and add-ins.

A variety of features have been discovered in Outlook that pode ser abusado para obtain persistence, such as Outlook rules, forms, and Home Page. `[Ref: SensePost Ruler GitHub]` These mecanismo de persistências can work within Outlook or be used through Office 365. `[Ref: TechNet O365 Outlook Rules]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Follow Office macro security best practices suitable for your environment. Disable Office VBA macros from executing.

Disable Office add-ins. If they are required, follow best practices for securing them by requiring them to be signed and disabling user notification for allowing add-ins. For some add-ins types (WLL, VBA) additional mitigation is likely required as disabling add-ins in the Office Trust Center does not disable WLL nor does it prevent VBA code from executing.  `[Ref: MRWLabs Office Persistence Add-ins]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent Office applications from creating child processes and from writing potentially malicious executable content to disk.  `[Ref: win10_asr]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: For the Outlook methods, blocking macros may be ineffective as the Visual Basic engine used for these features is separate from the macro scripting engine. `[Ref: SensePost Outlook Forms]` Microsoft has released patches to try to address each issue. Ensure KB3191938 which blocks Outlook Visual Basic and displays a código malicioso warning, KB4011091 which disables custom forms by default, and KB4011162 which removes the legacy Home Page feature, are applied to systems. `[Ref: SensePost Outlook Home Page]`

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: For the Office Test method, create the Registry key used to execute it and set the permissions to "Read Control" to prevent easy access to the key without administrator permissions or requiring Privilege Escalation.  `[Ref: Palo Alto Office Test Sofacy]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Office Application Startup: Office Template Macros
techniques.fullNamePt: Inicialização de Aplicação Office: Office Template Macros
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Microsoft Office templates to obtain persistence num sistema comprometido. Microsoft Office contains templates that are part of common Office applications and são utilizados para customize styles. The base templates within the application are used each time an application starts. `[Ref: Microsoft Change Normal Template]` Office Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) macros `[Ref: MSDN VBA in Office]` can be inserted into the base template and used to execute code when the respective Office application starts com o objetivo de obtain persistence. Examples for both Word and Excel have been discovered and published. Por omissão, Word has a Normal.dotm template created that can be modified to include a malicious macro. Excel does not have a template file created by default, but one can be added that will automatically be loaded. `[Ref: enigma0x3 normal.dotm]` `[Ref: Hexacorn Office Template Macros]` Shared templates may also be stored and pulled from remote locations. `[Ref: GlobalDotName Jun 2019]` Word Normal.dotm location:
`C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Templates\Normal.dotm` Excel Personal.xlsb location:
`C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Excel\XLSTART\PERSONAL.XLSB` Os adversários podem também change the location of the base template to point to their own by hijacking the application's search order, e.g. Word 2016 will first look for Normal.dotm under `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\`, or by modifying the GlobalDotName registry key. By modifying the GlobalDotName registry key an adversary can specify an arbitrary location, file name, and file extension to use for the template that will be loaded on application startup. To abuse GlobalDotName, adversaries may first need to register the template as a trusted document or place it in a trusted location. `[Ref: GlobalDotName Jun 2019]` Um adversário pode need to enable macros to execute unrestricted depending on the system or enterprise security policy on use of macros.

mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent Office applications from creating child processes and from writing potentially malicious executable content to disk.  `[Ref: win10_asr]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Follow Office macro security best practices suitable for your environment. Disable Office VBA macros from executing.

Disable Office add-ins. If they are required, follow best practices for securing them by requiring them to be signed and disabling user notification for allowing add-ins. For some add-ins types (WLL, VBA) additional mitigation is likely required as disabling add-ins in the Office Trust Center does not disable WLL nor does it prevent VBA code from executing.  `[Ref: MRWLabs Office Persistence Add-ins]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Inicialização de Aplicação Office: Office Test
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de the Microsoft Office "Office Test" Registry key to obtain persistence num sistema comprometido. An Office Test Registry location exists that allows a user to specify an arbitrary DLL that will be executed every time an Office application is started. This Registry key is thought to be used by Microsoft to load DLLs for testing and debugging purposes while developing Office applications. This Registry key is not created by default during an Office installation. `[Ref: Hexacorn Office Test]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Office Test Sofacy]`

There exist user and global Registry keys for the Office Test feature, such as:

* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Office test\Special\Perf`
* `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Office test\Special\Perf`

Os adversários podem add this Registry key and specify a malicious DLL that will be executed whenever an Office application, such as Word or Excel, is started.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Create the Registry key used to execute it and set the permissions to "Read Control" to prevent easy access to the key without administrator permissions or requiring Privilege Escalation. `[Ref: Palo Alto Office Test Sofacy]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Desofuscação/Descodificação de Ficheiros ou Informação
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar **Obfuscated Files or Information** (`T1027`) to hide artifacts of an intrusion from analysis. They may require separate mechanisms to decode or deobfuscate that information depending on how they intend to use it. Methods for doing that include built-in functionality of malware or by using utilities present on the system.

One such example is the use of **certutil** (`S0160`) to decode a remote access tool portable executable file that has been hidden inside a certificate file. `[Ref: Malwarebytes Targeted Attack against Saudi Arabia]` Another example is using the Windows `copy /b` or `type` command to reassemble binary fragments into a malicious payload. `[Ref: Carbon Black Obfuscation Sept 2016]` `[Ref: Sentinel One Tainted Love 2023]`

Sometimes a user's action may be required to open it for deobfuscation or decryption as part of **User Execution** (`T1204`). The user may also be required to input a password to open a password protected compressed/encrypted file that was provided by the adversary. `[Ref: Volexity PowerDuke November 2016]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Software Extensions
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de software extensions to establish persistent access to victim systems. Software extensions are modular components that enhance or customize the functionality of software applications, including web browsers, Integrated Development Environments (IDEs), and other platforms. `[Ref: Chrome Extension C2 Malware]` `[Ref: Abramovsky VSCode Security]` Extensions are typically installed via official marketplaces, app stores, or manually loaded by users, and they often inherit the permissions and access levels of the host application. 

  
Malicious extensions can be introduced through various methods, including engenharia social, compromised marketplaces, or direct installation by users or by adversaries who have already gained access to a system. Malicious extensions can be named similarly or identically to benign extensions in marketplaces. Security mechanisms in extension marketplaces may be insufficient to detect malicious components, allowing adversaries para contornar (bypass) automated scanners or exploit trust established during the installation process. Os adversários podem também abuse benign extensions to achieve their objectives, such as using legitimate functionality to tunnel data or bypass controlos de segurança. 

The modular nature of extensions and their integration with host applications make them an attractive target for adversaries seeking to exploit trusted software ecosystems. Detection can be challenging due to the inherent trust placed in extensions during installation and their ability to blend into normal application workflows.

mitigations.name: Limit Software Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Only install extensions from trusted sources that can be verified.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure extensions that are installed are the intended ones, as many malicious extensions may masquerade as legitimate ones.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Train users to minimize extension use, and to only install trusted extensions.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure sistema operativos and software are using the most current version.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Set an extension allow or deny list as appropriate for your security policy.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: Software Extensions: Extensões de Browser
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de internet browser extensions to establish persistent access to victim systems. Browser extensions or plugins are small programs that can add functionality to and customize aspects of internet browsers. They can be installed directly via a local file or custom URL or through a browser's app store - an official online platform where users can browse, install, and manage extensions for a specific web browser. Extensions generally inherit the web browser's permissions previously granted. `[Ref: Wikipedia Browser Extension]` `[Ref: Chrome Extensions Definition]` 
 
Malicious extensions can be installed into a browser through malicious app store downloads masquerading as legitimate extensions, through engenharia social, or by an adversary that has already compromised a system. Security can be limited on browser app stores, so it may not be difficult for malicious extensions to defeat automated scanners. `[Ref: Malicious Chrome Extension Numbers]` Dependendo de the browser, adversaries may also manipulate an extension's update url to install updates from an adversary-controlled server or manipulate the mobile configuration file to silently install additional extensions. 

Os adversários podem abusar de how chromium-based browsers load extensions by modifying or replacing the Preferences and/or Secure Preferences files to silently install malicious extensions. When the browser is not running, adversaries can alter these files, ensuring the extension is loaded, granted desired permissions, and will persist in browser sessions. This method does not require user consent and extensions are silently loaded in the background from disk or from the browser's trusted store. `[Ref: Pulsedive]`
  
Previous to macOS 11, adversaries could silently install browser extensions via the command line using the `profiles` tool to install malicious `.mobileconfig` files. In macOS 11+, the use of the `profiles` tool can no longer install configuration profiles; however, `.mobileconfig` files can be planted and installed with user interaction. `[Ref: xorrior chrome extensions macOS]` 
 
Uma vez que the extension is installed, it can browse to websites in the background, steal all information that a user enters into a browser (including credentials), and be used as an installer for a RAT for persistence. `[Ref: Chrome Extension Crypto Miner]` `[Ref: ICEBRG Chrome Extensions]` `[Ref: Banker Google Chrome Extension Steals Creds]` `[Ref: Catch All Chrome Extension]` 

There have also been instances of botnets using a persistent backdoor through malicious Chrome extensions for **Command and Control** (`TA0011`). `[Ref: Stantinko Botnet]` `[Ref: Chrome Extension C2 Malware]` Os adversários podem também use browser extensions to modify browser permissions and components, privacy settings, and other controlos de segurança for **Stealth** (`TA0005`). `[Ref: Browers FriarFox]` `[Ref: Browser Adrozek]`

mitigations.name: Limit Software Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Only install browser extensions from trusted sources that can be verified. Browser extensions for some browsers can be controlled through Group Policy. Change settings to prevent the browser from installing extensions without sufficient permissions.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure extensions that are installed are the intended ones, as many malicious extensions will masquerade as legitimate ones.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure sistema operativos and browsers are using the most current version.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Close out all browser sessions when finished using them to prevent any potentially malicious extensions from continuing to run.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Set a browser extension allow or deny list as appropriate for your security policy. `[Ref: Technospot Chrome Extensions GP]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: Software Extensions: IDE Extensions
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de an integrated development environment (IDE) extension to establish persistent access to victim systems. `[Ref: Mnemonic misuse visual studio]` IDEs such as Visual Studio Code, IntelliJ IDEA, and Eclipse support extensions - software components that add features like code linting, auto-completion, task automation, or integration with tools like Git and Docker. A malicious extension can be installed through an extension marketplace (i.e., **Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools** (`T1195.001`)) or side-loaded directly into the IDE. `[Ref: Abramovsky VSCode Security]` `[Ref: Lakshmanan Visual Studio Marketplace]`   

Adicionalmente a installing malicious extensions, adversaries may also leverage benign ones. Por exemplo, adversaries may establish persistent SSH tunnels via the use of the VSCode Remote SSH extension (i.e., **IDE Tunneling** (`T1219.001`)).  

Trust is typically established through the installation process; once installed, the malicious extension is run every time that the IDE is launched. The extension can then be used to execute código arbitrário, establish a backdoor, mine cryptocurrency, or exfiltrate data. `[Ref: ExtensionTotal VSCode Extensions  2025]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Browser Session Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem take advantage of security vulnerabilities and inherent functionality in browser software to change content, modify user-behaviors, and intercept information as part of various browser session hijacking techniques. `[Ref: Wikipedia Man in the Browser]`

A specific example is when an adversary injects software into a browser that allows them to inherit cookies, HTTP sessions, and SSL client certificates of a user then use the browser as a way to pivot into an authenticated intranet. `[Ref: Cobalt Strike Browser Pivot]` `[Ref: ICEBRG Chrome Extensions]` Executing browser-based behaviors such as pivoting may require specific process permissions, such as `SeDebugPrivilege` and/or high-integrity/administrator rights.

Another example involves pivoting browser traffic from the adversary's browser through the user's browser by setting up a proxy which will redirect web traffic. This does not alter the user's traffic in any way, and the proxy connection can be severed as soon as the browser is closed. The adversary assumes the security context of whichever browser process the proxy is injected into. Browsers typically create a new process for each tab that is opened and permissions and certificates are separated accordingly. With these permissions, an adversary could potentially browse to any resource on an intranet, such as **Sharepoint** (`T1213.002`) or webmail, that is accessible through the browser and which the browser has sufficient permissions. Browser pivoting may also bypass security provided by 2-factor authentication. `[Ref: cobaltstrike manual]`

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Close all browser sessions regularly and when they are no longer needed.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Since browser pivoting requires a high integrity process to launch from, restricting user permissions and addressing Privilege Escalation and **Bypass User Account Control** (`T1548.002`) opportunities can limit the exposure to this technique.
