techniques.fullNamePt: Forced Authentication
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem recolher material de credenciais by invoking or forcing a user to automatically provide authentication information through a mechanism in which they can intercept.

The Server Message Block (SMB) protocol is commonly used in Windows networks for authentication and communication between systems for access to resources and file sharing. When a Windows system attempts to connect to an SMB resource it will automatically attempt to authenticate and send credential information for the current user to the remote system. `[Ref: Wikipedia Server Message Block]` This behavior is typical in enterprise environments so that users do not need to enter credentials to access network resources.

Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV) is also typically used by Windows systems as a backup protocol when SMB is blocked or fails. WebDAV is an extension of HTTP and will typically operate over TCP ports 80 and 443. `[Ref: Didier Stevens WebDAV Traffic]` `[Ref: Microsoft Managing WebDAV Security]`

Os adversários podem take advantage of this behavior para obter acesso a user account hashes through forced SMB/WebDAV authentication. Um adversário consegue send an attachment to a user through spearphishing that contains a resource link to an external server controlled by the adversary  (i.e. **Template Injection** (`T1221`)), or place a specially crafted file on navigation path for privileged accounts (e.g. .SCF file placed on desktop) or on a publicly accessible share to be accessed by victim(s). When the user's system accesses the untrusted resource, it will attempt authentication and send information, including the user's hashed credentials, over SMB to the adversary-controlled server. `[Ref: GitHub Hashjacking]` With access to the credential hash, an adversary can perform off-line **Brute Force** (`T1110`) cracking para obter acesso a plaintext credentials. `[Ref: Cylance Redirect to SMB]`

There are several different ways this can occur. `[Ref: Osanda Stealing NetNTLM Hashes]` Some specifics from in-the-wild use include:

* A spearphishing attachment containing a document with a resource that is automatically loaded when the document is opened (i.e. **Template Injection** (`T1221`)). The document can include, for example, a request similar to `file[:]//[remote address]/Normal.dotm` to trigger the SMB request. `[Ref: US-CERT APT Energy Oct 2017]`
* A modified .LNK or .SCF file with the icon filename pointing to an external reference such as `\\[remote address]\pic.png` that will force the system to load the resource when the icon is rendered to repeatedly gather credentials. `[Ref: US-CERT APT Energy Oct 2017]`

Alternatively, by leveraging the `EfsRpcOpenFileRaw` function, an adversary can send SMB requests to a remote system's MS-EFSRPC interface and force the victim computer to initiate an authentication procedure and share its authentication details. The Encrypting File System Remote Protocol (EFSRPC) is a protocol used in Windows networks for maintenance and management operations on encrypted data that is stored remotely to be accessed over a network. Utilization of `EfsRpcOpenFileRaw` function in EFSRPC é utilizado para open an encrypted object on the server for backup or restore. Adversaries can collect this data and abuse it as part of a NTLM relay attack para obter acesso a sistemas remotos on the same internal network. `[Ref: Rapid7]` `[Ref: GitHub]`

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use strong passwords to increase the difficulty of credential hashes from being cracked if they are obtained.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Block SMB traffic from exiting an enterprise network with egress filtering or by blocking TCP ports 139, 445 and UDP port 137. Filter or block WebDAV protocol traffic from exiting the network. If access to external resources over SMB and WebDAV is necessary, then traffic should be tightly limited with allowlisting.  `[Ref: US-CERT SMB Security]`  `[Ref: US-CERT APT Energy Oct 2017]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

analytics.name: Analytic 0065
analytics.descriptionPt: Adversary stages a lure that references a remote resource (e.g., LNK/SCF/Office template). When the user opens/renders the file or a shell enumerates icons, the host automatically attempts SMB or WebDAV authentication to the attacker host. The chain is: (1) lure file is created or modified in a user-exposed location → (2) user or system accesses the lure → (3) host makes outbound NTLM (SMB 139/445 or WebDAV over 80/443) to an untrusted destination → (4) repeated attempts from multiple users/hosts or from privileged workstations.

bypasses: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

Evitar abrir handles diretos com `PROCESS_VM_READ`. Preferir extração indireta via SSPI/Kerberos (`Rubeus tgtdeleg` / `kerberoast`), decifragem offline de blobs DPAPI usando a Backup Key do domínio, extração de SAM/SECURITY via registo/VSS ou abuso de certificados AD CS (`T1649`).
blindSpots: **UserLocations**: Folders where lures are most effective (Desktop, Public, Downloads, Temp, Cache, Start Menu, Startup). Adjust to enterprise layout.
**LureExtensions**: File types commonly abused (.lnk, .scf, .url, .doc/.xls/.ppt/.pdf/.html). Extend for your tooling and languages.
**UntrustedCIDR/DNS**: Org-specific list of external/unknown networks or domains; used to suppress sanctioned file servers and WebDAV gateways.
**TimeWindow**: Correlation horizon (e.g., 15–30 minutes) between file access and outbound NTLM attempt.
**WorkstationZones**: Asset/zone tags that distinguish workstations from servers; helps flag workstation→workstation SMB, which is often abnormal.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comprometimento Drive-by
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem gain access to a system through a user visiting a website over the normal course of browsing. Multiple ways of delivering exploit code to a browser exist (i.e., **Drive-by Target** (`T1608.004`)), including:

* A legitimate website is compromised, allowing adversaries to inject código malicioso
* Script files served to a legitimate website from a publicly writeable cloud storage bucket are modified by an adversary
* Malicious ads are paid for and served through legitimate ad providers (i.e., **Malvertising** (`T1583.008`))
* Built-in web application interfaces that allow user-controllable content are leveraged for the insertion of malicious scripts or iFrames (e.g., cross-site scripting)

Browser push notifications may also be abused by adversaries and leveraged for código malicioso injection via **User Execution** (`T1204`). By clicking "allow" on browser push notifications, users may be granting a website permission to run JavaScript code on their browser. `[Ref: Push notifications - viruspositive]` `[Ref: push notification -mcafee]` `[Ref: push notifications - malwarebytes]`

Often the website used by an adversary is one visited by a specific community, such as government, a particular industry, or a particular region, where the goal is to compromise a specific user or set of users based on a shared interest. This kind of targeted campaign is often referred to a strategic web compromise or watering hole attack. There are several known examples of this occurring. `[Ref: Shadowserver Strategic Web Compromise]`

Typical drive-by compromise process:

1. A user visits a website that é utilizado para host the adversary controlled content.
2. Scripts automatically execute, typically searching versions of the browser and plugins for a potentially vulnerable version. The user may be required to assist in this process by enabling scripting, notifications, or active website components and ignoring warning dialog boxes.
3. Upon finding a vulnerable version, exploit code is delivered to the browser.
4. If exploitation is successful, the adversary will gain code execution on the user's system unless other protections are in place. In some cases, a second visit to the website after the initial scan is required before exploit code is delivered.

Unlike **Exploit Public-Facing Application** (`T1190`), the focus of this technique is to exploit software on a client endpoint upon visiting a website. This will commonly give an adversary access to systems on the internal network instead of external systems that may be in a DMZ.

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Security applications that look for behavior used during exploitation such as Windows Defender Exploit Guard (WDEG) and the Enhanced Mitigation Experience Toolkit (EMET) pode ser utilizado para mitigate some exploitation behavior. `[Ref: TechNet Moving Beyond EMET]` Control flow integrity checking is another way to potentially identify and stop a software exploit from occurring. `[Ref: Wikipedia Control Flow Integrity]` Many of these protections depend on the architecture and target application binary for compatibility.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensuring that all browsers and plugins are kept updated can help prevent the exploit phase of this technique. Use modern browsers with security features turned on. `[Ref: Browser-updates]`

mitigations.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Browser sandboxes pode ser utilizado para mitigate some of the impact of exploitation, but sandbox escapes may still exist. `[Ref: Windows Blogs Microsoft Edge Sandbox]` `[Ref: Ars Technica Pwn2Own 2017 VM Escape]`

Other types of virtualization and application microsegmentation may also mitigate the impact of client-side exploitation. The risks of additional exploits and weaknesses in implementation may still exist for these types of systems. `[Ref: Ars Technica Pwn2Own 2017 VM Escape]`

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Adblockers can help prevent código malicioso served through ads from executing in the first place. Script blocking extensions can also help to prevent the execution of JavaScript. 

Consider disabling browser push notifications from certain applications and browsers. `[Ref: mac security virus popup]` `[Ref: push notifications -infosecinstitute]` `[Ref: site notifications - krebsonsecurity]`

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Train users to be aware of access or manipulation attempts by an adversary to reduce the risk of successful spearphishing, engenharia social, and other techniques that involve user interaction.

analytics.name: Analytic 0498

Defender sees network requests to previously unseen/suspicious domains or resources + browser process spawning unusual children or loading unsigned modules + file writes or registry changes shortly after those requests.

techniques.fullNamePt: Exploração de Aplicação Exposta (Public-Facing)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system to initially access a network. The weakness in the system can be a software bug, a temporary glitch, or a misconfiguration.

Exploited applications are often websites/web servers, but can also include databases (like SQL), standard services (like SMB or SSH), network device administration and management protocols (like SNMP and Smart Install), and any other system with Internet-accessible open sockets. `[Ref: NVD CVE-2016-6662]` `[Ref: CIS Multiple SMB Vulnerabilities]` `[Ref: US-CERT TA18-106A Network Infrastructure Devices 2018]` `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]` `[Ref: NVD CVE-2014-7169]` On ESXi infrastructure, adversaries may exploit exposed OpenSLP services; they may alternatively exploit exposed VMware vCenter servers. `[Ref: Recorded Future ESXiArgs Ransomware 2023]` `[Ref: Ars Technica VMWare Code Execution Vulnerability 2021]` Dependendo de the flaw being exploited, this may also involve **Exploitation for Stealth** (`T1211`) or **Exploitation for Client Execution** (`T1203`).

If an application is hosted on cloud-based infrastructure and/or is containerized, then exploiting it may lead to compromise of the underlying instance or container. This can allow an adversary a path to access the cloud or container APIs (e.g., via the **Cloud Instance Metadata API** (`T1552.005`)), exploit container host access via **Escape to Host** (`T1611`), or take advantage of weak identity and access management policies.

Os adversários podem também exploit edge network infrastructure and related appliances, specifically targeting devices that do not support robust host-based defenses. `[Ref: Mandiant Fortinet Zero Day]` `[Ref: Wired Russia Cyberwar]`

For websites and databases, the OWASP top 10 and CWE top 25 highlight the most common web-based vulnerabilities. `[Ref: OWASP Top 10]` `[Ref: CWE top 25]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Ars Technica VMWare Code Execution Vulnerability 2021]

mitigations.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Application isolation will limit what other processes and system features the exploited target can access.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict outbound tráfego de rede from public-facing servers to prevent unauthorized connections from initiating communications with attacker-controlled infrastructure. While this may not prevent the initial exploitation, it limits the attacker's ability to verify and control the compromised server post-exploit, reducing the overall impact of the attack.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Segment externally facing servers and services from the rest of the network with a DMZ or on separate hosting infrastructure.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Vulnerability Scanning
mitigations.descriptionPt: Regularly scan externally facing systems for vulnerabilities and establish procedures to rapidly patch systems when critical vulnerabilities are discovered through scanning and through public disclosure. `[Ref: OWASP Top 10]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use least privilege for service accounts will limit what permissions the exploited process gets on the rest of the system.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Web Application Firewalls pode ser empregue para limit exposure of applications to prevent exploit traffic from reaching the application.

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que all publicly exposed services are actually intended to be so, and restrict access to any that should only be available internally.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Update software regularly by employing patch management for externally exposed applications.

blockers: M1037 (Filter Network Traffic): Movimentação lateral via `PsExec`, `evil-winrm` ou `wmiexec` falha por timeout de porta.
M1030 (Network Segmentation): Sem conectividade direta da sub-rede atual para servidores de produção ou Domain Controllers.
M1026 (Privileged Account Management): Pass-the-Hash com conta de Administrador Local (`RID 500`) falha noutros hosts porque cada máquina possui password única gerida pelo LAPS.
bypasses: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).
blindSpots: **PublicVIPs**: List of public IPs/hostnames that front apps; used to scope web log and Zeek/proxy data.
**SuspiciousPatterns**: Regex set for exploit-like inputs (../, union select, cmd=, ${jndi:, rO0AB (Java serialization), %00, ${env:}, ${${::-j}ndi}).
**ErrorRateThreshold**: Spike threshold for HTTP status 5xx/4xx per client or URI (e.g., >5 in 5m).
**TimeWindow**: Correlation horizon between request, error, process spawn, and egress (e.g., 15 minutes).
**AllowedChildList**: Known child processes of app pools (e.g., msbuild.exe in CI) to reduce false positives.

techniques.namePt: Comprometimento da Cadeia de Fornecimento (Supply Chain)
techniques.fullNamePt: Comprometimento da Cadeia de Fornecimento (Supply Chain)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem manipular products or product delivery mechanisms prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

Supply chain compromise can take place at any stage of the Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) including:

* Manipulation of development tools
* Manipulation of a development environment
* Manipulation of source code repositories (public or private)
* Manipulation of source code in open-source dependencies
* Manipulation of software update/distribution mechanisms
* Compromised/infected system images (removable media infected at the factory) `[Ref: IBM Storwize]` `[Ref: Schneider Electric USB Malware]` 
* Replacement of legitimate software with modified versions
* Sales of modified/counterfeit products to legitimate distributors
* Shipment interdiction

While Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) compromise can impact any component of hardware or software, adversaries looking to gain execution have often focused on malicious additions to legitimate software in software distribution or update channels. `[Ref: Avast CCleaner3 2018]` `[Ref: Microsoft Dofoil 2018]` `[Ref: Command Five SK 2011]` Os adversários podem limit targeting to a desired victim set or distribute malicious software to a broad set of consumers but only follow up with specific victims. `[Ref: Symantec Elderwood Sept 2012]` `[Ref: Avast CCleaner3 2018]` `[Ref: Command Five SK 2011]` Popular open-source projects that are used as dependencies in many applications may also be targeted as a means to add código malicioso to users of the dependency. `[Ref: Trendmicro NPM Compromise]`

In some cases, adversaries may conduct “second-order” Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) compromises by leveraging the access gained from an initial Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) compromise to further compromise a software component. `[Ref: Krebs 3cx overview 2023]` This may allow the threat actor to spread to even more victims.

mitigations.name: Boot Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use secure methods to boot a system and verify the integrity of the sistema operativo and loading mechanisms.

mitigations.name: Application Developer Guidance
mitigations.descriptionPt: Application developers should be cautious when selecting third-party libraries to integrate into their application. Additionally, where possible, developers should lock software dependencies to specific versions rather than pulling the latest version on build. `[Ref: Cider Security Top 10 CICD Security Risks]`

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: A patch management process should be implemented to check unused dependencies, unmaintained and/or previously vulnerable dependencies, unnecessary features, components, files, and documentation.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar robust user account management practices to limit permissions associated with software execution. Garantir que software runs with the lowest necessary privileges, avoiding the use of root or administrator accounts when possible. By restricting permissions, you can minimize the risk of propagation and unauthorized actions in the event of a Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) compromise, reducing the attack surface for adversaries to exploit within compromised systems.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Continuous monitoring of vulnerability sources and the use of automatic and manual code review tools should also be implemented as well. `[Ref: OWASP Top 10]`

techniques.nameEn: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
techniques.fullNameEn: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
techniques.namePt: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
techniques.fullNamePt: Comprometimento da Cadeia de Fornecimento (Supply Chain): Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem manipular software dependencies and development tools prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise. Applications often depend on external software to function properly. Popular open source projects that are used as dependencies in many applications, such as pip and NPM packages, may be targeted as a means to add código malicioso to users of the dependency. `[Ref: Trendmicro NPM Compromise]` `[Ref: Bitdefender NPM Repositories Compromised 2021]` `[Ref: MANDVI Malicious npm and PyPI Packages Disguised]` This may also include abandoned packages, which in some cases could be re-registered by threat actors after being removed by adversaries. `[Ref: The Hacker News PyPi Revival Hijack 2024]` Os adversários podem também employ "typosquatting" or name-confusion by choosing names similar to existing popular libraries or packages com o objetivo de deceive a user. `[Ref: Ahmed Backdoors in Python and NPM Packages]` `[Ref: Meyer PyPI Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) Attack Uncovered]` `[Ref: Checkmarx-oss-seo]`

Additionally, CI/CD pipeline components, such as GitHub Actions, may be targeted com o objetivo de gain access to the building, testing, and deployment cycles of an application. `[Ref: Unit 42 Palo Alto GitHub Actions Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) Attack 2025]` By adding código malicioso into a GitHub action, a threat actor may be able to collect runtime credentials (e.g., via **Proc Filesystem** (`T1003.007`)) or insert further malicious components into the build pipelines for a second-order Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) compromise. `[Ref: OWASP CICD-SEC-4]` As GitHub Actions are often dependent on other GitHub Actions, threat actors may be able to infect a large number of repositories via the compromise of a single Action. `[Ref: Palo Alto Networks GitHub Actions Worm 2023]`

Os adversários podem também target the configuration and instruction files consumed by integrated development environments and AI coding agents. Project files such as tasks.json may execute commands when a developer opens or builds a project, while agent skill files (SKILL.md) supply an agent with instructions and resources that it loads on demand and runs with the permissions of the agent process. `[Ref: Microsoft - Agent Skills Docs]` `[Ref: Google Agent Files May 2026]` `[Ref: CrowdStrike Threat Hunting Report 2026]` `[Ref: Microsoft Contagious Interview March 2026]` To encourage downloads, adversaries may publish these files under benign-appearing or typo-squatted names, upload unmodified copies of the genuine skills first so the listings accumulate installs before the content behind them is weaponized, or may place the malicious instructions in a secondary document that the reviewed entry point references. `[Ref: Zenity Skill Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) August 2026]` `[Ref: ESET Agent Skills March 2026]` Because these artifacts are natural language or configuration rather than executable code, they may pass registry screening and signature-based scanning. `[Ref: ESET Agent Skills March 2026]` `[Ref: TrendMicro - OpenClaw Skills Distribute ATMOS]` 

Targeting may be specific to a desired victim set or may be distributed to a broad set of consumers but only move on to additional tactics on specific victims.

analytics.name: Analytic 0862
analytics.descriptionPt: Adversary ships a tampered application or update: an updater/installer (msiexec/setup/update.exe/vendor service) writes or replaces binaries; on first run it spawns scripts/shells or unsigned DLLs and beacons to non-approved update CDNs/hosts. techniques.fullNamePt: BITS Jobs
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de BITS jobs to persistently execute code and perform various background tasks. Windows Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) is a low-bandwidth, asynchronous file transfer mechanism exposed through **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`) (COM). `[Ref: Microsoft COM]` `[Ref: Microsoft BITS]` BITS is commonly used by updaters, messengers, and other applications preferred to operate in the background (using available idle bandwidth) without interrupting other networked applications. File transfer tasks are implemented as BITS jobs, which contain a queue of one or more file operations.

The interface to create and manage BITS jobs is accessible through **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) and the **BITSAdmin** (`S0190`) tool. `[Ref: Microsoft BITS]` `[Ref: Microsoft BITSAdmin]`

Os adversários podem abusar de BITS to download (e.g. **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`)), execute, and even clean up after running código malicioso (e.g. **Indicator Removal** (`T1070`)). BITS tasks are self-contained in the BITS job database, without new files or registry modifications, and often permitted by host firewalls. `[Ref: CTU BITS Malware June 2016]` `[Ref: Mondok Windows PiggyBack BITS May 2007]` `[Ref: Symantec BITS May 2007]` BITS enabled execution may also enable persistence by creating long-standing jobs (the default maximum lifetime is 90 days and extendable) or invoking an arbitrary program when a job completes or errors (including after system reboots). `[Ref: PaloAlto UBoatRAT Nov 2017]` `[Ref: CTU BITS Malware June 2016]`

BITS upload functionalities pode também ser utilizado para perform **Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol** (`T1048`). `[Ref: CTU BITS Malware June 2016]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider limiting access to the BITS interface to specific users or groups. `[Ref: Symantec BITS May 2007]`

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Modify network and/or host firewall rules, as well as other network controls, to only allow legitimate BITS traffic.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider reducing the default BITS job lifetime in Group Policy or by editing the `JobInactivityTimeout` and `MaxDownloadTime` Registry values in ` HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\BITS`. `[Ref: Microsoft BITS]`

detections.name: Detect abuse of Windows BITS Jobs for download, execution and persistence

analytics.name: Analytic 0274
analytics.descriptionPt: Behavioral chain: (1) An actor creates or modifies a BITS job via bitsadmin.exe, PowerShell BITS cmdlets, or COM; (2) the job performs HTTP(S)/SMB network transfers while the owning user is logged on; (3) upon job completion/error, BITS launches a notify command (SetNotifyCmdLine) from svchost.exe -k netsvcs -s BITS, often establishing persistence by keeping long-lived jobs. The strategy correlates process creation, command/script telemetry, BITS-Client operational events, and network connections initiated by BITS.

mutableElements.description: Correlation window linking job creation, transfer, and notify execution (e.g., 30m–24h depending on environment and BITS retry behavior).
Allow-list of corporate update/CDN endpoints that legitimately use BITS (WSUS, MEMCM, vendor updaters).
BITSAdmin flags of interest (/transfer, /addfile, /SetNotifyCmdLine, /resume, /setcustomheaders, /setminretrydelay).
Known risky binaries or folders (e.g., %TEMP%\*.exe, powershell.exe, cmd.exe) used as BITS notify commands.
Scope by interactive users, service accounts, or high-value targets (admins/servers) to reduce benign noise.
Definition of external/non-corp destinations for network correlation.
Maximum age or retry count for benign jobs before flagging persistence (e.g., >3 days or retry>20).

techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Relação de Confiança
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem breach or otherwise leverage organizations who have access to intended victims. Access through trusted third party relationship abuses an existing connection that may not be protected or receives less scrutiny than standard mechanisms of gaining access to a network.

Organizations often grant elevated access to second or third-party external providers com o objetivo de allow them to manage internal systems as well as cloud-based environments. Some examples of these relationships include IT services contractors, managed security providers, infrastructure contractors (e.g. HVAC, elevators, physical security). The third-party provider's access may be intended to be limited to the infrastructure being maintained, but may exist on the same network as the rest of the enterprise. As such, **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) used by the other party for access to internal network systems may be compromised and used. `[Ref: CISA IT Service Providers]`

In Office 365 environments, organizations may grant Microsoft partners or resellers delegated administrator permissions. By compromising a partner or reseller account, an adversary may be able to leverage existing delegated administrator relationships or send new delegated administrator offers to clients com o objetivo de gain administrative control over the victim tenant. `[Ref: Office 365 Delegated Administration]`

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Require MFA for all delegated administrator accounts. `[Ref: Microsoft Nobelium Admin Privileges]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Properly manage accounts and permissions used by parties in trusted relationships to minimize potential abuse by the party and if the party is compromised by an adversary. In Office 365 environments, partner relationships and roles can be viewed under the “Partner Relationships” page. `[Ref: Office 365 Partner Relationships]`

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network segmentation pode ser utilizado para isolate infrastructure components that do not require broad network access.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Hardware Additions
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem physically introduce computer accessories, networking hardware, or other computing devices into a system or network that can be used as a vector to gain access. Rather than just connecting and distributing payloads via removable storage (i.e. **Replication Through Removable Media** (`T1091`)), more robust hardware additions pode ser utilizado para introduce new functionalities and/or features into a system that can then be abused.

While public references of usage by threat actors are scarce, many red teams/penetration testers leverage hardware additions for initial access. Commercial and open source products can be leveraged with capabilities such as passive network tapping, tráfego de rede modification (i.e. **Adversary-in-the-Middle** (`T1557`)), keystroke injection, kernel memory reading via DMA, addition of new wireless access points to an existing network, and others. `[Ref: Ossmann Star Feb 2011]` `[Ref: Aleks Weapons Nov 2015]` `[Ref: Frisk DMA August 2016]` `[Ref: McMillan Pwn March 2012]`

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Establish network access control policies, such as using device certificates and the 802.1x standard.  `[Ref: Wikipedia 802.1x]` Restrict use of DHCP to registered devices to prevent unregistered devices from communicating with trusted systems.

mitigations.name: Limit Hardware Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Block unknown devices and accessories by endpoint security configuration and monitoring agent.

detections.name: Detect unauthorized or suspicious Hardware Additions (USB/Thunderbolt/Network)

analytics.descriptionPt: Chain: (1) a new external device is recognized by Windows (USB/Thunderbolt/PCIe) or a new block device appears; (2) within a short window, the same user/session spawns processes or the OS mounts a new volume; (3) optional follow-on activity such as HID keystroke injection, DMA driver load, or new network interface MAC on DHCP. techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Política de Passwords
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar access detailed information about the password policy used within an enterprise network or cloud environment. Password policies are a way to enforce complex passwords that are difficult to guess or crack through **Brute Force** (`T1110`). This information may help the adversary to create a list of common passwords and launch dictionary and/or brute force attacks which adheres to the policy (e.g. if the minimum password length should be 8, then not trying passwords such as 'pass123'; not checking for more than 3-4 passwords per account if the lockout is set to 6 as to not lock out accounts).

Password policies can be set and discovered on Windows, Linux, and macOS systems via various command shell utilities such as `net accounts (/domain)`, `Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy`, `chage -l <username>`, `cat /etc/pam.d/common-password`, and `pwpolicy getaccountpolicies`  `[Ref: Superuser Linux Password Policies]`  `[Ref: Jamf User Password Policies]`. Os adversários podem também leverage a **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) on network devices to discover password policy information (e.g. `show aaa`, `show aaa common-criteria policy all`). `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]`

Password policies can be discovered in cloud environments using available APIs such as `GetAccountPasswordPolicy` in AWS  `[Ref: AWS GetPasswordPolicy]`.

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure only valid password filters are registered. Filter DLLs must be present in Windows installation directory (`C:\Windows\System32\` by default) of a Domain Controller (DC) and/or local computer with a corresponding entry in `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Notification Packages`.  `[Ref: Microsoft Install Password Filter n.d]`

Correlate sysmon process creation with PowerShell ScriptBlock and Security logs.

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Indireta de Comandos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de utilities that allow for command execution para contornar (bypass) security restrictions that limit the use of command-line interpreters. Various Windows utilities pode ser empregue para execute commands, possibly without invoking **cmd** (`S0106`). Por exemplo, **Forfiles** (`S0193`), the Program Compatibility Assistant (`pcalua.exe`), components of the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), `Scriptrunner.exe`, as well as other utilities may invoke the execution of programs and commands from a **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`), Run window, or via scripts. `[Ref: VectorSec ForFiles Aug 2017]` `[Ref: Evi1cg Forfiles Nov 2017]` `[Ref: Secure Team - Scriptrunner.exe]` `[Ref: SS64]` `[Ref: Bleeping Computer - Scriptrunner.exe]` Os adversários podem também abuse the `ssh.exe` binary para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos commands via the `ProxyCommand` and `LocalCommand` options, which can be invoked via the `-o` flag or by modifying the SSH config file. `[Ref: Threat Actor Targets the Manufacturing industry with Lumma Stealer and Amadey Bot]`

Os adversários podem abusar de these features for **Stealth** (`TA0005`), specifically to perform arbitrary execution while subverting detections and/or mitigation controls (such as Group Policy) that limit/prevent the usage of **cmd** (`S0106`) or file extensions more commonly associated with malicious payloads.

detections.name: Indirect Command Execution – Windows utility abuse behavior chain

analytics.name: Analytic 0576
analytics.descriptionPt: Cause→effect chain: (1) A user or service launches an indirection utility (e.g., forfiles.exe, pcalua.exe, wsl.exe, scriptrunner.exe, ssh.exe with -o ProxyCommand/LocalCommand). (2) That utility spawns a secondary program/command (PowerShell, cmd, msiexec, regsvr32, curl, arbitrary EXE) and/or opens outbound network connections. (3) Optional precursor modification of SSH config to persist LocalCommand/ProxyCommand. Correlate process creation, command/script content, file access to %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\config, and network connections from the utility or its child.

mutableElements.description: Correlation window between indirect launcher and spawned child/network activity (e.g., 10–30 minutes).
Utilities permitted on admin/Jumphosts (forfiles, wsl, ssh) to reduce noise.
Child images that indicate abuse (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, rundll32.exe, regsvr32.exe, mshta.exe, msiexec.exe, curl.exe, bitsadmin.exe).
Raise severity when the actor is a standard/interactive user on a workstation rather than a server or CI agent.
Known-good egress networks for SSH/WSL activity to suppress expected admin automations.

techniques.fullNamePt: Exploração para Execução em Cliente
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem explorar software vulnerabilities in client applications to execute code. Vulnerabilities can exist in software due to unsecure coding practices that can lead to unanticipated behavior. Adversaries can take advantage of certain vulnerabilities through targeted exploitation for the purpose of código arbitrário execution. Oftentimes the most valuable exploits to an offensive toolkit are those that pode ser utilizado para obtain code execution on a remote system because they pode ser utilizado para gain access to that system. Users will expect to see files related to the applications they commonly used to do work, so they are a useful target for exploit research and development because of their high utility.

Several types exist:

### Browser-based Exploitation

Web browsers are a common target through **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`) and **Spearphishing Link** (`T1566.002`). Endpoint systems may be compromised through normal web browsing or from certain users being targeted by links in spearphishing emails to adversary controlled sites used to exploit the web browser. These often do not require an action by the user for the exploit to be executed.

### Office Applications

Common office and productivity applications such as Microsoft Office are also targeted through **Phishing** (`T1566`). Malicious files will be transmitted directly as attachments or through links to download them. These require the user to open the document or file for the exploit to run.

### Common Third-party Applications

Other applications that are commonly seen or are part of the software deployed in a rede alvo may also be used for exploitation. Applications such as Adobe Reader and Flash, which are common in enterprise environments, have been routinely targeted by adversaries attempting para obter acesso a systems. Dependendo de the software and nature of the vulnerability, some may be exploited in the browser or require the user to open a file. A título de exemplo, some Flash exploits have been delivered as objects within Microsoft Office documents.

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Security applications that look for behavior used during exploitation such as Windows Defender Exploit Guard (WDEG) and the Enhanced Mitigation Experience Toolkit (EMET) pode ser utilizado para mitigate some exploitation behavior.  `[Ref: TechNet Moving Beyond EMET]` Control flow integrity checking is another way to potentially identify and stop a software exploit from occurring.  `[Ref: Wikipedia Control Flow Integrity]` Many of these protections depend on the architecture and target application binary for compatibility.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Perform regular software updates to mitigate exploitation risk. Keeping software up-to-date with the latest security patches helps prevent adversaries from exploiting known vulnerabilities in client software, reducing the risk of successful attacks.

mitigations.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Browser sandboxes pode ser utilizado para mitigate some of the impact of exploitation, but sandbox escapes may still exist.  `[Ref: Windows Blogs Microsoft Edge Sandbox]`  `[Ref: Ars Technica Pwn2Own 2017 VM Escape]`

Other types of virtualization and application microsegmentation may also mitigate the impact of client-side exploitation. Risks of additional exploits and weaknesses in those systems may still exist.  `[Ref: Ars Technica Pwn2Own 2017 VM Escape]`

Correlate application logs, file writes, process lineage, and network egress within a short window.

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Induzida pelo Utilizador
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode rely upon specific actions by a user com o objetivo de gain execution. Users may be subjected to engenharia social to get them para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos code by, for example, opening a malicious document file or link. These user actions will typically be observed as follow-on behavior from forms of **Phishing** (`T1566`).

While **User Execution** (`T1204`) frequently occurs shortly after Initial Access it may occur at other phases of an intrusion, such as when an adversary places a file in a shared directory or on a user's desktop hoping that a user will click on it. This activity may also be seen shortly after **Internal Spearphishing** (`T1534`).

Os adversários podem também deceive users into performing actions such as:

* Enabling **Remote Access Tools** (`T1219`), allowing direct control of the system to the adversary
* Running malicious JavaScript in their browser, allowing adversaries to **Steal Web Session Cookie** (`T1539`)s `[Ref: Talos Roblox Scam 2023]` `[Ref: Krebs Discord Bookmarks 2023]`
* Downloading and executing malware for **User Execution** (`T1204`)
* Coerceing users to copy, paste, and execute código malicioso manually `[Ref: Reliaquest-execution]` `[Ref: proofpoint-selfpwn]`

Por exemplo, tech support scams can be facilitated through **Phishing** (`T1566`), vishing, or various forms of user interaction. Adversaries can use a combination of these methods, such as spoofing and promoting toll-free numbers or call centers that são utilizados para direct victims to malicious websites, to deliver and execute payloads containing malware or **Remote Access Tools** (`T1219`). `[Ref: Telephone Attack Delivery]`

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use user training as a way to bring awareness to common phishing and spearphishing techniques and how to raise suspicion for potentially malicious events.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Application control may be able to prevent the running of executables masquerading as other files.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint

Note: cloud-delivered protection must be enabled to use certain rules.  `[Ref: win10_asr]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Induzida pelo Utilizador: Malicious File
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode rely upon a user opening a malicious file com o objetivo de gain execution. Users may be subjected to engenharia social to get them to open a file that will lead to code execution. This user action will typically be observed as follow-on behavior from **Spearphishing Attachment** (`T1566.001`). Os adversários podem utilizar several types of files that require a user to execute them, including .doc, .pdf, .xls, .rtf, .scr, .exe, .lnk, .pif, .cpl, .reg, and .iso. `[Ref: Mandiant Trojanized Windows 10]`

Os adversários podem employ various forms of **Masquerading** (`T1036`) and **Obfuscated Files or Information** (`T1027`) to increase the likelihood that a user will open and successfully execute a malicious file. These methods may include using a familiar naming convention and/or password protecting the file and supplying instructions to a user on how to open it. `[Ref: Password Protected Word Docs]` 

While **Malicious File** (`T1204.002`) frequently occurs shortly after Initial Access it may occur at other phases of an intrusion, such as when an adversary places a file in a shared directory or on a user's desktop hoping that a user will click on it. This activity may also be seen shortly after **Internal Spearphishing** (`T1534`).

blockers: M1038 (Execution Prevention): Erro "This program is blocked by group policy" ao tentar executar binários em `C:\Users\*` ou `C:\Windows\Temp`.
M1040 (Behavior Prevention on Endpoint): Processo terminado instantaneamente pelo EDR ao tentar `VirtualAllocEx` / `WriteProcessMemory` / `CreateRemoteThread` ou acesso ao `lsass.exe`.
bypasses: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.
blindSpots: **TimeWindow**: Seconds/minutes to correlate file write to child spawn (e.g., 0–5m).

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Induzida pelo Utilizador: Malicious Image
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem rely on a user running a malicious image to facilitate execution. Amazon Web Services (AWS) Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Images, and Azure Images as well as popular container runtimes such as Docker can be backdoored. Backdoored images may be uploaded to a public repository via **Upload Malware** (`T1608.001`), and users may then download and deploy an instance or container from the image without realizing the image is malicious, thus bypassing techniques that specifically achieve Initial Access. This can lead to the execution of código malicioso, such as code that executes cryptocurrency mining, in the instance or container. `[Ref: Summit Route Malicious AMIs]`

Os adversários podem também name images a certain way to increase the chance of users mistakenly deploying an instance or container from the image (ex: **Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location** (`T1036.005`)). `[Ref: Aqua Security Cloud Native Threat Report June 2021]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Aqua Security Cloud Native Threat Report June 2021]

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilize a trust model such as Docker Content Trust with assinaturas digitais to ensure runtime verification of the integrity and publisher of specific image tags. `[Ref: Content trust in Docker]` `[Ref: Content trust in Azure Container Registry]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Recorrer a DLL Side-Loading (`T1574.002`) utilizando um executável legítimo assinado (vulnerável a sequestro de ordem de procura de DLL) que carregue a nossa DLL em memória, ou utilizar binários assinados nativos (LOLBAS - `T1218`). Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network prevention intrusion systems and systems designed to scan and remove malicious downloads pode ser utilizado para block activity.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

techniques.fullNameEn: User Execution: Malicious Copy and Paste
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Induzida pelo Utilizador: Malicious Copy and Paste
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode rely upon a user copying and pasting code com o objetivo de gain execution. Users may be subjected to engenharia social to get them to copy and paste code directly into a **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`). One such strategy is "ClickFix," in which adversaries present users with seemingly helpful solutions—such as prompts to fix errors or complete CAPTCHAs—that instead instruct the user to copy and paste código malicioso.

Malicious websites, such as those used in **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`), may present fake error messages or CAPTCHA prompts that instruct users to open a terminal or the Windows Run Dialog box and execute an arbitrary command. These commands may be obfuscated using encoding or other techniques to conceal malicious intent. Uma vez que executed, the adversary will typically be able to establish a foothold on the victim's machine. `[Ref: CloudSEK Lumma Stealer 2024]` `[Ref: Sekoia ClickFake 2025]` `[Ref: Reliaquest CAPTCHA 2024]` `[Ref: AhnLab LummaC2 2025]`

Os adversários podem também leverage phishing emails for this purpose. When a user attempts to open an attachment, they may be presented with a fake error and offered a malicious command to paste as a solution, consistent with the "ClickFix" strategy. `[Ref: Proofpoint ClickFix 2024]` `[Ref: AhnLab Malicioys Copy Paste 2024]`

Tricking a user into executing a command themselves may help para contornar (bypass) email filtering, browser sandboxing, or other mitigations designed to protect users against malicious downloaded files.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) where appropriate. PowerShell Constrained Language mode pode ser utilizado para restrict access to sensitive or otherwise dangerous language elements such as those used to execute arbitrary Windows APIs or files (e.g., `Add-Type`). `[Ref: Microsoft PowerShell CLM]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Induzida pelo Utilizador: Malicious Library
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem rely on a user installing a malicious library to facilitate execution. Threat actors may **Upload Malware** (`T1608.001`) to package managers such as NPM and PyPi, as well as to public code repositories such as GitHub. User may install libraries without realizing they are malicious, thus bypassing techniques that specifically achieve Initial Access. This can lead to the execution of código malicioso, such as code that establishes persistence, steals data, or mines cryptocurrency. `[Ref: Datadog Security Labs Malicious PyPi Packages 2024]` `[Ref: Fortinet Malicious NPM Packages 2023]`

In some cases, threat actors may compromise and backdoor existing popular libraries (i.e., **Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools** (`T1195.001`)). Alternatively, they may create entirely new packages and leverage behaviors such as typosquatting to encourage users to install them.

techniques.namePt: Sinalização de Tráfego (Port Knocking / Magic Packets)
techniques.fullNamePt: Sinalização de Tráfego (Port Knocking / Magic Packets)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar traffic signaling to hide open ports or other malicious functionality used for persistence or Command and Control (C2). Traffic signaling involves the use of a magic value or sequence that must be sent to a system to trigger a special response, such as opening a closed port or executing a malicious task. This may take the form of sending a series of packets with certain characteristics before a port will be opened that the adversary can use for Command and Control (C2). Usually this series of packets consists of attempted connections to a predefined sequence of closed ports (i.e. **Port Knocking** (`T1205.001`)), but can involve unusual flags, specific strings, or other unique characteristics. After the sequence is completed, opening a port may be accomplished by the host-based firewall, but could also be implemented by custom software.

Os adversários podem também communicate with an already open port, but the service listening on that port will only respond to commands or trigger other malicious functionality if passed the appropriate magic value(s).

The observation of the signal packets to trigger the communication can be conducted through different methods. One means, originally implemented by Cd00r  `[Ref: Hartrell cd00r 2002]`, is to use the libpcap libraries to sniff for the packets in question. Another method leverages raw sockets, which enables the malware to use ports that are already open for use by other programs.

On network devices, adversaries may use crafted packets to enable **Network Device Authentication** (`T1556.004`) for standard services offered by the device such as telnet.  Such signaling may also be used to open a closed service port such as telnet, or to trigger module modification of malware implants on the device, adding, removing, or changing malicious capabilities.  Os adversários podem utilizar crafted packets to attempt to connect to one or more (open or closed) ports, but may also attempt to connect to a router interface, broadcast, and network address IP on the same port com o objetivo de achieve their goals and objectives. `[Ref: Cisco Synful Knock Evolution]` `[Ref: Mandiant - Synful Knock]` `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`  To enable this traffic signaling on embedded devices, adversaries must first achieve and leverage **Patch System Image** (`T1601.001`) due to the monolithic nature of the architecture.

Os adversários podem também use the Wake-on-LAN feature to turn on powered off systems. Wake-on-LAN is a hardware feature that allows a powered down system to be powered on, or woken up, by sending a magic packet to it. Uma vez que the system is powered on, it may become a target for lateral movement. `[Ref: Bleeping Computer - Ryuk WoL]` `[Ref: AMD Magic Packet]`

mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

Another method leverages raw sockets, which enables the malware to use ports that are already open for use by other programs.

techniques.fullNamePt: Sinalização de Tráfego (Port Knocking / Magic Packets): Socket Filters
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem attach filters to a network socket to monitor then activate backdoors used for persistence or Command and Control (C2). With elevated permissions, adversaries can use features such as the `libpcap` library to open sockets and install filters to allow or disallow certain types of data to come through the socket. The filter may apply to all traffic passing through the specified network interface (or every interface if not specified). When the network interface receives a packet matching the filter criteria, additional actions can be triggered on the host, such as activation of a reverse shell.

To establish a connection, an adversary sends a crafted packet to the targeted host that matches the installed filter criteria. `[Ref: haking9 libpcap network sniffing]` Adversaries have used these socket filters to trigger the installation of implants, conduct ping backs, and to invoke command shells. Communication with these socket filters may also be used in conjunction with **Protocol Tunneling** (`T1572`). `[Ref: exatrack bpf filters passive backdoors]` `[Ref: Leonardo Turla Penquin May 2020]`

Filters can be installed on any Unix-like platform with `libpcap` installed or on Windows hosts using `Winpcap`.  Os adversários podem utilizar either `libpcap` with `pcap_setfilter` or the standard library function `setsockopt` with `SO_ATTACH_FILTER` options. Since the socket connection is not active until the packet is received, this behavior may be difficult to detect due to the lack of activity on a host, low CPU overhead, and limited visibility into raw socket usage.

techniques.fullNamePt: Rogue Domain Controller
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem register a rogue Domain Controller (DC) to enable manipulation of Active Directory (AD) data. DCShadow pode ser empregue para create a rogue Domain Controller (DC) (DC). DCShadow is a method of manipulating Active Directory (AD) (AD) data, including objects and schemas, by registering (or reusing an inactive registration) and simulating the behavior of a DC.  `[Ref: DCShadow Blog]` Uma vez que registered, a rogue DC may be able to inject and replicate changes into AD infrastructure for any domain object, including credentials and keys.

Registering a rogue DC involves creating a new server and nTDSDSA objects in the Configuration partition of the AD schema, which requires Administrator privileges (either Domain or local to the DC) or the KRBTGT hash.  `[Ref: Adsecurity Mimikatz Guide]`

This technique may bypass system logging and security monitors such as security information and event management (SIEM) products (since actions taken on a rogue DC may not be reported to these sensors).  `[Ref: DCShadow Blog]` The technique may also be used to alter and delete replication and other associated metadata to obstruct forensic analysis. Os adversários podem também utilize this technique to perform **SID-History Injection** (`T1134.005`) and/or manipulate AD objects (such as accounts, access control lists, schemas) to establish backdoors for Persistence.  `[Ref: DCShadow Blog]`

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Rogue Domain Controller (DCShadow) Registration and Replication Abuse

analytics.name: Analytic 0770
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection of rogue Domain Controller (DC) registration and Active Directory (AD) replication abuse by correlating: (1) creation/modification of nTDSDSA and server objects in the Configuration partition, (2) unexpected usage of Directory Replication Service SPNs (GC/ or E3514235-4B06-11D1-AB04-00C04FC2DCD2), (3) replication RPC calls (DrsAddEntry, DrsReplicaAdd, GetNCChanges) originating from non-DC hosts, and (4) Kerberos authentication by non-DC machines using DRS-related SPNs. These events in combination, especially from hosts outside the Domain Controller (DC)s OU, may indicate DCShadow or rogue DC activity.

techniques.fullNamePt: Exploração de Serviços Remotos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem explorar remote services to gain unauthorized access to internal systems once inside of a network. Exploitation of a software vulnerability occurs when an adversary takes advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the sistema operativo software or kernel itself to execute adversary-controlled code. A common goal for post-compromise exploitation of remote services is for lateral movement to enable access to a remote system.

Um adversário pode need to determine if the remote system is in a vulnerable state, which may be done through **Network Service Discovery** (`T1046`) or other Discovery methods looking for common, vulnerable software that may be deployed in the network, the lack of certain patches that may indicate vulnerabilities,  or security software that pode ser empregue para detect or contain remote exploitation. Servers are likely a high value target for lateral movement exploitation, but endpoint systems may also be at risk if they provide an advantage or access to additional resources.

There are several well-known vulnerabilities that exist in common services such as SMB `[Ref: CIS Multiple SMB Vulnerabilities]` and RDP `[Ref: NVD CVE-2017-0176]` as well as applications that may be used within internal networks such as MySQL `[Ref: NVD CVE-2016-6662]` and web server services. `[Ref: NVD CVE-2014-7169]` `[Ref: Ars Technica VMWare Code Execution Vulnerability 2021]` Additionally, there have been a number of vulnerabilities in VMware vCenter installations, which may enable threat actors para realizar movimentação lateral from the compromised vCenter server to máquina virtual (VM)s or even to ESXi hypervisors. `[Ref: Broadcom VMSA-2024-0019]`

Dependendo de the permissions level of the vulnerable remote service an adversary may achieve **Exploitation for Privilege Escalation** (`T1068`) as a result of lateral movement exploitation as well.
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Ars Technica VMWare Code Execution Vulnerability 2021]

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Minimize available services to only those that are necessary.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Vulnerability Scanning
mitigations.descriptionPt: Regularly scan the internal network for available services to identify new and potentially vulnerable services.

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Security applications that look for behavior used during exploitation such as Windows Defender Exploit Guard (WDEG) and the Enhanced Mitigation Experience Toolkit (EMET) pode ser utilizado para mitigate some exploitation behavior.  `[Ref: TechNet Moving Beyond EMET]` Control flow integrity checking is another way to potentially identify and stop a software exploit from occurring.  `[Ref: Wikipedia Control Flow Integrity]` Many of these protections depend on the architecture and target application binary for compatibility and may not work for all software or services targeted.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Segment networks and systems appropriately to reduce access to critical systems and services to controlled methods.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Threat Intelligence Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Develop a robust cyber threat intelligence capability to determine what types and levels of threat may use software exploits and 0-days against a particular organization.

mitigations.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Make it difficult for adversaries to advance their operation through exploitation of undiscovered or unpatched vulnerabilities by using sandboxing. Other types of virtualization and application microsegmentation may also mitigate the impact of some types of exploitation. Risks of additional exploits and weaknesses in these systems may still exist.  `[Ref: Ars Technica Pwn2Own 2017 VM Escape]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Minimize permissions and access for service accounts to limit impact of exploitation.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Update software regularly by employing patch management for internal enterprise endpoints and servers.

blockers: M1042 (Disable or Remove Feature or Program): `powershell.exe` bloqueado por GPO, ou Macros VBA desativadas por política de Mark-of-the-Web (MotW).
M1030 (Network Segmentation): Sem conectividade direta da sub-rede atual para servidores de produção ou Domain Controllers.
M1026 (Privileged Account Management): Pass-the-Hash com conta de Administrador Local (`RID 500`) falha noutros hosts porque cada máquina possui password única gerida pelo LAPS.
Segmentação de rede (VLANs), bloqueio de portas administrativas (445/5985/3389), SMB Signing obrigatório ou restrições de NTLM.
bypasses: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

Pivotar para protocolos alternativos como DCOM (`MMC20.Application`), WMI sobre RPC, MSSQL Links (`1433`), RDP em modo `RestrictedAdmin`, ou autenticação Kerberos com chaves AES256 (`Overpass-the-Hash`) usando o FQDN do host em vez do endereço IP.
blindSpots: **ServicePortSet**: List of monitored service ports (default: 445,135,3389,5985,5986,1433,3306).
**TimeWindow**: Correlation window between inbound access and crash/child-process (default: 10 minutes).
**AllowedAdminCIDRs**: Known management networks to suppress benign admin traffic.
**MinConnErrorRate**: Percent of failed/aborted connections to treat as anomalous (default: 30%).
**ServiceNames**: Linux daemons to watch (sshd, smbd, nfsd, httpd/nginx, mysqld, postgres, redis).

techniques.fullNamePt: Exploitation for Stealth
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem explorar vulnerabilities para evadir deteção by hiding activity, suppressing logging, or operating within trusted or unmonitored components. 

Os adversários podem explorar a system or application vulnerability para evitar deteção while maintaining access dentro do ambiente alvo. Exploitation occurs when an adversary leverages a programming flaw to execute code in a manner that minimizes visibility or blends in with legitimate activity. 

Rather than directly disabling defenses, adversaries may use exploitation to circumvent monitoring and logging mechanisms. This can include abusing vulnerabilities in logging pipelines, security tools, or cloud infrastructure to evade audit trails, suppress alerts, or operate without generating telemetry. 

Os adversários podem identify these opportunities through prior reconnaissance or by performing discovery of controlos de segurança after initial access. In some cases, vulnerabilities in SaaS or public cloud environments may be exploited to evade logging, obscure activity, or deploy infrastructure that remains hidden from standard monitoring tools. `[Ref: Bypassing CloudTrail in AWS Service Catalog]` `[Ref: GhostToken GCP flaw]`

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Security applications that look for behavior used during exploitation such as Windows Defender Exploit Guard (WDEG) and the Enhanced Mitigation Experience Toolkit (EMET) pode ser utilizado para mitigate some exploitation behavior.  `[Ref: TechNet Moving Beyond EMET]` Control flow integrity checking is another way to potentially identify and stop a software exploit from occurring.  `[Ref: Wikipedia Control Flow Integrity]` Many of these protections depend on the architecture and target application binary for compatibility and may not work for software targeted for defense evasion.

techniques.fullNamePt: Exploração para Acesso a Credenciais
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem explorar software vulnerabilities in an attempt to collect credentials. Exploitation of a software vulnerability occurs when an adversary takes advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the sistema operativo software or kernel itself to execute adversary-controlled code. 

Credentialing and authentication mechanisms may be targeted for exploitation by adversaries as a means para obter acesso a useful credentials or circumvent the process to gain authenticated access to systems. One example of this is `MS14-068`, which targets Kerberos and pode ser utilizado para forge Kerberos tickets using domain user permissions. `[Ref: Technet MS14-068]` `[Ref: ADSecurity Detecting Forged Tickets]` Another example of this is replay attacks, in which the adversary intercepts data packets sent between parties and then later replays these packets. If services don't properly validate authentication requests, these replayed packets may allow an adversary to impersonate one of the parties and gain unauthorized access or privileges. `[Ref: Bugcrowd Replay Attack]` `[Ref: Comparitech Replay Attack]` `[Ref: Microsoft Midnight Blizzard Replay Attack]`

Such exploitation has been demonstrated in cloud environments as well. Por exemplo, adversaries have exploited vulnerabilities in public cloud infrastructure that allowed for unintended authentication token creation and renewal. `[Ref: Storm-0558 techniques for unauthorized email access]`

Exploitation for credential access may also result in Privilege Escalation depending on the process targeted or credentials obtained.
