techniques.fullNamePt: Restrições Ambientais de Execução (Execution Guardrails)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar execution guardrails to constrain execution or actions based on adversary supplied and environment specific conditions that are expected to be present on the target. Guardrails ensure that a payload only executes against an intended target and reduces collateral damage from an adversary’s campaign. `[Ref: FireEye Kevin Mandia Guardrails]` Values an adversary can provide about a target system or environment to use as guardrails may include specific network share names, attached physical devices, files, joined Active Directory (AD) (AD) domains, and local/external IP addresses. `[Ref: FireEye Outlook Dec 2019]`

Guardrails pode ser utilizado para prevent exposure of capabilities in environments that are not intended to be compromised or operated within. This use of guardrails is distinct from typical **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`). While use of **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`) may involve checking for known sandbox values and continuing with execution only if there is no match, the use of guardrails will involve checking for an expected target-specific value and only continuing with execution if there is such a match.

Os adversários podem identify and block certain user-agents to evade defenses and narrow the scope of their attack to victims and platforms on which it will be most effective. A user-agent self-identifies data such as a user's software application, sistema operativo, vendor, and version. Os adversários podem check user-agents for sistema operativo identification and then only serve malware for the exploitable software while ignoring all other sistema operativos. `[Ref: Trellix-Qakbot]`

mitigations.name: Do Not Mitigate
mitigations.descriptionPt: **Execution Guardrails** (`T1480`) likely should not be mitigated with preventative controls because it may protect unintended targets from being compromised. If targeted, efforts should be focused on preventing adversary tools from running earlier in the chain of activity and on identifying subsequent malicious behavior if compromised.

techniques.fullNamePt: Restrições Ambientais de Execução (Execution Guardrails): Environmental Keying
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem environmentally key payloads or other features of malware to evade defenses and constraint execution to a specific target environment. Environmental keying uses cryptography to constrain execution or actions based on adversary supplied environment specific conditions that are expected to be present on the target. Environmental keying is an implementation of **Execution Guardrails** (`T1480`) that utilizes cryptographic techniques for deriving encryption/decryption keys from specific types of values in a given computing environment. `[Ref: EK Clueless Agents]`

Values can be derived from target-specific elements and used to generate a decryption key for an encrypted payload. Target-specific values can be derived from specific network shares, physical devices, software/software versions, files, joined AD domains, system time, and local/external IP addresses. `[Ref: Kaspersky Gauss Whitepaper]` `[Ref: Proofpoint Router Malvertising]` `[Ref: EK Impeding Malware Analysis]` `[Ref: Environmental Keyed HTA]` By generating the decryption keys from target-specific environmental values, environmental keying can make sandbox detection, anti-virus detection, crowdsourcing of information, and reverse engineering difficult. `[Ref: Kaspersky Gauss Whitepaper]` These difficulties can slow down the incident response process and help adversaries hide their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).

De forma semelhante a **Obfuscated Files or Information** (`T1027`), adversaries may use environmental keying to help protect their TTPs and evade detection. Environmental keying pode ser empregue para deliver an encrypted payload to the target that will use target-specific values to decrypt the payload before execution. `[Ref: Kaspersky Gauss Whitepaper]` `[Ref: EK Impeding Malware Analysis]` `[Ref: Environmental Keyed HTA]` `[Ref: Demiguise Guardrail Router Logo]` By utilizing target-specific values to decrypt the payload the adversary can avoid packaging the decryption key with the payload or sending it over a potentially monitored network connection. Dependendo de the technique for gathering target-specific values, reverse engineering of the encrypted payload can be exceptionally difficult. `[Ref: Kaspersky Gauss Whitepaper]` This pode ser utilizado para prevent exposure of capabilities in environments that are not intended to be compromised or operated within.

Like other **Execution Guardrails** (`T1480`), environmental keying pode ser utilizado para prevent exposure of capabilities in environments that are not intended to be compromised or operated within. This activity is distinct from typical **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`). While use of **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`) may involve checking for known sandbox values and continuing with execution only if there is no match, the use of environmental keying will involve checking for an expected target-specific value that must match for decryption and subsequent execution to be successful.

mitigations.name: Do Not Mitigate
mitigations.descriptionPt: **Environmental Keying** (`T1480.001`) likely should not be mitigated with preventative controls because it may protect unintended targets from being compromised via confusion of keys by the adversary. Mitigation of this technique is also unlikely to be feasible within most contexts because there are no standard attributes from which an adversary may derive keys. If targeted, efforts should be focused on preventing adversary tools from running earlier in the chain of activity and on identifying subsequent malicious behavior if compromised.

techniques.fullNamePt: Restrições Ambientais de Execução (Execution Guardrails): Mutual Exclusion
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem constrain execution or actions based on the presence of a mutex associated with malware. A mutex is a locking mechanism used to synchronize access to a resource. Only one thread or process can acquire a mutex at a given time. `[Ref: Microsoft Mutexes]`

While local mutexes only exist within a given process, allowing multiple threads to synchronize access to a resource, system mutexes pode ser utilizado para synchronize the activities of multiple processes. `[Ref: Microsoft Mutexes]` By creating a unique system mutex associated with a particular malware, adversaries can verify whether or not a system has already been compromised. `[Ref: Sans Mutexes 2012]`

In Linux environments, malware may instead attempt to acquire a lock on a mutex file. If the malware is able to acquire the lock, it continues to execute; if it fails, it exits to avoid creating a second instance of itself. `[Ref: Intezer RedXOR 2021]` `[Ref: Deep Instinct BPFDoor 2023]`

Mutex names may be hard-coded or dynamically generated using a predictable algorithm. `[Ref: ICS Mutexes 2015]`

mitigations.name: Do Not Mitigate
mitigations.descriptionPt: **Execution Guardrails** (`T1480`) likely should not be mitigated with preventative controls because it may protect unintended targets from being compromised. If targeted, efforts should be focused on preventing adversary tools from running earlier in the chain of activity and on identifying subsequent malicious behavior if compromised.

analytics.name: Analytic 0372
analytics.descriptionPt: Adversary-created named mutex using system APIs (e.g., CreateMutexW) followed by conditional process termination or alternate code path indicating malware avoiding reinfection.

mutableElements.description: Filter out common benign mutex names; highlight suspicious high-entropy/dynamic names.
Limit alerting to non-standard parent-child relationships indicative of malware staging or self-spawning.
Correlate mutex creation + rapid process exit or lack of further activity within a short timeframe.

mutableElements.description: Detect patterns like /tmp/.lock*, /var/run/*lock used by malware.
Track specific exit codes (e.g., 1, 2) that signal lock acquisition failure.
Correlate lockfile access + early process termination within N seconds.

techniques.namePt: Descoberta de Relações de Confiança (Domain Trusts)
techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Relações de Confiança (Domain Trusts)
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar gather information on domain trust relationships that pode ser empregue para identify lateral movement opportunities in Windows multi-domain/forest environments. Domain trusts provide a mechanism for a domain to allow access to resources based on the authentication procedures of another domain. `[Ref: Microsoft Trusts]` Domain trusts allow the users of the trusted domain to access resources in the trusting domain. The information discovered may help the adversary conduct **SID-History Injection** (`T1134.005`), **Pass the Ticket** (`T1550.003`), and **Kerberoasting** (`T1558.003`). `[Ref: AdSecurity Forging Trust Tickets]` `[Ref: Harmj0y Domain Trusts]` Domain trusts can be enumerated using the `DSEnumerateDomainTrusts()` Win32 API call, .NET methods, and LDAP. `[Ref: Harmj0y Domain Trusts]` The Windows utility **Nltest** (`S0359`) is known to be used by adversaries to enumerate domain trusts. `[Ref: Microsoft Operation Wilysupply]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Map the trusts within existing domains/forests and keep trust relationships to a minimum.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Employ network segmentation for sensitive domains. `[Ref: Harmj0y Domain Trusts]`.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar the configuration settings of a domain or identity tenant to evade defenses and/or escalate privileges in centrally managed environments. Such services provide a centralized means of managing identity resources such as devices and accounts, and often include configuration settings that may apply between domains or tenants such as trust relationships, identity syncing, or identity federation.

Modifications to domain or tenant settings may include altering domain Group Policy Objects (GPOs) in Microsoft Active Directory (AD) (AD) or changing trust settings for domains, including federation trusts relationships between domains or tenants.

With sufficient permissions, adversaries can modify domain or tenant policy settings. Since configuration settings for these services apply to a large number of identity resources, there are a great number of potential attacks malicious outcomes that can stem from this abuse. Examples of such abuse include:  

* modifying GPOs to push a malicious **Scheduled Task** (`T1053.005`) to computers throughout the domain environment `[Ref: ADSecurity GPO Persistence 2016]` `[Ref: Wald0 Guide to GPOs]` `[Ref: Harmj0y Abusing GPO Permissions]`
* modifying domain trusts to include an adversary-controlled domain, allowing adversaries to  forge access tokens that will subsequently be accepted by victim domain resources `[Ref: Microsoft - Customer Guidance on Recent Nation-State Cyber Attacks]`
* changing configuration settings within the AD environment to implement a **Rogue Domain Controller (DC)** (`T1207`).
* adding new, adversary-controlled federated identity providers to identity tenants, allowing adversaries to authenticate as any user managed by the victim tenant  `[Ref: Okta Cross-Tenant Impersonation 2023]`

Os adversários podem temporarily modify domain or tenant policy, carry out a malicious action(s), and then revert the change to remove suspicious indicators.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Identify and correct GPO permissions abuse opportunities (ex: GPO modification privileges) using auditing tools such as **BloodHound** (`S0521`) (version 1.5.1 and later) `[Ref: GitHub Bloodhound]`.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use least privilege and protect administrative access to the Domain Controller (DC) and Active Directory (AD) Federation Services (AD FS) server. Do not create service accounts with privilégios administrativos.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification
techniques.fullNamePt: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar Group Policy Objects (GPOs) to subvert the intended discretionary access controls for a domain, usually with the intention of escalating privileges on the domain. Group policy allows for centralized management of user and computer settings in Active Directory (AD) (AD). GPOs are containers for group policy settings made up of files stored within a predictable network path `\<DOMAIN>\SYSVOL\<DOMAIN>\Policies\`. `[Ref: TechNet Group Policy Basics]` `[Ref: ADSecurity GPO Persistence 2016]` 

Like other objects in AD, GPOs have access controls associated with them. By default all user accounts in the domain have permission to read GPOs. It is possible to delegate GPO access control permissions, e.g. write access, to specific users or groups in the domain.

Malicious GPO modifications pode ser utilizado para implement many other malicious behaviors such as **Scheduled Task/Job** (`T1053`), **Disable or Modify Tools** (`T1685`), **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`), **Create Account** (`T1136`), **Service Execution** (`T1569.002`),  and more. `[Ref: ADSecurity GPO Persistence 2016]` `[Ref: Wald0 Guide to GPOs]` `[Ref: Harmj0y Abusing GPO Permissions]` `[Ref: Mandiant M Trends 2016]` `[Ref: Microsoft Hacking Team Breach]` Since GPOs can control so many user and machine settings in the AD environment, there are a great number of potential attacks that can stem from this GPO abuse. `[Ref: Wald0 Guide to GPOs]`

Por exemplo, publicly available scripts such as `New-GPOImmediateTask` can be leveraged to automate the creation of a malicious **Scheduled Task/Job** (`T1053`) by modifying GPO settings, in this case modifying `<GPO_PATH>\Machine\Preferences\ScheduledTasks\ScheduledTasks.xml`. `[Ref: Wald0 Guide to GPOs]` `[Ref: Harmj0y Abusing GPO Permissions]` In some cases an adversary might modify specific user rights like SeEnableDelegationPrivilege, set in `<GPO_PATH>\MACHINE\Microsoft\Windows NT\SecEdit\GptTmpl.inf`, to achieve a subtle AD backdoor with complete control of the domain because the user account under the adversary's control would then be able to modify GPOs. `[Ref: Harmj0y SeEnableDelegationPrivilege Right]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Trust Modification
techniques.fullNamePt: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Trust Modification
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem add new domain trusts, modify the properties of existing domain trusts, or otherwise change the configuration of trust relationships between domains and tenants to evade defenses and/or elevate privileges.Trust details, such as whether or not user identities are federated, allow authentication and authorization properties to apply between domains or tenants for the purpose of accessing shared resources. `[Ref: Microsoft - Azure AD Federation]` These trust objects may include accounts, credentials, and other authentication material applied to servers, tokens, and domains.

Manipulating these trusts may allow an adversary para escalar privilégios and/or evade defenses by modifying settings to add objects which they control. Por exemplo, in Microsoft Active Directory (AD) (AD) environments, this pode ser empregue para forge **SAML Tokens** (`T1606.002`) without the need to compromise the signing certificate to forge new credentials. Instead, an adversary can manipulate domain trusts to add their own signing certificate. Um adversário pode also convert an AD domain to a federated domain using Active Directory (AD) Federation Services (AD FS), which may enable malicious trust modifications such as altering the claim issuance rules to log in any valid set of credentials as a specified user. `[Ref: AADInternals zure AD Federated Domain]` 

Um adversário pode also add a new federated identity provider to an identity tenant such as Okta or AWS IAM Identity Center, which may enable the adversary to authenticate as any user of the tenant. `[Ref: Okta Cross-Tenant Impersonation 2023]` This may enable the threat actor to gain broad access into a variety of cloud-based services that leverage the identity tenant. Por exemplo, in AWS environments, an adversary that creates a new identity provider for an AWS Organization will be able to federate into all of the AWS Organization member accounts without creating identities for each of the member accounts. `[Ref: AWS re Inforce Trust Mod]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use the principal of least privilege and protect administrative access to domain trusts and identity tenants.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Em ambientes Cloud, limit permissions to create new identity providers to only those accounts that require them. In AWS environments, consider using Service Control policies to limit the use of API calls such as `CreateSAMLProvider` or `CreateOpenIDConnectProvider`.

Explorar objetos COM auto-elevados (`ICMLuaUtil`), sequestro de chaves em `HKCU\Software\Classes` lidas por binários `autoElevate`, abuso de privilégios de Token (`SeImpersonatePrivilege` via PrintSpoofer/GodPotato) ou DLL Hijacking em serviços `SYSTEM`.
blindSpots: **ObjectType**: Focus on `trustedDomain` or `foreignSecurityPrincipal` AD objects in trust containers.
**AttributeModified**: Monitor attributes like `trustPartner`, `trustDirection`, `trustType`, `msDS-TrustForestTrustInfo`.
**TimeWindow**: Correlate trust creation with unusual logon events or certificate modifications.
**UserContext**: Flag rare accounts or non-standard admin users performing trust changes.
**OperationName**: Identify rare trust-modification operations (SetDomainAuthentication, Update-MsolFederatedDomain).

techniques.fullNamePt: Destruição de Dados
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem destruir data and files on specific systems or in large numbers on a network to interrupt availability to systems, services, and network resources. Data destruction is likely to render stored data irrecoverable by forensic techniques through overwriting files or data on local and remote drives. `[Ref: Symantec Shamoon 2012]` `[Ref: FireEye Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Kaspersky StoneDrill 2017]` `[Ref: Unit 42 Shamoon3 2018]` `[Ref: Talos Olympic Destroyer 2018]` Common sistema operativo file deletion commands such as `del` and `rm` often only remove pointers to files without wiping the contents of the files themselves, making the files recoverable by proper forensic methodology. This behavior is distinct from **Disk Content Wipe** (`T1561.001`) and **Disk Structure Wipe** (`T1561.002`) because individual files are destroyed rather than sections of a storage disk or the disk's logical structure.

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar overwrite files and directories with randomly generated data to make it irrecoverable. `[Ref: Kaspersky StoneDrill 2017]` `[Ref: Unit 42 Shamoon3 2018]` In some cases politically oriented image files have been used to overwrite data. `[Ref: FireEye Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Kaspersky StoneDrill 2017]`

To maximize impact on the organização alvo in operations where network-wide availability interruption is the goal, malware designed for destroying data may have worm-like features to propagate across a network by leveraging additional techniques like **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`), **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`), and **SMB/Windows Admin Shares** (`T1021.002`). `[Ref: Symantec Shamoon 2012]` `[Ref: FireEye Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Kaspersky StoneDrill 2017]` `[Ref: Talos Olympic Destroyer 2018]`.

Em ambientes Cloud, adversaries may leverage access to delete cloud storage objects, machine images, database instances, and other infrastructure crucial to operations to damage an organization or their customers. `[Ref: Data Destruction - Threat Post]` `[Ref: DOJ  - Cisco Insider]` Similarly, they may delete máquina virtual (VM)s from on-prem virtualized environments.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar multi-factor authentication (MFA) delete for cloud storage resources, such as AWS S3 buckets, to prevent unauthorized deletion of critical data and infrastructure. MFA delete requires additional authentication steps, making it significantly more difficult for adversaries to destroy data without proper credentials. This additional security layer helps protect against the impact of data destruction in cloud environments by ensuring that only authenticated actions can irreversibly delete storage or machine images.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Data Backup
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for taking regular data backups that pode ser utilizado para restore organizational data. `[Ref: Ready.gov IT DRP]` Ensure backups are stored off system and protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and destroy the backups to prevent recovery.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Em ambientes Cloud, limit permissions to modify cloud bucket lifecycle policies (e.g., `PutLifecycleConfiguration` in AWS) to only those accounts that require it. In AWS environments, consider using Service Control policies to limit the use of the `PutBucketLifecycle` API call.

techniques.fullNamePt: Destruição de Dados: Lifecycle-Triggered Deletion
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar the lifecycle policies of a cloud storage bucket to destroy all objects stored within.  

Cloud storage buckets often allow users to set lifecycle policies to automate the migration, archival, or deletion of objects after a set period of time. `[Ref: AWS Storage Lifecycles]` `[Ref: GCP Storage Lifecycles]` `[Ref: Azure Storage Lifecycles]` If a threat actor has sufficient permissions to modify these policies, they may be able to delete all objects at once. 

Por exemplo, in AWS environments, an adversary with the `PutLifecycleConfiguration` permission may use the `PutBucketLifecycle` API call to apply a lifecycle policy to an S3 bucket that deletes all objects in the bucket after one day. `[Ref: Palo Alto Cloud Ransomware]` `[Ref: Halcyon AWS Ransomware 2025]` Adicionalmente a destroying data for purposes of extortion and **Financial Theft** (`T1657`), adversaries may also perform this action on buckets storing cloud logs for **Indicator Removal** (`T1070`). `[Ref: Datadog S3 Lifecycle CloudTrail Logs]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Em ambientes Cloud, limit permissions to modify cloud bucket lifecycle policies (e.g., `PutLifecycleConfiguration` in AWS) to only those accounts that require it. In AWS environments, consider using Service Control policies to limit the use of the `PutBucketLifecycle` API call.

This is often used to trigger impact (destruction), remove logs (defense evasion), or force extortion (ransomware).

techniques.fullNamePt: Encriptação de Dados para Impacto (Ransomware)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem encriptar data on target systems or on large numbers of systems in a network to interrupt availability to system and network resources. They can attempt to render stored data inaccessible by encrypting files or data on local and remote drives and withholding access to a decryption key. This may be done com o objetivo de extract monetary compensation from a victim in exchange for decryption or a decryption key (ransomware) or to render data permanently inaccessible in cases where the key is not saved or transmitted. `[Ref: US-CERT Ransomware 2016]` `[Ref: FireEye WannaCry 2017]` `[Ref: US-CERT NotPetya 2017]` `[Ref: US-CERT SamSam 2018]`

In the case of ransomware, it is typical that common user files like Office documents, PDFs, images, videos, audio, text, and source code files will be encrypted (and often renamed and/or tagged with specific file markers). Os adversários podem need to first employ other behaviors, such as **File and Directory Permissions Modification** (`T1222`) or **System Shutdown/Reboot** (`T1529`), com o objetivo de unlock and/or gain access to manipulate these files. `[Ref: CarbonBlack Conti July 2020]` In some cases, adversaries may encrypt critical system files, disk partitions, and the MBR. `[Ref: US-CERT NotPetya 2017]` Os adversários podem também encrypt máquina virtual (VM)s hosted on ESXi or other hypervisors. `[Ref: Crowdstrike Hypervisor Jackpotting Pt 2 2021]` 

To maximize impact on the organização alvo, malware designed for encrypting data may have worm-like features to propagate across a network by leveraging other attack techniques like **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`), **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`), and **SMB/Windows Admin Shares** (`T1021.002`). `[Ref: FireEye WannaCry 2017]` `[Ref: US-CERT NotPetya 2017]` Encryption malware may also leverage **Internal Defacement** (`T1491.001`), such as changing victim wallpapers or ESXi server login messages, or otherwise intimidate victims by sending ransom notes or other messages to connected printers (known as "print bombing"). `[Ref: NHS Digital Egregor Nov 2020]` `[Ref: Varonis]`

Em ambientes Cloud, storage objects within compromised accounts may also be encrypted. `[Ref: Rhino S3 Ransomware Part 1]` Por exemplo, in AWS environments, adversaries may leverage services such as AWS’s Server-Side Encryption with Customer Provided Keys (SSE-C) to encrypt data. `[Ref: Halcyon AWS Ransomware 2025]`

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable cloud-delivered protection and Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to block the execution of files that resemble ransomware. `[Ref: win10_asr]` In AWS environments, create an IAM policy to restrict or block the use of SSE-C on S3 buckets. `[Ref: Halcyon AWS Ransomware 2025]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: Data Backup
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for regularly taking and testing data backups that pode ser utilizado para restore organizational data. `[Ref: Ready.gov IT DRP]` Ensure backups are stored off system and is protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and destroy the backups to prevent recovery. Consider enabling versioning in cloud environments to maintain backup copies of storage objects. `[Ref: Rhino S3 Ransomware Part 2]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Paragem de Serviços Críticos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem stop or disable services on a system to render those services unavailable to legitimate users. Stopping critical services or processes can inhibit or stop response to an incident or aid in the adversary's overall objectives to cause damage to the environment. `[Ref: Talos Olympic Destroyer 2018]` `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster]` 

Os adversários podem accomplish this by disabling individual services of high importance to an organization, such as `MSExchangeIS`, which will make Exchange content inaccessible. `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster]` In some cases, adversaries may stop or disable many or all services to render systems unusable. `[Ref: Talos Olympic Destroyer 2018]` Services or processes may not allow for modification of their data stores while running. Os adversários podem stop services or processes com o objetivo de conduct **Data Destruction** (`T1485`) or **Data Encrypted for Impact** (`T1486`) on the data stores of services like Exchange and SQL Server, or on máquina virtual (VM)s hosted on ESXi infrastructure. `[Ref: SecureWorks WannaCry Analysis]` `[Ref: Crowdstrike Hypervisor Jackpotting Pt 2 2021]`

Threat actors may also disable or stop service in cloud environments. Por exemplo, by leveraging the `DisableAPIServiceAccess` API in AWS, a threat actor may prevent the service from creating service-linked roles on new accounts in the AWS Organization. `[Ref: Datadog Security Labs Cloud Persistence 2025]` `[Ref: AWS DisableAWSServiceAccess]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Inibição de Recuperação do Sistema
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem eliminar or remove built-in data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery. `[Ref: Talos Olympic Destroyer 2018]` `[Ref: FireEye WannaCry 2017]` This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Os adversários podem desativar or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of **Data Destruction** (`T1485`) and **Data Encrypted for Impact** (`T1486`). `[Ref: Talos Olympic Destroyer 2018]` `[Ref: FireEye WannaCry 2017]` Ademais, adversaries may disable recovery notifications, then corrupt backups. `[Ref: disable_notif_synology_ransom]`

A number of native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:

* `vssadmin.exe` pode ser utilizado para delete all volume shadow copies on a system - `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet`
* **Windows Management Instrumentation** (`T1047`) pode ser utilizado para delete volume shadow copies - `wmic shadowcopy delete`
* `wbadmin.exe` pode ser utilizado para delete the Windows Backup Catalog - `wbadmin.exe delete catalog -quiet`
* `bcdedit.exe` pode ser utilizado para disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data - `bcdedit.exe /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled no`
* `REAgentC.exe` pode ser utilizado para disable Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) repair/recovery options of an infected system
* `diskshadow.exe` pode ser utilizado para delete all volume shadow copies on a system - `diskshadow delete shadows all`  `[Ref: Diskshadow]`  `[Ref: Crytox Ransomware]`

On network devices, adversaries may leverage **Disk Wipe** (`T1561`) to delete backup firmware images and reformat the sistema de ficheiros, then **System Shutdown/Reboot** (`T1529`) to reload the device. Together this activity may leave network devices completely inoperable and inhibit recovery operations.

On ESXi servers, adversaries may delete or encrypt snapshots of máquina virtual (VM)s to support **Data Encrypted for Impact** (`T1486`), preventing them from being leveraged as backups (e.g., via ` vim-cmd vmsvc/snapshot.removeall`). `[Ref: Cybereason]`

Os adversários podem também delete “online” backups that are connected to their network – whether via network storage media or through folders that sync to cloud services. `[Ref: ZDNet Ransomware Backups 2020]` Em ambientes Cloud, adversaries may disable versioning and backup policies and delete snapshots, database backups, machine images, and prior versions of objects designed to be used in disaster recovery scenarios. `[Ref: Dark Reading Code Spaces Cyber Attack]` `[Ref: Rhino Security Labs AWS S3 Ransomware]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider using application control configured to block execution of utilities such as `diskshadow.exe` that may not be required for a given system or network to prevent potential misuse by adversaries.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider technical controls to prevent the disabling of services or deletion of files involved in system recovery. Additionally, ensure that WinRE is enabled using the following command: `reagentc /enable`. `[Ref: reagentc_cmd]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the user accounts that have access to backups to only those required. In AWS environments, consider using Service Control Policies to restrict API calls to delete backups, snapshots, and images.

mitigations.name: Data Backup
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for taking regular data backups that pode ser utilizado para restore organizational data. `[Ref: Ready.gov IT DRP]` Ensure backups are stored off system and is protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and destroy the backups to prevent recovery. Em ambientes Cloud, enable versioning on storage objects where possible, and copy backups to other accounts or regions to isolate them from the original copies. `[Ref: Unit 42 Palo Alto Ransomware in Public Clouds 2022]` On ESXi servers, ensure that disk images and snapshots of máquina virtual (VM)s are regularly taken, with copies stored off system. `[Ref: Crowdstrike Hypervisor Jackpotting Pt 2 2021]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Defacement: External Defacement
techniques.descriptionPt: Um adversário pode deface systems external to an organization in an attempt to deliver messaging, intimidate, or otherwise mislead an organization or users. **External Defacement** (`T1491.002`) may ultimately cause users to distrust the systems and to question/discredit the system’s integrity. Externally-facing websites are a common victim of defacement; often targeted by adversary and hacktivist groups com o objetivo de push a political message or spread propaganda. `[Ref: FireEye Cyber Threats to Media Industries]` `[Ref: Kevin Mandia Statement to US Senate Committee on Intelligence]` `[Ref: Anonymous Hackers Deface Russian Govt Site]` **External Defacement** (`T1491.002`) may be used as a catalyst to trigger events, or as a response to actions taken by an organization or government. Similarly, website defacement may also be used as setup, or a precursor, for future attacks such as **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`). `[Ref: Trend Micro Deep Dive Into Defacement]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Firmware Corruption
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem sobrescrever or corrupt the flash memory contents of system BIOS or other firmware in devices attached to a system com o objetivo de render them inoperable or unable to boot, thus denying the availability to use the devices and/or the system. `[Ref: Symantec Chernobyl W95.CIH]` Firmware is software that is loaded and executed from non-volatile memory on hardware devices com o objetivo de initialize and manage device functionality. These devices may include the motherboard, hard drive, or video cards.

In general, adversaries may manipulate, overwrite, or corrupt firmware com o objetivo de deny the use of the system or devices. Por exemplo, corruption of firmware responsible for loading the sistema operativo for network devices may render the network devices inoperable. `[Ref: dhs_threat_to_net_devices]` `[Ref: cisa_malware_orgs_ukraine]` Dependendo de the device, this attack may also result in **Data Destruction** (`T1485`).

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Patch the BIOS and other firmware as necessary to prevent successful use of known vulnerabilities.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent adversary access to privileged accounts or access necessary to replace system firmware.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Recursos Computacionais
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de the resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability. 

Resource hijacking may take a number of different forms. Por exemplo, adversaries may:

* Leverage compute resources com o objetivo de mine cryptocurrency
* Sell network bandwidth to proxy networks
* Generate SMS traffic for profit
* Abuse cloud-based messaging services to send large quantities of spam messages

In some cases, adversaries may leverage multiple types of Resource Hijacking at once. `[Ref: Sysdig Cryptojacking Proxyjacking 2023]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Recursos Computacionais: Compute Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de the compute resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability. 

One common purpose for **Compute Hijacking** (`T1496.001`) is to validate transactions of cryptocurrency networks and earn virtual currency. Os adversários podem consume enough system resources to negatively impact and/or cause affected machines to become unresponsive. `[Ref: Kaspersky Lazarus Under The Hood Blog 2017]` Servers and cloud-based systems are common targets because of the high potential for available resources, but user endpoint systems may also be compromised and used for **Compute Hijacking** (`T1496.001`) and cryptocurrency mining. `[Ref: CloudSploit - Unused AWS Regions]` Containerized environments may also be targeted due to the ease of deployment via exposed APIs and the potential for scaling mining activities by deploying or compromising multiple containers dentro do ambiente alvo or cluster. `[Ref: Unit 42 Hildegard Malware]` `[Ref: Trend Micro Exposed Docker APIs]`

Additionally, some cryptocurrency mining malware identify then kill off processes for competing malware to ensure it’s not competing for resources. `[Ref: Trend Micro War of Crypto Miners]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Recursos Computacionais: Bandwidth Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de the network bandwidth resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability. 

Os adversários podem também use malware that leverages a system's network bandwidth as part of a botnet com o objetivo de facilitate **Network Denial of Service** (`T1498`) campaigns and/or to seed malicious torrents. `[Ref: GoBotKR]` Alternatively, they may engage in proxyjacking by selling use of the victims' network bandwidth and IP address to proxyware services. `[Ref: Sysdig Proxyjacking]` Finally, they may engage in internet-wide scanning com o objetivo de identify additional targets for compromise. `[Ref: Unit 42 Leaked Environment Variables 2024]`

Adicionalmente a incurring potential financial costs or availability disruptions, this technique may cause reputational damage if a victim’s bandwidth is used for illegal activities. `[Ref: Sysdig Proxyjacking]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Recursos Computacionais: SMS Pumping
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de messaging services for SMS pumping, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability. `[Ref: Twilio SMS Pumping]` SMS pumping is a type of telecommunications fraud whereby a threat actor first obtains a set of phone numbers from a telecommunications provider, then leverages a victim’s messaging infrastructure to send large amounts of SMS messages to numbers in that set. By generating SMS traffic to their phone number set, a threat actor may earn payments from the telecommunications provider. `[Ref: Twilio SMS Pumping Fraud]`

Threat actors often use publicly available web forms, such as one-time password (OTP) or account verification fields, com o objetivo de generate SMS traffic. These fields may leverage services such as Twilio, AWS SNS, and Amazon Cognito in the background. `[Ref: Twilio SMS Pumping]` `[Ref: AWS RE:Inforce Threat Detection 2024]` In response to the large quantity of requests, SMS costs may increase and communication channels may become overwhelmed. `[Ref: Twilio SMS Pumping]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Recursos Computacionais: Cloud Service Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de compromised software-as-a-service (SaaS) applications to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact hosted service availability. 

Por exemplo, adversaries may leverage email and messaging services, such as AWS Simple Email Service (SES), AWS Simple Notification Service (SNS), SendGrid, and Twilio, com o objetivo de send large quantities of spam / **Phishing** (`T1566`) emails and SMS messages. `[Ref: Invictus IR DangerDev 2024]` `[Ref: Permiso SES Abuse 2023]` `[Ref: SentinelLabs SNS Sender 2024]` Alternatively, they may engage in LLMJacking by leveraging reverse proxies to hijack the power of cloud-hosted AI models. `[Ref: Sysdig LLMJacking 2024]` `[Ref: Lacework LLMJacking 2024]`

In some cases, adversaries may leverage services that the victim is already using. In others, particularly when the service is part of a larger cloud platform, they may first enable the service. `[Ref: Sysdig LLMJacking 2024]` Leveraging SaaS applications may cause the victim to incur significant financial costs, use up service quotas, and otherwise impact availability.

techniques.fullNamePt: Evasão de Virtualização e Sandbox
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem employ various means to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments. This may include changing behaviors based on the results of checks for the presence of artifacts indicative of a máquina virtual (VM) environment (VME) or sandbox. If the adversary detects a VME, they may alter their malware to disengage from the victim or conceal the core functions of the implant. They may also search for VME artifacts before dropping secondary or additional payloads. Os adversários podem utilizar the information learned from **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors. `[Ref: Deloitte Environment Awareness]`

Os adversários podem utilizar several methods to accomplish **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`) such as checking for security monitoring tools (e.g., Sysinternals, Wireshark, etc.) or other system artifacts associated with analysis or virtualization. Os adversários podem também check for legitimate user activity to help determine if it is in an analysis environment. Additional methods include use of sleep timers or loops within malware code to avoid operating within a temporary sandbox. `[Ref: Unit 42 Pirpi July 2015]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Evasão de Virtualização e Sandbox: System Checks
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem employ various system checks to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments. This may include changing behaviors based on the results of checks for the presence of artifacts indicative of a máquina virtual (VM) environment (VME) or sandbox. If the adversary detects a VME, they may alter their malware to disengage from the victim or conceal the core functions of the implant. They may also search for VME artifacts before dropping secondary or additional payloads. Os adversários podem utilizar the information learned from **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors. `[Ref: Deloitte Environment Awareness]`

Specific checks will vary based on the target and/or adversary, but may involve behaviors such as **Windows Management Instrumentation** (`T1047`), **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`), **System Information Discovery** (`T1082`), and **Query Registry** (`T1012`) to obtain system information and search for VME artifacts. Os adversários podem pesquisar for VME artifacts in memory, processes, sistema de ficheiros, hardware, and/or the Registry. Os adversários podem utilizar scripting to automate these checks  into one script and then have the program exit if it determines the system to be a virtual environment. 

Checks could include generic system properties such as host/domain name and samples of tráfego de rede. Os adversários podem também check the network adapters addresses, CPU core count, and available memory/drive size. Uma vez que executed, malware may also use **File and Directory Discovery** (`T1083`) to check if it was saved in a folder or file with unexpected or even analysis-related naming artifacts such as `malware`, `sample`, or `hash`.

Other common checks may enumerate services running that are unique to these applications, installed programs on the system, manufacturer/product fields for strings relating to máquina virtual (VM) applications, and VME-specific hardware/processor instructions. `[Ref: McAfee Virtual Jan 2017]` In applications like VMWare, adversaries can also use a special I/O port to send commands and receive output. 
 
Hardware checks, such as the presence of the fan, temperature, and audio devices, could also be used to gather evidence that can be indicative a virtual environment. Os adversários podem também query for specific readings from these devices. `[Ref: Unit 42 OilRig Sept 2018]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion: User Activity Based Checks
techniques.fullNamePt: Evasão de Virtualização e Sandbox: User Activity Based Checks
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem employ various user activity checks to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments. This may include changing behaviors based on the results of checks for the presence of artifacts indicative of a máquina virtual (VM) environment (VME) or sandbox. If the adversary detects a VME, they may alter their malware to disengage from the victim or conceal the core functions of the implant. They may also search for VME artifacts before dropping secondary or additional payloads. Os adversários podem utilizar the information learned from **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors. `[Ref: Deloitte Environment Awareness]`

Os adversários podem pesquisar for user activity on the host based on variables such as the speed/frequency of mouse movements and clicks  `[Ref: Sans Virtual Jan 2016]` , browser history, cache, bookmarks, or number of files in common directories such as home or the desktop. Other methods may rely on specific user interaction with the system before the código malicioso is activated, such as waiting for a document to close before activating a macro  `[Ref: Unit 42 Sofacy Nov 2018]` or waiting for a user to double click on an embedded image to activate. `[Ref: FireEye FIN7 April 2017]`

techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem employ various time-based methods to detect virtualization and analysis environments, particularly those that attempt to manipulate time mechanisms to simulate longer elapses of time. This may include enumerating time-based properties, such as uptime or the system clock.

techniques.fullNamePt: Negação de Serviço de Rede
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem realizar Network Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources to users. Network DoS can be performed by exhausting the network bandwidth services rely on. Example resources include specific websites, email services, DNS, and web-based applications. Adversaries have been observed conducting network DoS attacks for political purposes `[Ref: FireEye OpPoisonedHandover February 2016]` and to support other malicious activities, including distraction `[Ref: FSISAC FraudNetDoS September 2012]`, hacktivism, and extortion. `[Ref: Symantec DDoS October 2014]`

A Network DoS will occur when the bandwidth capacity of the network connection to a system is exhausted due to the volume of malicious traffic directed at the resource or the network connections and network devices the resource relies on. Por exemplo, an adversary may send 10Gbps of traffic to a server that is hosted by a network with a 1Gbps connection to the internet. This traffic can be generated by a single system or multiple systems spread across the internet, which is commonly referred to as a distributed DoS (DDoS).

To perform Network DoS attacks several aspects apply to multiple methods, including IP address spoofing, and botnets.

Os adversários podem utilizar the original IP address of an attacking system, or spoof the source IP address to make the attack traffic more difficult to trace back to the attacking system or to enable reflection. This can increase the difficulty defenders have in defending against the attack by reducing or eliminating the effectiveness of filtering by the source address on network defense devices.

For DoS attacks targeting the hosting system directly, see **Endpoint Denial of Service** (`T1499`).

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt:
When flood volumes exceed the capacity of the network connection being targeted, it is typically necessary to intercept the incoming traffic upstream to filter out the attack traffic from the legitimate traffic. Such defenses can be provided by the hosting Internet Service Provider (ISP) or by a 3rd party such as a Content Delivery Network (CDN) or providers specializing in DoS mitigations. `[Ref: CERT-EU DDoS March 2017]`

Dependendo de flood volume, on-premises filtering may be possible by blocking source addresses sourcing the attack, blocking ports that are being targeted, or blocking protocols being used for transport. `[Ref: CERT-EU DDoS March 2017]`

As immediate response may require rapid engagement of 3rd parties, analyze the risk associated to critical resources being affected by Network DoS attacks and create a disaster recovery plan/business continuity plan to respond to incidents. `[Ref: CERT-EU DDoS March 2017]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Network Denial of Service: Direct Network Flood
techniques.fullNamePt: Negação de Serviço de Rede: Direct Network Flood
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar cause a denial of service (DoS) by directly sending a high-volume of tráfego de rede to a target. This DoS attack may also reduce the availability and functionality of the targeted system(s) and network. **Direct Network Flood** (`T1498.001`)s are when one or more systems são utilizados para send a high-volume of network packets towards the targeted service's network. Almost any network protocol may be used for flooding. Stateless protocols such as UDP or ICMP are commonly used but stateful protocols such as TCP can be used as well.

Botnets are commonly used to conduct network flooding attacks against networks and services. Large botnets can generate a significant amount of traffic from systems spread across the global Internet. Os adversários podem have the resources to build out and control their own botnet infrastructure or may rent time on an existing botnet to conduct an attack. In some of the worst cases for distributed DoS (DDoS), so many systems são utilizados para generate the flood that each one only needs to send out a small amount of traffic to produce enough volume to saturate the rede alvo. In such circumstances, distinguishing DDoS traffic from legitimate clients becomes exceedingly difficult. Botnets have been used in some of the most high-profile DDoS flooding attacks, such as the 2012 series of incidents that targeted major US banks. `[Ref: USNYAG IranianBotnet March 2016]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Network Denial of Service: Reflection Amplification
techniques.fullNamePt: Negação de Serviço de Rede: Reflection Amplification
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar cause a denial of service (DoS) by reflecting a high-volume of tráfego de rede to a target. This type of Network DoS takes advantage of a third-party server intermediary that hosts and will respond to a given spoofed source IP address. This third-party server is commonly termed a reflector. An adversary accomplishes a reflection attack by sending packets to reflectors with the spoofed address of the victim. De forma semelhante a Direct Network Floods, more than one system pode ser empregue para conduct the attack, or a botnet may be used. Likewise, one or more reflectors pode ser empregue para focus traffic on the target. `[Ref: Cloudflare ReflectionDoS May 2017]` This Network DoS attack may also reduce the availability and functionality of the targeted system(s) and network.

Reflection attacks often take advantage of protocols with larger responses than requests com o objetivo de amplify their traffic, commonly known as a Reflection Amplification attack. Os adversários podem be able to generate an increase in volume of attack traffic that is several orders of magnitude greater than the requests sent to the amplifiers. The extent of this increase will depending upon many variables, such as the protocol in question, the technique used, and the amplifying servers that actually produce the amplification in attack volume. Two prominent protocols that have enabled Reflection Amplification Floods are DNS `[Ref: Cloudflare DNSamplficationDoS]` and NTP `[Ref: Cloudflare NTPamplifciationDoS]`, though the use of several others in the wild have been documented. `[Ref: Arbor AnnualDoSreport Jan 2018]`  In particular, the memcache protocol showed itself to be a powerful protocol, with amplification sizes up to 51,200 times the requesting packet. `[Ref: Cloudflare Memcrashed Feb 2018]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Negação de Serviço em Endpoint (DoS)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem realizar Endpoint Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of services to users. Endpoint DoS can be performed by exhausting the system resources those services are hosted on or exploiting the system to cause a persistent crash condition. Example services include websites, email services, DNS, and web-based applications. Adversaries have been observed conducting DoS attacks for political purposes `[Ref: FireEye OpPoisonedHandover February 2016]` and to support other malicious activities, including distraction `[Ref: FSISAC FraudNetDoS September 2012]`, hacktivism, and extortion. `[Ref: Symantec DDoS October 2014]`

An Endpoint DoS denies the availability of a service without saturating the network used to provide access to the service. Adversaries can target various layers of the application stack that is hosted on the system used to provide the service. These layers include the Operating Systems (OS), server applications such as web servers, DNS servers, databases, and the (typically web-based) applications that sit on top of them. Attacking each layer requires different techniques that take advantage of bottlenecks that are unique to the respective components. A DoS attack may be generated by a single system or multiple systems spread across the internet, which is commonly referred to as a distributed DoS (DDoS).

To perform DoS attacks against endpoint resources, several aspects apply to multiple methods, including IP address spoofing and botnets.

Os adversários podem utilizar the original IP address of an attacking system, or spoof the source IP address to make the attack traffic more difficult to trace back to the attacking system or to enable reflection. This can increase the difficulty defenders have in defending against the attack by reducing or eliminating the effectiveness of filtering by the source address on network defense devices.

Botnets are commonly used to conduct DDoS attacks against networks and services. Large botnets can generate a significant amount of traffic from systems spread across the global internet. Os adversários podem have the resources to build out and control their own botnet infrastructure or may rent time on an existing botnet to conduct an attack. In some of the worst cases for DDoS, so many systems são utilizados para generate requests that each one only needs to send out a small amount of traffic to produce enough volume to exhaust the target's resources. In such circumstances, distinguishing DDoS traffic from legitimate clients becomes exceedingly difficult. Botnets have been used in some of the most high-profile DDoS attacks, such as the 2012 series of incidents that targeted major US banks. `[Ref: USNYAG IranianBotnet March 2016]`

In cases where traffic manipulation is used, there may be points in the global network (such as high traffic gateway routers) where packets can be altered and cause legitimate clients to execute code that directs network packets toward a target in high volume. This type of capability was previously used for the purposes of web censorship where client HTTP traffic was modified to include a reference to JavaScript that generated the DDoS code to overwhelm target web servers. `[Ref: ArsTechnica Great Firewall of China]`

For attacks attempting to saturate the providing network, see **Network Denial of Service** (`T1498`).

mitigations.descriptionPt: Leverage services provided by Content Delivery Networks (CDN) or providers specializing in DoS mitigations to filter traffic upstream from services. `[Ref: CERT-EU DDoS March 2017]` Filter boundary traffic by blocking source addresses sourcing the attack, blocking ports that are being targeted, or blocking protocols being used for transport. To defend against SYN floods, enable SYN Cookies.

techniques.fullNameEn: Endpoint Denial of Service: OS Exhaustion Flood
techniques.fullNamePt: Negação de Serviço em Endpoint (DoS): OS Exhaustion Flood
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem launch a denial of service (DoS) attack targeting an endpoint's sistema operativo (OS). A system's OS is responsible for managing the finite resources as well as preventing the entire system from being overwhelmed by excessive demands on its capacity. These attacks do not need to exhaust the actual resources on a system; the attacks may simply exhaust the limits and available resources that an OS self-imposes.

Different ways to achieve this exist, including TCP state-exhaustion attacks such as SYN floods and ACK floods. `[Ref: Arbor AnnualDoSreport Jan 2018]` With SYN floods, excessive amounts of SYN packets are sent, but the 3-way TCP handshake is never completed. Because each OS has a maximum number of concurrent TCP connections that it will allow, this can quickly exhaust the ability of the system to receive new requests for TCP connections, thus preventing access to any TCP service provided by the server. `[Ref: Cloudflare SynFlood]`

ACK floods leverage the stateful nature of the TCP protocol. A flood of ACK packets are sent to the target. This forces the OS to search its state table for a related TCP connection that has already been established. Because the ACK packets are for connections that do not exist, the OS will have to search the entire state table to confirm that no match exists. When it is necessary to do this for a large flood of packets, the computational requirements can cause the server to become sluggish and/or unresponsive, due to the work it must do to eliminate the rogue ACK packets. This greatly reduces the resources available for providing the targeted service. `[Ref: Corero SYN-ACKflood]`

To defend against SYN floods, enable SYN Cookies.

techniques.fullNameEn: Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
techniques.fullNamePt: Negação de Serviço em Endpoint (DoS): Service Exhaustion Flood
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem target the different network services provided by systems to conduct a denial of service (DoS). Adversaries often target the availability of DNS and web services, however others have been targeted as well. `[Ref: Arbor AnnualDoSreport Jan 2018]` Web server software can be attacked through a variety of means, some of which apply generally while others are specific to the software being used to provide the service.

One example of this type of attack is known as a simple HTTP flood, where an adversary sends a large number of HTTP requests to a web server to overwhelm it and/or an application that runs on top of it. This flood relies on raw volume to accomplish the objective, exhausting any of the various resources required by the victim software to provide the service. `[Ref: Cloudflare HTTPflood]`

Another variation, known as a SSL renegotiation attack, takes advantage of a protocol feature in SSL/TLS. The SSL/TLS protocol suite includes mechanisms for the client and server to agree on an encryption algorithm to use for subsequent secure connections. If SSL renegotiation is enabled, a request can be made for renegotiation of the crypto algorithm. In a renegotiation attack, the adversary establishes a SSL/TLS connection and then proceeds to make a series of renegotiation requests. Because the cryptographic renegotiation has a meaningful cost in computation cycles, this can cause an impact to the availability of the service when done in volume. `[Ref: Arbor SSLDoS April 2012]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application or System Exploitation
techniques.fullNamePt: Negação de Serviço em Endpoint (DoS): Application or System Exploitation
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem explorar software vulnerabilities that can cause an application or system to crash and deny availability to users.  `[Ref: Sucuri BIND9 August 2015]` Some systems may automatically restart critical applications and services when crashes occur, but they can likely be re-exploited to cause a persistent denial of service (DoS) condition.

Os adversários podem explorar known or zero-day vulnerabilities to crash applications and/or systems, which may also lead to dependent applications and/or systems to be in a DoS condition. Crashed or restarted applications or systems may also have other effects such as **Data Destruction** (`T1485`), **Firmware Corruption** (`T1495`), **Service Stop** (`T1489`) etc. which may further cause a DoS condition and deny availability to critical information, applications and/or systems.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Leverage services provided by Content Delivery Networks (CDN) or providers specializing in DoS mitigations to filter traffic upstream from services. `[Ref: CERT-EU DDoS March 2017]` Filter boundary traffic by blocking source addresses sourcing the attack, blocking ports that are being targeted, or blocking protocols being used for transport.

Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

mitigations.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider using Group Policy to configure and block modifications to service and other critical server parameters in the Registry. `[Ref: Microsoft System Services Fundamentals]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling software components from servers when possible to prevent abuse by adversaries. `[Ref: ITSyndicate Disabling PHP functions]`

mitigations.name: Boot Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enabling secure boot allows validation of software and drivers during initial system boot.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de the principle of least privilege by limiting privileges of user accounts so only authorized accounts can modify and/or add server software components. `[Ref: NSA and ASD Detect and Prevent Web Shells 2020]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not allow administrator accounts that have permissions to add component software on these services to be used for day-to-day operations that may expose them to potential adversaries on unprivileged systems.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. techniques.fullNamePt: Componente de Software de Servidor (Web Shell / Módulo): SQL Stored Procedures
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de SQL stored procedures to establish persistent access to systems. SQL Stored Procedures are code that can be saved and reused so that database users do not waste time rewriting frequently used SQL queries. Stored procedures can be invoked via SQL statements to the database using the procedure name or via defined events (e.g. when a SQL server application is started/restarted).

Os adversários podem craft malicious stored procedures that can provide a mecanismo de persistência in SQL database servers. `[Ref: NetSPI Startup Stored Procedures]` `[Ref: Kaspersky MSSQL Aug 2019]` To execute sistema operativo commands through SQL syntax the adversary may have to enable additional functionality, such as xp_cmdshell for MSSQL Server. `[Ref: NetSPI Startup Stored Procedures]` `[Ref: Kaspersky MSSQL Aug 2019]` `[Ref: Microsoft xp_cmdshell 2017]` 

Microsoft SQL Server can enable common language runtime (CLR) integration. With CLR integration enabled, application developers can write stored procedures using any .NET framework language (e.g. VB .NET, C#, etc.). `[Ref: Microsoft CLR Integration 2017]` Os adversários podem craft or modify CLR assemblies that are linked to stored procedures since these CLR assemblies can be made to execute comandos arbitrários. `[Ref: NetSPI SQL Server CLR]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Componente de Software de Servidor (Web Shell / Módulo): Transport Agent
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Microsoft transport agents to establish persistent access to systems. Microsoft Exchange transport agents can operate on email messages passing through the transport pipeline to perform various tasks such as filtering spam, filtering malicious attachments, journaling, or adding a corporate signature to the end of all outgoing emails. `[Ref: Microsoft TransportAgent Jun 2016]` `[Ref: ESET LightNeuron May 2019]` Transport agents can be written by application developers and then compiled to .NET assemblies that are subsequently registered with the Exchange server. Transport agents will be invoked during a specified stage of email processing and carry out developer defined tasks. 

Os adversários podem register a malicious transport agent to provide a mecanismo de persistência in Exchange Server that can be triggered by adversary-specified email events. `[Ref: ESET LightNeuron May 2019]` Though a malicious transport agent may be invoked for all emails passing through the Exchange transport pipeline, the agent can be configured to only carry out specific tasks in response to adversary defined criteria. Por exemplo, the transport agent may only carry out an action like copying in-transit attachments and saving them for later exfiltration if the recipient email address matches an entry on a list provided by the adversary.

techniques.fullNamePt: Componente de Software de Servidor (Web Shell / Módulo): Web Shell
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem backdoor web servers with web shells to establish persistent access to systems. A Web shell is a Web script that is placed on an openly accessible Web server to allow an adversary to access the Web server as a gateway into a network. A Web shell may provide a set of functions to execute or a interface de linha de comandos (CLI) on the system that hosts the Web server. `[Ref: volexity_0day_sophos_FW]`

Adicionalmente a a server-side script, a Web shell may have a client interface program that é utilizado para talk to the Web server (e.g. **China Chopper** (`S0020`) Web shell client). `[Ref: Lee 2013]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de the principle of least privilege by limiting privileges of user accounts so only authorized accounts can modify the web directory. `[Ref: NSA and ASD Detect and Prevent Web Shells 2020]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Componente de Software de Servidor (Web Shell / Módulo): IIS Components
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem install malicious components that run on Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers to establish persistence. IIS provides several mechanisms to extend the functionality of the web servers. Por exemplo, Internet Server Application Programming Interface (ISAPI) extensions and filters can be installed to examine and/or modify incoming and outgoing IIS web requests. Extensions and filters are deployed as DLL files that export three functions: `Get{Extension/Filter}Version`, `Http{Extension/Filter}Proc`, and (optionally) `Terminate{Extension/Filter}`. IIS modules may also be installed to extend IIS web servers. `[Ref: Microsoft ISAPI Extension Overview 2017]` `[Ref: Microsoft ISAPI Filter Overview 2017]` `[Ref: IIS Backdoor 2011]` `[Ref: Trustwave IIS Module 2013]`

Os adversários podem install malicious ISAPI extensions and filters to observe and/or modify traffic, execute commands on compromised machines, or proxy Command and Control (C2) traffic. ISAPI extensions and filters may have access to all IIS web requests and responses. Por exemplo, an adversary may abuse these mechanisms to modify HTTP responses com o objetivo de distribute malicious commands/content to previously comprised hosts. `[Ref: Microsoft ISAPI Filter Overview 2017]` `[Ref: Microsoft ISAPI Extension Overview 2017]` `[Ref: Microsoft ISAPI Extension All Incoming 2017]` `[Ref: Dell TG-3390]` `[Ref: Trustwave IIS Module 2013]` `[Ref: MMPC ISAPI Filter 2012]`

Os adversários podem também install malicious IIS modules to observe and/or modify traffic. IIS 7.0 introduced modules that provide the same unrestricted access to HTTP requests and responses as ISAPI extensions and filters. IIS modules can be written as a DLL that exports `RegisterModule`, or as a .NET application that interfaces with ASP.NET APIs to access IIS HTTP requests. `[Ref: Microsoft IIS Modules Overview 2007]` `[Ref: Trustwave IIS Module 2013]` `[Ref: ESET IIS Malware 2021]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not allow administrator accounts that have permissions to add IIS components to be used for day-to-day operations that may expose these permissions to potential adversaries and/or other unprivileged systems.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Server Software Component: Terminal Services DLL
techniques.fullNamePt: Componente de Software de Servidor (Web Shell / Módulo): Terminal Services DLL
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de components of Terminal Services to enable persistent access to systems. Microsoft Terminal Services, renamed to Remote Desktop Services in some Windows Server OSs as of 2022, enable remote terminal connections to hosts. Terminal Services allows servers to transmit a full, interactive, interface gráfica (GUI) to clients via RDP. `[Ref: Microsoft Remote Desktop Services]`

**Windows Service** (`T1543.003`)s that are run as a "generic" process (ex: `svchost.exe`) load the service's DLL file, the location of which is stored in a Registry entry named `ServiceDll`. `[Ref: Microsoft System Services Fundamentals]` The `termsrv.dll` file, typically stored in `%SystemRoot%\System32\`, is the default `ServiceDll` value for Terminal Services in `HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\services\TermService\Parameters\`.

Os adversários podem modificar and/or replace the Terminal Services DLL to enable persistent access to victimized hosts. `[Ref: James TermServ DLL]` Modifications to this DLL could be done to execute arbitrary payloads (while also potentially preserving normal `termsrv.dll` functionality) as well as to simply enable abusable features of Terminal Services. Por exemplo, an adversary may enable features such as concurrent **Remote Desktop Protocol** (`T1021.001`) sessions by either patching the `termsrv.dll` file or modifying the `ServiceDll` value to point to a DLL that provides increased RDP functionality. `[Ref: Windows OS Hub RDP]` `[Ref: RDPWrap Github]` On a non-server Windows OS this increased functionality may also enable an adversary to avoid Terminal Services prompts that warn/log out users of a system when a new RDP session is created.
