techniques.fullNameEn: Server Software Component: vSphere Installation Bundles
techniques.fullNamePt: Componente de Software de Servidor (Web Shell / Módulo): vSphere Installation Bundles
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de vSphere Installation Bundles (VIBs) to establish persistent access to ESXi hypervisors. VIBs are collections of files used for software distribution and virtual system management in VMware environments. Since ESXi uses an in-memory filesystem where changes made to most files are stored in RAM rather than in persistent storage, these modifications are lost after a reboot. Contudo, VIBs pode ser utilizado para create startup tasks, apply custom firewall rules, or deploy binaries that persist across reboots. Typically, administrators use VIBs for updates and system maintenance.

VIBs can be broken down into three components: `[Ref: VMware VIBs]`

* VIB payload: a `.vgz` archive containing the directories and files to be created and executed on boot when the VIBs are loaded.  
* Signature file: verifies the host acceptance level of a VIB, indicating what testing and validation has been done by VMware or its partners before publication of a VIB. Por omissão, ESXi hosts require a minimum acceptance level of PartnerSupported for VIB installation, meaning the VIB is published by a trusted VMware partner. Contudo, privileged users can change the default acceptance level using the `esxcli` command line interface. Additionally, VIBs are able to be installed regardless of acceptance level by using the ` esxcli software vib install --force` command. 
* XML descriptor file: a configuration file containing associated VIB metadata, such as the name of the VIB and its dependencies.  

Os adversários podem tirar partido de malicious VIB packages to maintain persistent access to ESXi hypervisors, allowing system changes to be executed upon each bootup of ESXi – such as using  `esxcli` to enable firewall rules for backdoor traffic, creating listeners on hard coded ports, and executing backdoors. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence ESXi VIBs 2022]` Os adversários podem também masquerade their malicious VIB files as PartnerSupported by modifying the XML descriptor file. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence ESXi VIBs 2022]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence ESXi VIBs 2022]

mitigations.name: Boot Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enabling secure boot allows ESXi to validate software and drivers during initial system boot. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence ESXi Hardening 2023]`

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enabling the `execInstalledOnly` feature prevents unsigned binaries from being run on ESXi hosts. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence ESXi Hardening 2023]`

Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

techniques.fullNamePt: Software Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of software and software versions that are installed on a system or in a cloud environment. Os adversários podem utilizar the information from **Software Discovery** (`T1518`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions.

Such software may be deployed widely across the environment for configuration management or security reasons, such as **Software Deployment Tools** (`T1072`), and may allow adversaries broad access to infect devices or move laterally.

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar enumerate software for a variety of reasons, such as figuring out what security measures are present or if the compromised system has a version of software that is vulnerable to **Exploitation for Privilege Escalation** (`T1068`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Software Discovery: Security Software Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of security software, configurations, defensive tools, and sensors that are installed on a system or in a cloud environment. This may include things such as cloud monitoring agents and anti-virus. Os adversários podem utilizar the information from **Security Software Discovery** (`T1518.001`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions.

Example commands that pode ser utilizado para obtain security software information are **netsh** (`S0108`), `reg query` with **Reg** (`S0075`), `dir` with **cmd** (`S0106`), and **Tasklist** (`S0057`), but other indicators of discovery behavior may be more specific to the type of software or security system the adversary is looking for. It is becoming more common to see macOS malware perform checks for LittleSnitch and KnockKnock software.

Os adversários podem também utilize the **Cloud API** (`T1059.009`) to discover cloud-native security software installed on compute infrastructure, such as the AWS CloudWatch agent, Azure VM Agent, and Google Cloud Monitor agent. These agents  may collect  metrics and logs from the VM, which may be centrally aggregated in a cloud-based monitoring platform.

techniques.fullNamePt: Software Discovery: Backup Software Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar get a listing of backup software or configurations that are installed on a system. Os adversários podem utilizar this information to shape follow-on behaviors, such as **Data Destruction** (`T1485`), **Inhibit System Recovery** (`T1490`), or **Data Encrypted for Impact** (`T1486`).  

Commands that pode ser utilizado para obtain security software information are **netsh** (`S0108`), `reg query` with **Reg** (`S0075`), `dir` with **cmd** (`S0106`), and **Tasklist** (`S0057`), but other indicators of discovery behavior may be more specific to the type of software or security system the adversary is looking for, such as Veeam, Acronis, Dropbox, or Paragon. `[Ref: Symantec Play Ransomware 2023]`

Behavior often includes parent-child lineage involving PowerShell or cmd.exe with discovery syntax, and enumeration of services, directories, or registry paths tied to backup software.

This often includes command lines that recursively search `/etc/`, `/opt/`, or `/var/` directories for keywords like `backup`, and parent-child relationships involving shell or Python scripts.

techniques.fullNamePt: Implantação de Imagem Interna
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem implant cloud or container images with código malicioso to establish persistence after gaining access to an environment. Amazon Web Services (AWS) Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Images, and Azure Images as well as popular container runtimes such as Docker can be implanted or backdoored. Unlike **Upload Malware** (`T1608.001`), this technique focuses on adversaries implanting an image in a registry within a victim’s environment. Dependendo de how the infrastructure is provisioned, this could provide persistent access if the infrastructure provisioning tool is instructed to always use the latest image. `[Ref: Rhino Labs Cloud Image Backdoor Technique Sept 2019]`

A tool has been developed to facilitate planting backdoors in cloud container images. `[Ref: Rhino Labs Cloud Backdoor September 2019]` If an adversary has access to a compromised AWS instance, and permissions to list the available container images, they may implant a backdoor such as a **Web Shell** (`T1505.003`). `[Ref: Rhino Labs Cloud Image Backdoor Technique Sept 2019]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Rhino Labs Cloud Image Backdoor Technique Sept 2019]

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Several cloud service providers support content trust models that require container images be signed by trusted sources. `[Ref: Content trust in Azure Container Registry]` `[Ref: Content trust in Docker]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Recorrer a DLL Side-Loading (`T1574.002`) utilizando um executável legítimo assinado (vulnerável a sequestro de ordem de procura de DLL) que carregue a nossa DLL em memória, ou utilizar binários assinados nativos (LOLBAS - `T1218`). Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit permissions associated with creating and modifying platform images or containers based on the principle of least privilege.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Periodically check the integrity of images and containers used in cloud deployments to ensure they have not been modified to include malicious software.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Serviços Cloud
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode attempt to enumerate the cloud services running on a system after gaining access. These methods can differ from platform-as-a-service (PaaS), to infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), or software-as-a-service (SaaS). Many services exist throughout the various cloud providers and can include Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD), Lambda Functions, Entra ID, etc. They may also include security services, such as AWS GuardDuty and Microsoft Defender for Cloud, and logging services, such as AWS CloudTrail and Google Cloud Auditar regularmente Logs.

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar discover information about the services enabled throughout the environment. Azure tools and APIs, such as the Microsoft Graph API and Azure Resource Manager API, can enumerate resources and services, including applications, management groups, resources and policy definitions, and their relationships that are accessible by an identity. `[Ref: Azure - Resource Manager API]` `[Ref: Azure AD Graph API]`

Por exemplo, Stormspotter is an open source tool for enumerating and constructing a graph for Azure resources and services, and Pacu is an open source AWS exploitation framework that supports several methods for discovering cloud services. `[Ref: Azure - Stormspotter]` `[Ref: GitHub Pacu]`

Os adversários podem utilizar the information gained to shape follow-on behaviors, such as targeting data or credentials from enumerated services or evading identified defenses through **Disable or Modify Tools** (`T1685`) or **Disable or Modify Cloud Log** (`T1685.002`).

techniques.namePt: Roubo de Token de Acesso Aplicacional
techniques.fullNamePt: Roubo de Token de Acesso Aplicacional
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries can steal application access tokens as a means of acquiring credentials to access sistemas remotos and resources.

Application access tokens são utilizados para make authorized API requests on behalf of a user or service and are commonly used as a way to access resources in cloud and container-based applications and software-as-a-service (SaaS). `[Ref: Auth0 - Why You Should Always Use Access Tokens to Secure APIs Sept 2019]`  Adversaries who steal account API tokens in cloud and containerized environments may be able to access data and perform actions with the permissions of these accounts, which can lead to privilege escalation and further compromise of the environment.

Por exemplo, in Kubernetes environments, processes running inside a container may communicate with the Kubernetes API server using service account tokens. If a container is compromised, an adversary may be able to steal the container’s token and thereby gain access to Kubernetes API commands. `[Ref: Kubernetes Service Accounts]`  

Similarly, instances within continuous-development / continuous-integration (CI/CD) pipelines will often use API tokens to authenticate to other services for testing and deployment. `[Ref: Cider Security Top 10 CICD Security Risks]` If these pipelines are compromised, adversaries may be able to steal these tokens and leverage their privileges. 

In Azure, an adversary who compromises a resource with an attached Managed Identity, such as an Azure VM, can request short-lived tokens through the Azure Instance Metadata Service (IMDS). These tokens can then facilitate unauthorized actions or further access to other Azure services, bypassing typical credential-based authentication. `[Ref: Entra Managed Identities 2025]` `[Ref: SpecterOps Managed Identity 2022]`

Token theft can also occur through engenharia social, in which case user action may be required to grant access. OAuth is one commonly implemented framework that issues tokens to users for access to systems. An application desiring access to cloud-based services or protected APIs can gain entry using OAuth 2.0 through a variety of authorization protocols. An example commonly-used sequence is Microsoft's Authorization Code Grant flow. `[Ref: Microsoft Identity Platform Protocols May 2019]` `[Ref: Microsoft - OAuth Code Authorization flow - June 2019]` An OAuth access token enables a third-party application to interact with resources containing user data in the ways requested by the application without obtaining user credentials. 
 
Adversaries can leverage OAuth authorization by constructing a malicious application designed to be granted access to resources with the target user's OAuth token. `[Ref: Amnesty OAuth Phishing Attacks, August 2019]` `[Ref: Trend Micro Pawn Storm OAuth 2017]` The adversary will need to complete registration of their application with the authorization server, for example Microsoft Identity Platform using Azure Portal, the Visual Studio IDE, the interface de linha de comandos (CLI), PowerShell, or REST API calls. `[Ref: Microsoft - Azure AD App Registration - May 2019]` Then, they can send a **Spearphishing Link** (`T1566.002`) to the target user to entice them to grant access to the application. Uma vez que the OAuth access token is granted, the application can gain potentially long-term access to features of the user account through **Application Access Token** (`T1550.001`). `[Ref: Microsoft - Azure AD Identity Tokens - Aug 2019]`

Application access tokens may function within a limited lifetime, limiting how long an adversary can utilize the stolen token. Contudo, in some cases, adversaries can also steal application refresh tokens `[Ref: Auth0 Understanding Refresh Tokens]`, allowing them to obtain new access tokens without prompting the user.

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Administrators can block end-user consent to OAuth applications, disabling users from authorizing third-party apps through OAuth 2.0 and forcing administrative consent for all requests. They can also block end-user registration of applications by their users, to reduce risk. A Cloud Access Security Broker pode também ser utilizado para ban applications.

Azure offers a couple of enterprise policy settings in the Azure Management Portal that may help:

"Users -> User settings -> App registrations: Users can register applications" can be set to "no" to prevent users from registering new applications. 
"Enterprise applications -> User settings -> Enterprise applications: Users can consent to apps accessing company data on their behalf" can be set to "no" to prevent users from consenting to allow third-party multi-tenant applications

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Administrators should audit all cloud and container accounts to ensure that they are necessary and that the permissions granted to them are appropriate.  Additionally, administrators should perform an audit of all OAuth applications and the permissions they have been granted to access organizational data. This should be done extensively on all applications com o objetivo de establish a baseline, followed up on with periodic audits of new or updated applications. Suspicious applications should be investigated and removed.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Users need to be trained to not authorize third-party applications they don’t recognize. The user should pay particular attention to the redirect URL: if the URL is a misspelled or convoluted sequence of words related to an expected service or SaaS application, the website is likely trying to spoof a legitimate service. Users should also be cautious about the permissions they are granting to apps. Por exemplo, offline access and access to read emails should excite higher suspicions because adversaries can utilize SaaS APIs to discover credentials and other sensitive communications.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de role-based access control to limit accounts to the least privileges they require. A Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) pode ser utilizado para set usage policies and manage user permissions on cloud applications to prevent access to application access tokens. In Kubernetes applications, set “automountServiceAccountToken: false” in the YAML specification of pods that do not require access to service account tokens. `[Ref: Kubernetes Hardening Guide]`

techniques.fullNamePt: System Shutdown/Reboot
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem shutdown/reboot systems to interrupt access to, or aid in the destruction of, those systems. Operating systems may contain commands to initiate a shutdown/reboot of a machine or network device. In some cases, these commands may also be used to initiate a shutdown/reboot of a remote computer or network device via **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) (e.g. `reload`). `[Ref: Microsoft Shutdown Oct 2017]` `[Ref: alert_TA18_106A]` They may also include shutdown/reboot of a máquina virtual (VM) via hypervisor / cloud consoles or command line tools.

Shutting down or rebooting systems may disrupt access to computer resources for legitimate users while also impeding incident response/recovery.

Os adversários podem também use Windows API functions, such as `InitializeSystemShutdownExW` or `ExitWindowsEx`, to force a system to shut down or reboot. `[Ref: CrowdStrike Blog]` `[Ref: Unit42 Agrius 2023]` Alternatively, the `NtRaiseHardError`or `ZwRaiseHardError` Windows API functions with the `ResponseOption` parameter set to `OptionShutdownSystem` may deliver a “blue screen of death” (BSOD) to a system. `[Ref: SonicWall]` `[Ref: NtRaiseHardError]` `[Ref: NotMe-BSOD]` In order to leverage these API functions, an adversary may need to acquire `SeShutdownPrivilege` (e.g., via **Access Token Manipulation** (`T1134`)). `[Ref: Unit42 Agrius 2023]`
 In some cases, the system may not be able to boot again. 

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar shutdown/reboot a system after impacting it in other ways, such as **Disk Structure Wipe** (`T1561.002`) or **Inhibit System Recovery** (`T1490`), to hasten the intended effects on system availability. `[Ref: Talos Nyetya June 2017]` `[Ref: Talos Olympic Destroyer 2018]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Dados de Cloud Storage
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem access data from cloud storage.

Many IaaS providers offer solutions for online data object storage such as Amazon S3, Azure Storage, and Google Cloud Storage. Similarly, SaaS enterprise platforms such as Office 365 and Google Workspace provide cloud-based document storage to users through services such as OneDrive and Google Drive, while SaaS application providers such as Slack, Confluence, Salesforce, and Dropbox may provide cloud storage solutions as a peripheral or primary use case of their platform. 

In some cases, as with IaaS-based cloud storage, there exists no overarching application (such as SQL or Elasticsearch) with which to interact with the stored objects: instead, data from these solutions is retrieved directly though the **Cloud API** (`T1059.009`). In SaaS applications, adversaries may be able to collect this data directly from APIs or backend cloud storage objects, rather than through their front-end application or interface (i.e., **Data from Information Repositories** (`T1213`)). 

Os adversários podem recolher dados sensíveis from these cloud storage solutions. Providers typically offer security guides to help end users configure systems, though misconfigurations are a common problem. `[Ref: Amazon S3 Security, 2019]` `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Storage Security, 2019]` `[Ref: Google Cloud Storage Best Practices, 2019]` There have been numerous incidents where cloud storage has been improperly secured, typically by unintentionally allowing public access to unauthenticated users, overly-broad access by all users, or even access for any anonymous person outside the control of the Identity Access Management system without even needing basic user permissions.

This open access may expose various types of dados sensíveis, such as credit cards, personally identifiable information, or medical records. `[Ref: Trend Micro S3 Exposed PII, 2017]` `[Ref: Wired Magecart S3 Buckets, 2019]` `[Ref: HIPAA Journal S3 Breach, 2017]` `[Ref: Rclone-mega-extortion_05_2021]`

Os adversários podem também obtain then abuse leaked credentials from source repositories, logs, or other means as a way para obter acesso a cloud storage objects.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar user permissions groups and roles for access to cloud storage. `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Storage Security, 2019]` Implementar strict Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls to prevent access to storage solutions except for the applications, users, and services that require access. `[Ref: Amazon S3 Security, 2019]` Garantir que temporary access tokens are issued rather than permanent credentials, especially when access is being granted to entities outside of the internal security boundary. `[Ref: Amazon  AWS Temporary Security Credentials]`

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Encrypt data stored at rest in cloud storage. `[Ref: Amazon S3 Security, 2019]` `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Storage Security, 2019]` Managed chaves de encriptação can be rotated by most providers. At a minimum, ensure an incident response plan to storage breach includes rotating the keys and test for impact on client applications. `[Ref: Google Cloud Encryption Key Rotation]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use access control lists on storage systems and objects.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Cloud service providers support IP-based restrictions when accessing cloud resources. Consider using IP allowlisting along with user account management to ensure that data access is restricted not only to valid users but only from expected IP ranges to mitigate the use of stolen credentials to access data.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Frequently check permissions on cloud storage to ensure proper permissions are set to deny open or unprivileged access to resources. `[Ref: Amazon S3 Security, 2019]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider using multi-factor authentication to restrict access to resources and cloud storage APIs. `[Ref: Amazon S3 Security, 2019]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Account Access Removal
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem interrupt availability of system and network resources by inhibiting access to accounts utilized by legitimate users. Accounts may be deleted, locked, or manipulated (ex: changed credentials, revoked permissions for SaaS platforms such as Sharepoint) to remove access to accounts. `[Ref: Obsidian Security SaaS Ransomware June 2023]` Os adversários podem também subsequently log off and/or perform a **System Shutdown/Reboot** (`T1529`) to set malicious changes into place. `[Ref: CarbonBlack LockerGoga 2019]` `[Ref: Unit42 LockerGoga 2019]`

In Windows, **Net** (`S0039`) utility, `Set-LocalUser` and `Set-ADAccountPassword` **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) cmdlets may be used by adversaries to modify user accounts. Accounts could also be disabled by Group Policy. In Linux, the `passwd` utility pode ser empregue para change passwords. On ESXi servers, accounts can be removed or modified via esxcli (`system account set`, `system account remove`).

Adversaries who use ransomware or similar attacks may first perform this and other Impact behaviors, such as **Data Destruction** (`T1485`) and **Defacement** (`T1491`), com o objetivo de impede incident response/recovery before completing the **Data Encrypted for Impact** (`T1486`) objective.

techniques.fullNamePt: Spearphishing Interno
techniques.descriptionPt:
After they already have access to accounts or systems within the environment, adversaries may use internal spearphishing para obter acesso a additional information or compromise other users within the same organization. Internal spearphishing is multi-staged campaign where a legitimate account is initially compromised either by controlling the user's device or by compromising the account credentials of the user. Os adversários podem then attempt to take advantage of the trusted internal account to increase the likelihood of tricking more victims into falling for phish attempts, often incorporating **Impersonation** (`T1684.001`). `[Ref: Trend Micro - Int SP]`

Por exemplo, adversaries may leverage **Spearphishing Attachment** (`T1566.001`) or **Spearphishing Link** (`T1566.002`) as part of internal spearphishing to deliver a payload or redirect to an external site to capture credentials through **Input Capture** (`T1056`) on sites that mimic login interfaces.

Os adversários podem também leverage internal chat apps, such as Microsoft Teams, to spread malicious content or engage users in attempts to capture informação sensível and/or credentials. `[Ref: Int SP - chat apps]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Unused/Unsupported Cloud Regions
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar cloud instances in unused geographic service regions com o objetivo de evade detection. Access is usually obtained through compromising accounts used to manage cloud infrastructure.

Cloud service providers often provide infrastructure throughout the world com o objetivo de improve performance, provide redundancy, and allow customers to meet compliance requirements. Oftentimes, a customer will only use a subset of the available regions and may not actively monitor other regions. If an adversary creates resources in an unused region, they may be able to operate undetected.

A variation on this behavior takes advantage of differences in functionality across cloud regions. An adversary could utilize regions which do not support advanced detection services com o objetivo de avoid detection of their activity.

An example of adversary use of unused AWS regions is to mine cryptocurrency through **Resource Hijacking** (`T1496`), which can cost organizations substantial amounts of money over time depending on the processing power used. `[Ref: CloudSploit - Unused AWS Regions]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem exfiltrar data by transferring the data, including through sharing/syncing and creating backups of cloud environments, to another cloud account they control on the same service.

A defender who is monitoring for large transfers to outside the cloud environment through normal file transfers or over Command and Control (C2) channels may not be watching for data transfers to another account within the same cloud provider. Such transfers may utilize existing cloud provider APIs and the internal address space of the cloud provider to blend into normal traffic or avoid data transfers over external network interfaces. `[Ref: TLDRSec AWS Attacks]`

Os adversários podem também use cloud-native mechanisms to share victim data with adversary-controlled cloud accounts, such as creating anonymous file sharing links or, in Azure, a shared access signature (SAS) URI. `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Storage Shared Access Signature]`

Incidents have been observed where adversaries have created backups of cloud instances and transferred them to separate accounts. `[Ref: DOJ GRU Indictment Jul 2018]`

techniques.namePt: Roubo de Cookie de Sessão Web
techniques.fullNamePt: Roubo de Cookie de Sessão Web
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode steal web application or service session cookies and use them para obter acesso a web applications or Internet services as an authenticated user without needing credentials. Web applications and services often use session cookies as an authentication token after a user has authenticated to a website.

Cookies are often valid for an extended period of time, even if the web application is not actively used. Cookies can be found on disk, in the memória do processo of the browser, and in tráfego de rede to sistemas remotos. Additionally, other applications on the targets machine might store sensitive authentication cookies in memory (e.g. apps which authenticate to cloud services). Session cookies pode ser utilizado para bypasses some multi-factor authentication protocols. `[Ref: Pass The Cookie]`

There are several examples of malware targeting cookies from web browsers on the local system. `[Ref: Kaspersky TajMahal April 2019]` `[Ref: Unit 42 Mac Crypto Cookies January 2019]` Os adversários podem também steal cookies by injecting malicious JavaScript content into websites or relying on **User Execution** (`T1204`) by tricking victims into running malicious JavaScript in their browser. `[Ref: Talos Roblox Scam 2023]` `[Ref: Krebs Discord Bookmarks 2023]`

There are also open source frameworks such as `Evilginx2` and `Muraena` that can gather session cookies through a malicious proxy (e.g., **Adversary-in-the-Middle** (`T1557`)) that can be set up by an adversary and used in phishing campaigns. `[Ref: Github evilginx2]` `[Ref: GitHub Mauraena]`

After an adversary acquires a valid cookie, they can then perform a **Web Session Cookie** (`T1550.004`) technique to login to the corresponding web application.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar auditing for authentication activities and user logins to detect the use of stolen session cookies. Monitor for impossible travel scenarios and anomalous behavior that could indicate the use of compromised session tokens or cookies.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Configurar browsers or tasks to regularly delete persistent cookies.

Additionally, minimize the length of time a web cookie is viable to potentially reduce the impact of stolen cookies while also increasing the needed frequency of cookie theft attempts – providing defenders with additional chances at detection. `[Ref: Token tactics]` Por exemplo, use non-persistent cookies to limit the duration a session ID will remain on the web client cache where an attacker could obtain it. `[Ref: Session Management Cheat Sheet]`

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict or block web-based content that could be used to extract session cookies or credentials stored in browsers. Use browser security settings, such as disabling third-party cookies and restricting browser extensions, to limit the attack surface.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Deploy hardware-based token (e.g., YubiKey or FIDO key), which incorporates the target login domain as part of the negotiation protocol, will prevent session cookie theft through proxy methods.

Implementar Conditional Access policies to only allow logins from trusted devices, such as those enrolled in Intune or joined via Hybrid/Entra. This mitigates the risk of session cookie replay attacks by ensuring that stolen tokens cannot be reused on unauthorized devices.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Regularly update web browsers, password managers, and all related software to the latest versions. Keeping software up-to-date reduces the risk of vulnerabilities being exploited by attackers to extract stored credentials or session cookies.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Train users to identify aspects of phishing attempts where they're asked to enter credentials into a site that has the incorrect domain for the application they are logging into. Additionally, train users not to run untrusted JavaScript in their browser, such as by copying and pasting code or dragging and dropping bookmarklets.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comprometimento Pré-Boot (Bootkit/UEFI)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Pre-OS Boot mechanisms as a way to establish persistence on a system. During the booting process of a computer, firmware and various startup services are loaded before the sistema operativo. These programs control flow of execution before the sistema operativo takes control. `[Ref: Wikipedia Booting]`

Os adversários podem sobrescrever data in boot drivers or firmware such as BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) and The Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) to persist on systems at a layer below the sistema operativo. This can be particularly difficult to detect as malware at this level will not be detected by host software-based defenses.

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent access to file shares, remote access to systems, unnecessary services. Mechanisms to limit access may include use of network concentrators, RDP gateways, etc.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comprometimento Pré-Boot (Bootkit/UEFI): System Firmware
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar system firmware to persist on systems.The BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) and The Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) or Extensible Firmware Interface (EFI) are examples of system firmware that operate as the software interface between the sistema operativo and hardware of a computer. `[Ref: Wikipedia BIOS]` `[Ref: Wikipedia UEFI]` `[Ref: About UEFI]`

System firmware like BIOS and (U)EFI underly the functionality of a computer and may be modified by an adversary to perform or assist in malicious activity. Capabilities exist to overwrite the system firmware, which may give sophisticated adversaries a means to install malicious firmware updates as a means of persistence on a system that may be difficult to detect.

mitigations.name: Boot Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: Check the integrity of the existing BIOS or EFI to determine if it is vulnerable to modification. Use Trusted Platform Module technology.  `[Ref: TCG Trusted Platform Module]` Move system's root of trust to hardware to prevent tampering with the SPI flash memory. `[Ref: ESET LoJax Sept 2018]` Technologies such as Intel Boot Guard can assist with this.  `[Ref: Intel Hardware-based Security Technologies]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Comprometimento Pré-Boot (Bootkit/UEFI): Component Firmware
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar component firmware to persist on systems. Some adversaries may employ sophisticated means to compromise computer components and install malicious firmware that will execute adversary code outside of the sistema operativo and main system firmware or BIOS. This technique may be similar to **System Firmware** (`T1542.001`) but conducted upon other system components/devices that may not have the same capability or level of integrity checking.

Malicious component firmware could provide both a persistent level of access to systems despite potential typical failures to maintain access and hard disk re-images, as well as a way to evade host software-based defenses and integrity checks.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comprometimento Pré-Boot (Bootkit/UEFI): Bootkit
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar bootkits to persist on systems. A bootkit is a malware variant that modifies the boot sectors of a hard drive, allowing código malicioso to execute before a computer's sistema operativo has loaded. Bootkits reside at a layer below the sistema operativo and may make it difficult to perform full remediation unless an organization suspects one was used and can act accordingly.

In BIOS systems, a bootkit may modify the Master Boot Record (MBR) and/or Volume Boot Record (VBR). `[Ref: Mandiant M Trends 2016]` The MBR is the section of disk that is first loaded after completing hardware initialization by the BIOS. It is the location of the boot loader. An adversary who has raw access to the boot drive may overwrite this area, diverting execution during startup from the normal boot loader to adversary code. `[Ref: Lau 2011]`

The MBR passes control of the boot process to the VBR. De forma semelhante a the case of MBR, an adversary who has raw access to the boot drive may overwrite the VBR to divert execution during startup to adversary code.

In UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) systems, a bootkit may instead create or modify files in the EFI system partition (ESP). The ESP is a partition on data storage used by devices containing UEFI that allows the system to boot the OS and other utilities used by the system. Um adversário consegue use the newly created or patched files in the ESP to run malicious kernel code. `[Ref: Microsoft Security]` `[Ref: welivesecurity]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: Use Trusted Platform Module technology and a secure or trusted boot process to prevent system integrity from being compromised. `[Ref: TCG Trusted Platform Module]` `[Ref: TechNet Secure Boot Process]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Comprometimento Pré-Boot (Bootkit/UEFI): ROMMONkit
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de the ROM Monitor (ROMMON) by loading an unauthorized firmware with adversary code to provide persistent access and manipulate device behavior that is difficult to detect.  `[Ref: Cisco Synful Knock Evolution]` `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`


ROMMON is a Cisco network device firmware that functions as a boot loader, boot image, or boot helper to initialize hardware and software when the platform is powered on or reset. De forma semelhante a **TFTP Boot** (`T1542.005`), an adversary may upgrade the ROMMON image locally or remotely (for example, through TFTP) with adversary code and restart the device com o objetivo de overwrite the existing ROMMON image. This provides adversaries with the means to update the ROMMON to gain persistence on a system in a way that may be difficult to detect.

mitigations.name: Boot Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable secure boot features to validate the digital signature of the boot environment and system image using a special purpose hardware device. If the validation check fails, the device will fail to boot preventing loading of unauthorized software.  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - Secure Boot]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Periodically check the integrity of system image to ensure it has not been modified.  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - Image File Integrity]`  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - Image File Verification]`  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - Change Control]`

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific protocols, such as TFTP, pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific technique used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various network configurations.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comprometimento Pré-Boot (Bootkit/UEFI): TFTP Boot
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de netbooting to load an unauthorized network device sistema operativo from a Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) server. TFTP boot (netbooting) is commonly used by network administrators to load configuration-controlled network device images from a centralized management server. Netbooting is one option in the boot sequence and pode ser utilizado para centralize, manage, and control device images.

Os adversários podem manipular the configuration on the network device specifying use of a malicious TFTP server, which may be used in conjunction with **Modify System Image** (`T1601`) to load a modified image on device startup or reset. The unauthorized image allows adversaries to modify device configuration, add malicious capabilities to the device, and introduce backdoors to maintain control of the network device while minimizing detection through use of a standard functionality. This technique is similar to **ROMMONkit** (`T1542.004`) and may result in the network device running a modified image.  `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`

techniques.namePt: Criação ou Modificação de Processo de Sistema
techniques.fullNamePt: Criação ou Modificação de Processo de Sistema
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or modify system-level processes to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence. When sistema operativos boot up, they can start processes that perform background system functions. On Windows and Linux, these system processes are referred to as services. `[Ref: TechNet Services]` Em sistemas macOS, launchd processes known as **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`) and **Launch Agent** (`T1543.001`) are run to finish system initialization and load user specific parameters. `[Ref: AppleDocs Launch Agent Daemons]` 

Os adversários podem install new services, daemons, or agents that can be configured to execute at startup or a repeatable interval com o objetivo de establish persistence. Similarly, adversaries may modify existing services, daemons, or agents to achieve the same effect.  

Services, daemons, or agents may be created with administrator privileges but executed under root/SYSTEM privileges. Os adversários podem tirar partido de this functionality to create or modify system processes com o objetivo de escalate privileges. `[Ref: OSX Malware Detection]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limitar os privilégios das contas de utilizador and groups so that only authorized administrators can interact with system-level process changes and service configurations.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent an application from writing a signed vulnerable driver to the system. `[Ref: Malicious Driver Reporting Center]` On Windows 10 and 11, enable Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist to assist in hardening against third party-developed drivers. `[Ref: Microsoft driver block rules]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

techniques.fullNameEn: Create or Modify System Process: Launch Agent
techniques.fullNamePt: Criação ou Modificação de Processo de Sistema: Launch Agent
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or modify launch agents to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence. When a user logs in, a per-user launchd process is started which loads the parameters for each launch-on-demand user agent from the property list (.plist) file found in `/System/Library/LaunchAgents`, `/Library/LaunchAgents`, and `~/Library/LaunchAgents`. `[Ref: AppleDocs Launch Agent Daemons]` `[Ref: OSX Keydnap malware]`  `[Ref: Antiquated Mac Malware]` Property list files use the `Label`, `ProgramArguments `, and `RunAtLoad` keys to identify the Launch Agent's name, executable location, and execution time. `[Ref: OSX.Dok Malware]` Launch Agents are often installed to perform updates to programs, launch user specified programs at login, or to conduct other developer tasks.

 Launch Agents can also be executed using the **Launchctl** (`T1569.001`) command.
 
Os adversários podem install a new Launch Agent that executes at login by placing a .plist file into the appropriate folders with the `RunAtLoad` or `KeepAlive` keys set to `true`. `[Ref: Sofacy Komplex Trojan]` `[Ref: Methods of Mac Malware Persistence]` The Launch Agent name may be disguised by using a name from the related sistema operativo or benign software. techniques.fullNameEn: Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service
techniques.fullNamePt: Criação ou Modificação de Processo de Sistema: Systemd Service
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or modify systemd services to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence. Systemd is a system and service manager commonly used for managing background daemon processes (also known as services) and other system resources. `[Ref: Linux man-pages: systemd January 2014]` Systemd is the default initialization (init) system on many Linux distributions replacing legacy init systems, including SysVinit and Upstart, while remaining backwards compatible.  

Systemd utilizes unit ficheiros de configuração with the `.service` file extension to encode information about a service's process. Por omissão, system level unit files are stored in the `/systemd/system` directory of the root owned directories (`/`). User level unit files are stored in the `/systemd/user` directories of the user owned directories (`$HOME`). `[Ref: lambert systemd 2022]` 

Inside the `.service` unit files, the following directives são utilizados para execute commands: `[Ref: freedesktop systemd.service]`  

* `ExecStart`, `ExecStartPre`, and `ExecStartPost` directives execute when a service is started manually by `systemctl` or on system start if the service is set to automatically start.
* `ExecReload` directive executes when a service restarts. 
* `ExecStop`, `ExecStopPre`, and `ExecStopPost` directives execute when a service is stopped.  

Adversaries have created new service files, altered the commands a `.service` file’s directive executes, and modified the user directive a `.service` file executes as, which could result in privilege escalation. Os adversários podem também place symbolic links in these directories, enabling systemd to find these payloads regardless of where they reside on the filesystem. `[Ref: Anomali Rocke March 2019]` `[Ref: airwalk backdoor unix systems]` `[Ref: Rapid7 Service Persistence 22JUNE2016]` 

The `.service` file’s User directive pode ser utilizado para run service as a specific user, which could result in privilege escalation based on specific user/group permissions. 

Systemd services can be created via systemd generators, which support the dynamic generation of unit files. Systemd generators are small executables that run during boot or configuration reloads to dynamically create or modify systemd unit files by converting non-native configurations into services, symlinks, or drop-ins (i.e., **Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts** (`T1037`)). `[Ref: Elastic Security Labs Linux Persistence 2024]` `[Ref: Pepe Berba Systemd 2022]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
techniques.fullNamePt: Criação ou Modificação de Processo de Sistema: Windows Service
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or modify Windows services to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence. When Windows boots up, it starts programs or applications called services that perform background system functions. `[Ref: TechNet Services]` Windows service configuration information, including the file path to the service's executable or recovery programs/commands, is stored in the Windows Registry.

Os adversários podem install a new service or modify an existing service to execute at startup com o objetivo de persist on a system. Service configurations can be set or modified using system utilities (such as sc.exe), by directly modifying the Registry, or by interacting directly with the Windows API. 

Os adversários podem também use services to install and execute malicious drivers. Por exemplo, after dropping a driver file (ex: `.sys`) to disk, the payload can be loaded and registered via **Native API** (`T1106`) functions such as `CreateServiceW()` (or manually via functions such as `ZwLoadDriver()` and `ZwSetValueKey()`), by creating the required service Registry values (i.e. **Modify Registry** (`T1112`)), or by using command-line utilities such as `PnPUtil.exe`. `[Ref: Symantec W.32 Stuxnet Dossier]` `[Ref: Crowdstrike DriveSlayer February 2022]` `[Ref: Unit42 AcidBox June 2020]` Os adversários podem tirar partido de these drivers as **Rootkit** (`T1014`)s to hide the presence of malicious activity on a system. Os adversários podem também load a signed yet vulnerable driver onto a compromised machine (known as "Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver" (BYOVD)) as part of **Exploitation for Privilege Escalation** (`T1068`). `[Ref: ESET InvisiMole June 2020]` `[Ref: Unit42 AcidBox June 2020]`

Services may be created with administrator privileges but are executed under SYSTEM privileges, so an adversary may also use a service para escalar privilégios. Os adversários podem também directly start services through **Service Execution** (`T1569.002`).

To make detection analysis more challenging, malicious services may also incorporate **Masquerade Task or Service** (`T1036.004`) (ex: using a service and/or payload name related to a legitimate OS or benign software component). Os adversários podem também create ‘hidden’ services (i.e., **Hide Artifacts** (`T1564`)), for example by using the `sc sdset` command to set service permissions via the Service Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL). This may hide a Windows service from the view of standard service enumeration methods such as `Get-Service`, `sc query`, and `services.exe`. `[Ref: SANS 1]` `[Ref: SANS 2]`

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent an application from writing a signed vulnerable driver to the system. `[Ref: Malicious Driver Reporting Center]` On Windows 10 and 11, enable Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist to assist in hardening against third party-developed service drivers. `[Ref: Microsoft driver block rules]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

techniques.fullNameEn: Create or Modify System Process: Launch Daemon
techniques.fullNamePt: Criação ou Modificação de Processo de Sistema: Launch Daemon
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or modify Launch Daemons para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos payloads as part of persistence. Launch Daemons are plist files used to interact with Launchd, the service management framework used by macOS. Launch Daemons require privilégios elevados to install, are executed for every user on a system prior to login, and run in the background without the need for user interaction. During the macOS initialization startup, the launchd process loads the parameters for launch-on-demand system-level daemons from plist files found in `/System/Library/LaunchDaemons/` and `/Library/LaunchDaemons/`. Required Launch Daemons parameters include a `Label` to identify the task, `Program` to provide a path to the executable, and `RunAtLoad` to specify when the task is run. Launch Daemons are often used to provide access to shared resources, updates to software, or conduct automation tasks. `[Ref: AppleDocs Launch Agent Daemons]` `[Ref: Methods of Mac Malware Persistence]` `[Ref: launchd Keywords for plists]`

Os adversários podem install a Launch Daemon configured to execute at startup by using the `RunAtLoad` parameter set to `true` and the `Program` parameter set to the malicious executable path. The daemon name may be disguised by using a name from a related sistema operativo or benign software (i.e. **Masquerading** (`T1036`)). When the Launch Daemon is executed, the program inherits administrative permissions. `[Ref: WireLurker]` `[Ref: OSX Malware Detection]`

Additionally, system configuration changes (such as the installation of third party package managing software) may cause folders such as `usr/local/bin` to become globally writeable. So, it is possible for poor configurations to allow an adversary to modify executables referenced by current Launch Daemon's plist files. `[Ref: LaunchDaemon Hijacking]` `[Ref: sentinelone macos persist Jun 2019]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limitar os privilégios das contas de utilizador and remediate Privilege Escalation vectors so only authorized administrators can create new Launch Daemons.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use auditing tools capable of detecting folder permissions abuse opportunities on systems, especially reviewing changes made to folders by third-party software.

techniques.fullNameEn: Create or Modify System Process: Container Service
techniques.fullNamePt: Criação ou Modificação de Processo de Sistema: Container Service
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or modify container or container cluster management tools that run as daemons, agents, or services on individual hosts. These include software for creating and managing individual containers, such as Docker and Podman, as well as container cluster node-level agents such as kubelet. By modifying these services, an adversary may be able to achieve persistence or escalate their privileges on a host.

Por exemplo, by using the `docker run` or `podman run` command with the `restart=always` directive, a container can be configured to persistently restart on the host. `[Ref: AquaSec TeamTNT 2023]` A user with access to the (rootful) docker command may also be able to escalate their privileges on the host. `[Ref: GTFOBins Docker]`

In Kubernetes environments, DaemonSets allow an adversary to persistently **Deploy Container** (`T1610`)s on all nodes, including ones added later to the cluster. `[Ref: Aquasec Kubernetes Attack 2023]` `[Ref: Kubernetes DaemonSet]` Pods can also be deployed to specific nodes using the `nodeSelector` or `nodeName` fields in the pod spec. `[Ref: Kubernetes Assigning Pods to Nodes]` `[Ref: AppSecco Kubernetes Namespace Breakout 2020]`

Note that containers can also be configured to run as **Systemd Service** (`T1543.002`)s. `[Ref: Podman Systemd]` `[Ref: Docker Systemd]`

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Where possible, consider enforcing the use of container services in rootless mode to limit the possibility of privilege escalation or malicious effects on the host running the container.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit access to utilities such as docker to only users who have a legitimate need, especially if using docker in rootful mode. In Kubernetes environments, only grant privileges to deploy pods to users that require it.

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence and/or elevate privileges using system mechanisms that trigger execution based on specific events. Various sistema operativos have means to monitor and subscribe to events such as logons or other user activity such as running specific applications/binaries. Cloud environments may also support various functions and services that monitor and can be invoked in response to specific cloud events. `[Ref: Backdooring an AWS account]` `[Ref: Varonis Power Automate Data Exfiltration]` `[Ref: Microsoft DART Case Report 001]`

Os adversários podem abusar de these mechanisms as a means of maintaining persistent access to a victim via repeatedly executing código malicioso. After gaining access to a victim system, adversaries may create/modify event triggers to point to malicious content that will be executed whenever the event trigger is invoked. `[Ref: FireEye WMI 2015]` `[Ref: Malware Persistence on OS X]` `[Ref: amnesia malware]`

Since the execution can be proxied by an account with higher permissions, such as SYSTEM or service accounts, an adversary may be able to abuse these triggered execution mechanisms to escalate their privileges.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Manage the creation, modification, use, and permissions associated to privileged accounts, including SYSTEM and root.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Event Triggered Execution: Change Default File Association
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Change Default File Association
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence by executing malicious content triggered by a file type association. When a file is opened, the default program used to open the file (also called the file association or handler) is checked. File association selections are stored in the Windows Registry and can be edited by users, administrators, or programs that have Registry access or by administrators using the built-in assoc utility. `[Ref: Microsoft Change Default Programs]` `[Ref: Microsoft File Handlers]` `[Ref: Microsoft Assoc Oct 2017]` Applications can modify the file association for a given file extension to call an arbitrary program when a file with the given extension is opened.

System file associations are listed under `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\.[extension]`, for example `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\.txt`. The entries point to a handler for that extension located at `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\\[handler]`. The various commands are then listed as subkeys underneath the shell key at `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\\[handler]\shell\\[action]\command`. For example: 

* `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\txtfile\shell\open\command`
* `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\txtfile\shell\print\command`
* `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\txtfile\shell\printto\command`

The values of the keys listed are commands that are executed when the handler opens the file extension. Adversaries can modify these values to continually execute comandos arbitrários. `[Ref: TrendMicro TROJ-FAKEAV OCT 2012]`

This includes tracking changes under HKCU and HKCR for file extension mappings, and correlating them with new or suspicious handler paths launching unusual child processes (e.g., PowerShell, cmd, wscript).

techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity. Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension. `[Ref: Wikipedia Screensaver]` The Windows screensaver application scrnsave.scr is located in `C:\Windows\System32\`, and `C:\Windows\sysWOW64\`  on 64-bit Windows systems, along with screensavers included with base Windows installations.

The following screensaver settings are stored in the Registry (`HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\`) and could be manipulated to achieve persistence:

* `SCRNSAVE.exe` - set to malicious PE path
* `ScreenSaveActive` - set to '1' to enable the screensaver
* `ScreenSaverIsSecure` - set to '0' to not require a password to unlock
* `ScreenSaveTimeout` - sets user inactivity timeout before screensaver is executed

Adversaries can use screensaver settings to maintain persistence by setting the screensaver to run malware after a certain timeframe of user inactivity. `[Ref: ESET Gazer Aug 2017]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Block .scr files from being executed from non-standard locations.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use Group Policy to disable screensavers if they are unnecessary. `[Ref: TechNet Screensaver GP]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

Monitor for registry modification performed by unusual processes (e.g., powershell.exe, reg.exe).

techniques.fullNameEn: Event Triggered Execution: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
techniques.namePt: Execução via Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) Event Subscription
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Execução via Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) Event Subscription
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence and elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by a Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) event subscription. WMI pode ser utilizado para install event filters, providers, consumers, and bindings that execute code when a defined event occurs. Examples of events that may be subscribed to are the wall clock time, user login, or the computer's uptime. `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2015]`

Os adversários podem utilizar the capabilities of WMI to subscribe to an event and execute código arbitrário when that event occurs, providing persistence on a system. `[Ref: FireEye WMI SANS 2015]` `[Ref: FireEye WMI 2015]` Os adversários podem também compile WMI scripts – using `mofcomp.exe`  –into Windows Management Object (MOF) files (.mof extension) that pode ser utilizado para create a malicious subscription. `[Ref: Dell WMI Persistence]` `[Ref: Microsoft MOF May 2018]`

WMI subscription execution is proxied by the WMI Provider Host process (WmiPrvSe.exe) and thus may result in elevated SYSTEM privileges.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Por omissão, only administrators are allowed to connect remotely using WMI; restrict other users that are allowed to connect, or disallow all users from connecting remotely to WMI.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent credential overlap across systems of administrator and privileged accounts. `[Ref: FireEye WMI 2015]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent malware from abusing WMI to attain persistence. `[Ref: win10_asr]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

techniques.fullNameEn: Event Triggered Execution: Unix Shell Configuration Modification
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Unix Shell Configuration Modification
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence through executing malicious commands triggered by a user’s shell. User **Unix Shell** (`T1059.004`)s execute several configuration scripts at different points throughout the session based on events. Por exemplo, when a user opens a interface de linha de comandos (CLI) or remotely logs in (such as via SSH) a login shell is initiated. The login shell executes scripts from the system (`/etc`) and the user’s home directory (`~/`) to configure the environment. All login shells on a system use /etc/profile when initiated. These configuration scripts run at the permission level of their directory and are often used to set variáveis de ambiente, create aliases, and customize the user’s environment. When the shell exits or terminates, additional shell scripts are executed to ensure the shell exits appropriately. 

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar establish persistence by inserting commands into scripts automatically executed by shells. Using bash as an example, the default shell for most GNU/Linux systems, adversaries may add commands that launch malicious binaries into the `/etc/profile` and `/etc/profile.d` files. `[Ref: intezer-kaiji-malware]` `[Ref: bencane blog bashrc]` These files typically require root permissions to modify and are executed each time any shell on a system launches. For user level permissions, adversaries can insert malicious commands into `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, or `~/.profile` which are sourced when a user opens a interface de linha de comandos (CLI) or connects remotely. `[Ref: anomali-rocke-tactics]` `[Ref: Linux manual bash invocation]` Since the system only executes the first existing file in the listed order, adversaries have used `~/.bash_profile` to ensure execution. Adversaries have also leveraged the `~/.bashrc` file which is additionally executed if the connection is established remotely or an additional interactive shell is opened, such as a new tab in the interface de linha de comandos (CLI). `[Ref: Tsunami]` `[Ref: anomali-rocke-tactics]` `[Ref: anomali-linux-rabbit]` `[Ref: Magento]` Some malware targets the termination of a program to trigger execution, adversaries can use the `~/.bash_logout` file para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos commands at the end of a session. 

For macOS, the functionality of this technique is similar but may leverage zsh, the default shell for macOS 10.15+. When the Terminal.app is opened, the application launches a zsh login shell and a zsh interactive shell. The login shell configures the system environment using `/etc/profile`, `/etc/zshenv`, `/etc/zprofile`, and `/etc/zlogin`. `[Ref: ScriptingOSX zsh]` `[Ref: PersistentJXA_leopitt]` `[Ref: code_persistence_zsh]` `[Ref: macOS MS office sandbox escape]` The login shell then configures the user environment with `~/.zprofile` and `~/.zlogin`. The interactive shell uses the `~/.zshrc` to configure the user environment. Upon exiting, `/etc/zlogout` and `~/.zlogout` are executed. For legacy programs, macOS executes `/etc/bashrc` on startup.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Making these files immutable and only changeable by certain administrators will limit the ability for adversaries to easily create user level persistence.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Trap
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence by executing malicious content triggered by an interrupt signal. The `trap` command allows programs and shells to specify commands that will be executed upon receiving interrupt signals. A common situation is a script allowing for graceful termination and handling of common keyboard interrupts like `ctrl+c` and `ctrl+d`.

Adversaries can use this to register code to be executed when the shell encounters specific interrupts as a mecanismo de persistência. Trap commands are of the following format `trap 'command list' signals` where "command list" will be executed when "signals" are received. `[Ref: Trap Manual]` `[Ref: Cyberciti Trap Statements]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: LC_LOAD_DYLIB Addition
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence by executing malicious content triggered by the execution of tainted binaries. Mach-O binaries have a series of headers that são utilizados para perform certain operations when a binary is loaded. The LC_LOAD_DYLIB header in a Mach-O binary tells macOS and OS X which dynamic libraries (dylibs) to load during execution time. These can be added ad-hoc to the compiled binary as long as adjustments are made to the rest of the fields and dependencies. `[Ref: Writing Bad Malware for OSX]` There are tools available to perform these changes.

Os adversários podem modificar Mach-O binary headers to load and execute malicious dylibs every time the binary is executed. Although any changes will invalidate assinaturas digitais on binaries because the binary is being modified, this can be remediated by simply removing the LC_CODE_SIGNATURE command from the binary so that the signature isn’t checked at load time. `[Ref: Malware Persistence on OS X]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Binaries can also be baselined for what dynamic libraries they require, and if an app requires a new dynamic library that wasn't included as part of an update, it should be investigated.

techniques.fullNameEn: Event Triggered Execution: Netsh Helper DLL
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Netsh Helper DLL
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence by executing malicious content triggered by Netsh Helper DLLs. Netsh.exe (also referred to as Netshell) is a command-line scripting utility used to interact with the network configuration of a system. It contains functionality to add helper DLLs for extending functionality of the utility. `[Ref: TechNet Netsh]` The paths to registered netsh.exe helper DLLs are entered into the Windows Registry at `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Netsh`.

Adversaries can use netsh.exe helper DLLs to trigger execution of código arbitrário in a persistent manner. This execution would take place anytime netsh.exe is executed, which could happen automatically, with another persistence technique, or if other software (ex: VPN) is present on the system that executes netsh.exe as part of its normal functionality. `[Ref: Github Netsh Helper CS Beacon]` `[Ref: Demaske Netsh Persistence]`
