techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Accessibility Features
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by accessibility features. Windows contains accessibility features that may be launched with a key combination before a user has logged in (ex: when the user is on the Windows logon screen). Um adversário consegue modify the way these programs are launched to get a command prompt or backdoor without logging in to the system.

Two common accessibility programs are `C:\Windows\System32\sethc.exe`, launched when the shift key is pressed five times and `C:\Windows\System32\utilman.exe`, launched when the Windows + U key combination is pressed. The sethc.exe program is often referred to as "sticky keys", and has been used by adversaries for unauthenticated access through a remote desktop login screen.  `[Ref: FireEye Hikit Rootkit]`

Dependendo de the version of Windows, an adversary may take advantage of these features in different ways. Common methods used by adversaries include replacing accessibility feature binaries or pointers/references to these binaries in the Registry. In newer versions of Windows, the replaced binary needs to be digitally signed for x64 systems, the binary must reside in `%systemdir%\`, and it must be protected by Windows File or Resource Protection (WFP/WRP).  `[Ref: DEFCON2016 Sticky Keys]` The **Image File Execution Options Injection** (`T1546.012`) debugger method was likely discovered as a potential workaround because it does not require the corresponding accessibility feature binary to be replaced.

For simple binary replacement on Windows XP and later as well as and Windows Server 2003/R2 and later, for example, the program (e.g., `C:\Windows\System32\utilman.exe`) may be replaced with "cmd.exe" (or another program that provides backdoor access). Subsequently, pressing the appropriate key combination at the login screen while sitting at the keyboard or when connected over **Remote Desktop Protocol** (`T1021.001`) will cause the replaced file to be executed with SYSTEM privileges.  `[Ref: Tilbury 2014]`

Other accessibility features exist that may also be leveraged in a similar fashion:  `[Ref: DEFCON2016 Sticky Keys]` `[Ref: Narrator Accessibility Abuse]`

* On-Screen Keyboard: `C:\Windows\System32\osk.exe`
* Magnifier: `C:\Windows\System32\Magnify.exe`
* Narrator: `C:\Windows\System32\Narrator.exe`
* Display Switcher: `C:\Windows\System32\DisplaySwitch.exe`
* App Switcher: `C:\Windows\System32\AtBroker.exe`

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: If possible, use a Remote Desktop Gateway to manage connections and security configuration of RDP within a network. `[Ref: TechNet RDP Gateway]`

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: To use this technique remotely, an adversary must use it in conjunction with RDP. Garantir que Network Level Authentication is enabled to force the remote desktop session to authenticate before the session is created and the login screen displayed. It is enabled by default on Windows Vista and later. `[Ref: TechNet RDP NLA]`

Identify and block potentially malicious software executed through accessibility features functionality by using application control  `[Ref: Beechey 2010]` tools, like Windows Defender Application Control `[Ref: Microsoft Windows Defender Application Control]`, AppLocker,  `[Ref: Windows Commands JPCERT]`  `[Ref: NSA MS AppLocker]` or Software Restriction Policies  `[Ref: Corio 2008]` where appropriate.  `[Ref: TechNet Applocker vs SRP]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: AppCert DLLs
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by AppCert DLLs loaded into processes. Dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) that are specified in the `AppCertDLLs` Registry key under `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\` are loaded into every process that calls the ubiquitously used application programming interface (API) functions `CreateProcess`, `CreateProcessAsUser`, `CreateProcessWithLoginW`, `CreateProcessWithTokenW`, or `WinExec`.  `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]`

De forma semelhante a **Process Injection** (`T1055`), this value pode ser abusado para obtain privilégios elevados by causing a malicious DLL to be loaded and run in the context of separate processes on the computer. Malicious AppCert DLLs may also provide persistence by continuously being triggered by API activity.

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: AppInit DLLs
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by AppInit DLLs loaded into processes. Dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) that are specified in the `AppInit_DLLs` value in the Registry keys `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows` or `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows` are loaded by user32.dll into every process that loads user32.dll. In practice this is nearly every program, since user32.dll is a very common library.  `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]`

The AppInit DLL functionality is disabled in Windows 8 and later versions when secure boot is enabled.  `[Ref: AppInit Secure Boot]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Application Shimming
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims. The Microsoft Windows Application Compatibility Infrastructure/Framework (Application Shim) was created to allow for backward compatibility of software as the sistema operativo codebase changes over time. Por exemplo, the application shimming feature allows developers to apply fixes to applications (without rewriting code) that were created for Windows XP so that it will work with Windows 10.  `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]`

Within the framework, shims are created to act as a buffer between the program (or more specifically, the Import Address Table) and the Windows OS. When a program is executed, the shim cache is referenced to determine if the program requires the use of the shim database (.sdb). If so, the shim database uses hooking to redirect the code as necessary com o objetivo de communicate with the OS. 

A list of all shims currently installed by the default Windows installer (sdbinst.exe) is kept in:

* `%WINDIR%\AppPatch\sysmain.sdb` and
* `hklm\software\microsoft\windows nt\currentversion\appcompatflags\installedsdb`

Custom databases are stored in:

* `%WINDIR%\AppPatch\custom & %WINDIR%\AppPatch\AppPatch64\Custom` and
* `hklm\software\microsoft\windows nt\currentversion\appcompatflags\custom`

To keep shims secure, Windows designed them to run in user mode so they cannot modify the kernel and you must have administrator privileges to install a shim. Contudo, certain shims pode ser utilizado para **Bypass User Account Control** (`T1548.002`) (UAC and RedirectEXE), inject DLLs into processes (InjectDLL), disable Data Execution Prevention (DisableNX) and Structure Exception Handling (DisableSEH), and intercept memory addresses (GetProcAddress).

Utilizing these shims may allow an adversary to perform several malicious acts such as elevate privileges, install backdoors, disable defenses like Windows Defender, etc.  `[Ref: FireEye Application Shimming]` Shims can also be abused to establish persistence by continuously being invoked by affected programs.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Microsoft released an optional patch update - KB3045645 - that will remove the "auto-elevate" flag within the sdbinst.exe. This will prevent use of application shimming para contornar (bypass) UAC.

techniques.fullNameEn: Event Triggered Execution: Image File Execution Options Injection
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Image File Execution Options Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by Image File Execution Options (IFEO) debuggers. IFEOs enable a developer to attach a debugger to an application. When a process is created, a debugger present in an application’s IFEO will be prepended to the application’s name, effectively launching the new process under the debugger (e.g., `C:\dbg\ntsd.exe -g  notepad.exe`). `[Ref: Microsoft Dev Blog IFEO Mar 2010]`

IFEOs can be set directly via the Registry or in Global Flags via the GFlags tool. `[Ref: Microsoft GFlags Mar 2017]` IFEOs are represented as `Debugger` values in the Registry under `HKLM\SOFTWARE{\Wow6432Node}\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\<executable>` where `<executable>` is the binary on which the debugger is attached. `[Ref: Microsoft Dev Blog IFEO Mar 2010]`

IFEOs can also enable an arbitrary monitor program to be launched when a specified program silently exits (i.e. is prematurely terminated by itself or a second, non kernel-mode process). `[Ref: Microsoft Silent Process Exit NOV 2017]` `[Ref: Oddvar Moe IFEO APR 2018]` De forma semelhante a debuggers, silent exit monitoring can be enabled through GFlags and/or by directly modifying IFEO and silent process exit Registry values in `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\`. `[Ref: Microsoft Silent Process Exit NOV 2017]` `[Ref: Oddvar Moe IFEO APR 2018]`

De forma semelhante a **Accessibility Features** (`T1546.008`), on Windows Vista and later as well as Windows Server 2008 and later, a Registry key may be modified that configures "cmd.exe," or another program that provides backdoor access, as a "debugger" for an accessibility program (ex: utilman.exe). After the Registry is modified, pressing the appropriate key combination at the login screen while at the keyboard or when connected with **Remote Desktop Protocol** (`T1021.001`) will cause the "debugger" program to be executed with SYSTEM privileges. `[Ref: Tilbury 2014]`

De forma semelhante a **Process Injection** (`T1055`), these values may also be abused to obtain privilege escalation by causing a malicious executable to be loaded and run in the context of separate processes on the computer. `[Ref: Elastic Process Injection July 2017]` Installing IFEO mechanisms may also provide Persistence via continuous triggered invocation.

Malware may also use IFEO to impair defenses by registering invalid debuggers that redirect and effectively disable various system and security applications. `[Ref: FSecure Hupigon]` `[Ref: Symantec Ushedix June 2008]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: PowerShell Profile
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem gain persistence and elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by PowerShell profiles. A PowerShell profile  (`profile.ps1`) is a script that runs when **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) starts and can be used as a logon script to customize user environments.

**PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) supports several profiles depending on the user or host program. Por exemplo, there can be different profiles for **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) host programs such as the PowerShell console, PowerShell ISE or Visual Studio Code. An administrator can also configure a profile that applies to all users and host programs on the local computer.  `[Ref: Microsoft About Profiles]` 

Os adversários podem modificar these profiles to include comandos arbitrários, functions, modules, and/or **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) drives to gain persistence. Every time a user opens a **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) session the modified script will be executed unless the `-NoProfile` flag is used when it is launched.  `[Ref: ESET Turla PowerShell May 2019]` 

Um adversário pode also be able para escalar privilégios if a script in a PowerShell profile is loaded and executed by an account with higher privileges, such as a domain administrator.  `[Ref: Wits End and Shady PowerShell Profiles]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Wits End and Shady PowerShell Profiles]

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de execution of only signed PowerShell scripts. Sign profiles to avoid them from being modified.
mitigations.bypassHint: Recorrer a DLL Side-Loading (`T1574.002`) utilizando um executável legítimo assinado (vulnerável a sequestro de ordem de procura de DLL) que carregue a nossa DLL em memória, ou utilizar binários assinados nativos (LOLBAS - `T1218`). Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Making PowerShell profiles immutable and only changeable by certain administrators will limit the ability for adversaries to easily create user level persistence.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Avoid PowerShell profiles if not needed. Use the -No Profile flag with when executing PowerShell scripts remotely to prevent local profiles and scripts from being executed.

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Emond
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem gain persistence and elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by the Event Monitor Daemon (emond). Emond is a **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`) that accepts events from various services, runs them through a simple rules engine, and takes action. The emond binary at `/sbin/emond` will load any rules from the `/etc/emond.d/rules/` directory and take action once an explicitly defined event takes place.

The rule files are in the plist format and define the name, event type, and action to take. Some examples of event types include system startup and user authentication. Examples of actions are to run a system command or send an email. The emond service will not launch if there is no file present in the QueueDirectories path `/private/var/db/emondClients`, specified in the **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`) configuration file at`/System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.emond.plist`. `[Ref: xorrior emond Jan 2018]` `[Ref: magnusviri emond Apr 2016]` `[Ref: sentinelone macos persist Jun 2019]`

Os adversários podem abusar de this service by writing a rule to execute commands when a defined event occurs, such as system start up or user authentication. `[Ref: xorrior emond Jan 2018]` `[Ref: magnusviri emond Apr 2016]` `[Ref: sentinelone macos persist Jun 2019]` Os adversários podem também be able para escalar privilégios from administrator to root as the emond service is executed with root privileges by the **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`) service.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling emond by removing the **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`) plist file.

Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Event Triggered Execution: Component Object Model Hijacking
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Component Object Model Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence by executing malicious content triggered by hijacked references to Component Object Model (COM) objects. COM is a system within Windows to enable interaction between software components through the sistema operativo. `[Ref: Microsoft Component Object Model]`  References to various COM objects are stored in the Registry. 

Os adversários podem utilizar the COM system to insert código malicioso that can be executed in place of legitimate software through hijacking the COM references and relationships as a means for persistence. Hijacking a COM object requires a change in the Registry to replace a reference to a legitimate system component which may cause that component to not work when executed. When that system component is executed through normal system operation the adversary's code will be executed instead. `[Ref: GDATA COM Hijacking]` An adversary is likely to hijack objects that are used frequently enough to maintain a consistent level of persistence, but are unlikely to break noticeable functionality within the system as to avoid system instability that could lead to detection. 

One variation of COM hijacking involves abusing Type Libraries (TypeLibs), which provide metadata about COM objects, such as their interfaces and methods. Os adversários podem modificar Registry keys associated with TypeLibs to redirect legitimate COM object functionality to malicious scripts or payloads. Unlike traditional COM hijacking, which commonly uses local DLLs, this variation may leverage the "script:" moniker to execute remote scripts hosted on external servers. `[Ref: RELIAQUEST]` This approach enables stealthy execution of code while maintaining persistence, as the remote payload would be automatically downloaded whenever the hijacked COM object is accessed.

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Installer Packages
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence and elevate privileges by using an installer to trigger the execution of malicious content. Installer packages are OS specific and contain the resources an sistema operativo needs to install applications on a system. Installer packages can include scripts that run prior to installation as well as after installation is complete. Installer scripts may inherit elevated permissions when executed. Developers often use these scripts to prepare the environment for installation, check requirements, download dependencies, and remove files after installation. `[Ref: Installer Package Scripting Rich Trouton]`

Using legitimate applications, adversaries have distributed applications with modified installer scripts para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos content. When a user installs the application, they may be required to grant administrative permissions to allow the installation. At the end of the installation process of the legitimate application, content such as macOS `postinstall` scripts can be executed with the inherited elevated permissions. Adversaries can use these scripts to execute a malicious executable or install other malicious components (such as a **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`)) with the elevated permissions. `[Ref: Application Bundle Manipulation Brandon Dalton]` `[Ref: wardle evilquest parti]` `[Ref: Windows AppleJeus GReAT]` `[Ref: Debian Manual Maintainer Scripts]`

Dependendo de the distribution, Linux versions of package installer scripts are sometimes called maintainer scripts or post installation scripts. These scripts can include `preinst`, `postinst`, `prerm`, `postrm` scripts and run as root when executed.

For Windows, the Microsoft Installer services uses `.msi` files to manage the installing, updating, and uninstalling of applications. These installation routines may also include instructions to perform additional actions that may be abused by adversaries. `[Ref: Microsoft Installation Procedures]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Udev Rules
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem maintain persistence through executing malicious content triggered using udev rules. Udev is the Linux kernel device manager that dynamically manages device nodes, handles access to pseudo-device files in the `/dev` directory, and responds to hardware events, such as when external devices like hard drives or keyboards are plugged in or removed. Udev uses rule files with `match keys` to specify the conditions a hardware event must meet and `action keys` to define the actions that should follow. Root permissions are required to create, modify, or delete rule files located in `/etc/udev/rules.d/`, `/run/udev/rules.d/`, `/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/`, `/usr/local/lib/udev/rules.d/`, and `/lib/udev/rules.d/`. Rule priority is determined by both directory and by the digit prefix in the rule filename. `[Ref: Ignacio Udev research 2024]` `[Ref: Elastic Linux Persistence 2024]`

Os adversários podem abusar de the udev subsystem by adding or modifying rules in udev rule files para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos content. Por exemplo, an adversary may configure a rule to execute their binary each time the pseudo-device file, such as `/dev/random`, is accessed by an application. Although udev is limited to running short tasks and is restricted by systemd-udevd's sandbox (blocking network and filesystem access), attackers may use scripting commands under the action key `RUN+=` to detach and run the malicious content’s process in the background para contornar (bypass) these controls. `[Ref: Reichert aon sedexp 2024]`

analytics.descriptionPt: Monitor for creation or modification of udev rules files in key directories (/etc/udev/rules.d/, /lib/udev/rules.d/, /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/). Look for RUN+= or IMPORT keys invoking suspicious binaries or scripts. Correlate this with process execution from systemd-udevd context, and file writes near udev reload/restart events. Combine this with unexpected background process spawning from udevd-related forks.

techniques.fullNameEn: Event Triggered Execution: Python Startup Hooks
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Acionada por Eventos: Python Startup Hooks
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem achieve persistence by leveraging Python’s startup mechanisms, including path configuration (`.pth`) files and the `sitecustomize.py` or `usercustomize.py` modules. These files are automatically processed during the initialization of the Python interpreter, allowing for the execution of código arbitrário whenever Python is invoked. `[Ref: Volexity GlobalProtect CVE 2024]`

Path ficheiros de configuração are designed to extend Python’s module search paths through the use of import statements. If a `.pth` file is placed in Python's `site-packages` or `dist-packages` directories, any lines beginning with `import` will be executed automatically on Python invocation. `[Ref: DFIR Python Persistence 2025]` Similarly, if `sitecustomize.py` or `usercustomize.py` is present in the Python path, these files will be imported during interpreter startup, and any code they contain will be executed. `[Ref: Python Site Configuration Hook]`

Os adversários podem abusar de these mechanisms to establish persistence on systems where Python is widely used (e.g., for automation or scripting in production environments).

detections.name: Linux Python Startup Hook Persistence via .pth and Customize Files (T1546.018)

analytics.descriptionPt: Defender observes unauthorized modification or creation of Python hook files such as `.pth`, `sitecustomize.py`, or `usercustomize.py` in Python `site-packages`, `dist-packages`, or user paths. This is often correlated with subsequent unexpected interpreter execution (e.g., python3 running without user interaction), changes in interpreter behavior (e.g., malicious imports), and outbound connections initiated from Python. Defender links write/modify actions on hook files with execve of python process and/or anomalous child process or network activity.

Os adversários podem configure system settings to automatically execute a program during system boot or logon to maintain persistence or gain higher-level privileges on compromised systems. Operating systems may have mechanisms for automatically running a program on system boot or account logon. `[Ref: Microsoft Run Key]` `[Ref: MSDN Authentication Packages]` `[Ref: Microsoft TimeProvider]` `[Ref: Cylance Reg Persistence Sept 2013]` `[Ref: Linux Kernel Programming]` These mechanisms may include automatically executing programs that are placed in specially designated directories or are referenced by repositories that store configuration information, such as the Windows Registry. Um adversário pode achieve the same goal by modifying or extending features of the kernel.

Since some boot or logon autostart programs run with higher privileges, an adversary may leverage these to elevate privileges.

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem achieve persistence by adding a program to a startup folder or referencing it with a Registry run key. Adding an entry to the "run keys" in the Registry or startup folder will cause the program referenced to be executed when a user logs in. `[Ref: Microsoft Run Key]` These programs will be executed under the context of the user and will have the account's associated permissions level.

The following run keys are created by default on Windows systems:

* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`
* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce`
* `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`
* `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce`

Run keys may exist under multiple hives. `[Ref: Microsoft Wow6432Node 2018]` `[Ref: Malwarebytes Wow6432Node 2016]` The `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnceEx` is also available but is not created by default on Windows Vista and newer. Registry run key entries can reference programs directly or list them as a dependency. `[Ref: Microsoft Run Key]` Por exemplo, it is possible to load a DLL at logon using a "Depend" key with RunOnceEx: `reg add HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnceEx\0001\Depend /v 1 /d "C:\temp\evil[.]dll"`  `[Ref: Oddvar Moe RunOnceEx Mar 2018]`

Placing a program within a startup folder will also cause that program to execute when a user logs in. There is a startup folder location for individual user accounts as well as a system-wide startup folder that will be checked regardless of which user account logs in. The startup folder path for the current user is `C:\Users\\[Username]\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup`. The startup folder path for all users is `C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp`.

The following Registry keys pode ser utilizado para set startup folder items for persistence:

* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\User Shell Folders`
* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Shell Folders`
* `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Shell Folders`
* `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\User Shell Folders`

The following Registry keys can control automatic startup of services during boot:

* `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunServicesOnce`
* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunServicesOnce`
* `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunServices`
* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunServices`

Using policy settings to specify startup programs creates corresponding values in either of two Registry keys:

* `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer\Run`
* `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer\Run`

Programs listed in the load value of the registry key `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows` run automatically for the currently logged-on user.

Por omissão, the multistring `BootExecute` value of the registry key `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager` is set to `autocheck autochk *`. This value causes Windows, at startup, to check the file-system integrity of the hard disks if the system has been shut down abnormally. Adversaries can add other programs or processes to this registry value which will automatically launch at boot.

Adversaries can use these configuration locations to execute malware, such as remote access tools, to maintain persistence through system reboots. Os adversários podem também use **Masquerading** (`T1036`) to make the Registry entries look as if they are associated with legitimate programs.

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Authentication Package
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Authentication Package
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de authentication packages to execute DLLs when the system boots. Windows authentication package DLLs are loaded by the Local Security Authority (LSA) process at system start. They provide support for multiple logon processes and multiple security protocols to the sistema operativo. `[Ref: MSDN Authentication Packages]`

Adversaries can use the autostart mechanism provided by LSA authentication packages for persistence by placing a reference to a binary in the Windows Registry location `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\` with the key value of `"Authentication Packages"=<target binary>`. The binary will then be executed by the system when the authentication packages are loaded.

mitigations.name: Privileged Process Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: Windows 8.1, Windows Server 2012 R2, and later versions, may make LSA run as a Protected Process Light (PPL) by setting the Registry key `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RunAsPPL`, which requires all DLLs loaded by LSA to be signed by Microsoft.  `[Ref: Graeber 2014]`  `[Ref: Microsoft Configurar LSA]`

analytics.descriptionPt: Registry modification of the LSA Authentication Packages key followed by LSASS loading a non-standard or unsigned DLL. This includes unusual write access to `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa`, especially during non-installation timeframes. Correlated with `lsass.exe` loading DLLs not present in baseline or lacking valid signatures.

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Time Providers
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Time Providers
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de time providers to execute DLLs when the system boots. The Windows Time service (W32Time) enables time synchronization across and within domains. `[Ref: Microsoft W32Time Feb 2018]` W32Time time providers are responsible for retrieving time stamps from hardware/network resources and outputting these values to other network clients. `[Ref: Microsoft TimeProvider]`

Time providers are implemented as dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) that are registered in the subkeys of `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\W32Time\TimeProviders\`. `[Ref: Microsoft TimeProvider]` The time provider manager, directed by the service control manager, loads and starts time providers listed and enabled under this key at system startup and/or whenever parameters are changed. `[Ref: Microsoft TimeProvider]`

Os adversários podem abusar de this architecture to establish persistence, specifically by creating a new arbitrarily named subkey  pointing to a malicious DLL in the `DllName` value. Administrator privilégios são necessários for time provider registration, though execution will run in context of the Local Service account. `[Ref: Github W32Time Oct 2017]`

mitigations.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider using Group Policy to configure and block modifications to W32Time parameters in the Registry.  `[Ref: Microsoft W32Time May 2017]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider using Group Policy to configure and block additions/modifications to W32Time DLLs.  `[Ref: Microsoft W32Time May 2017]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Winlogon Helper DLL
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Winlogon Helper DLL
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de features of Winlogon to execute DLLs and/or executables when a user logs in. Winlogon.exe is a Windows component responsible for actions at logon/logoff as well as the secure attention sequence (SAS) triggered by Ctrl-Alt-Delete. Registry entries in `HKLM\Software[\\Wow6432Node\\]\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\` and `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\` são utilizados para manage additional helper programs and functionalities that support Winlogon. `[Ref: Cylance Reg Persistence Sept 2013]` 

Malicious modifications to these Registry keys may cause Winlogon to load and execute malicious DLLs and/or executables. Especificamente, the following subkeys have been known to be possibly vulnerable to abuse:  `[Ref: Cylance Reg Persistence Sept 2013]`

* Winlogon\Notify - points to notification package DLLs that handle Winlogon events
* Winlogon\Userinit - points to userinit.exe, the user initialization program executed when a user logs on
* Winlogon\Shell - points to explorer.exe, the system shell executed when a user logs on

Os adversários podem take advantage of these features to repeatedly execute código malicioso and establish persistence.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Identify and block potentially malicious software that may be executed through the Winlogon helper process by using application control  `[Ref: Beechey 2010]` tools like AppLocker  `[Ref: Windows Commands JPCERT]`  `[Ref: NSA MS AppLocker]` that are capable of auditing and/or blocking unknown DLLs.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the privileges of user accounts so that only authorized administrators can perform Winlogon helper changes.

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Security Support Provider
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Security Support Provider
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de security support providers (SSPs) to execute DLLs when the system boots. Windows SSP DLLs are loaded into the Local Security Authority (LSA) process at system start. Uma vez que loaded into the LSA, SSP DLLs have access to encrypted and passwords em plaintext that are stored in Windows, such as any logged-on user's Domain password or smart card PINs.

The SSP configuration is stored in two Registry keys: `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Security Packages` and `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\OSConfig\Security Packages`. Um adversário pode modify these Registry keys to add new SSPs, which will be loaded the next time the system boots, or when the AddSecurityPackage Windows API function is called. `[Ref: Graeber 2014]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Process Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: Windows 8.1, Windows Server 2012 R2, and later versions may make LSA run as a Protected Process Light (PPL) by setting the Registry key `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa\\RunAsPPL`, which requires all SSP DLLs to be signed by Microsoft.  `[Ref: Graeber 2014]`  `[Ref: Microsoft Configurar LSA]`

detections.name: Registry and LSASS Monitoring for Security Support Provider Abuse

analytics.name: Analytic 1495
analytics.descriptionPt: Monitor registry modifications to `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Security Packages` or `...\OSConfig\Security Packages`, especially insertions of new DLL entries. Correlate this with subsequent DLL module loads into `lsass.exe`. Track unsigned or anomalous DLLs loading into LSASS using image load auditing. LSASS loads unsigned DLL due to AuditLevel=8 registry configuration or System reboot followed by DLL load into lsass.exe

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Kernel Modules and Extensions
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Kernel Modules and Extensions
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar the kernel to automatically execute programs on system boot. Loadable Kernel Modules (LKMs) are pieces of code that can be loaded and unloaded into the kernel upon demand. They extend the functionality of the kernel without the need to reboot the system. Por exemplo, one type of module is the device driver, which allows the kernel to access hardware connected to the system. `[Ref: Linux Kernel Programming]` 

When used maliciously, LKMs can be a type of kernel-mode **Rootkit** (`T1014`) that run with the highest sistema operativo privilege (Ring 0). `[Ref: Linux Kernel Module Programming Guide]` Common features of LKM based rootkits include: hiding itself, selective hiding of files, processes and network activity, as well as log tampering, providing authenticated backdoors, and enabling root access to non-privileged users. `[Ref: iDefense Rootkit Overview]`

Kernel extensions, also called kext, are used in macOS to load functionality onto a system similar to LKMs for Linux. Since the kernel is responsible for enforcing security and the kernel extensions run as apart of the kernel, kexts are not governed by macOS security policies. Kexts are loaded and unloaded through `kextload` and `kextunload` commands. Kexts need to be signed with a developer ID that is granted privileges by Apple allowing it to sign Kernel extensions. Developers without these privileges may still sign kexts but they will not load unless SIP is disabled. If SIP is enabled, the kext signature is verified before being added to the AuxKC. `[Ref: System and kernel extensions in macOS]`

Since macOS Catalina 10.15, kernel extensions have been deprecated in favor of System Extensions. Contudo, kexts are still allowed as "Legacy System Extensions" since there is no System Extension for Kernel Programming Interfaces. `[Ref: Apple Kernel Extension Deprecation]`

Adversaries can use LKMs and kexts to conduct **Persistence** (`TA0003`) and/or **Privilege Escalation** (`TA0004`) on a system. Examples have been found in the wild, and there are some relevant open source projects as well. `[Ref: Volatility Phalanx2]` `[Ref: CrowdStrike Linux Rootkit]` `[Ref: GitHub Reptile]` `[Ref: GitHub Diamorphine]` `[Ref: RSAC 2015 San Francisco Patrick Wardle]` `[Ref: Synack Secure Kernel Extension Broken]` `[Ref: Securelist Ventir]` `[Ref: Trend Micro Skidmap]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: System and kernel extensions in macOS]

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit access to the root account and prevent users from loading kernel modules and extensions through proper privilege separation and limiting Privilege Escalation opportunities.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use MDM to disable user's ability to install or approve kernel extensions, and ensure all approved kernel extensions are in alignment with policies specified in `com.apple.syspolicy.kernel-extension-policy`. `[Ref: Apple TN2459 Kernel Extensions]` `[Ref: MDMProfileConfigMacOS]`

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Common tools for detecting Linux rootkits include: rkhunter  `[Ref: SourceForge rkhunter]`, chrootkit  `[Ref: Chkrootkit Main]`, although rootkits may be designed to evade certain detection tools.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Application control and software restriction tools, such as SELinux, KSPP, grsecurity MODHARDEN, and Linux kernel tuning can aid in restricting kernel module loading. `[Ref: Kernel.org Restrict Kernel Module]` `[Ref: Wikibooks Grsecurity]` `[Ref: Kernel Self Protection Project]` `[Ref: Increasing Linux kernel integrity]` `[Ref: LKM loading kernel restrictions]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Re-opened Applications
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Re-opened Applications
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar plist files to automatically run an application when a user logs in. When a user logs out or restarts via the macOS Graphical User Interface (GUI), a prompt is provided to the user with a checkbox to "Reopen windows when logging back in". `[Ref: Re-Open windows on Mac]` When selected, all applications currently open are added to a property list file named `com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist` within the `~/Library/Preferences/ByHost` directory. `[Ref: Methods of Mac Malware Persistence]` `[Ref: Wardle Persistence Chapter]` Applications listed in this file are automatically reopened upon the user’s next logon.

Adversaries can establish **Persistence** (`TA0003`) by adding a malicious application path to the `com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist` file to execute payloads when a user logs in.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: This feature can be disabled entirely with the following terminal command: `defaults write -g ApplePersistence -bool no`.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Holding the Shift key while logging in prevents apps from opening automatically. `[Ref: Re-Open windows on Mac]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: LSASS Driver
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: LSASS Driver
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar or add LSASS drivers to obtain persistence on compromised systems. The Windows security subsystem is a set of components that manage and enforce the security policy for a computer or domain. The Local Security Authority (LSA) is the main component responsible for local security policy and user authentication. The LSA includes multiple dynamic link libraries (DLLs) associated with various other security functions, all of which run in the context of the LSA Subsystem Service (LSASS) lsass.exe process. `[Ref: Microsoft Security Subsystem]`

Os adversários podem target LSASS drivers to obtain persistence. By either replacing or adding illegitimate drivers (e.g., **Hijack Execution Flow** (`T1574`)), an adversary can use LSA operations to continuously execute malicious payloads.

mitigations.name: Privileged Process Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 8.1 and Server 2012 R2, enable LSA Protection by setting the Registry key `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa\\RunAsPPL` to `dword:00000001`.  `[Ref: Microsoft LSA Protection Mar 2014]` LSA Protection ensures that LSA plug-ins and drivers are only loaded if they are digitally signed with a Microsoft signature and adhere to the Microsoft Security Development Lifecycle (SDL) process guidance.

mitigations.name: Credential Access Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10 and Server 2016, enable Windows Defender Credential Guard  `[Ref: Microsoft Enable Cred Guard April 2017]` to run lsass.exe in an isolated virtualized environment without any device drivers.  `[Ref: Microsoft Credential Guard April 2017]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Com RunAsPPL ativo, processos em User-Mode não conseguem abrir handles `PROCESS_VM_READ` no LSASS. Vetores de contorno: (1) Pivotar para extração sem tocar no LSASS: Kerberoasting (`T1558.003`), AS-REP Roasting (`T1558.004`), ou extração de segredos DPAPI/Vault (`T1555.004`); (2) Se for Domain Admin/equivalente, usar DCSync (`T1003.006`) remotamente; (3) Abusar de drivers assinados vulneráveis (BYOVD - `T1068`) como `mimidrv.sys` ou `procexp152.sys` para remover a flag `PS_PROTECTION` em Kernel-Mode; (4) Se Credential Guard (VBS) estiver ativo, hashes NTLM em cache ficam isolados em `LsaIso.exe` — contornar usando captura de Tickets Kerberos em memória via Rubeus (`monitor`/`tgtdeleg`) ou roubo de cookies de sessão browser.

mitigations.name: Restrict Library Loading
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure safe DLL search mode is enabled `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\SafeDllSearchMode` to mitigate risk that lsass.exe loads a código malicioso library.  `[Ref: Microsoft DLL Security]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Shortcut Modification
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Shortcut Modification
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or modify shortcuts that can execute a program during system boot or user login. Shortcuts or symbolic links são utilizados para reference other files or programs that will be opened or executed when the shortcut is clicked or executed by a system startup process.

Os adversários podem abusar de shortcuts in the startup folder to execute their tools and achieve persistence. `[Ref: Shortcut for Persistence ]` Although often used as payloads in an infection chain (e.g. **Spearphishing Attachment** (`T1566.001`)), adversaries may also create a new shortcut as a means of indirection, while also abusing **Masquerading** (`T1036`) to make the malicious shortcut appear as a legitimate program. Adversaries can also edit the target path or entirely replace an existing shortcut so their malware will be executed instead of the intended legitimate program.

Shortcuts can also be abused to establish persistence by implementing other methods. Por exemplo, LNK browser extensions may be modified (e.g. **Browser Extensions** (`T1176.001`)) to persistently launch malware.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Limit Privileges for Shortcut Creation: While the SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege is not directly related to .lnk file creation, you should still enforce least privilege principles by limiting user rights to create and modify shortcuts, especially in system-critical locations. This can be done through GPO: Computer Configuration > [Policies] > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment: Create symbolic links.  `[Ref: UCF STIG Symbolic Links]`

Regular User Permissions Review: Regularly review and audit user permissions to ensure that only necessary accounts have write access to startup folders and critical system directories.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevents malicious shortcuts or LNK files from executing unwanted code by ensuring only authorized applications and scripts are allowed to run.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Applying strict permissions to directories where shortcuts are stored, such as the startup folder, can prevent unauthorized modifications.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

detections.name: Detection Strategy for T1547.009 – Shortcut Modification (Windows)

analytics.name: Analytic 0510
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection correlates file creation or modification of `.lnk` (shortcut) files in autostart locations with anomalous parent-child process lineage or unsigned binaries. Defenders should watch for LNK creation/modification events outside of known software installations, patch events, or OS updates. techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Port Monitors
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Port Monitors
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar port monitors to run an adversary supplied DLL during system boot for persistence or privilege escalation. A port monitor can be set through the `AddMonitor` API call to set a DLL to be loaded at startup. `[Ref: AddMonitor]` This DLL can be located in `C:\Windows\System32` and will be loaded and run by the print spooler service, `spoolsv.exe`, under SYSTEM level permissions on boot. `[Ref: Bloxham]` 

Alternatively, an arbitrary DLL can be loaded if permissions allow writing a fully-qualified pathname for that DLL to the `Driver` value of an existing or new arbitrarily named subkey of `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Monitors`. The Registry key contains entries for the following:

* Local Port
* Standard TCP/IP Port
* USB Monitor
* WSD Port

detections.name: Detection Strategy for T1547.010 – Port Monitor DLL Persistence via spoolsv.exe (Windows)

analytics.name: Analytic 0580
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects suspicious registry modifications under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Monitors\*\Driver`, DLL loads by `spoolsv.exe` of non-standard or unsigned modules, and abnormal usage of the `AddMonitor` API by non-installation processes. This pattern often indicates an attempt to persist a malicious DLL via the print monitor mechanism, particularly when correlated with creation of files in `C:\Windows\System32` not tied to known patches or installations.

Define whether only SYSTEM/user installs are expected to make changes to the port monitor registry keys
Timeframe between registry modification and subsequent spoolsv.exe DLL load
Filter on calling process of AddMonitor API to detect anomalies outside installer/updater

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Print Processors
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Print Processors
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de print processors to run malicious DLLs during system boot for persistence and/or privilege escalation. Print processors are DLLs that are loaded by the print spooler service, `spoolsv.exe`, during boot. `[Ref: Microsoft Intro Print Processors]`

Os adversários podem abusar de the print spooler service by adding print processors that load malicious DLLs at startup. A print processor can be installed through the `AddPrintProcessor` API call with an account that has `SeLoadDriverPrivilege` enabled. Alternatively, a print processor can be registered to the print spooler service by adding the `HKLM\SYSTEM\\[CurrentControlSet or ControlSet001]\Control\Print\Environments\\[Windows architecture: e.g., Windows x64]\Print Processors\\[user defined]\Driver` Registry key that points to the DLL.

For the malicious print processor to be correctly installed, the payload must be located in the dedicated system print-processor directory, that can be found with the `GetPrintProcessorDirectory` API call, or referenced via a relative path from this directory. `[Ref: Microsoft AddPrintProcessor May 2018]` After the print processors are installed, the print spooler service, which starts during boot, must be restarted in order for them to run. `[Ref: ESET PipeMon May 2020]`

The print spooler service runs under SYSTEM level permissions, therefore print processors installed by an adversary may run under privilégios elevados.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit user accounts that can load or unload device drivers by disabling `SeLoadDriverPrivilege`.

detections.name: Windows Detection Strategy for T1547.012 - Print Processor DLL Persistence

analytics.name: Analytic 0074
analytics.descriptionPt: Correlated registry modifications under Print Processors path, followed by DLL file creation within the system print processor directory, and DLL load by spoolsv.exe. Malicious execution often occurs during service restart or system boot, with SYSTEM-level privileges.

mutableElements.description: Correlate Registry + DLL Write + Module Load within a short boot or spooler restart window (e.g., 5 minutes).
System-specific path derived from GetPrintProcessorDirectory API call; may differ across Windows versions or configurations.
Some environments may use custom or non-standard DLL naming conventions for print processors. Allowlist known values.
Check Authenticode signature and issuer chain for loaded DLLs to reduce false positives.
Monitor for spoolsv.exe restart events that trigger malicious print processor loading.

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: XDG Autostart Entries
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: XDG Autostart Entries
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem add or modify XDG Autostart Entries para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos programs or commands when a user’s desktop environment is loaded at login. XDG Autostart entries are available for any XDG-compliant Linux system. XDG Autostart entries use Desktop Entry files (`.desktop`) to configure the user’s desktop environment upon user login. These ficheiros de configuração determine what applications launch upon user login, define associated applications to open specific file types, and define applications used to open removable media. `[Ref: Free Desktop Application Autostart Feb 2006]` `[Ref: Free Desktop Entry Keys]`

Os adversários podem abusar de this feature to establish persistence by adding a path to a malicious binary or command to the `Exec` directive in the `.desktop` configuration file. When the user’s desktop environment is loaded at user login, the `.desktop` files located in the XDG Autostart directories are automatically executed. System-wide Autostart entries are located in the `/etc/xdg/autostart` directory while the user entries are located in the `~/.config/autostart` directory.

Os adversários podem combine this technique with **Masquerading** (`T1036`) to blend malicious Autostart entries with legitimate programs. `[Ref: Red Canary Netwire Linux 2022]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict write access to XDG autostart entries to only select privileged users.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limitar os privilégios das contas de utilizador so only authorized privileged users can create and modify XDG autostart entries.

mitigations.name: Limit Software Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict software installation to trusted repositories only and be cautious of orphaned software packages.

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Active Setup
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Active Setup
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem achieve persistence by adding a Registry key to the Active Setup of the local machine. Active Setup is a Windows mechanism that é utilizado para execute programs when a user logs in. The value stored in the Registry key will be executed after a user logs into the computer. `[Ref: Klein Active Setup 2010]` These programs will be executed under the context of the user and will have the account's associated permissions level.

Os adversários podem abusar de Active Setup by creating a key under ` HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\` and setting a malicious value for `StubPath`. This value will serve as the program that will be executed when a user logs into the computer. `[Ref: Mandiant Glyer APT 2010]` `[Ref: Citizenlab Packrat 2015]` `[Ref: FireEye CFR Watering Hole 2012]` `[Ref: SECURELIST Bright Star 2015]` `[Ref: paloalto Tropic Trooper 2016]`

Adversaries can abuse these components to execute malware, such as remote access tools, to maintain persistence through system reboots. Os adversários podem também use **Masquerading** (`T1036`) to make the Registry entries look as if they are associated with legitimate programs.

detections.name: Detect Active Setup Persistence via StubPath Execution

analytics.name: Analytic 0871
analytics.descriptionPt: Multi-event correlation of Registry creation under Active Setup with anomalous execution of processes at user logon. Behavioral patterns include creation/modification of HKLM Active Setup keys with non-standard StubPath values, followed by process execution from uncommon paths, unsigned binaries, or unusual parent-child lineage post-user login.

mutableElements.description: Correlate registry change and process execution within a specific user logon session (e.g., 5–10 minutes)
Expected parent processes for Active Setup launched binaries (e.g., explorer.exe). Deviations may indicate abuse.
Degree of randomness/uncommonness in StubPath values. High entropy may indicate obfuscation.
Flag if launched binary in StubPath is unsigned or uncommon for baseline
Check which user/context added the Active Setup key to detect privilege abuse

techniques.fullNameEn: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Login Items
techniques.fullNamePt: Execução Automática no Boot ou Logon: Login Items
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem add login items to execute upon user login to gain persistence or escalate privileges. Login items are applications, documents, folders, or server connections that are automatically launched when a user logs in. `[Ref: Open Login Items Apple]` Login items can be added via a shared file list or Service Management Framework. `[Ref: Adding Login Items]` Shared file list login items can be set using scripting languages such as **AppleScript** (`T1059.002`), whereas the Service Management Framework uses the API call `SMLoginItemSetEnabled`.

Login items installed using the Service Management Framework leverage `launchd`, are not visible in the System Preferences, and can only be removed by the application that created them. `[Ref: Adding Login Items]` `[Ref: SMLoginItemSetEnabled Schroeder 2013]` Login items created using a shared file list are visible in System Preferences, can hide the application when it launches, and are executed through LaunchServices, not launchd, to open applications, documents, or URLs without using Finder. `[Ref: Launch Services Apple Developer]` Users and applications use login items to configure their user environment to launch commonly used services or applications, such as email, chat, and music applications.

Adversaries can utilize **AppleScript** (`T1059.002`) and **Native API** (`T1106`) calls to create a login item to spawn malicious executables. `[Ref: ELC Running at startup]` Prior to version 10.5 on macOS, adversaries can add login items by using **AppleScript** (`T1059.002`) to send an Apple events to the “System Events” process, which has an AppleScript dictionary for manipulating login items. `[Ref: Login Items AE]` Adversaries can use a command such as `tell application “System Events” to make login item at end with properties /path/to/executable`. `[Ref: Startup Items Eclectic]` `[Ref: hexed osx.dok analysis 2019]` `[Ref: Add List Remove Login Items Apple Script]` This command adds the path of the malicious executable to the login item file list located in `~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.backgroundtaskmanagementagent/backgrounditems.btm`. `[Ref: Startup Items Eclectic]` Adversaries can also use login items to launch executables that pode ser utilizado para control the victim system remotely or as a means to gain privilege escalation by prompting for user credentials. `[Ref: objsee mac malware 2017]` `[Ref: CheckPoint Dok]` `[Ref: objsee netwire backdoor 2019]`

detections.name: Detection Strategy for T1547.015 – Login Items on macOS

analytics.descriptionPt: Creation or modification of Login Items using AppleScript or Service Management Framework. Detection focuses on file creation/modification of `backgrounditems.btm`, new executables in `Contents/Library/LoginItems/`, use of `SMLoginItemSetEnabled` API, or suspicious processes triggered post-login without user interaction. Behavioral pivot includes anomalous AppleEvents, suspicious parent-child process pairs, and login-triggered execution chains.

techniques.namePt: Abuso de Mecanismo de Controlo de Elevação
techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Mecanismo de Controlo de Elevação
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem circumvent mechanisms designed to control privilege elevation to gain higher-level permissions. Most modern systems contain native elevation control mechanisms that are intended to limit privileges that a user can perform on a machine. Authorization has to be granted to specific users com o objetivo de perform tasks that can be considered of higher risk. `[Ref: TechNet How UAC Works]` `[Ref: sudo man page 2018]` Um adversário consegue perform several methods to take advantage of built-in control mechanisms com o objetivo de escalate privileges on a system. `[Ref: OSX Keydnap malware]` `[Ref: Fortinet Fareit]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: System settings can prevent applications from running that haven't been downloaded from legitimate repositories which may help mitigate some of these issues. Not allowing unsigned applications from being run may also mitigate some risk.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Applications with known vulnerabilities or known shell escapes should not have the setuid or setgid bits set to reduce potential damage if an application is compromised. Additionally, the number of programs with setuid or setgid bits set should be minimized across a system. Ensuring that the sudo tty_tickets setting is enabled will prevent this leakage across tty sessions.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Perform regular software updates to mitigate exploitation risk.

mitigations.name: User Account Control
mitigations.descriptionPt: Although UAC bypass techniques exist, it is still prudent to use the highest enforcement level for UAC when possible and mitigate bypass opportunities that exist with techniques such as **DLL** (`T1574.001`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Remove users from the Administrador Local group on systems.

By requiring a password, even if an adversary can get terminal access, they must know the password to run anything in the sudoers file. Setting the timestamp_timeout to 0 will require the user to input their password every time sudo is executed.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the privileges of cloud accounts to assume, create, or impersonate additional roles, policies, and permissions to only those required. Where just-in-time access is enabled, consider requiring manual approval for temporary elevation of privileges.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Check for common UAC bypass weaknesses on Windows systems to be aware of the risk posture and address issues where appropriate. `[Ref: Github UACMe]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: The sudoers file should be strictly edited such that passwords are always required and that users can't spawn risky processes as users with higher privilege.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid
techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Mecanismo de Controlo de Elevação: Setuid and Setgid
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode abuse configurations where an application has the setuid or setgid bits set com o objetivo de get code running in a different (and possibly more privileged) user’s context. On Linux or macOS, when the setuid or setgid bits are set for an application binary, the application will run with the privileges of the owning user or group respectively. `[Ref: setuid man page]` Normally an application is run in the current user’s context, regardless of which user or group owns the application. Contudo, there are instances where programs need to be executed in an elevated context to function properly, but the user running them may not have the specific required privileges.

Instead of creating an entry in the sudoers file, which must be done by root, any user can specify the setuid or setgid flag to be set for their own applications (i.e. **Linux and Mac Permissions** (`T1222.002`)). The `chmod` command can set these bits with bitmasking, `chmod 4777 [file]` or via shorthand naming, `chmod u+s [file]`. This will enable the setuid bit. To enable the setgid bit, `chmod 2775` and `chmod g+s` can be used.

Adversaries can use this mechanism on their own malware to make sure they're able to execute in elevated contexts in the future. `[Ref: OSX Keydnap malware]` This abuse is often part of a "shell escape" or other actions para contornar (bypass) an execution environment with restricted permissions.

Alternatively, adversaries may choose to find and target vulnerable binaries with the setuid or setgid bits already enabled (i.e. **File and Directory Discovery** (`T1083`)). The setuid and setguid bits are indicated with an "s" instead of an "x" when viewing a file's attributes via `ls -l`. The `find` command pode também ser utilizado para search for such files. Por exemplo, `find / -perm +4000 2>/dev/null` pode ser utilizado para find files with setuid set and `find / -perm +2000 2>/dev/null` may be used for setgid. Binaries that have these bits set may then be abused by adversaries. `[Ref: GTFOBins Suid]`

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Applications with known vulnerabilities or known shell escapes should not have the setuid or setgid bits set to reduce potential damage if an application is compromised. Additionally, the number of programs with setuid or setgid bits set should be minimized across a system.

techniques.fullNameEn: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control
techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Mecanismo de Controlo de Elevação: Bypass User Account Control
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem contornar (bypass) UAC mechanisms to elevate process privileges on system. Windows User Account Control (UAC) allows a program to elevate its privileges (tracked as integrity levels ranging from low to high) to perform a task under administrator-level permissions, possibly by prompting the user for confirmation. The impact to the user ranges from denying the operation under high enforcement to allowing the user to perform the action if they are in the Administrador Locals group and click through the prompt or allowing them to enter an administrator password to complete the action. `[Ref: TechNet How UAC Works]`

If the UAC protection level of a computer is set to anything but the highest level, certain Windows programs can elevate privileges or execute some elevated **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`) objects without prompting the user through the UAC notification box. `[Ref: TechNet Inside UAC]` `[Ref: MSDN COM Elevation]` An example of this is use of **Rundll32** (`T1218.011`) to load a specifically crafted DLL which loads an auto-elevated **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`) object and performs a file operation in a protected directory which would typically require elevated access. Malicious software may also be injected into a trusted process to gain privilégios elevados without prompting a user. `[Ref: Davidson Windows]`

Many methods have been discovered para contornar (bypass) UAC. The Github readme page for UACME contains an extensive list of methods `[Ref: Github UACMe]` that have been discovered and implemented, but may not be a comprehensive list of bypasses. Additional bypass methods are regularly discovered and some used in the wild, such as:

* `eventvwr.exe` can auto-elevate and execute a specified binary or script. `[Ref: enigma0x3 Fileless UAC Bypass]` `[Ref: Fortinet Fareit]`

Another bypass is possible through some lateral movement techniques if credentials for an account with administrator privileges are known, since UAC is a single system security mechanism, and the privilege or integrity of a process running on one system will be unknown on sistemas remotos and default to high integrity. `[Ref: SANS UAC Bypass]`

detections.name: Detection Strategy for T1548.002 – Bypass User Account Control (UAC)

analytics.name: Analytic 1094
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects a multi-event behavior chain involving UAC bypass attempts via known auto-elevated binaries (e.g., eventvwr.exe, sdclt.exe), unauthorized Registry changes to UAC-related keys, and anomalous process execution with privilégios elevados but lacking standard parent-child lineage. Suspicious patterns include invocation of auto-elevated COM objects or manipulation of isolatedCommand Registry entries without consent prompts.

mutableElements.description: Correlate registry tampering and elevation within a tunable time window (e.g., 30 seconds) to reduce noise from benign admin activity.
Tunable list of suspicious elevated binaries (e.g., sdclt.exe, eventvwr.exe, computerdefaults.exe) known to support UAC bypass.
Define logic for parent-child mismatch (e.g., non-elevated process spawning auto-elevated one) to flag uncommon elevation paths.

techniques.fullNameEn: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Mecanismo de Controlo de Elevação: Sudo and Sudo Caching
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem realizar sudo caching and/or use the sudoers file to elevate privileges. Os adversários podem do this to execute commands as other users or spawn processes with higher privileges.

Within Linux and MacOS systems, sudo (sometimes referred to as "superuser do") allows users to perform commands from terminals with privilégios elevados and to control who can perform these commands on the system. The `sudo` command "allows a system administrator to delegate authority to give certain users (or groups of users) the ability to run some (or all) commands as root or another user while providing an audit trail of the commands and their arguments." `[Ref: sudo man page 2018]` Since sudo was made for the system administrator, it has some useful configuration features such as a `timestamp_timeout`, which is the amount of time in minutes between instances of `sudo` before it will re-prompt for a password. This is because `sudo` has the ability to cache credentials for a period of time. Sudo creates (or touches) a file at `/var/db/sudo` with a timestamp of when sudo was last run to determine this timeout. Additionally, there is a `tty_tickets` variable that treats each new tty (terminal session) in isolation. This means that, for example, the sudo timeout of one tty will not affect another tty (you will have to type the password again).

The sudoers file, `/etc/sudoers`, describes which users can run which commands and from which terminals. This also describes which commands users can run as other users or groups. This provides the principle of least privilege such that users are running in their lowest possible permissions for most of the time and only elevate to other users or permissions as needed, typically by prompting for a password. Contudo, the sudoers file can also specify when to not prompt users for passwords with a line like `user1 ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL`. `[Ref: OSX.Dok Malware]` Elevated privilégios são necessários to edit this file though.

Adversaries can also abuse poor configurations of these mechanisms para escalar privilégios without needing the user's password. Por exemplo, `/var/db/sudo`'s timestamp can be monitored to see if it falls within the `timestamp_timeout` range. If it does, then malware can execute sudo commands without needing to supply the user's password. Additional, if `tty_tickets` is disabled, adversaries can do this from any tty for that user.

In the wild, malware has disabled `tty_tickets` to potentially make scripting easier by issuing `echo \'Defaults !tty_tickets\' >> /etc/sudoers`. `[Ref: cybereason osx proton]` In order for this change to be reflected, the malware also issued `killall Terminal`. As of macOS Sierra, the sudoers file has `tty_tickets` enabled by default.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: The sudoers file should be strictly edited such that passwords are always required and that users can't spawn risky processes as users with higher privilege.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensuring that the `tty_tickets` setting is enabled will prevent this leakage across tty sessions.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: By requiring a password, even if an adversary can get terminal access, they must know the password to run anything in the sudoers file. Setting the `timestamp_timeout` to 0 will require the user to input their password every time `sudo` is executed.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).
