techniques.fullNameEn: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Elevated Execution with Prompt
techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Mecanismo de Controlo de Elevação: Elevated Execution with Prompt
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de the `AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges` API para escalar privilégios by prompting the user for credentials. `[Ref: AppleDocs AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges]` The purpose of this API is to give application developers an easy way to perform operations with root privileges, such as for application installation or updating. This API does not validate that the program requesting root privileges comes from a reputable source or has been maliciously modified. 

Although this API is deprecated, it still fully functions in the latest releases of macOS. When calling this API, the user will be prompted to enter their credentials but no checks on the origin or integrity of the program are made. The program calling the API may also load world writable files which can be modified to perform malicious behavior with privilégios elevados.

Os adversários podem abusar de `AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges` to obtain root privileges com o objetivo de install malicious software on victims and install mecanismo de persistências. `[Ref: Death by 1000 installers; it's all broken!]` `[Ref: Carbon Black Shlayer Feb 2019]` `[Ref: OSX Coldroot RAT]` This technique may be combined with **Masquerading** (`T1036`) to trick the user into granting escalated privileges to código malicioso. `[Ref: Death by 1000 installers; it's all broken!]` `[Ref: Carbon Black Shlayer Feb 2019]` This technique has also been shown to work by modifying legitimate programs present on the machine that make use of this API. `[Ref: Death by 1000 installers; it's all broken!]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access
techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Mecanismo de Controlo de Elevação: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de permission configurations that allow them to gain temporarily elevated access to cloud resources. Many cloud environments allow administrators to grant user or service accounts permission to request just-in-time access to roles, impersonate other accounts, pass roles onto resources and services, or otherwise gain short-term access to a set of privileges that may be distinct from their own. 

Just-in-time access is a mechanism for granting additional roles to cloud accounts in a granular, temporary manner. This allows accounts to operate with only the permissions they need on a daily basis, and to request additional permissions as necessary. Sometimes just-in-time access requests are configured to require manual approval, while other times the desired permissions are automatically granted. `[Ref: Azure Just in Time Access 2023]`

Account impersonation allows user or service accounts to temporarily act with the permissions of another account. Por exemplo, in GCP users with the `iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` role can create temporary access tokens or sign arbitrary payloads with the permissions of a service account, while service accounts with domain-wide delegation permission are permitted to impersonate Google Workspace accounts. `[Ref: Google Cloud Service Account Authentication Roles]` `[Ref: Hunters Domain Wide Delegation Google Workspace 2023]` `[Ref: Google Cloud Just in Time Access 2023]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Unit 42 Google Workspace Domain Wide Delegation 2023]` In Exchange Online, the `ApplicationImpersonation` role allows a service account to use the permissions associated with specified user accounts. `[Ref: Microsoft Impersonation and EWS in Exchange]` 

Many cloud environments also include mechanisms for users to pass roles to resources that allow them to perform tasks and authenticate to other services. While the user that creates the resource does not directly assume the role they pass to it, they may still be able to take advantage of the role's access -- for example, by configuring the resource to perform certain actions with the permissions it has been granted. In AWS, users with the `PassRole` permission can allow a service they create to assume a given role, while in GCP, users with the `iam.serviceAccountUser` role can attach a service account to a resource. `[Ref: AWS PassRole]` `[Ref: Google Cloud Service Account Authentication Roles]`

While users require specific role assignments com o objetivo de use any of these features, cloud administrators may misconfigure permissions. This could result in escalation paths that allow adversaries para obter acesso a resources beyond what was originally intended. `[Ref: Rhino Google Cloud Privilege Escalation]` `[Ref: Rhino Security Labs AWS Privilege Escalation]`

**Note:** this technique is distinct from **Additional Cloud Roles** (`T1098.003`), which involves assigning permanent roles to accounts rather than abusing existing permissions structures to gain temporarily elevated access to resources. Contudo, adversaries that compromise a sufficiently privileged account may grant another account they control **Additional Cloud Roles** (`T1098.003`) that would allow them to also abuse these features. This may also allow for greater stealth than would be had by directly using the highly privileged account, especially when logs do not clarify when role impersonation is taking place. `[Ref: CrowdStrike StellarParticle January 2022]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: TCC Manipulation
techniques.fullNamePt: Abuso de Mecanismo de Controlo de Elevação: TCC Manipulation
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries can manipulate or abuse the Transparency, Consent, & Control (TCC) service or database to grant malicious executables elevated permissions. TCC is a Privacy & Security macOS control mechanism used to determine if the running process has permission to access the data or services protected by TCC, such as screen sharing, camera, microphone, or Full Disk Access (FDA).

When an application requests to access data or a service protected by TCC, the TCC daemon (`tccd`) checks the TCC database, located at `/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db` (and `~/` equivalent), and an overwrites file (if connected to an MDM) for existing permissions. If permissions do not exist, then the user is prompted to grant permission. Uma vez que permissions are granted, the database stores the application's permissions and will not prompt the user again unless reset. Por exemplo, when a web browser requests permissions to the user's webcam, once granted the web browser may not explicitly prompt the user again. `[Ref: welivesecurity TCC]`

Os adversários podem access restricted data or services protected by TCC through abusing applications previously granted permissions through **Process Injection** (`T1055`) or executing a malicious binary using another application. Por exemplo, adversaries can use Finder, a macOS native app with FDA permissions, to execute a malicious **AppleScript** (`T1059.002`). When executing under the Finder App, the malicious **AppleScript** (`T1059.002`) inherits access to all files on the system sem necessitar de a user prompt. When System Integrity Protection (SIP) is disabled, TCC protections are also disabled. techniques.namePt: Uso de Material de Autenticação Alternativo (PtH/PtT)
techniques.fullNamePt: Uso de Material de Autenticação Alternativo (PtH/PtT)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar alternate authentication material, such as password hashes, Kerberos tickets, and application access tokens, com o objetivo de move laterally dentro do ambiente alvo and bypass normal system access controls. 

Authentication processes generally require a valid identity (e.g., username) along with one or more authentication factors (e.g., password, pin, physical smart card, token generator, etc.). Alternate authentication material is legitimately generated by systems after a user or application successfully authenticates by providing a valid identity and the required authentication factor(s). Alternate authentication material may also be generated during the identity creation process. `[Ref: NIST Authentication]` `[Ref: NIST MFA]`

Caching alternate authentication material allows the system to verify an identity has successfully authenticated without asking the user to reenter authentication factor(s). Because the alternate authentication must be maintained by the system—either in memory or on disk—it may be at risk of being stolen through **Credential Access** (`TA0006`) techniques. By stealing alternate authentication material, adversaries are able para contornar (bypass) system access controls and authenticate to systems without knowing the plaintext password or any additional authentication factors.

techniques.fullNameEn: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token
techniques.fullNamePt: Uso de Material de Autenticação Alternativo (PtH/PtT): Application Access Token
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar stolen application access tokens para contornar (bypass) the typical processo de autenticação and access restricted accounts, information, or services on sistemas remotos. These tokens are typically stolen from users or services and used in lieu of login credentials.

Application access tokens são utilizados para make authorized API requests on behalf of a user or service and are commonly used to access resources in cloud, container-based applications, and software-as-a-service (SaaS). `[Ref: Auth0 - Why You Should Always Use Access Tokens to Secure APIs Sept 2019]` 

OAuth is one commonly implemented framework that issues tokens to users for access to systems. These frameworks are used collaboratively to verify the user and determine what actions the user is allowed to perform. Uma vez que identity is established, the token allows actions to be authorized, without passing the actual credentials of the user. Consequentemente, compromise of the token can grant the adversary access to resources of other sites through a malicious application. `[Ref: okta]`

Por exemplo, with a cloud-based email service, once an OAuth access token is granted to a malicious application, it can potentially gain long-term access to features of the user account if a "refresh" token enabling background access is awarded. `[Ref: Microsoft Identity Platform Access 2019]` With an OAuth access token an adversary can use the user-granted REST API to perform functions such as email searching and contact enumeration. `[Ref: Staaldraad Phishing with OAuth 2017]`

Compromised access tokens may be used as an initial step in compromising other services. Por exemplo, if a token grants access to a victim’s primary email, the adversary may be able to extend access to all other services which the target subscribes by triggering forgotten password routines. In AWS and GCP environments, adversaries can trigger a request for a short-lived access token with the privileges of another user account. `[Ref: Google Cloud Service Account Credentials]` `[Ref: AWS Temporary Security Credentials]` The adversary can then use this token to request data or perform actions the original account could not. If permissions for this feature are misconfigured – for example, by allowing all users to request a token for a particular account - an adversary may be able to gain initial access to a Cloud Account or escalate their privileges. `[Ref: Rhino Security Labs Enumerating AWS Roles]`

Direct API access through a token negates the effectiveness of a second authentication factor and may be immune to intuitive countermeasures like changing passwords.  Por exemplo, in AWS environments, an adversary who compromises a user’s AWS API credentials may be able to use the `sts:GetFederationToken` API call to create a federated user session, which will have the same permissions as the original user but may persist even if the original user credentials are deactivated. `[Ref: Crowdstrike AWS User Federation Persistence]` Additionally, access abuse over an API channel can be difficult to detect even from the service provider end, as the access can still align well with a legitimate workflow.

mitigations.name: Account Use Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Where possible, consider restricting the use of access tokens outside of expected contexts. Por exemplo, in AWS environments, consider using data perimeters to prevent credential use outside of an expected network. `[Ref: AWS Data Perimeters]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Administrators should audit all cloud and container accounts to ensure that they are necessary and that the permissions granted to them are appropriate. Where possible, the ability to request temporary account tokens on behalf of another accounts should be disabled. Additionally, administrators can leverage audit tools to monitor actions that can be conducted as a result of OAuth 2.0 access. A título de exemplo, audit reports enable admins to identify privilege escalation actions such as role creations or policy modifications, which could be actions performed after initial access.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Update corporate policies to restrict what types of third-party applications may be added to any online service or tool that is linked to the company's information, accounts or network (e.g., Google, Microsoft, Dropbox, Basecamp, GitHub). Contudo, rather than providing high-level guidance on this, be extremely specific—include a list of per-approved applications and deny all others not on the list. Administrators may also block end-user consent through administrative portals, such as the Azure Portal, disabling users from authorizing third-party apps through OAuth and forcing administrative consent. `[Ref: Microsoft Azure AD Admin Consent]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
techniques.fullNamePt: Uso de Material de Autenticação Alternativo (PtH/PtT): Pass the Hash
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem “pass the hash” using stolen password hashes para realizar movimentação lateral dentro do ambiente alvo, bypassing normal system access controls. Pass the hash (PtH) is a method of authenticating as a user without having access to the user's cleartext password. This method bypasses standard authentication steps that require a cleartext password, moving directly into the portion of the authentication that uses the password hash.

When performing PtH, valid password hashes for the account being used are captured using a **Credential Access** (`TA0006`) technique. Captured hashes are used with PtH to authenticate as that user. Uma vez que authenticated, PtH pode ser empregue para perform actions on local or sistemas remotos.

Os adversários podem também use stolen password hashes to "overpass the hash." De forma semelhante a PtH, this involves using a password hash to authenticate as a user but also uses the password hash to create a valid Kerberos ticket. This ticket can then be used to perform **Pass the Ticket** (`T1550.003`) attacks. `[Ref: Stealthbits Overpass-the-Hash]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Ticket
techniques.fullNamePt: Uso de Material de Autenticação Alternativo (PtH/PtT): Pass the Ticket
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem “pass the ticket” using stolen Kerberos tickets para realizar movimentação lateral dentro do ambiente alvo, bypassing normal system access controls. Pass the ticket (PtT) is a method of authenticating to a system using Kerberos tickets without having access to an account's password. Kerberos authentication can be used as the first step to lateral movement to a remote system.

When preforming PtT, valid Kerberos tickets for **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) are captured by **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`). A user's service tickets or ticket granting ticket (TGT) may be obtained, depending on the level of access. A service ticket allows for access to a particular resource, whereas a TGT pode ser utilizado para request service tickets from the Ticket Granting Service (TGS) to access any resource the user has privileges to access. `[Ref: ADSecurity AD Kerberos Attacks]` `[Ref: GentilKiwi Pass the Ticket]`

A **Silver Ticket** (`T1558.002`) can be obtained for services that use Kerberos as an authentication mechanism and são utilizados para generate tickets to access that particular resource and the system that hosts the resource (e.g., SharePoint). `[Ref: ADSecurity AD Kerberos Attacks]`

A **Golden Ticket** (`T1558.001`) can be obtained for the domain using the Key Distribution Service account KRBTGT account NTLM hash, which enables generation of TGTs for any account in Active Directory (AD). `[Ref: Campbell 2014]`

Os adversários podem também create a valid Kerberos ticket using other user information, such as stolen password hashes or AES keys. Por exemplo, "overpassing the hash" involves using a NTLM password hash to authenticate as a user (i.e. **Pass the Hash** (`T1550.002`)) while also using the password hash to create a valid Kerberos ticket. `[Ref: Stealthbits Overpass-the-Hash]`

Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

Consider rotating the KRBTGT account password every 180 days. `[Ref: STIG krbtgt reset]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie
techniques.fullNamePt: Uso de Material de Autenticação Alternativo (PtH/PtT): Web Session Cookie
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries can use stolen session cookies to authenticate to web applications and services. This technique bypasses some multi-factor authentication protocols since the session is already authenticated. `[Ref: Pass The Cookie]`

Authentication cookies are commonly used in web applications, including cloud-based services, after a user has authenticated to the service so credentials are not passed and re-authentication does not need to occur as frequently. Cookies are often valid for an extended period of time, even if the web application is not actively used. After the cookie is obtained through **Steal Web Session Cookie** (`T1539`) or **Web Cookies** (`T1606.001`), the adversary may then import the cookie into a browser they control and is then able to use the site or application as the user for as long as the session cookie is active. Uma vez que logged into the site, an adversary can access informação sensível, read email, or perform actions that the victim account has permissions to perform.

There have been examples of malware targeting session cookies para contornar (bypass) multi-factor authentication systems. `[Ref: Unit 42 Mac Crypto Cookies January 2019]`

There are multiple methods of preventing a user's command history from being flushed to their .bash_history file, including use of the following commands:
`set +o history` and `set -o history` to start logging again;

`ln -s /dev/null ~/.bash_history` to write commands to `/dev/null`instead.

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais Desprotegidas (Unsecured Credentials): Credentials In Files
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem pesquisar local sistema de ficheiross and remote file shares for files containing insecurely stored credentials. These can be files created by users to store their own credentials, shared credential stores for a group of individuals, ficheiros de configuração containing passwords for a system or service, or source code/binary files containing embedded passwords.

It is possible to extract passwords from backups or saved máquina virtual (VM)s through **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`). `[Ref: CG 2014]` Passwords may also be obtained from Group Policy Preferences stored on the Windows Domain Controller (DC). `[Ref: SRD GPP]`

In cloud and/or containerized environments, authenticated user and service account credentials are often stored in local configuration and credential files. `[Ref: Unit 42 Hildegard Malware]` They may also be found as parameters to deployment commands in container logs. `[Ref: Unit 42 Unsecured Docker Daemons]` In some cases, these files can be copied and reused on another machine or the contents can be read and then used to authenticate without needing to copy any files. `[Ref: Specter Ops - Cloud Credential Storage]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais Desprotegidas (Unsecured Credentials): Credentials in Registry
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem pesquisar the Registry on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials. The Windows Registry stores configuration information that can be used by the system or other programs. Os adversários podem consultar (query) the Registry looking for credentials and passwords that have been stored for use by other programs or services. Sometimes these credentials are used for automatic logons.

Example commands to find Registry keys related to password information:  `[Ref: Pentestlab Stored Credentials]`

* Local Machine Hive: `reg query HKLM /f password /t REG_SZ /s`
* Current User Hive: `reg query HKCU /f password /t REG_SZ /s`

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not store credentials within the Registry.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: If it is necessary that software must store credentials in the Registry, then ensure the associated accounts have limited permissions so they cannot be abused if obtained by an adversary.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais Desprotegidas (Unsecured Credentials): Shell History
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem pesquisar the command history on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials.

On Linux and macOS systems, shells such as Bash and Zsh keep track of the commands users type on the command-line with the "history" utility. Uma vez que a user logs out, the history is flushed to the user's history file. For each user, this file resides at the same location: for example, `~/.bash_history` or `~/.zsh_history`. Typically, these files keeps track of the user's last 1000 commands.

Em ambientes Windows, PowerShell has both a command history that is wiped after the session ends, and one that contains commands used in all sessions and is persistent. The default location for persistent history can be found in `%userprofile%\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\PSReadline\ConsoleHost_history.txt`, but command history can also be accessed with `Get-History`. Command Prompt (CMD) on Windows does not have persistent history. `[Ref: Microsoft about_History]` `[Ref: Medium]`

Users often type usernames and passwords on the command-line as parameters to programs, which then get saved to this file when they log out. Adversaries can abuse this by looking through the file for potential credentials. `[Ref: External to DA, the OS X Way]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: External to DA, the OS X Way]

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt:
There are multiple methods of preventing a user's command history from being flushed to their .bash_history file, including use of the following commands:
`set +o history` and `set -o history` to start logging again;
`unset HISTFILE` being added to a user's .bash_rc file; and
`ln -s /dev/null ~/.bash_history` to write commands to `/dev/null` instead.

In Zsh, `fc -p` pode ser utilizado para create a private history session. Contudo, previous history will be unavailable to the user until the session ends. Using `unset HISTFILE` and writing commands to `/dev/null` can also be used, similarly to Bash.

In PowerShell, users can utilize `Set-PSReadLineOption` to modify how commands are saved into history. Setting `-HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing` prevents command history from being saved onto the file. Note that setting it from `SaveNothing` to `SaveIncrementally` in the same session will cause all commands from that session to be saved. Alternatively, `-AddToHistoryHandler` pode ser utilizado para filter certain commands from being saved into the history file.

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais Desprotegidas (Unsecured Credentials): Private Keys
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem pesquisar for private key certificate files on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials. Private cryptographic keys and certificates are used for authentication, encryption/decryption, and assinaturas digitais. `[Ref: Wikipedia Public Key Crypto]` Common key and certificate file extensions include: .key, .pgp, .gpg, .ppk., .p12, .pem, .pfx, .cer, .p7b, .asc. 

Os adversários podem também look in common key directories, such as `~/.ssh` for SSH keys on * nix-based systems or `C:\Users\(username)\.ssh\` on Windows. Adversary tools may also search compromised systems for file extensions relating to cryptographic keys and certificates. `[Ref: Kaspersky Careto]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Prince of Persia]`

When a device is registered to Entra ID, a device key and a transport key are generated and used to verify the device’s identity. `[Ref: Microsoft Primary Refresh Token]` An adversary with access to the device may be able to export the keys com o objetivo de impersonate the device. `[Ref: AADInternals Azure AD Device Identities]`

On network devices, private keys may be exported via **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) commands such as `crypto pki export`. `[Ref: cisco_deploy_rsa_keys]` 

Some private keys require a password or passphrase for operation, so an adversary may also use **Input Capture** (`T1056`) for keylogging or attempt to **Brute Force** (`T1110`) the passphrase off-line. These private keys pode ser utilizado para authenticate to **Remote Services** (`T1021`) like SSH or for use in decrypting other collected files such as email.

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use strong passphrases for private keys to make cracking difficult.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure permissions are properly set on folders containing sensitive private keys to prevent unintended access. Additionally, on Cisco devices, set the `nonexportable` flag during RSA key pair generation. `[Ref: cisco_deploy_rsa_keys]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure only authorized keys are allowed access to critical resources and audit access lists regularly.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: When possible, store keys on separate cryptographic hardware instead of on the local system. Por exemplo, on Windows systems use a TPM to secure keys and other sensitive material de credenciais. `[Ref: Microsoft Primary Refresh Token]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API
techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais Desprotegidas (Unsecured Credentials): Cloud Instance Metadata API
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar access the Cloud Instance Metadata API to collect credentials and other dados sensíveis.

Most cloud service providers support a Cloud Instance Metadata API which is a service provided to running virtual instances that allows applications to access information about the running virtual instance. Available information generally includes name, security group, and additional metadata including dados sensíveis such as credentials and UserData scripts that may contain additional secrets. The Instance Metadata API is provided as a convenience to assist in managing applications and is accessible by anyone who can access the instance. `[Ref: AWS Instance Metadata API]` A cloud metadata API has been used in at least one high profile compromise. `[Ref: Krebs Capital One August 2019]`

If adversaries have a presence on the running virtual instance, they may query the Instance Metadata API directly to identify credentials that grant access to additional resources. Additionally, adversaries may exploit a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in a public facing web proxy that allows them para obter acesso a the informação sensível via a request to the Instance Metadata API. `[Ref: RedLock Instance Metadata API 2018]`

The de facto standard across cloud service providers is to host the Instance Metadata API at `http[:]//169.254.169.254`.

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit access to the Instance Metadata API using a host-based firewall such as iptables.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable unnecessary metadata services and restrict or disable insecure versions of metadata services that are in use to prevent adversary access. `[Ref: Amazon AWS IMDS V2]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit access to the Instance Metadata API. A properly configured Web Application Firewall (WAF) may help prevent external adversaries from exploiting Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks that allow access to the Cloud Instance Metadata API. `[Ref: RedLock Instance Metadata API 2018]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais Desprotegidas (Unsecured Credentials): Group Policy Preferences
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar find unsecured credentials in Group Policy Preferences (GPP). GPP are tools that allow administrators to create domain policies with embedded credentials. These policies allow administrators to set local accounts. `[Ref: Microsoft GPP 2016]`

These group policies are stored in SYSVOL on a Domain Controller (DC). This means that any domain user can view the SYSVOL share and decrypt the password (using the AES key that has been made public). `[Ref: Microsoft GPP Key]`

The following tools and scripts pode ser utilizado para gather and decrypt the password file from Group Policy Preference XML files:

* Metasploit’s post exploitation module: `post/windows/gather/credentials/gpp`
* Get-GPPPassword `[Ref: Obscuresecurity Get-GPPPassword]`
* gpprefdecrypt.py

On the SYSVOL share, adversaries may use the following command to enumerate potential GPP XML files: `dir /s * .xml`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Search SYSVOL for any existing GGPs that may contain credentials and remove them. `[Ref: ADSecurity Finding Passwords in SYSVOL]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais Desprotegidas (Unsecured Credentials): Container API
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem recolher credentials via APIs within a containers environment. APIs in these environments, such as the Docker API and Kubernetes APIs, allow a user to remotely manage their container resources and cluster components. `[Ref: Docker API]` `[Ref: Kubernetes API]`

Um adversário pode access the Docker API to collect logs that contain credentials to cloud, container, and various other resources in the environment. `[Ref: Unit 42 Unsecured Docker Daemons]` An adversary with sufficient permissions, such as via a pod's service account, may also use the Kubernetes API to retrieve credentials from the Kubernetes API server. These credentials may include those needed for Docker API authentication or secrets from Kubernetes cluster components.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use the principle of least privilege for privileged accounts such as the service account in Kubernetes. Por exemplo, if a pod is not required to access the Kubernetes API, consider disabling the service account altogether. `[Ref: Kubernetes Service Accounts]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit communications with the container service to managed and secured channels, such as local Unix sockets or remote access via SSH. Require secure port access para comunicar com the APIs over TLS by disabling unauthenticated access to the Docker API and Kubernetes API Server. `[Ref: Docker Daemon Socket Protect]` `[Ref: Kubernetes API Control Access]` In Kubernetes clusters deployed in cloud environments, use native cloud platform features to restrict the IP ranges that are permitted to access to API server. `[Ref: Kubernetes Cloud Native Security]` Where possible, consider enabling just-in-time (JIT) access to the Kubernetes API to place additional restrictions on access. `[Ref: Microsoft AKS Azure AD 2023]`

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Deny direct remote access to internal systems through the use of network proxies, gateways, and firewalls.

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais Desprotegidas (Unsecured Credentials): Chat Messages
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem directly collect unsecured credentials stored or passed through user communication services. Credentials may be sent and stored in user chat communication applications such as email, chat services like Slack or Teams, collaboration tools like Jira or Trello, and any other services that support user communication. Users may share various forms of credentials (such as usernames and passwords, API keys, or authentication tokens) on private or public corporate internal communications channels.

Rather than accessing the stored chat logs (i.e., **Credentials In Files** (`T1552.001`)), adversaries may directly access credentials within these services on the user endpoint, through servers hosting the services, or through administrator portals for cloud hosted services. Os adversários podem também compromise integration tools like Slack Workflows to automatically search through messages to extract user credentials. These credentials may then be abused to perform follow-on activities such as lateral movement or privilege escalation  `[Ref: Slack Security Risks]`.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Preemptively search through communication services to find shared unsecured credentials. Searching for common patterns like "`password is `", “`password=`” and take actions to reduce exposure when found.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que developers and system administrators are aware of the risk associated with sharing unsecured passwords across communication services.

techniques.fullNamePt: Subversão de Controlos de Confiança
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem undermine controlos de segurança that will either warn users of untrusted activity or prevent execution of untrusted programs. Operating systems and security products may contain mechanisms to identify programs or websites as possessing some level of trust. Examples of such features would include a program being allowed to run because it is signed by a valid code signing certificate, a program prompting the user with a warning because it has an attribute set from being downloaded from the Internet, or getting an indication that you are about to connect to an untrusted site.

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar subvert these trust mechanisms. The method adversaries use will depend on the specific mechanism they seek to subvert. Os adversários podem conduzir **File and Directory Permissions Modification** (`T1222`) or **Modify Registry** (`T1112`) in support of subverting these controls. `[Ref: SpectorOps Subverting Trust Sept 2017]` Os adversários podem também create or steal code signing certificates to acquire trust on target systems. `[Ref: Securelist Digital Certificates]` `[Ref: Symantec Digital Certificates]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: System settings can prevent applications from running that haven't been downloaded through the Apple Store (or other legitimate repositories) which can help mitigate some of these issues. Also enable application control solutions such as AppLocker and/or Device Guard to block the loading of malicious content.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). techniques.fullNamePt: Subversão de Controlos de Confiança: Gatekeeper Bypass
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar file attributes and subvert Gatekeeper functionality to evade user prompts and execute untrusted programs. Gatekeeper is a set of technologies that act as layer of Apple’s security model to ensure only trusted applications are executed on a host. Gatekeeper was built on top of File Quarantine in Snow Leopard (10.6, 2009) and has grown to include Code Signing, security policy compliance, Notarization, and more. Gatekeeper also treats applications running for the first time differently than reopened applications. `[Ref: TheEclecticLightCompany Quarantine and the flag]` `[Ref: TheEclecticLightCompany apple notarization ]`

Based on an opt-in system, when files are downloaded an extended attribute (xattr) called `com.apple.quarantine` (also known as a quarantine flag) can be set on the file by the application performing the download. Launch Services opens the application in a suspended state. For first run applications with the quarantine flag set, Gatekeeper executes the following functions:

1. Checks extended attribute – Gatekeeper checks for the quarantine flag, then provides an alert prompt to the user to allow or deny execution. `[Ref: OceanLotus for OS X]` `[Ref: 20 macOS Common Tools and Techniques]`

2. Checks System Policies - Gatekeeper checks the system security policy, allowing execution of apps downloaded from either just the App Store or the App Store and identified developers.

3. Code Signing – Gatekeeper checks for a valid code signature from an Apple Developer ID.

4. Notarization - Using the `api.apple-cloudkit.com` API, Gatekeeper reaches out to Apple servers to verify or pull down the notarization ticket and ensure the ticket is not revoked. Users can override notarization, which will result in a prompt of executing an “unauthorized app” and the security policy will be modified.

Adversaries can subvert one or multiple controlos de segurança within Gatekeeper checks through logic errors (e.g. **Exploitation for Stealth** (`T1211`)), unchecked file types, and external libraries. Por exemplo, prior to macOS 13 Ventura, code signing and notarization checks were only conducted on first launch, allowing adversaries to write malicious executables to previously opened applications com o objetivo de bypass Gatekeeper security checks. `[Ref: theevilbit gatekeeper bypass 2021]` `[Ref: Application Bundle Manipulation Brandon Dalton]`

Applications and files loaded onto the system from a USB flash drive, optical disk, external hard drive, from a drive shared over the local network, or using the curl command may not set the quarantine flag. Additionally, it is possible to avoid setting the quarantine flag using **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Subversão de Controlos de Confiança: Code Signing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem create, acquire, or steal code signing materials to sign their malware or tools. Code signing provides a level of authenticity on a binary from the developer and a guarantee that the binary has not been tampered with.  `[Ref: Wikipedia Code Signing]` The certificates used during an operation may be created, acquired, or stolen by the adversary.  `[Ref: Securelist Digital Certificates]`  `[Ref: Symantec Digital Certificates]` Unlike **Invalid Code Signature** (`T1036.001`), this activity will result in a valid signature.

Code signing to verify software on first run can be used on modern Windows and macOS systems. It is not used on Linux due to the decentralized nature of the platform.  `[Ref: Wikipedia Code Signing]` `[Ref: EclecticLightChecksonEXECodeSigning]`

Code signing certificates pode ser empregue para bypass security policies that require signed code to execute on a system.

techniques.fullNameEn: Subvert Trust Controls: SIP and Trust Provider Hijacking
techniques.fullNamePt: Subversão de Controlos de Confiança: SIP and Trust Provider Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tamper with SIP and trust provider components to mislead the sistema operativo and application control tools when conducting signature validation checks. In user mode, Windows Authenticode  `[Ref: Microsoft Authenticode]` assinaturas digitais são utilizados para verify a file's origin and integrity, variables that pode ser empregue para establish trust in signed code (ex: a driver with a valid Microsoft signature may be handled as safe). The signature validation process is handled via the WinVerifyTrust application programming interface (API) function,   `[Ref: Microsoft WinVerifyTrust]` which accepts an inquiry and coordinates with the appropriate trust provider, which is responsible for validating parameters of a signature.  `[Ref: SpectorOps Subverting Trust Sept 2017]`

Because of the varying executable file types and corresponding signature formats, Microsoft created software components called Subject Interface Packages (SIPs)  `[Ref: EduardosBlog SIPs July 2008]` to provide a layer of abstraction between API functions and files. SIPs are responsible for enabling API functions to create, retrieve, calculate, and verify signatures. Unique SIPs exist for most file formats (Executable, PowerShell, Installer, etc., with catalog signing providing a catch-all   `[Ref: Microsoft Catalog Files and Signatures April 2017]`) and are identified by globally unique identifiers (GUIDs).  `[Ref: SpectorOps Subverting Trust Sept 2017]`

De forma semelhante a **Code Signing** (`T1553.002`), adversaries may abuse this architecture to subvert trust controls and bypass security policies that allow only legitimately signed code to execute on a system. Os adversários podem sequestrar (hijack) SIP and trust provider components to mislead sistema operativo and application control tools to classify malicious (or any) code as signed by:  `[Ref: SpectorOps Subverting Trust Sept 2017]`

* Modifying the `Dll` and `FuncName` Registry values in `HKLM\SOFTWARE[\WOW6432Node\]Microsoft\Cryptography\OID\EncodingType 0\CryptSIPDllGetSignedDataMsg\{SIP_GUID}` that point to the dynamic link library (DLL) providing a SIP’s CryptSIPDllGetSignedDataMsg function, which retrieves an encoded digital certificate from a signed file. By pointing to a maliciously-crafted DLL with an exported function that always returns a known good signature value (ex: a Microsoft signature for Portable Executables) rather than the file’s real signature, an adversary can apply an acceptable signature value to all files using that SIP  `[Ref: GitHub SIP POC Sept 2017]` (although a hash mismatch will likely occur, invalidating the signature, since the hash returned by the function will not match the value computed from the file).
* Modifying the `Dll` and `FuncName` Registry values in `HKLM\SOFTWARE\[WOW6432Node\]Microsoft\Cryptography\OID\EncodingType 0\CryptSIPDllVerifyIndirectData\{SIP_GUID}` that point to the DLL providing a SIP’s CryptSIPDllVerifyIndirectData function, which validates a file’s computed hash against the signed hash value. By pointing to a maliciously-crafted DLL with an exported function that always returns TRUE (indicating that the validation was successful), an adversary can successfully validate any file (with a legitimate signature) using that SIP  `[Ref: GitHub SIP POC Sept 2017]` (with or without hijacking the previously mentioned CryptSIPDllGetSignedDataMsg function). This Registry value could also be redirected to a suitable exported function from an already present DLL, avoiding the requirement to drop and execute a new file on disk.
* Modifying the `DLL` and `Function` Registry values in `HKLM\SOFTWARE\[WOW6432Node\]Microsoft\Cryptography\Providers\Trust\FinalPolicy\{trust provider GUID}` that point to the DLL providing a trust provider’s FinalPolicy function, which is where the decoded and parsed signature is checked and the majority of trust decisions are made. De forma semelhante a hijacking SIP’s CryptSIPDllVerifyIndirectData function, this value can be redirected to a suitable exported function from an already present DLL or a maliciously-crafted DLL (though the implementation of a trust provider is complex).
* **Note:** The above hijacks are also possible without modifying the Registry via **DLL** (`T1574.001`) search order hijacking.

Hijacking SIP or trust provider components can also enable persistent code execution, since these malicious components may be invoked by any application that performs code signing or signature validation.  `[Ref: SpectorOps Subverting Trust Sept 2017]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Microsoft Catalog Files and Signatures April 2017]

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable application control solutions such as AppLocker and/or Device Guard to block the loading of malicious SIP DLLs.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper permissions are set for Registry hives to prevent users from modifying keys related to SIP and trust provider components. Components may still be able to be hijacked to suitable functions already present on disk if malicious modifications to Registry keys are not prevented.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict storage and execution of SIP DLLs to protected directories, such as C:\\Windows, rather than user directories.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Subvert Trust Controls: Install Root Certificate
techniques.fullNamePt: Subversão de Controlos de Confiança: Install Root Certificate
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem install a root certificate num sistema comprometido to avoid warnings when connecting to adversary controlled web servers. Root certificates are used in public key cryptography to identify a root certificate authority (CA). When a root certificate is installed, the system or application will trust certificates in the root's chain of trust that have been signed by the root certificate. `[Ref: Wikipedia Root Certificate]` Certificates are commonly used for establishing secure TLS/SSL communications within a web browser. When a user attempts to browse a website that presents a certificate that is not trusted an error message will be displayed to warn the user of the security risk. Dependendo de the security settings, the browser may not allow the user to establish a connection to the website.

Installation of a root certificate num sistema comprometido would give an adversary a way to degrade the security of that system. Adversaries have used this technique to avoid security warnings prompting users when compromised systems connect over HTTPS to adversary controlled web servers that spoof legitimate websites com o objetivo de collect login credentials. `[Ref: Operation Emmental]`

Atypical root certificates have also been pre-installed on systems by the manufacturer or in the software Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) and were used in conjunction with malware/adware to provide **Adversary-in-the-Middle** (`T1557`) capability for intercepting information transmitted over secure TLS/SSL communications. `[Ref: Kaspersky Superfish]`

Root certificates (and their associated chains) can also be cloned and reinstalled. Cloned certificate chains will carry many of the same metadata characteristics of the source and pode ser utilizado para sign código malicioso that may then bypass signature validation tools (ex: Sysinternals, antivírus (AV), etc.) used to block execution and/or uncover artifacts of Persistence. `[Ref: SpectorOps Code Signing Dec 2017]`

In macOS, the Ay MaMi malware uses `/usr/bin/security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain /path/to/malicious/cert` to install a malicious certificate as a trusted root certificate into the system keychain. `[Ref: objective-see ay mami 2018]`

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: HTTP Public Key Pinning (HPKP) is one method to mitigate potential **Adversary-in-the-Middle** (`T1557`) situations where and adversary uses a mis-issued or fraudulent certificate to intercept encrypted communications by enforcing use of an expected certificate.  `[Ref: Wikipedia HPKP]`

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Windows Group Policy pode ser utilizado para manage root certificates and the `Flags` value of `HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\SystemCertificates\\Root\\ProtectedRoots` can be set to 1 to prevent non-administrator users from making further root installations into their own HKCU certificate store.  `[Ref: SpectorOps Code Signing Dec 2017]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Subversão de Controlos de Confiança: Mark-of-the-Web Bypass
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de specific file formats to subvert Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) controls. In Windows, when files are downloaded from the Internet, they are tagged with a hidden NTFS Alternate Data Stream (ADS) named `Zone.Identifier` with a specific value known as the MOTW. `[Ref: Microsoft Zone.Identifier 2020]` Files that are tagged with MOTW are protected and cannot perform certain actions. Por exemplo, starting in MS Office 10, if a MS Office file has the MOTW, it will open in Protected View. Executables tagged with the MOTW will be processed by Windows Defender SmartScreen that compares files with an allowlist of well-known executables. If the file is not known/trusted, SmartScreen will prevent the execution and warn the user not to run it. `[Ref: Beek Use of VHD Dec 2020]` `[Ref: Outflank MotW 2020]` `[Ref: Intezer Russian APT Dec 2020]`

Os adversários podem abusar de container files such as compressed/archive (.arj, .gzip) and/or disk image (.iso, .vhd) file formats to deliver malicious payloads that may not be tagged with MOTW. Container files downloaded from the Internet will be marked with MOTW but the files within may not inherit the MOTW after the container files are extracted and/or mounted. MOTW is a NTFS feature and many container files do not support NTFS alternative data streams. After a container file is extracted and/or mounted, the files contained within them may be treated as local files on disk and run without protections. `[Ref: Beek Use of VHD Dec 2020]` `[Ref: Outflank MotW 2020]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling auto-mounting of disk image files (i.e., .iso, .img, .vhd, and .vhdx). This can be achieved by modifying the Registry values related to the Windows Explorer file associations com o objetivo de disable the automatic Explorer "Mount and Burn" dialog for these file extensions. Note: this will not deactivate the mount functionality itself. `[Ref: GitHub MOTW]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider blocking container file types at web and/or email gateways. Consider unregistering container file extensions in Windows File Explorer. `[Ref: Dormann Dangers of VHD 2019]`

Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

blockers: M1042 (Disable or Remove Feature or Program): `powershell.exe` bloqueado por GPO, ou Macros VBA desativadas por política de Mark-of-the-Web (MotW).

bypasses: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

Aplicar Indirect Syscalls com Call Stack Spoofing, evitar permissões de memória `RWX` simultâneas (usar padrão `RW` -> `RX` com Sleep Encryption como Ekko/Cronos durante períodos de inatividade do beacon) e realizar patching de `EtwEventWrite` no processo local.

techniques.fullNameEn: Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing Policy Modification
techniques.fullNamePt: Subversão de Controlos de Confiança: Code Signing Policy Modification
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar code signing policies to enable execution of unsigned or self-signed code. Code signing provides a level of authenticity on a program from a developer and a guarantee that the program has not been tampered with. Security controls can include enforcement mechanisms to ensure that only valid, signed code can be run on an sistema operativo. 

Some of these controlos de segurança may be enabled by default, such as Driver Signature Enforcement (DSE) on Windows or System Integrity Protection (SIP) on macOS. `[Ref: Microsoft DSE June 2017]` `[Ref: Apple Disable SIP]` Other such controls may be disabled by default but are configurable through application controls, such as only allowing signed Dynamic-Link Libraries (DLLs) to execute on a system. Since it can be useful for developers to modify default signature enforcement policies during the development and testing of applications, disabling of these features may be possible with elevated permissions. `[Ref: Microsoft Unsigned Driver Apr 2017]` `[Ref: Apple Disable SIP]`

Os adversários podem modificar code signing policies in a number of ways, including through use of command-line or GUI utilities, **Modify Registry** (`T1112`), rebooting the computer in a debug/recovery mode, or by altering the value of variables in kernel memory. `[Ref: Microsoft TESTSIGNING Feb 2021]` `[Ref: Apple Disable SIP]` `[Ref: FireEye HIKIT Rootkit Part 2]` `[Ref: GitHub Turla Driver Loader]` Examples of commands that can modify the code signing policy of a system include `bcdedit.exe -set TESTSIGNING ON` on Windows and `csrutil disable` on macOS. `[Ref: Microsoft TESTSIGNING Feb 2021]` `[Ref: Apple Disable SIP]` Dependendo de the implementation, successful modification of a signing policy may require reboot of the compromised system. Additionally, some implementations can introduce visible artifacts for the user (ex: a watermark in the corner of the screen stating the system is in Test Mode). Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar remove such artifacts. `[Ref: F-Secure BlackEnergy 2014]`

To gain access to kernel memory to modify variables related to signature checks, such as modifying `g_CiOptions` to disable Driver Signature Enforcement, adversaries may conduct **Exploitation for Privilege Escalation** (`T1068`) using a signed, but vulnerable driver. `[Ref: Unit42 AcidBox June 2020]` `[Ref: GitHub Turla Driver Loader]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Compromise Host Software Binary
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar host software binaries to establish persistent access to systems. Software binaries/executables provide a wide range of system commands or services, programs, and libraries. Common software binaries are SSH clients, FTP clients, email clients, web browsers, and many other user or server applications.

Os adversários podem estabelecer persistence though modifications to host software binaries. Por exemplo, an adversary may replace or otherwise infect a legitimate application binary (or support files) with a backdoor. Since these binaries may be routinely executed by applications or the user, the adversary can leverage this for persistent access to the host. Um adversário pode also modify a software binary such as an SSH client com o objetivo de persistently collect credentials during logins (i.e., **Modify Authentication Process** (`T1556`)). `[Ref: Google Cloud Mandiant UNC3886 2024]`

Um adversário pode also modify an existing binary by patching in malicious functionality (e.g., IAT Hooking/Entry point patching) `[Ref: Unit42 Banking Trojans Hooking 2022]` prior to the binary’s legitimate execution. Por exemplo, an adversary may modify the entry point of a binary to point to código malicioso patched in by the adversary before resuming normal execution flow. `[Ref: ESET FontOnLake Analysis 2021]`

After modifying a binary, an adversary may attempt to impair defenses by preventing it from updating (e.g., via the `yum-versionlock` command or `versionlock.list` file in Linux systems that use the yum package manager). `[Ref: Google Cloud Mandiant UNC3886 2024]`

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure all application component binaries are signed by the correct application developers.
mitigations.bypassHint: Recorrer a DLL Side-Loading (`T1574.002`) utilizando um executável legítimo assinado (vulnerável a sequestro de ordem de procura de DLL) que carregue a nossa DLL em memória, ou utilizar binários assinados nativos (LOLBAS - `T1218`). Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais a partir de Password Stores
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem pesquisar for common password storage locations to obtain user credentials. `[Ref: F-Secure The Dukes]` Passwords are stored in several places on a system, depending on the sistema operativo or application holding the credentials. There are also specific applications and services that store passwords to make them easier for users to manage and maintain, such as password managers and cloud secrets vaults. Uma vez que credentials are obtained, they pode ser utilizado para perform lateral movement and access restricted information.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the number of accounts and services with permission to query information from password stores to only those required. Garantir que accounts and services with permissions to query password stores only have access to the secrets they require.

Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Perform regular software updates to mitigate exploitation risk.

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt:
The password for the user's login keychain can be changed from the user's login password. This increases the complexity for an adversary because they need to know an additional password.

Organizations may consider weighing the risk of storing credentials in password stores and web browsers. If system, software, or web browser credential disclosure is a significant concern, technical controls, policy, and user training pode ser empregue para prevent storage of credentials in improper locations.

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais a partir de Password Stores: Keychain
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem adquirir credentials from Keychain. Keychain (or Keychain Services) is the macOS credential management system that stores account names, passwords, private keys, certificates, sensitive application data, payment data, and secure notes. There are three types of Keychains: Login Keychain, System Keychain, and Local Items (iCloud) Keychain. The default Keychain is the Login Keychain, which stores user passwords and information. The System Keychain stores items accessed by the sistema operativo, such as items shared among users on a host. The Local Items (iCloud) Keychain is used for items synced with Apple’s iCloud service. 

Keychains can be viewed and edited through the Keychain Access application or using the command-line utility `security`. Keychain files are located in `~/Library/Keychains/`, `/Library/Keychains/`, and `/Network/Library/Keychains/`. `[Ref: Keychain Services Apple]` `[Ref: Keychain Decryption Passware]` `[Ref: OSX Keychain Schaumann]`

Os adversários podem recolher user credentials from Keychain storage/memory. Por exemplo, the command `security dump-keychain –d` will dump all Login Keychain credentials from `~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db`. Os adversários podem também directly read Login Keychain credentials from the `~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain` file. Both methods require a password, where the default password for the Login Keychain is the current user’s password to login to the macOS host. `[Ref: External to DA, the OS X Way]` `[Ref: Empire Keychain Decrypt]`

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: The password for the user's login keychain can be changed from the user's login password. This increases the complexity for an adversary because they need to know an additional password.

techniques.fullNameEn: Credentials from Password Stores: Securityd Memory
techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais a partir de Password Stores: Securityd Memory
techniques.descriptionPt:
An adversary with root access may gather credentials by reading `securityd`’s memory. `securityd` is a service/daemon responsible for implementing security protocols such as encryption and authorization. `[Ref: Apple Dev SecurityD]` A privileged adversary may be able to scan through `securityd`'s memory to find the correct sequence of keys to decrypt the user’s logon keychain. This may provide the adversary with various passwords em plaintext, such as those for users, WiFi, mail, browsers, certificates, secure notes, etc. `[Ref: OS X Keychain]` `[Ref: OSX Keydnap malware]`

In OS X prior to El Capitan, users with root access can read plaintext keychain passwords of logged-in users because Apple’s keychain implementation allows these credentials to be cached so that users are not repeatedly prompted for passwords. `[Ref: OS X Keychain]` `[Ref: External to DA, the OS X Way]` Apple’s `securityd` utility takes the user’s logon password, encrypts it with PBKDF2, and stores this master key in memory. Apple also uses a set of keys and algorithms to encrypt the user’s password, but once the master key is found, an adversary need only iterate over the other values to unlock the final password. `[Ref: OS X Keychain]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais a partir de Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem adquirir credentials from web browsers by reading files specific to the target browser. `[Ref: Talos Olympic Destroyer 2018]` Web browsers commonly save credentials such as website usernames and passwords so that they do not need to be entered manually in the future. Web browsers typically store the credentials in an encrypted format within a credential store; however, methods exist to extract plaintext credentials from web browsers.

Por exemplo, on Windows systems, encrypted credentials may be obtained from Google Chrome by reading a database file, `AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data` and executing a SQL query: `SELECT action_url, username_value, password_value FROM logins;`. The plaintext password can then be obtained by passing the encrypted credentials to the Windows API function `CryptUnprotectData`, which uses the victim’s cached logon credentials as the decryption key. `[Ref: Microsoft CryptUnprotectData April 2018]`
 
Adversaries have executed similar procedures for common web browsers such as FireFox, Safari, Edge, etc. `[Ref: Proofpoint Vega Credential Stealer May 2018]` `[Ref: FireEye HawkEye Malware July 2017]` Windows stores Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge credentials in Credential Lockers managed by the **Windows Credential Manager** (`T1555.004`).

Os adversários podem também acquire credentials by searching web browser memória do processo for patterns that commonly match credentials. `[Ref: GitHub Mimikittenz July 2016]`

After acquiring credentials from web browsers, adversaries may attempt to recycle the credentials across different systems and/or accounts com o objetivo de expand access. This can result in significantly furthering an adversary's objective in cases where credentials gained from web browsers overlap with privileged accounts (e.g. domain administrator).
codeArtifacts: SELECT action_url, username_value, password_value FROM logins;

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Regularly update web browsers, password managers, and all related software to the latest versions. Keeping software up-to-date reduces the risk of vulnerabilities being exploited by attackers to extract stored credentials or session cookies.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar strict user account management policies to prevent unnecessary accounts from accessing sensitive systems. Regularly audit user accounts to identify and disable inactive accounts that may be targeted by attackers to extract credentials or gain unauthorized access.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Provide user training on secure practices for managing credentials, including avoiding storing sensitive passwords in browsers and using password managers securely. Users should also be educated on identifying phishing attempts that could steal session cookies or credentials.

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict or block web-based content that could be used to extract session cookies or credentials stored in browsers. Use browser security settings, such as disabling third-party cookies and restricting browser extensions, to limit the attack surface.

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Organizations may consider weighing the risk of storing credentials in web browsers. If web browser credential disclosure is a significant concern, technical controls, policy, and user training pode ser empregue para prevent storage of credentials in web browsers.

techniques.fullNameEn: Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager
techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais a partir de Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem adquirir credentials from the Windows Credential Manager. The Credential Manager stores credentials for signing into websites, applications, and/or devices that request authentication through NTLM or Kerberos in Credential Lockers (previously known as Windows Vaults). `[Ref: Microsoft Credential Manager store]` `[Ref: Microsoft Credential Locker]`

The Windows Credential Manager separates website credentials from application or network credentials in two lockers. As part of **Credentials from Web Browsers** (`T1555.003`), Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge website credentials are managed by the Credential Manager and are stored in the Web Credentials locker. Application and network credentials are stored in the Windows Credentials locker.

Credential Lockers store credentials in encrypted `.vcrd` files, located under `%Systemdrive%\Users\\[Username]\AppData\Local\Microsoft\\[Vault/Credentials]\`. The encryption key can be found in a file named `Policy.vpol`, typically located in the same folder as the credentials. `[Ref: passcape Windows Vault]` `[Ref: Malwarebytes The Windows Vault]`

Os adversários podem list credentials managed by the Windows Credential Manager through several mechanisms. `vaultcmd.exe` is a native Windows executable that pode ser utilizado para enumerate credentials stored in the Credential Locker through a interface de linha de comandos (CLI). Os adversários podem também gather credentials by directly reading files located inside of the Credential Lockers. Windows APIs, such as `CredEnumerateA`, may also be absued to list credentials managed by the Credential Manager. `[Ref: Microsoft CredEnumerate]` `[Ref: Delpy Mimikatz Crendential Manager]`

Os adversários podem também obtain credentials from credential backups. Credential backups and restorations may be performed by running `rundll32.exe keymgr.dll KRShowKeyMgr` then selecting the “Back up...” button on the “Stored User Names and Passwords” GUI.

Password recovery tools may also obtain plain text passwords from the Credential Manager. `[Ref: Malwarebytes The Windows Vault]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider enabling the “Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication” setting that will prevent network credentials from being stored by the Credential Manager. `[Ref: Microsoft Network access Credential Manager]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais a partir de Password Stores: Password Managers
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem adquirir user credentials from third-party password managers. `[Ref: ise Password Manager February 2019]` Password managers are applications designed to store user credentials, normally in an encrypted database. Credentials are typically accessible after a user provides a master password that unlocks the database. After the database is unlocked, these credentials may be copied to memory. These databases can be stored as files on disk. `[Ref: ise Password Manager February 2019]`

Os adversários podem adquirir user credentials from password managers by extracting the master password and/or plain-text credentials from memory. `[Ref: FoxIT Wocao December 2019]` `[Ref: Github KeeThief]` Os adversários podem extract credentials from memory via **Exploitation for Credential Access** (`T1212`). `[Ref: NVD CVE-2019-3610]`
 Os adversários podem também try brute forcing via **Password Guessing** (`T1110.001`) to obtain the master password of a password manager. `[Ref: Cyberreason Anchor December 2019]`

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Regularly update web browsers, password managers, and all related software to the latest versions. Keeping software up-to-date reduces the risk of vulnerabilities being exploited by attackers to extract stored credentials or session cookies.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar strict user account management policies to prevent unnecessary accounts from accessing sensitive systems. Regularly audit user accounts to identify and disable inactive accounts that may be targeted by attackers to extract credentials or gain unauthorized access.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Provide user training on secure practices for managing credentials, including avoiding storing sensitive passwords in browsers and using password managers securely. Users should also be educated on identifying phishing attempts that could steal session cookies or credentials.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider re-locking password managers after a short timeout to limit the time plaintext credentials live in memory from decrypted databases.

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Refer to NIST guidelines when creating password policies for master passwords. `[Ref: NIST 800-63-3]`
