techniques.fullNameEn: Credentials from Password Stores: Cloud Secrets Management Stores
techniques.fullNamePt: Credenciais a partir de Password Stores: Cloud Secrets Management Stores
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem adquirir credentials from cloud-native secret management solutions such as AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, and Terraform Vault.  

Secrets managers support the secure centralized management of passwords, API keys, and other material de credenciais. Where secrets managers are in use, cloud services can dynamically acquire credentials via API requests rather than accessing secrets insecurely stored in plain text files or variáveis de ambiente.  

If an adversary is able to gain sufficient privileges in a cloud environment – for example, by obtaining the credentials of high-privileged **Cloud Accounts** (`T1078.004`) or compromising a service that has permission to retrieve secrets – they may be able to request secrets from the secrets manager. This can be accomplished via commands such as `get-secret-value` in AWS, `gcloud secrets describe` in GCP, and `az key vault secret show` in Azure. `[Ref: Permiso Scattered Spider 2023]` `[Ref: Sysdig ScarletEel 2.0 2023]` `[Ref: AWS Secrets Manager]` `[Ref: Google Cloud Secrets]` `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Key Vault]`

**Note:** this technique is distinct from **Cloud Instance Metadata API** (`T1552.005`) in that the credentials are being directly requested from the cloud secrets manager, rather than through the medium of the instance metadata API.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the number of cloud accounts and services with permission to query the secrets manager to only those required. Garantir que accounts and services with permissions to query the secrets manager only have access to the secrets they require.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar authentication mechanisms and processes to access user credentials or enable otherwise unwarranted access to accounts. The processo de autenticação is handled by mechanisms, such as the Local Security Authentication Server (LSASS) process and the Security Accounts Manager (SAM) on Windows, pluggable authentication modules (PAM) on Unix-based systems, and authorization plugins on MacOS systems, responsible for gathering, storing, and validating credentials. By modifying an processo de autenticação, an adversary may be able to authenticate to a service or system without using **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`).

Os adversários podem maliciously modify a part of this process to either reveal credentials or bypass authentication mechanisms. Compromised credentials or access pode ser empregue para bypass access controls placed on various resources on systems within the network and may even be used for persistent access to sistemas remotos and externally available services, such as VPNs, Outlook Web Access and remote desktop.

mitigations.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict Registry permissions to disallow the modification of sensitive Registry keys such as `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider\Order`.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Integrating multi-factor authentication (MFA) as part of organizational policy can greatly reduce the risk of an adversary gaining control of valid credentials that may be used for additional tactics such as initial access, lateral movement, and collecting information. MFA pode também ser utilizado para restrict access to cloud resources and APIs.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que `AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption` property is set to disabled unless there are application requirements. `[Ref: store_pwd_rev_enc]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict write access to the `/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins` directory.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que proper policies are implemented to dictate the the secure enrollment and deactivation of authentication mechanisms, such as MFA, for user accounts.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Auditar regularmente domain and local accounts as well as their permission levels routinely to look for situations that could allow an adversary to gain wide access by obtaining credentials of a privileged account.  `[Ref: TechNet Credential Theft]`  `[Ref: TechNet Least Privilege]` These audits should also include if default accounts have been enabled, or if new local accounts are created that have not be authorized. Follow best practices for design and administration of an enterprise network to limit privileged account use across administrative tiers.  `[Ref: Microsoft Securing Privileged Access]`

Limit access to the root account and prevent users from modifying protected components through proper privilege separation (ex SELinux, grsecurity, AppArmor, etc.) and limiting Privilege Escalation opportunities.

Limit on-premises accounts with access to the hybrid identity solution in place. Por exemplo, limit Azure AD Global Administrator accounts to only those required, and ensure that these are dedicated cloud-only accounts rather than hybrid ones. `[Ref: MagicWeb]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Process Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enabled features, such as Protected Process Light (PPL), for LSA. `[Ref: Microsoft LSA]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Review authentication logs to ensure that mechanisms such as enforcement of MFA are functioning as intended.

Periodically review the hybrid identity solution in use for any discrepancies. Por exemplo, review all Pass Through Authentication (PTA) agents in the Azure Management Portal to identify any unwanted or unapproved ones. `[Ref: Mandiant Azure AD Backdoors]` If ADFS is in use, review DLLs and executable files in the AD FS and Global Assembly Cache directories to ensure that they are signed by Microsoft. Note that in some cases binaries may be catalog-signed, which may cause the file to appear unsigned when viewing file properties. `[Ref: MagicWeb]`

Periodically review for new and unknown network provider DLLs within the Registry (`HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<NetworkProviderName>\NetworkProvider\ProviderPath`). Ensure only valid network provider DLLs are registered. The name of these can be found in the Registry key at `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider\Order`, and have corresponding service subkey pointing to a DLL at `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentC ontrolSet\Services\<NetworkProviderName>\NetworkProvider`.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Authentication Process: Domain Controller Authentication
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação: Domain Controller Authentication
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem patch the processo de autenticação on a Domain Controller (DC) para contornar (bypass) the typical authentication mechanisms and enable access to accounts. 

Malware pode ser empregue para inject false credentials into the processo de autenticação on a Domain Controller (DC) with the intent of creating a backdoor used to access any user’s account and/or credentials (ex: **Skeleton Key** (`S0007`)). Skeleton key works through a patch on an enterprise Domain Controller (DC) processo de autenticação (LSASS) with credentials that adversaries may use para contornar (bypass) the standard authentication system. Uma vez que patched, an adversary can use the injected password to successfully authenticate as any domain user account (until the the skeleton key is erased from memory by a reboot of the Domain Controller (DC)). Authenticated access may enable unfettered access to hosts and/or resources within single-factor authentication environments. `[Ref: Dell Skeleton]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Auditar regularmente domain and local accounts as well as their permission levels routinely to look for situations that could allow an adversary to gain wide access by obtaining credentials of a privileged account.  `[Ref: TechNet Credential Theft]`  `[Ref: TechNet Least Privilege]` These audits should also include if default accounts have been enabled, or if new local accounts are created that have not be authorized. Follow best practices for design and administration of an enterprise network to limit privileged account use across administrative tiers.  `[Ref: Microsoft Securing Privileged Access]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.descriptionPt: Enabled features, such as Protected Process Light (PPL), for LSA. `[Ref: Microsoft LSA]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: Integrating multi-factor authentication (MFA) as part of organizational policy can greatly reduce the risk of an adversary gaining control of valid credentials that may be used for additional tactics such as initial access, lateral movement, and collecting information. MFA pode também ser utilizado para restrict access to cloud resources and APIs.

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Authentication Process: Password Filter DLL
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação: Password Filter DLL
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem register malicious password filter dynamic link libraries (DLLs) into the processo de autenticação to acquire user credentials as they are validated. 

Windows password filters are password policy enforcement mechanisms for both domain and local accounts. Filters are implemented as DLLs containing a method to validate potential passwords against password policies. Filter DLLs can be positioned on local computers for local accounts and/or Domain Controller (DC)s for domain accounts. Before registering new passwords in the Security Accounts Manager (SAM), the Local Security Authority (LSA) requests validation from each registered filter. Any potential changes cannot take effect until every registered filter acknowledges validation. 

Adversaries can register malicious password filters to harvest credentials from local computers and/or entire domains. To perform proper validation, filters must receive plain-text credentials from the LSA. A malicious password filter would receive these plain-text credentials every time a password request is made. `[Ref: Carnal Ownage Password Filters Sept 2013]`

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure only valid password filters are registered. Filter DLLs must be present in Windows installation directory (C:\Windows\System32\ by default) of a Domain Controller (DC) and/or local computer with a corresponding entry in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Notification Packages.

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Authentication Process: Pluggable Authentication Modules
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação: Pluggable Authentication Modules
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar pluggable authentication modules (PAM) to access user credentials or enable otherwise unwarranted access to accounts. PAM is a modular system of ficheiros de configuração, libraries, and executable files which guide authentication for many services. The most common authentication module is `pam_unix.so`, which retrieves, sets, and verifies account authentication information in `/etc/passwd` and `/etc/shadow`. `[Ref: Apple PAM]` `[Ref: Man Pam_Unix]` `[Ref: Red Hat PAM]`

Os adversários podem modificar components of the PAM system to create backdoors. PAM components, such as `pam_unix.so`, can be patched to accept arbitrary adversary supplied values as credenciais legítimas. `[Ref: PAM Backdoor]`

Malicious modifications to the PAM system may also be abused to steal credentials. Os adversários podem infect PAM resources with code to harvest user credentials, since the values exchanged with PAM components may be plain-text since PAM does not store passwords. `[Ref: PAM Creds]` `[Ref: Apple PAM]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Authentication Process: Network Device Authentication
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação: Network Device Authentication
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar **Patch System Image** (`T1601.001`) to hard code a password in the sistema operativo, thus bypassing of native authentication mechanisms for local accounts on network devices.

**Modify System Image** (`T1601`) may include implanted code to the sistema operativo for network devices to provide access for adversaries using a specific password.  The modification includes a specific password which is implanted in the sistema operativo image via the patch.  Upon authentication attempts, the inserted code will first check to see if the user input is the password. If so, access is granted. Otherwise, the implanted code will pass the credentials on for verification of potentially valid credentials. `[Ref: Mandiant - Synful Knock]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação: Reversible Encryption
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode abuse Active Directory (AD) authentication encryption properties para obter acesso a credentials on Windows systems. The `AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption` property specifies whether reversible password encryption for an account is enabled or disabled. By default this property is disabled (instead storing user credentials as the output of one-way hashing functions) and should not be enabled unless legacy or other software require it. `[Ref: store_pwd_rev_enc]`

If the property is enabled and/or a user changes their password after it is enabled, an adversary may be able to obtain the plaintext of passwords created/changed after the property was enabled. To decrypt the passwords, an adversary needs four components:

1. Encrypted password (`G$RADIUSCHAP`) from the Active Directory (AD) user-structure `userParameters`
2. 16 byte randomly-generated value (`G$RADIUSCHAPKEY`) also from `userParameters`
3. Global LSA secret (`G$MSRADIUSCHAPKEY`)
4. Static key hardcoded in the Remote Access Subauthentication DLL (`RASSFM.DLL`)

With this information, an adversary may be able to reproduce the encryption key and subsequently decrypt the encrypted password value. `[Ref: how_pwd_rev_enc_1]` `[Ref: how_pwd_rev_enc_2]`

Um adversário pode set this property at various scopes through Local Group Policy Editor, user properties, Fine-Grained Password Policy (FGPP), or via the ActiveDirectory **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) module. Por exemplo, an adversary may implement and apply a FGPP to users or groups if the Domain Functional Level is set to "Windows Server 2008" or higher. `[Ref: dump_pwd_dcsync]` In PowerShell, an adversary may make associated changes to user settings using commands similar to `Set-ADUser -AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption $true`.

Follow best practices for design and administration of an enterprise network to limit privileged account use across administrative tiers. `[Ref: Microsoft Securing Privileged Access]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação: Multi-Factor Authentication
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem desativar or modify multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanisms to enable persistent access to compromised accounts.

Uma vez que adversaries have gained access to a network by either compromising an account lacking MFA or by employing an MFA bypass method such as **Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation** (`T1621`), adversaries may leverage their access to modify or completely disable MFA defenses. This can be accomplished by abusing legitimate features, such as excluding users from Azure AD Conditional Access Policies, registering a new yet vulnerable/adversary-controlled MFA method, or by manually patching MFA programs and ficheiros de configuração para contornar (bypass) expected functionality. `[Ref: Mandiant APT42]` `[Ref: Azure AD Conditional Access Exclusions]`

Por exemplo, modifying the Windows hosts file (`C:\windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts`) to redirect MFA calls to localhost instead of an MFA server may cause the MFA process to fail. If a "fail open" policy is in place, any otherwise successful authentication attempt may be granted access without enforcing MFA.  `[Ref: Russians Exploit Default MFA Protocol - CISA March 2022]` 

Dependendo de the scope, goals, and privileges of the adversary, MFA defenses may be disabled for individual accounts or for all accounts tied to a larger group, such as all domain accounts in a victim's network environment. `[Ref: Russians Exploit Default MFA Protocol - CISA March 2022]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação: Hybrid Identity
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem patch, modify, or otherwise backdoor cloud processo de autenticaçãoes that are tied to on-premises user identities com o objetivo de bypass typical authentication mechanisms, access credentials, and enable persistent access to accounts.  

Many organizations maintain hybrid user and device identities that are shared between on-premises and cloud-based environments. These can be maintained in a number of ways. Por exemplo, Microsoft Entra ID includes three options for synchronizing identities between Active Directory (AD) and Entra ID `[Ref: Azure AD Hybrid Identity]`:

* Password Hash Synchronization (PHS), in which a privileged on-premises account synchronizes user password hashes between Active Directory (AD) and Entra ID, allowing authentication to Entra ID to take place entirely in the cloud 
* Pass Through Authentication (PTA), in which Entra ID authentication attempts are forwarded to an on-premises PTA agent, which validates the credentials against Active Directory (AD) 
* Active Directory (AD) Federation Services (AD FS), in which a trust relationship is established between Active Directory (AD) and Entra ID 

AD FS can also be used with other SaaS and cloud platforms such as AWS and GCP, which will hand off the processo de autenticação to AD FS and receive a token containing the hybrid users’ identity and privileges. 

By modifying processo de autenticaçãoes tied to hybrid identities, an adversary may be able to establish persistent privileged access to cloud resources. Por exemplo, adversaries who compromise an on-premises server running a PTA agent may inject a malicious DLL into the `AzureADConnectAuthenticationAgentService` process that authorizes all attempts to authenticate to Entra ID, as well as records user credentials. `[Ref: Azure AD Connect for Read Teamers]` `[Ref: AADInternals Azure AD On-Prem to Cloud]` In environments using AD FS, an adversary may edit the `Microsoft.IdentityServer.Servicehost` configuration file to load a malicious DLL that generates authentication tokens for any user with any set of claims, thereby bypassing multi-factor authentication and defined AD FS policies. `[Ref: MagicWeb]`

In some cases, adversaries may be able to modify the hybrid identity processo de autenticação from the cloud. Por exemplo, adversaries who compromise a Global Administrator account in an Entra ID tenant may be able to register a new PTA agent via the web console, similarly allowing them to harvest credentials and log into the Entra ID environment as any user. `[Ref: Mandiant Azure AD Backdoors]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: Integrating multi-factor authentication (MFA) as part of organizational policy can greatly reduce the risk of an adversary gaining control of valid credentials that may be used for additional tactics such as initial access, lateral movement, and collecting information. MFA pode também ser utilizado para restrict access to cloud resources and APIs.

Evitar abrir handles diretos com `PROCESS_VM_READ`. Preferir extração indireta via SSPI/Kerberos (`Rubeus tgtdeleg` / `kerberoast`), decifragem offline de blobs DPAPI usando a Backup Key do domínio, extração de SAM/SECURITY via registo/VSS ou abuso de certificados AD CS (`T1649`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Authentication Process: Network Provider DLL
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação: Network Provider DLL
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem register malicious network provider dynamic link libraries (DLLs) to capture cleartext user credentials during the processo de autenticação. Network provider DLLs allow Windows to interface with specific network protocols and can also support add-on credential management functions. `[Ref: Network Provider API]` During the logon process, Winlogon (the interactive logon module) sends credentials to the local `mpnotify.exe` process via RPC. The `mpnotify.exe` process then shares the credentials in cleartext with registered credential managers when notifying that a logon event is happening. `[Ref: NPPSPY - Huntress]` `[Ref: NPPSPY Video]` `[Ref: NPLogonNotify]` 

Adversaries can configure a malicious network provider DLL to receive credentials from `mpnotify.exe`. `[Ref: NPPSPY]` Uma vez que installed as a credential manager (via the Registry), a malicious DLL can receive and save credentials each time a user logs onto a Windows workstation or domain via the `NPLogonNotify()` function. `[Ref: NPLogonNotify]`

Os adversários podem target planting malicious network provider DLLs on systems known to have increased logon activity and/or administrator logon activity, such as servers and Domain Controller (DC)s. `[Ref: NPPSPY - Huntress]`

mitigations.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict Registry permissions to disallow the modification of sensitive Registry keys such as `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider\Order`.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Periodically review for new and unknown network provider DLLs within the Registry (`HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<NetworkProviderName>\NetworkProvider\ProviderPath`).

Ensure only valid network provider DLLs are registered. The name of these can be found in the Registry key at `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider\Order`, and have corresponding service subkey pointing to a DLL at `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentC ontrolSet\Services\<NetworkProviderName>\NetworkProvider`.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Authentication Process: Conditional Access Policies
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação do Processo de Autenticação: Conditional Access Policies
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem desativar or modify conditional access policies to enable persistent access to compromised accounts. Conditional access policies are additional verifications used by identity providers and identity and access management systems to determine whether a user should be granted access to a resource.

Por exemplo, in Entra ID, Okta, and JumpCloud, users can be denied access to applications based on their IP address, device enrollment status, and use of multi-factor authentication. `[Ref: Microsoft Conditional Access]` `[Ref: JumpCloud Conditional Access Policies]` `[Ref: Okta Conditional Access Policies]` In some cases, identity providers may also support the use of risk-based metrics to deny sign-ins based on a variety of indicators. In AWS and GCP, IAM policies can contain `condition` attributes that verify arbitrary constraints such as the source IP, the date the request was made, and the nature of the resources or regions being requested. `[Ref: AWS IAM Conditions]` `[Ref: GCP IAM Conditions]` These measures help to prevent compromised credentials from resulting in unauthorized access to data or resources, as well as limit user permissions to only those required. 

By modifying conditional access policies, such as adding additional trusted IP ranges, removing **Multi-Factor Authentication** (`T1556.006`) requirements, or allowing additional **Unused/Unsupported Cloud Regions** (`T1535`), adversaries may be able to ensure persistent access to accounts and circumvent defensive measures.

techniques.fullNamePt: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar position themselves between two or more networked devices using an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) technique to support follow-on behaviors such as **Network Sniffing** (`T1040`), **Transmitted Data Manipulation** (`T1565.002`), or replay attacks (**Exploitation for Credential Access** (`T1212`)). By abusing features of common networking protocols that can determine the flow of tráfego de rede (e.g. ARP, DNS, LLMNR, etc.), adversaries may force a device to communicate through an adversary controlled system so they can collect information or perform additional actions. `[Ref: Rapid7 MiTM Basics]`

Por exemplo, adversaries may manipulate victim DNS settings to enable other malicious activities such as preventing/redirecting users from accessing legitimate sites and/or pushing additional malware. `[Ref: ttint_rat]` `[Ref: dns_changer_trojans]` `[Ref: ad_blocker_with_miner]` Os adversários podem também manipulate DNS and leverage their position com o objetivo de intercept user credentials, including access tokens (**Steal Application Access Token** (`T1528`)) and session cookies (**Steal Web Session Cookie** (`T1539`)). `[Ref: volexity_0day_sophos_FW]` `[Ref: Token tactics]` **Downgrade Attack** (`T1689`)s pode também ser utilizado para establish an AiTM position, such as by negotiating a less secure, deprecated, or weaker version of communication protocol (SSL/TLS) or encryption algorithm. `[Ref: mitm_tls_downgrade_att]` `[Ref: taxonomy_downgrade_att_tls]` `[Ref: tlseminar_downgrade_att]`

Os adversários podem também leverage the AiTM position to attempt to monitor and/or modify traffic, such as in **Transmitted Data Manipulation** (`T1565.002`). Adversaries can setup a position similar to AiTM to prevent traffic from flowing to the appropriate destination, potentially to impair defenses and/or in support of a **Network Denial of Service** (`T1498`).

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use network appliances and host-based security software to block tráfego de rede that is not necessary within the environment, such as legacy protocols that may be leveraged for AiTM conditions.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que all wired and/or wireless traffic is encrypted appropriately. Use best practices for authentication protocols, such as Kerberos, and ensure web traffic that may contain credentials is protected by SSL/TLS.

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit access to network infrastructure and resources that pode ser utilizado para reshape traffic or otherwise produce AiTM conditions.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable legacy network protocols that may be used   to intercept tráfego de rede if applicable, especially those that are not needed dentro do ambiente alvo.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Train users to be suspicious about certificate errors. Os adversários podem utilizar their own certificates in an attempt to intercept HTTPS traffic. Certificate errors may arise when the application’s certificate does not match the one expected by the host.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that can identify traffic patterns indicative of AiTM activity pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network segmentation pode ser utilizado para isolate infrastructure components that do not require broad network access. This may mitigate, or at least alleviate, the scope of AiTM activity.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM): Name Resolution Poisoning and SMB Relay
techniques.descriptionPt:
By responding to LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS tráfego de rede, adversaries may spoof an authoritative source for name resolution to force communication with an adversary controlled system. `[Ref: BlackCat ransomware]` This activity pode ser empregue para collect or relay authentication materials. 

Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution (LLMNR) and NetBIOS Name Service (NBT-NS) are Microsoft Windows components that serve as alternate methods of host identification. LLMNR is based upon the Domain Name System (DNS) format and allows hosts on the same local link to perform name resolution for other hosts. NBT-NS identifies systems on a local network by their NetBIOS name. `[Ref: Wikipedia LLMNR]` `[Ref: TechNet NetBIOS]`

Multicast Domain Name System(mDNS) is a zero-configuration service used to resolve hostnames to IP addresses with “.local” as a top-level domain. MDNS is based upon Domain Name System (DNS) format and allows hosts on the same network segment to perform name resolution for other hosts, using multicast. `[Ref: mDNS RFC]`

Adversaries can spoof an authoritative source for name resolution on a victim network by responding to LLMNR (UDP 5355)/NBT-NS (UDP 137)/mDNS (UDP 5353) traffic as if they know the identity of the requested host, effectively poisoning the service so that the victims will communicate with the adversary controlled system. If the requested host belongs to a resource that requires identification/authentication, the username and NTLMv2 hash will then be sent to the adversary controlled system. The adversary can then collect the hash information sent over the wire through tools that monitor the ports for traffic or through **Network Sniffing** (`T1040`) and crack the hashes offline through **Brute Force** (`T1110`) to obtain the passwords em plaintext.

In some cases where an adversary has access to a system that is in the authentication path between systems or when automated scans that use credentials attempt to authenticate to an adversary controlled system, the NTLMv1/v2 hashes can be intercepted and relayed to access and execute code against a target system. The relay step can happen in conjunction with poisoning but may also be independent of it. `[Ref: byt3bl33d3r NTLM Relaying]` `[Ref: Secure Ideas SMB Relay]` Additionally, adversaries may encapsulate the NTLMv1/v2 hashes into various other protocols, such as LDAP, MSSQL and HTTP, to expand and use multiple services with the valid NTLM response. 

Several tools pode ser empregue para poison name services within local networks such as NBNSpoof, Metasploit, and **Responder** (`S0174`). `[Ref: GitHub NBNSpoof]` `[Ref: Rapid7 LLMNR Spoofer]` `[Ref: GitHub Responder]`

Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). techniques.fullNamePt: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM): ARP Cache Poisoning
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem poison Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) caches to position themselves between the communication of two or more networked devices. This activity pode ser empregue para enable follow-on behaviors such as **Network Sniffing** (`T1040`) or **Transmitted Data Manipulation** (`T1565.002`).

The ARP protocol é utilizado para resolve IPv4 addresses to link layer addresses, such as a media access control (MAC) address. `[Ref: RFC826 ARP]` Devices in a local network segment communicate with each other by using link layer addresses. If a networked device does not have the link layer address of a particular networked device, it may send out a broadcast ARP request to the local network to translate the IP address to a MAC address. The device with the associated IP address directly replies with its MAC address. The networked device that made the ARP request will then use as well as store that information in its ARP cache.

Um adversário pode passively wait for an ARP request to poison the ARP cache of the requesting device. The adversary may reply with their MAC address, thus deceiving the victim by making them believe that they are communicating with the intended networked device. For the adversary to poison the ARP cache, their reply must be faster than the one made by the legitimate IP address owner. Os adversários podem também send a gratuitous ARP reply that maliciously announces the ownership of a particular IP address to all the devices in the local network segment.

The ARP protocol is stateless and does not require authentication. Consequentemente, devices may wrongly add or update the MAC address of the IP address in their ARP cache. `[Ref: Sans ARP Spoofing Aug 2003]` `[Ref: Cylance Cleaver]`

Os adversários podem utilizar ARP cache poisoning as a means to intercept tráfego de rede. This activity pode ser empregue para collect and/or relay data such as credentials, especially those sent over an insecure, unencrypted protocol. `[Ref: Sans ARP Spoofing Aug 2003]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM): DHCP Spoofing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem redirect tráfego de rede to adversary-owned systems by spoofing Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) traffic and acting as a malicious DHCP server on the victim network. By achieving the adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) position, adversaries may collect network communications, including passed credentials, especially those sent over insecure, unencrypted protocols. This may also enable follow-on behaviors such as **Network Sniffing** (`T1040`) or **Transmitted Data Manipulation** (`T1565.002`).

DHCP is based on a client-server model and has two functionalities: a protocol for providing network configuration settings from a DHCP server to a client and a mechanism for allocating network addresses to clients. `[Ref: rfc2131]` The typical server-client interaction is as follows: 

1. The client broadcasts a `DISCOVER` message.

2. The server responds with an `OFFER` message, which includes an available network address. 

3. The client broadcasts a `REQUEST` message, which includes the network address offered. 

4. The server acknowledges with an `ACK` message and the client receives the network configuration parameters.

Os adversários podem falsificar (spoof) as a rogue DHCP server on the victim network, from which legitimate hosts may receive malicious network configurations. Por exemplo, malware can act as a DHCP server and provide adversary-owned DNS servers to the victimized computers. `[Ref: new_rogue_DHCP_serv_malware]` `[Ref: w32.tidserv.g]` Through the malicious network configurations, an adversary may achieve the AiTM position, route client traffic through adversary-controlled systems, and collect information from the client network.

DHCPv6 clients can receive network configuration information without being assigned an IP address by sending a `INFORMATION-REQUEST (code 11)` message to the `All_DHCP_Relay_Agents_and_Servers` multicast address. `[Ref: rfc3315]` Os adversários podem utilizar their rogue DHCP server to respond to this request message with malicious network configurations.

Rather than establishing an AiTM position, adversaries may also abuse DHCP spoofing to perform a DHCP exhaustion attack (i.e, **Service Exhaustion Flood** (`T1499.002`)) by generating many broadcast DISCOVER messages to exhaust a network’s DHCP allocation pool.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Consider filtering DHCP traffic on ports 67 and 68 to/from unknown or untrusted DHCP servers. Additionally, port security may also be enabled on layer switches. Ademais, consider enabling DHCP snooping on layer 2 switches as it will prevent DHCP spoofing attacks and starvation attacks. Consider tracking available IP addresses through a script or a tool. 

Additionally, block DHCPv6 traffic and incoming router advertisements, especially if IPv6 is not commonly used in the network. `[Ref: ntlm_relaying_kerberos_del]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM): Evil Twin
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem host seemingly genuine Wi-Fi access points to deceive users into connecting to malicious networks as a way of supporting follow-on behaviors such as **Network Sniffing** (`T1040`), **Transmitted Data Manipulation** (`T1565.002`), or **Input Capture** (`T1056`). `[Ref: Australia ‘Evil Twin’]`

By using a Service Set Identifier (SSID) of a legitimate Wi-Fi network, fraudulent Wi-Fi access points may trick devices or users into connecting to malicious Wi-Fi networks. `[Ref: Kaspersky evil twin]` `[Ref: medium evil twin]`  Os adversários podem provide a stronger signal strength or block access to Wi-Fi access points to coerce or entice victim devices into connecting to malicious networks. `[Ref: specter ops evil twin]`  A Wi-Fi Pineapple – a network security auditing and penetration testing tool – may be deployed in Evil Twin attacks for ease of use and broader range. Custom certificates may be used in an attempt to intercept HTTPS traffic. 

Similarly, adversaries may also listen for client devices sending probe requests for known or previously connected networks (Preferred Network Lists or PNLs). When a malicious access point receives a probe request, adversaries can respond with the same SSID to imitate the trusted, known network. `[Ref: specter ops evil twin]`  Victim devices are led to believe the responding access point is from their PNL and initiate a connection to the fraudulent network.

Upon logging into the malicious Wi-Fi access point, a user may be directed to a fake login page or captive portal webpage to capture the victim’s credentials. Uma vez que a user is logged into the fraudulent Wi-Fi network, the adversary may able to monitor network activity, manipulate data, or steal additional credentials. Locations with high concentrations of public Wi-Fi access, such as airports, coffee shops, or libraries, may be targets for adversaries to set up illegitimate Wi-Fi access points.

techniques.namePt: Roubo ou Falsificação de Tickets Kerberos
techniques.fullNamePt: Roubo ou Falsificação de Tickets Kerberos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar subvert Kerberos authentication by stealing or forging Kerberos tickets to enable **Pass the Ticket** (`T1550.003`). Kerberos is an authentication protocol widely used in modern Windows domain environments. In Kerberos environments, referred to as “realms”, there are three basic participants: client, service, and Key Distribution Center (KDC). `[Ref: ADSecurity Kerberos Ring Decoder]` Clients request access to a service and through the exchange of Kerberos tickets, originating from KDC, they are granted access after having successfully authenticated. The KDC is responsible for both authentication and ticket granting.  Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar abuse Kerberos by stealing tickets or forging tickets to enable unauthorized access.

Em ambientes Windows, the built-in `klist` utility pode ser utilizado para list and analyze cached Kerberos tickets. `[Ref: Microsoft Klist]`

mitigations.name: Active Directory Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: For containing the impact of a previously generated golden ticket, reset the built-in KRBTGT account password twice, which will invalidate any existing golden tickets that have been created with the KRBTGT hash and other Kerberos tickets derived from it. For each domain, change the KRBTGT account password once, force replication, and then change the password a second time. Consider rotating the KRBTGT account password every 180 days. `[Ref: STIG krbtgt reset]`

mitigations.name: Credential Access Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Linux systems, protect resources with Security Enhanced Linux (SELinux) by defining entry points, process types, and file labels. `[Ref: Brining MimiKatz to Unix]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Com RunAsPPL ativo, processos em User-Mode não conseguem abrir handles `PROCESS_VM_READ` no LSASS. Vetores de contorno: (1) Pivotar para extração sem tocar no LSASS: Kerberoasting (`T1558.003`), AS-REP Roasting (`T1558.004`), ou extração de segredos DPAPI/Vault (`T1555.004`); (2) Se for Domain Admin/equivalente, usar DCSync (`T1003.006`) remotamente; (3) Abusar de drivers assinados vulneráveis (BYOVD - `T1068`) como `mimidrv.sys` ou `procexp152.sys` para remover a flag `PS_PROTECTION` em Kernel-Mode; (4) Se Credential Guard (VBS) estiver ativo, hashes NTLM em cache ficam isolados em `LsaIso.exe` — contornar usando captura de Tickets Kerberos em memória via Rubeus (`monitor`/`tgtdeleg`) ou roubo de cookies de sessão browser.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable AES Kerberos encryption (or another stronger encryption algorithm), rather than RC4, where possible. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]`

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure strong password length (ideally 25+ characters) and complexity for service accounts and that these passwords periodically expire. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]` Also consider using Group Managed Service Accounts or another third party product such as password vaulting. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Perform audits or scans of systems, permissions, insecure software, insecure configurations, etc. to identify potential weaknesses.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Limit domain admin account permissions to Domain Controller (DC)s and limited servers. Delegate other admin functions to separate accounts.

Limit service accounts to minimal required privileges, including membership in privileged groups such as Domain Administrators. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket
techniques.fullNamePt: Roubo ou Falsificação de Tickets Kerberos: Golden Ticket
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries who have the KRBTGT account password hash may forge Kerberos ticket-granting tickets (TGT), also known as a golden ticket. `[Ref: AdSecurity Kerberos GT Aug 2015]` Golden tickets enable adversaries to generate authentication material for any account in Active Directory (AD). `[Ref: CERT-EU Golden Ticket Protection]` 

Using a golden ticket, adversaries are then able to request ticket granting service (TGS) tickets, which enable access to specific resources. Golden tickets require adversaries to interact with the Key Distribution Center (KDC) com o objetivo de obtain TGS. `[Ref: ADSecurity Detecting Forged Tickets]`

The KDC service runs all on Domain Controller (DC)s that are part of an Active Directory (AD) domain. KRBTGT is the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) service account and is responsible for encrypting and signing all Kerberos tickets. `[Ref: ADSecurity Kerberos and KRBTGT]` The KRBTGT password hash may be obtained using **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`) and privileged access to a Domain Controller (DC).

techniques.fullNameEn: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Silver Ticket
techniques.fullNamePt: Roubo ou Falsificação de Tickets Kerberos: Silver Ticket
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries who have the password hash of a target service account (e.g. SharePoint, MSSQL) may forge Kerberos ticket granting service (TGS) tickets, also known as silver tickets. Kerberos TGS tickets are also known as service tickets. `[Ref: ADSecurity Silver Tickets]`

Silver tickets are more limited in scope in than golden tickets in that they only enable adversaries to access a particular resource (e.g. MSSQL) and the system that hosts the resource; however, unlike golden tickets, adversaries with the ability to forge silver tickets are able to create TGS tickets without interacting with the Key Distribution Center (KDC), potentially making detection more difficult. `[Ref: ADSecurity Detecting Forged Tickets]`

Password hashes for target services may be obtained using **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`) or **Kerberoasting** (`T1558.003`).

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure strong password length (ideally 25+ characters) and complexity for service accounts and that these passwords periodically expire. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]` Also consider using Group Managed Service Accounts or another third party product such as password vaulting. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit service accounts to minimal required privileges, including membership in privileged groups such as Domain Administrators. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable AES Kerberos encryption (or another stronger encryption algorithm), rather than RC4, where possible. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
techniques.fullNamePt: Roubo ou Falsificação de Tickets Kerberos: Kerberoasting
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de a valid Kerberos ticket-granting ticket (TGT) or sniff tráfego de rede to obtain a ticket-granting service (TGS) ticket that may be vulnerable to **Brute Force** (`T1110`). `[Ref: Empire InvokeKerberoast Oct 2016]` `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]` 

Service principal names (SPNs) são utilizados para uniquely identify each instance of a Windows service. To enable authentication, Kerberos requires that SPNs be associated with at least one service logon account (an account specifically tasked with running a service `[Ref: Microsoft Detecting Kerberoasting Feb 2018]`). `[Ref: Microsoft SPN]` `[Ref: Microsoft SetSPN]` `[Ref: SANS Attacking Kerberos Nov 2014]` `[Ref: Harmj0y Kerberoast Nov 2016]`

Adversaries possessing a valid Kerberos ticket-granting ticket (TGT) may request one or more Kerberos ticket-granting service (TGS) service tickets for any SPN from a Domain Controller (DC) (DC). `[Ref: Empire InvokeKerberoast Oct 2016]` `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]` Portions of these tickets may be encrypted with the RC4 algorithm, meaning the Kerberos 5 TGS-REP etype 23 hash of the service account associated with the SPN is used as the private key and is thus vulnerable to offline **Brute Force** (`T1110`) attacks that may expose plaintext credentials. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]` `[Ref: Empire InvokeKerberoast Oct 2016]`  `[Ref: Harmj0y Kerberoast Nov 2016]`

This same behavior could be executed using service tickets captured from tráfego de rede. `[Ref: AdSecurity Cracking Kerberos Dec 2015]`

Cracked hashes may enable **Persistence** (`TA0003`), **Privilege Escalation** (`TA0004`), and **Lateral Movement** (`TA0008`) via access to **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`). `[Ref: SANS Attacking Kerberos Nov 2014]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: AS-REP Roasting
techniques.fullNamePt: Roubo ou Falsificação de Tickets Kerberos: AS-REP Roasting
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem reveal credentials of accounts that have disabled Kerberos preauthentication by **Password Cracking** (`T1110.002`) Kerberos messages. `[Ref: Harmj0y Roasting AS-REPs Jan 2017]` 

Preauthentication offers protection against offline **Password Cracking** (`T1110.002`). When enabled, a user requesting access to a resource initiates communication with the Domain Controller (DC) (DC) by sending an Authentication Server Request (AS-REQ) message with a timestamp that is encrypted with the hash of their password. If and only if the DC is able to successfully decrypt the timestamp with the hash of the user’s password, it will then send an Authentication Server Response (AS-REP) message that contains the Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT) to the user. Part of the AS-REP message is signed with the user’s password. `[Ref: Microsoft Kerberos Preauth 2014]`

For each account found without preauthentication, an adversary may send an AS-REQ message without the encrypted timestamp and receive an AS-REP message with TGT data which may be encrypted with an insecure algorithm such as RC4. The recovered encrypted data may be vulnerable to offline **Password Cracking** (`T1110.002`) attacks similarly to **Kerberoasting** (`T1558.003`) and expose plaintext credentials.  `[Ref: Harmj0y Roasting AS-REPs Jan 2017]` `[Ref: Stealthbits Cracking AS-REP Roasting Jun 2019]` 

An account registered to a domain, with or without special privileges, pode ser abusado para list all domain accounts that have preauthentication disabled by utilizing Windows tools like **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) with an LDAP filter. Alternatively, the adversary may send an AS-REQ message for each user. If the DC responds without errors, the account does not require preauthentication and the AS-REP message will already contain the encrypted data.  `[Ref: Harmj0y Roasting AS-REPs Jan 2017]` `[Ref: Stealthbits Cracking AS-REP Roasting Jun 2019]`

Cracked hashes may enable **Persistence** (`TA0003`), **Privilege Escalation** (`TA0004`), and **Lateral Movement** (`TA0008`) via access to **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`). `[Ref: SANS Attacking Kerberos Nov 2014]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Kerberos preauthentication is enabled by default. Older protocols might not support preauthentication therefore it is possible to have this setting disabled. Make sure that all accounts have preauthentication whenever possible and audit changes to setting. Windows tools such as PowerShell pode ser empregue para easily find which accounts have preauthentication disabled.   `[Ref: Microsoft Preauthentication Jul 2012]` `[Ref: Stealthbits Cracking AS-REP Roasting Jun 2019]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Ccache Files
techniques.fullNamePt: Roubo ou Falsificação de Tickets Kerberos: Ccache Files
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar steal Kerberos tickets stored in credential cache files (or ccache). These files are used for short term storage of a user's active session credentials. The ccache file is created upon user authentication and allows for access to multiple services without the user having to re-enter credentials. 

The `/etc/krb5.conf` configuration file and the `KRB5CCNAME` environment variable são utilizados para set the storage location for ccache entries. Em sistemas Linux, credentials are typically stored in the `/tmp` directory with a naming format of `krb5cc_%UID%` or `krb5.ccache`. Em sistemas macOS, ccache entries are stored by default in memory with an `API:{uuid}` naming scheme. Typically, users interact with ticket storage using `kinit`, which obtains a Ticket-Granting-Ticket (TGT) for the principal; `klist`, which lists obtained tickets currently held in the credentials cache; and other built-in binaries. `[Ref: Kerberos GNU/Linux]` `[Ref: Binary Defense Kerberos Linux]`

Adversaries can collect tickets from ccache files stored on disk and authenticate as the current user without their password to perform **Pass the Ticket** (`T1550.003`) attacks. Adversaries can also use these tickets to impersonate legitimate users with privilégios elevados to perform **Privilege Escalation** (`TA0004`). Tools like Kekeo can also be used by adversaries to convert ccache files to Windows format for further **Lateral Movement** (`TA0008`). Em sistemas macOS, adversaries may use open-source tools or the Kerberos framework to interact with ccache files and extract TGTs or Service Tickets via lower-level APIs. `[Ref: SpectorOps Bifrost Kerberos macOS 2019]` `[Ref: Linux Kerberos Tickets]` `[Ref: Brining MimiKatz to Unix]` `[Ref: Kekeo]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable and perform audits or scans of systems, permissions, insecure software, insecure configurations, etc. to identify potential weaknesses. `[Ref: Brining MimiKatz to Unix]` Por exemplo, use `auditd` to audit access to hashes, machine tickets, or `/tmp` files. If using sssd and Vintela, ensure kerberos is disabled if not being used. `[Ref: audits linikatz]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Credential Access Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Protect resources with Security Enhanced Linux (SELinux) by defining entry points, process types, and file labels. `[Ref: Brining MimiKatz to Unix]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Com RunAsPPL ativo, processos em User-Mode não conseguem abrir handles `PROCESS_VM_READ` no LSASS. Vetores de contorno: (1) Pivotar para extração sem tocar no LSASS: Kerberoasting (`T1558.003`), AS-REP Roasting (`T1558.004`), ou extração de segredos DPAPI/Vault (`T1555.004`); (2) Se for Domain Admin/equivalente, usar DCSync (`T1003.006`) remotamente; (3) Abusar de drivers assinados vulneráveis (BYOVD - `T1068`) como `mimidrv.sys` ou `procexp152.sys` para remover a flag `PS_PROTECTION` em Kernel-Mode; (4) Se Credential Guard (VBS) estiver ativo, hashes NTLM em cache ficam isolados em `LsaIso.exe` — contornar usando captura de Tickets Kerberos em memória via Rubeus (`monitor`/`tgtdeleg`) ou roubo de cookies de sessão browser.

detections.name: Detect Kerberos Ccache File Theft or Abuse (T1558.005)

blockers: M1047 (Audit): Operações de enumeração ou persistência geram alertas imediatos no SOC devido a regras Sigma sobre argumentos de linha de comando.
M1043 (Credential Access Protection): Erro `0x00000005 (ACCESS_DENIED)` ao tentar fazer dump de `lsass.exe` mesmo com privilégio `SeDebugPrivilege` e `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`.
bypasses: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

Com RunAsPPL ativo, processos em User-Mode não conseguem abrir handles `PROCESS_VM_READ` no LSASS. Vetores de contorno: (1) Pivotar para extração sem tocar no LSASS: Kerberoasting (`T1558.003`), AS-REP Roasting (`T1558.004`), ou extração de segredos DPAPI/Vault (`T1555.004`); (2) Se for Domain Admin/equivalente, usar DCSync (`T1003.006`) remotamente; (3) Abusar de drivers assinados vulneráveis (BYOVD - `T1068`) como `mimidrv.sys` ou `procexp152.sys` para remover a flag `PS_PROTECTION` em Kernel-Mode; (4) Se Credential Guard (VBS) estiver ativo, hashes NTLM em cache ficam isolados em `LsaIso.exe` — contornar usando captura de Tickets Kerberos em memória via Rubeus (`monitor`/`tgtdeleg`) ou roubo de cookies de sessão browser.

**AllowedProcesses**: Baseline list of processes legitimately interacting with ccache (e.g., klist, kinit).
**TimeWindow**: Correlation window for linking file access, process execution, and Kerberos requests.
**KerberosAPIProcessBaseline**: Expected processes using the Kerberos framework (e.g., loginwindow, kinit).
**SuspiciousBinaryList**: List of tools or binaries not normally expected to query Kerberos ccache entries.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comunicação Entre Processos (IPC)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms for local code or command execution. IPC is typically used by processes to share data, communicate with each other, or synchronize execution. IPC is also commonly used to avoid situations such as deadlocks, which occurs when processes are stuck in a cyclic waiting pattern. 

Os adversários podem abusar de IPC to execute código arbitrário or commands. IPC mechanisms may differ depending on OS, but typically exists in a form accessible through programming languages/libraries or native interfaces such as Windows **Dynamic Data Exchange** (`T1559.002`) or **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`). Linux environments support several different IPC mechanisms, two of which being sockets and pipes. `[Ref: Linux IPC]` Higher level execution mediums, such as those of **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`)s, may also leverage underlying IPC mechanisms. Os adversários podem também use **Remote Services** (`T1021`) such as **Distributed Component Object Model** (`T1021.003`) to facilitate remote IPC execution. `[Ref: Fireeye Hunting COM June 2019]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Registry keys specific to Microsoft Office feature control security can be set to disable automatic DDE/OLE execution.  `[Ref: Microsoft DDE Advisory Nov 2017]` `[Ref: BleepingComputer DDE Disabled in Word Dec 2017]` `[Ref: GitHub Disable DDEAUTO Oct 2017]` Microsoft also created, and enabled by default, Registry keys to completely disable DDE execution in Word and Excel. `[Ref: Microsoft ADV170021 Dec 2017]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling embedded files in Office programs, such as OneNote, that do not work with Protected View. `[Ref: Enigma Reviving DDE Jan 2018]` `[Ref: GitHub Disable DDEAUTO Oct 2017]`

mitigations.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure all COM alerts and Protected View are enabled. `[Ref: Microsoft Protected View]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Modify Registry settings (directly or using Dcomcnfg.exe) in `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SOFTWARE\\Classes\\AppID\\{AppID_GUID}` associated with the process-wide security of individual COM applications. `[Ref: Microsoft Process Wide Com Keys]`

Modify Registry settings (directly or using Dcomcnfg.exe) in `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Ole` associated with system-wide security defaults for all COM applications that do no set their own process-wide security. `[Ref: Microsoft System Wide Com Keys]`  `[Ref: Microsoft COM ACL]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent DDE attacks and spawning of child processes from Office programs. `[Ref: Microsoft ASR Nov 2017]` `[Ref: Enigma Reviving DDE Jan 2018]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: Application Developer Guidance
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable the Hardened Runtime capability when developing applications. Do not include the `com.apple.security.get-task-allow` entitlement with the value set to any variation of true.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comunicação Entre Processos (IPC): Component Object Model
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar the Windows Component Object Model (COM) for local code execution. COM is an inter-process communication (IPC) component of the native Windows application programming interface (API) that enables interaction between software objects, or executable code that implements one or more interfaces. `[Ref: Fireeye Hunting COM June 2019]` Through COM, a client object can call methods of server objects, which are typically binary Dynamic Link Libraries (DLL) or executables (EXE). `[Ref: Microsoft COM]` Remote COM execution is facilitated by **Remote Services** (`T1021`) such as  **Distributed Component Object Model** (`T1021.003`) (DCOM). `[Ref: Fireeye Hunting COM June 2019]`

Various COM interfaces are exposed that pode ser abusado para invoke arbitrary execution via a variety of programming languages such as C, C++, Java, and **Visual Basic** (`T1059.005`). `[Ref: Microsoft COM]` Specific COM objects also exist to directly perform functions beyond code execution, such as creating a **Scheduled Task/Job** (`T1053`), fileless download/execution, and other adversary behaviors related to privilege escalation and persistence. `[Ref: Fireeye Hunting COM June 2019]` `[Ref: ProjectZero File Write EoP Apr 2018]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Comunicação Entre Processos (IPC): Dynamic Data Exchange
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar Windows Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) to execute comandos arbitrários. DDE is a client-server protocol for one-time and/or continuous inter-process communication (IPC) between applications. Uma vez que a link is established, applications can autonomously exchange transactions consisting of strings, warm data links (notifications when a data item changes), hot data links (duplications of changes to a data item), and requests for command execution.

Object Linking and Embedding (OLE), or the ability to link data between documents, was originally implemented through DDE. Despite being superseded by **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`), DDE may be enabled in Windows 10 and most of Microsoft Office 2016 via Registry keys. `[Ref: BleepingComputer DDE Disabled in Word Dec 2017]` `[Ref: Microsoft ADV170021 Dec 2017]` `[Ref: Microsoft DDE Advisory Nov 2017]`

Microsoft Office documents can be poisoned with DDE commands, directly or through embedded files, and used to deliver execution via **Phishing** (`T1566`) campaigns or hosted Web content, avoiding the use of Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) macros. `[Ref: SensePost PS DDE May 2016]` `[Ref: Kettle CSV DDE Aug 2014]` `[Ref: Enigma Reviving DDE Jan 2018]` `[Ref: SensePost MacroLess DDE Oct 2017]` Similarly, adversaries may infect payloads to execute applications and/or commands on a victim device by way of embedding DDE formulas within a CSV file intended to be opened through a Windows spreadsheet program. `[Ref: OWASP CSV Injection]` `[Ref: CSV Excel Macro Injection ]`

DDE could also be leveraged by an adversary operating on a compromised machine who does not have direct access to a **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`). DDE execution can be invoked remotely via **Remote Services** (`T1021`) such as **Distributed Component Object Model** (`T1021.003`) (DCOM). `[Ref: Fireeye Hunting COM June 2019]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Comunicação Entre Processos (IPC): XPC Services
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries can provide malicious content to an XPC service daemon for local code execution. macOS uses XPC services for basic inter-process communication between various processes, such as between the XPC Service daemon and third-party application privileged helper tools. Applications can send messages to the XPC Service daemon, which runs as root, using the low-level XPC Service `C API` or the high level `NSXPCConnection API` com o objetivo de handle tasks that require privilégios elevados (such as network connections). Applications are responsible for providing the protocol definition which serves as a blueprint of the XPC services. Developers typically use XPC Services to provide applications stability and privilege separation between the application client and the daemon. `[Ref: creatingXPCservices]` `[Ref: Designing Daemons Apple Dev]`

Adversaries can abuse XPC services para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos content. Requests for malicious execution can be passed through the application's XPC Services handler. `[Ref: CVMServer Vuln]` `[Ref: Learn XPC Exploitation]` This may also include identifying and abusing improper XPC client validation and/or poor sanitization of input parameters to conduct **Exploitation for Privilege Escalation** (`T1068`).

mitigations.name: Application Developer Guidance
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable the Hardened Runtime capability when developing applications. Do not include the `com.apple.security.get-task-allow` entitlement with the value set to any variation of true.

techniques.fullNamePt: Arquivamento de Dados Recolhidos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode compress and/or encrypt data that is collected prior to exfiltration. Compressing the data can help to obfuscate the collected data and minimize the amount of data sent over the network. `[Ref: DOJ GRU Indictment Jul 2018]` Encryption pode ser utilizado para hide information that is being exfiltrated from detection or make exfiltration less conspicuous upon inspection by a defender.

Both compression and encryption are done prior to exfiltration, and can be performed using a utility, 3rd party library, or custom method.

techniques.fullNamePt: Arquivamento de Dados Recolhidos: Archive via Utility
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar utilities to compress and/or encrypt collected data prior to exfiltration. Many utilities include functionalities to compress, encrypt, or otherwise package data into a format that is easier/more secure to transport.

Os adversários podem abusar de various utilities to compress or encrypt data before exfiltration. Some third party utilities may be preinstalled, such as `tar` on Linux and macOS or `zip` on Windows systems. 

Em ambientes Windows, `diantz` or ` makecab` pode ser empregue para package collected files into a cabinet (.cab) file. `diantz` may also be used to download and compress files from remote locations (i.e. **Remote Data Staging** (`T1074.002`)). `[Ref: diantz.exe_lolbas]` `xcopy` on Windows can copy files and directories with a variety of options. Additionally, adversaries may use **certutil** (`S0160`) to Base64 encode collected data before exfiltration. 

Os adversários podem utilizar also third party utilities, such as 7-Zip, WinRAR, and WinZip, to perform similar activities. `[Ref: 7zip Homepage]` `[Ref: WinRAR Homepage]` `[Ref: WinZip Homepage]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Library
techniques.fullNamePt: Arquivamento de Dados Recolhidos: Archive via Library
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode compress or encrypt data that is collected prior to exfiltration using 3rd party libraries. Many libraries exist that can archive data, including **Python** (`T1059.006`) rarfile  `[Ref: PyPI RAR]`, libzip  `[Ref: libzip]`, and zlib  `[Ref: Zlib Github]`. Most libraries include functionality to encrypt and/or compress data.

Some archival libraries are preinstalled on systems, such as bzip2 on macOS and Linux, and zip on Windows. Note that the libraries are different from the utilities. The libraries can be linked against when compiling, while the utilities require spawning a subshell, or a similar execution mechanism.

analytics.descriptionPt: Detects adversarial archiving using libraries (zlib, zip APIs) invoked by scripts or binaries. Correlates process executions of Python, PowerShell, or custom .NET binaries with DLL/module loads linked to compression libraries, followed by archive file creation.

techniques.fullNamePt: Disk Wipe
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem wipe or corrupt raw disk data on specific systems or in large numbers in a network to interrupt availability to system and network resources. With direct write access to a disk, adversaries may attempt to overwrite portions of disk data. Os adversários podem opt to wipe arbitrary portions of disk data and/or wipe disk structures like the master boot record (MBR). A complete wipe of all disk sectors may be attempted.

To maximize impact on the organização alvo in operations where network-wide availability interruption is the goal, malware used for wiping disks may have worm-like features to propagate across a network by leveraging additional techniques like **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`), **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`), and **SMB/Windows Admin Shares** (`T1021.002`). `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster Destructive Malware]`

On network devices, adversaries may wipe ficheiros de configuração and other data from the device using **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) commands such as `erase`. `[Ref: erase_cmd_cisco]`

mitigations.name: Data Backup
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for taking regular data backups that pode ser utilizado para restore organizational data. `[Ref: Ready.gov IT DRP]` Ensure backups are stored off system and is protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and destroy the backups to prevent recovery.

techniques.fullNamePt: Disk Wipe: Disk Content Wipe
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem erase the contents of storage devices on specific systems or in large numbers in a network to interrupt availability to system and network resources.

Os adversários podem partially or completely overwrite the contents of a storage device rendering the data irrecoverable through the storage interface. `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster]` `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster Destructive Malware]` `[Ref: DOJ Lazarus Sony 2018]` Instead of wiping specific disk structures or files, adversaries with destructive intent may wipe arbitrary portions of disk content. To wipe disk content, adversaries may acquire direct access to the hard drive com o objetivo de overwrite arbitrarily sized portions of disk with random data. `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster Destructive Malware]` Adversaries have also been observed leveraging third-party drivers like **RawDisk** (`S0364`) to directly access disk content. `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster]` `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster Destructive Malware]` This behavior is distinct from **Data Destruction** (`T1485`) because sections of the disk are erased instead of individual files.

To maximize impact on the organização alvo in operations where network-wide availability interruption is the goal, malware used for wiping disk content may have worm-like features to propagate across a network by leveraging additional techniques like **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`), **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`), and **SMB/Windows Admin Shares** (`T1021.002`). `[Ref: Novetta Blockbuster Destructive Malware]`
