techniques.fullNamePt: Disk Wipe: Disk Structure Wipe
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem corrupt or wipe the disk data structures on a hard drive necessary to boot a system; targeting specific critical systems or in large numbers in a network to interrupt availability to system and network resources. 

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar render the system unable to boot by overwriting critical data located in structures such as the master boot record (MBR) or partition table. `[Ref: Symantec Shamoon 2012]` `[Ref: FireEye Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Kaspersky StoneDrill 2017]` `[Ref: Unit 42 Shamoon3 2018]` The data contained in disk structures may include the initial executable code for loading an sistema operativo or the location of the sistema de ficheiros partitions on disk. If this information is not present, the computer will not be able to load an sistema operativo during the boot process, leaving the computer unavailable. **Disk Structure Wipe** (`T1561.002`) may be performed in isolation, or along with **Disk Content Wipe** (`T1561.001`) if all sectors of a disk are wiped.

On a network devices, adversaries may reformat the sistema de ficheiros using **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) commands such as `format`. `[Ref: format_cmd_cisco]`

To maximize impact on the organização alvo, malware designed for destroying disk structures may have worm-like features to propagate across a network by leveraging other techniques like **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`), **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`), and **SMB/Windows Admin Shares** (`T1021.002`). `[Ref: Symantec Shamoon 2012]` `[Ref: FireEye Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Shamoon Nov 2016]` `[Ref: Kaspersky StoneDrill 2017]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for taking regular data backups that pode ser utilizado para restore organizational data. `[Ref: Ready.gov IT DRP]` Ensure backups are stored off system and is protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and destroy the backups to prevent recovery.

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Sessão Remota
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem take control of preexisting sessions with remote services para realizar movimentação lateral in an environment. Users may use valid credentials to log into a service specifically designed to accept remote connections, such as telnet, SSH, and RDP. When a user logs into a service, a session will be established that will allow them to maintain a continuous interaction with that service.

Os adversários podem commandeer these sessions to carry out actions on sistemas remotos. **Remote Service Session Hijacking** (`T1563`) differs from use of **Remote Services** (`T1021`) because it hijacks an existing session rather than creating a new session using **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`). `[Ref: RDP Hijacking Medium]` `[Ref: Breach Post-mortem SSH Hijack]`

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation

techniques.fullNameEn: Remote Service Session Hijacking: SSH Hijacking
techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Sessão Remota: SSH Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem sequestrar (hijack) a legitimate user's SSH session para realizar movimentação lateral dentro do ambiente alvo. Secure Shell (SSH) is a standard means of remote access on Linux and macOS systems. It allows a user to connect to another system via an encrypted tunnel, commonly authenticating through a password, certificate or the use of an asymmetric encryption key pair.

In order para realizar movimentação lateral from a compromised host, adversaries may take advantage of trust relationships established with other systems via public key authentication in active SSH sessions by hijacking an existing connection to another system. This may occur through compromising the SSH agent itself or by having access to the agent's socket. If an adversary is able to obtain root access, then hijacking SSH sessions is likely trivial. `[Ref: Slideshare Abusing SSH]` `[Ref: SSHjack Blackhat]` `[Ref: Clockwork SSH Agent Hijacking]` `[Ref: Breach Post-mortem SSH Hijack]`

**SSH Hijacking** (`T1563.001`) differs from use of **SSH** (`T1021.004`) because it hijacks an existing SSH session rather than creating a new session using **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`).

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper file permissions are set and harden system to prevent root privilege escalation opportunities.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que agent forwarding is disabled on systems that do not explicitly require this feature to prevent misuse.  `[Ref: Symantec SSH and ssh-agent]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure SSH key pairs have strong passwords and refrain from using key-store technologies such as ssh-agent unless they are properly protected.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not allow remote access via SSH as root or other privileged accounts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Remote Service Session Hijacking: RDP Hijacking
techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Sessão Remota: RDP Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem sequestrar (hijack) a legitimate user’s remote desktop session para realizar movimentação lateral dentro do ambiente alvo. Remote desktop is a common feature in sistema operativos. It allows a user to log into an interactive session with a system desktop interface gráfica (GUI) on a remote system. Microsoft refers to its implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) as Remote Desktop Services (RDS). `[Ref: TechNet Remote Desktop Services]`

Os adversários podem realizar RDP session hijacking which involves stealing a legitimate user's remote session. Typically, a user is notified when someone else is trying to steal their session. With System permissions and using Terminal Services Console, `c:\windows\system32\tscon.exe [session number to be stolen]`, an adversary can hijack a session without the need for credentials or prompts to the user. `[Ref: RDP Hijacking Korznikov]` This can be done remotely or locally and with active or disconnected sessions. `[Ref: RDP Hijacking Medium]` It can also lead to **Remote System Discovery** (`T1018`) and Privilege Escalation by stealing a Domain Admin or higher privileged account session. All of this can be done by using native Windows commands, but it has also been added as a feature in red teaming tools. `[Ref: Kali Redsnarf]`

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use remote desktop gateways.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable firewall rules to block RDP traffic between network security zones within a network.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Change GPOs to define shorter timeouts sessions and maximum amount of time any single session can be active. Change GPOs to specify the maximum amount of time that a disconnected session stays active on the RD session host server. `[Ref: Windows RDP Sessions]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit remote user permissions if remote access is necessary.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Auditar regularmente the Remote Desktop Users group membership regularly. Remove unnecessary accounts and groups from Remote Desktop Users groups.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar hide artifacts associated with their behaviors para evadir deteção. Operating systems may have features to hide various artifacts, such as important system files and administrative task execution, to avoid disrupting user work environments and prevent users from changing files or features on the system. Os adversários podem abusar de these features to hide artifacts such as files, directories, user accounts, or other system activity para evadir deteção. `[Ref: Sofacy Komplex Trojan]` `[Ref: Cybereason OSX Pirrit]` `[Ref: MalwareBytes ADS July 2015]`

Os adversários podem também attempt to hide artifacts associated with malicious behavior by creating computing regions that are isolated from common security instrumentation, such as through the use of virtualization technology. `[Ref: Sophos Ragnar May 2020]`

mitigations.name: Limit Software Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict the installation of software that may be abused to create hidden desktops, such as hVNC, to user groups that require it.

mitigations.name: Application Developer Guidance
mitigations.descriptionPt: Application developers should consider limiting the requirements for custom or otherwise difficult to manage file/folder exclusions. Where possible, install applications to trusted system folder paths that are already protected by restricted file and directory permissions.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Periodically audit máquina virtual (VM)s for abnormalities.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Review and audit file/folder exclusions, and limit scope of exclusions to only what is required where possible. `[Ref: Microsoft File Folder Exclusions]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

techniques.fullNameEn: Hide Artifacts: Hidden Files and Directories
techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Hidden Files and Directories
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem set files and directories to be hidden para evadir deteção mechanisms. To prevent normal users from accidentally changing special files on a system, most sistema operativos have the concept of a ‘hidden’ file. These files don’t show up when a user browses the sistema de ficheiros with a GUI or when using normal commands on the command line. Users must explicitly ask to show the hidden files either via a series of Graphical User Interface (GUI) prompts or with command line switches (`dir /a` for Windows and `ls –a` for Linux and macOS).

On Linux and Mac, users can mark specific files as hidden simply by putting a “.” as the first character in the file or folder name   `[Ref: Sofacy Komplex Trojan]`  `[Ref: Antiquated Mac Malware]`. Files and folders that start with a period, ‘.’, are by default hidden from being viewed in the Finder application and standard command-line utilities like “ls”. Users must specifically change settings to have these files viewable.

Files on macOS can also be marked with the UF_HIDDEN flag which prevents them from being seen in Finder.app, but still allows them to be seen in Terminal.app  `[Ref: WireLurker]`. Em ambientes Windows, users can mark specific files as hidden by using the attrib.exe binary. Many applications create these hidden files and folders to store information so that it doesn’t clutter up the user’s workspace. Por exemplo, SSH utilities create a .ssh folder that’s hidden and contains the user’s known hosts and keys.

Additionally, adversaries may name files in a manner that would allow the file to be hidden such as naming a file only a “space” character.

Adversaries can use this to their advantage to hide files and folders anywhere on the system and evading a typical user or system analysis that does not incorporate investigation of hidden files.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Hidden Users
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar hidden users to hide the presence of user accounts they create or modify. Administrators may want to hide users when there are many user accounts on a given system or if they want to hide their administrative or other management accounts from other users. 

In macOS, adversaries can create or modify a user to be hidden through manipulating plist files, folder attributes, and user attributes. To prevent a user from being shown on the login screen and in System Preferences, adversaries can set the userID to be under 500 and set the key value `Hide500Users` to `TRUE` in the `/Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow` plist file. `[Ref: Cybereason OSX Pirrit]` Every user has a userID associated with it. When the `Hide500Users` key value is set to `TRUE`, users with a userID under 500 do not appear on the login screen and in System Preferences. Using the command line, adversaries can use the `dscl` utility to create hidden user accounts by setting the `IsHidden` attribute to `1`. Adversaries can also hide a user’s home folder by changing the `chflags` to hidden. `[Ref: Apple Support Hide a User Account]` 

Os adversários podem similarly hide user accounts in Windows. Adversaries can set the `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\UserList` Registry key value to `0` for a specific user to prevent that user from being listed on the logon screen. `[Ref: FireEye SMOKEDHAM June 2021]` `[Ref: US-CERT TA18-074A]`

On Linux systems, adversaries may hide user accounts from the login screen, also referred to as the greeter. The method an adversary may use depends on which Display Manager the distribution is currently using. Por exemplo, on an Ubuntu system using the GNOME Display Manger (GDM), accounts may be hidden from the greeter using the `gsettings` command (ex: `sudo -u gdm gsettings set org.gnome.login-screen disable-user-list true`). `[Ref: Hide GDM User Accounts]` Display Managers are not anchored to specific distributions and may be changed by a user or adversary.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Hidden Window
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar hidden windows to conceal malicious activity from the plain sight of users. In some cases, windows that would typically be displayed when an application carries out an operation can be hidden. This may be utilized by system administrators to avoid disrupting user work environments when carrying out administrative tasks. 

Os adversários podem abusar de these functionalities to hide otherwise visible windows from users so as not to alert the user to adversary activity on the system. `[Ref: Antiquated Mac Malware]`

Em sistemas macOS, the configurations for how applications run are listed in property list (plist) files. One of the tags in these files can be `apple.awt.UIElement`, which allows for Java applications to prevent the application's icon from appearing in the Dock. A common use for this is when applications run in the system tray, but don't also want to show up in the Dock.

Similarly, on Windows there are a variety of features in scripting languages, such as **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`), Jscript, and **Visual Basic** (`T1059.005`) to make windows hidden. One example of this is `powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden`. `[Ref: PowerShell About 2019]`

The Windows Registry can also be edited to hide application windows from the current user. Por exemplo, by setting the `WindowPosition` subkey in the `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Console\%SystemRoot%_System32_WindowsPowerShell_v1.0_PowerShell.exe` Registry key to a maximum value, PowerShell windows will open off screen and be hidden. `[Ref: Cantoris Computing]`

Além disso, Windows supports the `CreateDesktop()` API that can create a hidden desktop window with its own corresponding `explorer.exe` process. `[Ref: Hidden VNC]` `[Ref: Anatomy of an hVNC Attack]`  All applications running on the hidden desktop window, such as a hidden VNC (hVNC) session, `[Ref: Hidden VNC]` will be invisible to other desktops windows.

Os adversários podem também leverage cmd.exe `[Ref: Cybereason - Hidden Malicious Remote Access]` as a parent process, and then utilize a LOLBin, such as DeviceCredentialDeployment.exe, `[Ref: LOLBAS Project GitHub Device Cred Dep]` `[Ref: SecureList BlueNoroff Device Cred Dev]` to hide windows.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit or restrict program execution using anti-virus software. On MacOS, allowlist programs that are allowed to have the plist tag. All other programs should be considered suspicious.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Limit Software Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict the installation of software that may be abused to create hidden desktops, such as hVNC, to user groups that require it.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: NTFS File Attributes
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar NTFS file attributes to hide their malicious data com o objetivo de evade detection. Every New Technology File System (NTFS) formatted partition contains a Master File Table (MFT) that maintains a record for every file/directory on the partition.  `[Ref: SpectorOps Host-Based Jul 2017]` Within MFT entries are file attributes,  `[Ref: Microsoft NTFS File Attributes Aug 2010]` such as Extended Attributes (EA) and Data [known as Alternate Data Streams (ADSs) when more than one Data attribute is present], that pode ser utilizado para store arbitrary data (and even complete files).  `[Ref: SpectorOps Host-Based Jul 2017]`  `[Ref: Microsoft File Streams]`  `[Ref: MalwareBytes ADS July 2015]`  `[Ref: Microsoft ADS Mar 2014]`

Os adversários podem store malicious data or binaries in file attribute metadata instead of directly in files. This may be done to evade some defenses, such as static indicator scanning tools and anti-virus.  `[Ref: Journey into IR ZeroAccess NTFS EA]`  `[Ref: MalwareBytes ADS July 2015]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Journey into IR ZeroAccess NTFS EA]

mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Hidden File System
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar a hidden sistema de ficheiros to conceal malicious activity from users and security tools. File systems provide a structure to store and access data from physical storage. Typically, a user engages with a sistema de ficheiros through applications that allow them to access files and directories, which are an abstraction from their physical location (ex: disk sector). Standard sistema de ficheiross include FAT, NTFS, ext4, and APFS. File systems can also contain other structures, such as the Volume Boot Record (VBR) and Master File Table (MFT) in NTFS. `[Ref: MalwareTech VFS Nov 2014]`

Os adversários podem utilizar their own abstracted sistema de ficheiros, separate from the standard sistema de ficheiros present on the infected system. In doing so, adversaries can hide the presence of malicious components and file input/output from security tools. Hidden sistema de ficheiross, sometimes referred to as virtual sistema de ficheiross, can be implemented in numerous ways. One implementation would be to store a sistema de ficheiros in reserved disk space unused by disk structures or standard sistema de ficheiros partitions. `[Ref: MalwareTech VFS Nov 2014]` `[Ref: FireEye Bootkits]` Another implementation could be for an adversary to drop their own portable partition image as a file on top of the standard sistema de ficheiros. `[Ref: ESET ComRAT May 2020]` Os adversários podem também fragment files across the existing sistema de ficheiros structure in non-standard ways. `[Ref: Kaspersky Equation QA]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Run Virtual Instance
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem carry out malicious operations using a virtual instance para evitar deteção. A wide variety of virtualization technologies exist that allow for the emulation of a computer or computing environment. By running código malicioso inside of a virtual instance, adversaries can hide artifacts associated with their behavior from security tools that are unable to monitor activity inside the virtual instance. `[Ref: CyberCX Akira Ransomware]` Additionally, depending on the virtual networking implementation (ex: bridged adapter), tráfego de rede generated by the virtual instance can be difficult to trace back to the compromised host as the IP address and hostname might not match known values. `[Ref: SingHealth Breach Jan 2019]`

Os adversários podem utilize native support for virtualization (ex: Hyper-V), deploy lightweight emulators (ex: QEMU), or drop the necessary files to run a virtual instance (ex: VirtualBox binaries). `[Ref: Securonix CronTrap 2024]` After running a virtual instance, adversaries may create a shared folder between the guest and host with permissions that enable the virtual instance to interact with the host sistema de ficheiros. `[Ref: Sophos Ragnar May 2020]`

Threat actors may also leverage temporary virtualized environments such as the Windows Sandbox, which supports the use of `.wsb` ficheiros de configuração for defining execution parameters. Por exemplo, the `<MappedFolder>` property supports the creation of a shared folder, while the `<LogonCommand>` property allows the specification of a payload. `[Ref: ESET MirrorFace 2025]` `[Ref: ITOCHU Hack the Sandbox]` `[Ref: ITOCHU Sandbox PPT]`

In VMWare environments, adversaries may leverage the vCenter console to create new máquina virtual (VM)s. Contudo, they may also create máquina virtual (VM)s directly on ESXi servers by running a valid `.vmx` file with the `/bin/vmx` utility. Adding this command to `/etc/rc.local.d/local.sh` (i.e., **RC Scripts** (`T1037.004`)) will cause the VM to persistently restart. `[Ref: vNinja Rogue VMs 2024]` Creating a VM this way prevents it from appearing in the vCenter console or in the output to the `vim-cmd vmsvc/getallvms` command on the ESXi server, thereby hiding it from typical administrative activities. `[Ref: MITRE VMware Abuse 2024]`

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable native virtualization technologies such as Hyper-V if not necessary within a given environment. Consider also disabling Windows Sandbox if it is not needed to test or debug applications.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Periodically audit máquina virtual (VM)s for abnormalities. techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: VBA Stomping
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem ocultar malicious Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) payloads embedded within MS Office documents by replacing the VBA source code with benign data. `[Ref: FireEye VBA stomp Feb 2020]`

MS Office documents with embedded VBA content store source code inside of module streams. Each module stream has a `PerformanceCache` that stores a separate compiled version of the VBA source code known as p-code. The p-code is executed when the MS Office version specified in the `_VBA_PROJECT` stream (which contains the version-dependent description of the VBA project) matches the version of the host MS Office application. `[Ref: Evil Clippy May 2019]` `[Ref: Microsoft _VBA_PROJECT Stream]`

Um adversário pode hide malicious VBA code by overwriting the VBA source code location with zero’s, benign code, or random bytes while leaving the previously compiled malicious p-code. Tools that scan for malicious VBA source code may be bypassed as the unwanted code is hidden in the compiled p-code. If the VBA source code is removed, some tools might even think that there are no macros present. If there is a version match between the `_VBA_PROJECT` stream and host MS Office application, the p-code will be executed, otherwise the benign VBA source code will be decompressed and recompiled to p-code, thus removing malicious p-code and potentially bypassing dynamic analysis. `[Ref: Walmart Roberts Oct 2018]` `[Ref: FireEye VBA stomp Feb 2020]` `[Ref: pcodedmp Bontchev]`

Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Email Hiding Rules
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar email rules to hide inbound emails in a compromised user's mailbox. Many email clients allow users to create inbox rules for various email functions, including moving emails to other folders, marking emails as read, or deleting emails. Rules may be created or modified within email clients or through external features such as the `New-InboxRule` or `Set-InboxRule` **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) cmdlets on Windows systems. `[Ref: Microsoft Inbox Rules]` `[Ref: MacOS Email Rules]` `[Ref: Microsoft New-InboxRule]` `[Ref: Microsoft Set-InboxRule]`

Os adversários podem utilize email rules within a compromised user's mailbox to delete and/or move emails to less noticeable folders. Os adversários podem do this to hide security alerts, C2 communication, or responses to **Internal Spearphishing** (`T1534`) emails sent from the compromised account.

Any user or administrator within the organization (or adversary with valid credentials) may be able to create rules to automatically move or delete emails. These rules pode ser abusado para impair/delay detection had the email content been immediately seen by a user or defender. Malicious rules commonly filter out emails based on key words (such as `malware`, `suspicious`, `phish`, and `hack`) found in message bodies and subject lines.  `[Ref: Microsoft Cloud App Security]`

In some environments, administrators may be able to enable email rules that operate organization-wide rather than on individual inboxes. Por exemplo, Microsoft Exchange supports transport rules that evaluate all mail an organization receives against user-specified conditions, then performs a user-specified action on mail that adheres to those conditions. `[Ref: Microsoft Mail Flow Rules 2023]` Adversaries that abuse such features may be able to automatically modify or delete all emails related to specific topics (such as internal security incident notifications).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Enterprise email solutions may have monitoring mechanisms that may include the ability to audit inbox rules on a regular basis. 

In an Exchange environment, Administrators can use `Get-InboxRule` / `Remove-InboxRule` and `Get-TransportRule` / `Remove-TransportRule` to discover and remove potentially malicious inbox and transport rules. `[Ref: Microsoft Get-InboxRule]` `[Ref: Microsoft Manage Mail Flow Rules 2023]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Resource Forking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de resource forks to hide código malicioso or executables para evadir deteção and bypass security applications. A resource fork provides applications a structured way to store resources such as thumbnail images, menu definitions, icons, dialog boxes, and code. `[Ref: macOS Hierarchical File System Overview]` Usage of a resource fork is identifiable when displaying a file’s extended attributes, using `ls -l@` or `xattr -l` commands. Resource forks have been deprecated and replaced with the application bundle structure. Non-localized resources are placed at the top level directory of an application bundle, while localized resources are placed in the `/Resources` folder. `[Ref: Resource and Data Forks]` `[Ref: ELC Extended Attributes]`

Adversaries can use resource forks to hide malicious data that may otherwise be stored directly in files. Adversaries can execute content with an attached resource fork, at a specified offset, that is moved to an executable location then invoked. Resource fork content may also be obfuscated/encrypted until execution. `[Ref: sentinellabs resource named fork 2020]` `[Ref: tau bundlore erika noerenberg 2020]`

mitigations.name: Application Developer Guidance
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar applications to use the application bundle structure which leverages the `/Resources` folder location. `[Ref: Apple App Security Overview]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Process Argument Spoofing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar hide process command-line arguments by overwriting memória do processo. Process command-line arguments are stored in the process environment block (PEB), a data structure used by Windows to store various information about/used by a process. The PEB includes the process command-line arguments that are referenced when executing the process. When a process is created, defensive tools/sensors that monitor process creations may retrieve the process arguments from the PEB. `[Ref: Microsoft PEB 2021]` `[Ref: Xpn Argue Like Cobalt 2019]`

Os adversários podem manipular a process PEB to evade defenses. Por exemplo, **Process Hollowing** (`T1055.012`) pode ser abusado para spawn a process in a suspended state with benign arguments. After the process is spawned and the PEB is initialized (and process information is potentially logged by tools/sensors), adversaries may override the PEB to modify the command-line arguments (ex: using the **Native API** (`T1106`) `WriteProcessMemory()` function) then resume process execution with malicious arguments. `[Ref: Cobalt Strike Arguments 2019]` `[Ref: Xpn Argue Like Cobalt 2019]` `[Ref: Nviso Spoof Command Line 2020]`

Os adversários podem também execute a process with malicious command-line arguments then patch the memory with benign arguments that may bypass subsequent memória do processo analysis. `[Ref: FireEye FiveHands April 2021]`

This behavior may also be combined with other tricks (such as **Parent PID Spoofing** (`T1134.004`)) to manipulate or further evade process-based detections.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Ignore Process Interrupts
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem evade defensive mechanisms by executing commands that hide from process interrupt signals. Many sistema operativos use signals to deliver messages to control process behavior. Command interpreters often include specific commands/flags that ignore errors and other hangups, such as when the user of the active session logs off. `[Ref: Linux Signal Man]`  These interrupt signals may also be used by defensive tools and/or analysts to pause or terminate specified running processes. 

Os adversários podem invoke processes using `nohup`, **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`, or similar commands that may be immune to hangups. `[Ref: nohup Linux Man]` `[Ref: Microsoft PowerShell SilentlyContinue]` This may enable malicious commands and malware to continue execution through system events that would otherwise terminate its execution, such as users logging off or the termination of its C2 network connection.

Hiding from process interrupt signals may allow malware to continue execution, but unlike **Trap** (`T1546.005`) this does not establish **Persistence** (`TA0003`) since the process will not be re-invoked once actually terminated.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: File/Path Exclusions
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar hide their file-based artifacts by writing them to specific folders or file names excluded from antivírus (AV) (AV) scanning and other defensive capabilities. AV and other file-based scanners often include exclusions to optimize performance as well as ease installation and legitimate use of applications. These exclusions may be contextual (e.g., scans are only initiated in response to specific triggering events/alerts), but are also often hardcoded strings referencing specific folders and/or files assumed to be trusted and legitimate. `[Ref: Microsoft File Folder Exclusions]`

Os adversários podem abusar de these exclusions to hide their file-based artifacts. Por exemplo, rather than  tampering with tool settings to add a new exclusion (i.e., **Disable or Modify Tools** (`T1685`)), adversaries may drop their file-based payloads in default or otherwise well-known exclusions. Os adversários podem também use **Security Software Discovery** (`T1518.001`) and other **Discovery** (`TA0007`)/**Reconnaissance** (`TA0043`) activities to both discover and verify existing exclusions in a ambiente alvo.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Review and audit file/folder exclusions, and limit scope of exclusions to only what is required where possible. `[Ref: Microsoft File Folder Exclusions]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: Application Developer Guidance
mitigations.descriptionPt: Application developers should consider limiting the requirements for custom or otherwise difficult to manage file/folder exclusions. Where possible, install applications to trusted system folder paths that are already protected by restricted file and directory permissions.

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Bind Mounts
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de bind mounts on file structures to hide their activity and artifacts from native utilities. A bind mount maps a directory or file from one location on the filesystem to another, similar to a shortcut on Windows. It’s commonly used to provide access to specific files or directories across different environments, such as inside containers or chroot environments, and requires sudo access. 

Os adversários podem utilizar bind mounts to map either an empty directory or a benign `/proc` directory to a malicious process’s `/proc` directory. Using the commands `mount –o bind /proc/benign-process /proc/malicious-process` (or `mount –B`), the malicious process's `/proc` directory is overlayed with the contents of a benign process's `/proc` directory. When system utilities query process activity, such as `ps` and `top`, the kernel follows the bind mount and presents the benign directory’s contents instead of the malicious process's actual `/proc` directory. Como resultado, these utilities display information that appears to come from the benign process, effectively hiding the malicious process's metadata, executable, or other artifacts from detection. `[Ref: Cado Security Commando Cat 2024]` `[Ref: Ahn Lab CoinMiner 2023]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Ocultação de Artefactos: Extended Attributes
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de extended attributes (xattrs) on macOS and Linux to hide their malicious data com o objetivo de evade detection. Extended attributes are key-value pairs of file and directory metadata used by both macOS and Linux. They are not visible through standard tools like `Finder`,  `ls`, or `cat` and require utilities such as `xattr` (macOS) or `getfattr` (Linux) for inspection. Operating systems and applications use xattrs for tagging, integrity checks, and access control. Em sistemas Linux, xattrs are organized into namespaces such as `user.` (user permissions), `trusted.` (root permissions), `security.`, and `system.`, each with specific permissions. Em sistemas macOS, xattrs are flat strings without namespace prefixes, commonly prefixed with `com.apple.*` (e.g., `com.apple.quarantine`, `com.apple.metadata:_kMDItemUserTags`) and used by system features like Gatekeeper and Spotlight. `[Ref: Establishing persistence using extended attributes on Linux]`

Um adversário pode leverage xattrs by embedding a second-stage payload into the extended attribute of a legitimate file. Em sistemas macOS, a payload can be embedded into a custom attribute using the `xattr` command. A separate loader can retrieve the attribute with `xattr -p`, decode the content, and execute it using a scripting interpreter. Em sistemas Linux, an adversary may use `setfattr` to write a payload into the `user.` namespace of a legitimate file. A loader script can later extract the payload with `getfattr --only-values`, decode it, and execute it using bash or another interpreter. In both cases, because the primary file content remains unchanged, security tools and integrity checks that do not inspect extended attributes will observe the original file hash, allowing the malicious payload para evadir deteção. `[Ref: Low GroupIB xattrs nov 2024]`

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: During artifact review, packaging, or deployment stages, scan extended attributes alongside file contents to detect hidden payloads, obfuscated data, or suspicious attribute keys that may indicate malicious behavior.
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Dados
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem insert, delete, or manipulate data com o objetivo de influence external outcomes or hide activity, thus threatening the integrity of the data. `[Ref: Sygnia Elephant Beetle Jan 2022]` By manipulating data, adversaries may attempt to affect a business process, organizational understanding, or decision making.

The type of modification and the impact it will have depends on the target application and process as well as the goals and objectives of the adversary. For complex systems, an adversary would likely need special expertise and possibly access to specialized software related to the system that would typically be gained through a prolonged information gathering campaign com o objetivo de have the desired impact.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider encrypting important information to reduce an adversary’s ability to perform tailored data modifications.

mitigations.name: Remote Data Storage
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for taking regular data backups that pode ser utilizado para restore organizational data. `[Ref: Ready.gov IT DRP]` Ensure backups are stored off system and is protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and manipulate backups.

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Dados: Stored Manipulação de Dados
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem insert, delete, or manipulate data at rest com o objetivo de influence external outcomes or hide activity, thus threatening the integrity of the data. `[Ref: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018]` `[Ref: DOJ Lazarus Sony 2018]` By manipulating stored data, adversaries may attempt to affect a business process, organizational understanding, and decision making.

Stored data could include a variety of file formats, such as Office files, databases, stored emails, and custom file formats. The type of modification and the impact it will have depends on the type of data as well as the goals and objectives of the adversary. For complex systems, an adversary would likely need special expertise and possibly access to specialized software related to the system that would typically be gained through a prolonged information gathering campaign com o objetivo de have the desired impact.

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Dados: Transmitted Manipulação de Dados
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem alter data en route to storage or other systems com o objetivo de manipulate external outcomes or hide activity, thus threatening the integrity of the data. `[Ref: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018]` `[Ref: DOJ Lazarus Sony 2018]` By manipulating transmitted data, adversaries may attempt to affect a business process, organizational understanding, and decision making.

Manipulation may be possible over a network connection or between system processes where there is an opportunity deploy a tool that will intercept and change information. The type of modification and the impact it will have depends on the target transmission mechanism as well as the goals and objectives of the adversary. For complex systems, an adversary would likely need special expertise and possibly access to specialized software related to the system that would typically be gained through a prolonged information gathering campaign com o objetivo de have the desired impact.

techniques.fullNamePt: Manipulação de Dados: Runtime Manipulação de Dados
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar systems com o objetivo de manipulate the data as it is accessed and displayed to an end user, thus threatening the integrity of the data. `[Ref: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018]` `[Ref: DOJ Lazarus Sony 2018]` By manipulating runtime data, adversaries may attempt to affect a business process, organizational understanding, and decision making.

Os adversários podem alter application binaries used to display data com o objetivo de cause runtime manipulations. Os adversários podem também conduct **Change Default File Association** (`T1546.001`) and **Masquerading** (`T1036`) to cause a similar effect. The type of modification and the impact it will have depends on the target application and process as well as the goals and objectives of the adversary. For complex systems, an adversary would likely need special expertise and possibly access to specialized software related to the system that would typically be gained through a prolonged information gathering campaign com o objetivo de have the desired impact.

techniques.fullNamePt: Engenharia Social e Phishing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enviar phishing messages para obter acesso a victim systems. All forms of phishing are electronically delivered engenharia social. Phishing can be targeted, known as spearphishing. In spearphishing, a specific individual, company, or industry will be targeted by the adversary. More generally, adversaries can conduct non-targeted phishing, such as in mass malware spam campaigns.

Os adversários podem enviar victims emails containing malicious attachments or links, typically para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos code on victim systems. Phishing may also be conducted via third-party services (like social media platforms) or delivered via calendar invites. Phishing may also involve engenharia social techniques, such as posing as a trusted source, as well as evasive techniques such as removing or manipulating emails or metadata/headers from compromised accounts being abused to send messages (e.g., **Email Hiding Rules** (`T1564.008`)). `[Ref: Microsoft OAuth Spam 2022]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Unit 42 VBA Infostealer 2014]` Another way to accomplish this is by **Email Spoofing** (`T1684.002`) `[Ref: Proofpoint-spoof]` the identity of the sender, which pode ser utilizado para fool both the human recipient as well as automated security tools, `[Ref: cyberproof-double-bounce]` or by including the intended target as a party to an existing email thread that includes malicious files or links (i.e., "thread hijacking"). `[Ref: phishing-krebs]`

Victims may also receive phishing messages that instruct them to call a phone number where they are directed to visit a malicious URL, download malware, `[Ref: sygnia Luna Month]` `[Ref: CISA Remote Monitoring and Management Software]` or install adversary-accessible remote management tools onto their computer (i.e., **User Execution** (`T1204`)). `[Ref: Unit42 Luna Moth]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Perform audits or scans of systems, permissions, insecure software, insecure configurations, etc. to identify potential weaknesses.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion prevention systems and systems designed to scan and remove malicious email attachments or links pode ser utilizado para block activity.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use anti-spoofing and email authentication mechanisms to filter messages based on validity checks of the sender domain (using SPF) and integrity of messages (using DKIM). Enabling these mechanisms within an organization (through policies such as DMARC) may enable recipients (intra-org and cross domain) to perform similar message filtering and validation. `[Ref: Microsoft Anti Spoofing]` `[Ref: ACSC Email Spoofing]`

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: Determine if certain websites or attachment types (ex: .scr, .exe, .pif, .cpl, etc.) that can be used for phishing are necessary for business operations and consider blocking access if activity cannot be monitored well or if it poses a significant risk.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus can automatically quarantine suspicious files.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Users can be trained to identify engenharia social techniques and phishing emails.

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Phishing across platforms.

analytics.descriptionPt: Unusual inbound email activity where attachments or embedded URLs are delivered to users followed by execution of new processes or suspicious document behavior. techniques.fullNamePt: Engenharia Social e Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enviar spearphishing emails with a malicious attachment in an attempt para obter acesso a victim systems. Spearphishing attachment is a specific variant of spearphishing. Spearphishing attachment is different from other forms of spearphishing in that it employs the use of malware attached to an email. All forms of spearphishing are electronically delivered engenharia social targeted at a specific individual, company, or industry. In this scenario, adversaries attach a file to the spearphishing email and usually rely upon **User Execution** (`T1204`) to gain execution. `[Ref: Unit 42 DarkHydrus July 2018]` Spearphishing may also involve engenharia social techniques, such as posing as a trusted source.

There are many options for the attachment such as Microsoft Office documents, executables, PDFs, or archived files. Upon opening the attachment (and potentially clicking past protections), the adversary's payload exploits a vulnerability or directly executes on the user's system. The text of the spearphishing email usually tries to give a plausible reason why the file should be opened, and may explain how para contornar (bypass) system protections com o objetivo de do so. The email may also contain instructions on how to decrypt an attachment, such as a zip file password, com o objetivo de evade email boundary defenses. Adversaries frequently manipulate file extensions and icons com o objetivo de make attached executables appear to be document files, or files exploiting one application appear to be a file for a different one.

techniques.fullNamePt: Engenharia Social e Phishing: Spearphishing Link
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enviar spearphishing emails with a malicious link in an attempt para obter acesso a victim systems. Spearphishing with a link is a specific variant of spearphishing. It is different from other forms of spearphishing in that it employs the use of links to download malware contained in email, instead of attaching malicious files to the email itself, to avoid defenses that may inspect email attachments. Spearphishing may also involve engenharia social techniques, such as posing as a trusted source.

All forms of spearphishing are electronically delivered engenharia social targeted at a specific individual, company, or industry. In this case, the malicious emails contain links. Generally, the links will be accompanied by engenharia social text and require the user to actively click or copy and paste a URL into a browser, leveraging **User Execution** (`T1204`). The visited website may compromise the web browser using an exploit, or the user will be prompted to download applications, documents, zip files, or even executables depending on the pretext for the email in the first place.

Os adversários podem também include links that are intended to interact directly with an email reader, including embedded images intended to exploit the end system directly. Additionally, adversaries may use seemingly benign links that abuse special characters to mimic legitimate websites (known as an "IDN homograph attack"). `[Ref: CISA IDN ST05-016]` URLs may also be obfuscated by taking advantage of quirks in the URL schema, such as the acceptance of integer- or hexadecimal-based hostname formats and the automatic discarding of text before an “@” symbol: for example, `hxxp://google.com@1157586937`. `[Ref: Mandiant URL Obfuscation 2023]`

Os adversários podem também utilize links to perform consent phishing/spearphishing campaigns to **Steal Application Access Token** (`T1528`)s that grant immediate access to the ambiente alvo. Por exemplo, a user may be lured into granting adversaries permissions/access via a malicious OAuth 2.0 request URL that when accepted by the user provide permissions/access for malicious applications. `[Ref: Trend Micro Pawn Storm OAuth 2017]` `[Ref: Microsoft OAuth 2.0 Consent Phishing 2021]` These stolen access tokens allow the adversary to perform various actions on behalf of the user via API calls. `[Ref: Microsoft OAuth 2.0 Consent Phishing 2021]`

Similarly, malicious links may also target device-based authorization, such as OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant flow which is typically used to authenticate devices without UIs/browsers. Known as “device code phishing,” an adversary may send a link that directs the victim to a malicious authorization page where the user is tricked into entering a code/credentials that produces a device token. `[Ref: SecureWorks Device Code Phishing 2021]` `[Ref: Netskope Device Code Phishing 2021]` `[Ref: Optiv Device Code Phishing 2021]`

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Use anti-spoofing and email authentication mechanisms to filter messages based on validity checks of the sender domain (using SPF) and integrity of messages (using DKIM). Enabling these mechanisms within an organization (through policies such as DMARC) may enable recipients (intra-org and cross domain) to perform similar message filtering and validation. `[Ref: Microsoft Anti Spoofing]` `[Ref: ACSC Email Spoofing]`.

Ademais, policies may enforce / install browser extensions that protect against IDN and homograph attacks.

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: Determine if certain websites that can be used for spearphishing are necessary for business operations and consider blocking access if activity cannot be monitored well or if it poses a significant risk.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Auditar regularmente applications and their permissions to ensure access to data and resources are limited based upon necessity and principle of least privilege.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Azure AD Administrators apply limitations upon the ability for users to grant consent to unfamiliar or unverified third-party applications.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Users can be trained to identify engenharia social techniques and spearphishing emails with malicious links which includes phishing for consent with OAuth 2.0. Additionally, users may perform visual checks of the domains they visit; however, homographs in ASCII and in IDN domains and URL schema obfuscation may render manual checks difficult. Use email warning banners to alert users when emails contain links from external senders, prompting them to exercise caution and reducing the likelihood of falling victim to spearphishing attacks. Phishing training and other cybersecurity training may raise awareness to check URLs before visiting the sites.

techniques.fullNamePt: Engenharia Social e Phishing: Spearphishing via Service
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enviar spearphishing messages via third-party services in an attempt para obter acesso a victim systems. Spearphishing via service is a specific variant of spearphishing. It is different from other forms of spearphishing in that it employs the use of third party services rather than directly via enterprise email channels. 

All forms of spearphishing are electronically delivered engenharia social targeted at a specific individual, company, or industry. In this scenario, adversaries send messages through various social media services, personal webmail, and other non-enterprise controlled services. `[Ref: Lookout Dark Caracal Jan 2018]` These services are more likely to have a less-strict security policy than an enterprise. As with most kinds of spearphishing, the goal is to generate rapport with the target or get the target's interest in some way. Adversaries will create fake social media accounts and message employees for potential job opportunities. Doing so allows a plausible reason for asking about services, policies, and software that's running in an environment. The adversary can then send malicious links or attachments through these services.

A common example is to build rapport with a target via social media, then send content to a personal webmail service that the target uses on their work computer. This allows an adversary para contornar (bypass) some email restrictions on the work account, and the target is more likely to open the file since it's something they were expecting. If the payload doesn't work as expected, the adversary can continue normal communications and troubleshoot with the target on how to get it working.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Users can be trained to identify engenharia social techniques and spearphishing messages with malicious links.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de strict user account management policies on third-party service accounts to control access and limit privileges. Configurar accounts with the minimum permissions necessary to perform their roles and regularly review access levels. This minimizes the risk of adversaries exploiting service accounts to execute spearphishing attacks or gain unauthorized access to sensitive resources.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.descriptionPt: Anti-virus can also automatically quarantine suspicious files.
mitigations.bypassHint: Evitar escrita direta em disco (Fileless Execution / Reflective Loading). Em PowerShell/DotNet, aplicar AMSI Memory Patching em `amsi.dll` (`AmsiScanBuffer` ret patch) ou Hardware Breakpoints (VEH2) antes de carregar assemblies via `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()`. Para binários nativos, aplicar cifragem de secções (AES/ChaCha20) com resolução dinâmica de APIs (API Hashing) e Direct/Indirect Syscalls.

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: Determine if certain social media sites, personal webmail services, or other service that can be used for spearphishing is necessary for business operations and consider blocking access if activity cannot be monitored well or if it poses a significant risk.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar auditing and logging for interactions with third-party messaging services or collaboration platforms. Monitor user activity and review logs for signs of suspicious links, downloads, or file exchanges that could indicate spearphishing attempts. Effective auditing allows for the quick identification of malicious activity originating from compromised service accounts.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNamePt: Engenharia Social e Phishing: Spearphishing Voice
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar voice communications to ultimately gain access to victim systems. Spearphishing voice is a specific variant of spearphishing. It is different from other forms of spearphishing in that it employs the use of manipulating a user into providing access to systems through a phone call or other forms of voice communications. Spearphishing frequently involves engenharia social techniques, such as posing as a trusted source (ex: **Impersonation** (`T1684.001`)) and/or creating a sense of urgency or alarm for the recipient.

All forms of phishing are electronically delivered engenharia social. In this scenario, adversaries are not directly sending malware to a victim vice relying on **User Execution** (`T1204`) for delivery and execution. Por exemplo, victims may receive phishing messages that instruct them to call a phone number where they are directed to visit a malicious URL, download malware, `[Ref: sygnia Luna Month]` `[Ref: CISA Remote Monitoring and Management Software]` or install adversary-accessible remote management tools (**Remote Access Tools** (`T1219`)) onto their computer. `[Ref: Unit42 Luna Moth]`

Os adversários podem também combine voice phishing with **Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation** (`T1621`) com o objetivo de trick users into divulging MFA credentials or accepting authentication prompts. `[Ref: Proofpoint Vishing]`

techniques.namePt: Exfiltração via Comunicação via Web Service
techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração via Comunicação via Web Service
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar an existing, legitimate external Web service para exfiltrar dados rather than their primary Command and Control (C2) channel. Popular Web services acting as an exfiltration mechanism may give a significant amount of cover due to the likelihood that hosts within a network are already communicating with them prior to compromise. Firewall rules may also already exist to permit traffic to these services.

Web service providers also commonly use SSL/TLS encryption, giving adversaries an added level of protection.

techniques.fullNameEn: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Code Repository
techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração via Comunicação via Web Service: Exfiltration to Code Repository
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem exfiltrar data to a code repository rather than over their primary Command and Control (C2) channel. Code repositories are often accessible via an API (ex: https://api.github.com). Access to these APIs are often over HTTPS, which gives the adversary an additional level of protection.

Exfiltration to a code repository can also provide a significant amount of cover to the adversary if it is a popular service already used by hosts within the network.

mitigations.descriptionPt: Web proxies pode ser utilizado para enforce an external network communication policy that prevents use of unauthorized external services.

analytics.name: Analytic 0895

Os adversários podem exfiltrar data to a cloud storage service rather than over their primary Command and Control (C2) channel. Cloud storage services allow for the storage, edit, and retrieval of data from a remote cloud storage server over the Internet.

Examples of cloud storage services include Dropbox and Google Docs. Exfiltration to these cloud storage services can provide a significant amount of cover to the adversary if hosts within the network are already communicating with the service.

techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração via Comunicação via Web Service: Exfiltration to Text Storage Sites
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem exfiltrar data to text storage sites instead of their primary Command and Control (C2) channel. Text storage sites, such as `pastebin[.]com`, are commonly used by developers to share code and other information.  

Text storage sites are often used to host código malicioso for C2 communication (e.g., **Stage Capabilities** (`T1608`)), but adversaries may also use these sites to exfiltrate collected data. Ademais, paid features and encryption options may allow adversaries to conceal and store data more securely. `[Ref: Pastebin EchoSec]`

**Note:** This is distinct from **Exfiltration to Code Repository** (`T1567.001`), which highlight access to code repositories via APIs.

techniques.fullNameEn: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration Over Webhook
techniques.fullNamePt: Exfiltração via Comunicação via Web Service: Exfiltration Over Webhook
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem exfiltrar data to a webhook endpoint rather than over their primary Command and Control (C2) channel. Webhooks are simple mechanisms for allowing a server to push data over HTTP/S to a client without the need for the client to continuously poll the server. `[Ref: RedHat Webhooks]` Many public and commercial services, such as Discord, Slack, and `webhook.site`, support the creation of webhook endpoints that can be used by other services, such as Github, Jira, or Trello. `[Ref: Discord Intro to Webhooks]` When changes happen in the linked services (such as pushing a repository update or modifying a ticket), these services will automatically post the data to the webhook endpoint for use by the consuming application. 

Os adversários podem link an adversary-owned environment to a victim-owned SaaS service to achieve repeated **Automated Exfiltration** (`T1020`) of emails, chat messages, and other data. `[Ref: Push Security SaaS Attacks Repository Webhooks]` Alternatively, instead of linking the webhook endpoint to a service, an adversary can manually post staged data directly to the URL com o objetivo de exfiltrate it. `[Ref: Microsoft SQL Server]`

Access to webhook endpoints is often over HTTPS, which gives the adversary an additional level of protection. Exfiltration leveraging webhooks can also blend in with normal tráfego de rede if the webhook endpoint points to a commonly used SaaS application or collaboration service. `[Ref: CyberArk Labs Discord]` `[Ref: Talos Discord Webhook Abuse]` `[Ref: Checkmarx Webhooks]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Resolução Dinâmica
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem dynamically establish connections to Command and Control (C2) infrastructure to evade common detections and remediations. This may be achieved by using malware that shares a common algorithm with the infrastructure the adversary uses to receive the malware's communications. These calculations pode ser utilizado para dynamically adjust parameters such as the domain name, IP address, or port number the malware uses for Command and Control (C2).

Os adversários podem utilizar dynamic resolution for the purpose of **Fallback Channels** (`T1008`). When contact is lost with the primary Command and Control (C2) server malware may employ dynamic resolution as a means to reestablishing Command and Control (C2). `[Ref: Talos CCleanup 2017]` `[Ref: FireEye POSHSPY April 2017]` `[Ref: ESET Sednit 2017 Activity]`

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Malware researchers can reverse engineer malware variants that use dynamic resolution and determine future C2 infrastructure that the malware will attempt to contact, but this is a time and resource intensive effort. `[Ref: Cybereason Dissecting DGAs]` `[Ref: Cisco Umbrella DGA Brute Force]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

techniques.fullNamePt: Resolução Dinâmica: Fast Flux DNS
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar Fast Flux DNS to hide a Command and Control (C2) channel behind an array of rapidly changing IP addresses linked to a single domain resolution. This technique uses a fully qualified domain name, with multiple IP addresses assigned to it which are swapped with high frequency, using a combination of round robin IP addressing and short Time-To-Live (TTL) for a DNS resource record. `[Ref: MehtaFastFluxPt1]` `[Ref: MehtaFastFluxPt2]` `[Ref: Fast Flux - Welivesecurity]`

The simplest, "single-flux" method, involves registering and de-registering an addresses as part of the DNS A (address) record list for a single DNS name. These registrations have a five-minute average lifespan, resulting in a constant shuffle of IP address resolution. `[Ref: Fast Flux - Welivesecurity]`

In contrast, the "double-flux" method registers and de-registers an address as part of the DNS Name Server record list for the DNS zone, providing additional resilience for the connection. With double-flux additional hosts can act as a proxy to the C2 host, further insulating the true source of the C2 channel.

techniques.fullNamePt: Resolução Dinâmica: Domain Generation Algorithms
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem make use of Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs) to dynamically identify a destination domain for Command and Control (C2) traffic rather than relying on a list of static IP addresses or domains. This has the advantage of making it much harder for defenders to block, track, or take over the Command and Control (C2) channel, as there potentially could be thousands of domains that malware can check for instructions. `[Ref: Cybereason Dissecting DGAs]` `[Ref: Cisco Umbrella DGA]` `[Ref: Unit 42 DGA Feb 2019]`

DGAs can take the form of apparently random or “gibberish” strings (ex: istgmxdejdnxuyla.ru) when they construct domain names by generating each letter. Alternatively, some DGAs employ whole words as the unit by concatenating words together instead of letters (ex: cityjulydish.net). Many DGAs are time-based, generating a different domain for each time period (hourly, daily, monthly, etc). Others incorporate a seed value as well to make predicting future domains more difficult for defenders. `[Ref: Cybereason Dissecting DGAs]` `[Ref: Cisco Umbrella DGA]` `[Ref: Talos CCleanup 2017]` `[Ref: Akamai DGA Mitigation]`

Os adversários podem utilizar DGAs for the purpose of **Fallback Channels** (`T1008`). When contact is lost with the primary Command and Control (C2) server malware may employ a DGA as a means to reestablishing Command and Control (C2). `[Ref: Talos CCleanup 2017]` `[Ref: FireEye POSHSPY April 2017]` `[Ref: ESET Sednit 2017 Activity]`

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Malware researchers can reverse engineer malware variants that use DGAs and determine future domains that the malware will attempt to contact, but this is a time and resource intensive effort. `[Ref: Cybereason Dissecting DGAs]` `[Ref: Cisco Umbrella DGA Brute Force]` Malware is also increasingly incorporating seed values that can be unique for each instance, which would then need to be determined to extract future generated domains. In some cases, the seed that a particular sample uses can be extracted from DNS traffic. `[Ref: Akamai DGA Mitigation]` Even so, there can be thousands of possible domains generated per day; this makes it impractical for defenders to preemptively register all possible C2 domains due to the cost.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: In some cases a local DNS sinkhole pode ser empregue para help prevent DGA-based Command and Control (C2) at a reduced cost.

techniques.fullNamePt: Resolução Dinâmica: DNS Calculation
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem realizar calculations on addresses returned in DNS results to determine which port and IP address to use for Command and Control (C2), rather than relying on a predetermined port number or the actual returned IP address. A IP and/or port number calculation pode ser utilizado para bypass egress filtering on a C2 channel. `[Ref: Meyers Numbered Panda]`

One implementation of **DNS Calculation** (`T1568.003`) is to take the first three octets of an IP address in a DNS response and use those values to calculate the port for Command and Control (C2) traffic. `[Ref: Meyers Numbered Panda]` `[Ref: Moran 2014]` `[Ref: Rapid7G20Espionage]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução de Serviços do Sistema
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem abusar de system services or daemons to execute commands or programs. Adversaries can execute malicious content by interacting with or creating services either locally or remotely. Many services are set to run at boot, which can aid in achieving persistence (**Create or Modify System Process** (`T1543`)), but adversaries can also abuse services for one-time or temporary execution.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que permissions disallow services that run at a higher permissions level from being created or interacted with by a user with a lower permission level.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent users from installing their own launch agents or launch daemons.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to block processes created by **PsExec** (`S0029`) from running.  `[Ref: win10_asr]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que high permission level service binaries cannot be replaced or modified by users with a lower permission level.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).
