Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução de Serviços do Sistema: Launchctl
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de launchctl to execute commands or programs. Launchctl interfaces with launchd, the service management framework for macOS. Launchctl supports taking subcommands on the command-line, interactively, or even redirected from standard input. `[Ref: Launchctl Man]`

Adversaries use launchctl to execute commands and programs as **Launch Agent** (`T1543.001`)s or **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`)s. Common subcommands include: `launchctl load`,`launchctl unload`, and `launchctl start`. Adversaries can use scripts or manually run the commands `launchctl load -w "%s/Library/LaunchAgents/%s"` or `/bin/launchctl load` to execute **Launch Agent** (`T1543.001`)s or **Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`)s. `[Ref: Sofacy Komplex Trojan]` `[Ref: 20 macOS Common Tools and Techniques]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução de Serviços do Sistema: Service Execution
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de the Windows service control manager para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos commands or payloads. The Windows service control manager (`services.exe`) is an interface to manage and manipulate services. `[Ref: Microsoft Service Control Manager]` The service control manager is accessible to users via GUI components as well as system utilities such as `sc.exe` and **Net** (`S0039`).

**PsExec** (`S0029`) pode também ser utilizado para execute commands or payloads via a temporary Windows service created through the service control manager API. `[Ref: Russinovich Sysinternals]` Tools such as **PsExec** (`S0029`) and `sc.exe` can accept remote servers as arguments and pode ser empregue para conduct remote execution.

Os adversários podem tirar partido de these mechanisms para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos content. This can be done by either executing a new or modified service. This technique is the execution used in conjunction with **Windows Service** (`T1543.003`) during service persistence or privilege escalation.

techniques.fullNamePt: Execução de Serviços do Sistema: Systemctl
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de systemctl to execute commands or programs. Systemctl is the primary interface for systemd, the Linux init system and service manager. Typically invoked from a shell, Systemctl can also be integrated into scripts or applications.   

Os adversários podem utilizar systemctl to execute commands or programs as **Systemd Service** (`T1543.002`)s. Common subcommands include: `systemctl start`, `systemctl stop`, `systemctl enable`, `systemctl disable`, and `systemctl status`. `[Ref: Red Hat Systemctl 2022]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit user access to `systemctl` to only users who have a legitimate need.

analytics.descriptionPt: Abuse of systemctl to execute commands or manage systemd services. Defender perspective: correlate suspicious service creation or modification with execution of systemctl subcommands such as start, enable, or status. Detect cases where systemctl é utilizado para load services from unusual locations (e.g., /tmp, /dev/shm) or where new service units are created outside of expected administrative workflows.

techniques.fullNamePt: Transferência Lateral de Ferramentas
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem transfer tools or other files between systems in a compromised environment. Uma vez que brought into the ambiente alvo (i.e., **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`)) files may then be copied from one system to another to stage adversary tools or other files over the course of an operation.

Os adversários podem copiar files between internal victim systems to support lateral movement using inherent file sharing protocols such as file sharing over **SMB/Windows Admin Shares** (`T1021.002`) to connected network shares or with authenticated connections via **Remote Desktop Protocol** (`T1021.001`). `[Ref: Unit42 LockerGoga 2019]`

Files can also be transferred using native or otherwise present tools on the victim system, such as scp, rsync, curl, sftp, and **ftp** (`S0095`). In some cases, adversaries may be able to leverage **Web Service** (`T1102`)s such as Dropbox or OneDrive to copy files from one machine to another via shared, automatically synced folders. `[Ref: Dropbox Malware Sync]`

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider using the host firewall to restrict file sharing communications such as SMB.  `[Ref: Microsoft Preventing SMB]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware or unusual data transfer over known tools and protocols like FTP pode ser utilizado para mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific obfuscation technique used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various malware families and versions.  `[Ref: University of Birmingham C2]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

bypasses: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

Pivotar para protocolos alternativos como DCOM (`MMC20.Application`), WMI sobre RPC, MSSQL Links (`1433`), RDP em modo `RestrictedAdmin`, ou autenticação Kerberos com chaves AES256 (`Overpass-the-Hash`) usando o FQDN do host em vez do endereço IP.

techniques.fullNamePt: Porta Não-Standard
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem communicate using a protocol and port pairing that are typically not associated. Por exemplo, HTTPS over port 8088 `[Ref: Symantec Elfin Mar 2019]` or port 587 `[Ref: Fortinet Agent Tesla April 2018]` as opposed to the traditional port 443. Os adversários podem make changes to the standard port used by a protocol para contornar (bypass) filtering or muddle analysis/parsing of network data.

Os adversários podem também make changes to victim systems to abuse non-standard ports. Por exemplo, Registry keys and other configuration settings pode ser utilizado para modify protocol and port pairings. `[Ref: change_rdp_port_conti]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Tunelamento de Protocolo (Protocol Tunneling)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tunnel network communications to and from a victim system within a separate protocol para evitar deteção/network filtering and/or enable access to otherwise unreachable systems. Tunneling involves explicitly encapsulating a protocol within another. This behavior may conceal malicious traffic by blending in with existing traffic and/or provide an outer layer of encryption (similar to a VPN). Tunneling could also enable routing of network packets that would otherwise not reach their intended destination, such as SMB, RDP, or other traffic that would be filtered by network appliances or not routed over the Internet. 

There are various means to encapsulate a protocol within another protocol. Por exemplo, adversaries may perform SSH tunneling (also known as SSH port forwarding), which involves forwarding arbitrary data over an encrypted SSH tunnel. `[Ref: SSH Tunneling]` `[Ref: Sygnia Abyss Locker 2025]` 

**Protocol Tunneling** (`T1572`) may also be abused by adversaries during **Dynamic Resolution** (`T1568`). Known as DNS over HTTPS (DoH), queries to resolve C2 infrastructure may be encapsulated within encrypted HTTPS packets. `[Ref: BleepingComp Godlua JUL19]` 

Os adversários podem também leverage **Protocol Tunneling** (`T1572`) in conjunction with **Proxy** (`T1090`) and/or **Protocol or Service Impersonation** (`T1001.003`) to further conceal C2 communications and infrastructure.

techniques.fullNamePt: Canal Encriptado: Asymmetric Cryptography
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem employ a known asymmetric encryption algorithm to conceal Command and Control (C2) traffic rather than relying on any inherent protections provided by a communication protocol. Asymmetric cryptography, also known as public key cryptography, uses a keypair per party: one public that can be freely distributed, and one private. Due to how the keys are generated, the sender encrypts data with the receiver’s public key and the receiver decrypts the data with their private key. This ensures that only the intended recipient can read the encrypted data. Common public key encryption algorithms include RSA and ElGamal.

For efficiency, many protocols (including SSL/TLS) use symmetric cryptography once a connection is established, but use asymmetric cryptography to establish or transmit a key. As such, these protocols are classified as **Asymmetric Cryptography** (`T1573.002`). `[Ref: What is asymmetric encryption]` `[Ref: Symmetric vs Asymmetric Cryptography]`

techniques.namePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking)
techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking the way sistema operativos run programs. Hijacking execution flow can be for the purposes of persistence, since this hijacked execution may reoccur over time. Os adversários podem também use these mechanisms to elevate privileges or evade defenses, such as application control or other restrictions on execution.

There are many ways an adversary may hijack the flow of execution, including by manipulating how the sistema operativo locates programs to be executed. How the sistema operativo locates libraries to be used by a program can also be intercepted. Locations where the sistema operativo looks for programs/resources, such as file directories and in the case of Windows the Registry, could also be poisoned to include malicious payloads. `[Ref: Execution flow hijack attempt]`

mitigations.name: User Account Control
mitigations.descriptionPt: Turn off UAC's privilege elevation for standard users `[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System]` to automatically deny elevation requests, add: `"ConsentPromptBehaviorUser"=dword:00000000`. Consider enabling installer detection for all users by adding: `"EnableInstallerDetection"=dword:00000001`. This will prompt for a password for installation and also log the attempt. To disable installer detection, instead add: `"EnableInstallerDetection"=dword:00000000`. This may prevent potential elevation of privileges through exploitation during the process of UAC detecting the installer, but will allow the installation process to continue without being logged.   `[Ref: Executable Installers are Vulnerable]`

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: Some endpoint security solutions can be configured to block some types of behaviors related to process injection/memory tampering based on common sequences of indicators (ex: execution of specific API functions).
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

mitigations.name: Restrict Library Loading
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Disallow loading of remote DLLs. This is included by default in Windows Server 2012+ and is available by patch for XP+ and Server 2003+.

Enable Safe DLL Search Mode to force search for system DLLs in directories with greater restrictions (e.g. `%SYSTEMROOT%`)to be used before local directory DLLs (e.g. a user's home directory)

The Safe DLL Search Mode can be enabled via Group Policy at Computer Configuration > [Policies] > Administrative Templates > MSS (Legacy): MSS: (SafeDllSearchMode) Enable Safe DLL search mode. The associated Windows Registry key for this is located at `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\SafeDLLSearchMode` `[Ref: Microsoft More information about DLL]` `[Ref: Microsoft Dynamic Link Library Search Order]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Use auditing tools capable of detecting hijacking opportunities on systems within an enterprise and correct them. Toolkits like the PowerSploit framework contain PowerUp modules that pode ser utilizado para explore systems for hijacking weaknesses. `[Ref: Powersploit]`

Use the program sxstrace.exe that is included with Windows along with manual inspection to check manifest files for side-loading vulnerabilities in software.

Find and eliminate path interception weaknesses in program ficheiros de configuração, scripts, the PATH environment variable, services, and in shortcuts by surrounding PATH variables with quotation marks when functions allow for them. Be aware of the search order Windows uses for executing or loading binaries and use fully qualified paths wherever appropriate.

Clean up old Windows Registry keys when software is uninstalled to avoid keys with no associated legitimate binaries. Periodically search for and correct or report path interception weaknesses on systems that may have been introduced using custom or available tools that report software using insecure path configurations. `[Ref: Microsoft CreateProcess]` `[Ref: Microsoft Dynamic-Link Library Security]` `[Ref: Vulnerability and Exploit Detector]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Application Developer Guidance
mitigations.descriptionPt: When possible, include hash values in manifest files to help prevent side-loading of malicious libraries. `[Ref: FireEye DLL Side-Loading]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Limitar os privilégios das contas de utilizador and groups so that only authorized administrators can interact with service changes and service binary target path locations. Deny execution from user directories such as file download directories and temp directories where able.

Garantir que proper permissions and directory access control are set to deny users the ability to write files to the top-level directory `C:` and system directories, such as `C:\Windows\`, to reduce places where malicious files could be placed for execution.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Update software regularly to include patches that fix DLL side-loading vulnerabilities.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem utilizar new payloads to execute this technique. Identify and block potentially malicious software executed through hijacking by using application control solutions also capable of blocking libraries loaded by legitimate software.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): DLL
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de dynamic-link library files (DLLs) com o objetivo de achieve persistence, escalate privileges, and evade defenses. DLLs are libraries that contain code and data that can be simultaneously utilized by multiple programs. While DLLs are not malicious by nature, they can be abused through mechanisms such as side-loading, hijacking search order, and phantom DLL hijacking. `[Ref: unit 42]`

Specific ways DLLs are abused by adversaries include:

### DLL Sideloading
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by side-loading DLLs. Side-loading involves hijacking which DLL a program loads by planting and then invoking a legitimate application that executes their payload(s).

Side-loading positions both the victim application and malicious payload(s) alongside each other. Adversaries likely use side-loading as a means of masking actions they perform under a legitimate, trusted, and potentially elevated system or software process. Benign executables used to side-load payloads may not be flagged during delivery and/or execution. Adversary payloads may also be encrypted/packed or otherwise obfuscated until loaded into the memory of the trusted process.

Os adversários podem também side-load other packages, such as BPLs (Borland Package Library). `[Ref: kroll bpl]`

Os adversários podem chain DLL sideloading multiple times to fragment functionality hindering analysis. Adversaries using multiple DLL files can split the loader functions across different DLLs, with a main DLL loading the separated export functions.  `[Ref: Virus Bulletin]` Spreading loader functions across multiple DLLs makes analysis harder, since all files must be collected to fully understand the malware’s behavior.  Another method implements a “loader-for-a-loader”, where a malicious DLL’s sole role is to load a second DLL (or a chain of DLLs) that contain the real payload.  `[Ref: Sophos]`

### DLL Search Order Hijacking
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking the search order that Windows uses to load DLLs. This search order is a sequence of special and standard search locations that a program checks when loading a DLL. Um adversário consegue plant a trojan DLL in a directory that will be prioritized by the DLL search order over the location of a legitimate library. This will cause Windows to load the malicious DLL when it is called for by the victim program. `[Ref: unit 42]`

### DLL Redirection
Os adversários podem directly modify the search order via DLL redirection, which after being enabled (in the Registry or via the creation of a redirection file) may cause a program to load a DLL from a different location. `[Ref: Microsoft redirection]` `[Ref: Microsoft - manifests/assembly]`

### Phantom DLL Hijacking
Os adversários podem tirar partido de phantom DLL hijacking by targeting references to non-existent DLL files. They may be able to load their own malicious DLL by planting it with the correct name in the location of the missing module. `[Ref: Hexacorn DLL Hijacking]` `[Ref: Hijack DLLs CrowdStrike]`

### DLL Substitution
Os adversários podem target existing, valid DLL files and substitute them with their own malicious DLLs, planting them with the same name and in the same location as the valid DLL file. `[Ref: Wietze Beukema DLL Hijacking]`

Programs that fall victim to DLL hijacking may appear to behave normally because malicious DLLs may be configured to also load the legitimate DLLs they were meant to replace, evading defenses.

Remote DLL hijacking can occur when a program sets its current directory to a remote location, such as a Web share, before loading a DLL. `[Ref: dll pre load owasp]` `[Ref: microsoft remote preloading]`

If a valid DLL is configured to run at a higher privilege level, then the adversary-controlled DLL that is loaded will also be executed at the higher level. In this case, the technique could be used for privilege escalation.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Identify and block potentially malicious software executed through DLL hijacking by using application control solutions capable of blocking DLLs loaded by legitimate software. `[Ref: Microsoft AppLocker DLL]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Restrict Library Loading
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Disallow loading of remote DLLs. This is included by default in Windows Server 2012+ and is available by patch for XP+ and Server 2003+. `[Ref: Microsoft More information about DLL]`

Enable Safe DLL Search Mode to move the user's current folder later in the search order. This is included by default in modern versions of Windows; the associated Windows Registry key is located at `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\SafeDLLSearchMode`. `[Ref: Microsoft Dynamic Link Library Search Order]`

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Update software regularly to include patches that fix DLL side-loading vulnerabilities.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Use auditing tools capable of detecting DLL search order hijacking opportunities on systems within an enterprise and correct them. Toolkits like the PowerSploit framework contain PowerUp modules that pode ser utilizado para explore systems for DLL hijacking weaknesses. `[Ref: Powersploit]`

Use the program `sxstrace.exe` that is included with Windows, along with manual inspection, to check manifest files for side-by-side problems in software. `[Ref: Microsoft Sxstrace]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: When possible, include hash values in manifest files to help prevent side-loading of malicious libraries.

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): Dylib Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own payloads by placing a malicious dynamic library (dylib) with an expected name in a path a victim application searches at runtime. The dynamic loader will try to find the dylibs based on the sequential order of the search paths. Paths to dylibs may be prefixed with `@rpath`, which allows developers to use relative paths to specify an array of search paths used at runtime based on the location of the executable.  Additionally, if weak linking is used, such as the `LC_LOAD_WEAK_DYLIB` function, an application will still execute even if an expected dylib is not present. Weak linking enables developers to run an application on multiple macOS versions as new APIs are added.

Os adversários podem gain execution by inserting malicious dylibs with the name of the missing dylib in the identified path. `[Ref: Wardle Dylib Hijack Vulnerable Apps]` `[Ref: Wardle Dylib Hijacking OSX 2015]` `[Ref: Github EmpireProject HijackScanner]` `[Ref: Github EmpireProject CreateHijacker Dylib]` Dylibs are loaded into an application's address space allowing the malicious dylib to inherit the application's privilege level and resources. Based on the application, this could result in privilege escalation and uninhibited network access. This method may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process. `[Ref: Writing Bad Malware for OSX]` `[Ref: wardle artofmalware volume1]` `[Ref: MalwareUnicorn macOS Dylib Injection MachO]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Set directory access controls to prevent file writes to the search paths for applications, both in the folders where applications are run from and the standard dylib folders.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

techniques.fullNameEn: Hijack Execution Flow: Executable Installer File Permissions Weakness
techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): Executable Installer File Permissions Weakness
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking the binaries used by an installer. These processes may automatically execute specific binaries as part of their functionality or to perform other actions. If the permissions on the sistema de ficheiros directory containing a target binary, or permissions on the binary itself, are improperly set, then the target binary may be overwritten with another binary using user-level permissions and executed by the original process. If the original process and thread are running under a higher permissions level, then the replaced binary will also execute under higher-level permissions, which could include SYSTEM.

Another variation of this technique can be performed by taking advantage of a weakness that is common in executable, self-extracting installers. During the installation process, it is common for installers to use a subdirectory within the `%TEMP%` directory to unpack binaries such as DLLs, EXEs, or other payloads. When installers create subdirectories and files they often do not set appropriate permissions to restrict write access, which allows for execution of untrusted code placed in the subdirectories or overwriting of binaries used in the installation process. This behavior is related to and may take advantage of **DLL** (`T1574.001`) search order hijacking.

Os adversários podem utilizar this technique to replace legitimate binaries with malicious ones as a means of executing code at a higher permissions level. Some installers may also require privilégios elevados that will result in privilege escalation when executing adversary controlled code. This behavior is related to **Bypass User Account Control** (`T1548.002`). Several examples of this weakness in existing common installers have been reported to software vendors. `[Ref: mozilla_sec_adv_2012]`   `[Ref: Executable Installers are Vulnerable]` If the executing process is set to run at a specific time or during a certain event (e.g., system bootup) then this technique can also be used for persistence.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use auditing tools capable of detecting sistema de ficheiros permissions abuse opportunities on systems within an enterprise and correct them. Toolkits like the PowerSploit framework contain PowerUp modules that pode ser utilizado para explore systems for service sistema de ficheiros permissions weaknesses. `[Ref: Powersploit]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Control
mitigations.descriptionPt: Turn off UAC's privilege elevation for standard users `[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System]` to automatically deny elevation requests, add: `"ConsentPromptBehaviorUser"=dword:00000000`. Consider enabling installer detection for all users by adding: `"EnableInstallerDetection"=dword:00000001`. This will prompt for a password for installation and also log the attempt. To disable installer detection, instead add: `"EnableInstallerDetection"=dword:00000000`. This may prevent potential elevation of privileges through exploitation during the process of UAC detecting the installer, but will allow the installation process to continue without being logged.   `[Ref: Executable Installers are Vulnerable]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limitar os privilégios das contas de utilizador and groups so that only authorized administrators can interact with service changes and service binary target path locations. Deny execution from user directories such as file download directories and temp directories where able.

techniques.fullNameEn: Hijack Execution Flow: Dynamic Linker Hijacking
techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): Dynamic Linker Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking variáveis de ambiente the dynamic linker uses to load shared libraries. During the execution preparation phase of a program, the dynamic linker loads specified absolute paths of shared libraries from various variáveis de ambiente and files, such as `LD_PRELOAD` on Linux or `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` on macOS. `[Ref: TheEvilBit DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES]` `[Ref: Timac DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES]` `[Ref: Gabilondo DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES Catalina Bypass]` Libraries specified in variáveis de ambiente are loaded first, taking precedence over system libraries with the same function name. `[Ref: Man LD.SO]` `[Ref: TLDP Shared Libraries]` `[Ref: Apple Doco Archive Dynamic Libraries]` Each platform's linker uses an extensive list of variáveis de ambiente at different points in execution. These variables are often used by developers to debug binaries without needing to recompile, deconflict mapped symbols, and implement custom functions in the original library. `[Ref: Baeldung LD_PRELOAD]`

Hijacking dynamic linker variables may grant access to the victim process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados. Em sistemas Linux, adversaries may set `LD_PRELOAD` to point to malicious libraries that match the name of legitimate libraries which are requested by a victim program, causing the sistema operativo to load the adversary's código malicioso upon execution of the victim program. Por exemplo, adversaries have used `LD_PRELOAD` to inject a malicious library into every descendant process of the `sshd` daemon, resulting in execution under a legitimate process. When the executing sub-process calls the `execve` function, for example, the malicious library’s `execve` function is executed rather than the system function `execve` contained in the system library on disk. This allows adversaries to **Hide Artifacts** (`T1564`) from detection, as hooking system functions such as `execve` and `readdir` enables malware to scrub its own artifacts from the results of commands such as `ls`, `ldd`, `iptables`, and `dmesg`. `[Ref: ESET Ebury Oct 2017]` `[Ref: Intezer Symbiote 2022]` `[Ref: Elastic Security Labs Pumakit 2024]`

Hijacking dynamic linker variables may grant access to the victim process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly privilégios elevados.

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: When System Integrity Protection (SIP) is enabled in macOS, the aforementioned variáveis de ambiente are ignored when executing protected binaries. Third-party applications can also leverage Apple’s Hardened Runtime, ensuring these variáveis de ambiente are subject to imposed restrictions. `[Ref: Apple Developer Doco Hardened Runtime]` Admins can add restrictions to applications by setting the setuid and/or setgid bits, use entitlements, or have a __RESTRICT segment in the Mach-O binary.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem utilizar new payloads to execute this technique. Identify and block potentially malicious software executed through hijacking by using application control solutions also capable of blocking libraries loaded by legitimate software.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.nameEn: Path Interception by PATH Environment Variable
techniques.fullNameEn: Hijack Execution Flow: Path Interception by PATH Environment Variable
techniques.namePt: Path Interception by PATH Environment Variable
techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): Path Interception by PATH Environment Variable
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking variáveis de ambiente used to load libraries. The PATH environment variable contains a list of directories (User and System) that the OS searches sequentially through in search of the binary that was called from a script or the command line. 

Adversaries can place a malicious program in an earlier entry in the list of directories stored in the PATH environment variable, resulting in the sistema operativo executing the malicious binary rather than the legitimate binary when it searches sequentially through that PATH listing.

Por exemplo, on Windows if an adversary places a malicious program named "net.exe" in `C:\example path`, which by default precedes `C:\Windows\system32\net.exe` in the PATH environment variable, when "net" is executed from the command-line the `C:\example path` will be called instead of the system's legitimate executable at `C:\Windows\system32\net.exe`. Some methods of executing a program rely on the PATH environment variable to determine the locations that are searched when the path for the program is not given, such as executing programs from a **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`). `[Ref: ExpressVPN PATH env Windows 2021]`

Os adversários podem também directly modify the $PATH variable specifying the directories to be searched.  Um adversário consegue modify the `$PATH` variable to point to a directory they have write access. When a program using the $PATH variable is called, the OS searches the specified directory and executes the malicious binary. Em sistemas macOS, this can also be performed through modifying the $HOME variable. These variables can be modified using the command-line, launchctl, **Unix Shell Configuration Modification** (`T1546.004`), or modifying the `/etc/paths.d` folder contents. `[Ref: uptycs Fake POC linux malware 2023]` `[Ref: nixCraft macOS PATH variables]` `[Ref: Elastic Rules macOS launchctl 2022]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que proper permissions and directory access control are set to deny users the ability to write files to the top-level directory `C:` and system directories, such as `C:\Windows\`, to reduce places where malicious files could be placed for execution. Require that all executables be placed in write-protected directories.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Adversaries will likely need to place new binaries in locations to be executed through this weakness. Identify and block potentially malicious software executed path interception by using application control tools, like Windows Defender Application Control, AppLocker, or Software Restriction Policies where appropriate. `[Ref: SANS Application Whitelisting]` `[Ref: Microsoft Windows Defender Application Control]` `[Ref: Windows Commands JPCERT]` `[Ref: NSA MS AppLocker]` `[Ref: Microsoft Application Lockdown]` `[Ref: Microsoft Using Software Restriction ]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Find and eliminate path interception weaknesses in program ficheiros de configuração, scripts, the PATH environment variable, services, and in shortcuts by surrounding PATH variables with quotation marks when functions allow for them. Be aware of the search order Windows uses for executing or loading binaries and use fully qualified paths wherever appropriate.

Clean up old Windows Registry keys when software is uninstalled to avoid keys with no associated legitimate binaries. Periodically search for and correct or report path interception weaknesses on systems that may have been introduced using custom or available tools that report software using insecure path configurations. `[Ref: Microsoft CreateProcess]` `[Ref: Microsoft Dynamic-Link Library Security]` `[Ref: Vulnerability and Exploit Detector]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.nameEn: Path Interception by Search Order Hijacking
techniques.fullNameEn: Hijack Execution Flow: Path Interception by Search Order Hijacking
techniques.namePt: Path Interception by Search Order Hijacking
techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): Path Interception by Search Order Hijacking
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking the search order used to load other programs. Because some programs do not call other programs using the full path, adversaries may place their own file in the directory where the calling program is located, causing the sistema operativo to launch their malicious software at the request of the calling program.

Search order hijacking occurs when an adversary abuses the order in which Windows searches for programs that are not given a path. Unlike **DLL** (`T1574.001`) search order hijacking, the search order differs depending on the method that é utilizado para execute the program.  `[Ref: Microsoft CreateProcess]`  `[Ref: Windows NT Command Shell]`  `[Ref: Microsoft WinExec]` Contudo, it is common for Windows to search in the directory of the initiating program before searching through the Windows system directory. An adversary who finds a program vulnerable to search order hijacking (i.e., a program that does not specify the path to an executable) may take advantage of this vulnerability by creating a program named after the improperly specified program and placing it within the initiating program's directory.

Por exemplo, "example.exe" runs "cmd.exe" with the command-line argument `net user`. Um adversário pode place a program called "net.exe" within the same directory as example.exe, "net.exe" will be run instead of the Windows system utility net. Além disso, if an adversary places a program called "net.com" in the same directory as "net.exe", then `cmd.exe /C net user` will execute "net.com" instead of "net.exe" due to the order of executable extensions defined under PATHEXT.  `[Ref: Microsoft Environment Property]`

Search order hijacking is also a common practice for hijacking DLL loads and is covered in **DLL** (`T1574.001`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): Path Interception by Unquoted Path
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking vulnerable file path references. Adversaries can take advantage of paths that lack surrounding quotations by placing an executable in a higher level directory within the path, so that Windows will choose the adversary's executable to launch.

Service paths  `[Ref: Microsoft CurrentControlSet Services]` and shortcut paths may also be vulnerable to path interception if the path has one or more spaces and is not surrounded by quotation marks (e.g., `C:\unsafe path with space\program.exe` vs. `"C:\safe path with space\program.exe"`).  `[Ref: Help eliminate unquoted path]` (stored in Windows Registry keys) Um adversário consegue place an executable in a higher level directory of the path, and Windows will resolve that executable instead of the intended executable. Por exemplo, if the path in a shortcut is `C:\program files\myapp.exe`, an adversary may create a program at `C:\program.exe` that will be run instead of the intended program.  `[Ref: Windows Unquoted Services]`  `[Ref: Windows Privilege Escalation Guide]`

This technique can be used for persistence if executables are called on a regular basis, as well as privilege escalation if intercepted executables are started by a higher privileged process.

techniques.fullNameEn: Hijack Execution Flow: Services File Permissions Weakness
techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): Services File Permissions Weakness
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking the binaries used by services. Os adversários podem utilizar flaws in the permissions of Windows services to replace the binary that is executed upon service start. These service processes may automatically execute specific binaries as part of their functionality or to perform other actions. If the permissions on the sistema de ficheiros directory containing a target binary, or permissions on the binary itself are improperly set, then the target binary may be overwritten with another binary using user-level permissions and executed by the original process. If the original process and thread are running under a higher permissions level, then the replaced binary will also execute under higher-level permissions, which could include SYSTEM.

Os adversários podem utilizar this technique to replace legitimate binaries with malicious ones as a means of executing code at a higher permissions level. If the executing process is set to run at a specific time or during a certain event (e.g., system bootup) then this technique can also be used for persistence.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limitar os privilégios das contas de utilizador and groups so that only authorized administrators can interact with service changes and service binary target path locations. Deny execution from user directories such as file download directories and temp directories where able.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use auditing tools capable of detecting sistema de ficheiros permissions abuse opportunities on systems within an enterprise and correct them. Toolkits like the PowerSploit framework contain PowerUp modules that pode ser utilizado para explore systems for service sistema de ficheiros permissions weaknesses. `[Ref: Powersploit]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Control
mitigations.descriptionPt: Turn off UAC's privilege elevation for standard users `[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System]`to automatically deny elevation requests, add: `"ConsentPromptBehaviorUser"=dword:00000000`. Consider enabling installer detection for all users by adding: `"EnableInstallerDetection"=dword:00000001`. This will prompt for a password for installation and also log the attempt. To disable installer detection, instead add: `"EnableInstallerDetection"=dword:00000000`. This may prevent potential elevation of privileges through exploitation during the process of UAC detecting the installer, but will allow the installation process to continue without being logged. `[Ref: Executable Installers are Vulnerable]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Hijack Execution Flow: Services Registry Permissions Weakness
techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): Services Registry Permissions Weakness
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking the Registry entries used by services. Flaws in the permissions for Registry keys related to services can allow adversaries to redirect the originally specified executable to one they control, launching their own code when a service starts. Windows stores local service configuration information in the Registry under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services`. The information stored under a service's Registry keys can be manipulated to modify a service's execution parameters through tools such as the service controller, sc.exe,  **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`), or **Reg** (`S0075`). Access to Registry keys is controlled through access control lists and user permissions.  `[Ref: Registry Key Security]` `[Ref: malware_hides_service]`

If the permissions for users and groups are not properly set and allow access to the Registry keys for a service, adversaries may change the service's binPath/ImagePath to point to a different executable under their control. When the service starts or is restarted, the adversary-controlled program will execute, allowing the adversary to establish persistence and/or privilege escalation to the account context the service is set to execute under (local/domain account, SYSTEM, LocalService, or NetworkService).

Os adversários podem também alter other Registry keys in the service’s Registry tree. Por exemplo, the `FailureCommand` key may be changed so that the service is executed in an elevated context anytime the service fails or is intentionally corrupted. `[Ref: Kansa Service related collectors]` `[Ref: Tweet Registry Perms Weakness]`

The `Performance` key contains the name of a driver service's performance DLL and the names of several exported functions in the DLL. `[Ref: microsoft_services_registry_tree]` If the `Performance` key is not already present and if an adversary-controlled user has the `Create Subkey` permission, adversaries may create the `Performance` key in the service’s Registry tree to point to a malicious DLL. `[Ref: insecure_reg_perms]`

Os adversários podem também add the `Parameters` key, which can reference malicious drivers file paths. This technique has been identified to be a method of abuse by configuring DLL file paths within the `Parameters` key of a given services registry configuration. By placing and configuring the `Parameters` key to reference a malicious DLL, adversaries can ensure that their code is loaded persistently whenever the associated service or library is invoked.

Por exemplo, the registry path `[Ref: MDSec]` `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WinSock2\Parameters` `[Ref: hexacorn]` `[Ref: gendigital]` contains the `AutodiaDLL` value, which specifies the DLL to be loaded for autodial funcitionality. An adversary could set the `AutodiaDLL` to point to a hijacked or malicious DLL:

`"AutodialDLL"="c:\temp\foo.dll"`

This ensures persistence, as it causes the DLL (in this case, foo.dll) to be loaded each time the Winsock 2 library is invoked.

mitigations.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper permissions are set for Registry hives to prevent users from modifying keys for system components that may lead to privilege escalation.

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): COR_PROFILER
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem tirar partido de the COR_PROFILER environment variable to hijack the execution flow of programs that load the .NET CLR. The COR_PROFILER is a .NET Framework feature which allows developers to specify an unmanaged (or external of .NET) profiling DLL to be loaded into each .NET process that loads the Common Language Runtime (CLR). These profilers are designed to monitor, troubleshoot, and debug managed code executed by the .NET CLR. `[Ref: Microsoft Profiling Mar 2017]` `[Ref: Microsoft COR_PROFILER Feb 2013]`

The COR_PROFILER environment variable can be set at various scopes (system, user, or process) resulting in different levels of influence. System and user-wide environment variable scopes are specified in the Registry, where a **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`) (COM) object can be registered as a profiler DLL. A process scope COR_PROFILER can also be created in-memory without modifying the Registry. Starting with .NET Framework 4, the profiling DLL does not need to be registered as long as the location of the DLL is specified in the COR_PROFILER_PATH environment variable. `[Ref: Microsoft COR_PROFILER Feb 2013]`

Os adversários podem abusar de COR_PROFILER to establish persistence that executes a malicious DLL in the context of all .NET processes every time the CLR is invoked. The COR_PROFILER pode também ser utilizado para elevate privileges (ex: **Bypass User Account Control** (`T1548.002`)) if the victim .NET process executes at a higher permission level, as well as to hook and impair defenses provided by .NET processes. `[Ref: RedCanary Mockingbird May 2020]` `[Ref: Red Canary COR_PROFILER May 2020]` `[Ref: Almond COR_PROFILER Apr 2019]` `[Ref: GitHub OmerYa Invisi-Shell]` `[Ref: subTee .NET Profilers May 2017]`

mitigations.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper permissions are set for Registry hives to prevent users from modifying keys associated with COR_PROFILER.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Identify and block potentially malicious unmanaged COR_PROFILER profiling DLLs  by using application control solutions like AppLocker that are capable of auditing and/or blocking unapproved DLLs. `[Ref: Beechey 2010]` `[Ref: Windows Commands JPCERT]` `[Ref: NSA MS AppLocker]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the privileges of user accounts so that only authorized administrators can edit system variáveis de ambiente.

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): KernelCallbackTable
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de the `KernelCallbackTable` of a process to hijack its execution flow com o objetivo de run their own payloads. `[Ref: Lazarus APT January 2022]` `[Ref: FinFisher exposed ]` The `KernelCallbackTable` can be found in the Process Environment Block (PEB) and is initialized to an array of graphic functions available to a GUI process once `user32.dll` is loaded. `[Ref: Windows Process Injection KernelCallbackTable]`

Um adversário pode hijack the execution flow of a process using the `KernelCallbackTable` by replacing an original callback function with a malicious payload. Modifying callback functions can be achieved in various ways involving related behaviors such as **Reflective Code Loading** (`T1620`) or **Process Injection** (`T1055`) into another process.

A pointer to the memory address of the `KernelCallbackTable` can be obtained by locating the PEB (ex: via a call to the `NtQueryInformationProcess()` **Native API** (`T1106`) function). `[Ref: NtQueryInformationProcess]` Uma vez que the pointer is located, the `KernelCallbackTable` can be duplicated, and a function in the table (e.g., `fnCOPYDATA`) set to the address of a malicious payload (ex: via `WriteProcessMemory()`). The PEB is then updated with the new address of the table. Uma vez que the tampered function is invoked, the malicious payload will be triggered. `[Ref: Lazarus APT January 2022]`

The tampered function is typically invoked using a Windows message. After the process is hijacked and código malicioso is executed, the `KernelCallbackTable` may also be restored to its original state by the rest of the malicious payload. `[Ref: Lazarus APT January 2022]` Use of the `KernelCallbackTable` to hijack execution flow may evade detection from security products since the execution can be masked under a legitimate process.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.descriptionPt: Some endpoint security solutions can be configured to block some types of behaviors related to process injection/memory tampering based on common sequences of indicators (ex: execution of specific API functions).
mitigations.bypassHint: Contornar User-Mode Hooks em `ntdll.dll` através de: (1) Indirect Syscalls (ex: Halo's Gate / Tartarus' Gate / SysWhispers3 saltando para a instrução `syscall` dentro da própria `ntdll.dll` para legitimar a Call Stack); (2) Remapeamento de cópia limpa de `ntdll.dll` a partir de `KnownDlls` ou processo suspenso; (3) Uso de Threadless Injection, Module Stomping ou Callback-based Injection em vez de APIs clássicas monitorizadas; (4) Patching de ETW (`EtwEventWrite`) no processo atual.

techniques.fullNamePt: Sequestro de Fluxo de Execução (Execution Flow Hijacking): AppDomainManager
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem executar their own malicious payloads by hijacking how the .NET `AppDomainManager` loads assemblies. The .NET framework uses the `AppDomainManager` class to create and manage one or more isolated runtime environments (called application domains) inside a process to host the execution of .NET applications. Assemblies (`.exe` or `.dll` binaries compiled to run as .NET code) may be loaded into an application domain as executable code. `[Ref: Microsoft App Domains]` 

Known as "AppDomainManager injection," adversaries may execute código arbitrário by hijacking how .NET applications load assemblies. Por exemplo, malware may create a custom application domain inside a target process to load and execute an arbitrary assembly. Alternatively, ficheiros de configuração (`.config`) or process variáveis de ambiente that define .NET runtime settings may be tampered with to instruct otherwise benign .NET applications to load a malicious assembly (identified by name) into the target process. `[Ref: PenTestLabs AppDomainManagerInject]` `[Ref: PwC Yellow Liderc]` `[Ref: Rapid7 AppDomain Manager Injection]`

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Install .NET applications and related software in write-protected locations. Set directory access controls to prevent file writes to the search paths for .NET applications, both in the folders where applications are run from and the standard resources folders.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

Defenders may observe suspicious creation of new AppDomains within trusted processes, anomalous loading of assemblies via non-standard ficheiros de configuração, or registry/environment variable changes redirecting AppDomainManager to malicious assemblies. Correlated events include config file tampering, new process creation of .NET host processes (e.g., w3wp.exe, powershell.exe) with modified runtime parameters, and module loads of unusual or unsigned .NET DLLs.

techniques.namePt: Modificação de Infraestrutura de Computação Cloud
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Infraestrutura de Computação Cloud
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode attempt to modify a cloud account's compute service infrastructure to evade defenses. A modification to the compute service infrastructure can include the creation, deletion, or modification of one or more components such as compute instances, máquina virtual (VM)s, and snapshots.

Permissions gained from the modification of infrastructure components may bypass restrictions that prevent access to existing infrastructure. Modifying infrastructure components may also allow an adversary para evadir deteção and remove evidence of their presence. `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2020]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit permissions for creating, deleting, and otherwise altering compute components in accordance with least privilege. Organizations should limit the number of users within the organization with an IAM role that has privilégios administrativos, strive to reduce all permanent privileged role assignments, and conduct periodic entitlement reviews on IAM users, roles and policies. `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2020]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Routinely monitor user permissions to ensure only the expected users have the capability to modify cloud compute infrastructure components.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure

analytics.name: Analytic 0861
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection focuses on identifying unauthorized or anomalous changes to compute infrastructure components. Defender perspective: monitor for creation, deletion, or modification of instances, volumes, and snapshots outside of approved change management windows; correlate abnormal activity such as rapid snapshot creation followed by new instance mounts, or repeated infrastructure changes by rarely used accounts. Flagging activity linked to unusual geolocation, API client, or automation script is suspicious.

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Snapshot
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Infraestrutura de Computação Cloud: Create Snapshot
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode create a snapshot or data backup within a cloud account to evade defenses. A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of an existing cloud compute component such as a máquina virtual (VM) (VM), virtual hard drive, or volume. Um adversário pode leverage permissions to create a snapshot com o objetivo de bypass restrictions that prevent access to existing compute service infrastructure, unlike in **Revert Cloud Instance** (`T1578.004`) where an adversary may revert to a snapshot para evadir deteção and remove evidence of their presence.

Um adversário pode **Create Cloud Instance** (`T1578.002`), mount one or more created snapshots to that instance, and then apply a policy that allows the adversary access to the created instance, such as a firewall policy that allows them inbound and outbound SSH access. `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2020]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Routinely check user permissions to ensure only the expected users have the capability to create snapshots and backups.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit permissions for creating snapshots or backups in accordance with least privilege. Organizations should limit the number of users within the organization with an IAM role that has privilégios administrativos, strive to reduce all permanent privileged role assignments, and conduct periodic entitlement reviews on IAM users, roles and policies. `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2020]`

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Snapshot

analytics.name: Analytic 1187
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection focuses on correlating snapshot creation events with subsequent instance creation and mounting activities. From a defender perspective, suspicious sequences include snapshot creation by unexpected or newly created IAM users, snapshots created from sensitive volumes without preceding change-control activity, or snapshots immediately followed by mounting to unauthorized instances. Cross-referencing with user behavior, IP geolocation, and automation context helps distinguish benign backup operations from adversary-driven snapshot exploitation.

Frequency of snapshot creation in a defined period. Adjusted for environments with frequent automated backups.
Unusual regions or IPs from which snapshot creation API calls originate. Helps identify cross-region snapshot abuse.
Tagging or classification of volumes being snapshotted. Tuned to prioritize alerts when sensitive volumes are copied.

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Cloud Instance
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Infraestrutura de Computação Cloud: Create Cloud Instance
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode create a new instance or máquina virtual (VM) (VM) within the compute service of a cloud account to evade defenses. Creating a new instance may allow an adversary para contornar (bypass) firewall rules and permissions that exist on instances currently residing within an account. Um adversário pode **Create Snapshot** (`T1578.001`) of one or more volumes in an account, create a new instance, mount the snapshots, and then apply a less restrictive security policy to collect **Data from Local System** (`T1005`) or for **Remote Data Staging** (`T1074.002`). `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2020]`

Creating a new instance may also allow an adversary to carry out malicious activity dentro do ambiente alvo without affecting the execution of current running instances.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Routinely check user permissions to ensure only the expected users have the capability to create new instances.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit permissions for creating new instances in accordance with least privilege. Organizations should limit the number of users within the organization with an IAM role that has privilégios administrativos, strive to reduce all permanent privileged role assignments, and conduct periodic entitlement reviews on IAM users, roles and policies. `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2020]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Infraestrutura de Computação Cloud: Delete Cloud Instance

Um adversário pode delete a cloud instance after they have performed malicious activities in an attempt para evadir deteção and remove evidence of their presence.  Deleting an instance or máquina virtual (VM) can remove valuable forensic artifacts and other evidence of suspicious behavior if the instance is not recoverable.

Um adversário pode also **Create Cloud Instance** (`T1578.002`) and later terminate the instance after achieving their objectives. `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2020]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Revert Cloud Instance
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Infraestrutura de Computação Cloud: Revert Cloud Instance
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode revert changes made to a cloud instance after they have performed malicious activities in attempt para evadir deteção and remove evidence of their presence. In highly virtualized environments, such as cloud-based infrastructure, this may be accomplished by restoring máquina virtual (VM) (VM) or data storage snapshots through the cloud management dashboard or cloud APIs.

Another variation of this technique is to utilize temporary storage attached to the compute instance. Most cloud providers provide various types of storage including persistent, local, and/or ephemeral, with the ephemeral types often reset upon stop/restart of the VM. `[Ref: Tech Republic - Restore AWS Snapshots]` `[Ref: Google - Restore Cloud Snapshot]`

analytics.name: Analytic 0953
analytics.descriptionPt: Defenders can detect suspicious reversion of cloud compute instances by monitoring for unusual snapshot restores, rollback actions, or ephemeral storage resets that occur outside expected administrative workflows. From a defender’s perspective, relevant detection chains include: a snapshot restore triggered by a new or rarely used account, a sequence of snapshot creation immediately followed by a restore and instance start, or rollbacks performed from anomalous geographic or network locations. These patterns may indicate attempts to remove forensic evidence or re-establish a clean execution state for persistence.

mutableElements.description: Identity of the user or service account performing rollback actions; tuned to exclude automation or approved workflows.
Threshold for correlating snapshot creation followed by reversion within minutes; tuned to environment activity norms.
Region or source IP where the revert request originated; tuned to align with enterprise cloud geography.
Use of administrative tags or headers to distinguish legitimate restores from malicious activity.

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Modify Cloud Compute Configurations
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Infraestrutura de Computação Cloud: Modify Cloud Compute Configurations
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar settings that directly affect the size, locations, and resources available to cloud compute infrastructure com o objetivo de evade defenses. These settings may include service quotas, subscription associations, tenant-wide policies, or other configurations that impact available compute. Such modifications may allow adversaries to abuse the victim’s compute resources to achieve their goals, potentially without affecting the execution of running instances and/or revealing their activities to the victim.

Por exemplo, cloud providers often limit customer usage of compute resources via quotas. Customers may request adjustments to these quotas to support increased computing needs, though these adjustments may require approval from the cloud provider. Adversaries who compromise a cloud environment may similarly request quota adjustments com o objetivo de support their activities, such as enabling additional **Resource Hijacking** (`T1496`) without raising suspicion by using up a victim’s entire quota. `[Ref: Microsoft Cryptojacking 2023]` Os adversários podem também increase allowed resource usage by modifying any tenant-wide policies that limit the sizes of deployed máquina virtual (VM)s. `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Policy]`

Os adversários podem também modify settings that affect where cloud resources can be deployed, such as enabling **Unused/Unsupported Cloud Regions** (`T1535`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit permissions to request quotas adjustments or modify tenant-level compute setting to only those required.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Routinely monitor user permissions to ensure only the expected users have the capability to request quota adjustments or modify tenant-level compute settings.

From a defender’s perspective, suspicious behavior chains include a sudden increase in compute quota requests followed by new instance or resource creation, policy modifications that weaken security restrictions, or enabling previously unused/unsupported cloud regions. Correlation across identity, configuration, and subsequent provisioning logs is critical to distinguish legitimate administrative activity from adversarial abuse.

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Infraestrutura Cloud
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode attempt to discover infrastructure and resources that are available within an infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) environment. This includes compute service resources such as instances, máquina virtual (VM)s, and snapshots as well as resources of other services including the storage and database services.

Cloud providers offer methods such as APIs and commands issued through CLIs to serve information about infrastructure. Por exemplo, AWS provides a `DescribeInstances` API within the Amazon EC2 API that can return information about one or more instances within an account, the `ListBuckets` API that returns a list of all buckets owned by the authenticated sender of the request, the `HeadBucket` API to determine a bucket’s existence along with access permissions of the request sender, or the `GetPublicAccessBlock` API to retrieve access block configuration for a bucket. `[Ref: Amazon Describe Instance]` `[Ref: Amazon Describe Instances API]` `[Ref: AWS Get Public Access Block]` `[Ref: AWS Head Bucket]` Similarly, GCP's Cloud SDK CLI provides the `gcloud compute instances list` command to list all Google Compute Engine instances in a project  `[Ref: Google Compute Instances]`, and Azure's CLI command `az vm list` lists details of máquina virtual (VM)s. `[Ref: Microsoft AZ CLI]` Adicionalmente a API commands, adversaries can utilize open source tools to discover cloud storage infrastructure through **Wordlist Scanning** (`T1595.003`). `[Ref: Malwarebytes OSINT Leaky Buckets - Hioureas]`

Um adversário pode enumerate resources using a compromised user's access keys to determine which are available to that user. `[Ref: Expel IO Evil in AWS]` The discovery of these available resources may help adversaries determine their next steps in the Cloud environment, such as establishing Persistence. `[Ref: Mandiant M-Trends 2020]`Um adversário pode also use this information to change the configuration to make the bucket publicly accessible, allowing data to be accessed without authentication. Adversaries have also may use infrastructure discovery APIs such as `DescribeDBInstances` to determine size, owner, permissions, and network ACLs of database resources.  `[Ref: AWS Describe DB Instances]` Adversaries can use this information to determine the potential value of databases and discover the requirements to access them. Unlike in **Cloud Service Discovery** (`T1526`), this technique focuses on the discovery of components of the provided services rather than the services themselves.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit permissions to discover cloud infrastructure in accordance with least privilege. Organizations should limit the number of users within the organization with an IAM role that has privilégios administrativos, strive to reduce all permanent privileged role assignments, and conduct periodic entitlement reviews on IAM users, roles and policies.

analytics.name: Analytic 0481

Observable behaviors include repeated listing or description operations for compute instances, snapshots, storage buckets, and volumes. From a defender’s perspective, risky activity is often identified by new or untrusted identities making discovery calls (e.g., DescribeInstances, ListBuckets, az vm list, gcloud compute instances list), enumeration from unusual geolocations or IPs, or rapid multi-service discovery in sequence. Correlating discovery API usage with later snapshot creation or instance modification provides further context of adversary behavior.

mutableElements.description: Identity performing the discovery operation; tuned to filter known administrative or inventory accounts.
Source region or IP of discovery requests; tuned to expected operational regions to detect unusual access.
Correlation period to link enumeration calls with subsequent provisioning or exfiltration activity.
Rate or volume of discovery calls; tuned to suppress noise from inventory management tools.

techniques.fullNamePt: Aquisição de Infraestrutura
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem buy, lease, rent, or obtain infrastructure that can be used during targeting. A wide variety of infrastructure exists for hosting and orchestrating adversary operations. Infrastructure solutions include physical or cloud servers, domains, and third-party web services. `[Ref: TrendmicroHideoutsLease]` Some infrastructure providers offer free trial periods, enabling infrastructure acquisition at limited to no cost. `[Ref: Free Trial PurpleUrchin]` Additionally, botnets are available for rent or purchase.

Use of these infrastructure solutions allows adversaries to stage, launch, and execute operations. Solutions may help adversary operations blend in with traffic that is seen as normal, such as contacting third-party web services or acquiring infrastructure to support **Proxy** (`T1090`), including from residential proxy services. `[Ref: amnesty_nso_pegasus]` `[Ref: FBI Proxies Credential Stuffing]` `[Ref: Mandiant APT29 Microsoft 365 2022]` Dependendo de the implementation, adversaries may use infrastructure that makes it difficult to physically tie back to them as well as utilize infrastructure that can be rapidly provisioned, modified, and shut down.

mitigations.name: Pre-compromise
mitigations.descriptionPt: This technique cannot be easily mitigated with preventive controls since it is based on behaviors performed outside of the scope of enterprise defenses and controls.

Uma vez que adversaries have provisioned infrastructure (ex: a server for use in Command and Control (C2)), internet scans may help proactively discover adversary acquired infrastructure. Consider looking for identifiable patterns such as services listening, certificates in use, SSL/TLS negotiation features, or other response artifacts associated with adversary C2 software. `[Ref: ThreatConnect Infrastructure Dec 2020]` `[Ref: Mandiant SCANdalous Jul 2020]` `[Ref: Koczwara Beacon Hunting Sep 2021]` Detection efforts may be focused on related stages of the adversary lifecycle, such as during Command and Control (C2).
