techniques.fullNamePt: Engenharia Social e Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Link
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enviar spearphishing messages with a malicious link to elicit informação sensível that can be used during targeting. Spearphishing for information is an attempt to trick targets into divulging information, frequently credentials or other actionable information. Spearphishing for information frequently involves engenharia social techniques, such as posing as a source with a reason to collect information (ex: **Establish Accounts** (`T1585`) or **Compromise Accounts** (`T1586`)) and/or sending multiple, seemingly urgent messages.

All forms of spearphishing are electronically delivered engenharia social targeted at a specific individual, company, or industry. In this scenario, the malicious emails contain links generally accompanied by engenharia social text to coax the user to actively click or copy and paste a URL into a browser. `[Ref: TrendMictro Phishing]` `[Ref: PCMag FakeLogin]` The given website may be a clone of a legitimate site (such as an online or corporate login portal) or may closely resemble a legitimate site in appearance and have a URL containing elements from the real site. URLs may also be obfuscated by taking advantage of quirks in the URL schema, such as the acceptance of integer- or hexadecimal-based hostname formats and the automatic discarding of text before an “@” symbol: for example, `hxxp://google.com@1157586937`. `[Ref: Mandiant URL Obfuscation 2023]`

Os adversários podem também embed “tracking pixels,” "web bugs," or "web beacons" within phishing messages to verify the receipt of an email, while also potentially profiling and tracking victim information such as IP address. `[Ref: NIST Web Bug]` `[Ref: Ryte Wiki]` These mechanisms often appear as small images (typically one pixel in size) or otherwise obfuscated objects and are typically delivered as HTML code containing a link to a remote server. `[Ref: Ryte Wiki]` `[Ref: IAPP]`

Os adversários podem também be able to spoof a complete website using what is known as a "browser-in-the-browser" (BitB) attack. By generating a fake browser popup window with an HTML-based address bar that appears to contain a legitimate URL (such as an authentication portal), they may be able to prompt users to enter their credentials while bypassing typical URL verification methods. `[Ref: ZScaler BitB 2020]` `[Ref: Mr. D0x BitB 2022]`

Adversaries can use phishing kits such as `EvilProxy` and `Evilginx2` to perform adversary-in-the-middle phishing by proxying the connection between the victim and the legitimate website. On a successful login, the victim is redirected to the legitimate website, while the adversary captures their session cookie (i.e., **Steal Web Session Cookie** (`T1539`)) in addition to their username and password. This may enable the adversary to then bypass MFA via **Web Session Cookie** (`T1550.004`). `[Ref: Proofpoint Human Factor]`

Os adversários podem também send a malicious link in the form of Quick Response (QR) Codes (also known as “quishing”). These links may direct a victim to a credential phishing page. `[Ref: QR-campaign-energy-firm]` By using a QR code, the URL may not be exposed in the email and may thus go undetected by most automated email security scans. `[Ref: qr-phish-agriculture]` These QR codes may be scanned by or delivered directly  to a user’s mobile device (i.e., **Phishing** (`T1660`)), which may be less secure in several relevant ways. `[Ref: qr-phish-agriculture]` Por exemplo, mobile users may not be able to notice minor differences between genuine and credential harvesting websites due to mobile’s smaller form factor.

From the fake website, information is gathered in web forms and sent to the adversary. Os adversários podem também use information from previous reconnaissance efforts (ex: **Search Open Websites/Domains** (`T1593`) or **Search Victim-Owned Websites** (`T1594`)) to craft persuasive and believable lures.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Users can be trained to identify engenharia social techniques and spearphishing attempts. Additionally, users may perform visual checks of the domains they visit; however, homographs in ASCII and in IDN domains and URL schema obfuscation may render manual checks difficult. Phishing training and other cybersecurity training may raise awareness to check URLs before visiting the sites.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Use anti-spoofing and email authentication mechanisms to filter messages based on validity checks of the sender domain (using SPF) and integrity of messages (using DKIM). Enabling these mechanisms within an organization (through policies such as DMARC) may enable recipients (intra-org and cross domain) to perform similar message filtering and validation. `[Ref: Microsoft Anti Spoofing]` `[Ref: ACSC Email Spoofing]`

Ademais, policies may enforce / install browser extensions that protect against IDN and homograph attacks. Browser password managers may also be configured to only populate credential fields when the URL matches that of the original, legitimate site.

detections.name: Detection of Spearphishing Link

analytics.name: Analytic 2010
analytics.descriptionPt:
Monitor for suspicious email activity, such as numerous accounts receiving messages from a single unusual/unknown sender. Filtering based on DKIM+SPF or header analysis can help detect when the email sender is spoofed. `[Ref: Microsoft Anti Spoofing]` `[Ref: ACSC Email Spoofing]` Monitor for references to uncategorized or known-bad sites. URL inspection within email (including expanding shortened links and identifying obfuscated URLs) can also help detect links leading to known malicious sites. `[Ref: Mandiant URL Obfuscation 2023]`

Ademais, monitor browser logs for homographs in ASCII and in internationalized domain names abusing different character sets (e.g. Cyrillic vs Latin versions of trusted sites).
Monitor network data for uncommon data flows. Processes utilizing the network that do not normally have network communication or have never been seen before are suspicious.
Monitor and analyze traffic patterns and packet inspection associated to protocol(s), leveraging SSL/TLS inspection for encrypted traffic, that do not follow the expected protocol standards and traffic flows (e.g extraneous packets that do not belong to established flows, gratuitous or anomalous traffic patterns, anomalous syntax, or structure). Consider correlation with process monitoring and command line to detect anomalous processes execution and command line arguments associated to traffic patterns (e.g. monitor anomalies in use of files that do not normally initiate connections for respective protocol(s)).

Ademais, monitor tráfego de rede for homographs via the use of internationalized domain names abusing different character sets (e.g. Cyrillic vs Latin versions of trusted sites). Also monitor and analyze traffic patterns and packet inspection for indicators of cloned websites. Por exemplo, if adversaries use HTTrack to clone websites,  ` Mirrored from (victim URL)` may be visible in the HTML section of packets.

techniques.fullNamePt: Engenharia Social e Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar voice communications to elicit informação sensível that can be used during targeting. Spearphishing for information is an attempt to trick targets into divulging information, frequently credentials or other actionable information. Spearphishing for information frequently involves engenharia social techniques, such as posing as a source with a reason to collect information (ex: **Impersonation** (`T1684.001`)) and/or creating a sense of urgency or alarm for the recipient.

All forms of phishing are electronically delivered engenharia social. In this scenario, adversaries use phone calls to elicit informação sensível from victims. Known as voice phishing (or "vishing"), these communications can be manually executed by adversaries, hired call centers, or even automated via robocalls. Voice phishers may spoof their phone number while also posing as a trusted entity, such as a business partner or technical support staff. `[Ref: BOA Telephone Scams]`

Victims may also receive phishing messages that direct them to call a phone number ("callback phishing") where the adversary attempts to collect confidential information. `[Ref: Avertium callback phishing]`

Os adversários podem também use information from previous reconnaissance efforts (ex: **Search Open Websites/Domains** (`T1593`) or **Search Victim-Owned Websites** (`T1594`)) to tailor pretexts to be even more persuasive and believable for the victim.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Users can be trained to identify and report engenharia social techniques and spearphishing attempts, while also being suspicious of and verifying the identify of callers. `[Ref: CISA Phishing]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Transposição de Fronteiras de Rede
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem bridge network boundaries by compromising perimeter network devices or internal devices responsible for network segmentation. Breaching these devices may enable an adversary para contornar (bypass) restrictions on traffic routing that otherwise separate trusted and untrusted networks.

Devices such as routers and firewalls pode ser utilizado para create boundaries between trusted and untrusted networks.  They achieve this by restricting traffic types to enforce organizational policy in an attempt to reduce the risk inherent in such connections.  Restriction of traffic can be achieved by prohibiting IP addresses, layer 4 protocol ports, or through deep packet inspection to identify applications.  To participate with the rest of the network, these devices can be directly addressable or transparent, but their mode of operation has no bearing on how the adversary can bypass them when compromised.

When an adversary takes control of such a boundary device, they can bypass its policy enforcement to pass normally prohibited traffic across the trust boundary between the two separated networks without hinderance.  By achieving sufficient rights on the device, an adversary can reconfigure the device to allow the traffic they want, allowing them to then further achieve goals such as Command and Control (C2) via **Multi-hop Proxy** (`T1090.003`) or exfiltration of data via **Traffic Duplication** (`T1020.001`). Os adversários podem também target internal devices responsible for network segmentation and abuse these in conjunction with **Internal Proxy** (`T1090.001`) to achieve the same goals. `[Ref: Kaspersky ThreatNeedle Feb 2021]`  In the cases where a border device separates two separate organizations, the adversary can also facilitate lateral movement into new ambiente alvos.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication for user and privileged accounts. Most embedded network devices support TACACS+ and/or RADIUS.  Follow vendor prescribed best practices for hardening access control. `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - TACACS]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Refer to NIST guidelines when creating password policies.  `[Ref: NIST 800-63-3]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict administrator accounts to as few individuals as possible, following least privilege principles.  Prevent credential overlap across systems of administrator and privileged accounts, particularly between network and non-network platforms, such as servers or endpoints.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Upon identifying a compromised network device being used to bridge a network boundary, block the malicious packets using an unaffected network device in path, such as a firewall or a router that has not been compromised.  Continue to monitor for additional activity and to ensure that the blocks are indeed effective.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Credential Access Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Some embedded network devices are capable of storing passwords for local accounts in either plain-text or encrypted formats.  Ensure that, where available, local passwords are always encrypted, per vendor recommendations. `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - AAA]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Com RunAsPPL ativo, processos em User-Mode não conseguem abrir handles `PROCESS_VM_READ` no LSASS. Vetores de contorno: (1) Pivotar para extração sem tocar no LSASS: Kerberoasting (`T1558.003`), AS-REP Roasting (`T1558.004`), ou extração de segredos DPAPI/Vault (`T1555.004`); (2) Se for Domain Admin/equivalente, usar DCSync (`T1003.006`) remotamente; (3) Abusar de drivers assinados vulneráveis (BYOVD - `T1068`) como `mimidrv.sys` ou `procexp152.sys` para remover a flag `PS_PROTECTION` em Kernel-Mode; (4) Se Credential Guard (VBS) estiver ativo, hashes NTLM em cache ficam isolados em `LsaIso.exe` — contornar usando captura de Tickets Kerberos em memória via Rubeus (`monitor`/`tgtdeleg`) ou roubo de cookies de sessão browser.

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Network Boundary Bridging

analytics.name: Analytic 0015
analytics.descriptionPt: From a defender’s perspective, suspicious bridging is observed when network devices begin allowing traffic that contradicts existing segmentation or access policies. Observable behaviors include sudden modifications to ACLs or firewall rules, unusual cross-boundary traffic flows (e.g., east-west communications across separated VLANs), or simultaneous ingress/egress anomalies. Multi-event correlation is key: configuration changes on a router/firewall followed by unexpected traffic patterns, especially from unusual sources, is a strong indicator of compromise.

mutableElements.description: Correlation window between configuration changes and abnormal traffic; tuned to match expected administrative change cycles.
Known authorized ACL/firewall changes; suppresses noise from legitimate maintenance.
Geographic origin of new traffic patterns; helps distinguish benign remote offices from suspicious foreign access.
Volume of cross-segment traffic; tuned to detect large-scale lateral flows without flagging small test connections.

techniques.fullNameEn: Network Boundary Bridging: Network Address Translation Traversal
techniques.fullNamePt: Transposição de Fronteiras de Rede: Network Address Translation Traversal
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem bridge network boundaries by modifying a network device’s Network Address Translation (NAT) configuration. Malicious modifications to NAT may enable an adversary para contornar (bypass) restrictions on traffic routing that otherwise separate trusted and untrusted networks.

Network devices such as routers and firewalls that connect multiple networks together may implement NAT during the process of passing packets between networks. When performing NAT, the network device will rewrite the source and/or destination addresses of the IP address header. Some network designs require NAT for the packets to cross the border device.  A typical example of this is environments where internal networks make use of non-Internet routable addresses. `[Ref: RFC1918]`

When an adversary gains control of a network boundary device, they may modify NAT configurations to send traffic between two separated networks, or to obscure their activities.  In network designs that require NAT to function, such modifications enable the adversary to overcome inherent routing limitations that would normally prevent them from accessing protected systems behind the border device.  In network designs that do not require NAT, adversaries may use address translation to further obscure their activities, as changing the addresses of packets that traverse a network boundary device can make monitoring data transmissions more challenging for defenders.  

Os adversários podem utilizar **Patch System Image** (`T1601.001`) to change the sistema operativo of a network device, implementing their own custom NAT mechanisms to further obscure their activities.

analytics.name: Analytic 0465
analytics.descriptionPt: Defenders may observe unauthorized or anomalous changes to NAT configurations, including the addition of new translation rules or modifications to existing ones. Suspicious behaviors include sudden introduction of NAT mappings bridging segmented networks, new port address translation rules that obscure true source IPs, or traffic flows inconsistent with expected network design. Multi-event correlation includes detecting configuration changes on routers/firewalls, followed by traffic traversing unexpected internal/external address pairs.

mutableElements.description: Time correlation window between NAT rule change and unexpected traffic; adjustable to align with change management practices.
Whitelist of approved NAT policies and rules; prevents false positives from legitimate operations.
Threshold for abnormal traffic across NAT; tuned to differentiate testing from large-scale exfiltration or bridging.
Specific interfaces or zones monitored for NAT translation; allows tuning for internal vs. external-facing boundaries.

Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).
blindSpots: **TimeWindow**: Time correlation window between NAT rule change and unexpected traffic; adjustable to align with change management practices.
**AuthorizedNATRules**: Whitelist of approved NAT policies and rules; prevents false positives from legitimate operations.
**TrafficVolumeThreshold**: Threshold for abnormal traffic across NAT; tuned to differentiate testing from large-scale exfiltration or bridging.
**InterfaceScope**: Specific interfaces or zones monitored for NAT translation; allows tuning for internal vs. external-facing boundaries.

techniques.fullNamePt: Enfraquecimento de Encriptação
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem comprometer a network device’s encryption capability com o objetivo de bypass encryption that would otherwise protect data communications. `[Ref: Cisco Synful Knock Evolution]`

Encryption pode ser utilizado para protect transmitted tráfego de rede to maintain its confidentiality (protect against unauthorized disclosure) and integrity (protect against unauthorized changes). Encryption ciphers são utilizados para convert a plaintext message to ciphertext and can be computationally intensive to decipher without the associated decryption key. Typically, longer keys increase the cost of cryptanalysis, or decryption without the key.

Adversaries can compromise and manipulate devices that perform encryption of tráfego de rede. Por exemplo, through behaviors such as **Modify System Image** (`T1601`), **Reduce Key Space** (`T1600.001`), and **Disable Crypto Hardware** (`T1600.002`), an adversary can negatively effect and/or eliminate a device’s ability to securely encrypt tráfego de rede. This poses a greater risk of unauthorized disclosure and may help facilitate data manipulation, Credential Access, or Collection efforts. `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Weaken Encryption on Network Devices

analytics.name: Analytic 0961
analytics.descriptionPt: Defenders may observe unauthorized modifications to encryption-related ficheiros de configuração, firmware, or crypto modules on network devices. Suspicious patterns include changes to cipher suite configurations, unexpected firmware updates affecting crypto libraries, disabling of hardware cryptographic accelerators, or reductions in key length policies. Correlating configuration changes with anomalies in encrypted traffic characteristics (e.g., weaker ciphers or sudden plaintext transmission) strengthens detection.

logSources.channel: Configuration change events referencing encryption, TLS/SSL, or IPSec settings

logSources.name: NSM:Flow
logSources.channel: Traffic patterns showing downgrade from strong encryption (AES-256) to weaker or plaintext protocols

logSources.channel: Status change in cryptographic hardware modules (enabled -> disabled)

techniques.fullNamePt: Enfraquecimento de Encriptação: Reduce Key Space
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem reduce the level of effort required to decrypt data transmitted over the network by reducing the cipher strength of encrypted communications. `[Ref: Cisco Synful Knock Evolution]`

Adversaries can weaken the encryption software on a compromised network device by reducing the key size used by the software to convert plaintext to ciphertext (e.g., from hundreds or thousands of bytes to just a couple of bytes). Como resultado, adversaries dramatically reduce the amount of effort needed to decrypt the protected information without the key.

Os adversários podem modificar the key size used and other encryption parameters using specialized commands in a **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) introduced to the system through **Modify System Image** (`T1601`) to change the configuration of the device.  `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Weaken Encryption: Reduce Key Space on Network Devices

analytics.name: Analytic 0681
analytics.descriptionPt: Defenders may observe attempts to alter cryptographic settings on network devices that reduce key strength or allowable cipher suites. Suspicious indicators include configuration changes that downgrade encryption algorithms, key length parameters, or the disabling of strong encryption in favor of legacy ciphers. These activities often appear as CLI commands modifying crypto policies, firmware changes affecting crypto libraries, or unexpected updates to key management files. Correlation across device config logs and traffic analysis showing weaker ciphers provides higher confidence of malicious key space reduction.

techniques.fullNamePt: Enfraquecimento de Encriptação: Disable Crypto Hardware
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries disable a network device’s dedicated hardware encryption, which may enable them to leverage weaknesses in software encryption com o objetivo de reduce the effort involved in collecting, manipulating, and exfiltrating transmitted data.

Many network devices such as routers, switches, and firewalls, perform encryption on tráfego de rede to secure transmission across networks. Often, these devices are equipped with special, dedicated encryption hardware to greatly increase the speed of the encryption process as well as to prevent malicious tampering. When an adversary takes control of such a device, they may disable the dedicated hardware, for example, through use of **Modify System Image** (`T1601`), forcing the use of software to perform encryption on general processors. This is typically used in conjunction with attacks to weaken the strength of the cipher in software (e.g., **Reduce Key Space** (`T1600.001`)).  `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`

analytics.descriptionPt: Defenders may observe attempts to disable dedicated crypto hardware on network devices, often visible through anomalous CLI commands, unexpected firmware or configuration updates, and degraded encryption performance. Suspicious indicators include commands that alter hardware acceleration settings (e.g., disabling AES-NI or crypto engines), modification of system image files, or logs showing fallback from hardware to software encryption. Network traffic analysis may also reveal a sudden downgrade in throughput or cipher negotiation behavior consistent with the absence of hardware acceleration.

techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Imagem do Sistema
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem make changes to the sistema operativo of embedded network devices to weaken defenses and provide new capabilities for themselves.  On such devices, the sistema operativos are typically monolithic and most of the device functionality and capabilities are contained within a single file. `[Ref: Cisco Networking Software Product Lines]` `[Ref: Network Device Integrity Methodology]`

To change the sistema operativo, the adversary typically only needs to affect this one file, replacing or modifying it.  This can either be done live in memory during system runtime for immediate effect, or in storage to implement the change on the next boot of the network device.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use multi-factor authentication for user and privileged accounts. Most embedded network devices support TACACS+ and/or RADIUS.  Follow vendor prescribed best practices for hardening access control. `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - TACACS]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Refer to NIST guidelines when creating password policies.  `[Ref: NIST 800-63-3]`

mitigations.name: Credential Access Protection
mitigations.descriptionPt: Some embedded network devices are capable of storing passwords for local accounts in either plain-text or encrypted formats.  Ensure that, where available, local passwords are always encrypted, per vendor recommendations.  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - Credentials Management]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Com RunAsPPL ativo, processos em User-Mode não conseguem abrir handles `PROCESS_VM_READ` no LSASS. Vetores de contorno: (1) Pivotar para extração sem tocar no LSASS: Kerberoasting (`T1558.003`), AS-REP Roasting (`T1558.004`), ou extração de segredos DPAPI/Vault (`T1555.004`); (2) Se for Domain Admin/equivalente, usar DCSync (`T1003.006`) remotamente; (3) Abusar de drivers assinados vulneráveis (BYOVD - `T1068`) como `mimidrv.sys` ou `procexp152.sys` para remover a flag `PS_PROTECTION` em Kernel-Mode; (4) Se Credential Guard (VBS) estiver ativo, hashes NTLM em cache ficam isolados em `LsaIso.exe` — contornar usando captura de Tickets Kerberos em memória via Rubeus (`monitor`/`tgtdeleg`) ou roubo de cookies de sessão browser.

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.descriptionPt: Many vendors provide digitally signed sistema operativo images to validate the integrity of the software used on their platform.  Make use of this feature where possible com o objetivo de prevent and/or detect attempts by adversaries to compromise the system image.  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - Deploy Signed IOS]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Recorrer a DLL Side-Loading (`T1574.002`) utilizando um executável legítimo assinado (vulnerável a sequestro de ordem de procura de DLL) que carregue a nossa DLL em memória, ou utilizar binários assinados nativos (LOLBAS - `T1218`). Em Kernel-Mode, usar técnica BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) com um driver legítimo assinado pela Microsoft/fabricante que contenha primitivas de escrita arbitrária em kernel.

mitigations.name: Boot Integrity
mitigations.descriptionPt: Some vendors of embedded network devices provide cryptographic signing to ensure the integrity of sistema operativo images at boot time.  Implementar where available, following vendor guidelines.  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Software Integrity Assurance - Secure Boot]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict administrator accounts to as few individuals as possible, following least privilege principles.  Prevent credential overlap across systems of administrator and privileged accounts, particularly between network and non-network platforms, such as servers or endpoints.

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify System Image: Patch System Image
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Imagem do Sistema: Patch System Image
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar the sistema operativo of a network device to introduce new capabilities or weaken existing defenses. `[Ref: Killing the myth of Cisco IOS rootkits]`  `[Ref: Killing IOS diversity myth]`  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Shellcode]`  `[Ref: Cisco IOS Forensics Developments]`  `[Ref: Juniper Netscreen of the Dead]` Some network devices are built with a monolithic architecture, where the entire sistema operativo and most of the functionality of the device is contained within a single file.  Os adversários podem change this file in storage, to be loaded in a future boot, or in memory during runtime.

To change the sistema operativo in storage, the adversary will typically use the standard procedures available to device operators. This may involve downloading a new file via typical protocols used on network devices, such as TFTP, FTP, SCP, or a console connection.  The original file may be overwritten, or a new file may be written alongside of it and the device reconfigured to boot to the compromised image.

To change the sistema operativo in memory, the adversary typically can use one of two methods. In the first, the adversary would make use of native debug commands in the original, unaltered running sistema operativo that allow them to directly modify the relevant memory addresses containing the running sistema operativo.  This method typically requires administrative level access to the device.

In the second method for changing the sistema operativo in memory, the adversary would make use of the boot loader. The boot loader is the first piece of software that loads when the device starts that, in turn, will launch the sistema operativo.  Os adversários podem utilizar código malicioso previously implanted in the boot loader, such as through the **ROMMONkit** (`T1542.004`) method, to directly manipulate running sistema operativo code in memory.  This código malicioso in the bootloader provides the capability of direct memory manipulation to the adversary, allowing them to patch the live sistema operativo during runtime.

By modifying the instructions stored in the system image file, adversaries may either weaken existing defenses or provision new capabilities that the device did not have before. Examples of existing defenses that can be impeded include encryption, via **Weaken Encryption** (`T1600`), authentication, via **Network Device Authentication** (`T1556.004`), and perimeter defenses, via **Network Boundary Bridging** (`T1599`).  Adding new capabilities for the adversary’s purpose include **Keylogging** (`T1056.001`), **Multi-hop Proxy** (`T1090.003`), and **Port Knocking** (`T1205.001`).

Os adversários podem também compromise existing commands in the sistema operativo to produce false output to mislead defenders.   When this method is used in conjunction with **Downgrade System Image** (`T1601.002`), one example of a compromised system command may include changing the output of the command that shows the version of the currently running sistema operativo.  By patching the sistema operativo, the adversary can change this command to instead display the original, higher revision number that they replaced through the system downgrade. 

When the sistema operativo is patched in storage, this can be achieved in either the resident storage (typically a form of flash memory, which is non-volatile) or via **TFTP Boot** (`T1542.005`). 

When the technique is performed on the running sistema operativo in memory and not on the stored copy, this technique will not survive across reboots.  Contudo, live memory modification of the sistema operativo can be combined with **ROMMONkit** (`T1542.004`) to achieve persistence.

techniques.fullNameEn: Modify System Image: Downgrade System Image
techniques.fullNamePt: Modificação de Imagem do Sistema: Downgrade System Image
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem install an older version of the sistema operativo of a network device to weaken security.  Older sistema operativo versions on network devices often have weaker encryption ciphers and, in general, fewer/less updated defensive features.  `[Ref: Cisco Synful Knock Evolution]`

On embedded devices, downgrading the version typically only requires replacing the sistema operativo file in storage.  With most embedded devices, this can be achieved by downloading a copy of the desired version of the sistema operativo file and reconfiguring the device to boot from that file on next system restart.  The adversary could then restart the device to implement the change immediately or they could wait until the next time the system restarts.

Downgrading the system image to an older versions may allow an adversary to evade defenses by enabling behaviors such as **Weaken Encryption** (`T1600`).  Downgrading of a system image can be done on its own, or it can be used in conjunction with **Patch System Image** (`T1601.001`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Dados de Repositório de Configuração
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem recolher data related to managed devices from configuration repositories. Configuration repositories are used by management systems com o objetivo de configure, manage, and control data on sistemas remotos. Configuration repositories may also facilitate remote access and administration of devices.

Os adversários podem target these repositories com o objetivo de collect large quantities of sensitive system administration data. Data from configuration repositories may be exposed by various protocols and software and can store a wide variety of data, much of which may align with adversary Discovery objectives. `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` `[Ref: US-CERT TA17-156A SNMP Abuse 2017]`

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.descriptionPt: Keep system images and software updated and migrate to SNMPv3. `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Allowlist MIB objects and implement SNMP views. `[Ref: Cisco Securing SNMP]`

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Segregate SNMP traffic on a separate management network. `[Ref: US-CERT TA17-156A SNMP Abuse 2017]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Apply extended ACLs to block unauthorized protocols outside the trusted network. `[Ref: US-CERT TA17-156A SNMP Abuse 2017]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar intrusion prevention devices to detect SNMP queries and commands from unauthorized sources. `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar SNMPv3 to use the highest level of security (authPriv) available. `[Ref: US-CERT TA17-156A SNMP Abuse 2017]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Data from Configuration Repository: SNMP (MIB Dump)
techniques.fullNamePt: Dados de Repositório de Configuração: SNMP (MIB Dump)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem target the Management Information Base (MIB) to collect and/or mine valuable information in a network managed using Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP).

The MIB is a configuration repository that stores variable information accessible via SNMP in the form of object identifiers (OID). Each OID identifies a variable that can be read or set and permits active management tasks, such as configuration changes, through remote modification of these variables. SNMP can give administrators great insight in their systems, such as, system information, description of hardware, physical location, and software packages `[Ref: SANS Information Security Reading Room Securing SNMP Securing SNMP]`. The MIB may also contain device operational information, including running configuration, routing table, and interface details.

Os adversários podem utilizar SNMP queries to collect MIB content directly from SNMP-managed devices com o objetivo de collect network information that allows the adversary to build network maps and facilitate future targeted exploitation. `[Ref: US-CERT-TA18-106A]` `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Data from Configuration Repository: Network Device Configuration Dump
techniques.fullNamePt: Dados de Repositório de Configuração: Network Device Configuration Dump
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem access network ficheiros de configuração to collect dados sensíveis about the device and the network. The network configuration is a file containing parameters that determine the operation of the device. The device typically stores an in-memory copy of the configuration while operating, and a separate configuration on non-volatile storage to load after device reset. Adversaries can inspect the ficheiros de configuração to reveal information about the rede alvo and its layout, the network device and its software, or identifying legitimate accounts and credentials for later use.

Adversaries can use common management tools and protocols, such as Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) and Smart Install (SMI), to access network ficheiros de configuração. `[Ref: US-CERT TA18-106A Network Infrastructure Devices 2018]` `[Ref: Cisco Blog Legacy Device Attacks]` These tools pode ser empregue para query specific data from a configuration repository or configure the device to export the configuration for later analysis.

techniques.fullNamePt: Falsificação de Credenciais Web
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem forjar material de credenciaiss that pode ser utilizado para gain access to web applications or Internet services. Web applications and services (hosted in cloud SaaS environments or on-premise servers) often use session cookies, tokens, or other materials to authenticate and authorize user access.

Os adversários podem generate these material de credenciaiss com o objetivo de gain access to web resources. This differs from **Steal Web Session Cookie** (`T1539`), **Steal Application Access Token** (`T1528`), and other similar behaviors in that the credentials are new and forged by the adversary, rather than stolen or intercepted from legitimate users.

The generation of web credentials often requires secret values, such as passwords, **Private Keys** (`T1552.004`), or other cryptographic seed values. `[Ref: GitHub AWS-ADFS-Credential-Generator]` Os adversários podem também forge tokens by taking advantage of features such as the `AssumeRole` and `GetFederationToken` APIs in AWS, which allow users to request temporary security credentials (i.e., **Temporary Elevated Cloud Access** (`T1548.005`)), or the `zmprov gdpak` command in Zimbra, which generates a pre-authentication key that pode ser utilizado para generate tokens for any user in the domain. `[Ref: AWS Temporary Security Credentials]` `[Ref: Zimbra Preauth]`

Uma vez que forged, adversaries may use these web credentials to access resources (ex: **Use Alternate Authentication Material** (`T1550`)), which may bypass multi-factor and other authentication protection mechanisms. `[Ref: Pass The Cookie]` `[Ref: Unit 42 Mac Crypto Cookies January 2019]` `[Ref: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict permissions and access to the AD FS server to only originate from privileged access workstations. `[Ref: FireEye ADFS]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar browsers/applications to regularly delete persistent web credentials (such as cookies).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Administrators should perform an audit of all access lists and the permissions they have been granted to access web applications and services. This should be done extensively on all resources com o objetivo de establish a baseline, followed up on with periodic audits of new or updated resources. Suspicious accounts/credentials should be investigated and removed.
 
Enable advanced auditing on ADFS. Check the success and failure audit options in the ADFS Management snap-in. Enable Auditar regularmente Application Generated events on the AD FS farm via Group Policy Object. `[Ref: FireEye ADFS]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que user accounts with administrative rights follow best practices, including use of privileged access workstations, Just in Time/Just Enough Administration (JIT/JEA), and strong authentication. Reduce the number of users that are members of highly privileged Directory Roles. `[Ref: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance]` In AWS environments, prohibit users from calling the `sts:GetFederationToken` API unless explicitly required. `[Ref: Crowdstrike AWS User Federation Persistence]`

These events often correlate with sudden logon sessions from unfamiliar IP addresses or regions. The chain is usually secret material misuse (stolen private key or password) → API request generating a new token → access to high-value resources.

techniques.fullNamePt: Falsificação de Credenciais Web: Web Cookies
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem forjar web cookies that pode ser utilizado para gain access to web applications or Internet services. Web applications and services (hosted in cloud SaaS environments or on-premise servers) often use session cookies to authenticate and authorize user access.

Os adversários podem generate these cookies com o objetivo de gain access to web resources. This differs from **Steal Web Session Cookie** (`T1539`) and other similar behaviors in that the cookies are new and forged by the adversary, rather than stolen or intercepted from legitimate users. Most common web applications have standardized and documented cookie values that can be generated using provided tools or interfaces. `[Ref: Pass The Cookie]` The generation of web cookies often requires secret values, such as passwords, **Private Keys** (`T1552.004`), or other cryptographic seed values.

Uma vez que forged, adversaries may use these web cookies to access resources (**Web Session Cookie** (`T1550.004`)), which may bypass multi-factor and other authentication protection mechanisms. `[Ref: Volexity SolarWinds]` `[Ref: Pass The Cookie]` `[Ref: Unit 42 Mac Crypto Cookies January 2019]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Falsificação de Credenciais Web: SAML Tokens
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode forge SAML tokens with any permissions claims and lifetimes if they possess a valid SAML token-signing certificate. `[Ref: Microsoft SolarWinds Steps]` The default lifetime of a SAML token is one hour, but the validity period can be specified in the `NotOnOrAfter` value of the `conditions ...` element in a token. This value can be changed using the `AccessTokenLifetime` in a `LifetimeTokenPolicy`. `[Ref: Microsoft SAML Token Lifetimes]` Forged SAML tokens enable adversaries to authenticate across services that use SAML 2.0 as an SSO (single sign-on) mechanism. `[Ref: Cyberark Golden SAML]`

Um adversário pode utilize **Private Keys** (`T1552.004`) to compromise an organization's token-signing certificate to create forged SAML tokens. If the adversary has sufficient permissions to establish a new federation trust with their own Active Directory (AD) Federation Services (AD FS) server, they may instead generate their own trusted token-signing certificate. `[Ref: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance]` This differs from **Steal Application Access Token** (`T1528`) and other similar behaviors in that the tokens are new and forged by the adversary, rather than stolen or intercepted from legitimate users.

Um adversário pode gain administrative Entra ID privileges if a SAML token is forged which claims to represent a highly privileged account. This may lead to **Use Alternate Authentication Material** (`T1550`), which may bypass multi-factor and other authentication protection mechanisms. `[Ref: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance]`

mitigations.name: Active Directory Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: For containing the impact of a previously forged SAML token, rotate the token-signing AD FS certificate in rapid succession twice, which will invalidate any tokens generated using the previous certificate. `[Ref: Mandiant Defend UNC2452 White Paper]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable advanced auditing on AD FS. Check the success and failure audit options in the AD FS Management snap-in. Enable Auditar regularmente Application Generated events on the AD FS farm via Group Policy Object. `[Ref: FireEye ADFS]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que user accounts with administrative rights follow best practices, including use of privileged access workstations, Just in Time/Just Enough Administration (JIT/JEA), and strong authentication. Reduce the number of users that are members of highly privileged Directory Roles. `[Ref: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict permissions and access to the AD FS server to only originate from privileged access workstations. `[Ref: FireEye ADFS]`

Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Hospedagem e Preparação de Capacidades
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem upload, install, or otherwise set up capabilities that can be used during targeting. To support their operations, an adversary may need to take capabilities they developed (**Develop Capabilities** (`T1587`)) or obtained (**Obtain Capabilities** (`T1588`)) and stage them on infrastructure under their control. These capabilities may be staged on infrastructure that was previously purchased/rented by the adversary (**Acquire Infrastructure** (`T1583`)) or was otherwise compromised by them (**Compromise Infrastructure** (`T1584`)). Capabilities may also be staged on web services, such as GitHub or Pastebin, or on Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) offerings that enable users to easily provision applications. `[Ref: Volexity Ocean Lotus November 2020]` `[Ref: Dragos Heroku Watering Hole]` `[Ref: Malwarebytes Heroku Skimmers]` `[Ref: Netskope GCP Redirection]` `[Ref: Netskope Cloud Phishing]`

Staging of capabilities can aid the adversary in a number of initial access and post-compromise behaviors, including (but not limited to):

* Staging web resources necessary to conduct **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`) when a user browses to a site. `[Ref: FireEye CFR Watering Hole 2012]` `[Ref: Gallagher 2015]` `[Ref: ATT ScanBox]`
* Staging web resources for a link target to be used with spearphishing. `[Ref: Malwarebytes Silent Librarian October 2020]` `[Ref: Proofpoint TA407 September 2019]`
* Uploading malware or tools to a location accessible to a victim network to enable **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`). `[Ref: Volexity Ocean Lotus November 2020]`
* Installing a previously acquired SSL/TLS certificate to use to encrypt Command and Control (C2) traffic (ex: **Asymmetric Cryptography** (`T1573.002`) with **Web Protocols** (`T1071.001`)). `[Ref: DigiCert Install SSL Cert]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Hospedagem e Preparação de Capacidades: Upload Malware
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem upload malware to third-party or adversary controlled infrastructure to make it accessible during targeting. Malicious software can include payloads, droppers, post-compromise tools, backdoors, and a variety of other malicious content. Os adversários podem upload malware to support their operations, such as making a payload available to a victim network to enable **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`) by placing it on an Internet accessible web server.

Malware may be placed on infrastructure that was previously purchased/rented by the adversary (**Acquire Infrastructure** (`T1583`)) or was otherwise compromised by them (**Compromise Infrastructure** (`T1584`)). Malware can also be staged on web services, such as GitHub or Pastebin; hosted on the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS), where decentralized content storage makes the removal of malicious files difficult; or saved on the blockchain as smart contracts, which are resilient against takedowns that would affect traditional infrastructure. `[Ref: Volexity Ocean Lotus November 2020]` `[Ref: Talos IPFS 2022]` `[Ref: Guardio Etherhiding 2023]` `[Ref: Bleeping Computer Binance Smart Chain 2023]`

Os adversários podem upload backdoored files, such as software packages, application binaries, máquina virtual (VM) images, or container images, to third-party software stores, package libraries, extension marketplaces, or repositories (ex: GitHub, CNET, AWS Community AMIs, Docker Hub, PyPi, NPM). `[Ref: Datadog Security Labs Malicious PyPi Packages 2024]` By chance encounter, victims may directly download/install these backdoored files via **User Execution** (`T1204`). Masquerading, including typosquatting legitimate software, may increase the chance of users mistakenly executing these files.

techniques.fullNamePt: Hospedagem e Preparação de Capacidades: Upload Tool
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem upload tools to third-party or adversary controlled infrastructure to make it accessible during targeting. Tools can be open or closed source, free or commercial. Tools can be used for malicious purposes by an adversary, but (unlike malware) were not intended to be used for those purposes (ex: **PsExec** (`S0029`)). Os adversários podem upload tools to support their operations, such as making a tool available to a victim network to enable **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`) by placing it on an Internet accessible web server.

Tools may be placed on infrastructure that was previously purchased/rented by the adversary (**Acquire Infrastructure** (`T1583`)) or was otherwise compromised by them (**Compromise Infrastructure** (`T1584`)). `[Ref: Dell TG-3390]` Tools can also be staged on web services, such as an adversary controlled GitHub repo, or on Platform-as-a-Service offerings that enable users to easily provision applications. `[Ref: Dragos Heroku Watering Hole]` `[Ref: Malwarebytes Heroku Skimmers]` `[Ref: Intezer App Service Phishing]`

Adversaries can avoid the need to upload a tool by having compromised victim machines download the tool directly from a third-party hosting location (ex: a non-adversary controlled GitHub repo), including the original hosting site of the tool.

techniques.fullNamePt: Hospedagem e Preparação de Capacidades: Install Digital Certificate
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem install SSL/TLS certificates that can be used during targeting. SSL/TLS certificates are files that can be installed on servers to enable secure communications between systems. Digital certificates include information about the key, information about its owner's identity, and the digital signature of an entity that has verified the certificate's contents are correct. If the signature is valid, and the person examining the certificate trusts the signer, then they know they can use that key to communicate securely with its owner. Certificates can be uploaded to a server, then the server can be configured to use the certificate to enable encrypted communication with it. `[Ref: DigiCert Install SSL Cert]`

Os adversários podem install SSL/TLS certificates that pode ser utilizado para further their operations, such as encrypting C2 traffic (ex: **Asymmetric Cryptography** (`T1573.002`) with **Web Protocols** (`T1071.001`)) or lending credibility to a credential harvesting site. Installation of digital certificates may take place for a number of server types, including web servers and email servers. 

Adversaries can obtain digital certificates (see **Digital Certificates** (`T1588.004`)) or create self-signed certificates (see **Digital Certificates** (`T1587.003`)). Digital certificates can then be installed on adversary controlled infrastructure that may have been acquired (**Acquire Infrastructure** (`T1583`)) or previously compromised (**Compromise Infrastructure** (`T1584`)).

techniques.fullNamePt: Hospedagem e Preparação de Capacidades: Drive-by Target
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem prepare an operational environment to infect systems that visit a website over the normal course of browsing. Endpoint systems may be compromised through browsing to adversary controlled sites, as in **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`). In such cases, the user's web browser is typically targeted for exploitation (often not requiring any extra user interaction once landing on the site), but adversaries may also set up websites for non-exploitation behavior such as **Application Access Token** (`T1550.001`). Prior to **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`), adversaries must stage resources needed to deliver that exploit to users who browse to an adversary controlled site. Drive-by content can be staged on adversary controlled infrastructure that has been acquired (**Acquire Infrastructure** (`T1583`)) or previously compromised (**Compromise Infrastructure** (`T1584`)).

Os adversários podem upload or inject malicious web content, such as **JavaScript** (`T1059.007`), into websites. `[Ref: FireEye CFR Watering Hole 2012]` `[Ref: Gallagher 2015]` This may be done in a number of ways, including:

* Inserting malicious scripts into web pages or other user controllable web content such as forum posts
* Modifying script files served to websites from publicly writeable cloud storage buckets
* Crafting malicious web advertisements and purchasing ad space on a website through legitimate ad providers (i.e., **Malvertising** (`T1583.008`))

Adicionalmente a staging content to exploit a user's web browser, adversaries may also stage scripting content to profile the user's browser (as in **Gather Victim Host Information** (`T1592`)) to ensure it is vulnerable prior to attempting exploitation. `[Ref: ATT ScanBox]`

Websites compromised by an adversary and used to stage a drive-by may be ones visited by a specific community, such as government, a particular industry, or region, where the goal is to compromise a specific user or set of users based on a shared interest. This kind of targeted campaign is referred to a strategic web compromise or watering hole attack.

Os adversários podem purchase domains similar to legitimate domains (ex: homoglyphs, typosquatting, different top-level domain, etc.) during acquisition of infrastructure (**Domains** (`T1583.001`)) to help facilitate **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Hospedagem e Preparação de Capacidades: Link Target
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem put in place resources that are referenced by a link that can be used during targeting. Um adversário pode rely upon a user clicking a malicious link com o objetivo de divulge information (including credentials) or to gain execution, as in **Malicious Link** (`T1204.001`). Links can be used for spearphishing, such as sending an email accompanied by engenharia social text to coax the user to actively click or copy and paste a URL into a browser. Prior to a phish for information (as in **Spearphishing Link** (`T1598.003`)) or a phish to gain initial access to a system (as in **Spearphishing Link** (`T1566.002`)), an adversary must set up the resources for a link target for the spearphishing link. 

Typically, the resources for a link target will be an HTML page that may include some client-side script such as **JavaScript** (`T1059.007`) to decide what content to serve to the user. Os adversários podem clone legitimate sites to serve as the link target, this can include cloning of login pages of legitimate web services or organization login pages in an effort to harvest credentials during **Spearphishing Link** (`T1598.003`). `[Ref: Malwarebytes Silent Librarian October 2020]` `[Ref: Proofpoint TA407 September 2019]` Os adversários podem também **Upload Malware** (`T1608.001`) and have the link target point to malware for download/execution by the user.

Os adversários podem purchase domains similar to legitimate domains (ex: homoglyphs, typosquatting, different top-level domain, etc.) during acquisition of infrastructure (**Domains** (`T1583.001`)) to help facilitate **Malicious Link** (`T1204.001`).

Links can be written by adversaries to mask the true destination com o objetivo de deceive victims by abusing the URL schema and increasing the effectiveness of phishing. `[Ref: Kaspersky-masking]` `[Ref: mandiant-masking]`

Os adversários podem também use free or paid accounts on link shortening services and Platform-as-a-Service providers to host link targets while taking advantage of the widely trusted domains of those providers to avoid being blocked while redirecting victims to malicious pages. `[Ref: Netskope GCP Redirection]` `[Ref: Netskope Cloud Phishing]` `[Ref: Intezer App Service Phishing]` `[Ref: Cofense-redirect]` Além disso, adversaries may serve a variety of malicious links through uniquely generated URIs/URLs (including one-time, single use links). `[Ref: iOS URL Scheme]` `[Ref: URI]` `[Ref: URI Use]` `[Ref: URI Unique]` Finally, adversaries may take advantage of the decentralized nature of the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) to host link targets that are difficult to remove. `[Ref: Talos IPFS 2022]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Hospedagem e Preparação de Capacidades: SEO Poisoning
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem poison mechanisms that influence search engine optimization (SEO) to further lure staged capabilities towards potential victims. Search engines typically display results to users based on purchased ads as well as the site’s ranking/score/reputation calculated by their web crawlers and algorithms. `[Ref: Atlas SEO]` `[Ref: MalwareBytes SEO]`

To help facilitate **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`), adversaries may stage content that explicitly manipulates SEO rankings com o objetivo de promote sites hosting their malicious payloads (such as **Drive-by Target** (`T1608.004`)) within search engines. Poisoning SEO rankings may involve various tricks, such as stuffing keywords (including in the form of hidden text) into compromised sites. These keywords could be related to the interests/browsing habits of the intended victim(s) as well as more broad, seasonably popular topics (e.g. elections, trending news). `[Ref: ZScaler SEO]` `[Ref: Atlas SEO]`

Adicionalmente a internet search engines (such as Google), adversaries may also aim to manipulate specific in-site searches for developer platforms (such as GitHub) to deceive users towards **Supply Chain Compromise** (`T1195`) lures. In-site searches will rank search results according to their own algorithms and metrics such as popularity `[Ref: Chexmarx-seo]` which may be targeted and gamed by malicious actors. `[Ref: Checkmarx-oss-seo]`

Os adversários podem também purchase or plant incoming links to staged capabilities com o objetivo de boost the site’s calculated relevance and reputation. `[Ref: MalwareBytes SEO]` `[Ref: DFIR Report Gootloader]`

SEO poisoning may also be combined with evasive redirects and other cloaking mechanisms (such as measuring mouse movements or serving content based on browser user agents, user language/localization settings, or HTTP headers) com o objetivo de feed SEO inputs while avoiding scrutiny from defenders. `[Ref: ZScaler SEO]` `[Ref: Sophos Gootloader]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Hospedagem e Preparação de Capacidades: AI Result Poisoning
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem manipular publicly accessible web content to influence generative AI systems or AI-powered search engines into retrieving, citing, or recommending attacker-controlled information. `[Ref: Digiday AI Result Poisoning]` `[Ref: Netcraft AI Summaries]`

Unlike traditional **SEO Poisoning** (`T1608.006`), which primarily attempts to influence the ordering of conventional search results, AI Result Poisoning targets systems that synthesize information from multiple sources and provide a direct answer to the user. Os adversários podem criar malicious or misleading websites, publish fabricated claims, generate supporting articles, or establish multiple apparently independent sources that reinforce the same information. These sources may then be retrieved by AI systems using web search or retrieval-augmented generation and incorporated into generated responses. 

Os adversários podem utilizar this technique to recommend or link to phishing sites, fraudulent online stores, malicious downloads, impersonation pages, or other attacker-controlled infrastructure. `[Ref: dev.to Abusing AI Chatbot Recommendations]` `[Ref: darkreading geo poisoning]` `[Ref: darkreading ai result poisoning]` It pode também ser utilizado para promote misinformation or fabricated claims sem necessitar de access to the underlying AI model, system prompt, or application infrastructure. `[Ref: Lasso Security AI Engine Poisoning]` Because the malicious content can resemble ordinary marketing, editorial, or informational material, traditional prompt injection and malware-focused detections may not identify the activity.

techniques.fullNamePt: Comando de Administração de Containers
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de a container administration service to execute commands within a container. A container administration service such as the Docker daemon, the Kubernetes API server, or the kubelet may allow remote management of containers dentro do ambiente alvo. `[Ref: Docker Daemon CLI]` `[Ref: Kubernetes API]` `[Ref: Kubernetes Kubelet]`

In Docker, adversaries may specify an entrypoint during container deployment that executes a script or command, or they may use a command such as `docker exec` to execute a command within a running container. `[Ref: Docker Entrypoint]` `[Ref: Docker Exec]` In Kubernetes, if an adversary has sufficient permissions, they may gain remote execution in a container in the cluster via interaction with the Kubernetes API server, the kubelet, or by running a command such as `kubectl exec`. `[Ref: Kubectl Exec Get Shell]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de authentication and role-based access control on the container service to restrict users to the least privileges required. `[Ref: Kubernetes Hardening Guide]` When using Kubernetes, avoid giving users wildcard permissions or adding users to the `system:masters` group, and use `RoleBindings` rather than `ClusterRoleBindings` to limit user privileges to specific namespaces. `[Ref: Kubernetes RBAC]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure containers are not running as root by default. In Kubernetes environments, consider defining Pod Security Standards that prevent pods from running privileged containers and using the `NodeRestriction` admission controller to deny the kublet access to nodes and pods outside of the node it belongs to. `[Ref: Kubernetes Hardening Guide]`  `[Ref: Kubernetes Admission Controllers]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Remove unnecessary tools and software from containers.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit communications with the container service to managed and secured channels, such as local Unix sockets or remote access via SSH. Require secure port access para comunicar com the APIs over TLS by disabling unauthenticated access to the Docker API and Kubernetes API Server. `[Ref: Docker Daemon Socket Protect]` `[Ref: Kubernetes API Control Access]` In Kubernetes clusters deployed in cloud environments, use native cloud platform features to restrict the IP ranges that are permitted to access to API server. `[Ref: Kubernetes Cloud Native Security]` Where possible, consider enabling just-in-time (JIT) access to the Kubernetes API to place additional restrictions on access. `[Ref: Microsoft AKS Azure AD 2023]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use read-only containers, read-only sistema de ficheiross, and minimal images when possible to prevent the execution of commands. `[Ref: Kubernetes Hardening Guide]` Where possible, also consider using application control and software restriction tools (such as those provided by SELinux) to restrict access to files, processes, and system calls in containers. `[Ref: Kubernetes Security Context]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

analytics.name: Analytic 0177
analytics.descriptionPt: Defenders may detect abuse of container administration commands by observing anomalous use of management utilities (`docker exec`, `kubectl exec`, or API calls to kubelet) correlated with unexpected process creation inside containers. Behavioral chains include unauthorized API requests followed by command execution within running pods or containers, often originating from unusual user accounts, automation scripts, or IP addresses outside the expected cluster management plane.

techniques.fullNamePt: Implementação de Container
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem deploy a container into an environment to facilitate execution or evade defenses. In some cases, adversaries may deploy a new container to execute processes associated with a particular image or deployment, such as processes that execute or download malware. In others, an adversary may deploy a new container configured without network rules, user limitations, etc. para contornar (bypass) existing defenses within the environment. In Kubernetes environments, an adversary may attempt to deploy a privileged or vulnerable container into a specific node com o objetivo de **Escape to Host** (`T1611`) and access other containers running on the node.  `[Ref: AppSecco Kubernetes Namespace Breakout 2020]`

Containers can be deployed by various means, such as via Docker's `create` and `start` APIs or via a web application such as the Kubernetes dashboard or Kubeflow.  `[Ref: Docker Container]` `[Ref: Kubernetes Dashboard]` `[Ref: Kubeflow Pipelines]` In Kubernetes environments, containers may be deployed through workloads such as ReplicaSets or DaemonSets, which can allow containers to be deployed across multiple nodes. `[Ref: Kubernetes Workload Management]` Os adversários podem deploy containers based on retrieved or built malicious images or from benign images that download and execute malicious payloads at runtime. `[Ref: Aqua Build Images on Hosts]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de the principle of least privilege by limiting container dashboard access to only the necessary users. When using Kubernetes, avoid giving users wildcard permissions or adding users to the `system:masters` group, and use `RoleBindings` rather than `ClusterRoleBindings` to limit user privileges to specific namespaces. `[Ref: Kubernetes RBAC]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Scan images before deployment, and block those that are not in compliance with security policies. In Kubernetes environments, the admission controller pode ser utilizado para validate images after a container deployment request is authenticated but before the container is deployed. `[Ref: Kubernetes Hardening Guide]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Deny direct remote access to internal systems through the use of network proxies, gateways, and firewalls.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit communications with the container service to managed and secured channels, such as local Unix sockets or remote access via SSH. Require secure port access para comunicar com the APIs over TLS by disabling unauthenticated access to the Docker API, Kubernetes API Server, and container orchestration web applications. `[Ref: Docker Daemon Socket Protect]` `[Ref: Kubernetes API Control Access]` In Kubernetes clusters deployed in cloud environments, use native cloud platform features to restrict the IP ranges that are permitted to access to API server. `[Ref: Kubernetes Cloud Native Security]` Where possible, consider enabling just-in-time (JIT) access to the Kubernetes API to place additional restrictions on access. `[Ref: Microsoft AKS Azure AD 2023]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Fuga para o Host (Container Escape)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem break out of a container or virtualized environment para obter acesso a the underlying host. This can allow an adversary access to other containerized or virtualized resources from the host level or to the host itself. In principle, containerized / virtualized resources should provide a clear separation of application functionality and be isolated from the host environment. `[Ref: Docker Overview]`

There are multiple ways an adversary may escape from a container to a host environment. Examples include creating a container configured to mount the host’s filesystem using the bind parameter, which allows the adversary to drop payloads and execute control utilities such as cron on the host; utilizing a privileged container to run commands or load a malicious kernel module on the underlying host; or abusing system calls such as `unshare` and `keyctl` para escalar privilégios and steal secrets. `[Ref: Docker Bind Mounts]` `[Ref: Trend Micro Privileged Container]` `[Ref: Intezer Doki July 20]` `[Ref: Container Escape]` `[Ref: Crowdstrike Kubernetes Container Escape]` `[Ref: Keyctl-unmask]`

Additionally, an adversary may be able to exploit a compromised container with a mounted container management socket, such as `docker.sock`, to break out of the container via a **Container Administration Command** (`T1609`). `[Ref: Container Escape]` Os adversários podem também escape via **Exploitation for Privilege Escalation** (`T1068`), such as exploiting vulnerabilities in global symbolic links com o objetivo de access the root directory of a host machine. `[Ref: Windows Server Containers Are Open]`

In ESXi environments, an adversary may exploit a vulnerability com o objetivo de escape from a máquina virtual (VM) into the hypervisor. `[Ref: Broadcom VMSA-2025-004]`

Gaining access to the host may provide the adversary with the opportunity to achieve follow-on objectives, such as establishing persistence, moving laterally within the environment, accessing other containers or máquina virtual (VM)s running on the host, or setting up a Command and Control (C2) channel on the host.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use read-only containers, read-only sistema de ficheiross, and minimal images when possible to prevent the running of commands. `[Ref: Kubernetes Hardening Guide]` Where possible, also consider using application control and software restriction tools (such as those provided by SELinux) to restrict access to files, processes, and system calls in containers. `[Ref: Kubernetes Security Context]`

mitigations.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
