mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure containers are not running as root by default and do not use unnecessary privileges or mounted components. In Kubernetes environments, consider defining Pod Security Standards that prevent pods from running privileged containers. `[Ref: Kubernetes Hardening Guide]`

analytics.name: Analytic 0612
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection of container escape attempts via bind mounts, privileged containers, or abuse of docker.sock. Defenders may observe anomalous volume mount configurations (e.g., hostPath to / or /proc), unexpected privileged container launches, or use of container administration commands to access host resources. These events typically correlate with subsequent process execution on the host outside of normal container isolation.

techniques.fullNamePt: Build Image on Host
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem build a container image directly on a host para contornar (bypass) defenses that monitor for the retrieval of malicious images from a public registry. A remote `build` request may be sent to the Docker API that includes a Dockerfile that pulls a vanilla base image, such as alpine, from a public or local registry and then builds a custom image upon it. `[Ref: Docker Build Image]`

Um adversário pode take advantage of that `build` API to build a custom image on the host that includes malware downloaded from their C2 server, and then they may utilize **Deploy Container** (`T1610`) using that custom image. `[Ref: Aqua Build Images on Hosts]` `[Ref: Aqua Security Cloud Native Threat Report June 2021]` If the base image is pulled from a public registry, defenses will likely not detect the image as malicious since it’s a vanilla image. If the base image already resides in a local registry, the pull may be considered even less suspicious since the image is already in the environment.

mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Auditar regularmente images deployed within the environment to ensure they do not contain any malicious components.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Build Image on Host

analytics.name: Analytic 1261
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection of container image build activity directly on the host using Docker or Kubernetes APIs. Defenders may observe Docker build requests, anomalous Dockerfile instructions (such as downloading code from unknown IPs), or creation of new images followed by immediate deployment. This behavior chain typically consists of an unexpected image creation event correlated with outbound network communication to non-standard or untrusted destinations.

logSources.channel: docker build or POST /build API request

logSources.name: NSM:Flow

Threshold for number of new custom images created in a given time window. Exceeding this threshold may indicate malicious builds.
Defines correlation window (e.g., 5m) between suspicious build activity and subsequent network traffic anomalies.

blockers: M1026 (Privileged Account Management): Pass-the-Hash com conta de Administrador Local (`RID 500`) falha noutros hosts porque cada máquina possui password única gerida pelo LAPS.
M1030 (Network Segmentation): Sem conectividade direta da sub-rede atual para servidores de produção ou Domain Controllers.
M1047 (Audit): Operações de enumeração ou persistência geram alertas imediatos no SOC devido a regras Sigma sobre argumentos de linha de comando.
Inspeção de telemetria comportamental por EDR (ETW Threat Intelligence, User-Mode Inline Hooks em `ntdll.dll`, Memory Scanners para páginas `RWX`).
bypasses: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

Aplicar Indirect Syscalls com Call Stack Spoofing, evitar permissões de memória `RWX` simultâneas (usar padrão `RW` -> `RX` com Sleep Encryption como Ekko/Cronos durante períodos de inatividade do beacon) e realizar patching de `EtwEventWrite` no processo local.
blindSpots: **RegistryAllowList**: Defines trusted registries for image pulls/builds. Builds referencing unapproved registries may indicate adversary behavior.
**NewImageThreshold**: Threshold for number of new custom images created in a given time window. Exceeding this threshold may indicate malicious builds.
**TimeWindow**: Defines correlation window (e.g., 5m) between suspicious build activity and subsequent network traffic anomalies.

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Containers e Recursos
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar discover containers and other resources that are available within a containers environment. Other resources may include images, deployments, pods, nodes, and other information such as the status of a cluster.

These resources can be viewed within web applications such as the Kubernetes dashboard or can be queried via the Docker and Kubernetes APIs. `[Ref: Docker API]` `[Ref: Kubernetes API]` In Docker, logs may leak information about the environment, such as the environment’s configuration, which services are available, and what cloud provider the victim may be utilizing. The discovery of these resources may inform an adversary’s next steps in the environment, such as how to perform lateral movement and which methods to utilize for execution.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Deny direct remote access to internal systems through the use of network proxies, gateways, and firewalls.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit communications with the container service to managed and secured channels, such as local Unix sockets or remote access via SSH. Require secure port access para comunicar com the APIs over TLS by disabling unauthenticated access to the Docker API and Kubernetes API Server. `[Ref: Docker Daemon Socket Protect]` `[Ref: Kubernetes API Control Access]` In Kubernetes clusters deployed in cloud environments, use native cloud platform features to restrict the IP ranges that are permitted to access to API server. `[Ref: Kubernetes Cloud Native Security]` Where possible, consider enabling just-in-time (JIT) access to the Kubernetes API to place additional restrictions on access. `[Ref: Microsoft AKS Azure AD 2023]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Forçar a aplicação de the principle of least privilege by limiting dashboard visibility to only the required users. When using Kubernetes, avoid giving users wildcard permissions or adding users to the `system:masters` group, and use `RoleBindings` rather than `ClusterRoleBindings` to limit user privileges to specific namespaces. `[Ref: Kubernetes RBAC]`

techniques.fullNamePt: System Location Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem recolher information in an attempt to calculate the geographical location of a victim host. Os adversários podem utilizar the information from **System Location Discovery** (`T1614`) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions.

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar infer the location of a system using various system checks, such as time zone, keyboard layout, and/or language settings. `[Ref: FBI Ragnar Locker 2020]` `[Ref: Sophos Geolocation 2016]` `[Ref: Bleepingcomputer RAT malware 2020]` Windows API functions such as `GetLocaleInfoW` pode também ser utilizado para determine the locale of the host. `[Ref: FBI Ragnar Locker 2020]` Em ambientes Cloud, an instance's availability zone may also be discovered by accessing the instance metadata service from the instance. `[Ref: AWS Instance Identity Documents]` `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Instance Metadata 2021]`

Os adversários podem também attempt to infer the location of a victim host using IP addressing, such as via online geolocation IP-lookup services. `[Ref: Securelist Trasparent Tribe 2020]` `[Ref: Sophos Geolocation 2016]`

Detection can be enhanced by correlating with processes not typically associated with system configuration queries, such as unknown binaries or scripts.

techniques.fullNameEn: System Location Discovery: System Language Discovery
techniques.fullNamePt: System Location Discovery: System Language Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar gather information about the system language of a victim com o objetivo de infer the geographical location of that host. This information pode ser empregue para shape follow-on behaviors, including whether the adversary infects the target and/or attempts specific actions. This decision may be employed by malware developers and operators to reduce their risk of attracting the attention of specific law enforcement agencies or prosecution/scrutiny from other entities. `[Ref: Malware System Language Check]`

There are various sources of data an adversary could use to infer system language, such as system defaults and keyboard layouts. Specific checks will vary based on the target and/or adversary, but may involve behaviors such as **Query Registry** (`T1012`) and calls to **Native API** (`T1106`) functions. `[Ref: CrowdStrike Ryuk January 2019]` 

Por exemplo, on a Windows system adversaries may attempt to infer the language of a system by querying the registry key `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Nls\Language` or parsing the outputs of Windows API functions `GetUserDefaultUILanguage`, `GetSystemDefaultUILanguage`, `GetKeyboardLayoutList` and `GetUserDefaultLangID`. `[Ref: Darkside Ransomware Cybereason]` `[Ref: Securelist JSWorm]` `[Ref: SecureList SynAck Doppelgänging May 2018]`

On a macOS or Linux system, adversaries may query `locale` to retrieve the value of the `$LANG` environment variable.

detections.name: Detection Strategy for System Language Discovery

analytics.name: Analytic 1561
analytics.descriptionPt: Registry access to system language keys (e.g., HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Nls\Language) or suspicious processes invoking locale-related APIs (e.g., GetUserDefaultUILanguage, GetSystemDefaultUILanguage, GetKeyboardLayoutList). Defender visibility focuses on anomalous or non-standard processes issuing these queries, especially when run by unknown binaries or scripts.

mutableElements.description: Defines trusted processes allowed to query registry language keys or APIs. Unexpected parent-child process chains may indicate adversary use.
Frequency threshold for language registry or API calls within a set time window.

techniques.fullNamePt: Group Policy Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem recolher information on Group Policy settings to identify paths for privilege escalation, security measures applied within a domain, and to discover patterns in domain objects that can be manipulated or used to blend in the environment. Group Policy allows for centralized management of user and computer settings in Active Directory (AD) (AD). Group policy objects (GPOs) are containers for group policy settings made up of files stored within a predictable network path `\<DOMAIN>\SYSVOL\<DOMAIN>\Policies\`. `[Ref: TechNet Group Policy Basics]` `[Ref: ADSecurity GPO Persistence 2016]`

Os adversários podem utilizar commands such as `gpresult` or various publicly available PowerShell functions, such as `Get-DomainGPO` and `Get-DomainGPOLocalGroup`, to gather information on Group Policy settings. `[Ref: Microsoft gpresult]` `[Ref: Github PowerShell Empire]` Os adversários podem utilizar this information to shape follow-on behaviors, including determining potential attack paths within the rede alvo as well as opportunities to manipulate Group Policy settings (i.e. **Domain or Tenant Policy Modification** (`T1484`)) for their benefit.

detections.name: Detection strategy for Group Policy Discovery on Windows

analytics.name: Analytic 0152
analytics.descriptionPt: Detection of adversary attempts to enumerate Group Policy settings through suspicious command execution (gpresult), PowerShell enumeration (Get-DomainGPO, Get-DomainGPOLocalGroup), and abnormal LDAP queries targeting groupPolicyContainer objects. Defenders observe unusual process lineage, script execution, or LDAP filter activity against Domain Controller (DC)s.

logSources.name: NSM:Flow

mutableElements.description: Defines the correlation window to link suspicious PowerShell activity, gpresult execution, and LDAP enumeration.
Identifies accounts expected to perform GPO enumeration (administrators vs. standard users).
Patterns for detecting suspicious gpresult or PowerShell cmdlets; tunable to reduce noise in environments where these tools are common.

techniques.fullNamePt: Descoberta de Objetos em Cloud Storage
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enumerar objects in cloud storage infrastructure. Os adversários podem utilizar this information during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including requesting all or specific objects from cloud storage.  De forma semelhante a **File and Directory Discovery** (`T1083`) on a local host, after identifying available storage services (i.e. **Cloud Infrastructure Discovery** (`T1580`)) adversaries may access the contents/objects stored in cloud infrastructure.

Cloud service providers offer APIs allowing users to enumerate objects stored within cloud storage. Examples include ListObjectsV2 in AWS  `[Ref: ListObjectsV2]` and List Blobs in Azure `[Ref: List Blobs]` .

techniques.fullNamePt: Carregamento Reflexivo de Código (Reflective Loading)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem reflectively load code into a process com o objetivo de conceal the execution of malicious payloads. Reflective loading involves allocating then executing payloads directly within the memory of the process, vice creating a thread or process backed by a file path on disk (e.g., **Shared Modules** (`T1129`)).

Reflectively loaded payloads may be compiled binaries, anonymous files (only present in RAM), or just snubs of fileless executable code (ex: position-independent shellcode). `[Ref: Introducing Donut]` `[Ref: S1 Custom Shellcode Tool]` `[Ref: Stuart ELF Memory]` `[Ref: 00sec Droppers]` `[Ref: Mandiant BYOL]` Por exemplo, the `Assembly.Load()` method executed by **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) may be abused to load raw code into the running process. `[Ref: Microsoft AssemblyLoad]`

Reflective code injection is very similar to **Process Injection** (`T1055`) except that the “injection” loads code into the processes’ own memory instead of that of a separate process. Reflective loading may evade process-based detections since the execution of the código arbitrário may be masked within a legitimate or otherwise benign process. Reflectively loading payloads directly into memory may also avoid creating files or other artifacts on disk, while also enabling malware to keep these payloads encrypted (or otherwise obfuscated) until execution. `[Ref: Stuart ELF Memory]` `[Ref: 00sec Droppers]` `[Ref: Intezer ACBackdoor]` `[Ref: S1 Old Rat New Tricks]`

analytics.descriptionPt: Detect anomalous chains of memory allocation and execution inside the same process (e.g., VirtualAlloc → memcpy → VirtualProtect → CreateThread). Unlike process injection, reflective code loading does not perform cross-process memory writes — the suspicious activity occurs entirely within the process’s own PID context.

techniques.namePt: Geração de Pedidos MFA (MFA Fatigue / Push Bombing)
techniques.fullNamePt: Geração de Pedidos MFA (MFA Fatigue / Push Bombing)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanisms and gain access to accounts by generating MFA requests sent to users.

Adversaries in possession of credentials to **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) may be unable to complete the login process if they lack access to the 2FA or MFA mechanisms required as an additional credential and security control. To circumvent this, adversaries may abuse the automatic generation of push notifications to MFA services such as Duo Push, Microsoft Authenticator, Okta, or similar services to have the user grant access to their account. If adversaries lack credentials to victim accounts, they may also abuse automatic push notification generation when this option is configured for self-service password reset (SSPR). `[Ref: Obsidian SSPR Abuse 2023]`

In some cases, adversaries may continuously repeat login attempts com o objetivo de bombard users with MFA push notifications, SMS messages, and phone calls, potentially resulting in the user finally accepting the authentication request in response to “MFA fatigue.” `[Ref: Russian 2FA Push Annoyance - Cimpanu]` `[Ref: MFA Fatigue Attacks - PortSwigger]` `[Ref: Suspected Russian Activity Targeting Government and Business Entities Around the Globe]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Suspected Russian Activity Targeting Government and Business Entities Around the Globe]

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Implementar more secure 2FA/MFA mechanisms in replacement of simple push or one-click 2FA/MFA options. Por exemplo, having users enter a one-time code provided by the login screen into the 2FA/MFA application or utilizing other out-of-band 2FA/MFA mechanisms (such as rotating code-based hardware tokens providing rotating codes that need an accompanying user pin) may be more secure. Ademais, change default configurations and implement limits upon the maximum number of 2FA/MFA request prompts that can be sent to users in period of time. `[Ref: MFA Fatigue Attacks - PortSwigger]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Account Use Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Enable account restrictions to prevent login attempts, and the subsequent 2FA/MFA service requests, from being initiated from suspicious locations or when the source of the login attempts do not match the location of the 2FA/MFA smart device. Use conditional access policies to block logins from non-compliant devices or from outside defined organization IP ranges. `[Ref: Microsoft Common Conditional Access Policies]`

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Train users to only accept 2FA/MFA requests from login attempts they initiated, to review source location of the login attempt prompting the 2FA/MFA requests, and to report suspicious/unsolicited prompts.

techniques.fullNamePt: Evasão de Debugger
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem employ various means to detect and avoid debuggers. Debuggers are typically used by defenders to trace and/or analyze the execution of potential malware payloads. `[Ref: ProcessHacker Github]`

Debugger evasion may include changing behaviors based on the results of the checks for the presence of artifacts indicative of a debugged environment. De forma semelhante a **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`), if the adversary detects a debugger, they may alter their malware to disengage from the victim or conceal the core functions of the implant. They may also search for debugger artifacts before dropping secondary or additional payloads.

Specific checks will vary based on the target and/or adversary. Em ambientes Windows, this may involve **Native API** (`T1106`) function calls such as `IsDebuggerPresent()` and ` NtQueryInformationProcess()`, or manually checking the `BeingDebugged` flag of the Process Environment Block (PEB). Em sistemas Linux, this may involve querying `/proc/self/status` for the `TracerPID` field, which indicates whether or not the process is being traced by dynamic analysis tools. `[Ref: Cado Security P2PInfect 2023]` `[Ref: Positive Technologies Hellhounds 2023]` Other checks for debugging artifacts may also seek to enumerate hardware breakpoints, interrupt assembly opcodes, time checks, or measurements if exceptions are raised in the current process (assuming a present debugger would “swallow” or handle the potential error). `[Ref: hasherezade debug]` `[Ref: AlKhaser Debug]` `[Ref: vxunderground debug]`

Malware may also leverage Structured Exception Handling (SEH) to detect debuggers by throwing an exception and detecting whether the process is suspended. SEH handles both hardware and software expectations, providing control over the exceptions including support for debugging. If a debugger is present, the program’s control will be transferred to the debugger, and the execution of the code will be suspended. If the debugger is not present, control will be transferred to the SEH handler, which will automatically handle the exception and allow the program’s execution to continue. `[Ref: Apriorit]`

Os adversários podem utilizar the information learned from these debugger checks during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors. Debuggers can also be evaded by detaching the process or flooding debug logs with meaningless data via messages produced by looping **Native API** (`T1106`) function calls such as `OutputDebugStringW()`. `[Ref: wardle evilquest partii]` `[Ref: Checkpoint Dridex Jan 2021]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Plist File Modification
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem modificar property list files (plist files) to enable other malicious activity, while also potentially evading and bypassing system defenses. macOS applications use plist files, such as the `info.plist` file, to store properties and configuration settings that inform the sistema operativo how to handle the application at runtime. Plist files are structured metadata in key-value pairs formatted in XML based on Apple's Core Foundation DTD. Plist files can be saved in text or binary format. `[Ref: fileinfo plist file description]` 

Adversaries can modify key-value pairs in plist files to influence system behaviors, such as hiding the execution of an application (i.e. **Hidden Window** (`T1564.003`)) or running additional commands for persistence (ex: **Launch Agent** (`T1543.001`)/**Launch Daemon** (`T1543.004`) or **Re-opened Applications** (`T1547.007`)).

Por exemplo, adversaries can add a malicious application path to the `~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock.plist` file, which controls apps that appear in the Dock. Adversaries can also modify the `LSUIElement` key in an application’s `info.plist` file  to run the app in the background. Adversaries can also insert key-value pairs to insert variáveis de ambiente, such as `LSEnvironment`, to enable persistence via **Dynamic Linker Hijacking** (`T1574.006`). `[Ref: wardle chp2 persistence]` `[Ref: eset_osx_flashback]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Serverless Execution
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de serverless computing, integration, and automation services to execute código arbitrário in cloud environments. Many cloud providers offer a variety of serverless resources, including compute engines, application integration services, and web servers. 

Os adversários podem abusar de these resources in various ways as a means of executing comandos arbitrários. Por exemplo, adversaries may use serverless functions para executar código ou artefactos maliciosos code, such as crypto-mining malware (i.e. **Resource Hijacking** (`T1496`)). `[Ref: Cado Security Denonia]` Os adversários podem também create functions that enable further compromise of the cloud environment. Por exemplo, an adversary may use the `IAM:PassRole` permission in AWS or the `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` permission in Google Cloud to add **Additional Cloud Roles** (`T1098.003`) to a serverless cloud function, which may then be able to perform actions the original user cannot. `[Ref: Rhino Security Labs AWS Privilege Escalation]` `[Ref: Rhingo Security Labs GCP Privilege Escalation]`

Serverless functions can also be invoked in response to cloud events (i.e. **Event Triggered Execution** (`T1546`)), potentially enabling persistent execution over time. Por exemplo, in AWS environments, an adversary may create a Lambda function that automatically adds **Additional Cloud Credentials** (`T1098.001`) to a user and a corresponding CloudWatch events rule that invokes that function whenever a new user is created. `[Ref: Backdooring an AWS account]` This is also possible in many cloud-based office application suites. Por exemplo, in Microsoft 365 environments, an adversary may create a Power Automate workflow that forwards all emails a user receives or creates anonymous sharing links whenever a user is granted access to a document in SharePoint. `[Ref: Varonis Power Automate Data Exfiltration]` `[Ref: Microsoft DART Case Report 001]` In Google Workspace environments, they may instead create an Apps Script that exfiltrates a user's data when they open a file. `[Ref: Cloud Hack Tricks GWS Apps Script]` `[Ref: OWN-CERT Google App Script 2024]`

techniques.namePt: Roubo ou Falsificação de Certificados (AD CS)
techniques.fullNamePt: Roubo ou Falsificação de Certificados (AD CS)
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem roubar or forge certificates used for authentication to access sistemas remotos or resources. Digital certificates are often used to sign and encrypt messages and/or files. Certificates are also used as authentication material. Por exemplo, Entra ID device certificates and Active Directory (AD) Certificate Services (AD CS) certificates bind to an identity and can be used as credentials for domain accounts. `[Ref: O365 Blog Azure AD Device IDs]` `[Ref: Microsoft AD CS Overview]`

Authentication certificates can be both stolen and forged. Por exemplo, AD CS certificates can be stolen from encrypted storage (in the Registry or files) `[Ref: APT29 Deep Look at Credential Roaming]`, misplaced certificate files (i.e. **Unsecured Credentials** (`T1552`)), or directly from the Windows certificate store via various crypto APIs. `[Ref: SpecterOps Certified Pre Owned]` `[Ref: GitHub CertStealer]` `[Ref: GitHub GhostPack Certificates]` With appropriate enrollment rights, users and/or machines within a domain can also request and/or manually renew certificates from enterprise certificate authorities (CA). This enrollment process defines various settings and permissions associated with the certificate. Of note, the certificate’s extended key usage (EKU) values define signing, encryption, and authentication use cases, while the certificate’s subject alternative name (SAN) values define the certificate owner’s alternate names. `[Ref: Medium Certified Pre Owned]`

Abusing certificates for authentication credentials may enable other behaviors such as **Lateral Movement** (`TA0008`). Certificate-related misconfigurations may also enable opportunities for **Privilege Escalation** (`TA0004`), by way of allowing users to impersonate or assume privileged accounts or permissions via the identities (SANs) associated with a certificate. These abuses may also enable **Persistence** (`TA0003`) via stealing or forging certificates that can be used as **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) for the duration of the certificate's validity, despite user password resets. Authentication certificates can also be stolen and forged for machine accounts.

Adversaries who have access to root (or subordinate) CA certificate private keys (or mechanisms protecting/managing these keys) may also establish **Persistence** (`TA0003`) by forging arbitrary authentication certificates for the victim domain (known as “golden” certificates). `[Ref: Medium Certified Pre Owned]` Os adversários podem também target certificates and related services com o objetivo de access other forms of credentials, such as **Golden Ticket** (`T1558.001`) ticket-granting tickets (TGT) or NTLM plaintext. `[Ref: Medium Certified Pre Owned]`

mitigations.name: Active Directory Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Ensure certificate authorities (CA) are properly secured, including treating CA servers (and other resources hosting CA certificates) as tier 0 assets. Harden abusable CA settings and attributes.

Por exemplo, consider disabling the usage of AD CS certificate SANs within relevant authentication protocol settings to enforce strict user mappings and prevent certificates from authenticating as other identifies. `[Ref: SpecterOps Certified Pre Owned]` Also consider enforcing CA Certificate Manager approval for the templates that include SAN as an issuance requirement.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider disabling old/dangerous authentication protocols (e.g. NTLM), as well as unnecessary certificate features, such as potentially vulnerable AD CS web and other enrollment server roles. `[Ref: SpecterOps Certified Pre Owned]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Ensure certificates as well as associated private keys are appropriately secured. Consider utilizing additional hardware credential protections such as trusted platform modules (TPM) or hardware security modules (HSM). Forçar a aplicação de HTTPS and enable Extended Protection for
Authentication. `[Ref: SpecterOps Certified Pre Owned]`

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Check and remediate unneeded existing authentication certificates as well as common abusable misconfigurations of CA settings and permissions, such as AD CS certificate enrollment permissions and published overly permissive certificate templates (which define available settings for created certificates). Por exemplo, available AD CS certificate templates can be checked via the Certificate Authority MMC snap-in (`certsrv.msc`). `certutil.exe` pode também ser utilizado para examine various information within an AD CS CA database. `[Ref: SpecterOps Certified Pre Owned]` `[Ref: GitHub PSPKIAudit]` `[Ref: GitHub Certify]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNamePt: Acquire Access
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem purchase or otherwise acquire an existing access to a target system or network. A variety of online services and initial access broker networks are available to sell access to previously compromised systems. `[Ref: Microsoft Ransomware as a Service]` `[Ref: CrowdStrike Access Brokers]` `[Ref: Krebs Access Brokers Fortune 500]` In some cases, adversary groups may form partnerships to share compromised systems with each other. `[Ref: CISA Karakurt 2022]`

Footholds to compromised systems may take a variety of forms, such as access to planted backdoors (e.g., **Web Shell** (`T1505.003`)) or established access via **External Remote Services** (`T1133`). In some cases, access brokers will implant compromised systems with a “load” that pode ser utilizado para install additional malware for paying customers. `[Ref: Microsoft Ransomware as a Service]`

By leveraging existing access broker networks rather than developing or obtaining their own initial access capabilities, an adversary can potentially reduce the resources required to gain a foothold on a rede alvo and focus their efforts on later stages of compromise. Os adversários podem prioritize acquiring access to systems that have been determined to lack security monitoring or that have high privileges, or systems that belong to organizations in a particular sector. `[Ref: Microsoft Ransomware as a Service]` `[Ref: CrowdStrike Access Brokers]`

In some cases, purchasing access to an organization in sectors such as IT contracting, software development, or telecommunications may allow an adversary to compromise additional victims via a **Trusted Relationship** (`T1199`), **Multi-Factor Authentication Interception** (`T1111`), or even **Supply Chain Compromise** (`T1195`).

**Note:** while this technique is distinct from other behaviors such as **Purchase Technical Data** (`T1597.002`) and **Credentials** (`T1589.001`), they may often be used in conjunction (especially where the acquired foothold requires **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`)).

mitigations.name: Pre-compromise
mitigations.descriptionPt: This technique cannot be easily mitigated with preventive controls since it is based on behaviors performed outside of the scope of enterprise defenses and controls.

techniques.fullNamePt: Cloud Administration Command
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de cloud management services to execute commands within máquina virtual (VM)s. Resources such as AWS Systems Manager, Azure RunCommand, and Runbooks allow users to remotely run scripts in máquina virtual (VM)s by leveraging installed máquina virtual (VM) agents.  `[Ref: AWS Systems Manager Run Command]` `[Ref: Microsoft Run Command]`

If an adversary gains administrative access to a cloud environment, they may be able to abuse cloud management services to execute commands in the environment’s máquina virtual (VM)s. Additionally, an adversary that compromises a service provider or delegated administrator account may similarly be able to leverage a **Trusted Relationship** (`T1199`) to execute commands in connected máquina virtual (VM)s. `[Ref: MSTIC Nobelium Oct 2021]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the number of cloud accounts with permissions to remotely execute commands on máquina virtual (VM)s, and ensure that these are not used for day-to-day operations. In Azure, limit the number of accounts with the roles Azure Virtual Machine Contributer and above, and consider using temporary Just-in-Time (JIT) roles to avoid permanently assigning privileged access to máquina virtual (VM)s. `[Ref: Mandiant Azure Run Command 2021]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

Correlate cloud control-plane activity logs with host-level execution (process creation, script execution) to validate if commands materialized inside the guest OS.

techniques.fullNamePt: Device Driver Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar enumerate local device drivers on a victim host. Information about device drivers may highlight various insights that shape follow-on behaviors, such as the function/purpose of the host, present security tools (i.e. **Security Software Discovery** (`T1518.001`)) or other defenses (e.g., **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`)), as well as potential exploitable vulnerabilities (e.g., **Exploitation for Privilege Escalation** (`T1068`)).

Many OS utilities may provide information about local device drivers, such as `driverquery.exe` and the `EnumDeviceDrivers()` API function on Windows. `[Ref: Microsoft Driverquery]` `[Ref: Microsoft EnumDeviceDrivers]` Information about device drivers (as well as associated services, i.e., **System Service Discovery** (`T1007`)) may also be available in the Registry. `[Ref: Microsoft Registry Drivers]`

On Linux/macOS, device drivers (in the form of kernel modules) may be visible within `/dev` or using utilities such as `lsmod` and `modinfo`. `[Ref: Linux Kernel Programming]` `[Ref: lsmod man]` `[Ref: modinfo man]`

Correlate command execution, process creation, and registry access to build a behavioral chain of driver discovery.

techniques.fullNamePt: Power Settings
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem impair a system's ability to hibernate, reboot, or shut down com o objetivo de extend access to infected machines. When a computer enters a dormant state, some or all software and hardware may cease to operate which can disrupt malicious activity. `[Ref: Sleep, shut down, hibernate]`

Os adversários podem abusar de system utilities and configuration settings to maintain access by preventing machines from entering a state, such as standby, that can terminate malicious activity. `[Ref: Microsoft: Powercfg command-line options]` `[Ref: systemdsleep Linux]`

Por exemplo, `powercfg` controls all configurable power system settings on a Windows system and pode ser abusado para prevent an infected host from locking or shutting down. `[Ref: Two New Monero Malware Attacks Target Windows and Android Users]` Os adversários podem também extend system lock screen timeout settings. `[Ref: BATLOADER: The Evasive Downloader Malware]` Other relevant settings, such as disk and hibernate timeout, can be similarly abused to keep the infected machine running even if no user is active. `[Ref: CoinLoader: A Sophisticated Malware Loader Campaign]`

Aware that some malware cannot survive system reboots, adversaries may entirely delete files used to invoke system shut down or reboot. `[Ref: Condi-Botnet-binaries]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Log Enumeration
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enumerar system and service logs to find useful data. These logs may highlight various types of valuable insights for an adversary, such as user authentication records (**Account Discovery** (`T1087`)), security or vulnerable software (**Software Discovery** (`T1518`)), or hosts within a compromised network (**Remote System Discovery** (`T1018`)).

Host binaries may be leveraged to collect system logs. Examples include using `wevtutil.exe` or **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) on Windows to access and/or export security event information. `[Ref: WithSecure Lazarus-NoPineapple Threat Intel Report 2023]` `[Ref: Cadet Blizzard emerges as novel threat actor]` Em ambientes Cloud, adversaries may leverage utilities such as the Azure VM Agent’s `CollectGuestLogs.exe` to collect security logs from cloud hosted infrastructure. `[Ref: SIM Swapping and Abuse of the Microsoft Azure Serial Console]`

Os adversários podem também target centralized logging infrastructure such as SIEMs. Logs may also be bulk exported and sent to adversary-controlled infrastructure for offline analysis.

Adicionalmente a gaining a better understanding of the environment, adversaries may also monitor logs in real time to track incident response procedures. This may allow them to adjust their techniques com o objetivo de maintain persistence or evade defenses. `[Ref: Permiso GUI-Vil 2023]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Financial Theft
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem roubar monetary resources from targets through extortion, engenharia social, technical theft, or other methods aimed at their own financial gain at the expense of the availability of these resources for victims. Financial theft is the ultimate objective of several popular campaign types including extortion by ransomware, `[Ref: FBI-ransomware]` business email compromise (BEC) and fraud, `[Ref: FBI-BEC]` "pig butchering," `[Ref: wired-pig butchering]` bank hacking, `[Ref: DOJ-DPRK Heist]` and exploiting cryptocurrency networks. `[Ref: BBC-Ronin]` 

Os adversários podem **Compromise Accounts** (`T1586`) to conduct unauthorized transfers of funds. `[Ref: Internet crime report 2022]` In the case of business email compromise or email fraud, an adversary may utilize **Impersonation** (`T1684.001`) of a trusted entity. Uma vez que the engenharia social is successful, victims can be deceived into sending money to financial accounts controlled by an adversary. `[Ref: FBI-BEC]` This creates the potential for multiple victims (i.e., compromised accounts as well as the ultimate monetary loss) in incidents involving financial theft. `[Ref: VEC]`

Extortion by ransomware may occur, for example, when an adversary demands payment from a victim after **Data Encrypted for Impact** (`T1486`)  `[Ref: NYT-Colonial]` and **Exfiltration** (`TA0010`) of data, followed by threatening to leak dados sensíveis to the public unless payment is made to the adversary. `[Ref: Mandiant-leaks]` Os adversários podem utilizar dedicated leak sites to distribute victim data. `[Ref: Crowdstrike-leaks]`

Due to the potentially immense business impact of financial theft, an adversary may abuse the possibility of financial theft and seeking monetary gain to divert attention from their true goals such as **Data Destruction** (`T1485`) and business disruption. `[Ref: AP-NotPetya]`

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Train and encourage users to identify engenharia social techniques used to enable financial theft. Also consider training users on procedures to prevent and respond to swatting and doxing, acts increasingly deployed by financially motivated groups to further coerce victims into satisfying ransom/extortion demands. `[Ref: Cyber Safety Review Board: Lapsus]` `[Ref: SWAT-hospital]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit access/authority to execute sensitive transactions, and switch to systems and procedures designed to authenticate/approve payments and purchase requests outside of insecure communication lines such as email.

techniques.fullNamePt: Content Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem gain access and continuously communicate with victims by injecting malicious content into systems through online tráfego de rede. Rather than luring victims to malicious payloads hosted on a compromised website (i.e., **Drive-by Target** (`T1608.004`) followed by **Drive-by Compromise** (`T1189`)), adversaries may initially access victims through compromised data-transfer channels where they can manipulate traffic and/or inject their own content. These compromised online network channels may also be used to deliver additional payloads (i.e., **Ingress Tool Transfer** (`T1105`)) and other data to already compromised systems. `[Ref: ESET MoustachedBouncer]`

Os adversários podem injetar content to victim systems in various ways, including:

* From the middle, where the adversary is in-between legitimate online client-server communications (**Note:** this is similar but distinct from **Adversary-in-the-Middle** (`T1557`), which describes AiTM activity solely within an enterprise environment)  `[Ref: Kaspersky Encyclopedia MiTM]`
* From the side, where malicious content is injected and races to the client as a fake response to requests of a legitimate online server  `[Ref: Kaspersky ManOnTheSide]`

Content injection is often the result of compromised upstream communication channels, for example at the level of an internet service provider (ISP) as is the case with "lawful interception." `[Ref: Kaspersky ManOnTheSide]` `[Ref: ESET MoustachedBouncer]` `[Ref: EFF China GitHub Attack]`

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider blocking download/transfer and execution of potentially uncommon file types known to be used in adversary campaigns.

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Where possible, ensure that online traffic is appropriately encrypted through services such as trusted VPNs.

techniques.fullNamePt: Hide Infrastructure
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem manipular tráfego de rede com o objetivo de hide and evade detection of their C2 infrastructure. This can be accomplished by identifying and filtering traffic from defensive tools, `[Ref: TA571]` masking malicious domains to obfuscate the true destination from both automated scanning tools and security researchers, `[Ref: Schema-abuse]` `[Ref: Facad1ng]` `[Ref: Browser-updates]` and otherwise hiding malicious artifacts to delay discovery and prolong the effectiveness of adversary infrastructure that could otherwise be identified, blocked, or taken down entirely.

C2 networks may include the use of **Proxy** (`T1090`) or VPNs to disguise IP addresses, which can allow adversaries to blend in with normal tráfego de rede and bypass conditional access policies or anti-abuse protections. Por exemplo, an adversary may use a virtual private cloud to spoof their IP address to closer align with a victim's IP address ranges. This may also bypass security measures relying on geolocation of the source IP address. `[Ref: sysdig]` `[Ref: Orange Residential Proxies]`

Os adversários podem também attempt to filter tráfego de rede com o objetivo de evade defensive tools in numerous ways, including blocking/redirecting common incident responder or security appliance user agents. `[Ref: mod_rewrite]` `[Ref: SocGholish-update]` Filtering traffic based on IP and geo-fencing may also avoid automated sandboxing or researcher activity (i.e., **Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion** (`T1497`)). `[Ref: TA571]` `[Ref: mod_rewrite]`

Hiding C2 infrastructure may also be supported by **Resource Development** (`TA0042`) activities such as **Acquire Infrastructure** (`T1583`) and **Compromise Infrastructure** (`T1584`). Por exemplo, using widely trusted hosting services or domains such as prominent URL shortening providers or marketing services for C2 networks may enable adversaries to present benign content that later redirects victims to malicious web pages or infrastructure once specific conditions are met. `[Ref: StarBlizzard]` `[Ref: QR-cofense]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Modify Cloud Resource Hierarchy
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar modify hierarchical structures in infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) environments com o objetivo de evade defenses.  

IaaS environments often group resources into a hierarchy, enabling improved resource management and application of policies to relevant groups. Hierarchical structures differ among cloud providers. Por exemplo, in AWS environments, multiple accounts can be grouped under a single organization, while in Azure environments, multiple subscriptions can be grouped under a single management group. `[Ref: AWS Organizations]` `[Ref: Microsoft Azure Resources]`

Os adversários podem add, delete, or otherwise modify resource groups within an IaaS hierarchy. Por exemplo, in Azure environments, an adversary who has gained access to a Global Administrator account may create new subscriptions in which to deploy resources. They may also engage in subscription hijacking by transferring an existing pay-as-you-go subscription from a victim tenant to an adversary-controlled tenant. This will allow the adversary to use the victim’s compute resources without generating logs on the victim tenant. `[Ref: Microsoft Peach Sandstorm 2023]` `[Ref: Microsoft Subscription Hijacking 2022]`

In AWS environments, adversaries with appropriate permissions in a given account may call the `LeaveOrganization` API, causing the account to be severed from the AWS Organization to which it was tied and removing any Service Control Policies, guardrails, or restrictions imposed upon it by its former Organization. Alternatively, adversaries may call the `CreateAccount` API com o objetivo de create a new account within an AWS Organization. This account will use the same payment methods registered to the payment account but may not be subject to existing detections or Service Control Policies. `[Ref: AWS re Inforce Trust Mod]`

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: In Azure environments, consider setting a policy to block subscription transfers. `[Ref: Azure Subscription Policies]` In AWS environments, consider using Service Control Policies to prevent the use of the `LeaveOrganization` API call. `[Ref: AWS RE:Inforce Threat Detection 2024]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit permissions to add, delete, or modify resource groups to only those required.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Periodically audit resource groups in the cloud management console to ensure that only expected items exist, especially close to the top of the hierarchy (e.g., AWS accounts and Azure subscriptions). Typically, top-level accounts (such as the AWS management account) should not contain any workloads or resources. `[Ref: AWS Management Account Best Practices]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

analytics.descriptionPt: Monitor for unauthorized or unusual modifications to cloud resource hierarchies such as AWS Organizations or Azure Management Groups. Defenders may observe anomalous calls to APIs like `LeaveOrganization`, `CreateAccount`, `MoveAccount`, or Azure subscription transfers. Correlate account activity with administrative role assignments, tenant transfers, or new subscription creation that deviates from organizational baselines. Multi-event correlation should track role elevation followed by hierarchy modifications within a short time window.

techniques.fullNamePt: Email Bombing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem flood targeted email addresses with an overwhelming volume of messages. This may bury legitimate emails in a flood of spam and disrupt business operations. `[Ref: sophos-bombing]` `[Ref: krebs-email-bombing]`

Um adversário pode accomplish email bombing by leveraging an automated bot to register a targeted address for e-mail lists that do not validate new signups, such as online newsletters. The result can be a wave of thousands of e-mails that effectively overloads the victim’s inbox. `[Ref: krebs-email-bombing]` `[Ref: hhs-email-bombing]`

By sending hundreds or thousands of e-mails in quick succession, adversaries may successfully divert attention away from and bury legitimate messages including security alerts, daily business processes like help desk tickets and client correspondence, or ongoing scams. `[Ref: hhs-email-bombing]` This behavior can also be used as a tool of harassment. `[Ref: krebs-email-bombing]`

This behavior may be a precursor for **Spearphishing Voice** (`T1566.004`). Por exemplo, an adversary may email bomb a target and then follow up with a phone call to fraudulently offer assistance. This engenharia social may lead to the use of **Remote Access Software** (`T1663`) to steal credentials, deploy ransomware, conduct **Financial Theft** (`T1657`) `[Ref: sophos-bombing]`, or engage in other malicious activity. `[Ref: rapid7-email-bombing]`

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Train users to be aware of access or manipulation attempts by an adversary to reduce the risk of successful engenharia social via e-mail bombing.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use anti-spoofing and email authentication mechanisms to filter messages based on validity checks of the sender domain (using SPF) and integrity of messages (using DKIM). Enabling these mechanisms within an organization (through policies such as DMARC) may enable recipients (intra-org and cross domain) to perform similar message filtering and validation. `[Ref: Microsoft Anti Spoofing]` `[Ref: ACSC Email Spoofing]` Note that additional filtering may be necessary if emails are coming from legitimate sources.

techniques.fullNamePt: Exclusive Control
techniques.descriptionPt:
Adversaries who successfully compromise a system may attempt to maintain persistence by “closing the door” behind them  – in other words, by preventing other threat actors from initially accessing or maintaining a foothold on the same system. 

Por exemplo, adversaries may patch a vulnerable, compromised system `[Ref: Mandiant-iab-control]` `[Ref: CERT AT Fortinent Ransomware 2025]` to prevent other threat actors from leveraging that vulnerability in the future. They may “close the door” in other ways, such as disabling vulnerable services `[Ref: sophos-multiple-attackers]`, stripping privileges from accounts `[Ref: aquasec-postgres-processes]`, or removing other malware already on the compromised device. `[Ref: fsecure-netsky]`

Hindering other threat actors may allow an adversary to maintain sole access to a compromised system or network. This prevents the threat actor from needing to compete with or even being removed themselves by other threat actors. It also reduces the “noise” in the environment, lowering the possibility of being caught and evicted by defenders. Finally, in the case of **Resource Hijacking** (`T1496`), leveraging a compromised device’s full power allows the threat actor to maximize profit. `[Ref: sophos-multiple-attackers]`

detections.name: Detection Strategy for Exclusive Control

analytics.name: Analytic 0045
analytics.descriptionPt: Detects unusual command executions and service modifications that indicate self-patching or disabling of vulnerable services post-compromise. Defenders should monitor for service stop commands, suspicious process termination, and execution of binaries or scripts aligned with known patching or service management tools outside of expected admin contexts.

mutableElements.description: Tunable list of critical or vulnerable services that defenders want to monitor for unexpected disabling.
Defines correlation window (e.g., 5–15 minutes) between suspicious command execution and subsequent process termination.

techniques.fullNamePt: Wi-Fi Networks
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem gain initial access to target systems by connecting to wireless networks. They may accomplish this by exploiting open Wi-Fi networks used by target devices or by accessing secured Wi-Fi networks — requiring **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) — belonging to a organização alvo. `[Ref: DOJ GRU Charges 2018]` `[Ref: Nearest Neighbor Volexity]` Establishing a connection to a Wi-Fi access point requires a certain level of proximity to both discover and maintain a stable network connection. 

Os adversários podem estabelecer a wireless connection through various methods, such as by physically positioning themselves near a Wi-Fi network to conduct close access operations. To bypass the need for physical proximity, adversaries may attempt to remotely compromise nearby third-party systems that have both wired and wireless network connections available (i.e., dual-homed systems). These third-party compromised devices can then serve as a bridge to connect to a target’s Wi-Fi network. `[Ref: Nearest Neighbor Volexity]`

Uma vez que an initial wireless connection is achieved, adversaries may leverage this access for follow-on activities in the victim network or further targeting of specific devices on the network. Os adversários podem realizar **Network Sniffing** (`T1040`) or **Adversary-in-the-Middle** (`T1557`) activities for **Credential Access** (`TA0006`) or **Discovery** (`TA0007`).

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.descriptionPt: Harden access requirements for Wi-Fi networks through using two or more pieces of evidence to authenticate, such as a username and password in addition to a token from a physical smart card or token generator.
mitigations.bypassHint: Vetores de contorno de MFA: (1) Roubo de Session Cookies / PRT (Primary Refresh Token) já autenticados a partir do endpoint da vítima (`T1539` / `T1528`); (2) Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Reverse Proxy Phishing (ex: Evilginx2 - `T1557`) para capturar o token de sessão pós-MFA; (3) Device Code Phishing (`T1528`) ou abuso de Refresh Tokens OAuth; (4) Se o utilizador já tem sessão num host interno, operar por SOCKS proxy através do beacon na estação da vítima (`T1090.001`).

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Network segmentation pode ser utilizado para isolate infrastructure components that do not require broad network access. Separate networking environments for Wi-Fi and Ethernet-wired networks, particularly where Ethernet-based networks allow for access to sensitive resources.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que all wired and/or wireless traffic is encrypted appropriately. Use best practices for authentication protocols, such as Kerberos, and ensure that web traffic that may contain credentials is protected by SSL/TLS.

techniques.fullNamePt: Cloud Application Integration
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem achieve persistence by leveraging OAuth application integrations in a software-as-a-service environment. Os adversários podem criar a custom application, add a legitimate application into the environment, or even co-opt an existing integration to achieve malicious ends. `[Ref: Push Security SaaS Persistence 2022]` `[Ref: SaaS Attacks GitHub Evil Twin Integrations]`

OAuth is an open standard that allows users to authorize applications to access their information on their behalf. In a SaaS environment such as Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, users may integrate applications to improve their workflow and achieve tasks.  

Leveraging application integrations may allow adversaries to persist in an environment – for example, by granting consent to an application from a high-privileged adversary-controlled account com o objetivo de maintain access to its data, even in the event of losing access to the account. `[Ref: Wiz Midnight Blizzard 2024]` `[Ref: Microsoft Malicious OAuth Applications 2022]` `[Ref: Huntress Persistence Microsoft 365 Compromise 2024]` In some cases, integrations may remain valid even after the original consenting user account is disabled. `[Ref: Push Security Slack Persistence 2023]` Application integrations may also allow adversaries para contornar (bypass) multi-factor authentication requirements through the use of **Application Access Token** (`T1550.001`)s. Finally, they may enable persistent **Automated Exfiltration** (`T1020`) over time. `[Ref: Synes Cyber Corner Malicious Azure Application 2023]`

Creating or adding a new application may require the adversary to create a dedicated **Cloud Account** (`T1136.003`) for the application and assign it **Additional Cloud Roles** (`T1098.003`) – for example, in Microsoft 365 environments, an application can only access resources via an associated service principal. `[Ref: Microsoft Entra ID Service Principals]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: SaaS Attacks GitHub Evil Twin Integrations]
[Ref: Synes Cyber Corner Malicious Azure Application 2023]

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not allow users to add new application integrations into a SaaS environment. In Entra ID environments, consider enforcing the “Do not allow user consent” option. `[Ref: Microsoft Entra Configurar OAuth Consent]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Periodically review SaaS integrations for unapproved or potentially malicious applications.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

techniques.fullNamePt: Virtual Machine Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode attempt to enumerate running máquina virtual (VM)s (VMs) after gaining access to a host or hypervisor. Por exemplo, adversaries may enumerate a list of VMs on an ESXi hypervisor using a **Hypervisor CLI** (`T1059.012`) such as `esxcli` or `vim-cmd` (e.g. `esxcli vm process list or vim-cmd vmsvc/getallvms`). `[Ref: Crowdstrike Hypervisor Jackpotting Pt 2 2021]` `[Ref: TrendMicro Play]` Os adversários podem também directly leverage a interface gráfica (GUI), such as VMware vCenter, com o objetivo de view máquina virtual (VM)s on a host. 

Os adversários podem utilizar the information from **Virtual Machine Discovery** (`T1673`) during discovery to shape follow-on behaviors. Subsequently discovered VMs may be leveraged for follow-on activities such as **Service Stop** (`T1489`) or **Data Encrypted for Impact** (`T1486`). `[Ref: Crowdstrike Hypervisor Jackpotting Pt 2 2021]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Input Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem simulate keystrokes on a victim’s computer by various means to perform any type of action on behalf of the user, such as launching the command interpreter using keyboard shortcuts,  typing an inline script to be executed, or interacting directly with a GUI-based application.  These actions can be preprogrammed into adversary tooling or executed through physical devices such as Human Interface Devices (HIDs).

Por exemplo, adversaries have used tooling that monitors the Windows message loop to detect when a user visits bank-specific URLs. If detected, the tool then simulates keystrokes to open the developer console or select the address bar, pastes malicious JavaScript from the clipboard, and executes it - enabling manipulation of content within the browser, such as replacing bank account numbers during transactions. `[Ref: BleepingComputer BackSwap]` `[Ref: welivesecurity BackSwap]`

Adversaries have also used malicious USB devices to emulate keystrokes that launch PowerShell, leading to the download and execution of malware from adversary-controlled servers. `[Ref: BleepingComputer USB]`

mitigations.name: Limit Hardware Installation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit the use of USB devices and removable media within a network.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Denylist scripting and use application control where appropriate. Por exemplo, PowerShell Constrained Language mode pode ser utilizado para restrict access to sensitive or otherwise dangerous language elements such as those used to execute arbitrary Windows APIs or files (e.g., `Add-Type`). `[Ref: Microsoft PowerShell CLM]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.fullNamePt: ESXi Administration Command
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de ESXi administration services to execute commands on guest machines hosted within an ESXi virtual environment. Persistent background services on ESXi-hosted VMs, such as the VMware Tools Daemon Service, allow for remote management from the ESXi server. The tools daemon service runs as `vmtoolsd.exe` on Windows guest sistema operativos, `vmware-tools-daemon` on macOS, and `vmtoolsd ` on Linux. `[Ref: Broadcom VMware Tools Services]` 

Os adversários podem tirar partido de a variety of tools to execute commands on ESXi-hosted VMs – for example, by using the vSphere Web Services SDK to programmatically execute commands and scripts via APIs such as `StartProgramInGuest`, `ListProcessesInGuest`,  `ListFileInGuest`, and `InitiateFileTransferFromGuest`. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence VMWare ESXi Zero-Day 2023]` `[Ref: Broadcom Running Guest OS Operations]` This may enable follow-on behaviors on the guest VMs, such as **File and Directory Discovery** (`T1083`), **Data from Local System** (`T1005`), or **OS Credential Dumping** (`T1003`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: If not required, restrict the permissions of users to perform Guest Operations on ESXi-hosted VMs. `[Ref: Broadcom Virtual Machine Guest Operations Privileges]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Poisoned Pipeline Execution
techniques.descriptionPt: Os adversários podem manipular continuous integration / continuous development (CI/CD) processes by injecting código malicioso into the build process. There are several mechanisms for poisoning pipelines: * In a Direct Pipeline Execution scenario, the threat actor directly modifies the CI configuration file (e.g., `gitlab-ci.yml` in GitLab). They may include a command to exfiltrate credentials leveraged in the build process to a remote server, or to export them as a workflow artifact. `[Ref: Unit 42 Palo Alto GitHub Actions Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) Attack 2025]` `[Ref: OWASP CICD-SEC-4]` * In an Indirect Pipeline Execution scenario, the threat actor injects código malicioso into files referenced by the CI configuration file. These may include makefiles, scripts, unit tests, and linters. `[Ref: OWASP CICD-SEC-4]` * In a Public Pipeline Execution scenario, the threat actor does not have direct access to the repository but instead creates a malicious pull request from a fork that triggers a part of the CI/CD pipeline. Por exemplo, in GitHub Actions, the `pull_request_target` trigger allows workflows running from forked repositories to access secrets. If this trigger is combined with an explicit pull request checkout and a location for a threat actor to insert código malicioso (e.g., an `npm build` command), a threat actor may be able to leak pipeline credentials. `[Ref: Unit 42 Palo Alto GitHub Actions Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) Attack 2025]` `[Ref: GitHub Security Lab GitHub Actions Security 2021]` Similarly, threat actors may craft pull requests with malicious inputs (such as branch names) if the build pipeline treats those inputs as trusted. `[Ref: Wiz Ultralytics AI Library Hijack 2024]` `[Ref: Synactiv Hijacking GitHub Runners]` `[Ref: GitHub Security Labs GitHub Actions Security Part 2 2021]` Finally, if a pipeline leverages a self-hosted runner, a threat actor may be able to execute código arbitrário on a host inside the organization’s network. `[Ref: John Stawinski PyTorch Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) Attack 2024]` By poisoning CI/CD pipelines, threat actors may be able para obter acesso a credentials, laterally move to additional hosts, or input malicious components to be shipped further down the pipeline (i.e., **Supply Chain Compromise** (`T1195`)).
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Unit 42 Palo Alto GitHub Actions Supply Chain (cadeia de fornecimento) Attack 2025]
[Ref: GitHub Security Lab GitHub Actions Security 2021]

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que CI/CD pipelines only have permissions they require to complete their operations. Additionally, limit the number of users who have write access to internal repositories to only those necessary.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Where possible, avoid allowing pipelines to run unreviewed code. Where this is necessary, ensure that these pipelines are executed on isolated nodes without access to secrets. In GitHub, avoid using the `pull_request_target` trigger if possible, do not treat user-controlled inputs (such as branch names) as trusted, and do not use self-hosted runners on public repositories.

techniques.fullNamePt: Delay Execution
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem employ various time-based methods para evadir deteção and analysis. These techniques often exploit system clocks, delays, or timing mechanisms to obscure malicious activity, blend in with benign activity, and avoid scrutiny. Adversaries can perform this behavior within virtualization/sandbox environments or natively on host systems. 

Os adversários podem utilize programmatic `sleep` commands or native system scheduling functionality, for example **Scheduled Task/Job** (`T1053`). Benign commands or other operations may also be used to delay malware execution or ensure prior commands have had time to execute properly. Loops or otherwise needless repetitions of commands, such as `ping`, pode ser empregue para delay malware execution and potentially exceed time thresholds of automated analysis environments. `[Ref: Revil Independence Day]` `[Ref: Netskope Nitol]` Another variation, commonly referred to as API hammering, involves making various calls to Native API functions com o objetivo de delay execution (while also potentially overloading analysis environments with junk data). `[Ref: Joe Sec Nymaim]` `[Ref: Joe Sec Trickbot]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Selective Exclusion
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem intentionally exclude certain files, folders, directories, file types, or system components from encryption or tampering during a ransomware or malicious payload execution. Some file extensions that adversaries may avoid encrypting include `.dll`, `.exe`, and `.lnk`. `[Ref: Palo Alto Unit 42 Medusa Group Medusa Ransomware January 2024]`  

Os adversários podem realizar this behavior to avoid alerting users, para evadir deteção by security tools and analysts, or, in the case of ransomware, to ensure that the system remains operational enough to deliver the ransom notice. 

Exclusions may target files and components whose corruption would cause instability, break core services, or immediately expose the attack. By carefully avoiding these areas, adversaries maintain system responsiveness while minimizing indicators that could trigger alarms or otherwise inhibit achieving their goals.

techniques.fullNamePt: Local Storage Discovery
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem enumerar local drives, disks, and/or volumes and their attributes like total or free space and volume serial number. This can be done to prepare for ransomware-related encryption, to perform **Lateral Movement** (`TA0109`), or as a precursor to **Direct Volume Access** (`T1006`). 

On ESXi systems, adversaries may use **Hypervisor CLI** (`T1059.012`) commands such as `esxcli` to list storage connected to the host as well as `.vmdk` files. `[Ref: TrendMicro]` `[Ref: TrendMicro ESXI Ransomware]`

On Windows systems, adversaries can use `wmic logicaldisk get` to find information about local network drives. They can also use `Get-PSDrive` in PowerShell to retrieve drives and may additionally use Windows API functions such as `GetDriveType`. `[Ref: Trend Micro MUSTANG PANDA PUBLOAD HIUPAN SEPTEMBER 2024]` `[Ref: Volexity]`

Linux has commands such as `parted`, `lsblk`, `fdisk`, `lshw`, and `df` that can list information about disk partitions such as size, type, sistema de ficheiros types, and free space. The command `diskutil` on MacOS pode ser utilizado para list disks while `system_profiler SPStorageDataType` can additionally show information such as a volume’s mount path, sistema de ficheiros, and the type of drive in the system. 

Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) cloud providers also have commands for storage discovery such as `describe volume` in AWS, `gcloud compute disks list` in GCP, and `az disk list` in Azure. `[Ref: AWS docs describe volumes]` `[Ref: GCP gcloud compute disks list]` `[Ref: azure az disk]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Search Threat Vendor Data
techniques.descriptionPt:
Threat actors may seek information/indicators from closed or open threat intelligence sources gathered about their own campaigns, as well as those conducted by other adversaries that may align with their target industries, capabilities/objectives, or other operational concerns. These reports may include descriptions of behavior, detailed breakdowns of attacks, atomic indicators such as malware hashes or IP addresses, timelines of a group’s activity, and more. Os adversários podem change their behavior when planning their future operations. 

Adversaries have been observed replacing atomic indicators mentioned in blog posts in under a week. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence VMWare ESXi Zero-Day 2023]` Adversaries have also been seen searching for their own domain names in threat vendor data and then taking them down, likely to avoid seizure or further investigation. `[Ref: Sentinel One Contagious Interview ClickFix September 2025]`

This technique is distinct from **Threat Intel Vendors** (`T1597.001`) in that it describes threat actors performing reconnaissance on their own activity, not in search of victim information.

techniques.fullNamePt: Query Public AI Services
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem consultar (query) publicly accessible artificial intelligence (AI) services, such as large language models (LLMs), to support targeting and operations. Adicionalmente a searching websites or databases directly (i.e., **Search Open Websites/Domains** (`T1593`)), adversaries may use AI services to synthesize, aggregate, and analyze publicly available information at scale. This may include identifying individuals or organizations to target, researching organizational structures and personnel, identifying technologies used by organização alvos, researching business relationships to develop plausible pretexts for **Social Engineering** (`T1684`) approaches, identifying contact information for use in **Phishing** (`T1566`) or **Phishing for Information** (`T1598`), or gathering derogatory or informação sensível about individuals that may be used for extortion or coercion. `[Ref: MSFT-AI]` `[Ref: GTIG AI Threat Tracker]`

Information gathered through AI services may be leveraged for other behaviors, such as establishing operational resources (i.e., **Generate Content** (`T1683`) or **Establish Accounts** (`T1585`). For obtaining access to AI tools and services, see **Artificial Intelligence** (`T1588.007`).
