techniques.fullNamePt: Generate Content
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or generate content to support targeting and operations. This content pode ser empregue para establish personas, impersonate known individuals or organizations, and support **Social Engineering** (`T1684`), fraud, or influence activities. Written materials, audio, images, video, or other media may be developed and tailored to the target and objective. `[Ref: IBM AI-Generated Content]`

Content development may occur prior to or during an operation. Os adversários podem desenvolver or generate content in-house, source it through third parties, or produce it using AI-assisted tools. Os adversários podem utilizar AI to research targets, develop pretexts, and better understand the organizations and individuals they intend to target or deceive prior to generating content (i.e., **Query Public AI Services** (`T1682`)); for obtaining access to AI tools used in content generation, see **Artificial Intelligence** (`T1588.007`). 

Content may be leveraged in support of techniques such as **Phishing** (`T1566`), **Phishing for Information** (`T1598`), **Social Engineering** (`T1684`), **Financial Theft** (`T1657`), or **Establish Accounts** (`T1585`). Generated or developed content does not include código malicioso or scripts (i.e., **Develop Capabilities** (`T1587`) and **Artificial Intelligence** (`T1588.007`)).

techniques.fullNamePt: Generate Content: Written Content
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem criar or tailor written materials to support targeting and malicious operations. Content may include phishing lures, fraudulent financial communications, fabricated job postings, fabricated employment credentials and documentation, decoy documents, social media persona content, and supporting narratives used to sustain fabricated personas over time. `[Ref: GenAI Phishing]` `[Ref: GTIG AI Threat Tracker]` Content may be authored manually, commissioned through third parties, or produced using AI-assisted tools.

Written materials may impersonate legitimate government correspondence, diplomatic communications, or internal organizational documents to support targeting efforts. AI-assisted tools may also be used to tailor content to specific targets, industries, or regions. Por exemplo, adversaries may leverage AI to translate content into a target's native language or mimic the communication style of trusted senders.

Written content produced through these methods may be used in support of other techniques, such as **Phishing** (`T1660`), **Spearphishing via Service** (`T1566.003`), **Phishing for Information** (`T1598`), **Internal Spearphishing** (`T1534`), **Social Engineering** (`T1684`), **Financial Theft** (`T1657`), or **Establish Accounts** (`T1585`).

Written content does not include código malicioso or scripts; for development of código malicioso and scripts, see **Develop Capabilities** (`T1587`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Social Engineering
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar engenharia social techniques to influence users to take actions that result in unauthorized access, approval of changes, disclosure of informação sensível, or execution of adversary-supplied instructions (i.e., introduction of malicious payloads or software), while minimizing technical indicators. 

Os adversários podem tirar partido de trust-building methods across multiple channels (e.g., executive, vendor, or help desk scenarios, including AI-enabled voice interactions) to prompt user-authorized actions such as password resets, MFA changes, financial approvals, or the disclosure of informação sensível. Os adversários podem também leverage common business communications and workflows such as email, collaboration platforms, voice communications, recruiting processes, help desk interactions, and SaaS consent mechanisms to make malicious requests appear routine and legitimate. `[Ref: Proofpoint TA427 April 2024]` `[Ref: SE SentinelOne 2]` `[Ref: SE - Hackers Target Workday]`

Additionally, adversaries have persuaded victims to take actions through references of current events, harnessing relevant themes to the work role or the organizations mission. Por exemplo, adversaries may use scare tactics (i.e., threaten repercussions for non-compliance) or otherwise incite victims’ emotions com o objetivo de generate a sense of urgency to take action. `[Ref: SE Proofpoint]` `[Ref: SE SentinelOne]`

This technique may include common engenharia social patterns such as **Phishing** (`T1566`) and **Spearphishing Voice** (`T1566.004`), often supported by convincing and targeted narratives. `[Ref: SE SentinelOne 2]` `[Ref: Fortinet Trends 25-26]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Social Engineering: Impersonation
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem impersonate a trusted person or organization com o objetivo de persuade and trick a target into performing some action on their behalf. Por exemplo, adversaries may communicate with victims (via **Phishing for Information** (`T1598`), **Phishing** (`T1566`), or **Internal Spearphishing** (`T1534`)) while impersonating a known sender such as an executive, colleague, or third-party vendor. Established trust can then be leveraged to accomplish an adversary’s ultimate goals, possibly against multiple victims.

In many cases of business email compromise or email fraud campaigns, adversaries use impersonation to defraud victims -- deceiving them into sending money or divulging information that ultimately enables **Financial Theft** (`T1657`).

Adversaries will often also use engenharia social techniques such as manipulative and persuasive language in email subject lines and body text such as `payment`, `request`, or `urgent` to push the victim to act quickly before malicious activity is detected. These campaigns are often specifically targeted against people who, due to job roles and/or accesses, can carry out the adversary’s goal.  

Impersonation is typically preceded by reconnaissance techniques such as **Gather Victim Identity Information** (`T1589`) and **Gather Victim Org Information** (`T1591`) as well as acquiring infrastructure such as email domains (i.e. **Domains** (`T1583.001`)) to substantiate their false identity. `[Ref: Crowdstrike BEC]`

There is the potential for multiple victims in campaigns involving impersonation. Por exemplo, an adversary may Compromise Accounts targeting one organization which can then be used to support impersonation against other entities. `[Ref: VEC]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Social Engineering: Email Spoofing
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem fake, or spoof, a sender’s identity by modifying the value of relevant email headers com o objetivo de establish contact with victims under false pretenses. `[Ref: Proofpoint TA427 April 2024]` Adicionalmente a actual email content, email headers (such as the FROM header, which contains the email address of the sender) may also be modified. Email clients display these headers when emails appear in a victim's inbox, which may cause modified emails to appear as if they were from the spoofed entity.

Enterprise environments can use Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC) as an email authentication protocol that references results of the Sender Policy Framework (SPF) and DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) configurations. SPF and DKIM are configured separately in DNS: SPF verifies that the sending server is authorized for the domain, while DKIM uses a digital signature to verify email integrity and domain authentication. Together, they validate email authenticity and specify how receiving servers should handle authentication failures. Without enforced identity authentication, adversaries may compromise the integrity of an authentication check with altered headers that would not have otherwise passed. `[Ref: Cloudflare DMARC, DKIM, and SPF]` `[Ref: DMARC-overview]` `[Ref: Proofpoint-DMARC]`

An example of a weak or absent DMARC policy is `v=DMARC1; p=none; fo=1;`. The `p=none`. The `p=none` indicates no action should be taken, and therefore no filtering action will take place, even if an email fails authentication checks (i.e., SPF and/or DKIM fail). When a DMARC policy indicates no action, the email will still be delivered to the victim’s inbox. `[Ref: ic3-dprk]` 

Adversaries have abused weak or absent DMARC policies to circumvent authentication checks and conceal engenharia social attempts. Adversaries can alter email headers to include legitimate domain names with fake usernames or impersonate legitimate users via **Impersonation** (`T1684.001`) for **Phishing** (`T1566`). Additionally, adversaries may abuse Microsoft 365’s Direct Send functionality to spoof internal users by using internal devices like printers to send emails without authentication. `[Ref: Barnea DirectSend]`

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use anti-spoofing and email authentication mechanisms to filter messages based on validity checks of the sender domain (using SPF) and integrity of messages (using DKIM). Enabling these mechanisms within an organization (through policies such as DMARC) may enable recipients (intra-org and cross domain) to perform similar message filtering and validation. `[Ref: Microsoft Anti Spoofing]` `[Ref: ACSC Email Spoofing]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem disable, degrade, or tamper with security tools or applications (e.g., Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) (EDR) tools, intrusion detection systems (IDS), antivírus (AV), logging agents, sensors, etc.) to impair or reduce visibility of defensive capabilities. This may include stopping specific services, killing processes, modifying or deleting tool ficheiros de configuração and Registry keys, or preventing tools from updating. This may also include impairing defenses more broadly by disrupting preventative, detection, and response mechanisms across host, network, and cloud environments. `[Ref: SCADAfence_ransomware]` 

Adicionalmente a directly targeting tools, adversaries may block or manipulate indicators and telemetry used for detection. This includes maliciously disabling or redirecting sensors such as Event Tracing for Windows (ETW), modifying event log configurations (e.g., redirecting Security logs), or interfering with logging pipelines and forwarding mechanisms (e.g., SIEM ingestion). `[Ref: Microsoft Lamin Sept 2017]` `[Ref: ETW Palantir]`

More advanced techniques include leveraging legitimate drivers or debugging mechanisms to render tools non-functional, bypassing anti-tampering protections, and targeting specific defenses such as Sysmon or cloud monitoring agents. Os adversários podem também disrupt broader defensive operations, including update mechanisms, logging infrastructure (e.g., syslog), or event aggregation, further degrading an organization’s ability to detect and respond to malicious activity. `[Ref: Cocomazzi FIN7 Reboot]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper user permissions are in place to prevent adversaries from disabling or interfering with security services.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Periodically verify that tools are functioning appropriately – for example, that all expected hosts with EDRs or monitoring agents are checking in to the central console. Check EDRs to ensure that no unexpected exclusion paths have been added. In Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, exclusions can be reviewed with the `Get-MpPreference` cmdlet. `[Ref: CodeX Microsoft Defender 2021]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper process and file permissions are in place to prevent adversaries from disabling or interfering with security services.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider removing previous versions of tools that are unnecessary to the environment when possible.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Consider automatically relaunching forwarding mechanisms at recurring intervals (ex: temporal, on-logon, etc.) as well as applying appropriate change management to firewall rules and other related system configurations.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Utilizar Application Control (ex: AppLocker / WDAC) where appropriate, especially regarding the execution of tools outside of the organization's security policies (such as rootkit removal tools) that have been abused to impair system defenses. Garantir que only approved security applications are used and running on enterprise systems.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Ensure proper Registry permissions are in place to prevent adversaries from disabling or interfering with security services.

bypasses: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

techniques.nameEn: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log
techniques.fullNameEn: Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log
techniques.namePt: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log
techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem desativar or modify the Windows Event Log to limit data that can be leveraged for detections and audits. Windows Event Log records user and system activity such as login attempts and process creation. `[Ref: EventLog_Core_Technologies]` This data is used by security tools and analysts to generate detections. 

The EventLog service maintains event logs from various system components and applications. Por omissão, the service automatically starts when a system powers on. An audit policy, maintained by the Local Security Policy (secpol.msc), defines which system events the EventLog service logs. Security audit policy settings can be changed by running secpol.msc, then navigating to `Security Settings\Local Policies\Audit Policy` for basic audit policy settings or `Security Settings\Advanced Audit Policy Configuration` for advanced audit policy settings. `[Ref: Microsoft Auditar regularmente Policy]` `[Ref: Microsoft Adv Security Settings]` `auditpol.exe` may also be used to set audit policies. `[Ref: Microsoft auditpol]`

Os adversários podem target system-wide logging or just that of a particular application. Por exemplo, the Windows EventLog service may be disabled using the `Set-Service -Name EventLog -Status Stopped` or `sc config eventlog start=disabled` commands (followed by manually stopping the service using `Stop-Service -Name EventLog`). Additionally, the service may be disabled by modifying the "Start" value in `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\EventLog` then restarting the system for the change to take effect. `[Ref: Disable_Win_Event_Logging]` `[Ref: disable_win_evt_logging]`

There are several ways to disable the EventLog service via registry key modification. Without Administrator privileges, adversaries may modify the "Start" value in the key `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\WMI\Autologger\EventLog-Security`, then reboot the system to disable the Security EventLog. `[Ref: winser19_file_overwrite_bug_twitter]` With Administrator privilege, adversaries may modify the same values in `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\WMI\Autologger\EventLog-System` and `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\WMI\Autologger\EventLog-Application` to disable the entire EventLog.

Additionally, adversaries may use `auditpol` and its sub-commands in a command prompt to disable auditing or clear the audit policy. To enable or disable a specified setting or audit category, adversaries may use the `/success` or `/failure` parameters. Por exemplo, `auditpol /set /category:"Account Logon" /success:disable /failure:disable` turns off auditing for the Account Logon category. `[Ref: auditpol.exe_STRONTIC]` To clear the audit policy, adversaries may run the following lines: `auditpol /clear /y` or `auditpol /remove /allusers`. `[Ref: T1562.002_redcanaryco]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Cloud Log
techniques.descriptionPt:
Um adversário pode disable or modify cloud logging capabilities and integrations to limit what data is collected on their activities and avoid detection. Cloud environments allow for collection and analysis of audit and application logs that provide insight into what activities a user does within the environment. If an adversary has sufficient permissions, they can disable or modify logging para evitar deteção of their activities. 

Por exemplo, in AWS an adversary may disable CloudWatch/CloudTrail integrations prior to conducting further malicious activity. They may alternatively tamper with logging functionality, for example, by removing any associated SNS topics, disabling multi-region logging, or disabling settings that validate and/or encrypt log files. `[Ref: AWS Cloud Trail]` `[Ref: Pacu Detection Disruption Module]` In Office 365, an adversary may disable logging on mail collection activities for specific users by using the Set-MailboxAuditBypassAssociation cmdlet, by disabling M365 Advanced Auditing for the user, or by downgrading the user’s license from an Enterprise E5 to an Enterprise E3 license. `[Ref: Dark Reading]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify Tools: Modify or Spoof Tool UI
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem falsificar (spoof) or manipulate security tool user interfaces (UIs) to falsely indicate tools are functioning normally and delay detection and response. 

Os adversários podem present misleading or falsified security tool interfaces (UIs) that display normal or healthy status indicators, even when underlying security tools have been disabled, degraded, or otherwise tampered with. Security tools typically provide visibility into system health, alerting, and operational status; by misrepresenting this information, adversaries can undermine defender trust in these signals and obscure the true security posture of the system. 

This behavior is often used in conjunction with efforts to disable or modify tools, where adversaries first impair the functionality of defenses (e.g., EDR, logging agents) and then replace or mimic their interfaces to conceal the loss of visibility. By maintaining the appearance of normal operations, such as showing active protection, successful updates, or absence of threats, adversaries can delay investigation and response, enabling continued malicious activity. 

Por exemplo, adversaries may display a fake Windows Security interface or system tray icon indicating a “protected” or “healthy” state after disabling Windows Defender or related services. `[Ref: BlackBasta]`

techniques.nameEn: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System Log
techniques.fullNameEn: Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System Log
techniques.namePt: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System Log
techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System Log
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem desativar or modify the Linux Auditar regularmente system to hide malicious activity and avoid detection. Linux admins use the Linux Auditar regularmente system to track security-relevant information on a system. The Linux Auditar regularmente system operates at the kernel-level and maintains event logs on application and system activity such as process, network, file, and login events based on pre-configured rules. 

Often referred to as `auditd`, this is the name of the daemon used to write events to disk and is governed by the parameters set in the `audit.conf` configuration file. Two primary ways to configure the log generation rules are through the command line `auditctl` utility and the file `/etc/audit/audit.rules`, containing a sequence of `auditctl` commands loaded at boot time. `[Ref: IzyKnows auditd threat detection 2022]` `[Ref: Red Hat Linux Disable or Mod]`

With root privileges, adversaries may be able to ensure their activity is not logged through disabling the Auditar regularmente system service, editing the configuration/rule files, or by hooking the Auditar regularmente system library functions. Using the command line, adversaries can disable the Auditar regularmente system service through killing processes associated with `auditd` daemon or use `systemctl` to stop the Auditar regularmente service. Adversaries can also hook Auditar regularmente system functions to disable logging or modify the rules contained in the `/etc/audit/audit.rules` or `audit.conf` files to ignore malicious activity. `[Ref: ESET Ebury Feb 2014]`
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Red Hat Linux Disable or Mod]

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: An adversary must already have root level access on the local system to make full use of this technique; be sure to restrict users and accounts to the least privileges they require.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt:
Routinely check account role permissions to ensure only expected users and roles have permission to modify logging settings.

To ensure Auditar regularmente rules can not be modified at runtime, add the `auditctl -e 2` as the last command in the audit.rules files. Uma vez que started, any attempt to change the configuration in this mode will be audited and denied. The configuration can only be changed by rebooting the machine.

techniques.fullNameEn: Disable or Modify Tools: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify Tools: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem clear Windows Event Logs to hide the activity of an intrusion. Windows Event Logs are a record of a computer's alerts and notifications. There are three system-defined sources of events: System, Application, and Security, with five event types: Error, Warning, Information, Success Audit, and Failure Audit.

With administrator privileges, the event logs can be cleared with the following utility commands:

* `wevtutil cl system`
* `wevtutil cl application`
* `wevtutil cl security`

These logs may also be cleared through other mechanisms, such as the event viewer GUI or **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`). Por exemplo, adversaries may use the PowerShell command `Remove-EventLog -LogName Security` to delete the Security EventLog and after reboot, disable future logging. Note: events may still be generated and logged in the .evtx file between the time the command is run and the reboot. `[Ref: disable_win_evt_logging]`

Os adversários podem também attempt to clear logs by directly deleting the stored log files within `C:\Windows\System32\winevt\logs\`.

techniques.fullNameEn: Disable or Modify Tools: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
techniques.namePt: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify Tools: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem clear system logs to hide evidence of an intrusion. macOS and Linux both keep track of system or user-initiated actions via system logs. The majority of native system logging is stored under the `/var/log/` directory. Subfolders in this directory categorize logs by their related functions, such as: `[Ref: Linux Logs]`

* `/var/log/messages:`: General and system-related messages
* `/var/log/secure or /var/log/auth.log`: Authentication logs
* `/var/log/utmp or /var/log/wtmp`: Login records
* `/var/log/kern.log`: Kernel logs
* `/var/log/cron.log`: Crond logs
* `/var/log/maillog`: Mail server logs
* `/var/log/httpd/`: Web server access and error logs

techniques.fullNameEn: Disable or Modify Tools: Impair Autonomous Defenses
techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify Tools: Impair Autonomous Defenses
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilizar methods like **Indirect Prompt Injection** (`T1698`) to disrupt, disable, or otherwise impair autonomous defensive capabilities such as LLM-assisted processing of malware, artifacts, or activity. `[Ref: Prompt Injection LLM-Powered SOC Assistants]` This behavior may cause a system to ignore data, fail to alert on malicious activity, abort analysis, or to be disabled completely. 

Os adversários podem include content in malware implants that mimic an LLM prompt scaffold that contains fake system messages com o objetivo de convince the LLM that it has encountered an error. `[Ref: MacOS.Gaslight Prompt Injection]` `[Ref: Gaslight AI triage prompt injection]` Dependendo de the type of error, the LLM may abort analysis, truncate, or refuse to continue. Os adversários podem também embed prompts in malware intended to stop agents or systems from analyzing the malware. `[Ref: Shai-Hulud May 2026]`

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent content contained within an artifact under analysis from directly controlling the analysis workflow, terminating analysis, altering required analysis stages, or initiating unrelated tools and actions. Forçar a aplicação de workflow transitions independently of instructions generated from artifact content.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Limit AI-assisted analysis systems to the files and directories required for analysis and prevent artifacts under investigation from modifying agent configuration, instruction files, analysis state, or other trusted AI application resources.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.descriptionPt: Require AI-assisted security analysis workflows to preserve analysis status, artifact provenance, tool execution, termination reason, and completion state so that incomplete or unexpectedly redirected analysis can be independently identified and reviewed.
mitigations.bypassHint: Aplicar Command-Line Spoofing (criar processo suspenso com argumentos benignos como `svchost.exe -k netsvcs`, alterar `PEB->ProcessParameters->CommandLine` para o comando real e resumir a thread - `T1036.004`), Parent PID Spoofing (`PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS` - `T1134.004`) e substituir ferramentas de CLI barulhentas (`whoami`, `net user`, `nltest`) por chamadas diretas a APIs Win32/LDAP via BOFs (Beacon Object Files) em memória.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent AI-assisted analysis agents from exercising privileged capabilities solely as a consequence of artifact-derived instructions. Require independent authorization for privileged or consequential operations outside the expected analysis workflow.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Run AI-assisted analysis services using dedicated identities with permissions limited to required analysis functions. Separate analysis authority from broader analyst, administrative, or production access.

techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify System Firewall
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem desativar or modify host-based or network firewalls to impair defensive mechanisms and enable further action. Uma vez que an adversary has gathered sufficient privileges, they can tamper with firewall services, policies, or rule sets to remove restrictions on inbound or outbound traffic. Por exemplo, this may include turning off firewall profiles, altering existing rules to permit previously blocked ports or protocols, or adding new rules that create covert communication paths (e.g., adding a new firewall rule for a well-known protocol (such as RDP) using a non-traditional and potentially less securitized port. `[Ref: change_rdp_port_conti]`

Os adversários podem desativar or modify firewalls using different behaviors, depending on the platform. Por exemplo, in ESXi, firewall rules may be modified directly via the esxcli (e.g., via esxcli network firewall set) or via the vCenter user interface. `[Ref: Broadcom ESXi Firewall]` `[Ref: Trellix Rnasomhouse 2024]`

mitigations.descriptionPt: Routinely check account role permissions to ensure only expected users and roles have permission to modify system firewalls.

techniques.fullNameEn: Disable or Modify System Firewall: Cloud Firewall
techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify System Firewall: Cloud Firewall
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem desativar or modify a firewall within a cloud environment para contornar (bypass) controls that limit access to cloud resources.

Cloud environments typically utilize restrictive security groups and firewall rules that only allow network activity from trusted IP addresses via expected ports and protocols. An adversary with appropriate permissions may introduce new firewall rules or policies to allow access into a victim cloud environment and/or move laterally from the cloud control plane to the data plane.

Por exemplo, an adversary may use a script or utility that creates new ingress rules in existing security groups (or creates new security groups entirely) to allow any TCP/IP connectivity to a cloud-hosted instance. They may also remove networking limitations to support traffic associated with malicious activity (such as cryptomining). `[Ref: Palo Alto Unit 42 Compromised Cloud Compute Credentials 2022]` `[Ref: Expel AWS]`

techniques.fullNameEn: Disable or Modify System Firewall: Network Device Firewall
techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify System Firewall: Network Device Firewall
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem desativar network device-based firewall mechanisms entirely or add, delete, or modify particular rules com o objetivo de bypass controls limiting network usage.  

Os adversários podem obter access to devices such as routers, switches, or other perimeter/network devices and change access control lists (ACLs), security zones, or policy rules to permit otherwise blocked traffic. Por exemplo, adversaries may add new network firewall rules to allow access to all internal network subnets without restrictions. Allowing access to internal network subsets may enable unrestricted inbound/outbound connectivity or open paths for Command and Control (C2) and lateral movement.

Os adversários podem obter access to network device management interfaces via **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) or by exploiting vulnerabilities. In some cases, threat actors may target firewalls and other network infrastructure that are exposed to the internet by leveraging weaknesses in public-facing applications (**Exploit Public-Facing Application** (`T1190`)). `[Ref: CVE-2024-55591 Detail]`

Os adversários podem também modify host networking configurations that indirectly manipulate system firewalls, such as adjusting interface bandwidth or network connection request thresholds.

techniques.fullNamePt: Disable or Modify System Firewall: Windows Host Firewall
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem desativar or modify the Windows host firewall para contornar (bypass) controls limiting network usage. This can include disabling the Windows host firewall entirely, suppressing specific profiles (domain, private, public), or adding, deleting, and modifying firewall rules to allow or restrict traffic. `[Ref: Nearest Neighbor Volexity]`

Os adversários podem realizar these modifications through multiple mechanisms depending on the Windows sistema operativo and access level. Por exemplo, adversaries may use command-line utilities (e.g., `netsh advfirewall` or PowerShell cmdlets like `Set-NetFirewallProfile`, `New-NetFirewallRule`), Windows Registry modifications (e.g., altering firewall states and rule configurations via registry keys), or the Windows Control Panel to modify firewall settings through the Windows Security interface.

By disabling or modifying Windows firewall services, adversaries may enable access to remote services, open ports for Command and Control (C2) traffic, or configure rules for further actions.

techniques.fullNamePt: Exploitation for Defense Impairment
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem explorar vulnerabilities in security software, infrastructure, or defensive components to degrade, disable, or otherwise continue to impair their ability to prevent, detect, or respond to malicious activity. 
 
Os adversários podem explorar a system or application vulnerability to directly interfere with defensive mechanisms. Exploitation occurs when an adversary takes advantage of a programming error in software, services, or the sistema operativo to execute adversary-controlled code, often with the goal of weakening or disabling protections. 

Vulnerabilities may exist in security tools such as antivírus (AV), Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) (EDR), firewalls, or other monitoring solutions. Os adversários podem utilizar prior reconnaissance or perform discovery activities (e.g., **Software Discovery** (`T1518`)) to identify defensive tools present in an environment and target them for exploitation. 

Successful exploitation may allow adversaries to terminate security processes, disable protections, bypass enforcement mechanisms, or reduce the effectiveness of controlos defensivos. In some cases, vulnerabilities in cloud-based or SaaS infrastructure may also be leveraged para contornar (bypass) built-in security boundaries or disrupt visibility and enforcement across environments. `[Ref: Salesforce zero-day in facebook phishing attack]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Safe Mode Boot
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem abusar de Windows safe mode to disable endpoint defenses. Safe mode starts up the Windows sistema operativo with a limited set of drivers and services. Third-party security software such as Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) (EDR) tools may not start after booting Windows in safe mode. There are two versions of safe mode: Safe Mode and Safe Mode with Networking. It is possible to start additional services after a safe mode boot. `[Ref: Microsoft Windows Startup Settings]` `[Ref: Sophos Safe Mode Boot]`

Os adversários podem abusar de safe mode to disable endpoint defenses that may not start with a limited boot. Hosts can be forced into safe mode after the next reboot via modifications to Boot Configuration Data (BCD) stores, which are files that manage boot application settings. `[Ref: Microsoft bcdedit]`

Os adversários podem também add their malicious applications to the list of minimal services that start in safe mode by modifying relevant Registry values (i.e. **Modify Registry** (`T1112`)). Malicious **Component Object Model** (`T1559.001`) (COM) objects may also be registered and loaded in safe mode. `[Ref: CyberArk Labs Safe Mode 2016]` `[Ref: Cybereason safe mode boot]` `[Ref: BleepingComputer REvil 2021]`

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.descriptionPt: Garantir que endpoint defenses run in safe mode. `[Ref: CyberArk Labs Safe Mode 2016]`

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict administrator accounts to as few individuals as possible, following least privilege principles, that may be abused to remotely boot a machine in safe mode. `[Ref: CyberArk Labs Safe Mode 2016]`
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Downgrade Attack
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem downgrade or use a version of system features that may be outdated, vulnerable, and/or does not support updated controlos de segurança. Downgrade attacks typically take advantage of a system’s backward compatibility to force it into less secure modes of operation.

Os adversários podem downgrade and use various less-secure versions of features of a system, such as **Command and Scripting Interpreter** (`T1059`) or even network protocols that pode ser abusado para enable **Adversary-in-the-Middle** (`T1557`) or **Network Sniffing** (`T1040`). `[Ref: Praetorian TLS Downgrade Attack 2014]` Por exemplo, **PowerShell** (`T1059.001`) versions 5+ includes Script Block Logging (SBL), which can record executed script content. Contudo, adversaries may attempt to execute a previous version of PowerShell that does not support SBL with the intent to impair defenses while running malicious scripts that may have otherwise been detected. `[Ref: CrowdStrike downgrade attack]` `[Ref: Google Cloud downgrade attack]` `[Ref: att_def_ps_logging]`

Os adversários podem similarly target tráfego de rede to downgrade from an encrypted HTTPS connection to an unsecured HTTP connection that exposes network data in clear text. `[Ref: Targeted SSL Stripping Attacks Are Real]` `[Ref: CrowdStrike Downgrade attack 2]` On Windows systems, adversaries may downgrade the boot manager to a vulnerable version that bypasses Secure Boot, granting the ability to disable various sistema operativo security mechanisms. `[Ref: SafeBreach]`

techniques.fullNamePt: Prevent Command History Logging
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem impair command history logging to hide commands they run num sistema comprometido. Various command interpreters keep track of the commands users type in their terminal so that users can retrace what they have done.

On Linux and macOS, command history is tracked in a file pointed to by the environment variable `HISTFILE`. When a user logs off a system, this information is flushed to a file in the user's home directory called `~/.bash_history`. The `HISTCONTROL` environment variable keeps track of what should be saved by the history command and eventually into the `~/.bash_history` file when a user logs out. `HISTCONTROL` does not exist by default on macOS, but can be set by the user and will be respected. The `HISTFILE` environment variable is also used in some ESXi systems. `[Ref: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence ESXi VIBs 2022]`

Os adversários podem clear the history environment variable (`unset HISTFILE`) or set the command history size to zero (`export HISTFILESIZE=0`) to prevent logging of commands. Additionally, `HISTCONTROL` can be configured to ignore commands that start with a space by simply setting it to "ignorespace". `HISTCONTROL` can also be set to ignore duplicate commands by setting it to "ignoredups". In some Linux systems, this is set by default to "ignoreboth" which covers both of the previous examples. This means that " ls" will not be saved, but "ls" would be saved by history. Adversaries can abuse this to operate without leaving traces by simply prepending a space to all of their terminal commands.

On Windows systems, the `PSReadLine` module tracks commands used in all PowerShell sessions and writes them to a file (`$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\PSReadLine\ConsoleHost_history.txt` by default). Os adversários podem change where these logs are saved using `Set-PSReadLineOption -HistorySavePath {File Path}`. This will cause `ConsoleHost_history.txt` to stop receiving logs. Additionally, it is possible to turn off logging to this file using the PowerShell command `Set-PSReadlineOption -HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing`. `[Ref: Microsoft about_History prevent command history]` `[Ref: Sophos PowerShell Command History Forensics]`

Os adversários podem também leverage a **Network Device CLI** (`T1059.008`) on network devices to disable historical command logging (e.g. `no logging`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Anti-Automation Evasion
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem employ various means to evade or complete automation checks. Automation checks distinguish human users from bot traffic and prevent bots from reaching the web pages protected by automation checks. Por exemplo, a user may be required to solve a CAPTCHA challenge before accessing a form or login page. Traditional CAPTCHAs ask the user to decipher a string of characters, type the characters into a box, and submit the form. reCAPTCHA asks the user to identify images, click a checkbox, or evaluate the user’s behavior from mouse movement and device cookies. `[Ref: CAPTCHAS Cloudflare]` 

Os adversários podem pay for a service that forwards the CAPTCHA challenge to a remote human worker. The human service then solves the CAPTCHA on behalf of the bot. `[Ref: CAPTCHA Bypass]` AI tools, such as CapSolver, pode também ser utilizado para automatically solve CAPTCHA challenges. `[Ref: Capsolver]`

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use web application firewalls, bot-management controls, and application-layer traffic filtering to restrict automated access to protected resources. Apply filtering using request characteristics, client/session reputation, behavioral signals, rate limits, and validated client or bot identity. Block, rate-limit, or challenge traffic that violates established access policies.
mitigations.bypassHint: Procurar protocolos alternativos abertos no host de destino: (1) Se RPC/DCOM alternativo ou portas altas estiverem acessíveis, usar DCOM (`MMC20.Application`, `ShellWindows` - `T1021.003`); (2) Se MSSQL (1433) estiver acessível, usar `xp_cmdshell` ou CLR Assemblies; (3) Se SSH (22) ou RDP (3389) estiverem abertos, usar RestrictedAdmin Mode (`sekurlsa::pth` + `mstsc /restrictedadmin` - `T1021.001`); (4) Abusar de partilhas de ficheiros ou GPOs / SCCM para implantação indireta (`T1072`).

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Deploy inline application-layer protections capable of identifying and preventing automated activity before requests reach protected application functionality. Use multiple automation signals rather than relying exclusively on successful CAPTCHA completion.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

techniques.fullNamePt: Anti-Automation Evasion: Automate CAPTCHA Completion
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar use bots to successfully solve CAPTCHA challenges. CAPTCHA challenges are typically used by defenders to detect and prevent bot and spam traffic from accessing protected webpages. CAPTCHAs are automated tests often placed before login screens or form fields. Traditional CAPTCHAs ask the user to decipher a string of characters, type the characters into a box, and submit the form. reCAPTCHA asks the user to identify images, click a checkbox, or evaluate the user’s behavior from mouse movement and device cookies. `[Ref: CAPTCHAS Cloudflare]` 

Os adversários podem utilizar scripts or toolkits to automatically solve the CAPTCHA puzzle. Por exemplo, adversaries may develop a script that uses the ImageMagick toolkit to solve the CAPTCHA puzzles to then create multiple valid accounts. ImageMagick tool can convert the images into a RGB complemented image. The CAPTCHA challenge may be solved by identifying and comparing attributes of the RGB images to select the expected image. `[Ref: Free Trial PurpleUrchin]` Uma vez que the CAPTCHA challenge is solved, the adversary’s script may access the protected page. After accessing the protected the page, the adversary may submit valid forms to the target.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Configurar inline bot-management and web application protections to continue enforcing automation controls after a client successfully completes a CAPTCHA. Use challenge-token state as one input rather than as a durable trust determination, and prevent requests that subsequently exhibit automated or abusive behavior.
mitigations.bypassHint: Adaptar o transporte de C2 ao tráfego permitido no ambiente: (1) Respeitar o Proxy Corporativo (WPAD / variáveis de ambiente / WinINet API que usa automaticamente credenciais NTLM/Kerberos do utilizador atual); (2) Usar Domain Fronting ou Web Services legítimos permitidos pela whitelist (GitHub, Microsoft Graph, OneDrive, Slack API - `T1102`); (3) Configurar Malleable C2 Profiles para imitar tráfego HTTPS legítimo e usar certificados TLS válidos com idade/reputação (`T1588.004`); (4) Caso HTTP/HTTPS esteja totalmente isolado, testar DNS Tunneling (`T1071.004`) ou pivotar via SMB Named Pipes (`T1090.001`) através de outro host com saída.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Do not treat successful CAPTCHA completion alone as sufficient evidence that subsequent activity is human-generated. Continue evaluating requests using bot classification, request rate, client/session characteristics, token reuse, source reputation, and behavioral signals after successful challenge completion. Block or rate-limit activity that remains inconsistent with expected human use.

techniques.fullNamePt: Anti-Automation Evasion: Avoid CAPTCHA
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem avoid CAPTCHA challenges by mimicking human behavior. Automation tests, such as CAPTCHA, are typically used by defenders to detect and prevent bot and spam traffic from accessing protected webpages. CAPTCHAs are often placed before login screens or form fields. Traditional CAPTCHAs ask the user to decipher a string of characters, type the characters into a box, and submit the form. reCAPTCHA asks the user to identify images, click a checkbox, or evaluate the user’s behavior from mouse movement and device cookies. `[Ref: CAPTCHAS Cloudflare]` 

Os adversários (ou operadores de Red Team) podem tentar avoid CAPTCHA challenges by constructing a bot that mimics human behavior through browser automation. The automated browser may mimic a human by **Masquerading** (`T1036`) a **Browser Fingerprint** (`T1036.012`) and through attributes such as session history, IP reputation, and the use of browser APIs. `[Ref: CAPTCHA Bypass Olostep]` Por exemplo, adversaries may use Selenium browsers to simulate a human user. In the Selenium browsers, JavaScript is injected into the website’s Document Object Model (DOM). The injected script may modify browser attributes such as Audio Context and Voice engines, graphic rendering, installed fonts, and browser navigator objects. `[Ref: Sentinel CAPTCHA Bypass]`

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.descriptionPt: Apply bot-management and application-layer filtering independently of whether a CAPTCHA challenge is triggered. Evaluate protected requests using behavioral, client/session, rate, reputation, token, and automation signals, and block or rate-limit activity that violates policy even when no CAPTCHA was presented.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Deploy layered inline controls that prevent automated access based on observed request and session behavior rather than relying solely on challenge presentation. Use silent challenges, browser/client validation, rate controls, and bot-management signals to prevent clients that mimic legitimate users from obtaining unrestricted access to protected functionality.

techniques.fullNamePt: Steal Application Specific Passwords
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem roubar Application Specific Passwords (ASPs) para obter acesso a **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`), bypassing multifactor authentication (MFA) methods. ASPs are passwords typically used to give third-party applications or legacy devices (which do not support MFA methods) account access. `[Ref: Application Specific Passwords]` `[Ref: Application Specific Passwords Push Sec]` 
 
Um adversário pode socially engineer a user into providing an ASP `[Ref: UNC6293 ASP Creative Phishing Attack]` `[Ref: Application Specific Passwords Phishing]` (using methods like **Phishing for Information** (`T1598`)), generate an ASP for an already compromised account, `[Ref: Mandiant APT42-untangling]` `[Ref: TAG APT42]` or obtain an ASP stored on a system. Afterward, adversaries may use the ASP to access **Valid Accounts** (`T1078`) and, in some cases, maintain **Persistence** (`TA0003`), bypassing any form of MFA set on the account.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: ASPs can be obtained through engenharia social, which your technique explicitly includes. Train users not to generate or disclose ASPs in response to unsolicited instructions.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.descriptionPt: Disable ASP functionality where modern authentication is available. Microsoft specifically supports disabling users' ability to create app passwords and recommends disabling legacy authentication so existing app passwords no longer work.
mitigations.bypassHint: Para PowerShell bloqueado: o motor do PowerShell reside em `System.Management.Automation.dll`, não no executável `powershell.exe`. Carregar a DLL diretamente dentro de um binário C# compilado ou via `MSBuild.exe` / `InstallUtil.exe` (Unmanaged PowerShell - `T1059.001` + `T1127.001`). Para bloqueio de Macros Office (MotW): usar contentores `.ISO`/`.VHDX` ou ficheiros `.LNK` / `.WSF` / ClickOnce (`T1553.005`, `T1204.002`).

mitigations.name: Account Use Policies
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict authentication paths/clients/locations through which accounts using legacy/app-password authentication can authenticate. This matters because an ASP that has been stolen shouldn't automatically have unrestricted account reach.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict which users may create/use ASPs; disable ASP creation where unnecessary; remove existing ASPs. Microsoft allows admins to disable creation and separately delete existing ASPs; Google administrators can view/revoke users' application-specific passwords.

mutableElements.description: Time window used to correlate application-specific password creation, modification, retrieval, or use with subsequent authentication activity. Derive from the normal delay between ASP administration and legitimate first use. Increasing the window captures delayed malicious use but increases FP from unrelated account activity; decreasing it reduces FP but may miss delayed adversary use (FN).

Users or roles authorized to create, manage, or use application-specific passwords. Derive from IAM policy, role assignments, and approved exception records. Broadening the list reduces FP but increases FN from compromised authorized accounts; narrowing it increases FP for legitimate ASP users but reduces FN.

Applications, services, or integrations approved to authenticate using application-specific passwords. Derive from application inventory and IAM/integration configuration. Broadening the set reduces FP but may conceal unauthorized application use (FN); narrowing it increases FP when legitimate applications are omitted.

Approved user/application/use-case relationships for ASP authentication—for example, which user or service is expected to use an ASP with which application. Derive from documented integration workflows and service ownership. Broadening permitted relationships reduces FP but increases FN for abused legitimate credentials; narrowing them increases detection sensitivity and FP.

Devices or managed endpoints from which ASP-related account activity or authentication is expected. Derive from device inventory, endpoint management, and historical successful authentication. Broadening known-device criteria reduces FP but can suppress compromised devices; narrowing increases FP from new/rebuilt legitimate devices.

Expected geographic, network, tenant, or organizational locations for the associated identity/application activity. Derive from historical authentication telemetry and organizational network architecture. Broadening accepted locations reduces travel/remote-work FP but increases FN; narrowing increases sensitivity but also FP.

Authentication methods normally associated with the account/application workflow. Derive from identity-provider policy and historical authentication telemetry. Broadening expected methods reduces FP but can hide fallback or weaker authentication abuse; narrowing increases FP when legitimate authentication methods change.

Legacy clients explicitly permitted to authenticate using ASP-compatible mechanisms. Derive from application inventory and documented compatibility exceptions. Adding clients reduces FP but increases the opportunity for malicious use to blend with approved legacy authentication; removing clients increases FP until legitimate dependencies are remediated.

Network ranges from which approved ASP-backed applications or services normally authenticate. Derive from service/network architecture and historical authentication sources. Broadening ranges reduces FP but increases FN for adversary activity originating within accepted infrastructure; narrowing improves discrimination but increases FP from legitimate infrastructure changes.

techniques.fullNamePt: Indirect Prompt Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem deliver malicious prompts to an LLM indirectly by embedding the prompts in content that the adversary expects may be processed by an LLM. `[Ref: NIST indirect prompt injection]` These prompts can be included in web pages, `[Ref: Palo Alto Indirect Prompt Injection ITW]` documents, emails, tickets, `[Ref: Snyk Indirect Prompt Injection]` code, or other sources that an agent, copilot, or other AI system may retrieve and process. When an LLM processes this content, the embedded instructions may cause the system to perform unintended behaviors. `[Ref: GTIG AI Threats Sep 2026]` 

Os adversários podem utilizar indirect prompt injection to **Impair Autonomous Defenses** (`T1685.007`), and for unauthorized execution of any capabilities available to the LLM.
codeArtifacts: [Ref: Palo Alto Indirect Prompt Injection ITW]

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict AI agents to files, directories, repositories, and content stores required for their approved workflows. Limit write access separately from read access where possible to reduce the actions available following successful indirect prompt injection.
mitigations.bypassHint: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent AI agents processing untrusted or externally controlled content from automatically exercising privileged permissions. Require additional authorization for sensitive operations derived from retrieved content.
mitigations.bypassHint: Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent instructions contained in retrieved or externally supplied content from independently authorizing consequential agent actions. Require tool/API requests derived from external content to satisfy authorization and policy controls independent of the model-generated decision.
mitigations.bypassHint: Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.descriptionPt: Restrict network resources and external destinations accessible to AI agents that process untrusted content. Limit outbound communication and access to unrelated internal services to reduce exfiltration and lateral effects following successful injection.
mitigations.bypassHint: Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Use dedicated identities for AI agents and restrict their permissions to the minimum resources and actions required by the approved workflow. Do not allow retrieved content to change the authorization context associated with the agent.

blockers: M1022 (Restrict File and Directory Permissions): Permissão negada ao tentar modificar binários de serviços, chaves de registo ou diretórios de sistema.
M1026 (Privileged Account Management): Pass-the-Hash com conta de Administrador Local (`RID 500`) falha noutros hosts porque cada máquina possui password única gerida pelo LAPS.
M1038 (Execution Prevention): Erro "This program is blocked by group policy" ao tentar executar binários em `C:\Users\*` ou `C:\Windows\Temp`.
M1030 (Network Segmentation): Sem conectividade direta da sub-rede atual para servidores de produção ou Domain Controllers.
bypasses: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

Abandonar a tentativa de reutilização horizontal de credenciais locais. Em vez disso: (1) Enumerar quem tem permissão de leitura do atributo `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd` (LAPS v1) ou `msLAPS-Password` / `msLAPS-EncryptedPassword` (Windows LAPS) no Active Directory via LDAP (`T1087.002`); (2) Extrair Tokens ou Tickets Kerberos de utilizadores de domínio com sessão ativa na máquina comprometida (`T1134.001` / `T1550.003`); (3) Explorar delegações Kerberos (Unconstrained / Constrained / RBCD - `T1558`) ou certificados AD CS vulneráveis (ESC1-ESC8 - `T1649`).

Enumerar regras de AppLocker em `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2` e localizar diretórios graváveis dentro de `C:\Windows\` (ex: `C:\Windows\Tasks`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, `C:\Windows\tracing`, `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color`). Caso haja validação de assinatura/hash (WDAC), utilizar Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBAS) assinados pela Microsoft como `MSBuild.exe` (T1127.001), `InstallUtil.exe` (T1218.004), `Regsvr32.exe` (T1218.010) ou `Certutil.exe`.

Transformar o host comprometido num pivot multi-homed: (1) Enumerar interfaces de rede secundárias, sessões SSH/RDP ativas e tabelas ARP (`T1016`); (2) Estabelecer túneis SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 ou interface TUN virtual sobre o canal de C2 existente (ex: Ligolo-ng, Chisel - `T1572` / `T1090.001`); (3) Comprometer um Jump Host, servidor de gestão (SCCM, Ansible, vCenter - `T1072`) ou abusar de Internal Spearphishing (`T1534`).

techniques.fullNamePt: Direct Prompt Injection
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem input malicious prompts directly into an LLM’s user interface. `[Ref: NIST Direct Prompt Injection]` The prompts can be designed para contornar (bypass) safeguards, manipulate context, override previous instructions, or coerce the LLM into unauthorized behavior. `[Ref: OWASP Prompt Injection]` 

Os adversários podem utilizar direct prompt injection to **Generate Content** (`T1683`) prohibited by the LLM's guardrails or to induce the system to utilize its capabilities in unintended or prohibited ways. `[Ref: Gemini AI Misuse Jan 2025]` `[Ref: Palo Alto Prompt Injection]` Os adversários podem achieve this by instructing the LLM to ignore previous instructions or safety rules, or by impersonating a role such as a researcher or privileged user. `[Ref: Cybersec Guru Prompt Injection]`

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.descriptionPt: Associate AI interactions with authenticated identities and constrain AI-mediated actions to the permissions of the initiating user. Do not allow prompt content to establish or elevate the authorization context used by downstream tools or services.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.descriptionPt: Prevent user-supplied AI prompts from directly authorizing consequential actions. Forçar a aplicação de tool, API, command, and resource authorization outside the model and reject requested actions that exceed the permissions associated with the initiating user or agent task.

mitigations.name: User Training
mitigations.descriptionPt: Train users responsible for AI-enabled systems to recognize attempts to manipulate system instructions, role boundaries, or safety controls through user-provided prompts and to independently validate consequential AI-generated actions.

techniques.fullNamePt: AI-Enabled Exfiltration
techniques.descriptionPt:
Os adversários podem utilize **Direct Prompt Injection** (`T1699`), **Indirect Prompt Injection** (`T1698`) or other methods to instruct enterprise AI agents para exfiltrar dados. `[Ref: Prompt-Injection Exfil]` `[Ref: Anthropic Report Sep 2026]` When enterprise systems incorporate the use of AI assistants or other AI agents, adversaries may abuse these systems to weaponize sanctioned tools available to the agent. `[Ref: Google Security State of Prompt Injections]` 

As an AI agent processes queries or ingests data, an injected prompt can cause the agent to use its tool connections in unauthorized or unintended ways. When AI agents are induced para exfiltrar dados, other exfiltration techniques likely apply as well to transfer the information out of the network, such as **Exfiltration to Code Repository** (`T1567.001`) or **Exfiltration Over Web Service** (`T1567`). `[Ref: Google Cloud AI Risk Sep 2026]` `[Ref: Barracuda Prompt Injection Phishing Emails]`

analytics.name: Analytic 2079
analytics.descriptionPt: An analyst observes an AI-associated process access data outside $AuthorizedAIDataScope$, followed within $EndpointExfilWindow$ by transfer-capable execution and an outbound connection to a destination outside $AuthorizedAIEndpoints$ from the same process lineage.

bypasses: Auditar permissões efetivas com `AccessChk` / `PowerUp` procurando Unquoted Service Paths (`T1574.009`), Ghost DLL Hijacking (DLLs inexistentes que um serviço `SYSTEM` tenta carregar a partir de pastas no `PATH` onde o utilizador tem escrita - `T1574.001`) ou explorar privilégios de token como `SeBackupPrivilege` / `SeRestorePrivilege` para ignorar ACLs NTFS (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`).

Empregar canais sobre Web Services legítimos permitidos (Microsoft Graph, GitHub, OneDrive), respeitar o Proxy do sistema via `WinINet` com credenciais integradas da sessão atual, aplicar jitter/sleep randomization e fragmentar transferências abaixo dos limiares de DLP.

**AuthorizedAIEndpoints**: legitimate service/repository/API destinations
